book_title_en: Historical Architectural Map of Jiangsu & Shanghai

regions.name: 南京
regions.overview: 南京市位于长江下游，古称金陵、建邺、建康，建城史超过2500年，曾经先后成为东吴、东晋、宋、齐、梁、陈、南唐、明初、太平天国和国民政府的首都，号称"六朝古都""十朝都会"，现为江苏省的省会，简称"宁"。南京主城区位于长江东岸，东有钟山，一地兼有深水、平原、高山之形胜，山川秀美，人物俊彦，号称"虎踞龙盘""江南佳丽地，金陵帝王州"，古建筑数量之多、价值之高，堪与西安、洛阳、北京三大古都相媲美。重要古建筑包括陵寝、佛寺、古塔、园林、民居等类型。明代洪武年间修筑的南京城墙共分四重，曾经是世界第一大城垣，有20多公里得以幸存至今。南京保存着南朝陵墓石刻、南唐二陵、明孝陵等古代陵墓建筑遗迹，与自然环境融为一体。瞻园是明代开国功臣徐达后人的府邸花园，假山造型奇秀，跻身江南名园之列。甘熙住宅建于清朝中叶，俗称"九十九间半"，占地广阔，格局严谨，以"青砖小瓦马头墙，回廊挂落花格窗"著称于世。明故宫是北京紫禁城的蓝本，现仅存遗址。栖霞寺舍利塔是一座南唐时期重建的密檐古塔，造型秀丽。南京地区现辖玄武区（市政府驻地）、鼓楼区、秦淮区、建邺区、浦口区、栖霞区、雨花台区、六合区、江宁区、溧水区和高淳区11个区，有国家级文物保护单位49处，省级文物保护单位119处，本书介绍国保建筑29处，省保建筑10处。
regions.overview_en: Located in the lower reaches of the Yangtze River, Nanjing was historically known as Jinling, Jianye, and Jiankang. With a city-building history exceeding 2,500 years, it served as capital for the Eastern Wu, Eastern Jin, Song, Qi, Liang, Chen, Southern Tang, early Ming, Taiping Heavenly Kingdom, and the Nationalist government—earning the titles "Capital of Six Dynasties" and "Capital of Ten Dynasties." It is now the provincial capital of Jiangsu, abbreviated as "Ning." The main urban area lies on the east bank of the Yangtze, with Zhongshan Mountain to the east, combining deep water, plains, and mountains. Known as "a tiger crouching and a dragon coiling" and "the beautiful land south of the Yangtze, the imperial prefecture of Jinling," Nanjing's ancient architecture rivals that of Xi'an, Luoyang, and Beijing. Key types include mausoleums, Buddhist temples, pagodas, gardens, and residences. The Nanjing City Wall built during the Hongwu reign of the Ming Dynasty had four layers and was once the world's largest city wall, with over 20 km surviving today. Nanjing preserves Southern Dynasties tomb stone carvings, the Southern Tang Two Mausoleums, and the Ming Xiaoling Mausoleum, integrated with the natural environment. Zhan Garden was the mansion garden of descendants of Xu Da, a founding hero of the Ming Dynasty, with extraordinary rockery formations ranking among Jiangnan's famous gardens. Ganxi Residence, built in the mid-Qing Dynasty and popularly called "ninety-nine and a half rooms," features "blue bricks, small tiles, horse-head walls, winding corridors, and lattice windows." The Ming Palace was the blueprint for Beijing's Forbidden City, though only ruins remain. The Qixia Temple Stupa is an exquisitely shaped multi-eaved pagoda rebuilt during the Southern Tang. Nanjing currently administers 11 districts with 49 national and 119 provincial cultural heritage sites; this book introduces 29 national and 10 provincial protected buildings.

projects.name: 总统府
projects.level: 第七批全国重点文物保护单位（2013年）
projects.level_en: 7th Batch National Key Cultural Heritage Site (2013)
projects.address_en: No. 292 Changjiang Road, Xuanwu District
highlights: 中轴建筑群
东部轴线建筑群
西部轴线建筑群（煦园）
孙中山临时大总统办公室
子超楼
projects.content_zh: 总统府迄今已有600多年历史。明朝这里曾经是归德侯府和汉王府，清朝为江南总督署、两江总督署，并成为江宁织造府的一部分。清代康熙、乾隆下江南时曾驻跸于此。太平天国时期这里是洪秀全天朝宫殿所在地，太平天国失败后被焚毁，后来曾国藩在此重建两江总督署，1912年孙中山在此就任中华民国临时大总统。此后这里做过江苏总督府、副总统府；1927年国民政府成立，这里成为国民政府机关，抗日战争时期曾先后作为日军机关和汪伪政权机关。目前总统府景区是中国最大的近代史博物馆，共占地9万平方米，主要景区包括中、东、西三个区域。中区（中轴线）为国民政府、总统府及所属机构；西区为孙中山临时大总统办公室、秘书处、西花园、孙中山起居室及参谋本部；东区主要为行政院、马厩和东花园，以及近年迁建至此的陶林二公祠。景区中分布多个展览，包括总统府文物史料、孙中山与南京临时政府、太平天国、清两江总督、国民行政院等十多处史料和复原陈列。
projects.content_en: The President Palace has a history of over 600 years. During the Ming Dynasty, it was the Marquis of Guide Mansion and the Prince of Han Mansion. In the Qing Dynasty, it served as the Jiangnan Governor's Office and the Liangjiang Governor-General's Office, and became part of the Jiangning Textile Manufacturing Bureau. Emperors Kangxi and Qianlong stayed here during their southern inspection tours. During the Taiping Heavenly Kingdom, it was Hong Xiuquan's Heavenly King Palace; after the Taiping defeat it was burned down, and Zeng Guofan rebuilt the Liangjiang Governor-General's Office here. In 1912, Sun Yat-sen was inaugurated as the Provisional President of the Republic of China here. It later served as the Jiangsu Governor's Office and the Vice President's Office. In 1927, with the establishment of the Nationalist government, it became a Nationalist government institution. During the War of Resistance against Japan, it was used by Japanese forces and the Wang Jingwei puppet regime. Today, the President Palace scenic area is China's largest modern history museum, covering 90,000 square meters with three main zones: central, eastern, and western. The central zone (central axis) contains the Nationalist government, the President Palace, and affiliated institutions. The western zone includes Sun Yat-sen's Provisional President's Office, the Secretariat, the West Garden, Sun Yat-sen's living quarters, and the General Staff Headquarters. The eastern zone mainly contains the Executive Yuan, stables, the East Garden, and the relocated Tao-Lin Memorial Temple. The scenic area hosts multiple exhibitions including President Palace cultural relics, Sun Yat-sen and the Nanjing Provisional Government, the Taiping Heavenly Kingdom, the Qing Liangjiang Governor-General, and the Nationalist Executive Yuan.

projects.name: 明故宫遗址
projects.level: 第六批全国重点文物保护单位（2006年）
projects.level_en: 6th Batch National Key Cultural Heritage Site (2006)
projects.address_en: No. 311 East Zhongshan Road, Xuanwu District
highlights: 午门
西华门
西安门
奉天殿遗址
外五龙桥
projects.content_zh: 明故宫遗址位于南京城区东部，由内部的宫城和外部的皇城组成，原为明太祖朱元璋营建的皇宫。东至中山门，西至西华门，南至瑞金路，北至佛金桥，占地约16平方公里的广阔范围内均为皇城遗址，核心区域是大内紫禁城即宫城。元至正二十六年（1366年），明朝尚未建立，吴王朱元璋已经开始卜地营建新宫。相传他曾调集军民20万，在南京填燕雀湖、筑新宫。仅一年时间即建成，朱元璋在宫中正式登基。由于时间紧迫，建筑质量不高，明洪武八年（1375年）又推倒重建，洪武十年（1377年）建成，基础加固，工料比此前讲究。明故宫的设计遵循礼制，附会"三朝五门"制度，从南至北设洪武门、承天门、端门、午门、奉天门，前朝以奉天、华盖、谨身三大殿为核心，其北为后廷，在中轴线上建乾清、交泰、坤宁三宫，两侧设东西六宫，西侧设御花园。此外还在宫城前按"左祖右社"规制，设立太庙与社稷坛，并陆续在午门内和承天门外建金水桥（内外五龙桥），承天门外设千步廊，五府六部大小九卿衙署，多建于承天门两侧。今北京故宫即是仿南京明故宫建造的，规模更大一些。明永乐十九年（1421年）迁都北京后，明故宫日益倾颓，南明弘光帝在此即位时，仅武英殿尚可作为登基之所。清代此宫已成丘墟，太平天国时又拆走砖石修建天王府。国民政府成立后，将旧址西南部辟为机场。1928至1929年，为迎孙中山灵柩奉安中山陵，开辟中山东路，从明故宫当中穿过。日军占领期间，为扩大机场，拆除了西华门、社稷坛等遗迹。明故宫机场沿用至1956年。20世纪80年代中期建立明故宫遗址公园，对外开放，2000年将几处城门遗址改建为遗址广场。目前明故宫尚有外金水桥、五桥券等遗迹保存完好，1937年修筑御街道时改变了桥的弧度，并改为水泥栏杆，1990年对桥面和栏杆又有改建。午门原为凹字形平面，中部开三个券门，民国初年拆去两翼，将左右两侧掖门券洞暴露出来。墩台上有城楼和左右方亭柱础。墩台东西90米，南北27.5米，高11米，下部有雕刻精美的石须弥座。登城马道已毁，近年新修登城台阶。金水桥在午门内，桥券、桥面为原貌，栏杆已失。三大殿旧址堆砌出三个台阶，展示了一些柱础。午朝门公园内有明故宫石刻和考古出土的石柱础、石构件等。太庙遗址在御街道东侧，南京航空航天大学内，校长办公楼前有太庙柱础，近年还发现了刻有"祭"字的古井。东华门位于中山东路南侧532号东华门遗址公园，墩台保存尚好，台顶留有柱础。西华门位于中山东路524号，西华门遗址广场，仅存须弥座和路面。西安门位于龙蟠中路202号，西安门遗址公园内，墩台南北两端残损，有三个门洞，须弥座为明初卷叶纹样，与东华门、西华门须弥座素纹的简朴风格不同。御花园假山券门在中山东路北侧的南京军区体工队内，为一石砌建筑，南北设门，入门折向东为石砌拱券，其东段亦可出入，全长6.9米，高2.5米，石面打琢成凹凸不平状，曾被误传为马娘娘梳妆台，已被移入白马公园。奉天门遗址在中山东路南侧，现存部分须弥座台基和东南角的螭首，位置已被移动。2012年在午朝门公园内发现了奉天门的基址和皇宫排水通道。
projects.content_en: Located in the eastern part of Nanjing's urban area, the Ming Palace ruins consist of an inner palace city and an outer imperial city. Originally the imperial palace built by the Hongwu Emperor Zhu Yuanzhang, the site extends from Zhongshan Gate in the east to Xihua Gate in the west, from Ruijin Road in the south to Fojin Bridge in the north, covering approximately 16 square kilometers of imperial city ruins, with the core area being the Forbidden City palace. In 1366, before the Ming Dynasty was established, King Wu Zhu Yuanzhang began selecting a site and building a new palace. It is said he mobilized 200,000 soldiers and civilians to fill the Yanchue Lake and construct the new palace. Completed in just one year, Zhu Yuanzhang was enthroned in the palace. Due to the rushed construction, quality was poor; in 1375 it was demolished and rebuilt, completed in 1377 with reinforced foundations and better materials. The Ming Palace design followed ritual systems, incorporating the "Three Courts and Five Gates" arrangement. From south to north were Hongwu Gate, Chengtian Gate, Duan Gate, Meridian Gate, and Fengtian Gate. The outer court centered on the three grand halls of Fengtian, Huagai, and Jinshen. To the north was the inner court with the three palaces of Qianqing, Jiaotai, and Kunning on the central axis, flanked by the Six Eastern and Western Palaces, with an imperial garden to the west. The site also included the Imperial Ancestral Temple and Altar of Land and Grain following the "left ancestor, right altar" regulation. Today's Beijing Forbidden City was modeled after the Nanjing Ming Palace, though on a larger scale. After the capital moved to Beijing in 1421, the Ming Palace gradually fell into ruin. During the Southern Ming, only Wuying Hall could serve for the Hongguang Emperor's enthronement. By the Qing Dynasty it was already in ruins, and during the Taiping Heavenly Kingdom bricks and stones were removed to build the Heavenly King's Palace. After the Nationalist government was established, the southwestern part was converted into an airport. From 1928 to 1929, East Zhongshan Road was cut through the palace to welcome Sun Yat-sen's coffin to Zhongshan Mausoleum. During the Japanese occupation, Xihua Gate and the Altar of Land and Grain were demolished to expand the airport, which remained in use until 1956. A Ming Palace Ruins Park was established in the mid-1980s and opened to the public. In 2000, several gate ruins were converted into ruin plazas. Surviving relics include the Outer Golden Water Bridge and five bridge arches. The Meridian Gate originally had a U-shaped plan with three central archways; in the early Republican period the wings were demolished, exposing the side gate archways. The platform measures 90m east-west, 27.5m north-south, and 11m high, with exquisitely carved stone Sumeru pedestals at the base. Other surviving elements include the Golden Water Bridge within the Meridian Gate, column bases of the three grand halls, stone carvings in Wuchaomen Park, the Imperial Ancestral Temple ruins, Donghua Gate, Xihua Gate, Xi'an Gate, and the Fengtian Gate foundation discovered in 2012.

projects.name: 原国立中央博物院旧址（南京博物院）
projects.name_en: Site of Former National Central Museum (Nanjing Museum)
projects.level: 第五批全国重点文物保护单位（2001年）
projects.level_en: 5th Batch National Key Cultural Heritage Site (2001)
projects.address_en: No. 309 East Zhongshan Road, Xuanwu District
highlights: 仿辽代宫殿式风格
大殿仿蓟县独乐寺山门
黄琉璃庑殿顶
《营造法式》设计
projects.content_zh: 1933年由蔡元培提议，设立国立中央博物院筹备处，1934年开始筹建，由中央研究院补助征地拆迁，建筑费由管理中英庚款董事会补助150万。当时邀请李宗侃、李锦沛、徐敬直、杨廷宝等13位建筑师送建筑方案，共收到方案12份，由管理中英庚款董事会总干事杭立武、建筑师刘敦桢、梁思成及张道藩、李济等五人组成委员会。经审查所有方案均不合用，用无记名投票方式选取徐敬直的方案作为底本进行修改。修改的设计将原方案仿明清宫殿式风格改为仿辽代宫殿式风格。殿前有宽阔的三层平台，大殿仿辽代蓟县独乐寺山门的形式，结构多按《营造法式》设计，细部和装饰参考唐宋遗存，瓦当和鸱尾等构件都经过考证后制作，柱子有"侧脚""生起"，比例严谨，形制古朴。主体建筑为黄琉璃庑殿顶七开间大殿，内部主体三层，两翼及后部两层。四角有陈列室，平屋顶，四面屋檐作盝顶，以求风格协调。1936年11月举行奠基仪式，1937年抗日战争爆发，工程暂停，日军占据期间曾对已完成的部分加以改造，作为防空总机构，造成很大破坏。1945年后迁回南京，1946年12月开始按原设计方案进行设计，1948年4月完工，今为南京博物院。
projects.content_en: In 1933, Cai Yuanpei proposed establishing a preparatory office for the National Central Museum. Construction began in 1934, with land acquisition subsidized by the Academia Sinica and construction costs of 1.5 million yuan subsidized by the Sino-British Boxer Indemnity Board. Thirteen architects including Li Zongkan, Li Jinpei, Xu Jingzhi, and Yang Tingbao were invited to submit designs, with 12 proposals received. A committee of five including Hang Liwu, Liu Dunzhen, Liang Sicheng, Zhang Daofan, and Li Ji reviewed them. Finding none fully suitable, the committee selected Xu Jingzhi's design by secret ballot as the basis for modification. The revised design changed the style from Ming-Qing palace imitation to Liao Dynasty palace imitation. In front of the hall is a broad three-tier platform. The main hall imitates the form of the Dule Temple gate in Ji County from the Liao Dynasty, with structures designed according to the Yingzao Fashi (Building Standards). Details and decorations reference Tang and Song survivals; components such as tile ends and chiwei (roof ornaments) were produced after research. Columns feature "cejiao" (inward inclination) and "shengqi" (height variation), with rigorous proportions and an ancient form. The main building is a seven-bay hall with yellow glazed hip-and-gable roof, three interior stories, and two-story wings and rear section. Four corners house exhibition rooms with flat roofs and four-sided eaves in the luding style for stylistic harmony. The foundation ceremony was held in November 1936, but the War of Resistance against Japan broke out in 1937 and construction was suspended. During the Japanese occupation, completed portions were modified for use as an air defense headquarters, causing significant damage. After returning to Nanjing in 1945, design resumed according to the original plan in December 1946, and construction was completed in April 1948. Today it houses the Nanjing Museum.

projects.name: 国民党中央党史史料陈列馆旧址（中国第二历史档案馆）
projects.name_en: Site of Historical Museum of KMT's Central Party History (The Second Historical Archives of China)
projects.level: 第五批全国重点文物保护单位（2001年）
projects.level_en: 5th Batch National Key Cultural Heritage Site (2001)
projects.address_en: No. 309 East Zhongshan Road, Xuanwu District
highlights: 钢筋混凝土仿古宫殿式
黄琉璃歇山顶
回字形平面
牌楼大门
projects.content_zh: 国民党中央党史史料陈列馆在明故宫遗址西侧，又名国民党中央党史编纂委员会。中国国民党党史史料编纂委员会设立于1929年，此前曾在中央侨务委员会新房办公，1935春在明故宫西宫遗址上筹建新会舍。抗战爆发后这里成为日伪军兵营，1945年委员会迁回旧址，1949年南京解放，委员会会址与档案史料一同由人民政府接管，成为中国第二历史档案馆。该建筑群包括警亭、入口牌坊和陈列室等，由杨廷宝设计，馥记营造厂承建，中央大学建筑专业师生监理，1936年落成。主楼为钢筋混凝土仿古宫殿式，高四层，外观为黄琉璃歇山顶的两层大殿，底层设台基，有汉白玉栏杆围合的楼梯和月台，是办公用房和档案库房。办公室以回廊相连，中间是半地下的档案储藏库，两库各一百平方米，内呈"回"字阶梯型。二、三层是两层殿身，二层外部有周围外廊，为宽敞的史料陈列大厅。四楼为阁楼，内部采用仿古风格的装饰，有棱花门窗，天花藻井，沥粉彩画，富丽堂皇。主楼四角有方形绿琉璃攒尖顶的警卫房，入口有水泥仿木结构的四柱三间牌坊大门。
projects.content_en: Located west of the Ming Palace ruins, the Historical Museum of the KMT's Central Party History was also known as the KMT Central Party History Compilation Committee. Established in 1929, the committee previously operated from the new building of the Central Overseas Chinese Affairs Committee. In spring 1935, construction began on a new facility on the site of the Ming Palace's western palace. After the War of Resistance broke out, it became a Japanese-puppet military barracks. The committee returned in 1945, and after Nanjing's liberation in 1949, the premises and archives were taken over by the People's Government, becoming The Second Historical Archives of China. The complex includes guard pavilions, an entrance paifang (memorial archway), and exhibition halls, designed by Yang Tingbao, constructed by Fuji Construction Company, and supervised by faculty and students of the Department of Architecture at Central University. Completed in 1936, the main building is a reinforced concrete structure in the antique palace style, four stories high, appearing as a two-story grand hall with yellow glazed hip-and-gable roof. The ground floor has a platform base with stairs and a moon terrace enclosed by white marble railings, serving as offices and archive storage. Offices are connected by corridors, with semi-underground archive storage in the center, each storage room 100 square meters with a "回" (Hui)-shaped stepped plan. The second and third floors form the two-story hall body, with surrounding exterior corridors on the second floor creating spacious exhibition halls. The fourth floor is an attic with antique-style decoration including lattice doors and windows, coffered ceilings, and gilded polychrome paintings. At the four corners of the main building are square guard rooms with green glazed pyramidal roofs. The entrance features a four-column, three-bay paifang gate in cement imitating wood structure.

projects.name: 梅园新村（中共代表团办事处旧址）
projects.name_en: Meiyuan New Village (Former Office of CPC Delegation)
projects.level: 第四批全国重点文物保护单位（1996年）
projects.level_en: 4th Batch National Key Cultural Heritage Site (1996)
projects.address_en: Nos. 17, 30, 35 Meiyuan New Village, Xuanwu District
highlights: 30号主楼
17号代表团办事处
两层独院式别墅
砖木结构
projects.content_zh: 梅园新村是从20世纪20年代开始，到40年代末逐渐建成的国民政府官员的中高档住宅区，现存33栋民国住宅，多为两层独院式别墅，采用砖混结构和青砖墙面。1946年5月到1947年3月国共两党和平谈判，中共代表团曾住在梅园新村17号、30号、35号，周恩来、邓颖超、董必武、李维汉、廖承志、钱瑛等都曾在此居住办公。30号主体为西式二层别墅，坐北朝南，楼下是周恩来和邓颖超的起居室和卧室，楼上是机要室。当时驻地周围有国民党特务监视，代表团将30号院墙加高，并在传达室和北屋上加盖了一层小楼。35号在30号之西，仅一墙之隔，有门互通，也是二层楼房，楼下为董必武、廖承志的办公室和卧室，楼上为钱瑛、李维汉的办公室和卧室，叶剑英也曾在此居住。17号与其他两处房屋有道路相隔，在路东，门西向，二层楼房，是代表团对外办事机构，有外事组、新闻组、军事组和妇女组八路军驻京办事处等。代表团在园内南侧盖了一座二层楼房，楼上为宿舍，楼下为饭厅，周恩来曾在此举行记者招待会。
projects.content_en: Meiyuan New Village was a mid-to-high-end residential area for Nationalist government officials, gradually built from the 1920s to the late 1940s. Thirty-three Republican-era residences survive, mostly two-story detached villas with brick-concrete structure and blue brick walls. From May 1946 to March 1947, during the peace negotiations between the KMT and CPC, the CPC delegation lived at Nos. 17, 30, and 35 Meiyuan New Village. Zhou Enlai, Deng Yingchao, Dong Biwu, Li Weihan, Liao Chengzhi, and Qian Ying all lived and worked here. No. 30 is a Western-style two-story villa facing south, with Zhou Enlai and Deng Yingchao's living room and bedroom on the ground floor and a cipher room upstairs. Surrounded by KMT secret service surveillance, the delegation raised the courtyard wall and added a small story above the gatehouse and north room. No. 35, immediately west of No. 30 with a connecting door, is also a two-story building: Dong Biwu and Liao Chengzhi's offices and bedrooms on the ground floor, Qian Ying and Li Weihan's offices and bedrooms upstairs; Ye Jianying also lived here. No. 17, separated by a road on the east side with a west-facing entrance, is a two-story building serving as the delegation's external office, housing the foreign affairs, news, military, and women's groups as well as the Eighth Route Army's Nanjing office. The delegation built a two-story building on the south side of the garden, with dormitories upstairs and a dining hall downstairs, where Zhou Enlai held press conferences.

projects.name: 国民大会堂旧址和国立美术陈列馆旧址
projects.name_en: Site of the National Great Hall of the People and Site of the National Art Gallery
projects.level: 第六批全国重点文物保护单位（2006年）
projects.level_en: 6th Batch National Key Cultural Heritage Site (2006)
projects.address_en: No. 262 Changjiang Road, Xuanwu District
highlights: 现代风格
2500个席位
钢筋混凝土结构
中国第一个国家美术馆
projects.content_zh: 国民大会堂旧址在总统府东侧，是民国时期规模最大，设施最先进的会堂，现为南京人民大会堂。大会堂是为筹备"国民大会"召开而兴建，由公利工程司奚福泉设计，上海陆根记营造厂承建，1936年5月竣工。施工过程中陶记工程师事务所的李宗侃曾对方案进行局部修改，使其更符合"中国固有形式"的要求。建筑坐北朝南，地上四层，地下一层。立面横向分为三段，整体为现代风格，平屋顶，仅在檐口、雨棚和门厅等处添加了民族风格的装饰。会堂内部大厅分为前厅、剧场和表演台三部分，前厅为砖混结构，中部剧场为钢筋混凝土结构，型钢屋架。剧场内共设2500个席位，内部采用冷暖通风、消防、盥洗洗等先进设施。抗战胜利后对国民大会堂进行修复，每个座椅背后设置了投票按钮。会场西端有仅通一人的暗道，通向蒋介石专用休息室，供蒋介石进出会场专用，平时锁闭。大会堂东侧是国立美术陈列馆旧址，与国民大会堂同时设计，同年建成，风格也一致，是中国第一个国家美术馆。建筑采用钢筋混凝土结构，主体四层，两翼三层，现为江苏省美术馆，2011年列为省保单位。
projects.content_en: Located east of the President Palace, the former National Great Hall of the People was the largest and most advanced auditorium of the Republican era, now the Nanjing People's Great Hall. Built in preparation for the "National Assembly," it was designed by Xi Fuquan of the Gongli Engineering Company and constructed by Shanghai Lugenji Construction Company, completed in May 1936. During construction, Li Zongkan of the Taoji Engineering Firm made partial modifications to better meet the requirements of "China's inherent form." The building faces south, with four above-ground stories and one basement. The facade is horizontally divided into three sections, overall in modern style with a flat roof, with ethnic-style decorations only at the eaves, canopies, and entrance hall. The interior hall consists of a front hall, theater, and stage. The front hall is brick-concrete structure, the central theater is reinforced concrete with steel roof trusses. The theater has 2,500 seats with advanced facilities including heating/cooling ventilation, fire protection, and restrooms. After the War of Resistance victory, the hall was restored and voting buttons were installed behind each seat. At the west end of the venue is a narrow passage for one person, leading to Chiang Kai-shek's private lounge, used exclusively for his entry and exit, normally locked. East of the hall is the former National Art Gallery, designed and completed in the same year with a consistent style—it was China's first national art museum. The reinforced concrete building has a four-story main body and three-story wings, now housing the Jiangsu Provincial Art Museum, listed as a provincial protected site in 2011.

projects.name: 国立中央大学旧址（东南大学）
projects.name_en: Site of the National Central University (Southeast University)
projects.level: 第六批全国重点文物保护单位（2006年）
projects.level_en: 6th Batch National Key Cultural Heritage Site (2006)
projects.address_en: No. 2 Sipailou, Xuanwu District
highlights: 四馆一堂
大礼堂（文艺复兴风格）
孟芳图书馆
法国梧桐林荫道
projects.content_zh: 东南大学的前身是1902年张之洞创办的三江师范学堂，1915年改为南京高等师范学校。1920年春，郭秉文联合张謇、蔡元培、蒋梦麟等10人提出建立东南大学的建议。1921年9月国立东南大学正式成立。1927年国民政府建都南京后，将东南大学与其他8所学校合并，第二年定名为国立中央大学，成为首都的第一大学。成立东南大学后，郭秉文又聘请美国建筑师韦尔逊拟定通盘校园规划。整座校园坐北朝南，两条交通干道形成"T"字形，以南校门—大礼堂的南北轴线为主轴，大礼堂前的东西大道为次轴。校园的主体建筑是所谓"四馆一堂"——图书馆（1923年）、体育馆（1923年）、科学馆（1927年）、生物馆（1929年）和大礼堂（1931年），都采用地道的西方古典建筑形式。整座校园一次规划成形，后来则按实际情况，筹措到经费后分期建造。早期建造的图书馆和体育馆聘请外国建筑师，稍后的科学馆和生物馆则由中国建筑师设计。学校正门在南面，入门后是一条长长的法国梧桐林荫道，大礼堂便坐落在道路尽端，位于校园的中心。大礼堂以弗吉尼亚大学图书馆为母本，采用文艺复兴风格，中央是铜制大穹顶，高耸挺拔，成为视觉的焦点，南面凸出带爱奥尼列柱和三角山花的前廊。大礼堂前的林荫道两侧分别是图书馆和生物馆（现为中大院），呈对称布置，强化了大礼堂的中心地位。这两座建筑都在南面设门廊，采用四柱三间的形式，与大礼堂的前廊呼应。科学馆（现为健雄馆）位于大礼堂东南部，入口处也是四根爱奥尼列柱支撑的门廊，虽然未用三角形山花，但大片的红色瓦屋面和老虎窗仍带有浓郁的西方古典韵味。体育馆位于大礼堂西北部，入口设有大楼梯和两根塔司干立柱支撑的门廊，体现出粗犷之感。
projects.content_en: Southeast University traces its origins to the Sanjiang Normal School founded by Zhang Zhidong in 1902, renamed Nanjing Higher Normal School in 1915. In spring 1920, Guo Bingwen, together with Zhang Jian, Cai Yuanpei, Jiang Menglin and nine others, proposed establishing Southeast University, which was formally founded in September 1921. After the Nationalist government established its capital in Nanjing in 1927, Southeast University merged with eight other schools, and the following year was renamed National Central University, becoming the capital's foremost university. After founding Southeast University, Guo Bingwen hired American architect Wilson to create a comprehensive campus plan. The campus faces south, with two main roads forming a "T" shape—the north-south axis from the south gate to the auditorium as the main axis, and the east-west road in front of the auditorium as the secondary axis. The main buildings are the so-called "Four Halls and One Auditorium": the Library (1923), Gymnasium (1923), Science Hall (1927), Biology Hall (1929), and Auditorium (1931), all in authentic Western classical style. The entire campus was planned at once and built in phases as funding became available. The earlier Library and Gymnasium were designed by foreign architects, while the later Science and Biology Halls were designed by Chinese architects. The main entrance is on the south; entering leads to a long plane tree-lined avenue, with the auditorium at its end in the campus center. Modeled after the University of Virginia Library, the auditorium is in Renaissance style with a tall copper dome as the visual focal point, and a projecting portico with Ionic columns and triangular pediment on the south. The Library and Biology Hall (now Zhongda Hall) flank the avenue symmetrically, reinforcing the auditorium's central position, both with four-column, three-bay porticos on the south echoing the auditorium. The Science Hall (now Jianxiong Hall) is southeast of the auditorium, also with a four-Ionic-column portico entrance; though without a triangular pediment, its large red tile roof and dormer windows retain strong Western classical character. The Gymnasium is northwest of the auditorium, with a grand staircase and a portico supported by two Tuscan columns at the entrance, conveying a robust feel.

projects.name: 国立中央研究院旧址
projects.level: 第六批全国重点文物保护单位（2006年）
projects.level_en: 6th Batch National Key Cultural Heritage Site (2006)
projects.address_en: No. 2 Sipailou, Xuanwu District
highlights: 地质研究所
社会科学研究所
历史语言研究所
总办事处大楼
仿明清宫殿式风格
projects.content_zh: 国立中央研究院在玄武湖南侧的鸡笼山南麓，是民国时期成立的最高学术研究机构，隶属国民政府。1928年6月中央研究院成立，蔡元培担任院长，设立物理、化学、工程、地质、天文、气象、历史语言、心理、社会科学及动植物等十个研究所，分别设在南京、上海和北平（今北京）。后来设在北平（今北京）的研究所陆续迁往南京，仅化学、物理和工程三个研究所留在上海。抗战时期各研究所内迁，研究院旧址成为汪伪政府的文物保管委员会。抗战胜利后地质研究所、历史语言研究所、社会科学研究所和总办事处都设在此地。地质研究所在研究院旧址的西北角，依顺山势朝向东南。大楼建于1931年，由基泰工程司杨廷宝设计，朱森记营造厂承建，楼高两层，采用仿明清宫殿式风格，钢筋混凝土结构。建筑平面呈"凸"字形，单檐歇山顶，屋面覆绿色琉璃瓦，梁枋及檐口有彩绘仿木的混凝土斗拱。大楼入口向外伸出卷棚顶门厅，一楼中部为地质标本陈列室，其余为制作、资料、科研和办公用房，东南角地下室有锅炉房。该楼现为中国科学院南京地质、古生物研究所和古生物陈列室。社会科学研究所在地质研究所东南方，研究院旧址中轴北侧。建于1931年，蔡元培题写奠基碑。大楼坐北朝南，高三层，坡屋顶，现为中科院南京地质、古生物研究所办公楼。历史语言研究所在社会科学研究所东南侧，建于1936年，由杨廷宝设计，六合营造厂承建，采用仿明清宫殿式风格，钢筋混凝土结构。大楼坐北向南，两侧各有侧门，楼高三层，绿琉璃单檐歇山顶，青砖外墙，下部用水泥人造石涂饰。大楼两端为阅览室和小型书库，其余为办公用房，现为中国科学院南京地质、古生物研究所。总办事处大楼在研究院最南端，由杨廷宝设计，新金记康号营造厂建造。建于1947年，时间最晚，体量最大，结构也最复杂。楼高三层，屋顶铺绿琉璃筒瓦。屋顶较复杂，采用两坡顶，两侧跌落各出歇山顶，前出歇山式龟头屋。平面呈"T"字形，北侧尽端有突出的纵向三层书库，西侧尽端为会堂和阅览室，其他部分为内走廊布局的办公室。现为中国科学院江苏分院、江苏省科学技术委员会、中共江南省科学技术工作委员会所在地。门前两侧及围墙东侧有方形攒尖顶警卫室，均采用同一风格。
projects.content_en: Located at the southern foot of Jilong Mountain south of Xuanwu Lake, the former National Academia Sinica was the highest academic research institution of the Republican era, under the Nationalist government. Established in June 1928 with Cai Yuanpei as president, it had ten research institutes—physics, chemistry, engineering, geology, astronomy, meteorology, history and philology, psychology, social sciences, and botany/zoology—located in Nanjing, Shanghai, and Beiping (now Beijing). Institutes in Beiping later moved to Nanjing, leaving only chemistry, physics, and engineering in Shanghai. During the War of Resistance, institutes moved inland, and the site became the Wang Jingwei puppet regime's Cultural Relics Preservation Committee. After the war, the Geology, History and Philology, and Social Science Institutes, plus the General Administration Office, were all located here. The Geology Institute, at the northwest corner facing southeast following the terrain, was built in 1931, designed by Yang Tingbao of Jitai Engineering Company and constructed by Zhu Senji Construction Company. The two-story reinforced concrete building is in the style imitating Ming-Qing palaces, with a "convex" plan, single-eave hip-and-gable roof covered in green glazed tiles, and painted concrete dougong imitating wood on beams and eaves. The entrance has a projecting rolling-roof vestibule; the first floor center is a geological specimen exhibition room, with the rest for preparation, archives, research, and offices, and a boiler room in the southeast basement. It now houses the CAS Nanjing Institute of Geology and Paleontology and its exhibition room. The Social Science Institute, southeast of the Geology Institute on the north side of the central axis, was built in 1931 with a foundation stone inscribed by Cai Yuanpei. The three-story south-facing building with a pitched roof now serves as the office building of the CAS Nanjing Institute of Geology and Paleontology. The History and Philology Institute, southeast of the Social Science Institute, was built in 1936, designed by Yang Tingbao and constructed by Liuhe Construction Company, in the Ming-Qing palace imitation style with reinforced concrete. The three-story south-facing building has side doors, green glazed single-eave hip-and-gable roof, blue brick exterior walls, and cement artificial stone coating on the lower part. Both ends house reading rooms and small stacks, with the rest as offices; it now houses the CAS Nanjing Institute of Geology and Paleontology. The General Administration Building, at the southernmost end, was designed by Yang Tingbao and constructed by Xinjinkanghao Construction Company. Built in 1947—the latest, largest, and most structurally complex—it is three stories high with green glazed tube tiles on a complex roof: two-slope roof with stepped hip-and-gable roofs on both sides and a projecting hip-and-gable "turtle-head" room in front. The "T"-shaped plan has a projecting three-story book stack at the north end and an assembly hall and reading room at the west end, with the rest as corridor-layout offices. It now houses the CAS Jiangsu Branch, Jiangsu Provincial Science and Technology Commission, and the CPC Jiangnan Provincial Science and Technology Working Committee. Square pyramidal-roof guard rooms flank the entrance and on the east side of the perimeter wall, all in the same style.

projects.name: 鼓楼
projects.level: 第三批江苏省文物保护单位（1982年）
projects.level_en: 3rd Batch Jiangsu Provincial Cultural Heritage Site (1982)
projects.address_en: West of Gulou Square
highlights: 明洪武十五年建
城阙状基座
清康熙"圣谕"碑
明鼓清碑
projects.content_zh: 南京鼓楼始建于明洪武十五年（1382年），用来昼夜报时和迎王、选妃、接诏时使用。清初被毁，仅存下部台座和台坪上的石柱。清代康熙南巡时曾登上鼓楼台座，康熙二十四年（1685年）两江总督王新命将"圣谕"刻碑竖在台座正中，并建楼保护，更名为"碑楼"，故有"明鼓清碑"之称。如今楼阙上方仍遗留清代刻石"碑楼"字样。民国初年将鼓楼上半部的阁楼改建为重楼，碑穿楼板而过，使石碑形成顶天立地的格局。1923年以鼓楼为主体建立鼓楼公园。现存的鼓楼基座为明洪武十五年（1382年）所建，砖石结构，下长44.5米，宽22.8米，上长43.8米，宽22.6米，高9米，呈城阙状。基座并列开辟三道券门，左右各筑一条券顶石级楼梯；台座横向正中和偏前方各开两扇漏窗，配拱券巷道，接左、右门道与台阶，用来自然采光和通风。基座上方为清康熙二十四年（1685年）所建城楼，采用三开间两层歇山顶，楼中树"圣谕"石碑。台面梯孔之上各建一座歇山顶亭，以防水下注。"圣谕"碑现保存完整，由碑额、碑身和龟趺三部分组成。碑通高5.4米，宽1.45米，厚0.39米，中刻篆书"圣谕"二字，碑文皆用楷书。碑四周围案均为多姿多态的盘龙穿云，其中龟趺高1.25米，长2.15米，宽1.5米。碑文内容是皇帝对官员的谕诫，碑背面镌刻两江总督王新命、江苏巡抚汤斌等20名参与立碑官员的官衔和姓名。
projects.content_en: Nanjing's Drum Tower was first built in the 15th year of the Hongwu reign of the Ming Dynasty (1382), used for day and night timekeeping, as well as for welcoming princes, selecting imperial concubines, and receiving imperial edicts. It was destroyed in the early Qing Dynasty, leaving only the lower platform and stone columns on the platform. During the Kangxi Emperor's southern tour, he climbed the drum tower platform; in the 24th year of Kangxi (1685), Liangjiang Governor-General Wang Xinming had the "Sacred Edict" inscribed on a stele erected in the center of the platform, with a building built to protect it, and renamed it "Stele Tower"—hence the saying "Ming drum, Qing stele." Today, the Qing-dynasty carved characters "Stele Tower" still remain above the tower gate. In the early Republican period, the upper pavilion was rebuilt as a two-story tower, with the stele passing through the floor, creating a heaven-and-earth spanning arrangement. In 1923, Gulou Park was established with the drum tower as its centerpiece. The surviving drum tower base was built in 1382, of brick-stone structure, measuring 44.5m long and 22.8m wide at the bottom, 43.8m long and 22.6m wide at the top, 9m high, in the form of a city gate tower. The base has three parallel archways, with vaulted stone staircases on each side; two lattice windows on the transverse center and front connect to arched passageways leading to the side doors and stairs, providing natural light and ventilation. Above the base is the tower built in 1685, a three-bay two-story hip-and-gable roof building housing the "Sacred Edict" stele. Hip-and-gable roof pavilions are built above the stair openings on the platform to prevent water from pouring in. The "Sacred Edict" stele is fully preserved, consisting of stele head, body, and tortoise base. It stands 5.4m high, 1.45m wide, 0.39m thick, with the seal-script characters "Sacred Edict" in the center and regular-script text. The stele is surrounded by coiling dragons piercing clouds; the tortoise base is 1.25m high, 2.15m long, 1.5m wide. The inscription contains the emperor's admonitions to officials, and the back records the titles and names of 20 officials involved in erecting the stele, including Liangjiang Governor-General Wang Xinming and Jiangsu Governor Tang Bin.

projects.name: 金陵大学旧址（南京大学）
projects.name_en: Site of University of Nanking (Nanjing University)

projects.level_en: 6th Batch National Key Cultural Heritage Site (2006)
projects.address_en: No. 22 Hankou Road, Gulou District
highlights: 北大楼
东大楼
西大楼
大礼堂
图书馆
中式风格灰瓦屋顶
projects.content_zh: 金陵大学前身是清光绪十四年（1888年）由美国传教士创办的汇文书院。1910年汇文书院和宏育书院合并成为金陵大学堂，1927年收归国民政府，日本占领时期，金陵大学校园曾作为国际安全区收容大批难民。1941年汪伪政府在此兴办中央大学，1945年金陵大学在原址复课，1951年与金陵女子文理学院合并，改称公立金陵大学，1952年更名南京大学。1910年由首任校长包文和汇文书院创办人福开森（John Calvin Ferguson）主持，筹建金陵大学校区，由以擅长设计大学校园闻名的美国帕金斯建筑师事务所（Perkins, Fellows & Hamilton Architects）规划设计，陈明记营造厂建造施工。1915年建成部分校舍，1921年基本落成，师生从汇文书院迁入新校址，到1926年已成规模，代表建筑有北大楼、东大楼、西大楼、东北大楼、礼拜堂、图书馆和学生宿舍等十余幢，均采用中式风格，灰瓦屋顶，青砖墙面，部分建筑使用了明南京城墙砖。北大楼为学校主楼，在校园中轴线最北端，1919年建成。大楼采用砖木结构，地上两层，地下一层，墙壁用明城墙砖砌筑，屋顶两侧为灰瓦歇山顶，中部耸出五层高的方形钟楼，楼顶用十字脊，四面歇山顶。东大楼在北大楼东南，原名"科学馆"，建于1913年。采用砖木结构，地上三层，地下一层，青砖砌筑，歇山顶，屋脊中部凸起，加高成为又一重歇山。西大楼与东大楼相对，形式相似，1925年建成，底部用明代城墙砖，上部用烟色黏土砖。图书馆在中轴线最南端，建于1936年，由杨廷宝设计，陈明记承建。地上二层，地下一层，采用钢筋混凝土结构，仿明清宫殿风格。东北大楼在东大楼南侧，建于1935年，采用混合结构，高四层，卷棚屋顶。礼拜堂在西大楼南侧，现为大礼堂，1918年建成。以明代城墙砖砌筑，外观为中式，内部采用西方教堂格局。由歇山顶大殿构成中部主廊空间，两侧出侧廊，前有前廊，各廊两端出硬山顶小屋。学生宿舍在北大楼西侧，共四栋，分别为甲乙楼、丙丁楼、戊己庚楼和辛壬楼，建于1925年。采用砖木结构，青砖墙，卷棚屋顶。
projects.content_en: The predecessor of the University of Nanking was the Huiwen Academy founded by American missionaries in 1888 (14th year of Guangxu). In 1910, Huiwen Academy and Hongyu Academy merged to form the University of Nanking. It was transferred to the Nationalist government in 1927. During the Japanese occupation, the campus served as an international safety zone sheltering large numbers of refugees. In 1941, the Wang Jingwei puppet regime established Central University here; in 1945, the University of Nanking resumed classes on the original site. In 1951 it merged with Ginling Women's College of Arts and Sciences to become the public University of Nanking, and in 1952 was renamed Nanjing University. In 1910, under the leadership of first president Bowen and Huiwen Academy founder John Calvin Ferguson, the new campus was planned by the American firm Perkins, Fellows & Hamilton Architects, renowned for university campus design, and constructed by Chenmingji Construction Company. Partial buildings were completed in 1915, and the campus was essentially finished by 1921 when faculty and students moved from Huiwen Academy. By 1926 it had taken shape, with over ten representative buildings including the North Building, East Building, West Building, Northeast Building, Chapel, Library, and student dormitories—all in Chinese style with gray tile roofs and blue brick walls, some using bricks from the Ming Nanjing City Wall. The North Building, the main building at the northernmost end of the central axis, was completed in 1919. The brick-wood structure has two above-ground stories and one basement, with walls built from Ming city wall bricks. The roof has gray tile hip-and-gable roofs on both sides, with a five-story square bell tower rising in the center, topped with a cross ridge and four-sided hip-and-gable roofs. The East Building, southeast of the North Building and originally named "Science Hall," was built in 1913. The brick-wood structure has three above-ground stories and one basement, built of blue brick with a hip-and-gable roof whose ridge center is raised to form another hip-and-gable layer. The West Building, opposite the East Building in similar form, was completed in 1925, with Ming city wall bricks at the base and smoky clay bricks above. The Library, at the southernmost end of the central axis, was built in 1936, designed by Yang Tingbao and constructed by Chenmingji. The two-story (plus basement) reinforced concrete building is in the Ming-Qing palace imitation style. The Northeast Building, south of the East Building, was built in 1935, a four-story composite structure with a rolling roof. The Chapel, south of the West Building and now the main auditorium, was completed in 1918. Built with Ming city wall bricks, it has a Chinese exterior but Western church interior layout: the hip-and-gable main hall forms the central nave, with side aisles, a front narthex, and gable-roof rooms at each aisle end. Student dormitories, west of the North Building, consist of four buildings (A/B, C/D, E/F/G, H/I/J buildings) built in 1925, with brick-wood structure, blue brick walls, and rolling roofs.

projects.name: 拉贝旧居
projects.level: 第七批全国重点文物保护单位（2013年）
projects.level_en: 7th Batch National Key Cultural Heritage Site (2013)
projects.address_en: No. 1 Xiaofenqiao, Gulou District
highlights: 《拉贝日记》
南京安全区
西式砖木结构
花园小别墅
projects.content_zh: 拉贝旧居为时任德国西门子公司南京分公司经理约翰·拉贝（John H. D. Rabe，1882—1950）在南京的住宅。拉贝1908年来到中国工作，1932年夏他与金陵大学农学院院长谢家声签订协议，学校建造一座兼具办公和居住功能的房屋租给拉贝。这是一座花园小别墅，高两层，采用西式砖木结构，清水砖墙和坡屋顶，入口有门廊。房屋1934年建成，1938年3月拉贝在回国之前都是在此居住。1937年日军入侵南京前夕，拉贝被推选为南京国际安全委员会主席。在南京大屠杀期间，拉贝利用自己的纳粹党员身份，在这处住宅内收容了600多名中国难民；在他负责的不足4平方公里的安全区内，他和十多位安全区国际委员会成员挽救了25万中国人的生命。拉贝在此楼内写下了著名的《拉贝日记》。如今这处旧居改为拉贝纪念馆，展览他在艰难时期的英雄壮举及他与南京人民的深厚友谊。
projects.content_en: The former residence of John Rabe was the Nanjing home of John H. D. Rabe (1882-1950), then manager of the Nanjing branch of Siemens Germany. Rabe came to work in China in 1908. In summer 1932, he signed an agreement with Xie Jiasheng, dean of the University of Nanking's College of Agriculture, for the university to build a combined office and residence for rent to Rabe. This is a two-story garden villa in Western brick-wood style with exposed brick walls and a pitched roof, with a portico at the entrance. Completed in 1934, Rabe lived here until his return to Germany in March 1938. On the eve of the Japanese invasion of Nanjing in 1937, Rabe was elected chairman of the Nanjing International Safety Zone Committee. During the Nanjing Massacre, using his Nazi Party membership, Rabe sheltered over 600 Chinese refugees in this residence; in the safety zone of less than 4 square kilometers under his responsibility, he and over a dozen international committee members saved the lives of 250,000 Chinese people. Rabe wrote his famous "Diary of John Rabe" in this building. Today the former residence has been converted into the John Rabe Memorial Hall, exhibiting his heroic deeds during those difficult times and his deep friendship with the people of Nanjing.

projects.name: 金陵女子大学旧址（南京师范大学随园校区）
projects.name_en: Site of Ginling College (Suiyuan Campus of Nanjing Normal University)
projects.level: 第六批全国重点文物保护单位（2006年）
projects.level_en: 6th Batch National Key Cultural Heritage Site (2006)
projects.address_en: No. 122 Ninghai Road, Gulou District
highlights: 中国第一所女子大学
会议楼（100号）
科学馆（200号）
文学馆（300号）
大礼堂（10号）
图书馆（11号）
projects.content_zh: 金陵女子大学建在南京清凉山东脉小仓山、清乾隆年间名士袁枚的随园遗址上。金陵女子大学是中国第一所女子大学，始建于1915年，由在江浙传教办学的八个美国教会组织联合开办。最初校址位于南京绣花巷李家花园，1923年迁入新校舍。1927年国民政府收回教育权，原美籍校长劳伦斯·德本康夫人被迫辞职，推选首届毕业生吴贻芳为校长。1930年政府规定，高等学校需有三个学院才可称"大学"，由此改名"金陵女子文理学院"。1937年学校内迁，在日军占领时期，校园成为接受妇女和儿童的难民营，最多时曾容纳一万多难民。1942年因美国对日宣战，校舍被日军占用。1946年师生返回南京校内时设备已丢失，但建筑基本保持原貌。1951年金陵女子大学与金陵大学合并，1952年改为南京师范学院，1984年更名南京师范大学。金陵女子大学校舍由美国建筑师亨利·墨菲规划设计，陈明记营造厂承建，当时在墨菲事务所工作的吕彦直参与设计了大部分建筑。校园始建于1922年，1923年完成6栋主要建筑。这批建筑依顺基址的山形水势，围绕中部草坪沿东西向轴线分布：位于校园主轴中心的是会议楼（100号），在其前方两侧为科学馆（200号）和文学馆（300号），在会议楼后部东西布置3幢学生宿舍（400号、500号、600号）。1924年又建成一栋学生宿舍（700号），1934年在科学馆和文学馆前方建成大礼堂（10号）和图书馆（11号），建筑间以仿古走廊相连。会议楼（100号）为校园主楼，原为接待室和室内体育场，坐西朝东，主体高三层，地下室一层，采用白墙红柱，主体为歇山灰瓦顶，中部前后高出成歇山顶。后侧屋顶正中开天窗，檐下有仿木梁枋斗拱，但斗拱与立柱未正确对位，仅平均分布在檐下。科学馆（200号）在会议楼东南，现为国际文化教育学院和国际交流处。采用钢筋混凝土结构，主体高三层，灰瓦单檐歇山顶，柱间斗拱未正确对位。文学馆（300号）在会议楼东北，与科学馆外观相似，仅入口增加了宽阔的门廊，柱间斗拱已正确对位。学生宿舍（400—700号）在会议楼西南与西北两侧，高三层，采用钢筋混凝土结构，木屋架，两端出外廊。大礼堂（10号）在科学馆东侧，高三层，地下室一层，单檐歇山顶。图书馆（11号）在文学馆东侧，现为华夏图书馆，外观与大礼堂相似。
projects.content_en: Ginling College was built on the site of Suiyuan Garden—the former residence of Yuan Mei, a famous scholar of the Qianlong reign—on the eastern branch of Qingliang Mountain in Nanjing. Ginling College was China's first women's university, founded in 1915 through the joint efforts of eight American missionary organizations operating schools in Jiangsu and Zhejiang. Originally located at the Li Family Garden on Xiuhua Lane, it moved to the new campus in 1923. In 1927, the Nationalist government reclaimed educational authority, forcing the resignation of American president Mrs. Lawrence Thurston, and the first graduate Wu Yifang was elected president. In 1930, government regulations required three colleges to be called a "university," so it was renamed "Ginling Women's College of Arts and Sciences." In 1937 the school moved inland; during the Japanese occupation, the campus became a refugee camp for women and children, sheltering over 10,000 refugees at its peak. In 1942, after the U.S. declared war on Japan, the campus was occupied by Japanese forces. When faculty and students returned in 1946, equipment had been lost but the buildings remained essentially intact. In 1951, Ginling College merged with the University of Nanking; in 1952 it became Nanjing Normal College, and in 1984 was renamed Nanjing Normal University. The campus was planned by American architect Henry Murphy, constructed by Chenmingji Construction Company, with Lü Yanzhi—then working at Murphy's firm—participating in the design of most buildings. Construction began in 1922, with six main buildings completed in 1923. Following the terrain's mountains and water, the buildings are distributed along an east-west axis around a central lawn: the Conference Building (No. 100) at the center of the main axis, the Science Hall (No. 200) and Literature Hall (No. 300) flanking it in front, and three student dormitories (Nos. 400, 500, 600) to the east and west behind the Conference Building. A fourth dormitory (No. 700) was added in 1924, and in 1934 the Auditorium (No. 10) and Library (No. 11) were built in front of the Science and Literature Halls, connected by antique-style corridors. The Conference Building (No. 100), the main building originally serving as reception room and indoor gymnasium, faces east with three main stories and one basement, featuring white walls and red columns, a gray-tile hip-and-gable main roof with a raised hip-and-gable section at the front and back center. A skylight opens at the center of the rear roof; under the eaves are imitation wood beams and dougong, though the dougong are not properly aligned with columns but evenly distributed. The Science Hall (No. 200), southeast of the Conference Building and now housing the International College of Culture and Education and International Exchange Office, is a three-story reinforced concrete building with gray-tile single-eave hip-and-gable roof, with misaligned inter-columnar dougong. The Literature Hall (No. 300), northeast of the Conference Building, resembles the Science Hall externally but adds a broad portico at the entrance with properly aligned inter-columnar dougong. Student dormitories (Nos. 400-700), southwest and northwest of the Conference Building, are three-story reinforced concrete buildings with wooden roof trusses and exterior corridors at both ends. The Auditorium (No. 10), east of the Science Hall, is three stories with one basement and a single-eave hip-and-gable roof. The Library (No. 11), east of the Literature Hall and now the Huaxia Library, resembles the auditorium in appearance.

projects.name: 石头城遗迹
projects.level: 第二批江苏省文物保护单位（1982年）
projects.level_en: 2nd Batch Jiangsu Provincial Cultural Heritage Site (1982)
projects.address_en: West of Qingliang Mountain
highlights: 南京现存最古老城垣
鬼脸城
鬼脸照镜
孙权建城
projects.content_zh: 石头城遗迹是南京现存最古老的城垣之一。东汉建安十七年（212年）孙权在楚国金陵邑旧址筑城，命名为石头城，周长七里一百步，南面开二门，东面开一门，北面临江，不设门，城内高处设有堡垒和烽火台，作为军事要塞。石头城与钟山一东一西，遥相呼应，相传诸葛亮曾评论金陵风水称："钟阜龙蟠，石头虎踞，真帝王之宅！"后"石头城"逐渐成为南京城的代称。明初筑都城时，石头城作为城墙的一部分被围入城内。现存石头城段城墙南起红土山路，北至国防园，包括城门清凉门。大部分城墙是在赭红色山崖上直接砌筑红砖，仅清凉门南侧一段用条石砌成。山崖高低起伏，最高处的一段称为"鬼脸城"，在南侧城墙转角的悬崖顶部有一块长7.8米，宽3.2米，凹凸不平的岩石，状如面目狰狞的人脸，由此得名。"鬼脸"对面20米处有方形池塘，天气晴朗时可见"鬼脸"倒映在水中，形成"鬼脸照镜"的奇观。
projects.content_en: The Stone City ruins are among the oldest surviving city walls in Nanjing. In the 17th year of Jian'an of the Eastern Han Dynasty (212), Sun Quan built a city on the site of the former Chu Kingdom's Jinling Yi, naming it Stone City. It had a circumference of seven li and one hundred paces, with two gates on the south, one on the east, and no gate on the north facing the river. High places within the city had fortresses and beacon towers, serving as a military stronghold. Stone City and Zhongshan Mountain face each other from east and west; legend has it that Zhuge Liang commented on Jinling's feng shui: "Zhongfu Mountain coils like a dragon, Stone City crouches like a tiger—truly an emperor's residence!" Later, "Stone City" gradually became a synonym for Nanjing. When the capital city was built in the early Ming Dynasty, Stone City was enclosed as part of the city wall. The surviving Stone City section of the wall runs from Hongtushan Road in the south to the National Defense Park in the north, including the Qingliang Gate. Most of the wall is built directly with red bricks on the ochre-red cliff, except for a section south of Qingliang Gate built with dressed stone. The cliff undulates; the highest section is called "Ghost Face City"—at the top of the cliff at the southern wall corner is a 7.8m long, 3.2m wide, uneven rock resembling a ferocious human face, hence the name. Twenty meters opposite the "Ghost Face" is a square pond; on clear days, the "Ghost Face" reflection can be seen in the water, creating the spectacle of "Ghost Face Gazing in the Mirror."

projects.name: 南京城墙
projects.level: 第三批全国重点文物保护单位（1988年）
projects.level_en: 3rd Batch National Key Cultural Heritage Site (1988)
projects.address_en: Multiple locations in Nanjing
projects.ticket: 神策门—九华山30元（含明城垣博物馆）；富贵山—光华东街20元；东水关—西水关50元（含中华门瓮城）；富贵山—光华东街一段因后半山园小区至中山门实行有限开放，票价降为10元
highlights: 世界最大都城城墙
13座城门
聚宝门（中华门）瓮城
铭文城砖
projects.content_zh: 南京城墙是明代都城（又名应天府城）的城墙。元至正二十六年（1366年）八月，朱元璋接受谋士朱升"高筑墙"的建议，改筑应天府城墙，明洪武十九年（1386年）十二月竣工，历时二十多年，共设有外郭、京城、皇城和宫城四重城垣，其中外郭利用岗垅以土筑成，仅在险要处用城砖筑城门，俗称"土城头"。皇城和宫城位于京城东隅，为明故宫遗址，如今所称的南京城墙为明京城遗迹。明京城利用南京山川的自然走势，将南朝建康城、南唐金陵城的城墙加以扩宽、加高等，南、东、西三侧沿外秦淮河延伸，北至玄武湖南岸、钟山山麓，最北将狮子山纳入城中，全长33.676公里，城高14米到21米，是存世最大的首都城墙。城墙下层用花岗岩、石灰岩基础，墙体用碎砖、砾石和黄土夯实，内外和上部用特大型城砖砌筑，以石灰、糯米汁和桐油做灰缝填料，十分坚固。建造城墙的砖按统一规格，由不同地区烧制，每块砖上都有铭文，记录城砖的来历。城墙上原开有13门，自通济门后顺时针方向分别为：聚宝门、三山门、石城门、清凉门、定淮门、仪凤门、钟阜门、金川门、神策门、太平门、朝阳门和正阳门。各门土原来均有敌楼，装设木门与千斤闸，具有军事重要性的城门则设有道数不等的瓮城，聚宝门（今中华门）、通济门、三山门（今水西门）各有三道瓮城，石城门有两道，神策门（今和平门）有一道。与前代将瓮城外置不同的是，朱元璋通常将瓮城置于城内，以迷惑敌人。现存有明代的聚宝门（中华门）、石城门（汉西门）、神策门（和平门）和清凉门以及重修的朝阳门，其中仅神策门尚存清代重修的城楼。
projects.content_en: The Nanjing City Wall was the wall of the Ming Dynasty capital (also known as Yingtian Prefecture City). In August 1366 (26th year of Zhizheng, Yuan Dynasty), Zhu Yuanzhang accepted advisor Zhu Sheng's suggestion to "build high walls" and began rebuilding the Yingtian Prefecture wall. Completed in December 1386 (19th year of Hongwu) after over twenty years, it had four layers: outer wall, capital city, imperial city, and palace city. The outer wall used earthen mounds with brick gates only at strategic points, commonly called "earth city top." The imperial and palace cities were in the eastern part of the capital, now the Ming Palace ruins; today's "Nanjing City Wall" refers to the capital city remains. The Ming capital city utilized Nanjing's natural terrain, expanding and heightening the walls of the Southern Dynasties Jiankang City and Southern Tang Jinling City. The south, east, and west sides extend along the outer Qinhuai River, the north reaches the south bank of Xuanwu Lake and the foothills of Zhongshan Mountain, with Lion Mountain incorporated at the northernmost point. With a total length of 33.676 km and height of 14-21m, it is the largest surviving capital city wall in the world. The lower layer uses granite and limestone foundations; the wall body is rammed with broken bricks, gravel, and loess; the interior, exterior, and upper parts are built with extra-large city bricks, using lime, glutinous rice juice, and tung oil as mortar—extremely solid. Wall bricks were fired to uniform specifications by different regions, each inscribed with text recording its origin. Thirteen gates originally opened on the wall, clockwise from Tongji Gate: Jubao Gate (now Zhonghua Gate), Sanshan Gate, Shicheng Gate, Qingliang Gate, Dinghuai Gate, Yifeng Gate, Zhongfu Gate, Jinchuan Gate, Shence Gate, Taiping Gate, Chaoyang Gate, and Zhengyang Gate. Each gate originally had a watchtower with wooden doors and portcullises; militarily important gates had varying numbers of barbicans (wengcheng): Jubao (Zhonghua), Tongji, and Sanshan (Shuiximen) each had three, Shicheng had two, and Shence (Heping) had one. Unlike previous dynasties that placed barbicans outside, Zhu Yuanzhang typically placed them inside the city to confuse enemies. Surviving Ming gates include Jubao (Zhonghua), Shicheng (Hanximen), Shence (Heping), and Qingliang, plus the rebuilt Chaoyang Gate; only Shence Gate retains a Qing-dynasty rebuilt tower.

projects.name: 堂子街太平天国壁画
projects.name_en: Murals Created during Taiping Heavenly Kingdom Period on Tangzi Street
projects.level: 第三批全国重点文物保护单位（1988年）
projects.level_en: 3rd Batch National Key Cultural Heritage Site (1988)
projects.address: 白下区汉西门堂子街108号
projects.address_en: No. 108 Tangzi Street, Hanximen, Baixia District
highlights: 太平天国东王杨秀清属官衙署
18幅水墨壁画
《江防望楼图》
禁止绘人物的太平天国艺术
projects.content_zh: 堂子街曾为太平天国东王杨秀清属官的衙署。官署坐北朝南，原有六进，均为三开间，七架梁。第一进已毁，现存正中大殿、二厅、三厅、四厅和后檐房。东侧有花厅，各厅堂间有天井。原每进东、西、北壁均有水墨壁画，现存18幅，正厅8幅，二厅板壁8幅和三厅板壁2幅，内容有《鹤寿图》《江防望楼图》《山亭悬瀑图》《柳荫骏马图》和《双鹿灵芝图》等。其中最引人注目的是表现天京军事斗争的《江防望楼图》，图中描绘屹立江畔的五层望楼，是太平天国军防历史的写照。所有壁画皆不绘人物，遵循太平天国反对偶像崇拜、禁止绘制人物的禁令，壁画题材多为山水花鸟或龙凤祥瑞，笔法粗犷浓艳，颇具乡土气息，是太平天国艺术的珍稀遗存。
projects.content_en: Tangzi Street was once the office of a subordinate official of Yang Xiuqing, the East King of the Taiping Heavenly Kingdom. The government office faces south, originally with six courtyards, each three bays wide with seven-purlin beams. The first courtyard has been destroyed; surviving are the main hall, second hall, third hall, fourth hall, and rear eaves rooms. There is a flower hall on the east side, with courtyards between each hall. Originally, the east, west, and north walls of each courtyard had ink murals; 18 survive: 8 in the main hall, 8 on the plank walls of the second hall, and 2 on the plank walls of the third hall. Subjects include "Crane and Longevity," "River Defense Watchtower," "Mountain Pavilion with Waterfall," "Horse in Willow Shade," and "Two Deer and Lingzhi." The most striking is the "River Defense Watchtower" depicting the military struggle of Tianjing (Nanjing), showing a five-story watchtower standing by the river—a portrayal of Taiping military defense history. None of the murals depict human figures, following the Taiping Heavenly Kingdom's ban on idolatry and figure painting. Subjects are mostly landscapes, flowers, birds, or auspicious dragons and phoenixes, with bold and vivid brushwork and a strong folk character—rare surviving examples of Taiping Heavenly Kingdom art.

projects.name: 龙江宝船厂遗址
projects.level: 第六批全国重点文物保护单位（2006年）
projects.level_en: 6th Batch National Key Cultural Heritage Site (2006)
projects.address: 鼓楼区江东街道中保村（漓江路57）
projects.address_en: Zhongbao Village, Jiangdong Subdistrict, Gulou District (No. 57 Lijiang Road)
highlights: 明代官办船厂
郑和下西洋船队建造地
七作塘（船坞）
出土文物千余件
projects.content_zh: 宝船厂遗址在南京西北中保村，西邻夹江，此地至今仍俗称"龙江宝船厂"。这一带是古代漕河的入江口岸，从南唐开始就在这里造船，宋元时期，船厂规模极为宏大。据《龙江船厂志》记载，明洪武初年（1368年）在此设厂，是明代官办船厂之一。郑和下西洋的船队中，很大一部分船只只是在这里建造的。当地仍留有上四坞、下四坞、头滩、四滩和七滩等地名，均为当年船厂遗迹。到20世纪70年代末，七条被称为作塘的船坞仍保存较好，后来四条被填埋，仅留下四、五、六作塘。这三条作塘成东北—西南走向列，距长江350米。其中六作塘已完成考古挖掘，地下遗址结构多为木桩基址，出土文物千余件，有船用构件、造船工具和造船设施构件等。另外两条作塘为原生态保护。
projects.content_en: The Longjiang Shipyard site is located in Zhongbao Village, northwest Nanjing, adjacent to the Jiajiang River branch, still commonly known as "Longjiang Treasure Shipyard." This area was the river port of the ancient canal, with shipbuilding dating back to the Southern Tang Dynasty. By the Song and Yuan dynasties, the shipyard was extremely large. According to the "Longjiang Shipyard Annals," a shipyard was established here in the early Hongwu reign (1368), one of the Ming Dynasty's official shipyards. A large portion of the ships in Zheng He's voyages to the Western Oceans were built here. Local place names such as Upper Four Docks, Lower Four Docks, First Beach, Fourth Beach, and Seventh Beach all remain as relics of the former shipyard. By the late 1970s, seven ship docks called "zuotang" were still well preserved; four were later filled in, leaving only the 4th, 5th, and 6th zuotang. These three docks run northeast-southwest, 350 meters from the Yangtze River. The 6th zuotang has completed archaeological excavation, with underground remains mostly consisting of timber pile foundations, yielding over a thousand artifacts including ship components, shipbuilding tools, and facility components. The other two docks are under original-state protection.

projects.name: 朝天宫（南京市博物馆）
projects.level: 第七批全国重点文物保护单位（2013年）
projects.level_en: 7th Batch National Key Cultural Heritage Site (2013)
projects.address: 白下区王府大街朝天宫6号
projects.address_en: No. 6 Chaotian Palace, Wangfu Street, Baixia District
highlights: 金陵第一胜迹
清同治五年重建
万仞宫墙
棂星门
大成殿
江南最大文庙建筑群
projects.content_zh: 朝天宫位于南京市中心新街口南段，背依冶山，前临古运渎，明清两代被誉为"金陵第一胜迹"。现存建筑为清同治五年（1866年）重建，占地面积约四万平方米。相传2500年前吴王夫差曾在此设冶铸剑，后人遂称此山为"冶山"。三国东吴时期，孙权在这里设置冶官，冶山成为东吴制造铜铁器的重要场所。东晋初年，冶山为丞相王导之"西园"。王导常邀文人在此雅集。此后这里成为道教圣地，南朝刘宋泰始六年（470年）在冶山建立"总明观"，唐代改为"太极宫"，宋代称"天庆观"，元代称"玄妙观"，又改为"大元兴永寿宫"。明洪武十七年（1385年）朱元璋下诏改建，并赐名"朝天宫"，取"朝拜上天"之意。明代的朝天宫既是皇室贵族焚香祈福的道场，又是节庆前文武百官演习朝拜天子礼仪的场所。朝天宫是明中后期南京最大、最著名的道观，占地300多亩，有殿堂房庑数百间。明末朝天宫部分建筑毁于战火，清代康乾时期重修，规模宏大。太平天国时期将朝天宫改为制造和储存火药的"红粉衙"，清同治三年（1864年）毁于战火，同治五年（1866年）两江总督曾国藩将朝天宫改为孔庙并把江宁府学迁来，形成中为文庙、东为府学、西为卞公祠的格局。民国时期作为中央教育馆，后改为首都高等法院，现为南京市博物馆。朝天宫目前保存着清同治时期孔庙的格局，自南而北最前方是临街宫墙，嵌"万仞宫墙"砖雕；墙内有泮池，其北是棂星门，东西两面各有一座砖雕牌楼，三间三拱门，中门较为高大，上有曾国藩所书砖刻横额，东为"德配天地"，西为"道贯古今"。棂星门北为戟门，入门庭院两侧有配殿和廊房。第二进院落为朝天宫主体建筑大成殿，宽七间，重檐歇山顶。大殿前后两廊，均有巨大的木柱，前设露台，围以石栏，丹墀四角刻螭首。殿前两侧为配殿和廊房。第三进主体建筑为崇圣殿，又称先贤祠，宽五间，风格与大成殿类似。在冶山最高处建有敬一亭，亭东院落内有飞云阁和飞霞阁，阁前设御碑亭。朝天宫东侧为江宁府学，原有尊经阁等主要建筑，民国时期被毁，现存明伦堂等少数房屋，为江苏省昆剧院院部。此外还有民国时期所建的中央博物院库房建筑，现归南京博物院使用。
projects.content_en: Chaotian Palace is located at the southern end of Xinjiekou in central Nanjing, backed by Ye Mountain and facing the ancient Yundu Canal. During the Ming and Qing dynasties it was hailed as the "Foremost Scenic Spot of Jinling." The surviving buildings were rebuilt in the 5th year of Tongzhi (1866), covering approximately 40,000 square meters. According to legend, 2,500 years ago King Fuchai of Wu established a foundry here to cast swords, and later generations called the mountain "Ye Mountain" (Foundry Mountain). During the Three Kingdoms Eastern Wu period, Sun Quan established a foundry office here, making Ye Mountain an important site for manufacturing bronze and iron implements. In the early Eastern Jin, it became Chancellor Wang Dao's "West Garden," where he often invited scholars for gatherings. It later became a Taoist holy site: in the 6th year of Taishi of the Liu Song Dynasty (470), the "Zongming Temple" was established on Ye Mountain; in the Tang it was renamed "Taiji Palace"; in the Song, "Tianqing Temple"; in the Yuan, "Xuanmiao Temple," later changed to "Dayuan Xingyongshou Palace." In the 17th year of Hongwu (1385), Zhu Yuanzhang ordered reconstruction and bestowed the name "Chaotian Palace," meaning "worshipping heaven." In the Ming, Chaotian Palace served both as a site for imperial family and nobility to burn incense and pray, and as a place for civil and military officials to practice court etiquette before festivals. It was the largest and most famous Taoist temple in Nanjing in the mid-to-late Ming, covering over 300 mu with hundreds of halls and rooms. In the late Ming, part was destroyed in war; rebuilt on a grand scale during the Kangxi-Qianlong period of the Qing. During the Taiping Heavenly Kingdom, it was converted into the "Red Powder Office" for manufacturing and storing gunpowder, and was destroyed in war in 1864. In 1866, Liangjiang Governor-General Zeng Guofan converted it into a Confucian temple and moved the Jiangning Prefecture School here, forming a layout with the Confucian temple in the center, prefecture school to the east, and Bian Gong Shrine to the west. In the Republican era it served as the Central Education Museum, later the Capital High Court, and now houses the Nanjing Municipal Museum. Chaotian Palace preserves the Qing Tongzhi-period Confucian temple layout. From south to north: the street-facing palace wall with brick carving "Myriad-Ren Palace Wall"; inside is a pan pool (half-moon pond), north of which is the Lingxing Gate, with brick-carved paifang on east and west sides—three bays with three archways, the central gate taller, bearing brick inscriptions by Zeng Guofan: "Virtue Matches Heaven and Earth" on the east and "The Way贯 through Past and Present" on the west. North of Lingxing Gate is the Ji Gate (Halberd Gate), with side halls and corridors flanking the entrance courtyard. The second courtyard contains the main building Dacheng Hall, seven bays wide with double-eave hip-and-gable roof. The front and rear corridors have massive wooden columns; a terrace with stone railings sits in front, with chi dragon-head carvings at the four corners of the red stone courtyard. Side halls and corridors flank the hall. The third main building is Chongsheng Hall (also called Xianxian Shrine), five bays wide in a similar style. At the highest point of Ye Mountain stands Jingyi Pavilion; the courtyard to its east contains Feiyun Pavilion and Feixia Pavilion, with an imperial stele pavilion in front. East of Chaotian Palace was the Jiangning Prefecture School, originally with major buildings including the Zunjing Pavilion, destroyed in the Republican period; only a few buildings such as Minglun Hall survive, now the headquarters of the Jiangsu Kunqu Opera Theater. There is also a Republican-era Central Museum warehouse building, now used by the Nanjing Museum.

projects.name: 甘熙宅第（南京民俗博物馆）
projects.name_en: Residence of Gan Xi (Nanjing Folk Customs Museum)
projects.level: 第六批全国重点文物保护单位（2006年）
projects.level_en: 6th Batch National Key Cultural Heritage Site (2006)
projects.address: 秦淮区南捕厅15、17、19号，大板巷42号、46号，熙南里文化街区
projects.address_en: Nos. 15, 17, 19 Nanbuting, Nos. 42, 46 Daban Lane, Xinanli Cultural Block, Qinhuai District
highlights: 九十九间半
六组多进穿堂式
风火火山墙
津逮楼
友恭堂
projects.content_zh: 甘熙宅第始建于清嘉庆初年，是南京现存规模最大、保存较完整的大型民居，俗称"九十九间半"，占地近万平方米，由六组多进穿堂式建筑组成，今为南京民俗博物馆。甘熙（1787—1853）字石庵，安徽歙县人，是晚清学者与藏书家，著有《白下琐言》《桐荫随笔》《栖霞寺志》和《后湖水道考》等。他是甘氏家族中的名人，因此这处老宅以他来命名。明弘治年间甘氏迁来南京。后来甘国栋率子从事丝织业，清嘉庆四年（1799年）迁居南捕厅，在祖籍地"有相堂"下创立分支"友恭堂"。同年甘国栋去世，长子甘福主持家政，清嘉庆十七年（1812年）前后在南捕厅旧宅基础上扩建，奠定了这组宅第的规模。甘家通过经商致富，相信风水，因堪舆术认为商家不宜南向，南方为火克金，北方为水生金，因此整座宅邸北向，六组建筑中的五组坐南朝北，一组坐西朝东，在东南隅建有花园。各座房屋以高大的风火火山墙隔成院落，共有大小天井35处。由于南京夏季炎热，天井尺度较小，避免日晒。天井铺地较为讲究，用卵石和瓦片拼出各种吉祥图案。格栅门和梁枋的木雕以及门墙上的砖雕内容丰富，题材广泛，极具生活气息。花园内有池水假山，园亭廊榭。园内原有南京最大的私人藏书楼——"津逮楼"，并嵌有宋砖的书舍"三十六宋砖室"等，清咸丰三年（1853年）毁于兵火，近年重建津逮楼。
projects.content_en: The Gan Xi Residence, built in the early Jiaqing reign of the Qing Dynasty, is the largest and best-preserved large-scale traditional residence surviving in Nanjing, popularly called "ninety-nine and a half rooms." Covering nearly 10,000 square meters, it consists of six groups of multi-courtyard through-hall buildings, now housing the Nanjing Folk Customs Museum. Gan Xi (1787-1853), courtesy name Shi'an, was a native of She County, Anhui, a late-Qing scholar and book collector who authored "Baixia Suoyan," "Tongyin Suibi," "Qixia Temple Annals," and "Houhu Waterway Study." As the most famous member of the Gan family, the residence is named after him. The Gan family moved to Nanjing during the Hongzhi reign of the Ming. Later, Gan Guodong led his sons in the silk weaving business; in 1799 (4th year of Jiaqing), they moved to Nanbuting and established the branch "Yougong Tang" under the ancestral "Youxiang Tang." Gan Guodong died the same year, and his eldest son Gan Fu managed the household, expanding the old residence around 1812 (17th year of Jiaqing) to establish its current scale. The Gan family grew wealthy through commerce and believed in feng shui; according to geomancy, merchants should not face south because south corresponds to fire overcoming metal, while north corresponds to water generating metal. Therefore the entire complex faces north: five of the six building groups face south (entrance on north), one faces west (entrance on east), with a garden in the southeast corner. Each building group is separated by tall fire gable walls into courtyards, with 35 small and large courtyards (tianjing). Due to Nanjing's hot summers, the courtyards are small to avoid direct sunlight. The courtyard paving is elaborate, with pebbles and tiles forming auspicious patterns. The wood carvings on lattice doors and beams, and the brick carvings on gate walls, are rich in content and subject matter, full of life气息. The garden contains ponds, rockeries, pavilions, and corridors. It originally housed Nanjing's largest private book collection tower—the "Jindai Tower"—and the "Thirty-Six Song Brick Studio" with Song-dynasty bricks embedded in walls; these were destroyed in the 1853 (3rd year of Xianfeng) warfare, and the Jindai Tower has been recently rebuilt.

projects.name: 净觉寺
projects.level: 第五批江苏省文物保护单位（2002年）
projects.level_en: 5th Batch Jiangsu Provincial Cultural Heritage Site (2002)
projects.address_en: No. 28 Shengzhou Road, Qinhuai District
highlights: 明洪武二十五年建
砖雕牌坊
无像宝殿
米哈拉布书法
望月楼
projects.content_zh: 净觉寺始建于明洪武二十五年（1392年），后遭火焚，明宣德五年（1430年）郑和奏请重建，明弘治五年（1492年）大修，明嘉靖年间（1522—1566）敕建一座砖石牌坊，牌坊正中御书"净觉寺"三字。清乾隆四十七年（1782年）由穆斯林二百余人集资捐银建寺。太平天国时期毁坏严重，清光绪三年（1877年）桂月重建。1932年拓宽升州路，大门向内压缩，1957年修葺，"文革"时期被工厂占用，明代建造的砖石牌坊和蝴蝶厅被毁，1985年原样重建牌坊。今寺内有大殿、二殿、望月楼以及小花园、石碑亭、南北讲堂和南京回族史与伊斯兰教史料陈列室等。望月楼为两层砖木结构，楼梯利用封火墙与望月楼山墙之间的空隙建造，较为隐蔽，构思巧妙。望月楼后部有南北讲堂各三间。南讲堂正门悬"慕贤堂"匾额，现为南京回族伊斯兰教发展史陈列室，并介绍回族的代表性人物。北讲堂正门悬"额思齐轩"匾额，现为阅览室，有中、外三十余种版本《古兰经》，其中最贵重的是清代手抄本。两屋后部隔一堵横墙，中辟月门，其后为宽、深皆为三间的二殿。二殿曾作为礼拜殿，随着教徒增多，在殿后又建大殿，此殿改为厅堂。大殿建于清光绪年间，宽七间，深五间，正脊饰有"无像宝殿"四字，为国内仅有。殿内"米哈拉布"书法严谨，雕刻精细，生漆贴金，非常精美。
projects.content_en: Jingjue Temple was first built in the 25th year of Hongwu (1392) of the Ming Dynasty, later destroyed by fire. In the 5th year of Xuande (1430), Zheng He petitioned for reconstruction; major repairs were made in the 5th year of Hongzhi (1492); during the Jiajing reign (1522-1566), an imperial edict ordered the construction of a brick-stone paifang with the emperor's calligraphy "Jingjue Temple" in the center. In the 47th year of Qianlong (1782), over 200 Muslims raised funds to build the temple. It was severely damaged during the Taiping Heavenly Kingdom period and rebuilt in the 3rd year of Guangxu (1877). In 1932, when Shengzhou Road was widened, the gate was moved inward; repairs were made in 1957. During the Cultural Revolution it was occupied by a factory, and the Ming-dynasty brick-stone paifang and Butterfly Hall were destroyed; the paifang was rebuilt to original specifications in 1985. Today the temple contains the main prayer hall, second hall, Wangyue (Moon-Gazing) Tower, a small garden, stele pavilion, north and south lecture halls, and an exhibition room on Nanjing Hui history and Islamic history. The Wangyue Tower is a two-story brick-wood structure, with stairs built in the gap between the fire-sealing wall and the tower's gable wall—concealed and ingeniously designed. Behind the tower are three-bay north and south lecture halls. The south lecture hall, with a plaque reading "Muxian Hall" (Admiring Sages Hall) above the main entrance, now serves as an exhibition room on the development history of Nanjing Hui Islam, introducing representative Hui figures. The north lecture hall, with a plaque reading "Esiqi Xuan" above the main entrance, is now a reading room with over 30 editions of the Quran in Chinese and foreign languages, the most valuable being a Qing-dynasty hand-copied version. Behind the two halls, separated by a transverse wall with a moon gate, is the second hall, three bays wide and deep. It originally served as the prayer hall; as the number of worshippers grew, a main hall was built behind it and this hall was converted to a reception hall. The main hall, built during the Guangxu reign, is seven bays wide and five bays deep, with the characters "Wuxiang Baodian" (Hall Without Images) on the main ridge—unique in China. The mihrab inside features rigorous calligraphy, exquisite carving, and lacquer with gold leaf—extremely beautiful.

highlights: 金陵第一园
明代开国元勋徐达府邸
太平天国历史博物馆
静妙堂
南北假山
projects.content_zh: 瞻园原为明代开国元勋魏国公徐达的府邸，明嘉靖年间徐达的七世孙徐鹏在府西创建园林，明万历年间又有增建。入清后魏国公府改为江宁布政使司衙门，此园成为衙署园林。清初画家袁江绘有《瞻园图》，表现了此园盛期的景象。乾隆南巡时驻跸在园中，御题"瞻园"匾额，回京后在圆明园仿瞻园建造如园，取欧阳修诗"瞻望玉堂，如在天上"之意。太平天国时期瞻园被毁，到20世纪30年代童寯前去考察时，仅剩八亩多的南北狭长的遗址。由于瞻园久负盛名，素称"金陵第一园"，新中国成立后由建筑学家刘敦桢主持，全面恢复瞻园，成为复建古代园林的杰出范例。今瞻园包括东部府邸、西部园林和2009年扩建的北部园区，有东南、东北和西北三处入口。东部府邸南部为主入口，自南向北有大厅、仪门、大堂、二堂、三堂和后楼等，由大堂向北的四进建筑联络成一体，今为太平天国历史博物馆，是国内展览太平天国历史最全面的博物馆。大堂檐廊西侧的角门通向西部园林，分为东、西两园。东园建筑较多，具有现代气息；西园以山池取胜，充满古典韵味。东园分为南北三区。南区西南角辟有入口，入园是一串大小庭院，通过曲廊相连，空间多变；中区以草坪为主，为现代公园作法，北侧靠墙建造廊亭，夜间有演员在亭中弹奏古乐；园墙北侧是座幽静的庭园，一览阁坐北居中，前有台地，南临水池，周围贴墙架设游廊，高低起伏，串起厅堂轩榭。东园和西园之间是一道南北通贯的曲廊，使两园风景隔中有透，互相资借。西园是瞻园的精华所在，以静妙堂为中心，分为南北两区，各有水池和湖石假山，叠造精妙；园西是逶迤的土丘，林木葱郁，具有山林野趣。静妙堂北是一片开阔的平地，向北形成斜坡倾向水池，池面浩淼，池北耸立一座大型湖石假山。假山南部临水处基本保持明代原貌，背倚石壁，外侧石矶平贴水面随池岸蜿蜒，东西各有贴水梁桥与岸相连，山、水的结合浑融天然。山间有多条道路可登至山顶，山巅平台上耸立一扇巨大的石屏，远观增高了山势，近看则又可赏山石肌理。山腹穿凿洞穴，辗转相连，可惜今已封堵，无法入洞探幽。静妙堂南侧廊下设美人靠，向南隔着水池可欣赏另一座湖石假山，此为刘敦桢先生的力作。此山运用小块石料叠筑成浑然一体的大山，体势自然，纹理如真。下部以石矶、汀步与池水结合，中部构筑溶洞奇观，洞顶悬下巨大的钟乳石，洞口还营造出人工瀑布。这座假山石中带土，既节省了石料，又利于植物生长，山间覆满花木，增添了天然气息。瞻园作为南京最著名的园林，西园主景区仍保持着明代的疏朗风格，南、北两座假山一古一今，俱臻妙境；东园建筑空间曲折多变，东路博物馆历史厚重，共同构成一处绝佳的游赏景点。
projects.content_en: Zhanyuan Garden was originally the mansion of Xu Da, the Duke of Wei and a founding hero of the Ming Dynasty. During the Jiajing reign, Xu Peng, the seventh-generation descendant of Xu Da, created a garden west of the mansion, with further additions during the Wanli reign. After the Qing conquest, the Duke of Wei's mansion was converted into the Jiangning Provincial Administration Commissioner's Office, and the garden became an official garden. In the early Qing, painter Yuan Jiang painted "Zhanyuan Garden," depicting the garden at its peak. During the Qianlong Emperor's southern tour, he stayed in the garden and personally inscribed the plaque "Zhanyuan"; after returning to Beijing, he had Ruyuan Garden built in the Old Summer Palace in imitation of Zhanyuan, taking the meaning from Ouyang Xiu's poem "Gazing at the Jade Hall, as if in heaven." Zhanyuan was destroyed during the Taiping Heavenly Kingdom period; when architectural historian Tong Jun visited in the 1930s, only a narrow north-south site of over eight mu remained. Due to its long-standing reputation as the "Foremost Garden of Jinling," after the founding of New China, architect Liu Dunzhen presided over a comprehensive restoration, making it an outstanding example of reconstructing ancient gardens. Today Zhanyuan includes the eastern mansion, western garden, and the northern area expanded in 2009, with three entrances at southeast, northeast, and northwest. The southern part of the eastern mansion is the main entrance; from south to north are the main hall, ceremonial gate, grand hall, second hall, third hall, and rear building. The four courtyards north of the grand hall are connected as one, now housing the Taiping Heavenly Kingdom History Museum—the most comprehensive museum of Taiping history in China. A side gate west of the grand hall's eaves corridor leads to the western garden, divided into east and west gardens. The east garden has more buildings with a modern feel; the west garden excels in rockery and ponds, full of classical charm. The east garden is divided into three north-south zones. The southwest corner of the south zone has an entrance; entering leads to a series of courtyards connected by winding corridors with varied spaces. The central zone features a lawn in modern park style, with a corridor-pavilion built against the north wall where musicians play ancient music at night. North of the garden wall is a quiet courtyard with Yilan Pavilion facing south in the center, fronted by a terrace and a pond to the south, with wandering corridors along the walls at varying heights connecting halls and pavilions. Between the east and west gardens runs a north-south winding corridor, allowing views through while separating the two gardens. The west garden is the essence of Zhanyuan, centered on Jingmiao Hall (Hall of Quiet Wonder), divided into north and south zones, each with ponds and Taihu rockeries exquisitely stacked. The west side features rolling earth mounds with lush trees, creating a mountain-forest wildness. North of Jingmiao Hall is an open flat area sloping north toward a vast pond; a large Taihu rockery rises on the north bank. The waterside southern part of the rockery essentially preserves its Ming-dynasty original form, leaning against a stone wall with stone outcrops hugging the water surface along the winding bank; beam bridges at the east and west connect to the shore, integrating mountain and water naturally. Multiple paths lead to the summit, where a huge stone screen stands on the platform—enhancing the mountain's grandeur from afar and revealing stone texture up close. Caves are carved through the mountain's midsection, connected in winding passages, though unfortunately sealed today. A "beauty's rest" (curved railing bench) is set under the corridor south of Jingmiao Hall, facing south across the pond to another Taihu rockery—Liu Dunzhen's masterpiece. This rockery uses small stones stacked into a unified mountain with natural form and authentic texture. The lower part combines stone outcrops and stepping stones with the pond; the middle creates a spectacular cave with huge stalactites hanging from the ceiling and an artificial waterfall at the entrance. This rockery incorporates soil among stones, saving material while benefiting plant growth, with flowers and trees covering the mountain for a natural atmosphere. As Nanjing's most famous garden, the west garden's main scenic area retains the Ming-dynasty open style; the south and north rockeries, one ancient and one modern, both achieve excellence. The east garden's architectural spaces are winding and varied, while the east-side museum carries rich history—together forming an outstanding scenic destination.

projects.content_zh: 夫子庙始建于北宋景祐元年（1034年），原为建康府学，后来设在浮桥的孔庙迁至此处，宋绍兴九年（1199年）重建。元代称集庆路学，明初称国子学，后在鸡笼山建国子监，这里改称应天府学，清朝改为上元、江宁两县学。清咸丰时期夫子庙毁于兵燹，同治八年（1869年）重建。抗日战争时期日军焚毁了大成殿、魁星阁、得月台和思乐亭等，"文革"时期拆除尊经阁建四层文化馆。1984年按明清夫子庙格局重建。明清时期夫子庙将南面一段秦淮河扩宽为半圆形，作为泮池，河南岸有明万历三年（1575年）所立的八字形大照壁，明弘治年间（1488—1505）在泮池周围筑石堤，明正德九年（1514年）又在石堤上加石栏。清乾隆四十年（1775年）在泮池东侧建魁星阁，1981年重建。泮池北侧有"天下文枢"牌坊，始建于明万历十四年（1586年），原为木质，民国时拆除，后用水泥仿制。牌坊后为道路，东西有下马牌，牌西为聚星亭和思乐亭。路北有棂星门，1984年重建，门内为大成门，1985年重建，大成门内左右两侧有四块古碑，东侧是元至顺二年（1331年）的"封至圣夫人碑"和"封四氏碑"，西侧是南齐永明二年（484年）的"孔子问礼图碑"和元至顺元年（1330年）的"集庆孔子庙碑"。大成门内为大成殿，左右有两庑。殿后为学宫，有明德堂、尊经阁、崇圣祠、青云楼和敬一亭等，均为20世纪80年代复建。江南贡院坐北朝南，原大门外有牌坊，其后有龙门，入龙门为明远楼和致公堂，楼两侧是考生号舍。向北有飞虹桥跨在水池上，是内外帘官分界处。内帘官掌管阅卷，外帘官掌管考场事务，互相不可往来，有公事只能在内帘门口接洽。桥北原有衡鉴堂，为内帘主考阅卷和住宿之处。清末废除科举，贡院逐渐荒废，仅存明远楼、飞虹桥以及22块明清碑刻。近年复原了部分号舍和致公堂等，以供参观。明远楼是江南贡院的中心建筑，始建于明永乐年间，清道光年间重建。楼高三层，灰瓦歇山顶，底层砖砌，四面辟拱门，是监临、巡查等外帘官员发号施令和负责警戒的地方。楼内有清康熙年间李渔所题对联："矩令若霜严，看多士俯伏低徊，群器尽息；襟期同月朗，喜此地江山人物，一览无遗。"楼下两侧的号舍以《千字文》编号，但不用"天、地、玄、黄"，不用孟轲的"轲"，不用数目易混淆之字，也不用"荒""吊"等不吉利字眼。致公堂位于明远楼后部，是外帘官聚会办公的地方。江南贡院现为历史陈列馆，包括北区遗址陈列（明远楼、致公堂、号舍、碑刻）、南区沿河长廊科举民俗文化展示以及一处地下一层的科举博物馆。飞虹桥现在南京市中医院内，为单孔石桥，桥长12米，宽5.5米。
projects.content_en: The Confucius Temple was first built in the 1st year of Jingyou of the Northern Song (1034), originally the Jiankang Prefecture School. The Confucius Temple at Fuqiao was later moved here and rebuilt in the 9th year of Shaoxing (1199). In the Yuan Dynasty it was called Jiqing Road School; in the early Ming it was the National Academy (Guozixue), and after the National Academy was built on Jilong Mountain, it was renamed Yingtian Prefecture School. In the Qing it became the Shangyuan and Jiangning County Schools. It was destroyed in warfare during the Xianfeng period and rebuilt in the 8th year of Tongzhi (1869). During the War of Resistance, Japanese forces burned the Dacheng Hall, Kuixing Pavilion, Deyue Terrace, and Sile Pavilion; during the Cultural Revolution, the Zunjing Pavilion was demolished to build a four-story cultural center. It was reconstructed in 1984 following the Ming-Qing layout. During the Ming and Qing, a section of the Qinhuai River to the south was widened into a semicircle as the pan pool (half-moon pond). On the south bank stands the eight-character-shaped large screen wall erected in the 3rd year of Wanli (1575). Stone embankments were built around the pan pool during the Hongzhi period (1488-1505), and stone railings added in the 9th year of Zhengde (1514). The Kuixing Pavilion was built east of the pan pool in the 40th year of Qianlong (1775) and rebuilt in 1981. North of the pan pool stands the "Tianxia Wenshu" (Pivot of Literature Under Heaven) paifang, first built in the 14th year of Wanli (1586), originally wooden, demolished in the Republican period, later reproduced in cement. Behind the paifang is a road with dismount steles on east and west; west of the steles are the Juxing Pavilion and Sile Pavilion. North of the road is the Lingxing Gate, rebuilt in 1984; inside is the Dacheng Gate, rebuilt in 1985, with four ancient steles on left and right: on the east, the "Enfeoffment of the Most Holy Lady Stele" and "Enfeoffment of Four Clans Stele" from the 2nd year of Zhishun (1331); on the west, the "Confucius Asking About Rites Stele" from the 2nd year of Yongming of the Southern Qi (484) and the "Jiqing Confucius Temple Stele" from the 1st year of Zhishun (1330). Inside the Dacheng Gate is the Dacheng Hall, flanked by two wings. Behind the hall is the school compound with Mingde Hall, Zunjing Pavilion, Chongsheng Shrine, Qingyun Tower, and Jingyi Pavilion—all rebuilt in the 1980s. The Jiangnan Examination Hall faces south. Originally there was a paifang outside the main gate, followed by the Dragon Gate; entering the Dragon Gate leads to the Mingyuan Tower and Zhigong Hall, with candidate examination cells (haoshe) on both sides of the tower. To the north, the Feihong Bridge spans a pond, marking the boundary between inner and outer curtain officials. Inner curtain officials managed grading, outer curtain officials managed examination affairs—they could not interact, and official business could only be conducted at the inner curtain gate. North of the bridge was originally the Hengjian Hall, where inner curtain chief examiners graded papers and stayed. After the abolition of the imperial examination at the end of the Qing, the examination hall gradually fell into disrepair, with only the Mingyuan Tower, Feihong Bridge, and 22 Ming-Qing steles surviving. In recent years, some examination cells and the Zhigong Hall have been restored for visitors. The Mingyuan Tower, the central building of the Jiangnan Examination Hall, was first built during the Yongle reign and rebuilt during the Daoguang reign. Three stories high with gray tile hip-and-gable roof and brick ground floor with archways on all four sides, it was where outer curtain officials such as supervisors and inspectors issued orders and maintained security. Inside the tower is a couplet by Li Yu from the Kangxi reign: "Rules as strict as frost, watching scholars bow and hesitate, all noise ceases; aspirations as bright as the moon, delighting in the landscape and figures here, all visible at a glance." The examination cells on both sides below are numbered by the Thousand Character Classic, but excluding characters like "heaven, earth, dark, yellow," the character "Ke" from Mencius's name, easily confused numerals, and inauspicious characters like "barren" or "mourning." The Zhigong Hall, behind the Mingyuan Tower, was where outer curtain officials gathered and worked. The Jiangnan Examination Hall is now a historical exhibition museum, including the north area ruins exhibition (Mingyuan Tower, Zhigong Hall, examination cells, steles), the south area riverside corridor exhibition of imperial examination folk culture, and an underground imperial examination museum. The Feihong Bridge is now inside the Nanjing Hospital of Traditional Chinese Medicine—a single-arch stone bridge, 12m long and 5.5m wide.

projects.name: 金陵机器制造局旧址（南京晨光1865创业产业园）
projects.name_en: Site of Jinling Machine Manufacturing Bureau (Nanjing Chenguang 1865 Creative Industry Park)
projects.level: 第七批全国重点文物保护单位（2013年）
projects.level_en: 7th Batch National Key Cultural Heritage Site (2013)
projects.address_en: Chengguang Avenue, Qinhuai District
highlights: 李鸿章创办
清代军火生产基地
7处清代厂房
多跨连续厂房
锯齿形天窗
projects.content_zh: 金陵制造局遗址又称金陵兵工厂，在中华门外，雨花台东北，外秦淮河南。1865年李鸿章建立金陵机器制造局，10月30日奠基，1866年8月建成。据《续纂江宁府志》记载，当时有委员住房12间，机器汽炉房等80余间，廊50余间，均为西式建筑。制造局生产军火物资，供应淮军，工厂规模逐年扩大，成为清政府主要的军火生产基地。1929年6月，金陵机器局改称金陵兵工厂。抗日期间兵工厂内迁，1946年迁回，改称六〇兵工厂。1948年机器被运往台湾，1949年改为军械总厂，后来一直为军用。1957年改名"国营晨光机器厂"，对外公开使用，1980年3月改为南京晨光机器厂，1996年6月组建晨光集团。现原机器厂厂址改建为"南京晨光1865创意产业园"，对外出租办公空间，局部作为展馆使用。目前的遗址风貌区有制造厂厂房7处，包括机器正厂（同治五年，1866年）、右厂（同治十二年，1873年）、左厂、炎铜厂、卷铜厂（皆为光绪七年，1881年）、熔铜房（光绪十一年，1885年）和木厂大楼及机器大厂（光绪十二年，1886年）等。这些建筑均为青砖坡屋顶，内部采用三角桁架，门窗为拱券式。兵工厂尚存20余处厂房，主要为建于1935年的七座二层西式厂房楼群，向南呈"凹"形分布，以过街楼相连。另有两组建于1936年的多跨连续厂房，屋顶面北设锯齿形天窗，避阳光直射，获得柔和的室内光线，以利于生产。此外还有两排带气楼的厂房，原为机关枪装配线。
projects.content_en: The Jinling Manufacturing Bureau site, also known as the Jinling Arsenal, is located outside Zhonghua Gate, northeast of Yuhuatai, south of the outer Qinhuai River. In 1865, Li Hongzhang established the Jinling Machine Manufacturing Bureau, with the foundation laid on October 30 and construction completed in August 1866. According to the "Continued Compilation of Jiangning Prefecture Annals," there were 12 rooms for committee members, over 80 rooms for machinery and steam furnaces, and over 50 corridors—all in Western style. The bureau produced military supplies for the Huai Army, and the factory expanded year by year, becoming the Qing government's main arms production base. In June 1929, it was renamed the Jinling Arsenal. During the War of Resistance, the arsenal moved inland; it returned in 1946 and was renamed the 60th Arsenal. In 1948, machinery was shipped to Taiwan; in 1949 it became the Ordnance General Factory, and remained for military use thereafter. In 1957 it was renamed "State-owned Chenguang Machinery Factory," used publicly; in March 1980 it became the Nanjing Chenguang Machinery Factory; in June 1996 the Chenguang Group was established. The original factory site has now been converted into the "Nanjing Chenguang 1865 Creative Industry Park," renting office space with some areas used as exhibition halls. The current heritage area contains 7 manufacturing factory buildings, including the Machine Main Factory (5th year of Tongzhi, 1866), Right Factory (12th year of Tongzhi, 1873), Left Factory, Copper Rolling Factory, Copper Coiling Factory (all 7th year of Guangxu, 1881), Copper Melting House (11th year of Guangxu, 1885), Wood Factory Building, and Machine Large Factory (12th year of Guangxu, 1886). These buildings all have blue brick pitched roofs with internal triangular trusses and arched doors and windows. Over 20 arsenal factory buildings survive, mainly seven two-story Western-style factory buildings built in 1935, distributed in a "concave" shape facing south, connected by overhead walkways. There are also two groups of multi-bay continuous factories built in 1936, with sawtooth skylights on the north-facing roof to avoid direct sunlight and obtain soft indoor light favorable for production. Additionally, there are two rows of factories with monitor roofs, originally the machine gun assembly line.
