projects.content_zh: 中山陵是中国近代民主革命先行者孙中山的陵墓。从南京城到中山陵有中山大道直通，沿紫金山山麓有环陵路，东至灵谷寺，西至明孝陵，主体纪念建筑占地两千余亩，总面积45872亩，四周皆为森林，环境优美。1925年3月12日孙中山在北京逝世，生前他希望能归葬在南京的紫金山，当时国民党成立了丧事筹备委员会，选定了墓址，并悬奖5000元，向全球征集陵墓设计图案。最后收到中外设计师应征图案四十余份，从中推选出当时只有31岁的中国建筑师吕彦直的作品为头奖，作为中山陵的设计方案。吕彦直的设计符合中国古代建筑传统，采用现代建筑材料和结构，创造出了具有中国精神的纪念性建筑风格。整座陵园平面布置呈警钟型，寓意"唤起民众"，建筑庄严简朴又别具新格，体现了孙中山的精神和气概。孙中山奉安大典在1929年6月1日举行，而年轻的建筑师吕彦直当年3月18日凌晨则因主持中山陵工程建设积劳成疾，不幸逝世。中山陵的建筑布局汲取了中国传统陵墓设计的特点，未使用营造神秘、压抑气氛的神道石刻，而保留了"牌坊""陵门""碑亭""祭堂"和"墓室"的序列，显得肃穆庄严而又开阔明朗。博爱坊是墓道南段入口处的牌坊，为拜谒中山陵的起点。牌坊高11米，四柱三间，采用福建花岗岩建造，柱间有蓝色琉璃瓦屋檐，柱头有莲瓣云朵等传统图案，坊间有经过抽象简化的雀替、斗拱等装饰图案。横楣嵌石额，上题孙中山手书"博爱"二字，以此得名。博爱坊至陵门间有长440米，宽36米的甬道，分三段路面，两侧各设花池，植松柏。陵门在花岗石台阶的尽端，用花岗岩砌成，面阔五间，中部设三拱门，蓝色琉璃瓦歇山顶，檐下有石刻的额枋与斗栱。南面三门为梅花空格仿紫铜门窗，中部门额题孙中山手书"天下为公"四字。碑亭在陵门后第二层平台上，平面方形，边长12米，高17米，蓝琉璃瓦重檐歇山顶，全用花岗岩砌筑。亭内有高8.1米、宽4米的石碑，石碑底座和顶端都有装饰，上题三行国民党元老谭延闿手书的碑文："中国国民党葬/总理孙先生于此/中华民国十八年六月一日"。"文革"时期石碑顶端和底座的国民党党徽被铲除，1981年按原样修复。中山陵依山而建，占地8万多平方米。从山下博爱坊到山上的祭堂，有73米的高差。吕彦直利用这个高差，在牌坊和祭堂之间设置了392级石阶，象征当时中华民国3亿9千2百万的人口。这些台阶被分成10段，设计精妙，由下向上仰视，只见台阶不见平台，而从上向下俯视则只见平台不见台阶。当初征集设计图时要求祭堂前有可供5万人站立的大平台，吕彦直巧妙地将平台分布在台阶之间。第六层平台上有一座巨大的仿古铜鼎，上刻"奉安大典"四字，是上海特别市政府为纪念孙中山葬礼捐献的，铜鼎西侧留有日军弹孔。第七层平台上有一对石狮。第十层平台后为祭堂，祭堂左右有一对石华表。祭堂采用蓝琉璃重檐歇山顶，面阔进深皆为五间，正面开三拱门，门上有梅花空格紫铜双扉，门额上自东向西分别刻有"民族""民权"和"民生"字样，为"国民党四大元老"之一的张静江书写，重檐之间悬孙中山手书"天地正气"四字竖匾。祭堂四隅各建有堡垒式方形房屋，内藏纪念品，并供谒陵人休息。祭堂内地面铺白色大理石，室内设12根直径80厘米的青岛黑色大理石柱。祭堂顶部采用覆斗式天花，以瓷砖砌出色彩浓丽的图案，中部为国民党青天白日旗图案，四周墙边为斗栱额枋。四壁有黑色大理石护壁，壁上刻孙中山手书的《建国大纲》，左右上方各开一扇紫铜花格窗。设计方案要求在祭堂中央摆放一尊孙中山的坐像供人们祭祀拜谒。波兰著名雕塑家保罗·兰窦斯基在雕塑设计竞赛中夺标，他为孙中山雕刻了一座大理石坐像，安放在祭堂中央。底座四周辅以表现孙中山革命事迹的浮雕。在祭堂后边设计两重墓门，前部为两扇紫铜门，门框以黑色大理石砌成，上题孙中山手书"浩气长存"横额。后部为独扇紫铜门，上方刻着"孙中山先生之墓"几个大字。墓室在祭堂门后，采用中国南方传统的圆形平面，状若覆釜，直径18米，高11米。中央是长方形墓穴，上置孙中山先生汉白玉卧像，人们可绕着汉白玉栏杆瞻观灵柩上的卧像。这座卧像由捷克雕刻家高祺按遗体原形塑造，在陵座下方安葬着孙中山的遗体。墓穴外侧用香港花岗石铺砌，中层以钢筋混凝土密封，非常坚固；内侧用米色人造大理石贴面，内部穹顶正中用蓝色瓷砖砌出青天白日党徽的图案。除了中山陵主体建筑，陵区内还有音乐台（门票10元）、行健亭、革命历史图书馆、光华亭、仰止亭、流徽榭和藏经楼等附属纪念性建筑。
projects.content_en: Sun Yat-sen's Mausoleum is the tomb of Sun Yat-sen, the pioneer of China's modern democratic revolution. Zhongshan Avenue leads directly from Nanjing city to the mausoleum; a ring road runs along the foot of Purple Mountain, east to Linggu Temple and west to the Ming Xiaoling Mausoleum. The main memorial buildings cover over 2,000 mu, with a total area of 45,872 mu, surrounded by forest in a beautiful environment. On March 12, 1925, Sun Yat-sen died in Beijing. During his lifetime he wished to be buried on Purple Mountain in Nanjing. The KMT established a funeral preparatory committee, selected the site, and offered a 5,000-yuan prize for global design submissions. Over 40 designs were received from Chinese and foreign architects, and the first prize was awarded to 31-year-old Chinese architect Lü Yanzhi, whose design became the mausoleum's plan. Lü's design followed Chinese architectural traditions while using modern materials and structures, creating a commemorative architectural style with Chinese spirit. The entire mausoleum complex has a bell-shaped plan, symbolizing "arousing the people," with solemn yet innovative architecture embodying Sun Yat-sen's spirit and stature. The state funeral was held on June 1, 1929, but the young architect Lü Yanzhi died in the early hours of March 18 that year from overwork supervising the construction. The mausoleum's layout draws on traditional Chinese tomb design, omitting the mysterious and oppressive spirit-way stone carvings while retaining the sequence of "paifang," "tomb gate," "stele pavilion," "sacrificial hall," and "burial chamber," appearing solemn yet open and bright. The Bo'ai (Universal Love) Paifang at the south entrance of the tomb road is the starting point for visiting the mausoleum. The 11m-high, four-column, three-bay paifang is built of Fujian granite, with blue glazed tile eaves between columns, traditional lotus-petal and cloud patterns on column capitals, and abstracted simplified queti and dougong decorative patterns between bays. The horizontal lintel bears a stone plaque with Sun Yat-sen's calligraphy "Bo'ai" (Universal Love), giving it its name. Between the paifang and the tomb gate is a 440m-long, 36m-wide approach road in three sections, with flower beds on both sides planted with pines and cypresses. The tomb gate at the end of the granite steps is built of granite, five bays wide with three central archways, blue glazed tile hip-and-gable roof, and carved stone architraves and dougong under the eaves. The three south doors have plum-pattern lattice imitating purple bronze doors and windows; the central lintel bears Sun Yat-sen's calligraphy "Tianxia Wei Gong" (The World Belongs to All). The stele pavilion on the second platform behind the tomb gate has a square plan, 12m on each side and 17m high, with blue glazed double-eave hip-and-gable roof, entirely built of granite. Inside is an 8.1m-high, 4m-wide stele with decorated base and top, bearing three lines of inscription by KMT elder Tan Yankai: "The Chinese Nationalist Party buries / Premier Sun here / June 1, 18th year of the Republic of China." During the Cultural Revolution, the KMT party emblems on the stele's top and base were chiseled away, restored to original in 1981. Built against the mountain, the mausoleum covers over 80,000 square meters. From the Bo'ai Paifang at the foot to the sacrificial hall on the mountain, there is a 73m elevation difference. Lü Yanzhi used this difference to set 392 stone steps between the paifang and hall, symbolizing the 392 million population of the Republic of China at the time. The steps are divided into 10 sections, ingeniously designed so that looking up from below one sees only steps and no platforms, while looking down from above one sees only platforms and no steps. The original design competition required a large platform in front of the sacrificial hall capable of holding 50,000 people; Lü cleverly distributed platforms between the steps. On the sixth platform stands a huge antique bronze ding cauldron inscribed "Feng'an Dadian" (State Funeral Ceremony), donated by the Shanghai Special Municipal Government to commemorate Sun Yat-sen's funeral, with Japanese bullet holes on its west side. On the seventh platform are a pair of stone lions. Behind the tenth platform is the sacrificial hall, flanked by a pair of stone huabiao ornamental pillars. The sacrificial hall has a blue glazed double-eave hip-and-gable roof, five bays wide and deep, with three archways on the front bearing plum-pattern lattice purple bronze double doors; the lintels from east to west are inscribed "Minzu" (Nationalism), "Minquan" (Democracy), and "Minsheng" (People's Livelihood), written by Zhang Jingjiang, one of the "Four Elders of the KMT." Between the double eaves hangs a vertical plaque with Sun Yat-sen's calligraphy "Tiandi Zhengqi" (Righteous Spirit of Heaven and Earth). At each corner of the hall is a fortress-like square building housing souvenirs and serving as rest areas for visitors. The hall floor is paved with white marble, with 12 Qingdao black marble columns 80cm in diameter. The ceiling is a coffered inverted pyramid with colorful tile patterns, the center featuring the KMT Blue Sky and White Sun flag, with dougong and architraves along the walls. The walls have black marble wainscoting inscribed with Sun Yat-sen's "Outline of National Reconstruction," with purple bronze lattice windows on the upper left and right. The design required a seated statue of Sun Yat-sen in the center of the hall for worship. Renowned Polish sculptor Paul Landowski won the sculpture competition and carved a marble seated statue placed in the center, with reliefs around the base depicting Sun Yat-sen's revolutionary deeds. Behind the hall are two tomb gates: the front has two purple bronze doors with black marble frames, bearing Sun Yat-sen's calligraphy "Haoqi Changcun" (Noble Spirit Endures); the rear is a single purple bronze door inscribed "Tomb of Mr. Sun Yat-sen." The burial chamber behind the sacrificial hall uses a traditional southern Chinese circular plan, shaped like an inverted cauldron, 18m in diameter and 11m high. In the center is a rectangular grave pit, topped by a white marble reclining statue of Sun Yat-sen; visitors can walk around the white marble railing to view the reclining statue above the coffin. This reclining statue was sculpted by Czech sculptor G. Koci based on the body's original form; Sun Yat-sen's remains are buried below the statue base. The outside of the grave pit is paved with Hong Kong granite, the middle layer sealed with reinforced concrete—extremely solid; the inside is faced with beige artificial marble, and the center of the interior dome features the Blue Sky and White Sun party emblem in blue tiles. Besides the main mausoleum buildings, the precinct includes附属 memorial structures such as the Music Terrace (10 yuan admission), Xingjian Pavilion, Revolutionary History Library, Guanghua Pavilion, Yangzhi Pavilion, Liuhui Pavilion, and Cangjing Building (Scripture Library).

projects.name: 明孝陵
projects.level: 第一批全国重点文物保护单位（1961年）
projects.level_en: 1st Batch National Key Cultural Heritage Site (1961)
projects.address: 玄武区紫金山南麓独龙阜珠峰下
projects.address_en: At the foot of Dulongfu Peak, southern foot of Purple Mountain, Xuanwu District
highlights: 朱元璋与马皇后合葬墓
前方后圆陵宫制度
2.62公里神道
石像路神道
神功圣德碑
方城明楼
projects.content_zh: 明孝陵是明太祖朱元璋与马皇后的合葬陵墓，在南京东郊紫金山南麓独龙阜珠峰下。朱元璋称帝后就开始择址，明洪武十四年（1381年）开工，翌年葬入皇后马氏，因马皇后谥号"孝慈"，故称孝陵。洪武十六年（1383年）建成孝陵大殿，洪武二十五年（1392年）葬皇太子朱标于孝陵东，称"东陵"。洪武三十一年（1398年），71岁的朱元璋归葬孝陵。其后陆续有所营建，直到明永乐十一年（1413年）建成"大明孝陵神功圣德碑"才算全部完工，共耗时三十余年。明孝陵开创了新的帝陵制度，影响了后世的明十三陵和清代皇陵。陵宫布局采用前方后圆、"前朝后寝"的制度，依顺地形而设，前方有蜿蜒曲折的神道，全长2.62公里。陵园四周原有22.5公里长的红墙，陵内植松十万株，养鹿千头，到清代已不存。孝陵神道起于下马坊，这是一座单间两柱的石牌坊，高7.85米，额上刻有"诸司官员下马"六个大字，坊东36.6米处有明嘉靖十年（1531年）立的神烈山碑，再东17米有明崇祯十四年（1641年）立的禁约碑，碑面镌刻禁止损坏陵墓及谒陵条款。禁约碑东是孝陵卫，曾驻兵五千余人保卫孝陵。下马坊西北775米是孝陵陵园大门。从陵园路进入明孝陵博物馆（免费参观），可由后部天桥直达大金门。大金门是明孝陵外郭正门，为进入陵区的第一道大门，门南向，有三个券门，门下为石造须弥座，束腰雕花，上部砖砌。大金门原为黄琉璃单檐歇山顶，如今屋顶已毁，门西仍可看出与外郭红墙相连接的痕迹。大金门正北方70米处，是明永乐十一年（1413年）建的神功圣德碑楼，采用正方形平面，因楼顶被毁，俗称"四方城"。楼内是朱棣为朱元璋立的"大明孝陵神功圣德碑"，上刻朱棣撰写的2746字碑文，碑高6.7米，龟趺座高2.08米，是南京附近明代碑刻中最大的一块。但比起当初计划使用的总高78米的阳山碑材（见景点30），仅为其十分之一。阳山碑材因无法运输树立放弃使用，最终采用了现存规格的碑石。碑楼西北过御河桥有神道石刻，分为两段。第一段为石像路神道，长615米，依次排列狮子、獬豸、骆驼、象、麒麟和马六种圆雕石兽，每种2对，共12对24件，相对跪立，夹道迎侍。石兽尽处，神道折向正北，为翁仲路神道，长250米，前有一对白石望柱，其后为两对武将和两对文臣，皆为一人有须，一人无须。由翁仲向北18米处有棂星门，六柱排成三组，原本只留有柱础，近年修复。再向东北275米为御河桥，原为五孔，现存三孔，桥基和石堤为原物，桥面栏杆为后配。过桥往北一直到方城宝顶为陵墓主体建筑，坐北朝南，轴线不再变更。主轴线上排列文武方门、孝陵门、孝陵殿、内红门、方城明楼和宝顶等，筑有围墙。御河桥北200米是文武方门，原有三大二小五间门洞，现仅开一洞，为清同治时期改建，上嵌青石门额，阴刻"明孝陵"三字。门外有用日德意英法俄六国文字刊刻的告示，禁止破坏孝陵。进门为开阔地，有两口井。东井已废，西井完好，井亭仅存柱础。文武方门北部原有孝陵门，现仅存台基，上有清康熙年间修建的碑殿，内部陈列五块石碑，正中是清康熙三十八年（1699年）康熙皇帝谒陵时所书"治隆唐宋"四字，其余为乾隆题诗和康熙谒陵纪事。碑殿后部为孝陵殿。原殿规模宏大，宽九间，深五间，清咸丰三年（1853年）毁于战火。现仅存三层须弥座台基，长57.3米，宽26.6米，通高3.03米，雕刻精致，四角有石螭首。台基上排列56个石柱础。清同治四年（1865年）和同治十二年（1873年）在台基上修建了宽三间的小享殿。殿后为内红门，门后133.3米为大石桥，南北长57.5米，单孔，桥北7.8米为方城。方城是陵墓最后一座地面建筑，外部用大石条砌成，东西长75.26米，前高16.25米，中间开拱门，有隧道拾阶而上。出隧道为方城与宝顶之间的夹道，其北为宝顶南墙，用13层条石垒筑，其上横刻"此山明太祖之墓"，宝顶下部即为地宫所在。沿夹道西上坡可登方城顶端明楼，明楼原屋顶已毁，仅余砖墙，近年修复。
projects.content_en: The Ming Xiaoling Mausoleum is the joint tomb of the Hongwu Emperor Zhu Yuanzhang and Empress Ma, located at the foot of Dulongfu Peak on the southern slope of Purple Mountain in the eastern suburbs of Nanjing. After ascending the throne, Zhu Yuanzhang began selecting a site; construction started in the 14th year of Hongwu (1381), and Empress Ma was buried the following year. Because her posthumous title was "Xiaoci" (Filial and Kind), the mausoleum was named Xiaoling. The Xiaoling Hall was completed in the 16th year of Hongwu (1383); in the 25th year (1392), Crown Prince Zhu Biao was buried east of Xiaoling, called the "East Mausoleum." In the 31st year of Hongwu (1398), the 71-year-old Zhu Yuanzhang was buried in Xiaoling. Construction continued afterward until the 11th year of Yongle (1413), when the "Great Ming Xiaoling Divine Merit and Sacred Virtue Stele" was completed—taking over thirty years in total. Ming Xiaoling pioneered a new imperial mausoleum system that influenced the later Ming Thirteen Tombs and Qing imperial tombs. The mausoleum palace layout follows the "front square, rear round" and "front court, rear chamber" system, following the terrain, with a winding spirit way 2.62 km long in front. The mausoleum originally had a 22.5 km red wall, with 100,000 pine trees and 1,000 deer inside—no longer surviving by the Qing Dynasty. The spirit way begins at the Xiamafang (Dismounting Archway), a single-bay, two-column stone paifang 7.85m high, inscribed with "All officials dismount here." 36.6m east of the paifang is the Shenlieshan Stele erected in the 10th year of Jiajing (1531); 17m further east is the Jinyue Stele erected in the 14th year of Chongzhen (1641), inscribed with prohibitions against damaging the mausoleum and terms for visiting. East of the Jinyue Stele was the Xiaoling Guard, once garrisoned with over 5,000 soldiers. 775m northwest of the Xiamafang is the main gate of the mausoleum precinct. Entering from the mausoleum road to the Ming Xiaoling Museum (free admission), one can reach the Dajin Gate via an overhead bridge at the rear. The Dajin Gate is the outer gate of the outer wall, the first gate into the mausoleum area, facing south with three archways. The base is a stone Sumeru pedestal with carved waist, and the upper part is brick. The Dajin Gate originally had a yellow glazed single-eave hip-and-gable roof; the roof is now destroyed, but traces of connection to the outer red wall remain on the west side. 70m due north of the Dajin Gate is the Shengong Shengde Stele Tower built in the 11th year of Yongle (1413), with a square plan. Because its roof was destroyed, it is commonly called "Sifangcheng" (Square City). Inside is the "Great Ming Xiaoling Divine Merit and Sacred Virtue Stele" erected by Zhu Di for Zhu Yuanzhang, bearing a 2,746-character inscription written by Zhu Di. The stele is 6.7m high, with a 2.08m-high tortoise base—the largest Ming stele near Nanjing. However, compared to the originally planned 78m-high Yangshan quarry stone (see attraction 30), it is only one-tenth the size. The Yangshan stone was abandoned because it could not be transported and erected, and the existing-sized stele was ultimately used. Northwest of the stele tower, across the imperial river bridge, are the spirit way stone carvings in two sections. The first section is the Stone Animal Spirit Way, 615m long, with six types of round-carved stone animals arranged in sequence: lions, xiezhi (mythical beasts), camels, elephants, qilin, and horses—two pairs of each, 12 pairs totaling 24 pieces, facing each other in kneeling and standing positions, lining the path. At the end of the stone animals, the spirit way turns due north as the Wengzhong (Stone Figure) Spirit Way, 250m long, preceded by a pair of white stone ornamental pillars, followed by two pairs of military officers and two pairs of civil officials—each pair with one bearded and one clean-shaven figure. 18m north of the Wengzhong figures is the Lingxing Gate, with six columns in three groups; originally only column bases remained, restored in recent years. Further northeast 275m is the Imperial River Bridge, originally five arches but now three; the bridge foundation and stone embankment are original, with later railings. Crossing the bridge north to the square city and treasure top is the main mausoleum building complex, facing south with an unchanged axis. Along the main axis are the Wenwu Fang Gate, Xiaoling Gate, Xiaoling Hall, Inner Red Gate, Square City and Ming Tower, and Treasure Top, enclosed by walls. 200m north of the Imperial River Bridge is the Wenwu Fang Gate, originally with five doorways (three large, two small); now only one opening remains, rebuilt during the Tongzhi period, with a blue stone lintel carved "Ming Xiaoling." Outside the gate is a notice inscribed in Japanese, German, Italian, British, French, and Russian prohibiting damage to Xiaoling. Inside is an open area with two wells; the east well is ruined, the west well intact with only column bases of its well pavilion remaining. North of the Wenwu Fang Gate was originally the Xiaoling Gate, now only the platform base remains, on which stands a stele hall built during the Kangxi period, displaying five steles: the center one bears "Zhilong Tangsong" (Governing surpassing Tang and Song) written by the Kangxi Emperor during his visit in the 38th year of Kangxi (1699); the others are Qianlong's poems and records of Kangxi's visits. Behind the stele hall is the Xiaoling Hall. The original hall was grand—nine bays wide and five bays deep—but was destroyed in warfare in the 3rd year of Xianfeng (1853). Now only a three-tier Sumeru pedestal remains, 57.3m long, 26.6m wide, 3.03m high overall, with exquisite carvings and stone chi dragon-head ornaments at the four corners. 56 stone column bases are arranged on the pedestal. In the 4th year (1865) and 12th year (1873) of Tongzhi, a small three-bay worship hall was built on the pedestal. Behind the hall is the Inner Red Gate; 133.3m behind it is the Great Stone Bridge, 57.5m long north-south with a single arch; 7.8m north of the bridge is the Square City. The Square City is the last above-ground building of the mausoleum, built with large stone blocks, 75.26m east-west, 16.25m high at the front, with a central archway and a tunnel with steps leading up. Exiting the tunnel leads to a passage between the Square City and the Treasure Top; to the north is the south wall of the Treasure Top, built with 13 layers of dressed stone, inscribed horizontally "This mountain is the tomb of the Ming Taizu Emperor," with the underground palace below the Treasure Top. Climbing west along the passage leads to the top of the Square City and the Ming Tower; the original roof of the Ming Tower was destroyed, leaving only brick walls, restored in recent years.

projects.name: 美龄宫（国民政府主席官邸旧址）
projects.name_en: Meiling Palace (Former Official Residence of President of National Government)
projects.level: 第五批全国重点文物保护单位（2001年）
projects.level_en: 5th Batch National Key Cultural Heritage Site (2001)
projects.address_en: No. 9 Zhongshanling, Xuanwu District
highlights: 仿明清宫殿式风格
凤凰图案装饰
34只凤凰栏杆
凸字形露台
基督凯歌堂
projects.content_zh: 美龄宫在明孝陵四方城附近小红山的山坡上，是蒋介石和宋美龄在南京东郊的别墅，又称"小红山官邸"，俗称"美龄宫"。建筑为仿明清宫殿式风格，极富民族气息，内部装修为西洋风格，四周环境清幽，绿树环抱，郁郁葱葱。1931年秋，蒋介石向中山陵园提出借小红山地块建别墅，经陵园同意，交由南京市政府负责，市工务局长赵志游亲自设计，市工务技正陈品善主持督办，上海新金记康号营造厂投标承建，这座别墅占地百余亩，1931年春动工兴建，1934年竣工，总耗资36万银元。官邸主楼面积2000余平方米，另有门楼、警卫用房、花园和环形车道等。主楼地下一层，地上三层，绿琉璃歇山屋顶，瓦当和搏风板露台柱头均用凤凰图案装饰，两端纵向出歇山顶，前出门廊，后为大平台，左右有露台。地下室东部为仆役警卫用房，西部为厨房。地面一层有门厅、应接室、衣帽间、盥洗间、侍卫室、秘书卧室、秘书办公室、仆役卧室、洗衣间、汽炉间、煤间和厨房等。二层主要为会客室和休息室，有会客厅、机要秘书室、书房、大饭厅和配膳间等。现东侧改为展览空间，有一间影音室。通过大饭厅可至"凸"字形露台，露台面积宽阔，可供露天茶饮活动，外侧围以凤凰柱头装饰的汉白玉栏杆，据说34只凤凰象征1930年34岁的女主人宋美龄。三层有四间卧室，中间南侧是高出几级台阶的小餐厅。中部厅堂设置成祈祷室，供礼拜使用。1945年蒋介石"还都"南京后，将祈祷室改为基督凯歌堂，当时中外政要周日经常在此作礼拜。
projects.content_en: Meiling Palace is located on the slope of Xiaohongshan near the Sifangcheng of the Ming Xiaoling Mausoleum. It was the villa of Chiang Kai-shek and Soong May-ling in the eastern suburbs of Nanjing, also known as the "Xiaohongshan Official Residence," commonly called "Meiling Palace." The building is in the style imitating Ming-Qing palaces, rich in national character, with Western-style interior decoration, surrounded by a quiet environment and lush green trees. In autumn 1931, Chiang Kai-shek requested to borrow the Xiaohongshan plot from the Zhongshan Cemetery Administration for building a villa. With the cemetery's approval, it was handed to the Nanjing Municipal Government; Zhao Zhiyou, director of the Municipal Public Works Bureau, personally designed it; Chen Pinshan, municipal public works technician, supervised construction; the Shanghai Xinjinkanghao Construction Company won the bid. The villa covers over 100 mu, with construction starting in spring 1931 and completed in 1934, costing 360,000 silver dollars. The main building has over 2,000 square meters, plus a gatehouse, guard quarters, garden, and circular driveway. The main building has one basement and three above-ground stories, with a green glazed hip-and-gable roof. The tile ends, wind boards, and terrace column capitals are all decorated with phoenix patterns; both ends have longitudinal hip-and-gable roofs, with a front entrance porch, a large rear platform, and terraces on left and right. The basement's east part is for servant and guard quarters, the west part is the kitchen. The ground floor has an entrance hall, reception room, cloakroom, washroom, guard room, secretary's bedroom, secretary's office, servant's bedroom, laundry room, boiler room, coal room, and kitchen. The second floor mainly contains reception and resting rooms, including a reception hall, confidential secretary's room, study, large dining room, and pantry. The east side is now converted into exhibition space with an audio-visual room. Through the large dining room one can reach the "convex"-shaped terrace, which is spacious for outdoor tea activities, enclosed by white marble railings with phoenix-decorated capitals—reportedly 34 phoenixes symbolizing Soong May-ling, who was 34 years old in 1930. The third floor has four bedrooms, with a small dining room several steps higher on the south center. The central hall was set up as a prayer room for worship. After Chiang Kai-shek "returned the capital" to Nanjing in 1945, the prayer room was converted into the Christ Kaige Church, where Chinese and foreign dignitaries often worshipped on Sundays.

projects.name: 灵谷寺无梁殿
projects.level: 第三批江苏省文物保护单位（1982年）
projects.level_en: 3rd Batch Jiangsu Provincial Cultural Heritage Site (1982)
projects.address: 紫金山南麓灵谷公园灵谷寺2号
projects.address_en: No. 2 Linggu Temple, Linggu Park, southern foot of Purple Mountain
highlights: 明洪武十四年建
砖石拱券结构
江苏最早最大无梁殿
国民革命军阵亡将士公墓
正气堂
projects.content_zh: 灵谷寺原在钟山西南独龙阜，始建于南朝，原名开善寺，明太祖修建孝陵时将其迁至今址，改名"灵谷寺"。明代时寺院规模宏大，清咸丰、同治年间毁于战火，仅存明代无梁殿一座和清同治六年（1867年）所建龙神殿。1928年国民政府修建北伐战士陵园，将灵谷寺佛像迁至龙神殿，即今灵谷寺。无梁殿建于明洪武十四年（1381年），殿内曾供奉无量寿佛，因称无量殿；大殿采用砖石拱券结构，不施梁木，因此又称无梁殿。在江苏的五座无梁殿中，这是时间最早、规模最大的一座。殿前有宽大月台，殿身朝东南，宽五间，深三间，灰琉璃瓦重檐歇山顶，正脊上装饰三座白色琉璃喇嘛塔，中塔直通殿内屋顶，檐下施仿木斗栱，为民国时改用混凝土制成。南向开三拱门，两拱窗，北向为三拱门，两侧各开四扇拱窗。大殿长53.8米，宽37.85米，高22米，殿身横向并排三座砖筒拱券，将殿内分为前、中、后三个狭长的空间，中槽最大，宽11.25米，高14米，两侧各宽5米，高7.4米，为了平衡拱券侧推力，前后墙厚近4米。殿内前槽和中槽之间横向构筑五间拱券，中槽与后槽之间仅在梢间构筑拱券，中部内墙直接砌为屏墙。明正统年间曾在此藏经，中祀三尊大佛，四周塑24天象。清代多次重修，清咸丰年间清军曾在此设江南大营与太平军对峙。1931年国民党在灵谷寺旧址修建阵亡将士公墓，将无梁殿改为公墓祭堂，称"正气堂"。佛龛改为大砖台陈列祭器，四壁设"国民革命军阵亡将士题名碑"，大殿正中嵌"国民革命烈士之灵位"，左嵌《国父遗嘱》碑，右嵌民国《国歌》。
projects.content_en: Linggu Temple was originally located at Dulongfu southwest of Zhongshan Mountain, first built in the Southern Dynasties under the name Kaishan Temple. When the Hongwu Emperor built the Xiaoling Mausoleum, the temple was moved to its current site and renamed "Linggu Temple" (Spirit Valley Temple). During the Ming Dynasty the temple was vast in scale; it was destroyed by warfare during the Xianfeng-Tongzhi period of the Qing, leaving only the Ming-dynasty Beamless Hall and the Dragon God Hall built in the 6th year of Tongzhi (1867). In 1928, the Nationalist government built a cemetery for soldiers who died in the Northern Expedition, moving the Linggu Temple Buddhist statues to the Dragon God Hall—today's Linggu Temple. The Beamless Hall was built in the 14th year of Hongwu (1381). It originally enshrined the Amitayus Buddha (Buddha of Infinite Life), hence the name Wuliang Hall (Infinite Life Hall); the main hall uses brick-stone vault structure without timber beams, hence also called Beamless Hall. Among Jiangsu's five beamless halls, this is the earliest and largest. In front of the hall is a broad terrace. The hall faces southeast, five bays wide and three bays deep, with gray glazed double-eave hip-and-gable roof. The main ridge is decorated with three white glazed Lamaist pagodas, the central one extending through to the interior roof; under the eaves are imitation-wood dougong, replaced with concrete during the Republican period. The south side has three arch doors and two arched windows; the north side has three arch doors, with four arched windows on each side. The hall is 53.8m long, 37.85m wide, and 22m high. Three brick barrel vaults run transversely side by side, dividing the interior into three narrow spaces—front, middle, and rear. The middle bay is largest, 11.25m wide and 14m high; the sides are each 5m wide and 7.4m high. To balance the vault's lateral thrust, the front and rear walls are nearly 4m thick. Between the front and middle bays, five transverse vaults are constructed; between the middle and rear bays, vaults are built only at the end bays, with the central inner wall built directly as a screen wall. During the Zhengtong reign of the Ming, scriptures were stored here, with three large Buddha statues in the center and 24 heavenly figures around. It was repaired multiple times in the Qing; during the Xianfeng period, Qing troops set up the Jiangnan Great Camp here to confront the Taiping forces. In 1931, the KMT built a cemetery for fallen soldiers on the former Linggu Temple site, converting the Beamless Hall into the cemetery's memorial hall, called "Zhengqi Hall" (Hall of Righteous Spirit). The Buddhist niches were converted to large brick platforms displaying ritual vessels; the four walls bear "Stele of Names of Fallen Soldiers of the National Revolutionary Army," the center bears "Spirit Seat of National Revolutionary Martyrs," the left bears the "Father of the Nation's Will" stele, and the right bears the Republican-era "National Anthem."

projects.name: 中央体育场旧址（南京体育学院）
projects.name_en: Site of the Central Stadium (Nanjing Sport Institute)
projects.level: 第六批全国重点文物保护单位（2006年）
projects.level_en: 6th Batch National Key Cultural Heritage Site (2006)
projects.address_en: No. 8 Linggu Temple Road, Xuanwu District
highlights: 远东最大体育建筑群
对称布局
传统牌楼式外观
田径场
游泳池
8个赛场
projects.content_zh: 中央体育场旧址在灵谷寺南，现属南京体育学院。1930年蒋介石提议建造体育场，迎接第五届全国运动会，由基泰工程司关颂声、杨廷宝等设计绘图，新记公司承担全部土方工程，利源公司承担建筑工程。1931年奠基，原计划当年10月10日召开第五届全国运动大会，因水灾和"九·一八"影响未能如期开办，一直推迟到1933年。中央体育场采用对称布局，建筑外观为传统牌楼式，细部装饰为中国传统式。建筑为钢筋混凝土结构，场馆多利用地形，因地制宜设计，包括田径、游泳、棒球、篮球、国术、网球、足球和赛马八个赛场，总占地1000亩，可容纳60000多观众，是中国当时最大的工程之一，也是远东最大的体育建筑群。田径场是中央体育场的主体建筑，位于最东侧，占地77亩，呈椭圆形，长轴南北向。场内设有500米环形跑道和两条200米直道，跑道内是一座标准足球场，包含跳高、跳远和投掷等田径赛场，南北两端设篮球场、排球场和网球场等，使各项运动决赛可同时在场内举行。田径场有完备的排水系统，四周设看台，看台下部为运动员宿舍、浴室和厕所。北部看台利用土坡，原土压实，全部看台可容纳观众35000余人。田径场设东西两个主入口，皆为七开间传统牌楼，中部三间牌楼下部有三个拱形花格铁门，牌楼两侧尽端为四层小楼，设有办公室、裁判员休息室和新闻记者休息室，楼上为带大雨棚的司令台。场内布局严谨，观众需从各区大门入座，否则无法进入赛场，因此观众虽多却秩序井然。游泳池在体育场中部北侧。入口为仿明清宫殿式建筑，面朝西南，内有男女更衣室、淋浴和厕所等。建筑西南是长方形露天泳池，东南、西北为普通看台，西南为特别看台，可容观众4000人。其他网球场（排球场）、国术场、篮球场、棒球场和跑马场等均为露天场馆，按比赛需要修建为不同的几何形场地，周围设看台，外侧围以牌坊式入口。
projects.content_en: The former Central Stadium is located south of Linggu Temple, now part of Nanjing Sport Institute. In 1930, Chiang Kai-shek proposed building a stadium to host the 5th National Games. Designs were by Guan Songsheng and Yang Tingbao of Jitai Engineering Company; Xinji Company handled all earthwork, and Liyuan Company handled construction. The foundation was laid in 1931; originally planned to host the 5th National Games on October 10 of that year, it was delayed due to floods and the September 18th Incident, finally held in 1933. The Central Stadium uses a symmetrical layout, with traditional paifang-style building exteriors and Chinese traditional decorative details. The buildings are reinforced concrete structures, with venues mostly utilizing the terrain and designed according to local conditions. It includes eight competition venues: track and field, swimming, baseball, basketball, national martial arts (guoshu), tennis, football, and horse racing, covering 1,000 mu total and accommodating over 60,000 spectators—one of China's largest projects at the time and the largest sports complex in the Far East. The track and field stadium is the main building, at the easternmost side, covering 77 mu in an oval shape with the long axis north-south. It has a 500m circular track and two 200m straights; inside the track is a standard football field, plus track and field areas for high jump, long jump, and throwing events; basketball, volleyball, and tennis courts at the north and south ends allow multiple event finals to be held simultaneously. The track and field stadium has a complete drainage system, with stands on all sides; below the stands are athlete dormitories, bathrooms, and toilets. The north stand utilizes an earth slope with compacted original soil; all stands can accommodate over 35,000 spectators. The track and field stadium has two main entrances, east and west, both seven-bay traditional paifang. The lower part of the central three bays has three arched lattice iron gates; at the ends of the paifang sides are four-story small buildings with offices, referee lounges, and press lounges, with a command platform with a large rain canopy upstairs. The interior layout is rigorous: spectators must enter through their designated zone gates or cannot reach the field, maintaining order despite large crowds. The swimming pool is on the north side of the stadium's central area. The entrance is a building imitating Ming-Qing palace style, facing southwest, with men's and women's changing rooms, showers, and toilets inside. Southwest of the building is a rectangular outdoor pool; the southeast and northwest sides have ordinary stands, and the southwest has special stands accommodating 4,000 spectators. Other venues—tennis (volleyball), national martial arts, basketball, baseball, and horse racing—are all outdoor, built in different geometric shapes according to competition needs, with surrounding stands and paifang-style entrances on the exterior.

projects.name: 国立紫金山天文台旧址
projects.name_en: Site of the Purple Mountain Observatory
projects.level: 第四批全国重点文物保护单位（1996年）
projects.level_en: 4th Batch National Key Cultural Heritage Site (1996)
projects.address_en: Third Peak of Purple Mountain, Xuanwu District
highlights: 中国第一座自行设计建造的现代天文台
余青松设计
中国传统建筑风格
600毫米口径折反射望远镜
明清天文仪器
projects.content_zh: 紫金山天文台在紫金山第三峰，是我国第一座自行设计建造的现代天文台。1929年由国民政府中央研究院天文研究所筹建，首任台长余青松亲自设计并监督施工，1934年建成，1950年改称中国科学院紫金山天文台。天文台共由六栋建筑组成，外墙采用就地取材的虎皮石，包括台本部、子午仪室、赤道仪室、变星仪室、东宿舍和西宿舍，散落布置在山顶上。其中台本部建成最早，由余青松、杨廷宝设计，具有中国传统建筑风格。底层平台入口有钢筋混凝土牌坊，四柱三间，紫红琉璃顶，上刻天文台三字。穿过牌坊登上台阶可达平台上的望远镜观测室，内设从德国蔡司公司订购的600毫米口径折反射式望远镜。观测室采用钢架结构，为直径8米的半圆形，配有可升降平台，屋顶天窗可配合望远镜旋转，全部电动操作，对天空任一位置进行观测。台本部下方陈列明清时期的天文仪器，也是珍贵文物。
projects.content_en: The Purple Mountain Observatory is located on the third peak of Purple Mountain and is China's first modern observatory designed and built independently. In 1929, it was initiated by the Institute of Astronomy of the Nationalist government's Academia Sinica. The first director, Yu Qingsong, personally designed and supervised construction, completed in 1934. In 1950 it was renamed the Purple Mountain Observatory of the Chinese Academy of Sciences. The observatory consists of six buildings with exterior walls of locally quarried rough stone (hupi stone), including the main headquarters, meridian instrument room, equatorial instrument room, variable star instrument room, east dormitory, and west dormitory, scattered across the mountain top. The main headquarters was built earliest, designed by Yu Qingsong and Yang Tingbao, in traditional Chinese architectural style. At the ground-level platform entrance is a reinforced concrete paifang with four columns and three bays, purple-red glazed tile roof, inscribed with the characters "Observatory." Passing through the paifang and climbing steps leads to the telescope observation room on the platform, housing a 600mm aperture catadioptric telescope ordered from Carl Zeiss in Germany. The observation room uses a steel frame structure, is semicircular with an 8m diameter, equipped with a liftable platform; the roof skylight can rotate in coordination with the telescope, all electrically operated, allowing observation of any position in the sky. Below the main headquarters, Ming and Qing dynasty astronomical instruments are displayed—also precious cultural relics.

projects.name: 天堡城遗址
projects.level: 第三批江苏省文物保护单位（1982年）
projects.level_en: 3rd Batch Jiangsu Provincial Cultural Heritage Site (1982)
projects.address: 玄武区紫金山天文台内部
projects.address_en: Inside Purple Mountain Observatory, Xuanwu District
highlights: 太平天国要塞
巨石依山垒砌
南京北部护城河唯一通路
地堡城
projects.content_zh: 天堡城与山下城墙根龙脖子处的地堡城同为太平天国守卫天京的要塞。天堡城筑于太平天国癸好三年（1853年）春，用巨石依山垒砌而成。这里是南京北部护城河之间唯一的通路，乃兵家必争之地。两城上下呼应，易守难攻，太平军曾据此与清军对峙长达十一年，最后天堡城失守，地堡城也很快被攻克，天京陷落。辛亥革命期间，这里是江浙联军与清军激烈争夺的要塞。天堡城现仅存石垒墙基一座。在太平门外东侧城墙下的地堡城，仅余石块、石垒和壕沟等遗迹。
projects.content_en: Tianbao Fort and Dibao Fort at the foot of the city wall at Longbozi were both fortresses of the Taiping Heavenly Kingdom defending Tianjing (Nanjing). Tianbao Fort was built in the spring of the 3rd year of Guihao of the Taiping Heavenly Kingdom (1853), constructed with huge stones piled against the mountain. This was the only passage between the northern moats of Nanjing—a strategic point contested by all military forces. The two forts supported each other from above and below, easy to defend and difficult to attack. The Taiping army held out against Qing forces here for eleven years; when Tianbao Fort finally fell, Dibao Fort was soon captured as well, and Tianjing fell. During the Xinhai Revolution, this was a fiercely contested fortress between the Jiangsu-Zhejiang Allied Army and Qing forces. Today, Tianbao Fort retains only one stone rampart foundation. Dibao Fort, below the city wall east of the Taiping Gate, leaves only traces of stones, stone ramparts, and trenches.

projects.name: 阳山碑材
projects.level: 第七批全国重点文物保护单位（2013年）
projects.level_en: 7th Batch National Key Cultural Heritage Site (2013)
projects.address: 江宁区汤山温泉西路8号
projects.address_en: No. 8 West Tangshan Hot Spring Road, Jiangning District
highlights: 明成祖为朱元璋建神功圣德碑
世界罕见巨碑
70余米高
2.6万吨
坟头村
projects.content_zh: 阳山碑材位于江宁区汤山镇西北阳山西南麓半山腰，辟山凿成。原为明成祖朱棣为其父朱元璋建造神功圣德碑所选碑材。据明嘉靖《皇明文衡》记载："永乐三年秋八月，皇帝因建碑孝陵碑石，于都城东北之阳山，得良材焉，其长十四丈有奇，阔不及长者三之一，厚二丈，色黝泽如漆，无疵莹。"碑材分碑身、碑额和碑座三部分。碑座长30.35米，厚13米，高16米，底部已凿空，仅留两行岩石支撑，西北端仍与山体相连。碑额呈椭圆形，在碑座东北约100米处，高10.7米，宽20.3米，厚8.4米，通体凿有14个石牙，拟镌刻蟠龙形象，底部也已凿空，仅留三行石柱支撑。碑身横卧在碑座北面6米处，平面为长方形，长49.4米，宽10.7米，厚4.4米，东北端尚与山岩相连，底部留有三行石柱支撑，其余均与山体分离。三块碑材竖起来高度为70余米，重2.6万吨，乃世界罕见之巨碑。据说因开凿碑材，死人无数，白骨堆满山沟，因此离碑材最近的村庄叫"坟头村"。由于碑材过大，无法运输竖立，因此被弃置不用，在明孝陵中建造了现在较小的"大明孝陵神功圣德碑"。
projects.content_en: The Yangshan Stele Quarry is located on the mountainside of the southwestern slope of Yangshan, northwest of Tangshan Town in Jiangning District, carved into the mountain. It was originally the stele material selected by the Yongle Emperor Zhu Di for the Divine Merit and Sacred Virtue Stele of his father Zhu Yuanzhang. According to the Ming Jiajing-era "Huangming Wenheng": "In the eighth month of autumn in the 3rd year of Yongle, for building the stele at Xiaoling, the emperor found fine material at Yangshan northeast of the capital. Its length exceeds 14 zhang, its width is less than one-third of its length, its thickness is 2 zhang, its color is dark and lustrous like lacquer, flawless and bright." The stele material is divided into three parts: stele body, stele head, and stele base. The stele base is 30.35m long, 13m thick, and 16m high, with the bottom already hollowed out, leaving only two rows of rock support; its northwest end remains connected to the mountain. The stele head is oval, about 100m northeast of the base, 10.7m high, 20.3m wide, 8.4m thick, entirely carved with 14 stone teeth intended for coiling dragon imagery; its bottom is also hollowed out, leaving only three rows of stone pillar supports. The stele body lies horizontally 6m north of the base, rectangular in plan, 49.4m long, 10.7m wide, 4.4m thick, with its northeast end still connected to the rock and three rows of stone pillar supports at the bottom, the rest separated from the mountain. If erected, the three pieces would stand over 70m high and weigh 26,000 tons—a giant stele rare in the world. It is said that countless people died quarrying the stele, with white bones filling the gullies, hence the nearest village is called "Fentou Village" (Grave Head Village). Because the stele was too large to transport and erect, it was abandoned, and the smaller existing "Great Ming Xiaoling Divine Merit and Sacred Virtue Stele" was built at the Ming Xiaoling Mausoleum instead.

projects.name: 栖霞寺及舍利塔
projects.level: 第三批全国重点文物保护单位（1988年）
projects.level_en: 3rd Batch National Key Cultural Heritage Site (1988)
projects.address_en: Qixia Temple, Qixia Mountain, Qixia District
highlights: 南朝始建
南唐重建石塔
八角形五层密檐式
八相图石刻
千佛崖
projects.content_zh: 栖霞寺始建于南朝齐永明七年（489年）。南朝名士明僧绍（？—483）号栖霞，曾在山中建造栖霞精舍隐居，朝廷屡次征召不就，百姓称其为"明征君"。后来他的儿子与主持僧度在寺后山崖开造"千佛崖"，隋代在千佛崖下建舍利塔。唐高祖时改栖霞寺为功德寺，大加增建。唐高宗李治亲撰征君碑，立于寺前，改寺名为隐君栖霞寺。唐会昌年间毁寺，唐宣宗大中五年（851年）重建。南唐建舍利塔，改名妙因寺，宋时改名普云寺，宋真宗景德五年（1008年）改称栖霞禅寺，宋哲宗元祐八年（1093年）改称严因崇报禅院，又改为景德栖霞寺，也称虎穴寺。明洪武二十五年（1392年）赐名栖霞寺，沿用至今。清咸丰年间寺庙毁于战火，清光绪三十四年（1908年）重建毗卢宝殿、藏经楼、五观堂、金汤阁、五云阁、鹿野堂、挹翠楼和客库房等，1930年建弥勒殿。现寺院坐东朝西，依山布置，沿中轴线依次为山门、弥勒殿、毗卢宝殿和藏经楼，两侧轴线分布碑亭、客堂和斋堂等。栖霞山舍利塔位于栖霞寺东南角，千佛崖前。塔始建于隋仁寿元年（601年），原为木构，据传隋文帝曾获尼僧智仙所赠数百颗佛舍利，分授各州，建造了83座舍利塔，栖霞寺舍利塔即为其中之一。唐武宗会昌年间，木塔毁坏，南唐时高越和林仁肇主持重建为石塔。塔高18米，八角形，共五层，下有须弥宝座，台上为仿木密檐式塔。须弥座下部有两层八角形底座，刻海石榴和凤凰图案，座下设覆莲，束柱装饰蛟龙和力士，壁面内为佛陀八相图石刻画像。座上有仰莲台，首层塔身正面和背面设雕饰逼真的板门，有门钉和铺首。西侧为普贤像，东侧为文殊像（已毁）。其余四面为高浮雕力士，神情肌肉饱满有力。塔檐下横楣刻飞天像，其上五层石檐，檐间有佛龛装饰。1931年修复了塔刹，并根据发掘遗物复原了栏杆。
projects.content_en: Qixia Temple was first built in the 7th year of Yongming of the Southern Qi (489). The Southern Dynasties scholar Ming Sengshao (?-483), whose hao was Qixia, built the Qixia Retreat in the mountains for seclusion; the court repeatedly summoned him but he refused, and the people called him "Ming Zhengjun" (Conqueror Ming). Later, his son and the presiding monk Du carved the "Thousand Buddha Cliff" on the mountain cliff behind the temple. In the Sui Dynasty, a sarira pagoda was built below the Thousand Buddha Cliff. In the Tang Dynasty, Emperor Gaozu renamed it Gongde Temple and greatly expanded it. Emperor Gaozong Li Zhi personally wrote the Zhengjun Stele, erected in front of the temple, and renamed it Yinjun Qixia Temple. It was destroyed during the Huichang persecution of Buddhism and rebuilt in the 5th year of Dazhong (851) of Emperor Xuanzong. During the Southern Tang, the sarira pagoda was built and the temple renamed Miaoyin Temple; in the Song it was renamed Puyun Temple, then Qixia Chan Temple in the 5th year of Jingde (1008), then Yanyin Chongbao Chan Monastery in the 8th year of Yuanyou (1093), also called Jingde Qixia Temple or Huxue Temple. In the 25th year of Hongwu (1392), the Ming Hongwu Emperor bestowed the name Qixia Temple, still in use today. The temple was destroyed by warfare during the Xianfeng period of the Qing; in the 34th year of Guangxu (1908), the Pilu Hall, Scripture Library, Wuguan Hall, Jintang Pavilion, Wuyun Pavilion, Luye Hall, Yicui Building, and guest rooms were rebuilt; the Maitreya Hall was built in 1930. The temple now faces west, arranged along the mountain slope, with the mountain gate, Maitreya Hall, Pilu Hall, and Scripture Library along the central axis, and stele pavilions, guest halls, and dining halls on the side axes. The Qixia Sarira Pagoda is located southeast of Qixia Temple, in front of the Thousand Buddha Cliff. It was first built in the 1st year of Renshou of the Sui (601), originally wooden. According to legend, Emperor Wen of Sui received several hundred Buddha relics from the nun Zhixian and distributed them to various prefectures, building 83 sarira pagodas—Qixia Temple's being one of them. The wooden pagoda was destroyed during the Huichang period; during the Southern Tang, Gao Yue and Lin Renzhao oversaw its reconstruction as a stone pagoda. The pagoda is 18m high, octagonal, with five stories, on a Sumeru pedestal with an imitation-wood multi-eave form above. The lower part of the Sumeru pedestal has two octagonal bases carved with sea pomegranate and phoenix patterns; below the pedestal is an inverted lotus, with binding pillars decorated with dragons and guardian figures, and the wall interior features stone carvings of the Eight Phases of the Buddha. Above the pedestal is an upward lotus platform; the first story's front and back have exquisitely carved panel doors with door nails and knockers. The west side has a Samantabhadra statue, the east side a Manjushri statue (destroyed). The other four sides have high-relief guardian figures with powerful musculature. Under the eaves are horizontal lintels carved with apsaras (flying celestial beings); above are five stone eaves with Buddha niches between them. The spire was restored in 1931, and railings were reconstructed based on excavated relics.

projects.name: 千佛崖石窟及明征君碑
projects.name_en: Thousand-Buddha Grottoes and Stele of Ming Zhengjun
projects.level: 第五批全国重点文物保护单位（2001年）
projects.level_en: 5th Batch National Key Cultural Heritage Site (2001)
projects.address_en: East of Qixia Temple, Qixia District
highlights: 南朝齐永明二年开凿
无量殿（三圣殿）
254个佛龛553尊佛像
明征君碑（唐高宗撰文）
梅花石
projects.content_zh: 千佛崖位于栖霞寺舍利塔东侧山上，始凿于南朝齐永明二年（484年），永明七年（489年）明僧绍次子明仲璋继承父亲遗志，与法度禅师在栖霞山西峰石壁凿"三圣像"。南朝梁天监十年（511年）凿成"无量殿"（又称三圣殿、大佛殿），殿内正坐无量寿佛，两侧侍立观世音和大势至，均高约10米；殿前左右现有两尊接引佛，为隋代遗物，民国年间从舍利塔移至此地。无量殿是崖上开凿最早、规模最大的石窟，其后齐、梁太子和大臣陆续在崖上建窟，宋、明及后世皆有增刻。邻近无量殿的次大龛也是南朝时期所刻，在两个大窟附近还有许多南朝时期的中小型龛窟，造像以弥勒佛、阿弥陀佛和千佛为主。在南朝诸龛西北方高处分布着一些唐龛，多为中小型龛和千佛龛。现存大小佛龛254个，佛像553尊，号称千佛崖。1924年寺僧修补佛像时，用水泥涂覆，使之失去原貌；"文革"时期又遭到破坏，现大部分残损。少数保存尚好的佛像造型生动，雕刻精致，端雅秀丽，堪称艺术精品。一些石窟内还保存着早期彩绘遗迹、佛像背光及火焰图案等。在山崖西侧的"中102号"窟中，主窟右壁下侧的小佛龛顶部有一对飞天图案仍清晰可见，体态轻盈，衣带随风飘动，与敦煌莫高窟中的飞天形象颇为相似。明征君碑在栖霞寺山门右侧碑亭中，碑文记载了明僧绍的事迹。明僧绍多次坚辞皇帝征召不就，人们尊称他为"征君"。唐代明僧绍第五世孙明崇俨成为李治和武则天的宠臣，他恳请皇帝为先祖树碑立传，李治慨然应允，亲自撰写了碑文，由书法家高正臣书丹，王知敬篆额。高正臣书法取王羲之、褚遂良遗范，既具魏晋神韵，又兼初唐端严，乃碑中逸品，书坛佳构。石碑背面有"栖霞"二字，相传是高宗李治手笔，构架工整，颇有大家风范。碑高2.74米，宽1.31米，厚0.36米，碑额为六龙拱额，上有篆书"明征君碑"，两侧为狮首绶带西番莲纹，碑文行书2376字，均为四六韵文，最后以十首铭文作结，碑下端员为龙首。碑身石材上有豆粒状白色斑纹，状若含苞未放之梅花，故有"梅花石"之美誉。
projects.content_en: The Thousand Buddha Cliff is located on the mountain east of the Qixia Temple sarira pagoda. Carving began in the 2nd year of Yongming of the Southern Qi (484). In the 7th year of Yongming (489), Ming Zhongzhang, the second son of Ming Sengshao, inherited his father's behest and, together with Chan Master Fadu, carved the "Three Sage Images" on the cliff of the western peak of Qixia Mountain. In the 10th year of Tianjian of the Southern Liang (511), the "Wuliang Hall" (also called Three Sage Hall or Great Buddha Hall) was carved, with Amitayus Buddha seated in the center flanked by Guanyin and Mahasthamaprapta, each about 10m high. In front, on left and right, stand two guiding Buddha statues—Sui Dynasty relics moved here from the sarira pagoda during the Republican period. The Wuliang Hall is the earliest and largest grotto carved into the cliff. Subsequently, Qi and Liang princes and ministers continued carving grottoes on the cliff, with additions in the Song, Ming, and later periods. The second-largest niche near the Wuliang Hall was also carved in the Southern Dynasties; near the two large grottoes are many medium and small Southern Dynasties niches, with statues mainly of Maitreya, Amitabha, and Thousand Buddhas. In the northwest above the Southern Dynasties niches are some Tang Dynasty niches, mostly medium-small and thousand-Buddha niches. Today there are 254 niches of various sizes with 553 Buddha statues, known as the Thousand Buddha Cliff. In 1924, when monks repaired the statues, they covered them with cement, destroying their original appearance; further damage occurred during the Cultural Revolution, leaving most damaged. A few well-preserved statues are vividly modeled, exquisitely carved, elegant and graceful—true artistic masterpieces. Some grottoes still preserve early polychrome traces, Buddha halos, and flame patterns. In grotto "Zhong 102" on the west side of the cliff, at the top of a small niche below the main grotto's right wall, a pair of apsaras (flying celestial beings) is still clearly visible—light in form with ribbons fluttering in the wind, similar to the apsaras in the Mogao Grottoes at Dunhuang. The Ming Zhengjun Stele stands in a stele pavilion to the right of the Qixia Temple mountain gate. The inscription records the deeds of Ming Sengshao, who repeatedly refused imperial summons and was respectfully called "Zhengjun" (Conqueror). In the Tang Dynasty, Ming Chongyan, the fifth-generation descendant of Ming Sengshao, became a favorite official of Li Zhi (Emperor Gaozong) and Wu Zetian. He petitioned the emperor to erect a stele for his ancestor; Li Zhi graciously agreed and personally wrote the inscription, with calligraphy by Gao Zhengchen and seal-script heading by Wang Zhijing. Gao Zhengchen's calligraphy follows the legacy of Wang Xizhi and Chu Suiliang, combining Wei-Jin charm with early Tang solemnity—a superior stele and fine calligraphic work. On the back of the stele are the characters "Qixia," said to be in the hand of Emperor Gaozong Li Zhi, with rigorous structure and masterful style. The stele is 2.74m high, 1.31m wide, 0.36m thick, with a six-dragon arching forehead bearing the seal script "Ming Zhengjun Stele," lion-head ribbon and passionflower patterns on both sides, and 2,376 characters of running-script inscription in parallel prose, concluding with ten inscribed eulogies; the lower end of the stele is a dragon head. The stone material has bean-sized white markings resembling unopened plum blossoms, hence the reputation "Plum Blossom Stone."

projects.content_zh: 南朝陵墓石刻是南北朝时期宋、齐、梁、陈四个朝代（420—589）的帝后陵、王侯墓前的石刻，分布在南京市及其附近的丹阳市和句容市一带。南京目前发现十七处，其中刘裕初宁陵、陈霸先万安陵和陈蒨永宁陵为帝陵，其余均为王侯墓，已发现的王侯墓均在南京。南北朝普遍流行薄葬，是否起坟依地形而定，主要以神道石刻作为标示，一般为3种6件，依次为石兽1对、石柱1对和石碑1对。帝陵前置石麒麟、石天禄各1只，两者形象差异不大，唯麒麟头上为独角，天禄则为双角。王侯墓前石兽为辟邪，状若狮子。这些石兽多用整块石头雕刻而成，体型雄大，昂首挺胸，双目圆睁，张口吐舌或垂舌，腹侧带双翼，长尾曳地，一足前迈。整套神道石刻保存最完整的，是甘家巷小学内的萧秀墓石刻，共3种8件，包括石麒麟、石天禄各1只，1对石柱和4件石碑。麒麟以甘家巷陈文帝永宁陵前石麒麟、石天禄最为灵动俊美，矫健秀逸，二兽张口露齿，足跟着地，足趾翘起，掌心朝前，极富动感。辟邪中的佳作是栖霞区十月村农田中的萧景墓石辟邪，身长、身高各3.8米，体态壮硕，曲线雄健，长舌垂胸，舌尖上卷，鬃毛卷曲，羽翼刻云勾纹，爪趾骨节嶙峋，栩栩如生。另外仙鹤门萧宏墓的辟邪造型雄浑简练，亦为精品。神道石柱以萧景墓西石柱保存最为完好。石柱多由柱头、柱身和柱座构成。柱头包括装饰着覆莲的柱盖和顶部小辟邪；柱身有收分，为圆形或椭圆平面，雕刻直棱纹20至28道不等，柱身上方为长方形柱额，两柱柱额一般一为正书、一为反文；下部底座上圆下方，上部为头部相连、尾部相交的螭龙，下方为方形基座，座周刻画浮雕。石碑最佳者为萧儋墓。石碑由碑首、碑身和碑座三部分组成。碑首两侧皆为浮雕互相纠缠的双龙，正中为长方额，刻有朝代、官衔和谥号之类，额下有圆形穿孔。碑身正、反皆有文字，周围线刻纹饰，有些侧面也有纹饰。碑座为龟趺，形似大乌龟，凸目昂首，一足向前，作负重爬行状。南京南朝陵墓石刻一览表（参考梁白泉《南京的六朝石刻》）：1.宋武帝刘裕初宁陵石刻（422年，江宁区麒麟镇麒麟铺村中马路两旁，石麒麟、石天禄各一）；2.梁桂阳王萧融墓石刻（502年，栖霞区南京炼油厂小学，石辟邪二，石柱一）；3.梁安成康王萧秀墓石刻（518年，栖霞区尧化门甘家巷小学，石辟邪二，石柱二，石碑四）；4.梁始兴忠武王萧憺墓石刻（522年，栖霞区栖霞镇甘家巷西公园东部，石辟邪二，石碑一，龟趺二）；5.梁吴平忠侯萧景墓石刻（523年，栖霞区尧化门十月乡十月村南，石辟邪二，石柱一）；6.梁鄱阳忠烈王萧恢墓石刻（526年，栖霞区栖霞镇甘家巷西公园西部，与萧憺墓石刻东西相对，石辟邪二）；7.梁临川靖惠王萧宏墓石刻（526年，栖霞区仙鹤门仙林大学城应天学院东侧，石辟邪一，石柱二，石碑二）；8.梁南康平王萧绩墓石刻（523年，栖霞区尧化镇北家边，石柱二）；9.梁新渝宽侯萧暎墓石刻（544年，栖霞区甘家巷甘东线北董家边村36号屋西，石柱一）；10.梁建安敏侯萧正立墓（548年？，江宁区江苏海事职业技术学院东面洼地，石辟邪二，石柱二）；11.陈武帝陈霸先万安陵石刻（？，559年，江宁区上坊镇石马冲白马公园，石辟邪二）；12.陈文帝陈蒨永宁陵石刻（？，566年？，栖霞区栖霞镇新合村狮子冲，石麒麟、石天禄各一）；13.方旗庙失名墓石刻（南朝，江宁区江宁镇建中村中滨江开发区，宁铜路北侧，石辟邪二）；14.太平村失名墓石刻（？，南朝，栖霞区燕子矶镇太平村太子凹出土，现迁至南京博物院（朝天宫），石辟邪一）；15.宋墅失名墓石刻（南朝，江宁区淳化镇宋墅村，石柱一，石柱础一）；16.耿岗失名墓石刻（南朝，江宁区上坊镇耿岗村，石柱一）；17.徐家村失名墓石刻（南朝，栖霞区燕子矶镇金陵石化公司化工一厂院内，石柱一）；18.侯村失名墓石刻（？，南朝，江宁区上坊镇南汽1号路南侧，石辟邪二，石柱一）；19.狮子坝失名墓石刻（南朝，栖霞区马群镇狮子坝村旁菜畦中，石辟邪一）。
projects.content_en: The Southern Dynasties mausoleum stone sculptures are the stone carvings in front of imperial and noble tombs of the Song, Qi, Liang, and Chen dynasties (420-589), distributed in Nanjing and nearby Danyang and Jurong. Seventeen sites have been discovered in Nanjing: the Liu Yu Chuning Mausoleum, Chen Baxian Wan'an Mausoleum, and Chen Qian Yongning Mausoleum are imperial tombs; the rest are noble tombs, all discovered in Nanjing. Simple burials were common in the Northern and Southern Dynasties; whether to raise a mound depended on terrain, and spirit-way stone sculptures served as markers—generally 3 types and 6 pieces: one pair of stone beasts, one pair of stone pillars, and one pair of stone steles. In front of imperial tombs are one stone qilin and one stone tianlu, similar in appearance except the qilin has a single horn and the tianlu has double horns. In front of noble tombs are stone bixie (mythical beasts), resembling lions. These stone beasts are mostly carved from single blocks of stone, with massive bodies, raised heads and thrust-out chests, wide-open eyes, open mouths with tongues protruding or hanging, wings on the belly sides, long tails dragging on the ground, and one paw stepping forward. The most complete set of spirit-way sculptures is the Xiao Xiu tomb set at Ganjiaxiang Primary School—3 types and 8 pieces including one qilin, one tianlu, one pair of pillars, and four steles. The most agile and handsome qilin and tianlu are those in front of the Chen Wen Emperor Yongning Mausoleum at Shizichong, Qixia Town—both beasts with open mouths showing teeth, heels on ground, toes lifted, palms facing forward, full of dynamism. The finest bixie is the Xiao Jing tomb bixie in farmland at Shiyue Village, Yaohua Gate, Qixia District—3.8m long and 3.8m high, with a robust body, vigorous curves, long tongue hanging to the chest with tip curled up, curly mane, cloud-scroll patterns on wings, and sharply defined claws and joints—lifelike. The bixie at the Xiao Hong tomb at Xianhe Gate is also a masterpiece with its powerful and concise form. The best-preserved spirit-way pillar is the west pillar of the Xiao Jing tomb. Pillars usually consist of capital, shaft, and base. The capital includes an inverted-lotus-decorated pillar cover and a small bixie on top; the shaft has entasis, circular or elliptical in plan, carved with 20-28 vertical flutes; above the shaft is a rectangular pillar tablet, usually one in regular script and one in reverse script on the two pillars. The lower base is round on top and square below, the upper part being interlocking chi dragons with joined heads and tails, the lower part a square base with relief carvings around. The finest stele is at the Xiao Dan tomb. Steles consist of head, body, and base. The head has relief interlocking double dragons on both sides, with a rectangular tablet in the center inscribed with dynasty, official title, and posthumous name, and a circular perforation below. The front and back of the body bear inscriptions, with line-carved decorations around the edges and sometimes on the sides. The base is a gui (tortoise), resembling a large turtle with protruding eyes and raised head, one foot forward, as if crawling under a heavy load.

projects.name: 七桥瓮
projects.level: 第七批全国重点文物保护单位（2013年）
projects.level_en: 7th Batch National Key Cultural Heritage Site (2013)
projects.address: 秦淮区红花街道七桥村
projects.address_en: Qiqiao Village, Honghua Subdistrict, Qinhuai District
highlights: 南京现存体量最大古桥
明正统五年建
中国唯一以"瓮"命名古桥
7座桥瓮
15只螭兽头
projects.content_zh: 七桥瓮是南京现存体量最大的古桥，建于明正统五年（1440年），是中国唯一一座以"瓮"命名的古桥。该桥全长89.60米，宽13米，高25米，桥身酷似弯弓，用花岗岩掺合灰浆、秫米和桐油砌成，岩石长、宽皆为0.65米，厚0.18米。桥下共有七孔桥瓮，中间最大，其余三组两两相对，依次缩小。桥两头的瓮宽9米，拱洞由长1.15米、宽0.45米、厚0.25米的略带弧形的240块条石砌成，相邻桥瓮相差48块条石。桥拱上方两翼各雕有15只面目狰狞的螭兽头。桥下有7座桥墩，宽2.5米，由高0.30米、宽0.45米的长短不一的块石砌成，为减少水流阻力而呈梭船形。桥墩两头巨石上各雕6只分水兽头，呈人面兽头像，向前凸出约3米。1956年曾维修桥身两侧和瓮壁，并修补了残损的分水兽头，1964年增建水泥桥栏，1974年铺设沥青桥面，2008年对整座桥梁进行全面修缮。
projects.content_en: Qiqiaoweng Bridge is the largest surviving ancient bridge in Nanjing, built in the 5th year of Zhengtong of the Ming (1440). It is the only ancient bridge in China named with "weng" (vault/arch). The bridge is 89.60m long, 13m wide, and 25m high, its body resembling a bent bow, built with granite mixed with mortar, sorghum rice, and tung oil. The stones are 0.65m long and wide, 0.18m thick. Below the bridge are seven arch vaults, the central one largest, with the remaining three pairs facing each other and decreasing in size. The vaults at both ends are 9m wide; the archways are built from 240 slightly curved stone strips 1.15m long, 0.45m wide, and 0.25m thick, with adjacent vaults differing by 48 stone strips. Above the bridge arches, on both wings, are carved 15 ferocious-looking chi beast heads each. Below the bridge are 7 piers, 2.5m wide, built from stone blocks of varying lengths 0.30m high and 0.45m wide, shaped like shuttle boats to reduce water resistance. On the large stones at both ends of each pier are carved 6 water-dividing beast heads each, in human-faced beast form, protruding about 3m forward. In 1956, both sides of the bridge and the arch walls were repaired, and damaged water-dividing beast heads were mended; in 1964, concrete bridge railings were added; in 1974, an asphalt deck was laid; in 2008, the entire bridge underwent comprehensive restoration.

projects.name: 南唐二陵
projects.name_en: Two Mausoleums of Southern Tang Dynasty
projects.level: 第三批全国重点文物保护单位（1988年）
projects.level_en: 3rd Batch National Key Cultural Heritage Site (1988)
projects.address: 江宁区东善桥镇祖堂山南
projects.address_en: South of Zutang Mountain, Dongshanqiao Town, Jiangning District
highlights: 南唐烈祖李昪钦陵
中主李璟顺陵
太子墩
砖石仿木结构
天象图
projects.content_zh: 南唐二陵位于祖堂山南麓的"太子墩"，是南唐烈祖李昪（888—943）和中主李璟（916—961）的陵墓，其中李昪与皇后的合陵为钦陵，李璟与皇后的合陵为顺陵。二陵相距50米，均坐北朝南，钦陵略偏西，顺陵略偏东。二陵均无地面建筑留存，仅留坟包。1950年发现钦陵遭到盗掘，于是对二陵进行考古发掘，发现二陵从宋代开始就多次被盗，但仍出土了600多件文物。二陵中钦陵规模较大，圆形封土高5米，直径30米，俗称"太子墩"。墓门为砖砌拱形，表面涂朱，外有石灰粉饰的八字砖墙，拱门四周是用砖砌筑的仿木构件，拱顶有彩绘一斗三升式斗栱，下有两道额枋，东西两端各有半个一斗三升斗栱，其上绘彩色花叶。门两旁立方形倚柱，梁枋柱上皆有彩绘牡丹花纹。墓内分为前、中、后三室，全长21米，高5米多，宽10米。前、中两室用砖砌，顶部砌筑为尖顶穹窿，后室用石砌，壁面都砌出仿木构件，如八棱倚柱、梁枋和一斗三升式斗栱等，其上有色彩艳丽的彩绘。前室和中室之间设195厘米厚的拱门，中室和后室之间设130厘米厚的短过道。前室和中室各带两个较大的侧室，后室两侧对称布置三处较小的侧室，以拱门相通。中室北壁辟后室墓门，门上横梁刻双龙夺珠浮雕，宝珠四周有火焰，下以祥云承托。墓门两旁石壁左右各立一尊大型浮雕武士像，头戴盔胄，身披细甲，足踏祥云，双手倚长剑，其上有敷金涂彩的痕迹。石像之间是石砌墓门，表面涂朱。中室通向后室的过道原以石块封砌。后室有两扇石门，一扇被盗墓者打开，另一扇上部遭到少许破坏。后室最大，四壁均涂朱，柱子斗栱皆用整石雕磨，上施彩画，花纹线有雕刻痕迹。室顶东西两侧以大石条砌出叠涩，其上为由横列的石梁组成的平顶。室顶绘有天象图，东有红日，西有素月，南北有南北斗，以朱色线条勾画相连，并用朱线勾画出漫天北斗。地面铺大青石板，凿出江河迂回之状。室北正中为安置棺椁的大青石座，上有浮雕花纹。李璟顺陵构造与李昪陵大致相同，只是规模略小，形制也较简单。前、中、后三室均用砖砌，无石刻浮雕等装饰，后室两侧各有两间侧室，未刻天文、地理图，石棺座也较为粗糙无雕饰。当时已是南唐后期，结构装饰与艺术已失去盛世气象。
projects.content_en: The Two Mausoleums of the Southern Tang are located at "Taizi Dun" (Crown Prince Mound) on the southern slope of Zutang Mountain. They are the tombs of Li Bian (888-943), the Liezu (Founding Emperor) of the Southern Tang, and Li Jing (916-961), the second ruler. Li Bian's joint tomb with his empress is the Qin Mausoleum; Li Jing's joint tomb with his empress is the Shun Mausoleum. The two tombs are 50m apart, both facing south—the Qin Mausoleum slightly west, the Shun Mausoleum slightly east. No above-ground buildings survive, only burial mounds. In 1950, the Qin Mausoleum was found looted, so archaeological excavation of both tombs was conducted. They had been looted multiple times since the Song Dynasty, but over 600 artifacts were still unearthed. The Qin Mausoleum is larger, with a circular earthen mound 5m high and 30m in diameter, commonly called "Taizi Dun." The tomb gate is a brick arch, surface painted red, with an exterior of whitewashed splayed brick walls; around the arch are brick imitation-wood components, with painted one-dou-three-sheng dougong on the arch top, two architraves below, and half one-dou-three-sheng dougong at each east-west end, painted with colorful leaves and flowers. Square engaged pillars stand on both sides of the gate, with painted peony patterns on beams, architraves, and pillars. The tomb interior is divided into front, middle, and rear chambers, 21m long, over 5m high, and 10m wide. The front and middle chambers are brick-built with pointed domed ceilings; the rear chamber is stone-built, with walls featuring imitation-wood components such as octagonal engaged pillars, beams, architraves, and one-dou-three-sheng dougong, all with vivid polychrome paintings. Between the front and middle chambers is a 195cm-thick archway; between the middle and rear chambers is a 130cm-thick short passage. The front and middle chambers each have two larger side chambers; the rear chamber has three smaller symmetric side chambers on each side, connected by archways. The north wall of the middle chamber opens to the rear chamber gate; the beam above the gate is carved with a relief of two dragons seizing a pearl, with flames around the pearl and auspicious clouds below. On the stone walls on both sides of the gate stand two large relief warrior statues, wearing helmets and fine armor, standing on auspicious clouds, leaning on long swords with both hands, with traces of gilding and color. Between the stone statues is a stone tomb gate, surface painted red. The passage from the middle to rear chamber was originally sealed with stone blocks. The rear chamber has two stone doors—one opened by tomb robbers, the other slightly damaged at the top. The rear chamber is the largest, with all walls painted red; pillars and dougong are carved from whole stone with painted decorations and incised pattern lines. On the east and west sides of the chamber ceiling, large stone strips form corbels, above which is a flat ceiling of horizontal stone beams. The ceiling is painted with a celestial map: a red sun in the east, a white moon in the west, Northern and Southern Dippers in the north and south, connected by red lines, with the Big Dipper scattered across the sky in red. The floor is paved with large bluestone slabs carved with winding rivers. In the center of the north wall is a large bluestone platform for the coffin, with relief patterns. The Shun Mausoleum of Li Jing has a similar structure to Li Bian's tomb, but slightly smaller and simpler in form. The front, middle, and rear chambers are all brick-built, without stone relief decorations; the rear chamber has two side chambers on each side, with no celestial or terrestrial maps carved, and the stone coffin platform is rough without carving. By this late Southern Tang period, structural decoration and art had lost their prosperous-era grandeur.

projects.name: 定林寺塔
projects.level: 第三批江苏省文物保护单位（1982年）
projects.level_en: 3rd Batch Jiangsu Provincial Cultural Heritage Site (1982)
projects.address_en: Northwest of Fangshan, Jiangning District
highlights: 南宋乾道九年建
八面七层仿木楼阁式砖塔
向北倾斜
底层石雕须弥座
projects.content_zh: 定林寺始建于南朝刘宋时期，原在钟山，南宋乾道九年（1173年）在方山重建定林寺，称上定林寺，在钟山者为下定林寺。后寺庙全毁，仅余佛塔。该塔位于寺西，由于屡遭兵燹，年久失修，塔顶、塔刹和腰檐皆毁，塔体大幅向北倾斜。定林寺塔高14.5米，底层直径3.45米，为八面七层仿木楼阁式砖塔。塔身内部一、二层为方筒形，三层以上为圆筒形。底层南面开门，内设石雕须弥座，东、西、北三面有佛龛，其后辟窗。塔内无楼梯，不可登临，第五层设有木架承塔刹刹杆。塔身各面有石砌仿木柱枋斗栱和平座，伸出石质仿木挑檐，大部分石椽和屋檐已毁，仅余檐脊向外伸出。
projects.content_en: Dinglin Temple was first built during the Liu Song period of the Southern Dynasties, originally on Zhongshan Mountain. In the 9th year of Qiandao of the Southern Song (1173), Dinglin Temple was rebuilt on Fangshan, called the Upper Dinglin Temple, while the one on Zhongshan was the Lower Dinglin Temple. Later the temple was entirely destroyed, leaving only the pagoda. Located west of the temple, the pagoda suffered repeated warfare and long neglect; its top, spire, and waist eaves were all destroyed, and the body tilts significantly northward. The Dinglin Temple Pagoda is 14.5m high, with a base diameter of 3.45m, an octagonal seven-story imitation-wood pavilion-style brick pagoda. The interior of the first and second stories is square-tube shaped; above the third story it is cylindrical. The ground floor has a door on the south with a stone-carved Sumeru pedestal inside; the east, west, and north sides have Buddha niches with windows behind them. There are no stairs inside, so it cannot be climbed; the fifth story has a wooden frame supporting the spire pole. Each face of the pagoda body has stone imitation-wood pillars, architraves, dougong, and pingzuo (balcony), with stone imitation-wood overhanging eaves; most stone rafters and eaves are destroyed, leaving only eave ridges protruding outward.

projects.name: 杨柳村古建筑群
projects.level: 第七批全国重点文物保护单位（2013年）
projects.level_en: 7th Batch National Key Cultural Heritage Site (2013)

projects.address_en: Yangliu Village, Hushu Subdistrict, Jiangning District
highlights: 朱姓家族所建
36座宅院
多进穿堂院落式
三堂上（思承堂/礼和堂/树德堂）
阳雕砖刻文字
projects.content_zh: 杨柳村民居群为杨柳村朱姓家族所建，以杨柳湖为基准，由南向北依次为前村、中村和后村，现存建筑主要位于前村。前杨柳村民居群始建于明万历七年（1579年），主体建于清乾隆、嘉庆年间。先后建成36座宅院，目前保留较完整的有17座，均为多进穿堂院落式民居，最多的翼圣堂达七进。院落布局基本为沿中轴布置门厅、轿厅和住宅，两翼布置客厅、书房、陪房、厨房及杂屋等，后部院落多采用二楼四面可连通的走马楼。原宅院间有门相通或以青石板路相连，每座院落前设门楼，门上有人物、花卉和瑞兽等砖雕图案，并镶嵌四字堂训，门窗格扇也有雕刻美观的图案。目前杨柳村保存最完好的是村西的一组民居，系清乾隆年间朱候昌出资修建，包括思承堂、礼和堂和树德堂，三堂并立，连为一体，俗称"三堂上"，是杨柳村民居群中建造最晚的建筑。其中思承堂和礼和堂均为三路三进，37间房，西边的树德堂有四进41间房。每组院落都有一座高大的门楼，砖雕精美生动，门上皆有阳雕砖刻文字，分别是"缓步凝思""斯道坦然"和"遵循韦训"等。新中国成立初期三堂上曾作为海军医院和杨柳中学使用。
projects.content_en: The Yangliu Village residential complex was built by the Zhu family of Yangliu Village, with Yangliu Lake as the reference point. From south to north are Qian Village, Zhong Village, and Hou Village; surviving buildings are mainly in Qian Village. The Qian Yangliu Village residential group was first built in the 7th year of Wanli of the Ming (1579), with the main buildings constructed during the Qianlong and Jiaqing reigns of the Qing. Thirty-six courtyard houses were built successively; 17 remain relatively intact today, all multi-courtyard through-hall residences, with the largest, Yisheng Hall, having seven courtyards. The courtyard layout generally places the entrance hall, sedan chair hall, and residence along the central axis, with living rooms, studies, attendant rooms, kitchens, and utility rooms on both wings; rear courtyards often use two-story "zouma towers" (galleries) connected on all four sides. Original courtyards were connected by doors or bluestone paths; each had a tall gate tower with brick-carved patterns of figures, flowers, and auspicious beasts, inlaid with four-character family mottoes, and beautifully carved lattice doors and windows. The best-preserved group in Yangliu Village is a set of residences in the west of the village, funded by Zhu Houchang during the Qianlong reign, including Sicheng Hall, Lihe Hall, and Shude Hall—three halls standing side by side and connected, commonly called "Santangshang" (Three Halls Above), the latest-built buildings in the Yangliu residential group. Sicheng Hall and Lihe Hall each have three lanes and three courtyards with 37 rooms; the western Shude Hall has four courtyards with 41 rooms. Each courtyard group has a tall gate tower with exquisite vivid brick carvings; the gates bear raised brick-carved inscriptions: "Walk slowly and meditate," "This path is calm," and "Follow the teachings of Wei," respectively. In the early years of New China, the Three Halls served as a naval hospital and Yangliu Middle School.

projects.name: 高淳保圣寺塔
projects.level: 第三批江苏省文物保护单位（1982年）
projects.level_en: 3rd Batch Jiangsu Provincial Cultural Heritage Site (1982)
projects.address_en: Baota Town, Gaochun District
highlights: 三国东吴赤乌二年始建
南宋绍兴四年重建
四面七层楼阁式
鸳鸯交首栱
projects.content_zh: 保圣寺始建于三国东吴赤乌二年（239年），唐贞元十七年（801年）改建，称龙城寺。北宋大中祥符年间（1008—1016）始称保圣寺。现寺庙已毁，塔为宋绍兴四年（1134年）重建，明清多次维修，1974年重修塔顶，1985年大修，更换了多处塔身部件，但主体和大部分构件仍为宋构。保圣寺塔是一座四面七层楼阁式塔，塔身用青砖砌筑，外有平缓的木檐。塔高31.5米，每边5.43米。塔身无底座，底层有深远披檐外廊。塔身转角处设角柱，不用柱础，柱间底部有地袱，柱顶有砖石阑额和砖雕斗栱。斗栱距离较密，横向均相连成鸳鸯交首栱形式，底层柱顶阑额间雕刻一斗三升斗栱形象。拱间壁原有砖雕佛像，现已无存。塔身底层和七层开四门，其余各层皆相对开两门，上下相闪。塔内为四方塔室，二、三层因高度较大，置有夹层，塔内架木梯，可登临至塔顶。
projects.content_en: Baosheng Temple was first built in the 2nd year of Chiwu of the Eastern Wu (239), rebuilt in the 17th year of Zhenyuan of the Tang (801) and called Longcheng Temple. It was first called Baosheng Temple during the Dazhong Xiangfu period of the Northern Song (1008-1016). The temple is now destroyed; the pagoda was rebuilt in the 4th year of Shaoxing of the Song (1134), repaired multiple times in the Ming and Qing, with the top rebuilt in 1974 and a major repair in 1985 replacing many body components, but the main body and most components remain Song structures. The Baosheng Temple Pagoda is a four-sided seven-story pavilion-style pagoda, with a body built of blue bricks and gentle wooden eaves outside. It is 31.5m high, 5.43m on each side. The body has no base; the ground floor has a deep overhanging eave corridor. Corner pillars are set at the body corners without pillar bases; between pillars at the bottom are ground sills, and at pillar tops are brick-stone architraves and brick-carved dougong. The dougong are densely spaced and transversely connected in the "yuanyang jiaoshou gong" (mandarin duck interlocking bracket) form; between the ground-floor pillar-top architraves are carved one-dou-three-sheng dougong forms. The walls between brackets originally had brick-carved Buddha statues, now gone. The ground floor and seventh story have four doors; the other stories each have two opposite doors, alternating positions between stories. The interior is a square chamber; the second and third stories, being taller, have mezzanines, with wooden ladders inside allowing climbing to the top.

projects.name: 高淳周氏宗祠
projects.level: 第七批江苏省文物保护单位（2011年）
projects.level_en: 7th Batch Jiangsu Provincial Cultural Heritage Site (2011)
projects.address_en: Sanhe Village, Zhuanqiang Town, Gaochun County
highlights: 周瑜后裔所建
明万历三十四年建
世德堂
减柱抬梁造
二十四孝图木雕
projects.content_zh: 周氏宗祠为周瑜后裔于明万历三十四年（1606年）所建，又名"世德堂"，清乾隆八年（1743年）建门房连廊庑，清咸丰十年（1860年）被太平军烧毁，清光绪十七年（1891年）修建后进享堂。20世纪50年代曾作为供销社仓库。这处宗祠原有前后三进，现存清光绪年间修建的后进享堂。建筑座西北朝东南，采用砖木结构，青砖小瓦硬山顶。面阔五间17.8米，进深14米，脊高9.8米。内部用楠木柱和柏木梁，明间及次间梁架采用扁作，减柱抬梁造，四柱十三檩；稍间为八柱十一檩。建筑的梁枋、雀替和斗栱均浮雕图案，内容包括麒麟、凤戏牡丹等吉祥纹饰和二十四孝图、文王访贤等历史典故。刀法遒劲流畅，线条明快清晰。
projects.content_en: The Zhou Family Ancestral Shrine was built in the 34th year of Wanli of the Ming (1606) by descendants of Zhou Yu, also known as "Shide Hall" (Hall of Inherited Virtue). In the 8th year of Qianlong of the Qing (1743), the gatehouse with connecting corridors was built; in the 10th year of Xianfeng (1860) it was burned by Taiping forces; in the 17th year of Guangxu (1891) the rear worship hall was built. In the 1950s it served as a supply and marketing cooperative warehouse. The shrine originally had three front-to-back courtyards; only the rear worship hall built during the Guangxu period survives. The building faces southeast, with brick-wood structure, blue bricks, small tiles, and a gable roof. It is five bays wide (17.8m), 14m deep, with a ridge height of 9.8m. The interior uses nanmu pillars and cypress beams; the main and secondary bays use flat-beam construction with column reduction and tai-beam (raised beam) structure, four pillars and thirteen purlins; the end bays have eight pillars and eleven purlins. The beams, architraves, queti (spandrel brackets), and dougong all feature relief patterns, including auspicious decorations such as qilin and phoenix playing with peony, as well as historical allusions such as the Twenty-four Filial Exemplars and King Wen of Zhou visiting the worthy. The carving is vigorous and fluid, with clear and lively lines.

regions.name: 苏州
regions.overview: 苏州位于江苏省东南部，北滨长江，西临太湖，古称吴、姑苏和平江等，是吴文化的发源地，水土丰腴，从远古时期就成为长江流域重要的人类聚居地，后世长期保持富庶繁盛，人文气息浓厚，有"人间天堂""东方威尼斯"之誉。商朝末年，岐山周部落首领古公亶父的长子泰伯、次子仲雍为了避位让贤，千里南奔至长江南岸的梅里，在所谓的"荆蛮之地"创立"勾吴之国"。周朝建立后，武王封其五世孙周章为诸侯，正式建立吴国，逐渐强盛，与中原各国争霸。公元前560年，吴王诸樊迁都至现苏州城址。公元前514年，吴王阖闾对旧城大加扩建，后世以此为苏州正式建城之始，距今已经超过2500年，一直保持原地，堪称中国历史最悠久的城市之一。春秋后期和战国时期，吴地先后被越国和楚国吞并。秦代属于会稽郡，郡治设在吴县。西汉时期先后属于楚王、荆王和吴王封地，后仍属会稽郡。东汉时期在此设吴郡，三国时期归属孙吴政权统治。两晋南北朝时期变置不一，吴郡曾属扬州，后改吴州。隋代改称苏州，复改吴州、吴郡。唐代仍称苏州，先后属江南道、江南东道辖区。五代时期为吴越国统治区。北宋时期称平江府，府城平面图有碑刻传世，其格局与今日苏州古城相似。元代在此设平江路，属江淮行省，元末起义军领袖张士诚在此建立大周政权。明代改平江路为苏州府，隶属南直隶。清康熙六年（1667年）江苏建省，苏州城成为江苏巡抚、江苏布政使驻地，同时也是苏州府治和长洲、元和、吴县三县的县治，地位相当于省会，极为繁盛，下辖各县也都富甲四方。苏州地区的古城、古镇风貌犹存，其中姑苏区是苏州古城所在地，与常熟古城同被列为国家级历史文化名城。此外，昆山市的周庄、锦溪、千灯，吴江区的同里、震泽、黎里，吴中区的甪直、木渎、东山，太仓市的沙溪，常熟市的沙家浜，张家港市的凤凰等12座古镇被列为中国历史文化名镇，现存古建筑数量之多、密度之大，在全国范围内都相当罕见。苏州地区是著名的水乡，占有太湖四分之三的面积。境内河网密布，古城、古镇和许多古建筑依水而建。其中苏州古城拥有纵横交错的河道，与陆路共同形成两套交通系统，呈现出"河街相邻""人家尽枕河"的独特风貌，城内散布着大量的古代寺观、园林和民居，平江路、山塘街两个街区被列为中国十大历史文化名街，古韵浓厚，令人目不暇接。苏州是古典园林之乡，被誉为江南园林的最高代表，旧城内的拙政园、留园、狮子林、沧浪亭、网师园、艺圃和环秀山庄等名园已经列为世界文化遗产，此外同里古镇的退思园、常熟的燕园均为园亭佳作，建筑、掇山、理水和花木配植技艺精湛，妙造自然，成为其他地区竞相模仿的范本。苏州地区保存着较多的古代佛寺、道观和古塔，如戒幢律寺、开元寺、寒山寺、兴福寺、玄妙观和报恩寺塔、瑞光塔、虎丘塔、万佛石塔、罗汉院双塔、聚沙塔、楞伽寺塔等，反映了当地宗教文化的兴盛。这一区域有大量的古代府邸、民居留存至今，太平天国忠王府、吴宅、潘宅和俞樾故居等，无论是深宅大院还是咫尺小庭，均表现出粉墙黛瓦、清新雅致的特点，是中国古代住宅建筑的精华。除此之外，苏州地区的古城门、会馆、文庙和古桥也都是富有地方特色的建筑，不容错过。苏州今辖姑苏区（市政府驻地）、虎丘区、吴中区、相城区和吴江区5个区，代管常熟市、昆山市、太仓市和张家港市4个县级市，有国家级文物保护单位59处，省级文物保护单位114处，本书介绍国保建筑45处，省保建筑18处，其他建筑4处。
regions.overview_en: Suzhou is located in southeastern Jiangsu Province, bordering the Yangtze River to the north and Lake Tai to the west. Historically called Wu, Gusu, and Pingjiang, it is the birthplace of Wu culture. With fertile land and abundant water, it has been an important human settlement in the Yangtze River basin since ancient times, maintaining long-term prosperity and rich cultural atmosphere, earning the reputations "Paradise on Earth" and "Venice of the East." At the end of the Shang Dynasty, Taibo and Zhongyong—eldest and second sons of Gugong Danfu, leader of the Zhou tribe at Qishan—fled south to Meili on the south bank of the Yangtze to yield the throne to their younger brother Jili, founding the "Gouwu Kingdom" in the so-called "land of Jingman." After the Zhou Dynasty was established, King Wu enfeoffed Zhouzhang, their fifth-generation descendant, as a feudal lord, formally establishing the State of Wu, which gradually grew powerful and contended with the Central Plains states. In 560 BC, King Zhufan of Wu moved the capital to the present Suzhou city site. In 514 BC, King Helü of Wu greatly expanded the old city, later regarded as the official founding of Suzhou—over 2,500 years ago, continuously occupying the same site, making it one of China's oldest cities. In the late Spring and Autumn and Warring States periods, Wu was successively annexed by Yue and Chu. In the Qin Dynasty it belonged to Kuaiji Commandery with the seat at Wu County. In the Western Han it successively belonged to the fiefs of the King of Chu, King of Jing, and King of Wu, then remained under Kuaiji Commandery. In the Eastern Han, Wu Commandery was established here; during the Three Kingdoms it was ruled by the Sun Wu regime. During the Two Jin and Northern and Southern Dynasties, administrative changes were frequent; Wu Commandery was once under Yangzhou, later changed to Wu Prefecture. In the Sui Dynasty it was renamed Suzhou, then changed back to Wu Prefecture and Wu Commandery. In the Tang it remained Suzhou, successively under Jiangnan Circuit and Jiangnan East Circuit. During the Five Dynasties it was ruled by the Wuyue Kingdom. In the Northern Song it was called Pingjiang Prefecture, with a stone-carved map of the prefectural city surviving, its layout similar to today's Suzhou old city. In the Yuan Dynasty, Pingjiang Route was established here under Jianghuai Province; at the end of the Yuan, rebel leader Zhang Shicheng established the Great Zhou regime here. In the Ming, Pingjiang Route was changed to Suzhou Prefecture under Nanzhili (South Zhili). In the 6th year of Kangxi (1667) of the Qing, Jiangsu Province was established, and Suzhou city became the seat of the Jiangsu Governor and Jiangsu Administrative Commissioner, as well as the seat of Suzhou Prefecture and the three counties of Changzhou, Yuanhe, and Wu—equivalent to a provincial capital, extremely prosperous, with all subordinate counties wealthy. The ancient cities and towns of the Suzhou region retain their historic character. Gusu District is the location of Suzhou's old city, listed as a national historical and cultural city together with the old city of Changshu. Additionally, 12 ancient towns have been listed as Chinese historical and cultural towns: Zhouzhuang, Jinxi, and Qiandeng in Kunshan; Tongli, Zhenze, and Lili in Wujiang; Luzhi, Mudu, and Dongshan in Wuzhong; Shaxi in Taicang; Shajiabang in Changshu; and Fenghuang in Zhangjiagang. The number and density of surviving ancient buildings here are rare nationwide. The Suzhou region is a famous water town, occupying three-quarters of Lake Tai. The river network is dense; ancient cities, towns, and many buildings are built along water. Suzhou's old city has crisscrossing waterways forming two transportation systems with land roads, presenting the unique features of "river and street adjacent" and "every family resting by the river," with numerous ancient temples, gardens, and residences scattered within. Pingjiang Road and Shantang Street are listed among China's Top Ten Historical and Cultural Streets, with rich ancient charm. Suzhou is the home of classical gardens, hailed as the highest representative of Jiangnan gardens. Famous gardens in the old city—Humble Administrator's Garden, Lingering Garden, Lion Grove Garden, Surging Wave Pavilion, Master of Nets Garden, Garden of Cultivation, and Mountain Villa with Embracing Beauty—are listed as World Cultural Heritage. Additionally, the Retreat and Reflection Garden in Tongli ancient town and Yan Garden in Changshu are both masterpieces, with exquisite architecture, rockery piling, water management, and plant arrangement, creating nature artificially and becoming models imitated elsewhere. The Suzhou region preserves many ancient Buddhist temples, Taoist temples, and pagodas, such as Jiechuanglü Temple, Kaiyuan Temple, Hanshan Temple, Xingfu Temple, Xuanmiao Temple, and the Bao'en Temple Pagoda, Ruiguang Pagoda, Huqiu Pagoda, Ten-Thousand-Buddha Stone Pagoda, Luohan Yuan Twin Pagodas, Jusha Pagoda, and Lengjia Temple Pagoda, reflecting the flourishing of local religious culture. This region has a large number of ancient mansions and residences surviving to this day, including the Taiping Heavenly Kingdom Loyal King's Palace, Wu Residence, Pan Residence, and Yu Yue's Former Residence—whether deep courtyard mansions or tiny courtyards, all display the features of whitewashed walls and dark tiles, fresh and elegant, representing the essence of ancient Chinese residential architecture. In addition, the ancient city gates, guildhalls, Confucian temples, and old bridges of the Suzhou region are all distinctive local buildings not to be missed. Suzhou currently administers 5 districts—Gusu (municipal government seat), Huqiu, Wuzhong, Xiangcheng, and Wujiang—and manages 4 county-level cities: Changshu, Kunshan, Taicang, and Zhangjiagang. It has 59 national and 114 provincial cultural heritage protection units; this book introduces 45 national protected buildings, 18 provincial protected buildings, and 4 other buildings.

明正德五年王献臣建
文徵明《王氏拙政园记》
东园（远香堂、见山楼）
