西天寺兜率宫极乐园
六处藻井
projects.content_zh: 寂鉴寺位于吴中区藏书镇天池山坞，内有3座元代石殿。该寺前身先后为南朝刘宋会稽太守张裕私第、南宋秘书监张廷杰别业，有天池十八景。元至正十七年（1357年）创建寂鉴禅庵，明弘治年间天目禅师普惠重修，更名华山天池院。寺庙平面呈椭圆形。最南侧为山门，1980年重建，只有抱鼓石是原物。门外两侧各有一座石屋，皆为坐南朝北的巨型佛龛。东为兜率宫，南侧巨石上雕2.55米高弥勒像，北侧覆一间单檐歇山顶石屋。西为极乐园，内供2.6米高阿弥陀佛立像，下有须弥座，上立石柱、石墙、石门窗隔扇及重檐歇山顶，屋脊有吻兽，平远较兜率宫精细。山门内是三开间的西天寺石殿，平面呈凸字形，南为单檐歇山顶，后出抱厦与北部山岩相接，有工字殿的意味。殿内分成前后两进，前部为祭祀活动场所，后部为佛龛和供案。室内顶部有六处藻井，以明间佛龛上部的最为华美，自下而上由方形、斗八和圆形藻井层层构成。寂鉴寺三座石殿是全国仅存的元代仿木石构建筑，内部石刻佛像精美，具有重要的建筑和雕塑价值。
projects.content_en: Jijian Temple is located in the Tianchi Mountain valley of Cangshu Town, Wuzhong District, containing three Yuan-dynasty stone halls. The temple's predecessors were successively the private residence of Zhang Yu, Governor of Kuaiji in the Liu Song of the Southern Dynasties, and the villa of Zhang Tingjie, Secretary of the Southern Song, with the Eighteen Scenes of Tianchi. In the 17th year of Zhizheng of the Yuan (1357), the Jijian Chan Nunnery was founded; during the Hongzhi reign of the Ming, Master Tianmu Puhui repaired it and renamed it Huashan Tianchi Courtyard. The temple has an oval plan. At the southernmost is the gate, rebuilt in 1980, with only the drum-shaped bearing stones being original. Outside the gate on both sides are stone houses, both giant Buddhist niches facing south toward north. The east is the Tusita Palace, with a 2.55-meter Maitreya statue carved on the huge stone to the south, and a single-eave hip-and-gable roof stone house covering the north. The west is the Bliss Garden, enshrining a 2.6-meter standing Amitabha statue, with a Sumeru pedestal below and stone columns, walls, door-window lattice, and double-eave hip-and-gable roof above, with roof ornaments on the ridge—more refined than the Tusita Palace. Inside the gate is the three-bay Western Heaven Temple stone hall, with a convex (凸) plan; the south has a single-eave hip-and-gable roof, with a rear portico connecting to the northern mountain rock, resembling an I-shaped hall. The interior is divided into front and rear sections: the front is for sacrificial activities, the rear for Buddhist niches and offering tables. There are six caisson ceilings inside, the most magnificent above the central bay's Buddhist niche, composed layer by layer from below upward of square, douba (eight-sided), and circular caissons. The three stone halls of Jijian Temple are the only surviving Yuan-dynasty wooden-imitating stone buildings in China, with exquisitely carved stone Buddha statues inside, having important architectural and sculptural value.

projects.name: 万佛石塔
projects.level: 第七批全国重点文物保护单位（2013年）
projects.level_en: 7th Batch National Key Cultural Heritage Site (2013)
projects.address_en: Xijing Village, Zhenhu Township, Wu County
highlights: 南宋绍兴年间始建
元大德十年重建
原名禅师塔
塔内须弥座上万余尊小佛像
仿印度窣堵坡单层方塔
总高10.8米
projects.content_zh: 万佛石塔始建于南宋绍兴年间，元大德十年（1306年）重建，原名禅师塔，因塔内须弥座上刻有万余尊小佛像，得名万佛石塔。此塔由台基、塔身和塔刹组成，总高10.8米，是一座仿印度窣堵坡的单层方塔，形制罕见。台基为长方形，南侧设宽约1米的如意踏跺。塔身位于台北侧，形如覆斗，底边宽3.3米，顶边宽2.8米，角部有四根方石柱向内倾斜支撑横梁，其上叠砌平台。平台上立塔刹，由石刻宝瓶、覆钵和相轮组成，正方形的塔檐微微上翘，覆盖着其下石座四面的佛像。塔身南侧辟火焰状的喇嘛塔式眼光门，内部为穹窿式洞窟，上小下大，底部有1.7米高的须弥座，座上环砌十层武康石，刻60排小型坐佛像，每排180余尊，共计10000余尊，每尊高约5厘米，宽约3厘米，小巧精美。北壁正对塔门是一尊高30厘米、宽20厘米的主像。
projects.content_en: The Ten Thousand-Buddha Stone Pagoda was first built during the Shaoxing reign of the Southern Song, rebuilt in the 10th year of Dade of the Yuan (1306), originally named the Chan Master Pagoda. Because over ten thousand small Buddha statues are carved on the Sumeru pedestal inside, it is named the Ten Thousand-Buddha Stone Pagoda. This pagoda consists of a platform base, pagoda body, and finial, with a total height of 10.8 meters. It is a single-story square pagoda imitating the Indian stupa, with a rare form. The platform base is rectangular, with a 1-meter-wide ruyi-shaped step on the south side. The pagoda body is on the north side of the platform, shaped like an inverted funnel (fudu), with a bottom width of 3.3 meters and top width of 2.8 meters. At the corners, four square stone pillars tilt inward to support the beams, above which a platform is laid. On the platform stands the finial, composed of a stone vase, inverted bowl, and chatra (umbrella); the square pagoda eave turns slightly upward, covering the Buddha statues on the four sides of the stone base below. On the south side of the pagoda body, a flame-shaped Tibetan-style light gate is opened; the interior is a domed cave, smaller at top and larger at bottom, with a 1.7-meter-high Sumeru pedestal at the base. Around the pedestal, ten layers of Wukang stone are laid, carved with 60 rows of small seated Buddha statues, over 180 per row, totaling over 10,000 statues, each about 5 cm high and 3 cm wide—small and exquisite. On the north wall facing the pagoda gate is a main statue 30 cm high and 20 cm wide.

projects.name: 天平山
projects.level: 第四批江苏省保（1982年）
projects.level_en: 4th Batch Jiangsu Provincial Protected Site (1982)
projects.address_en: 15 km west of Suzhou city
highlights: 范仲淹家族家山
北宋景祐年间宋仁宗赐山
万笏朝天奇石林立
白云泉镇山名泉
天平三绝
高义园乾隆十六年赐名
projects.content_zh: 天平山与以范仲淹（989—1052）为代表的范氏家族关系密切。范仲淹是苏州吴县人，先祖葬在天平山下，北宋景祐年间宋仁宗将此山赐给他作为家山。南宋绍兴年间苏州士绅在天平山西麓为范仲淹建忠烈庙，此后多次重修。从东南侧大门进入，沿中轴线依次有"先忧后乐"牌坊（1989年新建）、仪门、石桥、享堂和三太师祠。庙南为近年新建的范仲淹纪念馆。庙北有大片枫林，是明万历年间范仲淹的后人范允临（1558—1641）从福建移植而来，迄今已有400多年，每到仲秋，枫红如火，成为天平山的一大胜景。枫林东南立乾隆御碑亭，题有乾隆四次游览天平山的诗文。枫林西侧是白云庵，始建于唐宝历二年（826年），北宋庆历四年（1044年）范仲淹奏请改名"功德香院"，成为范氏家庵。明万历年间范允临重建，今为清同治年间范学炳重建，内有三间主殿。从白云庵向上可登天平山顶，沿路有更衣亭、鹦鹉石和一线天等景点。其中白云泉水味甘洌，得到白居易、范仲淹等人品题，为镇山名泉；"万笏朝天"奇石林立，有如朝臣所用的笏板，极为罕见，二者与山下的古枫并称为"天平三绝"。白云庵北侧为高义园，明万历年间范允临建，原名天平山庄。建成后范允临携妻子徐媛宴请四方宾客，遨游山水胜景，名扬吴中。晚明名士张岱曾被邀请游园，在《陶庵梦忆》里描述园景："进门则长廊复道，直达山麓……山之左为桃源，峭壁回湍，桃花片片流出。右孤山，种梅千树。渡涧为小兰亭，茂林修竹，曲水流觞，件件有之。"明清之际山庄废圮，清康熙、乾隆年间范氏后人两次重修，乾隆十六年（1751年）乾隆驾临山庄，赐名高义园。此园依山而筑，背倚"万笏朝天"，层层抬升。最前方为清乾隆十六年（1751年）所立四柱三间冲天式汉白玉牌坊，向西为接驾亭。穿过长堤是主体庭院，有轿厅、乐天楼、逍遥亭和正殿共四进，正殿内悬御匾"高义园"。园内建筑白墙黛瓦，与其北咒钵庵的黄墙黛瓦倒映在前方的十景塘中，景色秀美。此外周围还有来燕榭、桃花涧和范坟群等景点。
projects.content_en: Tianping Mountain is closely related to the Fan family, represented by Fan Zhongyan (989-1052). Fan Zhongyan was a native of Wu County, Suzhou; his ancestors were buried at the foot of Tianping Mountain. During the Jingyou reign of the Northern Song, Emperor Renzong bestowed this mountain on him as a family mountain. During the Shaoxing reign of the Southern Song, Suzhou gentry built the Zhonglie (Loyal Martyr) Temple for Fan Zhongyan at the western foot of Tianping Mountain, subsequently repaired multiple times. Entering from the southeast gate, along the central axis are successively the "First Worry, Later Joy" memorial archway (newly built in 1989), ceremonial gate, stone bridge, offering hall, and Three Grand Tutor Shrine. South of the temple is the Fan Zhongyan Memorial Hall built in recent years. North of the temple is a large maple forest, transplanted from Fujian by Fan Zhongyan's descendant Fan Yunlin (1558-1641) during the Wanli reign of the Ming—now over 400 years old. Every mid-autumn, the maples turn red like fire, becoming a major scenic spot of Tianping Mountain. Southeast of the maple forest stands the Qianlong Imperial Stele Pavilion, inscribed with poems and prose from Qianlong's four visits to Tianping Mountain. West of the maple forest is the Baiyun Nunnery, first built in the 2nd year of Baoli of the Tang (826); in the 4th year of Qingli of the Northern Song (1044), Fan Zhongyan petitioned to rename it "Merit and Virtue Fragrant Courtyard," becoming the Fan family nunnery. Rebuilt by Fan Yunlin during the Wanli reign of the Ming; today it was rebuilt by Fan Xuebing during the Tongzhi reign of the Qing, with three main bays inside. From Baiyun Nunnery upward, one can climb to the top of Tianping Mountain, with scenic spots along the way such as the Changing Clothes Pavilion, Parrot Rock, and Thread of Sky. Among them, Baiyun Spring has sweet, clear water, praised by Bai Juyi, Fan Zhongyan, and others—a famous spring guarding the mountain; the "Wanhu Chaotian" (Ten Thousand Tablets Facing Heaven) strange rocks stand in clusters, like the hu tablets used by court officials—extremely rare. These two, together with the ancient maples at the foot of the mountain, are called the "Three Wonders of Tianping." North of Baiyun Nunnery is Gaoyi Garden (High Righteousness Garden), built by Fan Yunlin during the Wanli reign of the Ming, originally named Tianping Mountain Villa. After completion, Fan Yunlin and his wife Xu Yuan entertained guests from all directions, roaming the scenic mountains and waters, becoming famous in Wu. Late-Ming scholar Zhang Dai was once invited to visit the garden and described its scenery in "Tao'an Dream Memories": "Entering the gate, long corridors and repeated paths lead directly to the mountain foot... left of the mountain is the Peach Blossom Spring, with sheer cliffs and rushing currents, peach blossom petals flowing out. Right is the Solitary Mountain, planted with a thousand plum trees. Crossing the stream is the Small Orchid Pavilion, with lush forests and tall bamboos, winding water for floating wine cups—everything is there." At the Ming-Qing transition the villa fell into ruin; during the Kangxi and Qianlong reigns of the Qing, Fan descendants rebuilt it twice. In the 16th year of Qianlong (1751), Qianlong visited the villa and bestowed the name Gaoyi Garden. This garden is built against the mountain, backed by the "Ten Thousand Tablets Facing Heaven," rising level by level. At the very front is a four-pillar, three-bay, sky-reaching white marble archway erected in the 16th year of Qianlong (1751); west is the Jieja Pavilion (Receiving the Emperor Pavilion). Crossing the long embankment is the main courtyard, with four bays: sedan hall, Letian Tower, Xiaoyao Pavilion, and main hall; the main hall hangs the imperial plaque "Gaoyi Garden." The garden buildings have white walls and dark tiles, which, together with the yellow walls and dark tiles of the Zhoubo Nunnery to its north, are reflected in the Ten-Scenery Pond in front—beautiful scenery. Additionally, there are scenic spots such as the Laiyan Pavilion, Peach Blossom Stream, and Fan family tombs.

projects.name: 木渎镇
projects.level: 中国历史文化名镇
projects.level_en: Chinese Historical and Cultural Town
projects.address_en: Mudu Town, Wuzhong District
highlights: 严家花园羡园
虹饮山房乾隆南巡驻跸
古松园明代罗汉松
榜眼府第冯桂芬故居
灵岩山吴王姑苏台
秀野园沈寿
projects.content_zh: 木渎镇是苏州著名的历史文化名镇，拥有多处古典园林和历史遗迹。1. 严家花园（羡园）：严家花园位于山塘街北，最初是清乾隆年间沈德潜（1673—1769）的寓所，清道光八年（1828年）归钱端溪，开池叠山改筑为端园。后又售予严国馨（1826—1905），清光绪二十八年（1902年）严氏聘请香山帮名匠姚承祖修葺一新，改称羡园，俗称严家花园。1958年在园内大炼钢铁，后又建农机厂，羡园被拆成平地，1999年在原址重建。此园坐北朝南，中部为住宅，包括门厅、怡宾厅、尚贤堂、明是楼和眺农楼；环宅三面为花园，采用春、夏、秋、冬主题，用青石和黄石叠筑四季假山。2. 虹饮山房：由羡园沿山塘街向东约300米为虹饮山房，清乾隆年间徐士元建。乾隆南巡经木渎曾驻跸在虹饮山房，其南临河建有御码头和石构的怡泉亭（市保单位）。虹饮山房包括三路，中路为住宅，沿轴线依次布置门厅、舞彩堂和春晖楼戏台，东、西两路为花园。东路花园原为明代李氏的小隐园，徐士元加以改筑，清末归陈氏，"绣圣"沈寿（1874—1921）是陈家的外孙女，幼年在此生活，今园中建有沈寿纪念馆。西路花园在明代是刑部侍郎王心一的秀野园。王心一在苏州拙政园东建有归田园居，后来喜爱木渎的幽静，又在此建造别业。今园中有与皇家相关的圣旨馆、科举制度馆和宫廷用品馆等。3. 古松园：紧邻虹饮山房东侧为古松园，原为清末蔡少渔的住宅，1998年在宅后扩建园林。住宅中轴包括门厅、轿厅、古松堂和凤凰楼。凤凰楼向东隔水有一株明代罗汉松，园林由此得名。水池贯穿全园，沿池布置建筑，堆叠假山，较为精雅。4. 榜眼府第：榜眼府第位于下塘街，是林则徐的弟子冯桂芬（1809—1874）故居，冯氏中清道光二十年（1840年）一甲二名，因而得名。府第采用前宅后园格局。住宅现存门厅、大厅显志堂和后部芙蓉楼共三进，今为冯桂芬纪念馆和周士心美术馆。后部花园围绕荷花池布置亭廊桥榭，在园北假山顶部的含山亭可眺望灵岩山。5. 灵岩山：沿山塘街向西，灵岩山入口在灵天路与中山西路交叉口处，门票20元，开放时间8:30—16:30。山内有吴王姑苏台、清代状元毕沅的灵岩山馆和清代诗人张永夫纪念馆等景点。山下有流水清池，沿路登山，则可寻访馆娃宫、西施洞和琴台等春秋时期的遗迹。
projects.content_en: Mudu Town is a famous historical and cultural town in Suzhou, with numerous classical gardens and historical relics. 1. Yan Family Garden (Xianyuan): Located north of Shantang Street, originally the residence of Shen Deqian (1673-1769) during the Qianlong reign of the Qing. In the 8th year of Daoguang (1828), it passed to Qian Duanxi, who dug ponds and piled rockeries to rebuild it as Duanyuan (Duan Garden). Later sold to Yan Guoxin (1826-1905); in the 28th year of Guangxu (1902), the Yan family hired Xiangshan master craftsman Yao Chengzu to renovate it completely, renaming it Xianyuan (Admiration Garden), commonly called Yan Family Garden. In 1958, steel was smelted in the garden, and later an agricultural machinery factory was built, with Xianyuan demolished to flat ground; rebuilt on the original site in 1999. This garden faces south, with the residence in the center including the gate hall, Yibin Hall, Shangxian Hall, Mingshi Tower, and Tiaonong Tower; the garden surrounds the residence on three sides, using spring, summer, autumn, and winter themes, with bluestone and yellow stone piled into four-season rockeries. 2. Hongyin Shanfang (Rainbow Drinking Mountain Villa): About 300 meters east along Shantang Street from Xianyuan is Hongyin Shanfang, built by Xu Shiyuan during the Qianlong reign of the Qing. When Qianlong's southern tour passed through Mudu, he stayed at Hongyin Shanfang; on its south side facing the river are an imperial dock and the stone-structured Yiquan Pavilion (municipal protected unit). Hongyin Shanfang includes three roads; the middle road is the residence, with the gate hall, Wucai Hall, and Chunhui Tower stage arranged along the axis; the east and west roads are gardens. The east garden was originally the Xiaoyin Garden of the Ming-dynasty Li family, modified by Xu Shiyuan; in the late Qing it passed to the Chen family. The "Embroidery Sage" Shen Shou (1874-1921) was the Chen family's granddaughter, living here as a child; today the Shen Shou Memorial Hall is in the garden. The west garden was the Xiuye Garden of Wang Xinyi, Vice Minister of Justice in the Ming. Wang Xinyi built the Gui Tian Yuan Ju east of Suzhou's Humble Administrator's Garden, and later, loving the tranquility of Mudu, built another villa here. Today the garden contains the Imperial Edict Hall, Imperial Examination System Hall, and Court Supplies Hall related to the imperial family. 3. Ancient Pine Garden: Immediately east of Hongyin Shanfang is the Ancient Pine Garden, originally the residence of Cai Shaoyu in the late Qing, with the garden expanded behind the residence in 1998. The residential central axis includes the gate hall, sedan hall, Ancient Pine Hall, and Phoenix Tower. East of the Phoenix Tower across water is a Ming-dynasty Buddhist pine (arhat pine), from which the garden takes its name. A pond runs through the entire garden, with buildings arranged along the pond and rockeries piled—quite elegant. 4. Bangyan Fudi (Second-place Graduate Mansion): Located on Xiatang Street, this is the former residence of Feng Guifen (1809-1874), a disciple of Lin Zexu. Feng won the second place (bangyan) in the 20th year of Daoguang of the Qing (1840), hence the name. The mansion adopts a front-residence, rear-garden layout. The residence survives in three bays: gate hall, main hall Xianzhi Hall, and rear Hibiscus Tower—today the Feng Guifen Memorial Hall and Zhou Shixin Art Museum. The rear garden arranges pavilions, corridors, bridges, and terraces around a lotus pond; the Hanshan Pavilion at the top of the north rockery offers views of Lingyan Mountain. 5. Lingyan Mountain: West along Shantang Street, the Lingyan Mountain entrance is at the intersection of Lingtian Road and West Zhongshan Road, admission 20 yuan, open 8:30-16:30. Inside the mountain are scenic spots such as the King of Wu's Gusu Terrace, the Lingyan Mountain Villa of Qing-dynasty zhuangyuan Bi Yuan, and the Memorial Hall of Qing-dynasty poet Zhang Yongfu. At the foot of the mountain are flowing water and clear ponds; climbing along the path, one can visit Spring and Autumn period relics such as the Guanwa Palace, Xishi Cave, and Qin (Zither) Terrace.

projects.name: 东山镇
projects.level: 中国历史文化名镇，4处国保（雕花楼、紫金庵、轩辕宫、东山民居）
projects.level_en: Chinese Historical and Cultural Town, 4 National Protected Sites
projects.address_en: Dongshan Town, Wuzhong District
highlights: 雕花楼江南第一楼
紫金庵南宋雷潮夫妇塑十六罗汉
轩辕宫元代断梁殿
东山民居明代建筑群
陆巷古村
启园
projects.content_zh: 东山又名东洞庭山，位于苏州西南，太湖东岸，最高峰为莫厘峰，与西洞庭山的缥缈峰东西相望。东山拥有4处国保：以雕刻艺术著称的民国雕花楼（春在楼），供有南宋彩塑罗汉的紫金庵，建于元代的轩辕宫，以及位于杨湾古街的明代民居明善堂、凝德堂和怀荫堂；6处省保：瑞霭堂、念勤堂楠木厅、诸公井亭、务本堂、绍德堂和三山古文化遗址；11处市保及100余处明清古建筑。与东山镇隔水相望的是西山镇。东山以名胜古迹居多，西山则以自然风光取胜，但也有栖贤巷门、锦绣堂、涵村店铺和仁本堂等省保建筑。1. 雕花楼（春在楼）：雕花楼主体建筑群坐西朝东，南北共三路。中路为雕花楼，自东向西依次为照壁、门楼、前厅、后厅和厨房餐厅；北路为花园，南路为状元府。雕花楼建于民国年间，集砖雕、木雕、金雕、石雕、泥塑于一体，是苏州香山帮工匠的杰作，被誉为"江南第一楼"。雕花楼的雕饰和格局充分体现了富商的品位和需求。雕饰内容皆含吉祥寓意。门楼前地面用碎石铺砌"瓶生三戟"，即"平升三级"，祈求升官富贵。门楼布满砖雕，以内侧为例：下枋刻"郭子仪上寿"，其上立福、禄、寿三星雕像；中枋镶蝠边砖额"聿修厥德"，左右兜肚分别为"尧舜禅让""文王访贤"圆雕，其上为横幅圆雕"福鹿十景"；上枋为"八仙庆寿"圆雕，其上垫拱板有五处透雕，正中为双喜，两侧为如意和绳带，比喻如意传代。屋顶垂脊塑天官赐福和鲤鱼跃龙门，正脊立植有万年青的青瓷聚宝盆。木雕主要集中在前厅和后厅。前厅为五间两层硬山造，是举办婚丧大礼和接待贵客之所，雕刻最多，堪称"江南满堂木雕"的代表作。梁上有48则黄杨木雕《三国演义》；月梁两端雕凤凰，全厅共86对，取其谐音"百乐"；前檐长窗和半窗的裙板上刻"二十四孝"。后厅是女眷的活动中心，主要刻《西厢记》故事。雕花楼的雕饰特点被总结为：出门有喜、进门有宝、抬头有寿、回头有官、伸手有钱和脚踏有福，充满了对福寿富贵的直白祈望。雕花楼的建筑布局主要依据现实需求。前厅一层为行礼和待客之所，后厅一层为内眷活动场所，两厅二层连通为走马楼，布置卧室和客房。前厅南侧藏有保险柜，后厅暗藏三层，储存奇珍异宝，以防强盗劫掠。一方面主人通过精美的雕饰炫耀富贵，一方面又绞尽脑汁保藏财富，求贵守富的复杂人性在雕花楼中展露无遗。北路的花园有山有水，四组湖石假山多依墙叠筑，与曲池体现趣味。湖石重形象欣赏，模仿熊、象、鹰、鼠等，体现世俗趣味。西端尽处是一座二层佛楼，为家中女眷烧香念佛之所。南路状元府有宅有园，展览东山的科举文化。2. 紫金庵罗汉塑像：紫金庵位于东洞庭山的西卯坞内，创建于唐初，盛唐和南宋两次大修，明初重建，清乾隆年间又有扩建。今头山门位于西南角，入门一直前行，左侧可见二山门。庵内主体建筑群坐北朝南，依次为二山门、罗汉殿和净因堂。西侧附属有晴川轩、白云居和听松堂等。整组建筑面积不大，簇拥在苍松翠竹间，古朴典雅。庵内最著名的是塑于南宋年间的十六罗汉（一堂），与济南长清灵岩寺的四十罗汉（一堂）、甪直保圣寺的九罗汉（半堂），合称"天下罗汉二堂半"。罗汉殿内面南正中为释迦三世佛，其间侍立迦叶、阿难二弟子；面北正中为望海观音金身像。十六罗汉分立在东、西两壁下，各有八尊。他们出自南宋雕塑名家雷潮夫妇之手，是二人的巅峰之作，清康熙《苏州府志》称："（紫金庵）内大士及罗汉像，系雷潮装塑。潮夫妇俱称善手，一生止塑三处，本庵尤为称首。"清人邱赓熙对紫金庵罗汉评价极高，他曾遍游苏杭的名山古寺，所见罗汉像往往高且大，而从未有"精神超乎、呼之欲活如金庵者"（《紫金庵净因堂记》）。这一评价点出了紫金庵罗汉的两大特点：一是与借助高大显示神威的惯用手法不同，紫金庵罗汉与真人大小相仿，坐像多在1.2米左右，头部、身体和手足的比例恰当协调。二是这16尊罗汉将神像人性化，通过不同的容貌、迥异的神情，赋予他们丰富的情感和性格。如第一尊者长眉罗汉，手撩长眉（已失），含笑侧坐，体现了"慈"；第二尊者托塔罗汉，左手横胸，神态从容，体现了"稳"；其他评酒罗汉"醉"态朦胧，讲经罗汉侃侃而谈，听经罗汉俯首倾听，愁思罗汉眉头紧锁，骄傲罗汉唯我独尊……各具情态。最具巧思的是东壁北侧的三尊罗汉：降龙罗汉袒胸露臂，怒目簇眉，顺着他的视线望去，柱头上盘着一条虬龙，完全被罗汉咄咄逼人的气势笼罩；旁边的钦佩罗汉全神贯注地观看，他右手摊开，嘴角抿起，似乎在连呼佩服；而他北边的藐视罗汉则架着右腿，摇晃两手，瞥视着虬龙，颇不以为然。在罗汉殿北侧像龛中还有八尊塑像，是晚明塑工邱弥陀仿照宋代罗汉风格所塑，表情略显僵硬，衬托出宋塑的生动。在西壁第七尊者上方有诸天手持的经盖，自然下垂，褶皱柔畅，飘然如丝绸手卷；在面北的观音像头顶则有印着紫红缠枝牡丹花的绛红色华盖，宛如真丝织品，它们与十六罗汉并称为"金庵三绝"。3. 轩辕宫正殿：轩辕宫是一处道教宫观，创建于唐贞观二年（628年），曾祭祀伍子胥，因称胥王庙。明代称显灵庙、灵顺宫，民国时期改供轩辕黄帝，始称轩辕宫。整组建筑位于东山西麓，坐东朝西，原有山门、正殿、碧霞元君祠、城隍庙和火神殿等，现仅存轩辕宫正殿与北侧的城隍庙三进建筑。入口位于北路城隍庙前，今为碑刻陈列室，展出东山发现的明清石刻，其中以阴亭最为珍贵。这是一座石构仿木六角亭，梁柱、门窗、斗栱和雕饰都刻画精细，亭子正面刻有"叶时敬妻周氏之墓"字样，内部储藏尸骨，是明代一种特殊的墓葬形式。轩辕宫正殿位于城隍庙后部偏南，建于元至正四年（1338年），以"断梁殿"著称。大殿坐东朝西，后依山峰，前有开阔的月台可向东欣赏湖景。殿宇面阔三间，进深九檩，平面接近正方形，上为单檐歇山屋顶。室内明间金柱上方的檩木为二木对接，技艺巧妙。殿内构件，如梭形金柱、檐柱，大部分梁架和斗栱都是元代遗构，构件粗壮，结构合理，是研究元代江南建筑的绝佳实例。4. 东山民居：东山民居是一组保存完好的明代民居建筑群，包括明善堂、怀荫堂和凝德堂等。建筑用料粗大，明间用月梁，结点处设斗栱，并采用荷叶墩、圆栌斗和无斗蜀柱等作法，体现了典型的明代风格。怀荫堂采用前店后宅的格局，凝德堂有72幅精美彩绘，规模最大的是明善堂，南距轩辕宫仅300米。明善堂坐北朝南，包括东、西两路。入口位于西南角，入门西路包括耳房、客堂和佛楼，楼后为花园；折向右为东部主路，东南角设花厅，正中为主厅。各房屋之间通过天井、石库门和塞口墙分隔相连，16处天井中9处尚存假山花木。主厅为三开间，两侧带稍间，梁柱、轩架、彩画都很精彩。厅前正对双面砖雕门楼，外侧相对简朴，内侧雕刻精细，有各种吉祥图案。
projects.content_en: Dongshan, also called East Dongting Mountain, is located southwest of Suzhou on the east bank of Lake Tai, with its highest peak Moli Peak facing the Piaomiao Peak of West Dongting Mountain across the lake. Dongshan has 4 national protected sites: the Republic-era Carved Flower Tower (Chunzai Lou) famous for its carving art; Zijin (Purple Gold) Nunnery with Southern Song painted arhat statues; Xuanyuan Palace built in the Yuan Dynasty; and the Ming-dynasty residences Mingshan Tang, Ningde Tang, and Huaiyin Tang on Yangwan Old Street. It also has 6 provincial protected sites: Rui'ai Tang, Nianqin Tang nanmu hall, Zhugong Well Pavilion, Wuben Tang, Shaode Tang, and the Sanshan ancient cultural site; 11 municipal protected sites and over 100 Ming-Qing ancient buildings. Across the water from Dongshan is Xishan (West Mountain) Town. Dongshan has more scenic spots and historical sites, while Xishan excels in natural scenery, though it also has provincial protected buildings such as Qixian Lane Gate, Jinxiu Tang, Hancun Shop, and Renben Tang. 1. Carved Flower Tower (Chunzai Lou): The main building complex faces east, with three roads north-south. The middle road is the Carved Flower Tower, from east to west: screen wall, gate tower, front hall, rear hall, and kitchen-dining room; the north road is a garden, the south road is the Zhuangyuan (Top Scholar) Mansion. Built in the Republic era, the Carved Flower Tower integrates brick carving, wood carving, gold carving, stone carving, and clay sculpture—a masterpiece of Suzhou Xiangshan craftsmen, hailed as "the foremost tower in Jiangnan." Its carvings and layout fully reflect a wealthy merchant's tastes and needs. The carvings all contain auspicious meanings. The ground in front of the gate tower is paved with broken stones forming "a vase with three halberds," meaning "promotion to three ranks," praying for official success and wealth. The gate tower is covered with brick carvings: on the inner side, the lower lintel carves "Guo Ziyi's Birthday Celebration," with statues of the Fu, Lu, Shou (Fortune, Prosperity, Longevity) Three Stars above; the middle lintel has a bat-bordered brick plaque "Cultivating Virtue," with round carvings "Yao and Shun's Abdication" and "King Wen's Visit to the Sage" on the left and right spandrels; above is a horizontal round carving "Ten Scenes of Fortune and Deer"; the upper lintel has the round carving "Eight Immortals Celebrating Longevity," with five openwork carvings on the arch-supporting plates above—double happiness in the center, ruyi and cords on both sides, symbolizing ruyi passed down through generations. The roof's vertical ridges mold the Heavenly Official Bestowing Fortune and Carp Leaping Over the Dragon Gate; the main ridge holds a celadon treasure basin with evergreen plants. Wood carvings are mainly concentrated in the front and rear halls. The front hall is a five-bay two-story gable-roof building, used for weddings, funerals, and receiving distinguished guests, with the most carvings—arguably the representative work of "Jiangnan full-hall wood carving." On the beams are 48 boxwood carvings of "Romance of the Three Kingdoms"; both ends of the crescent beams carve phoenixes, 86 pairs in the whole hall, a homophone for "hundred joys"; the skirt boards of the front eave long windows and half-windows carve the "Twenty-Four Filial Exemplars." The rear hall is the activity center for female family members, mainly carving stories from "Romance of the Western Chamber." The carving characteristics of the Carved Flower Tower are summarized as: joy when leaving the door, treasure when entering, longevity when looking up, official rank when looking back, money when reaching out, and fortune underfoot—full of straightforward prayers for fortune, longevity, and wealth. The building layout mainly follows practical needs: the first floor of the front hall is for ceremonies and receiving guests, the first floor of the rear hall is for female family members' activities; the second floors of both halls are connected as a "galloping horse corridor," with bedrooms and guest rooms. A safe is hidden south of the front hall, and the rear hall has three hidden layers for storing treasures against robbery. On one hand the owner shows off wealth through exquisite carvings, on the other he racks his brains to protect wealth—the complex human nature of seeking status and guarding wealth is fully revealed in the Carved Flower Tower. The north garden has mountains and water, with four groups of Taihu rockeries mostly piled against walls, complementing the winding pond with趣味. The Taihu rocks emphasize figurative appreciation, imitating bears, elephants, eagles, rats, etc., reflecting secular taste. At the west end is a two-story Buddhist tower, where female family members burn incense and chant. The south Zhuangyuan Mansion has both residence and garden, exhibiting Dongshan's imperial examination culture. 2. Zijin Nunnery Arhat Statues: Zijin Nunnery is located in the Ximao Valley of East Dongting Mountain, founded in the early Tang, majorly repaired in the High Tang and Southern Song, rebuilt in the early Ming, and expanded during the Qianlong reign of the Qing. Today the main gate is at the southwest corner; entering straight ahead, the second gate is visible on the left. The main building complex faces south, with the second gate, Arhat Hall, and Jingyin Hall in sequence. On the west side are attached Qingchuan Xuan, Baiyun Ju, and Tingsong Tang. The whole complex is not large, nestled among pines and bamboos, simple and elegant. The most famous in the nunnery are the sixteen arhats (one complete set) sculpted in the Southern Song, which, together with the forty arhats (one set) at Lingyan Temple in Changqing, Jinan, and the nine arhats (half a set) at Baosheng Temple in Luzhi, are called "two complete sets and one half set of arhats under heaven." In the center of the Arhat Hall facing south are the Sakyamuni Three Buddhas, with disciples Kashyapa and Ananda standing in between; facing north in the center is the golden statue of Guanyin Viewing the Sea. The sixteen arhats stand under the east and west walls, eight on each side. They were created by the Southern Song sculptor masters Lei Chao and his wife—their masterpiece. The Kangxi-era "Suzhou Prefecture Gazetteer" states: "The Bodhisattva and arhat statues in (Zijin Nunnery) were sculpted by Lei Chao. Both husband and wife were skilled hands, sculpting only three places in their lifetime, with this nunnery being the foremost." Qing scholar Qiu Gengxi highly praised the Zijin Nunnery arhats, having visited famous mountains and ancient temples throughout Suzhou and Hangzhou, finding arhat statues often tall and large, but never with "spirit transcending, seeming alive as at Zijin Nunnery" ("Record of Jingyin Hall of Zijin Nunnery"). This evaluation points out two major characteristics: first, unlike the common method of showing divine power through height, the Zijin Nunnery arhats are life-sized, with seated statues about 1.2 meters, with well-proportioned heads, bodies, hands, and feet. Second, these 16 arhats humanize the divine images, giving them rich emotions and personalities through different appearances and expressions. For example, the first arhat Long-Browed Arhat, lifting his long eyebrows (now lost), sits smiling sideways, embodying "compassion"; the second arhat Pagoda-Holding Arhat, with left hand across his chest, composed in demeanor, embodying "stability"; others include the Wine-Tasting Arhat with hazy "drunken" expression, the Sutra-Preaching Arhat speaking eloquently, the Sutra-Listening Arhat bowing to listen, the Sorrow-Thinking Arhat with furrowed brows, the Proud Arhat with self-importance... each with distinct demeanor. The most ingenious are the three arhats on the north side of the east wall: the Dragon-Subduing Arhat with bare chest and arms, angry eyes and knitted brows—following his gaze, a coiled dragon on the column capital is completely overshadowed by the arhat's imposing aura; beside him, the Admiring Arhat watches intently, right hand open, mouth corners pursed, as if repeatedly exclaiming admiration; while north of him, the Disdaining Arhat crosses his right leg, shakes both hands, and glances at the coiled dragon with considerable disapproval. In the niche north of the Arhat Hall are eight more statues, sculpted by late-Ming craftsman Qiu Mituo imitating the Song arhat style, with slightly stiff expressions, setting off the vividness of the Song sculptures. Above the seventh arhat on the west wall is a scripture canopy held by a deva, naturally drooping with soft, smooth folds like a silk handscroll; above the north-facing Guanyin statue's head is a crimson canopy printed with purple-red interlocking peony flowers, like real silk fabric—these, together with the sixteen arhats, are called the "Three Wonders of Zijin Nunnery." 3. Xuanyuan Palace Main Hall: Xuanyuan Palace is a Taoist temple founded in the 2nd year of Zhenguan of the Tang (628), originally sacrificing to Wu Zixu, hence called the Xu King Temple. In the Ming it was called Xianling Temple and Lingshun Palace; in the Republic era it was changed to enshrine the Yellow Emperor Xuanyuan, hence the name Xuanyuan Palace. The whole complex is at the western foot of Dongshan, facing west, originally with a gate, main hall, Bixia Yuanjun Shrine, City God Temple, and Fire God Temple—today only the Xuanyuan Palace main hall and the three-bay City God Temple to the north survive. The entrance is in front of the north City God Temple, now a stele exhibition room displaying Ming-Qing stone carvings found in Dongshan, with the Yin Pavilion being the most precious. This is a stone structure imitating a wooden hexagonal pavilion, with beams, columns, doors, windows, brackets, and carvings all finely detailed; the front of the pavilion is inscribed "Tomb of Ye Shijing's Wife Zhou," with bones stored inside—a special Ming-dynasty burial form. The Xuanyuan Palace main hall is south of the rear of the City God Temple, built in the 4th year of Zhizheng of the Yuan (1338), famous as a "Broken Beam Hall." The main hall faces west, backed by a mountain peak, with an open platform in front for viewing the lake to the east. The hall is three bays wide, nine purlins deep, nearly square in plan, with a single-eave hip-and-gable roof. Inside, the purlin above the central bay's golden columns is formed by two joined pieces of wood—a clever technique. The hall's components, such as the spindle-shaped golden columns and eave columns, most of the beam frame and brackets, are Yuan-dynasty originals, with sturdy components and reasonable structure—an excellent example for studying Yuan-dynasty Jiangnan architecture. 4. Dongshan Residences: Dongshan Residences are a well-preserved group of Ming-dynasty residential buildings, including Mingshan Tang, Huaiyin Tang, and Ningde Tang. The buildings use thick materials, with crescent beams in the central bay, brackets at joints, and techniques such as lotus-leaf piers, round block brackets, and bracketless short columns—reflecting typical Ming style. Huaiyin Tang adopts a front-shop, rear-residence layout; Ningde Tang has 72 exquisite painted decorations. The largest is Mingshan Tang, only 300 meters south of Xuanyuan Palace. Mingshan Tang faces south, including east and west roads. The entrance is at the southwest corner; entering, the west road includes an annex, guest hall, and Buddhist tower, with a garden behind the tower; turning right is the eastern main road, with a flower hall at the southeast corner and the main hall in the center. The buildings are separated and connected through courtyards, stone-frame doors, and partition walls; among 16 courtyards, 9 still retain rockeries, flowers, and trees. The main hall is three bays wide with side bays, with excellent beams, ceiling frames, and paintings. In front of the hall is a double-sided brick-carved gate tower, relatively simple on the outside and exquisitely carved on the inside with various auspicious patterns.

projects.content_zh: 甪直属吴中区，位于苏州东南，传说古代神兽"甪端"曾在此地流连栖居，角端形似麒麟，头仅一角，颇似角字，因而得名。镇内东市河与南市河形成L形，以保圣寺为起点向东北展开，河道西、北两侧为店铺，东、南两侧为住家，与两岸皆为店铺的周庄和两岸皆为住家的同里形成有趣对照。甪直河多、桥多、古迹多，其中最著名的是保圣寺，由直便围绕此寺逐渐发展繁荣，此外还有唐人陆龟蒙的斗鸭池、叶圣陶《多收了三五斗》中的万盛米行、王韬故居，以及沈氏、萧氏的大宅等。甪直的"船鼻子"独具特色，是河岸上镶嵌的拴船石，大多一尺见方，中部双孔对穿，覆孔石雕刻成芭蕉、如意、寿桃、灵芝、仙鹤等各种花样，精巧雅致。保圣寺：梁天监二年（503年）笃信佛教的梁武帝倡建保圣寺，唐会昌五年（845年）毁于武宗灭佛，北宋大中祥符六年（1013年）重建，最兴盛时有殿宇5000余间，僧侣上千人，占据了半座甪直镇。今寺庙包括山门、二门、天王殿和古物馆等，庙西为叶圣陶纪念馆、陆龟蒙墓和斗鸭池。斗鸭池建于明代正德年间，方形水池，池中央立四角清风亭，东西各有石拱桥与岸相通。寺门北侧为天王殿，明成化二十三年（1487年）在宋代殿址上重建，清同治年间大修，殿前的幡竿夹石和青石经幢为宋代遗物，上刻"宋皇五年（1053年）重立"，铁钟为明代遗物。天王殿北原为大雄宝殿，内有18尊唐代"塑圣"杨惠之塑造的罗汉，民国初年殿顶倒塌，砸坏了西壁9尊。蔡元培、马叙伦、顾颉刚等文化界名人为之奔走呼告，组成"唐塑罗汉保存会"，1932年由建筑师范文照设计，将大雄宝殿改为古物馆，保护尚存的9尊罗汉。杨惠之早年与吴道子一同跟随张僧繇学画，吴道子成名，被唐玄宗召入宫中，尊为"画圣"。杨惠之耻居人后，弃画学塑，最终成为"塑圣"，时有"道子画，惠之塑，夺得僧繇神笔路"的美誉。唐代杨惠之的作品遍布各地，长安、洛阳、开封皆有佳作，可惜泥塑不易保存，甪直保圣寺的罗汉成为他硕果仅存的杰作。与后世常见的各尊罗汉单独塑造不同，杨惠之的罗汉位于同一墙壁上，壁面塑有山云、石树、洞窟和海水等，营造出"崇卑之土坡，突兀之山崖，卷舒之云气"（大村西崖《吴郡奇迹塑壁残影》），其间上下各处配置罗汉。各尊罗汉与不同的自然环境结合，情态各异，这种巧妙的布置构图，在宋代以后已经失传。元代赵孟頫为大殿题写的对联称赞"罗汉溯源惠之，为江南佛像无双"，《吴郡甫里志》也称这批罗汉"神光闪耀，形貌如生，真得塑中三昧者。江南北诸郡莫能及"。1926年日本学者大村西崖特来考察参观，称其为"吴郡奇迹"，使保圣寺罗汉名扬海外。
projects.content_en: Luzhi belongs to Wuzhong District, located southeast of Suzhou. Legend says the ancient divine beast "Luduan" once lingered and dwelt here; Luduan resembles a qilin with only one horn on its head, quite like the character "lu" (角), hence the name. In the town, the East Market River and South Market River form an L-shape, spreading northeast from Baosheng Temple as the starting point. On the west and north sides of the river are shops, on the east and south sides are residences—forming an interesting contrast with Zhouzhuang (shops on both banks) and Tongli (residences on both banks). Luzhi has many rivers, bridges, and historical sites, the most famous being Baosheng Temple, around which the town gradually developed and prospered. Additionally, there are the Tang-dynasty Lu Guimeng's Duck-Fighting Pond, the Wansheng Rice Shop from Ye Shengtao's "A Few More Dou of Harvest," Wang Tao's former residence, and the large mansions of the Shen and Xiao families. Luzhi's "boat nose" is distinctive—ship-tying stones inlaid on the riverbank, mostly about one chi square, with double holes through the center, and the stone covering the holes carved into various patterns such as banana, ruyi, longevity peach, lingzhi, and crane—exquisite and elegant. Baosheng Temple: In the 2nd year of Tianjian of the Liang (503), the devout Buddhist Emperor Wu of Liang advocated building Baosheng Temple. In the 5th year of Huichang of the Tang (845), it was destroyed during Emperor Wuzong's persecution of Buddhism; rebuilt in the 6th year of Dazhong Xiangfu of the Northern Song (1013). At its peak it had over 5,000 halls and more than a thousand monks, occupying half of Luzhi Town. Today the temple includes the gate, second gate, Heavenly King Hall, and Antiquities Hall; west of the temple are the Ye Shengtao Memorial Hall, Lu Guimeng's Tomb, and the Duck-Fighting Pond. The Duck-Fighting Pond was built during the Zhengde reign of the Ming, a square pond with a four-corner Qingfeng (Clear Wind) Pavilion in the center, connected to the banks by stone arch bridges on east and west. North of the temple gate is the Heavenly King Hall, rebuilt in the 23rd year of Chenghua of the Ming (1487) on a Song-dynasty hall site, majorly repaired during the Tongzhi reign of the Qing. The banner-pole夹 stones and bluestone pillar in front of the hall are Song-dynasty relics, inscribed "re-erected in the 5th year of Huangyou (1053) of the Song," and the iron bell is a Ming-dynasty relic. North of the Heavenly King Hall was originally the Mahavira Hall, containing 18 arhats sculpted by the Tang-dynasty "Sculpture Sage" Yang Huizhi. In the early Republic, the hall roof collapsed, destroying 9 arhats on the west wall. Cultural figures including Cai Yuanpei, Ma Xulun, and Gu Jiegang campaigned on their behalf, forming the "Tang Sculpture Arhat Preservation Society." In 1932, architect Fan Wenzhao designed the conversion of the Mahavira Hall into an Antiquities Hall to protect the 9 surviving arhats. Yang Huizhi early studied painting with Wu Daozi under Zhang Sengyou; Wu Daozi became famous, was summoned to the palace by Emperor Xuanzong of Tang, and honored as the "Painting Sage." Ashamed to be behind, Yang Huizhi abandoned painting for sculpture, ultimately becoming the "Sculpture Sage," with the saying "Daozi's painting, Huizhi's sculpture—seizing the divine brush path of Sengyou." Yang Huizhi's works were spread across various places, with masterpieces in Chang'an, Luoyang, and Kaifeng; unfortunately clay sculptures do not survive easily, and the arhats of Luzhi's Baosheng Temple became his only surviving masterpiece. Unlike later common practice of sculpting each arhat separately, Yang Huizhi's arhats are on the same wall, with the wall surface sculpted with mountain clouds, stone trees, caves, and seawater, creating "lofty and humble earth slopes, precipitous mountain cliffs, rolling and舒展 cloud vapors" (Omura Seigai, "Remnants of Sculpted Walls: Wonders of Wu Commandery"), with arhats arranged at various positions above and below. Each arhat combines with a different natural environment with distinct expressions—this ingenious composition was lost after the Song Dynasty. The couplet written by Zhao Mengfu of the Yuan for the main hall praises "Arhats tracing to Huizhi, unmatched among Buddhist statues in Jiangnan"; the "Wujun Fuli Gazetteer" also calls these arhats "divine light shining, lifelike in form and expression, truly attaining the essence of sculpture. No place north or south of the Yangtze can match." In 1926, Japanese scholar Omura Seigai specially came to inspect and visit, calling it a "Wonder of Wu Commandery," making the Baosheng Temple arhats famous overseas.

projects.level: 中国历史文化名镇，退思园为世界文化遗产、第五批国保（2001年）
