明崇祯二年1629年两人创立复社
五人墓碑记明天启六年1626年
前正厅孝友堂后堂楼通廊连屋成通转走马楼
projects.content_zh: 张溥（1602—1641），字天如，是明代著名文学家，应社、复社领袖。张溥为庶出，常受排挤，他幼年发奋读书，必亲手抄录，抄完焚毁再抄，往往多达六七次，后来其书斋便称"七录斋"。张溥与同乡张采齐名，号称"娄东二张"，明崇祯二年（1629年）两人创立复社，继承东林遗风，抗争阉党。当时天下士子皆以入社为荣，社员多达2000人。张溥的名作是明天启六年（1626年）撰写的《五人墓碑记》。张溥宅第原为其曾任工部尚书的伯父张辅之住宅，建于明天启年间，是一座尚书的官宅。原有东、中、西三路，现仅存中路三进，沿中轴线依次为正厅、堂楼和后楼，两侧有厢房。东厢房后部通过备弄连接各进房屋，天井中布置山石花卉，还有一口古井，刻有"天启二年工部张衙"铭文，表明这处宅第的所属和建造年代。前部的正厅孝友堂开间宽阔，梁柱粗大，在主梁与金柱相交处，使用雕刻松鹤云纹图案的纱帽翅，点明其官宅身份。后部的堂楼与后楼通过廊屋连成"通转走马楼"，空间复杂，梁架采用抬梁、穿斗、童柱、中柱加抬梁等多种组合形式，具有典型的明代风格。宅第门楼、门扇上刻有精美的砖雕和木雕，古朴典雅。
projects.content_en: Zhang Pu (1602-1641), style name Tianru, was a famous Ming-dynasty writer and leader of the Ying Society and Fu Society (Restoration Society). Zhang Pu was born to a concubine and often faced排挤; in his youth he studied diligently, always copying by hand, burning the copy after finishing and copying again—often as many as six or seven times—later his study was called the "Seven Copies Studio." Zhang Pu and his fellow townsman Zhang Cai were equally famous, known as the "Two Zhangs of Loudong"; in the 2nd year of Chongzhen of the Ming (1629), the two founded the Fu Society, inheriting the Donglin legacy and resisting the eunuch faction. At that time, scholars throughout the land considered it an honor to join the society, with members reaching 2,000. Zhang Pu's famous work is the "Epitaph of the Five Men," written in the 6th year of Tianqi of the Ming (1626). Zhang Pu's residence was originally the home of his uncle Zhang Fuzhi, who served as Minister of Works, built during the Tianqi reign of the Ming—a minister's official residence. Originally with east, middle, and west roads, today only the middle road's three bays survive, along the central axis: main hall, hall tower, and rear tower, with wing rooms on both sides. The rear of the east wing room connects each bay through a service alley; the courtyard is arranged with rockery, flowers, and an ancient well inscribed with "2nd year of Tianqi, Ministry of Works Zhang Mansion," indicating the ownership and construction date of this residence. The front main hall Xiaoyou (Filial Friendship) Hall has a wide bay with thick beams and columns; at the intersection of the main beam and golden columns, official-hat wings carved with pine-crane-cloud patterns are used, indicating its official-residence identity. The rear hall tower and rear tower are connected through corridor buildings into a "continuous galloping horse corridor building," with complex space; the beam frame uses multiple combinations such as column-and-tie, post-and-lintel, child columns, and central column with column-and-tie—typical Ming style. The residence's gate tower and door leaves are carved with exquisite brick and wood carvings—simple and elegant.

projects.name: 王锡爵故居及赵孟頫书法碑
projects.name_en: Former Residence of Wang Xijue and Zhao Mengfu Calligraphy Stele
projects.level: 第七批全国重点文物保护单位（2013年）
projects.level_en: 7th Batch National Key Cultural Heritage Site (2013)
projects.address_en: No. 60 East Xinhua Road
highlights: 王锡爵1534-1614明嘉靖四十一年1562年会试第一殿试第二榜眼
明万历五年1577年张居正夺情事件持反对立场
明万历二十一年1593年入阁成为首辅
原有澄观堂燕喜堂鹤来堂三馀馆和乐颐堂等
门前悬万历皇帝赐额大学士第
元代赵孟頫书法石刻
projects.content_zh: 明嘉靖四十一年（1562年）王锡爵（1534—1614）会试第一，殿试第二，高中榜眼，同榜状元为申时行。在明万历五年（1577年）张居正的夺情事件中，他持反对立场，与张居正结怨，后来自请回乡省亲，张居正卒后始出任礼部尚书兼文渊阁大学士。继任首辅申时行素受张居正器重，当时"倒张派"欲牵制申时行，因而举荐王锡爵入阁，但他入阁后不计前嫌，以国事为重，与申时行积极配合，使朝局得以稳定。王锡爵性格刚直，明万历十六年（1588年）其子王衡中顺天试第一，两名朝臣非议此事，他连章辨讦，出语忿急；御史乔璧星疏请皇帝戒谕他"务扩其量，为休休有容之臣"，王锡爵又同御史争辩，从此与廷论不合，一度回乡退养。明万历二十一年（1593年）王锡爵入阁成为首辅，主政有方，次年受朝臣弹劾，再度辞官。此后皇帝多次征召，他辞不赴任，在太仓多种菊养花，度过余生。这处故居建于明万历年间，原有澄观堂、燕喜堂、鹤来堂、三馀馆和乐颐堂等，规模宏大，现仅存故居与宗祠两路各三进。门前悬万历皇帝赐额"大学士第"，门前石狮为明代旧物，雕工精细。入门为三间小屋，两侧游廊中嵌太仓历代碑刻，其中最珍贵的是元代赵孟頫的书法石刻。故居东侧为宗祠，展览王锡爵、王时敏等人的生平和事迹。
projects.content_en: In the 41st year of Jiajing of the Ming (1562), Wang Xijue (1534-1614) placed first in the metropolitan examination and second in the palace examination, achieving the bangyan (second-place graduate), with the top scholar of the same cohort being Shen Shixing. In the 5th year of Wanli of the Ming (1577), during Zhang Juzheng's "seizing mourning" (duoqing) incident, he took an opposing stance, incurring Zhang Juzheng's resentment, later requesting to return home to visit relatives; after Zhang Juzheng's death, he began serving as Minister of Rites and Grand Secretary of the Wenyuan Pavilion. The succeeding Grand Secretary Shen Shixing had long been valued by Zhang Juzheng; at that time, the "anti-Zhang faction" wanted to restrain Shen Shixing, hence recommending Wang Xijue to enter the cabinet, but after entering the cabinet he put aside past grievances, prioritizing state affairs, and actively cooperated with Shen Shixing, stabilizing the court situation. Wang Xijue had a forthright character; in the 16th year of Wanli (1588), his son Wang Heng placed first in the Shuntian examination, and two court officials criticized this matter. He submitted repeated memorials to defend and attack, speaking with anger and urgency; Censor Qiao Bixing memorialized the emperor to admonish him to "expand his tolerance, be a magnanimous and accommodating minister." Wang Xijue again argued with the censor,从此 disagreeing with court opinion, and once returned home to recuperate. In the 21st year of Wanli (1593), Wang Xijue entered the cabinet and became Grand Secretary, governing effectively; the following year he was impeached by court officials and resigned again. Thereafter the emperor summoned him multiple times, but he declined to take office, spending his remaining years in Taicang growing chrysanthemums and flowers. This former residence was built during the Wanli reign of the Ming, originally with Chengguan Hall, Yanxi Hall, Helai Hall, Sanyu Pavilion, and Leyi Hall—grand in scale. Today only the residence and ancestral hall, each with three bays, survive. In front of the gate hangs the plaque "Grand Secretary's Mansion" bestowed by Emperor Wanli; the stone lions in front are Ming-dynasty originals with fine carving. Entering the gate is a three-bay small house; in the corridors on both sides are embedded Taicang's historical steles, the most precious being the Yuan-dynasty Zhao Mengfu calligraphy stone carvings. East of the former residence is the ancestral hall, exhibiting the lives and deeds of Wang Xijue, Wang Shimin, and others.

projects.name: 王时敏南园
projects.level: 太仓市文物保护单位
projects.level_en: Taicang Municipal Protected Site
projects.address_en: No. 7 East Nanyuan Road
highlights: 王锡爵退隐种梅之所太仓城东的东园是他的芍药圃
明天启年间其孙王时敏聘请造园名家张南垣
绣雪堂潭影轩香涛阁水边林下和烟垂雾接诸胜
清顺治三年1646年春吴伟业闲步到南园隔墙听到琵琶声
白或如吴伟业专奏琵琶名手白或如
清嘉庆年间王恭之子在水边林下旧址建鹤梅仙馆
projects.content_zh: 南园最初为王锡爵退隐种梅之所，太仓城东的东园则是他的芍药圃，明天启年间其孙王时敏聘请造园名家张南垣将东园改筑为乐郊园，同时拓建南园，有绣雪堂、潭影轩、香涛阁、水边林下和烟垂雾接诸胜，成为一座名园。南园距离吴伟业的梅村仅一里，清顺治三年（1646年）春吴伟业闲步到南园，隔墙听到琵琶声，他"循墙侧听，当其妙处不觉拊掌"，王时敏开门发现吴伟业，赶忙延请入园。是日梅花盛放如雪，王时敏在园中宴客，王鉴、王翚、王原祁皆在座，一同欣赏琵琶名手白或如的演出。白或如为吴伟业专奏琵琶，一曲，述及明亡以来世况，在座的前朝侍从姚某因说起宫中旧事，吴伟业不胜感慨，为作《琵琶行》长诗，传为佳话。作为书画名家，王时敏不但喜画山水，更好构筑园池，后来他又在城西建西田别墅。园林太多不易维持，他不得已将南园典押给僧尼，此园"前后割裂，千树梅花，四围丛桂，悉摧为薪"。王时敏不胜痛惜，劝族侄王玠购下南园，细加打理。清乾隆年间传到王玠手中时，园景仍颇有可观，"有小艇曰拾受，时荡桨波间，歌声与林樾鸟声相乱。或宵漏初歇，明月欲来，问梅禅院钟磬数声，则又萧然若尘外"（王恭《南园风雅序》）。清嘉庆年间王恭之子在水边林下旧址建鹤梅仙馆，祀王锡爵，并以王世贞和吴伟业附祀。20世纪30年代童寯前往考察时仍存遗迹，并有从弇山园移来的簪云、侍儿两峰。抗日战争期间南园被炸，后又沦为日军的养马场，一片荒芜。1958年前后，园内建筑被拆除，河池填平，树木砍尽，簪云、侍儿两峰也被击碎，旧园荡为耕地，种植庄稼。1998年复建南园，恢复绣雪堂、香涛阁、潭影轩等景致，成为当地一处新的游赏名胜。
projects.content_en: The South Garden was originally Wang Xijue's place for retiring and planting plum blossoms; the East Garden east of Taicang city was his peony nursery. During the Tianqi reign of the Ming, his grandson Wang Shimin hired famous garden designer Zhang Nanyuan to rebuild the East Garden into the Lejiao Garden, while expanding the South Garden with scenic spots such as Xiuxue Hall, Tanying Xuan, Xiangtao Pavilion, Waterside Under Forest, and Smoke-Hanging Mist-Connecting—becoming a famous garden. The South Garden is only one li from Wu Weiye's Meicun; in the spring of the 3rd year of Shunzhi of the Qing (1646), Wu Weiye strolled to the South Garden and heard pipa music over the wall. He "followed the wall and listened sideways, unconsciously clapping at the wonderful moments." Wang Shimin opened the gate and discovered Wu Weiye, hurriedly inviting him in. That day plum blossoms were in full bloom like snow; Wang Shimin hosted a banquet in the garden, with Wang Jian, Wang Hui, and Wang Yuanqi all present, together enjoying a performance by the famous pipa player Bai Huoru. Bai Huoru played the pipa specifically for Wu Weiye; one piece described the world situation since the fall of the Ming, and a former palace attendant Yao present spoke of old palace stories. Wu Weiye was deeply moved and wrote the long poem "Pipa Xing" (Song of the Pipa), which became a famous anecdote. As a famous calligrapher and painter, Wang Shimin not only loved painting landscapes but also enjoyed constructing gardens and ponds; later he built the Xitian Villa west of the city. With too many gardens to maintain, he had no choice but to mortgage the South Garden to Buddhist nuns; this garden was "split front and rear, with a thousand plum trees and surrounding cassia groves all destroyed for firewood." Wang Shimin was deeply grieved and urged his clan nephew Wang Jie to purchase the South Garden and carefully manage it. During the Qianlong reign of the Qing, when it passed to Wang Jie, the garden scenery was still quite可观: "There was a small boat called 'Shishou,' sometimes rowing among the waves, with singing mingling with the birdsong in the forest. Or when the night watch had just ended and the bright moon was about to rise, the sound of bells and chimes from the Wenmei Chan Courtyard a few times would make one feel as if beyond the dusty world" (Wang Gong, "Preface to the Elegant Affairs of the South Garden"). During the Jiaqing reign of the Qing, Wang Gong's son built the Hemei Xian Pavilion on the site of Waterside Under Forest, enshrining Wang Xijue, with Wang Shizhen and Wu Weiye as accompanying deities. In the 1930s, when Tong Jun went to investigate, relics still remained, including the Zanyun and Shi'er peaks moved from the Yanshan Garden. During the War of Resistance against Japan, the South Garden was bombed, later becoming a Japanese military horse farm—barren. Around 1958, the garden buildings were demolished, ponds filled in, trees cut down, and the Zanyun and Shi'er peaks shattered; the old garden became farmland for crops. In 1998, the South Garden was rebuilt, restoring scenic spots such as Xiuxue Hall, Xiangtao Pavilion, and Tanying Xuan—becoming a new local scenic spot for sightseeing.

projects.name: 王世贞弇山园
projects.name_en: Yanshan Garden—Former Residence of Wang Shizhen
projects.level: 太仓市文物保护单位
projects.level_en: Taicang Municipal Protected Site
projects.address_en: No. 40 West Xianfu Street
highlights: 王世贞出自太原王氏19岁中进士才最高地望最显声华意气笼罩海内
与造园名家张南阳联手打造的弇山园奇幻巨丽
明人陈所蕴将弇山园与豫园并列称两园百里相望为东南名园冠
张凤翼称自己的乐志园不足以当弇山愚谷之培塿
张宝臣为晚明园林列榜娄水之王锡山之邹江都之俞燕台之米皆近代名区弇山园排在首位
明钱谷小祇园图
projects.content_zh: 王世贞弇山园在历史上名气极高，堪称晚明江南第一名园。王世贞出自太原王氏，19岁中进士，"才最高，地望最显，声华意气，笼罩海内"（《明史》卷287），他与造园名家张南阳联手打造的弇山园奇幻巨丽，为时人所艳称：明人陈所蕴将弇山园与豫园并列，称两园"百里相望，为东南名园冠"；张凤翼谦称自己的乐志园"不足以当弇山、愚谷之培塿"；张宝臣为晚明园林列榜，"娄水之王、锡山之邹、江都之俞、燕台之米，皆近代名区"，弇山园排在首位……这座园林的面貌可从当时画家钱穀为王世贞绘制的《小祇园图》中看到，此外王世贞还撰写了长达八千多字的《弇山园记》和数十首诗，对该园作了巨细无遗的描述和阐发。弇山园乃王世贞毕生心血凝成，他的文集皆题作《弇州山人四部稿》《弇山堂别集》等。他晚年叮嘱子孙，自己过世后"弃园能守则守之，不能守则速以售豪有力者。庶几善护持，不至损天物性，鞠为茂草"，为了保存园林不惜卖给别人。但他卒后王氏败落，弇山园还是荒废了，明末其孙王鉴（著名画家，与王时敏、王翚、王原祁合称四王）租住在园西，生活清苦。晚清弇山园归陆氏，又归蒋氏、汪氏，缩减改筑为"半园"，园林学家童寯曾去考察拍照。新中国成立后在园址建制药厂，旧园基本沦废。由于王世贞和弇山园的名气，又有大量图像和文字资料存世，近年由殷继山主持，在旧址复建了弇山园。其中的山形水势、亭桥湖石，仍可令人依稀想象旧时胜景。
projects.content_en: Wang Shizhen's Yanshan Garden was extremely famous in history, arguably the number one garden in late-Ming Jiangnan. Wang Shizhen came from the Taiyuan Wang family, passing the jinshi examination at age 19—"with the highest talent, the most prominent family status, and fame and spirit enveloping the land" ("History of Ming" vol. 287). The Yanshan Garden he created together with famous garden designer Zhang Nanyang was fantastical and magnificent, envied and praised by contemporaries: Ming scholar Chen Suoyun juxtaposed Yanshan Garden with Yu Garden, calling the two gardens "facing each other across a hundred li, the crown of famous gardens in the southeast"; Zhang Fengyi humbly said his own Lezhi Garden was "not enough to be a mound compared to Yanshan and Yugu"; Zhang Baochen made a ranking of late-Ming gardens—"the Wang of Loushui, the Zou of Xishan, the Yu of Jiangdu, the Mi of Yantai—all famous districts of recent times"—with Yanshan Garden ranked first... The appearance of this garden can be seen in the "Xiaoqi Garden Painting" drawn by contemporary painter Qian Gu for Wang Shizhen; additionally, Wang Shizhen wrote the over 8,000-character "Record of Yanshan Garden" and dozens of poems, providing exhaustive descriptions and elaborations of the garden. Yanshan Garden was the crystallization of Wang Shizhen's lifelong efforts; his collected works are all titled "Four Drafts of the Yanshan Mountain Man," "Collected Works of Yanshan Hall," etc. In his later years he instructed his descendants that after his death, "if the abandoned garden can be maintained, maintain it; if not, quickly sell it to a wealthy and powerful person. Hopefully it will be well protected, not damaging the natural properties of things and becoming overgrown with weeds"—willing to sell it to others to preserve the garden. But after his death the Wang family declined, and Yanshan Garden still fell into ruin. At the end of the Ming, his grandson Wang Jian (a famous painter, together with Wang Shimin, Wang Hui, and Wang Yuanqi called the Four Wangs) rented a place west of the garden, living in poverty. In the late Qing, Yanshan Garden passed to the Lu family, then to the Jiang and Wang families, reduced and rebuilt into a "Half Garden"; garden scholar Tong Jun once went to investigate and photograph. After the founding of New China, a pharmaceutical factory was built on the garden site, and the old garden was basically abandoned. Due to the fame of Wang Shizhen and Yanshan Garden, and the survival of大量 images and textual materials, in recent years, under the direction of Yin Jishan, Yanshan Garden was rebuilt on the old site. Its mountain forms, water features, pavilions, bridges, and lake rocks still allow people to vaguely imagine the former scenic splendor.

projects.name: 太仓石拱桥：皋桥、州桥、周泾桥、金鸡桥、井亭桥
projects.name_en: Five Stone Arch Bridges in Taicang: Gaoqiao, Zhouqiao, Zhoujing, Jinji, and Jingting Bridges
projects.level: 第六批全国重点文物保护单位（2006年）
projects.level_en: 6th Batch National Key Cultural Heritage Site (2006)
projects.address_en: Taicang City Area
highlights: 5座元代建造的石拱桥
皋桥元元统二年1334年本名兴福桥单孔拱桥俗称高桥
州桥元天历二年1329年又名安福桥因古代正对州署衙门俗称州桥三孔拱桥诸桥中建造最早
周泾桥元至顺元年1330年在太仓石桥中最负盛名桥中心拱石上方刻海门第一桥题字
井亭桥和金鸡桥皆建于元元统二年1334年在太仓南郊镇新丰村
projects.content_zh: 这是5座元代建造的石拱桥，皋桥、州桥、周泾桥皆在太仓城内致和塘上，金鸡桥和井亭桥位于城外。皋桥位于致和塘与长春南路交叉口东，元元统二年（1334年）建，本名兴福桥，为单孔拱桥，拱身较高，俗称高桥，后被雅化为皋桥。桥长15米，宽4.2米，高4.4米，正中地幅一侧刻有八卦图案，栏板上雕花卉，刻工细致。州桥在致和塘与府南街交叉口东，元天历二年（1329年）建，又名安福桥，因古代正对州署衙门，俗称州桥。这是一座三孔拱桥，体量较大，长32.4米，宽4米，是诸桥中建造最早的一座。周泾桥在致和塘与太平南路交叉口东，元至顺元年（1330年）建，在太仓石桥中最负盛名。桥长17.2米，宽4.7米，高5.2米，用青石建成。桥中心拱石上方刻"海门第一桥"题字，桥面中央雕八卦图案，桥栏有精美的缠莲枝图案。井亭桥和金鸡桥都在太仓南郊镇新丰村，皆建于元元统二年（1334年），井亭桥在南广教寺山门东南的张江门河上，是座南北走向的三孔石桥，长22.3米，宽4.3米，桥身平缓，倒映在水中，有宁静之感。由井亭桥向北约500米为金鸡桥，是一座南北走向的单孔石桥，跨在朱里泾河上，长11.7米，宽2.4米，较为简朴。
projects.content_en: These are five stone arch bridges built in the Yuan Dynasty. Gaoqiao, Zhouqiao, and Zhoujing Bridges are all on the Zhihe Pond in Taicang city, while Jinji Bridge and Jingting Bridge are located outside the city. Gaoqiao Bridge is east of the intersection of Zhihe Pond and South Changchun Road, built in the 2nd year of Yuantong of the Yuan (1334), originally named Xingfu Bridge. It is a single-arch bridge with a high arch, commonly called Gaoqiao (High Bridge), later refined to Gaoqiao. The bridge is 15 meters long, 4.2 meters wide, and 4.4 meters high; one side of the central deck is carved with a bagua (eight trigrams) pattern, and the railings are carved with flowers with fine craftsmanship. Zhouqiao Bridge is east of the intersection of Zhihe Pond and South Fu Street, built in the 2nd year of Tianli of the Yuan (1329), also named Anfu Bridge. Because in ancient times it directly faced the prefectural government office, it is commonly called Zhouqiao (Prefecture Bridge). This is a three-arch bridge with a large volume, 32.4 meters long and 4 meters wide—the earliest built among the bridges. Zhoujing Bridge is east of the intersection of Zhihe Pond and South Taiping Road, built in the 1st year of Zhishun of the Yuan (1330), the most famous among Taicang's stone bridges. The bridge is 17.2 meters long, 4.7 meters wide, and 5.2 meters high, built of bluestone. Above the central arch stone is inscribed the title "First Bridge of Haimen"; the center of the bridge deck is carved with a bagua pattern, and the bridge railings have exquisite interlocking lotus branch patterns. Jingting Bridge and Jinji Bridge are both in Xinfeng Village, Nanjiao Town, south of Taicang, both built in the 2nd year of Yuantong of the Yuan (1334). Jingting Bridge is on the Zhangjiangmen River southeast of the Nanguangjiao Temple gate, a north-south three-arch stone bridge, 22.3 meters long and 4.3 meters wide, with a gentle bridge body reflected in the water—giving a sense of tranquility. About 500 meters north from Jingting Bridge is Jinji Bridge, a north-south single-arch stone bridge spanning the Zhulijing River, 11.7 meters long and 2.4 meters wide—relatively simple.

projects.name: 浏河天妃宫
projects.level: 第七批全国重点文物保护单位（2013年）
projects.level_en: 7th Batch National Key Cultural Heritage Site (2013)
projects.address_en: No. 90 New East Street, Liuhe Town
highlights: 北宋景祐元年1034年苏州知州范仲淹拓浚漕口通刘家河
刘家港被誉为天下第一码头元明清三代长江通海外贸易的唯一良港
元明两代南北粮运的海运港还是明初郑和七下西洋的始发港和归泊港
北宋宣和五年1123年外来的闽粤商人在老浏河北岸五杨池建灵济宫供奉妈祖
元至元十八年1281年朝廷封妈祖为护国明著天妃始名天妃宫
明宣德五年1430年郑和第七次出海前
projects.content_zh: 北宋景祐元年（1034年）苏州知州范仲淹拓浚漕口通刘家河，此地逐渐发展成市集。元初称刘家港，清初简称刘河，后为避雷同改名浏河。刘家港被誉为"天下第一码头"，是元、明、清三代长江通海外贸易的唯一良港，又是元、明两代南北粮运的海运港，还是明初郑和七下西洋的始发港和归泊港。北宋宣和五年（1123年）外来的闽粤商人在老浏河北岸五杨池（今龙王湾东侧）建灵济宫，供奉妈祖。元至元十八年（1281年）朝廷封妈祖为"护国明著天妃"，始名天妃宫。元至正二年（1342年）宫殿基础受海潮侵袭坍塌，迁至今址重建。当时船只出海前必向天妃娘娘进香，浏河镇香火兴盛。明代郑和七下西洋，每次都修葺扩建天妃宫，明宣德五年（1430年）第七次出海前，郑和亲立《通番事迹之记》碑，在前庭植"西域海棠"，浏河天妃宫达到极盛。清乾隆五年（1740年）官民集资建造正殿和戏楼，三年后又建后殿，形成前殿、正殿和后殿的完整格局。清咸丰十一年（1861年）天妃宫毁于兵祸，清同治七年（1868年）重建，后来正殿多次遭火，1934年重修山门、后殿等，但未重建正殿。新中国成立后山门戏台及门外牌楼被拆除。1985年为纪念郑和首下西洋580周年，修缮后殿楼（天妃寝宫）、配殿和廊庑，复建前殿（山门移自原花神庙，雕饰精美），并修复整理了正殿遗址。浏河天妃宫是我国沿海沿江最早兴建、祭祀妈祖的宫庙之一，同时也是元明两代海运漕粮、郑和航海的历史遗存，具有重要的历史价值。
projects.content_en: In the 1st year of Jingyou of the Northern Song (1034), Fan Zhongyan, Prefect of Suzhou, dredged and expanded the canal mouth to connect with the Liu River, and this place gradually developed into a market town. In the early Yuan it was called Liujiagang; in the early Qing it was abbreviated to Liuhe, later renamed Liuhe to avoid duplication. Liujiagang was hailed as the "Number One Wharf Under Heaven," the only good port for Yangtze River foreign trade in the Yuan, Ming, and Qing dynasties; it was also the maritime transport port for north-south grain shipment in the Yuan and Ming, and the departure and return port for Zheng He's seven voyages to the Western Seas in the early Ming. In the 5th year of Xuanhe of the Northern Song (1123), visiting merchants from Fujian and Guangdong built the Lingji Palace at Wuyangchi (east of today's Longwang Bay) on the north bank of the Old Liu River, enshrining Mazu. In the 18th year of Zhiyuan of the Yuan (1281), the court enfeoffed Mazu as the "Protecting Nation and Manifesting Heavenly Consort," hence the name Tianfei Palace (Heavenly Consort Palace). In the 2nd year of Zhizheng of the Yuan (1342), the palace foundation was eroded and collapsed by sea tides, and it was moved to today's site for reconstruction. At that time, before ships went to sea, they必 burned incense to the Heavenly Consort, and Liuhe Town's incense flourished. During Zheng He's seven voyages to the Western Seas in the Ming, he repaired and expanded Tianfei Palace each time. In the 5th year of Xuande of the Ming (1430), before his seventh voyage, Zheng He personally erected the "Record of Deeds in Voyaging to Foreign Lands" stele and planted "Western Region Crabapple" in the front courtyard—Liuhe Tianfei Palace reached its peak. In the 5th year of Qianlong of the Qing (1740), officials and people raised funds to build the main hall and stage; three years later the rear hall was built, forming a complete layout of front hall, main hall, and rear hall. In the 11th year of Xianfeng of the Qing (1861), Tianfei Palace was destroyed by war; in the 7th year of Tongzhi (1868) it was rebuilt, later the main hall suffered multiple fires, and in 1934 the gate and rear hall were repaired, but the main hall was not rebuilt. After the founding of New China, the gate stage and the memorial archway outside the gate were demolished. In 1985, to commemorate the 580th anniversary of Zheng He's first voyage to the Western Seas, the rear hall tower (Heavenly Consort's Bedchamber), side halls, and corridors were repaired, the front hall was rebuilt (the gate moved from the original Flower God Temple, with exquisite carvings), and the main hall site was restored and整理. Liuhe Tianfei Palace is one of the earliest temples built along China's coast and rivers to sacrifice to Mazu, and also a historical relic of Yuan-Ming maritime grain transport and Zheng He's voyages—with important historical value.

projects.name: 沙溪镇
projects.level: 第二批中国历史文化名镇，现存两处省保（龚氏雕花厅2002年、吴晓邦故居2011年）
projects.level_en: 2nd Batch Chinese Historical and Cultural Town, 2 provincial protected sites (Gong Carved Hall 2002, Wu Xiaobang Former Residence 2011)
projects.address_en: Central-north Taicang
highlights: 始建于元末有东南十八镇沙溪第一镇的美称
镇内有一河戚浦河范仲淹主持开挖二街沿河两岸河南塘北古街三桥利济桥义兴桥庵桥和一岛橄榄岛1954年形成
龚氏雕花厅清乾隆年间富商龚氏建坐北朝南有东西两路梁架木雕精美
吴晓邦故居1927年吴晓邦祖母聘请上海工匠建造为二层欧式洋楼俗称小白楼
1937年日军占领后设特高组实施残酷统治
1965年四清运动期间林彪之妻叶群化名易敬在此居住
乐荫园元末隐士瞿孝祯筑水面尚存1982年复建
projects.content_zh: 沙溪位于太仓中北部，始建于元末，有"东南十八镇，沙溪第一镇"的美称。镇内有一河（戚浦河，范仲淹主持开挖）、二街（沿河两岸河南、塘北古街）、三桥（利济桥、义兴桥和庵桥）和一岛（橄榄岛，1954年形成），为第二批中国历史文化名镇，现存两处省保。一是位于中市街60号的龚氏雕花厅（2002年），清乾隆年间富商龚氏建，坐北朝南，有东西两路，梁架木雕精美。二是位于西市街的吴晓邦故居（2011年），1927年吴晓邦祖母聘请上海工匠建造，为二层欧式洋楼，俗称小白楼。1937年日军占领后设特高组实施残酷统治。1965年"四清"运动期间，林彪之妻叶群化名"易敬"在此居住。在白云中路170号还有一座乐荫园，元末隐士瞿孝祯筑，水面尚存，1982年复建。园林包括东、中、西三部分。中部围绕水池布置假山、长廊、厅榭和亭桥等，西部有雕花厅和临水平台，东部为茶室。【推荐游线：义兴桥（曾家桥）—庵桥—乐荫园—邱家弄—龚氏雕花厅和龚氏古宅—沙溪文史馆—新桥（利济桥）】
projects.content_en: Shaxi is located in central-north Taicang, first built at the end of the Yuan, with the reputation "among the eighteen towns of the southeast, Shaxi is the first." The town has one river (Qipu River, excavated under Fan Zhongyan's direction), two streets (the ancient Henan and Tangbei streets along both river banks), three bridges (Liji Bridge, Yixing Bridge, and An Bridge), and one island (Olive Island, formed in 1954). It is a second-batch Chinese Historical and Cultural Town, with two surviving provincial protected sites. One is the Gong Family Carved Hall at No. 60 Zhongshi Street (2002), built by wealthy merchant Gong during the Qianlong reign of the Qing, facing south, with east and west roads, with exquisite wood carvings on the beam frames. The other is the Wu Xiaobang Former Residence on Xishi Street (2011), built in 1927 by Wu Xiaobang's grandmother hiring Shanghai craftsmen—a two-story European-style building, commonly called the Small White Building. After the Japanese occupation in 1937, a special high group was established to implement brutal rule. During the "Four Cleanups" movement in 1965, Ye Qun, wife of Lin Biao, lived here under the alias "Yi Jing." At No. 170 Middle Baiyun Road there is also the Leyin Garden, built by late-Yuan hermit Qu Xiaozhen, with the water surface still surviving, rebuilt in 1982. The garden includes east, middle, and west parts. The middle arranges rockeries, long corridors, halls, pavilions, and bridges around a pond; the west has a carved hall and waterside platform; the east is a tea room. [Recommended tour route: Yixing Bridge (Zengjia Bridge) — An Bridge — Leyin Garden — Qiu Family Lane — Gong Family Carved Hall and Gong Family Ancient Residence — Shaxi Culture and History Museum — New Bridge (Liji Bridge)]

regions.name: 无锡
regions.overview: 考古勘探在无锡发现了六千多年前的原始聚居地。商末，周太王长子泰伯、次子仲雍为让位给三弟季历（季历之子为周文王），出奔梅里（今无锡梅村）建立勾吴国。《论语·泰伯》称誉他："泰伯可谓至德矣，三以天下让，民无德而称焉。"今无锡滨湖区有纪念泰伯的庙和墓。春秋时期，吴王阖闾建立大小两城，大城为吴都姑苏（今苏州），小城即位于今无锡、常州交界处的阖闾城。战国时期，这里属于春申君黄歇的封地，舜柯山黄城、惠山黄公涧、芙蓉湖黄埠墩都是因春申君得名。秦统一六国后，此地属会稽郡。西汉高祖五年（前202年）始设无锡县。无锡得名有两种说法。第一种据唐陆羽《游惠山寺记》称，东周、秦时锡山产铅锡，到汉代开采殆尽，因而设立了无锡县。东汉时有樵夫在山下看到石铭，曰："有锡兵，天下争；无锡宁，天下清。有锡沴，天下弊；无锡乂，天下济。"以无锡为地名，寄托了人们对和平生活的向往。第二种据当代语言学家研究，"无锡"应为古越语地名，"无"是无实义的发语词，"锡"另有含义，尚未破译。无锡与夫椒、余杭、句容、姑苏等一样，属于齐头式地名。无锡还有一个别称"梁溪"，得名于东汉居士梁鸿。梁鸿因批评建造宫殿滥用民力的《五噫歌》得罪东汉章帝刘炟，避居吴地（今无锡），他与妻子孟光"举案齐眉"的故事便发生在此（五代卫贤《高士图》）。三国时期无锡属吴国。东晋兴宁二年（364年）无锡建造首座佛寺——兴宁寺，南朝宋太平兴国初年赐名崇安寺，今天市中心崇安区便由此得名。南朝时期，境内大兴佛寺，创建了惠山寺、护国寺（今南禅寺）、胶山寺和远山寺等。隋朝开通了大运河，在无锡境内西北起于五牧，东南止于望亭，今以水弄堂一段最具风情（南起南水仙庙、清名桥，北折西流，经西水墩，向北直到黄埠墩）。元明时期，城西的惠山和锡山逐渐成为游览胜地，《惠山记》《惠山古今考》和《锡山景物略》等志书记载了当时的兴旺景象。两山之间分布着二泉亭、漪澜堂、听松石床、碧山吟社、点易台、春申涧和若冰泉等众多胜迹，同时兴建了大量园林，以惠山寺南、北的愚公谷和寄畅园最著名。自宋代以来，在惠山东麓还建造了许多祠堂，保存至今的有118处，成为无锡的一大特色。在无锡城内，晚明学者们倡导经世致用之学，兴建了东林学院，影响到整个晚明的政局。清末民初，借助京杭大运河和沪宁铁路，无锡发展成为重要的近代城市，有"小上海"之称。近代的民族工业家不但在城内留下许多近代建筑，还在太湖边兴建了梅园、蠡园和鼋头渚等近代园林，大气磅礴，使太湖成为媲美惠山的另一风景区。无锡今辖崇安区（市政府驻地）、南长区、北塘区、锡山区、惠山区和滨湖区6个区，代管江阴市、宜兴市2个县级市，无锡市和宜兴市分别于2007年、2011年被国务院确定为国家历史文化名城，有全国重点文物保护单位31处，省级文物保护单位83处，本书介绍国保建筑19处，省保建筑10处。
regions.overview_en: Archaeological exploration has discovered primitive settlements over 6,000 years old in Wuxi. At the end of the Shang Dynasty, Taibo, the eldest son of King Tai of Zhou, and his second brother Zhongyong, in order to yield the throne to their third brother Jili (whose son was King Wen of Zhou), fled to Meili (today's Meicun in Wuxi) and established the state of Gouwu. The "Analects·Taibo" praised him: "Taibo may indeed be called supremely virtuous. He thrice declined the empire, and the people could find no words to praise him." Today in Binhu District of Wuxi there are temples and tombs commemorating Taibo. During the Spring and Autumn period, King Helü of Wu built two cities, large and small: the large city was the Wu capital Gusu (today's Suzhou), and the small city was Helü City, located at today's border between Wuxi and Changzhou. During the Warring States period, this area belonged to the fief of Huang Xie, Lord Chunshen; Shunke Mountain Yellow City, Huishan Huanggong Stream, and Furong Lake Huangbu Dun are all named after Lord Chunshen. After Qin unified the six states, this area belonged to Kuaiji Commandery. In the 5th year of Emperor Gaozu of the Western Han (202 BC), Wuxi County was first established. There are two theories about the origin of the name Wuxi. The first, according to Tang Lu Yu's "Record of Visiting Huishan Temple," states that during the Eastern Zhou and Qin dynasties, Xishan produced lead and tin, which was exhausted by the Han Dynasty, hence the establishment of Wuxi County ("No Tin"). In the Eastern Han, a woodcutter found a stone inscription at the foot of the mountain reading: "When there is tin, soldiers fight; when there is no tin, the world is peaceful. When there is tin calamity, the world suffers; when there is no tin, the world prospers." Using Wuxi as a place name expressed people's aspiration for a peaceful life. The second theory, based on contemporary linguists' research, holds that "Wuxi" should be an ancient Yue language place name, where "Wu" is a meaningless prefix and "Xi" has another meaning not yet deciphered. Wuxi, like Fujiao, Yuhang, Jurong, and Gusu, belongs to the "prefix-style" place names. Wuxi also has an alias "Liangxi," named after the Eastern Han hermit Liang Hong. Liang Hong offended Emperor Zhang of the Eastern Han Liu Da with his "Five Sighs Song" criticizing the abuse of people's labor in palace construction, and took refuge in Wu (today's Wuxi), where the story of him and his wife Meng Guang "raising the tray level with her eyebrows" (mutual respect) took place (as depicted in Five Dynasties Wei Xian's "Hermits Painting"). During the Three Kingdoms period, Wuxi belonged to Wu. In the 2nd year of Xingning of the Eastern Jin (364), Wuxi built its first Buddhist temple—Xingning Temple; in the early Taiping Xingguo period of the Southern Song, it was granted the name Chong'an Temple, from which today's city center Chong'an District gets its name. During the Southern Dynasties, Buddhist temples were vigorously built in the territory, including Huishan Temple, Huguo Temple (today's Nanchan Temple), Jiaoshan Temple, and Yuanshan Temple. The Sui Dynasty opened the Grand Canal, which in Wuxi territory starts at Wumu in the northwest and ends at Wangting in the southeast; today the "water alley" section is the most charming (starting from South Shuixian Temple and Qingming Bridge in the south, turning north and flowing west, passing Xishui Dun, and going north until Huangbu Dun). During the Yuan and Ming periods, Huishan and Xishan west of the city gradually became tourist destinations, with gazetteers such as "Huishan Record," "Past and Present Studies of Huishan," and "Xishan Scenic Spots" recording the prosperous scenes at that time. Between the two mountains are distributed many scenic spots such as the Second Spring Pavilion, Yilan Hall, Listening-to-Pine Stone Bed, Bishan Poetry Society, Point-Yi Platform, Chunshen Stream, and Ruobing Spring; meanwhile, many gardens were built, the most famous being Yugong Valley and Jichang Garden south and north of Huishan Temple. Since the Song Dynasty, many ancestral halls have been built at the eastern foot of Huishan, with 118 surviving today—becoming a major feature of Wuxi. In Wuxi city, late-Ming scholars advocated practical learning and established the Donglin Academy, influencing the political situation of the entire late Ming. In the late Qing and early Republic,借助 the Grand Canal and the Shanghai-Nanjing Railway, Wuxi developed into an important modern city, known as "Little Shanghai." Modern national industrialists not only left many modern buildings in the city but also built modern gardens such as Plum Garden, Li Garden, and Yuantouzhu by Taihu Lake—grand and majestic, making Taihu Lake another scenic area comparable to Huishan. Wuxi today administers 6 districts: Chong'an (where the municipal government is located), Nanchang, Beitang, Xishan, Huishan, and Binhu, and manages 2 county-level cities: Jiangyin and Yixing. Wuxi and Yixing were respectively designated as National Historical and Cultural Cities by the State Council in 2007 and 2011, with 31 national key cultural heritage protection units and 83 provincial cultural heritage protection units. This book introduces 19 national protected buildings and 10 provincial protected buildings.

projects.name: 东林书院
projects.level: 第六批全国重点文物保护单位（2006年）
projects.level_en: 6th Batch National Key Cultural Heritage Site (2006)
projects.address_en: No. 867 East Jiefang Road, Chong'an District
highlights: 北宋政和元年1111年杨时1044-1130创办
程门立雪杨时程颢程颐得意门生
明万历三十二年1604年顾宪成与顾允成高攀龙等依附道南祠重建
天下言书院首东林东林党人
明天启五年1625年魏忠贤发布东林党人榜
风声雨声读书声声声入耳家事国事天下事事事关心
projects.content_zh: 北宋政和元年（1111年）杨时（1044—1130）在无锡创办东林书院，他是程颢、程颐的得意门生，"程门立雪"讲的便是他在洛阳拜见程颐时侍立门外，积雪盈身的故事。他学成南归时，程颢倚门目送，欣慰地说："吾道南矣！"杨时果然把二程的学说带到南方，深刻影响了罗从彦、李侗和朱熹等大儒。杨时对庐山东林寺情有独钟，曾作《东林道上闲步》："寂寞莲塘七百秋，溪云庭月两悠悠。我来欲问林间道，万叠松声自唱酬……"他认为此地颇似道林寺，题名东林书院。杨时卒后，弟子们在今东林书院建造道南祠，杨时所建书院则逐渐荒废。东林书院再度声名鹊起是在明代。明万历三十二年（1604年）顾宪成与顾允成、高攀龙等依附道南祠重建东林书院，追随杨时遗风，讲求经世致用之学，《东林道上闲步》成为院歌，每次讲会前都要众声齐唱。顾宪成、高攀龙先后担任院长，他们在探求学术之余，讽议朝政、指陈时弊，成为士林领袖，"天下言书院首东林"；但他们也由此成为权贵和阉党的眼中钉，被目为"东林党人"。明天启五年（1632年）魏忠贤发布《东林党人榜》，通缉逮捕东林人士。次年高攀龙投水自尽，东林书院被拆除变卖，夷为平地。崇祯皇帝即位后为东林学派平反，复建书院。今东林书院包括东、中、西三路，中路为讲学礼堂等主体建筑，左右为附属建筑和园林。中路入门后是一座三开间五楼石牌坊，始建于1604年，被毁后于清乾隆五年（1740年）复建，近年修补。牌坊结构严谨、雕刻精美，为石构精品。坊北为泮池，当初是半圆形，1994年改砌为方池和拱桥。过桥为仪门，上题"东林精舍"，当年与讲学相关者方可入内。门北的丽泽堂是会众讲学之所，寓意道友切磋共进。其北依庸堂是会讲前学者们分列序齿，对揖交拜，举行仪式之所，清康熙三十三年（1694年）复建，成为东林学派学术领地的象征，清人认为"脚迹得入依庸堂，人生一大幸"。堂内今悬顾宪成的名联："风声雨声读书声声声入耳；家事国事天下事事事关心。"堂北为祭祀孔子的专祠，穿过圣域小城门，燕居庙内供有孔子的牌位和绣像。庙后为三公祠，祭祀因保护东林党人而遭到迫害的三位地方官。向西进入西花园，有长廊、心鉴斋、明道亭、寻乐处、来复斋和晚翠山房等，围绕一泓清池参差布置，为学子们提供了一处偃息休憩、冥思悟道的天然园亭。中路建筑偏东有东林报功祠、再得草庐、时雨斋、还经亭、东长廊、道南祠和正心亭等。东侧依傍弓河，不设围墙，人们可隔河望见林亭之美，聆听朗朗书声。
projects.content_en: In the 1st year of Zhenghe of the Northern Song (1111), Yang Shi (1044-1130) founded the Donglin Academy in Wuxi. He was a prized student of Cheng Hao and Cheng Yi; the story of "standing in the snow at the Cheng gate" tells of him waiting outside the door when visiting Cheng Yi in Luoyang, with snow accumulating on his body. When he completed his studies and returned south, Cheng Hao watched him leave from the door and said with satisfaction: "My way goes south!" Yang Shi indeed brought the Cheng brothers' teachings to the south, profoundly influencing great Confucians such as Luo Congyan, Li Dong, and Zhu Xi. Yang Shi had a special affection for Donglin Temple on Mount Lu, once writing "Strolling on the Donglin Road": "The lonely lotus pond has seen seven hundred autumns, stream clouds and courtyard moon both lingering. I come to ask the way among the trees, ten thousand layers of pine sound sing in response..." He thought this place quite like Daolin Temple, naming it Donglin Academy. After Yang Shi's death, his disciples built the Daonan (Way Goes South) Shrine at today's Donglin Academy, while the academy built by Yang Shi gradually fell into ruin. Donglin Academy rose to fame again in the Ming Dynasty. In the 32nd year of Wanli of the Ming (1604), Gu Xiancheng, together with Gu Yuncheng and Gao Panlong, rebuilt Donglin Academy attached to the Daonan Shrine, following Yang Shi's legacy and advocating practical learning. "Strolling on the Donglin Road" became the academy song, sung in unison before every lecture. Gu Xiancheng and Gao Panlong successively served as academy heads; in addition to pursuing scholarship, they criticized court politics and pointed out current abuses, becoming leaders of the scholar class—"when the world speaks of academies, Donglin is first"; but they thus became thorns in the eyes of the powerful and the eunuch faction, labeled as "Donglin partisans." In the 5th year of Tianqi of the Ming (1625), Wei Zhongxian issued the "Donglin Partisans List," ordering the arrest of Donglin figures. The following year Gao Panlong drowned himself, and Donglin Academy was demolished and sold, leveled to the ground. After Emperor Chongzhen ascended the throne, he rehabilitated the Donglin school and rebuilt the academy. Today's Donglin Academy includes east, middle, and west roads; the middle road is the main buildings such as lecture halls, with auxiliary buildings and gardens on left and right. After entering the middle road gate is a three-bay, five-story stone memorial archway, first built in 1604, rebuilt in the 5th year of Qianlong of the Qing (1740) after destruction, and repaired in recent years. The archway has a rigorous structure and exquisite carvings—a fine stone structure. North of the archway is the Pan Pond, originally semicircular, rebuilt as a square pond with an arch bridge in 1994. Crossing the bridge is the Ceremonial Gate, inscribed "Donglin Jingshe" (Donglin Retreat), where only those related to lectures could enter in olden times. North of the gate, the Lize Hall is the place for collective lectures, meaning friends切磋 and advancing together. North of it, the Yiyong Hall is where scholars lined up by seniority, bowed to each other, and held ceremonies before lectures; rebuilt in the 33rd year of Kangxi of the Qing (1694), it became a symbol of the Donglin school's academic territory, with Qing people believing "to set foot in Yiyong Hall is a great blessing in life." Inside the hall today hangs Gu Xiancheng's famous couplet: "The sounds of wind, rain, and reading all enter the ears; the affairs of family, state, and world all concern the heart." North of the hall is a special shrine for Confucius; passing through the small gate of the Holy City, the Yanju Temple enshrines Confucius's memorial tablet and embroidered portrait. Behind the temple is the Three Dukes Shrine, sacrificing to three local officials who were persecuted for protecting Donglin partisans. Going west into the West Garden, there are long corridors, Xinjian Studio, Mingdao Pavilion, Xunle Chu, Laifu Studio, and Wancui Mountain Room, arranged irregularly around a clear pond—providing students with a natural garden pavilion for rest, relaxation, and meditation. East of the middle road buildings are the Donglin Baogong Shrine, Zaide Thatched Hut, Shiyu Studio, Huanjing Pavilion, East Long Corridor, Daonan Shrine, and Zhengxin Pavilion. The east side borders the Bow River without a wall, allowing people to see the beauty of the forest pavilions across the river and hear the sound of loud reading.

projects.name: 阿炳故居
projects.level: 第六批全国重点文物保护单位（2006年）
projects.level_en: 6th Batch National Key Cultural Heritage Site (2006)
projects.address_en: No. 30 Library Road, Chong'an District
highlights: 阿炳本名华彦钧1893-1950
观内偏殿雷尊殿当家道士华清和与秦氏寡妇的私生子
华清和精通民族乐器以琵琶最精人称铁手琵琶
阿炳十七八岁已成为无锡闻名的小天师二胡琵琶击鼓说唱和滩簧都很擅长人称巧嘴阿炳
1927年双目失明到街头卖艺
二泉映月大浪淘沙等民乐杰作
projects.content_zh: 阿炳故居原属道观洞虚宫。阿炳本名华彦钧（1893—1950），是观内偏殿雷尊殿当家道士华清和与秦氏寡妇的私生子，1893年出生在观内一和山房（20世纪50年代拆除），后随其父从小做道士。华清和精通民族乐器，以琵琶最精，人称"铁手琵琶"，靠做法事维持小康生活。他曾送阿炳进私塾，后发现阿炳很有音乐才能，便亲自教授。阿炳十七八岁已成为无锡闻名的小天师，二胡、琵琶、击鼓、说唱和滩簧都很擅长，人称"巧嘴阿炳"。后来他得知自己的私生子身份，自尊受到打击，变得倔强孤僻。华清和去世后，阿炳继任为当家道士，沉迷于吸毒、宿娼，不得不变卖法器、道具，甚至道观房产。不久阿炳染上梅毒，1927年双目失明，无法再做法事，只好到街头卖艺，除了演奏二胡、琵琶，他的主业是在崇安寺茶馆前说唱新闻。1932年他与烟馆女佣董催娣结合，两人一起卖艺乞讨。无论寒暑，他常常上午在面馆弹奏，下午在茶馆说唱，晚上又由董催娣搀着到车站、旅店走唱。下层社会的生活使阿炳备尝酸楚，加上日军入侵，民族危亡，他在凄苦的心境中创作出《二泉映月》《大浪淘沙》等民乐杰作。
projects.content_en: A Bing's former residence originally belonged to the Daoist temple Dongxu Palace. A Bing, originally named Hua Yanjun (1893-1950), was the illegitimate son of Hua Qinghe, the chief Daoist priest of the side hall Leizun Hall in the temple, and a widowed woman surnamed Qin. Born in 1893 in the Yihe Mountain Room within the temple (demolished in the 1950s), he later became a Daoist priest from childhood under his father. Hua Qinghe was proficient in traditional instruments, especially the pipa (lute), known as the "Iron-Hand Pipa," and maintained a comfortable life by performing religious rituals. He once sent A Bing to a private school, later discovering A Bing's musical talent and teaching him personally. By age 17 or 18, A Bing had become a famous young master in Wuxi, skilled at the erhu (two-stringed fiddle), pipa, drum beating, storytelling-singing, and tanhuang (a local opera form)—known as the "Silver-Tongued A Bing." Later he learned of his illegitimate identity, his self-esteem was dealt a blow, and he became stubborn and withdrawn. After Hua Qinghe's death, A Bing succeeded as chief Daoist priest, indulging in drug use and visiting prostitutes, and had to sell ritual implements, props, and even temple property. Soon A Bing contracted syphilis, going blind in both eyes in 1927, unable to perform religious rituals anymore, so he had to perform on the street. Besides playing the erhu and pipa, his main occupation was telling news stories in front of the Chong'an Temple teahouse. In 1932 he partnered with Dong Chuidi, a maidservant at an opium den, and the two performed and begged together. Regardless of cold or heat, he often played at noodle shops in the morning, told stories at teahouses in the afternoon, and in the evening was led by Dong Chuidi to sing at stations and inns. Life in the lower class made A Bing taste bitterness to the full; coupled with the Japanese invasion and national peril, he created masterpieces of traditional music such as "The Moon Over a Fountain" (Erquan Yingyue) and "Big Waves Wash Away Sand" (Dalang Taosha) in a desolate state of mind.

projects.name: 小娄巷民居群
projects.level: 第七批全国重点文物保护单位（2013年）
projects.level_en: 7th Batch National Key Cultural Heritage Site (2013)
projects.address_en: Xiaolou Lane, Chong'an District
projects.type_en: Historical and Cultural Block / Dwelling Group
highlights: 无锡五大历史文化街区之一
谈氏秦氏等无锡望族世居之地曾出过1名状元13名进士和15名举人
南宋时期谈氏族人开始在小娄巷居住宋高宗曾赐谈信溯派汴梁匾
明代无锡有半城风雨半城谈之谚
秦氏始祖为秦观在无锡有河上秦和西关秦两支
巷南有来鹤楼和永锡堂属于孙氏明万历二年1574年孙继皋中状元
projects.content_zh: 小娄巷与清名桥古街（景点9）、惠山古镇（景点11）、荣巷（景点13）和荡口古镇（景点18）并称为无锡五大历史文化街区。小娄巷是谈氏、秦氏等无锡望族世居之地，曾出过1名状元、13名进士和15名举人。现存建筑以清末民初为主，20世纪90年代巷南西侧拆除殆尽，巷北和巷南西侧保存较好，2013年列为国保单位，目前正在整修，较为残破。南宋时期谈氏族人开始在小娄巷居住，宋高宗曾赐谈信"溯派汴梁"匾，明代无锡有"半城风雨半城谈"之谚，可想见其家族规模之大。清初谈氏衰落后，宅第逐渐转归秦氏、孙氏和王氏等所有，今尚存巷北48号的谈氏宗祠。巷北50号为秦氏故居福寿堂。秦氏始祖为秦观，在无锡有"河上秦"和"西关秦"两支。西关秦住在西水关内，今薛福成故居一带；小娄巷则属河上秦。河上秦之河为六箭河，无锡旧城呈菱形，中部有南北向的直河穿城而过，东半部的内河被称作弓河，从弓河分出9条东西向支流，称为箭河。9条箭河与惠山的九峰、九涧呼应，元代《无锡志》云："无锡有九龙峰，下有九涧，城中有九箭河，应之。谚云：九箭通，出三公。"这些河流具有重要的风水意义，关系到无锡的兴旺昌盛。六箭河是9河中最长的一条，又名师姑河、大河上，1958年填平为崇宁路。明清时期河上秦的宅第便沿此河东西展开，蔚为壮观，今尚存崇宁路88号的章庆堂。河上秦最初住在六箭河边的挺秀堂，"再迁为鸿绪堂，分仓桥下为敷庆堂。后复迁于小河上之新宝彝堂，至我果亭公为大雅堂。景仪公迁小娄巷，为修俭堂。修俭堂复分为福寿堂"（秦平甫语）。可知随着家族繁衍壮大，秦氏宅第逐渐扩展，从六箭河发展到小河上，又延伸至小娄巷。最先迁到小娄巷的是景仪公秦楷，他成婚后由岳父出资购得谈氏旧宅，即今修俭堂（今小娄巷46号）。秦楷幼子秦焕成亲后依例出宅，购得修俭堂西的谈氏旧宅，不幸太平天国时期被毁，清同治三年（1864年）秦焕在原址重新起屋，建造福寿堂。福寿堂南北共七进，秦焕建造了后面五进，其后人又建造了前面两进。宅第西北为佚园，民国初年秦毓鎏筑，自作《佚园记》，秦淦绘《佚园十景图册》，园中山池清丽，卉木扶疏，颇有可观。巷南有来鹤楼和永锡堂，属于孙氏。明万历二年（1574年）孙继皋中状元，御史谈恺以谈氏"万备堂"相赠，即今之嘉乐堂，后园假山上立有湖石"五老峰"，为宋高宗赐给谈信的花石纲遗物。孙继皋买下其西房屋扩建成少宰第，作为孙氏世居之地。
projects.content_en: Xiaolou Lane, together with Qingming Bridge Old Street (Attraction 9), Huishan Ancient Town (Attraction 11), Rongxiang (Attraction 13), and Dangkou Ancient Town (Attraction 18), are called the Five Major Historical and Cultural Districts of Wuxi. Xiaolou Lane was the ancestral home of prominent Wuxi families such as the Tan and Qin families, producing 1 top scholar (zhuangyuan), 13 jinshi, and 15 juren. The surviving buildings are mainly from the late Qing and early Republic; in the 1990s the south-lane west side was almost entirely demolished, while the north lane and south-lane west side are better preserved. Designated a national protected site in 2013, it is currently under renovation and relatively dilapidated. During the Southern Song, the Tan family began living in Xiaolou Lane; Emperor Gaozong of Song once bestowed the plaque "Tracing Origins to Bianliang" on Tan Xin. In the Ming, Wuxi had the proverb "half the city's wind and rain, half the city's Tan," indicating the family's enormous scale. After the Tan family declined in the early Qing, the residences gradually passed to the Qin, Sun, Wang, and other families; today the Tan Family Ancestral Hall at No. 48 North Lane still survives. No. 50 North Lane is the Qin Family Former Residence Fushou Hall. The Qin family's ancestor was Qin Guan; in Wuxi there are two branches: the "River Qin" and the "West Pass Qin." The West Pass Qin lived inside West Water Pass, today's Xue Fucheng Former Residence area; Xiaolou Lane belongs to the River Qin. The River Qin's river is the Sixth Arrow River. Wuxi's old city was diamond-shaped, with a north-south straight river running through the center; the inner river in the eastern half was called the Bow River, from which 9 east-west tributaries branched out, called Arrow Rivers. The 9 Arrow Rivers correspond to the Nine Peaks and Nine Streams of Huishan; the Yuan-dynasty "Wuxi Gazetteer" says: "Wuxi has Nine Dragon Peaks, below are Nine Streams, and in the city are Nine Arrow Rivers, corresponding to them. The proverb says: When the nine arrows flow, three dukes emerge." These rivers had important fengshui significance, related to Wuxi's prosperity. The Sixth Arrow River was the longest of the 9 rivers, also called Shigu River or Great River, filled in as Chongning Road in 1958. During the Ming and Qing, the River Qin's residences spread east-west along this river, spectacular in scale; today the Zhangqing Hall at No. 88 Chongning Road still survives. The River Qin initially lived at the Tingxiu Hall by the Sixth Arrow River, "then moved to Hongxu Hall, divided under Cangqiao Bridge as Fuqing Hall. Later moved to the New Baoyi Hall on the Small River, to our Guoting Gong as Daya Hall. Jingyi Gong moved to Xiaolou Lane as Xiujian Hall. Xiujian Hall was again divided into Fushou Hall" (Qin Pingfu's words). This shows that as the family multiplied and grew, the Qin residences gradually expanded, from the Sixth Arrow River to the Small River, then extending to Xiaolou Lane. The first to move to Xiaolou Lane was Jingyi Gong Qin Kai; after marriage, his father-in-law funded the purchase of the Tan family's old residence, today's Xiujian Hall (today's No. 46 Xiaolou Lane). Qin Kai's youngest son Qin Huan, after marriage, moved out according to custom and purchased the Tan family's old residence west of Xiujian Hall, unfortunately destroyed during the Taiping Rebellion; in the 3rd year of Tongzhi of the Qing (1864), Qin Huan rebuilt on the original site, constructing Fushou Hall. Fushou Hall has seven bays north-south; Qin Huan built the rear five bays, and his descendants built the front two bays. Northwest of the residence is the Yi Garden, built by Qin Yuliu in the early Republic, who wrote the "Record of Yi Garden" himself; Qin Gan painted the "Album of Ten Scenes of Yi Garden," with clear mountains and ponds and lush flowers and trees—quite可观. South of the lane are the Laihe Tower and Yongxi Hall, belonging to the Sun family. In the 2nd year of Wanli of the Ming (1574), Sun Jigao passed the top scholar exam; Censor Tan Kai presented the Tan family's "Wanbei Hall" as a gift, today's Jiale Hall. On the rockery in the rear garden stands the lake stone "Five Old Men Peak," a relic of the Huashigang (flower and stone convoy) bestowed by Emperor Gaozong of Song to Tan Xin. Sun Jigao bought the house to its west and expanded it into the Shaizai Di, as the Sun family's ancestral home.

projects.name: 秦邦宪故居
projects.level: 第七批全国重点文物保护单位（2013年）
projects.level_en: 7th Batch National Key Cultural Heritage Site (2013)
projects.address_en: No. 112 Chongning Road, Chong'an District
highlights: 秦邦宪1907-1946先祖秦观出自无锡望族西关秦氏
幼年家境贫寒生性沉静喜读古文因此又名博古
1931年至1936年间担任中共最高领导人与李德周恩来合称为最高三人团
遵义会议后他失去最高统帅地位但仍担任中央政治局委员
1946年他赴重庆参加宪章审议工作4月8日返回延安途中与王若飞叶挺邓发等17人飞机失事遇难史称四八烈士
此宅原属秦邦宪的同族无锡名流秦琢如建于清光绪末年包括东西两路
projects.content_zh: 秦邦宪（1907—1946）先祖秦观，出自无锡望族西关秦氏，他幼年家境贫寒，生性沉静，喜读古文，因此又名博古。他在1931年至1936年间担任中共最高领导人，与李德、周恩来合称为"最高三人团"。遵义会议后他失去最高统帅地位，但仍担任中央政治局委员。1946年他赴重庆参加宪章审议工作，4月8日返回延安途中与王若飞、叶挺、邓发等17人飞机失事遇难，史称"四八烈士"。此宅原属秦邦宪的同族，无锡名流秦琢如，建于清光绪末年，包括东西两路。西路为住宅，有门厅、轿厅、既翕堂和慎得堂等共七进；东路为秦淮海祠遗址，始建于明，祭祀秦观。1916年至1921年间秦邦宪随贫困的父母赁居在西路第四进的慎得堂，度过了少年时光。今宅内设有"秦邦宪生平事迹陈列展"。
projects.content_en: Qin Bangxian (1907-1946)'s ancestor was Qin Guan, from the prominent West Pass Qin family of Wuxi. In his childhood his family was poor; he was quiet by nature and fond of reading classical texts, hence also named Bogu. He served as the top leader of the Chinese Communist Party from 1931 to 1936, together with Otto Braun (Li De) and Zhou Enlai called the "Top Three Person Group." After the Zunyi Conference he lost his top leadership position but still served as a member of the Political Bureau of the Central Committee. In 1946 he went to Chongqing to participate in constitutional review work; on April 8, returning to Yan'an, he died in a plane crash with 17 others including Wang Ruofei, Ye Ting, and Deng Fa—historically called the "April 8 Martyrs." This residence originally belonged to Qin Zhuoru, a prominent Wuxi figure of the same clan as Qin Bangxian, built in the late Guangxu reign of the Qing, including east and west roads. The west road is the residence, with seven bays including the gate hall, sedan hall, Jixi Hall, and Shende Hall; the east road is the site of the Qin Huaihai Shrine, first built in the Ming, sacrificing to Qin Guan. From 1916 to 1921, Qin Bangxian lived with his impoverished parents, renting the Shende Hall in the fourth bay of the west road, spending his youth there. Today the residence has the "Exhibition of Qin Bangxian's Life and Deeds."

highlights: 薛福成1838-1894清末维新派代表人物曾先后担任曾国藩李鸿章的幕僚长达20余年
清光绪十五年1889年他被授为驻英兼驻法意比四国钦差大臣时回无锡购地亲自设计筹建新宅1890年他出洋后由长子薛翼运字南溟负责建造门内悬光绪皇帝御题钦使第匾额
宅基原为明代秦金尚书第的一部分秦金在惠山建造凤谷行窝寄畅园前身宅第西南为西水关城门当年秦金即由此出城沿水路前往惠山
薛福成相信风水曾手抄阳宅举要认为门前若有玉带水高官必定容易起此宅南临束带河1956年填平为学前街西依环城河北靠西溪后来填平为前溪街三面环水是一块文脉悠远的风水宝地
薛福成将住宅设计为南窄北宽的倒凸形宛如一只展翼高飞的大鹏中路为鹏之躯干由门厅轿厅正厅后堂转盘楼和后花园组成东路有吟风轩戏台对照厅枇杷园和西式弹子房西路有传经楼和西花园等为鹏之两翼
projects.content_zh: 薛福成（1838—1894）是清末维新派代表人物，曾先后担任曾国藩、李鸿章的幕僚长达20余年。清光绪十五年（1889年）他被授为驻英兼驻法、意、比四国钦差大臣时，回无锡购地亲自设计筹建新宅，1890年他出洋后由长子薛翼运（字南溟）负责建造，门内悬光绪皇帝御题"钦使第"匾额。宅基原为明代秦金"尚书第"的一部分，秦金在惠山建造"凤谷行窝"（寄畅园前身），宅第西南为西水关城门，当年秦金即由此出城沿水路前往惠山。薛福成相信风水，曾手抄《阳宅举要》，认为"门前若有玉带水，高官必定容易起"，此宅南临束带河（1956年填平为学前街）、西依环城河、北靠西溪（后来填平为前溪街），三面环水，是一块文脉悠远的风水宝地。薛福成将住宅设计为南窄北宽的倒"凸"形，宛如一只展翼高飞的大鹏：中路为鹏之躯干，由门厅、轿厅、正厅、后堂、转盘楼和后花园组成；东路有吟风轩、戏台、对照厅、枇杷园和西式弹子房，西路有传经楼和西花园等，为鹏之两翼。住宅中路采用前堂后宅格局：最前为将军门，门前原有九间照壁，1937年被日机炸断，1956年拆除。门内左右各有一处小天井，凿池置石，幽静雅致。院北为轿厅西绍堂，喻指主人出使西洋；又北为正厅务本堂。两堂皆为九开间，僭越逾制，因此采用"对剖双排柱"分成三座三间堂。即将两根半圆柱并列，其间相隔数厘米，远看为一柱，实则为两柱，柱下的石鼓，柱上的大梁和步梁，也都剖为两半。这样既能保持九开间的规模和气势，又巧妙地避开了越轨之嫌。务本堂内左右通过西式风格的移门相通，门可推入左右墙体中，反映了主人对西方建筑文化的引进。1894年宅第建成，准备迎接薛福成任满荣归。薛福成归国途中在香港染上时疾，抵达上海时病逝。崭新的宅院迎来的首件大事竟是主人的丧事，当时薛福成的灵柩就停放在务本堂中。轿厅和正堂之间左右各有一处庭园，设置对称的半亭和太湖石，为旱院，与前面的水院呼应。务本堂北有一道围墙，墙北为九开间的后堂惠然堂，是内眷理事、聚会之所。与雕饰华丽的外堂不同，这座内堂较为朴素。西侧三间今为无锡精品泥人馆，陈列工艺大师的戏曲人物泥人杰作；东侧三间为锡绣工作室和竹刻工作室，小学生可在此学习传统手艺，成为无锡非物质文化遗产的保护基地。惠然堂北又有一座更高的围墙，其北为女眷居住的转盘楼。高两层，11开间，规模宏大。楼下一层展览薛福成生平事迹。楼北即后花园，近年在考古基础上做了复原，西北角有当年仿天一阁建造的传经楼。薛福成曾在宁波任官，登天一阁编撰《天一阁见存书目》，并勾勒草图寄给薛南溟仿建此阁。住宅东路是辅助和娱乐用房。南部为戏台庭园，由正厅吟风厅、偏厅、回廊、辅房、戏台、曲桥和水池组成。戏台坐南朝北，前临水池，下支山石，是无锡城内最为精致完整的私家戏台。台前两株百年老树，石榴寓意多子多福，松树祈求延年益寿。其北为枇杷园，园东原为仓厅，是收租储粮之所，现在布置薛家实业展。厅北为西式弹子房，内置英式桌球，是当时相当高端时髦的娱乐。西花园原为宅内最大的花园，新中国成立后曾作为民居，近年结合遗存和文献做了细致的复原，有清风绿屿、西虹桥、听雨舫、春和亭、怀顾堂、滴翠轩、潭思阁、温经斋、怡心斋和适然亭等各景。
projects.content_en: Xue Fucheng (1838-1894) was a representative figure of the reformist faction in the late Qing, serving successively as a幕僚 (advisor) to Zeng Guofan and Li Hongzhang for over 20 years. In the 15th year of Guangxu of the Qing (1889), when he was appointed Imperial Envoy to Britain, France, Italy, and Belgium, he returned to Wuxi to purchase land and personally design and prepare the construction of a new residence. After he went abroad in 1890, his eldest son Xue Yiyun (style name Nanming) oversaw construction; inside the gate hangs the plaque "Imperial Envoy's Mansion" inscribed by Emperor Guangxu. The residence site was originally part of the Ming-dynasty Qin Jin's "Minister's Mansion"; Qin Jin built the "Fenggu Xingwo" (Phoenix Valley Travel Nest, predecessor of Jichang Garden) at Huishan, and southwest of the residence was the West Water Pass city gate, from which Qin Jin would leave the city by water to Huishan. Xue Fucheng believed in fengshui and once hand-copied "Essentials of Yang Residences," believing that "if there is jade-belt water in front of the gate, high office will surely come easily." This residence faces the Belt-Tying River to the south (filled in as Xueqian Street in 1956), borders the City Moat to the west, and backs onto West Stream (later filled in as Qianxi Street) to the north—surrounded by water on three sides, a fengshui treasure land with profound cultural lineage. Xue Fucheng designed the residence in an inverted "convex" shape, narrow in the south and wide in the north, like a great roc spreading its wings and flying high: the middle road is the roc's trunk, composed of the gate hall, sedan hall, main hall, rear hall, revolving corridor building, and rear garden; the east road has the Yinfeng Pavilion, stage, mirror hall, loquat garden, and Western-style billiard room; the west road has the Chuanjing (Scripture-Transmitting) Tower and West Garden—the roc's two wings. The middle road adopts a front-hall, rear-residence layout: at the very front is the General's Gate, originally with a nine-bay screen wall in front, bombed and broken by Japanese aircraft in 1937 and demolished in 1956. Inside the gate, left and right each have a small courtyard with ponds and rocks—quiet and elegant. North of the courtyard is the sedan hall Xishao Hall, alluding to the master's mission to the Western Ocean; further north is the main hall Wuben Hall. Both halls are nine bays wide, exceeding the regulated standard, hence the "split double-row columns" method was used to divide them into three three-bay halls. That is, two half-columns are placed side by side, separated by a few centimeters—looking like one column from afar but actually two; the stone drums below, the main beams and step beams above are also split in half. This both maintains the scale and grandeur of nine bays and cleverly avoids the suspicion of exceeding regulations. Inside Wuben Hall, left and right connect through Western-style sliding doors, which can be pushed into the left and right walls—reflecting the master's introduction of Western architectural culture. The residence was completed in 1894, preparing to welcome Xue Fucheng's triumphant return after his term. On his way back, Xue Fucheng contracted an epidemic in Hong Kong and died upon arriving in Shanghai. The first major event the brand-new residence welcomed was actually the master's funeral; at that time Xue Fucheng's coffin was placed in Wuben Hall. Between the sedan hall and main hall, left and right each have a garden, with symmetrical half-pavilions and Taihu rocks—a dry courtyard, echoing the water courtyard in front. North of Wuben Hall is a wall; north of the wall is the nine-bay rear hall Huiran Hall, where female family members managed affairs and gathered. Unlike the ornately carved outer halls, this inner hall is relatively plain. The west three bays are today the Wuxi Fine Clay Figure Museum, displaying master craftsmen's masterpieces of opera-character clay figures; the east three bays are tin-embroidery and bamboo-carving studios, where primary school students can learn traditional crafts—becoming a protection base for Wuxi's intangible cultural heritage. North of Huiran Hall is another higher wall; north of it is the revolving corridor building where female family members lived. Two stories high, 11 bays wide, grand in scale. The first floor exhibits Xue Fucheng's life and deeds. North of the building is the rear garden, restored in recent years based on archaeology; at the northwest corner is the Chuanjing Tower, built in imitation of the Tianyi Pavilion in those years. Xue Fucheng once served in Ningbo, climbed the Tianyi Pavilion to compile the "Catalogue of Existing Books in Tianyi Pavilion," and sketched a blueprint to send to Xue Nanming to imitate and build this pavilion. The east road of the residence is auxiliary and entertainment space. The south is the stage garden, composed of the main hall Yinfeng Hall, side hall, winding corridor, auxiliary rooms, stage, zigzag bridge, and pond. The stage faces south toward north, fronting the pond, supported by rocks below—the most exquisite and complete private stage in Wuxi city. In front of the stage are two century-old trees: pomegranate symbolizing many sons and blessings, pine praying for longevity. North of it is the loquat garden; east of the garden was originally the granary hall, for collecting rent and storing grain, now exhibiting the Xue family's industrial enterprises. North of the hall is the Western-style billiard room, with English billiards inside—a quite high-end and fashionable entertainment at the time. The West Garden was originally the largest garden in the residence; after the founding of New China it was used as residential housing, and in recent years has been carefully restored结合 surviving remains and documents, with scenic spots such as Qingfeng Green Islet, West Rainbow Bridge, Rain-Listening Boat, Chunhe Pavilion, Huaigu Hall, Dicui Studio, Tansi Pavilion, Wenjing Studio, Yixin Studio, and Shiran Pavilion.

highlights: 薛汇东故居1911-1917年薛福成之子薛南溟建巴洛克风格中国人设计的最早的西式住宅之一原为薛南溟与人合办公司时的写字楼后作为其次子薛学海1897-1965字汇东与袁世凯之女袁昭的结婚新居民间戏称为驸马府
钱钟书故居1923年钱钟书祖父钱福烔筹建绳武堂1926年其叔父钱孙卿续建包括前后两进庭院正房均为七开间建筑采用江南清式做法局部吸取西洋风格1926年钱基厚又在后园增建楼房称梅花书屋大门东侧三间房分别用作家祠和钱钟书之父钱基博讲学的家塾钱钟书1910-1998在这里度过了青少年时期直到1929年考入清华大学

张闻天旧居张闻天又名洛甫祖籍无锡1900年出生在南汇县今上海浦东新区是中国共产党早期重要领导人遵义会议中对确定毛泽东的领导地位起到关键作用他被誉为红色教授式的学者领袖曾短期担任党的总书记三次主动让贤传为佳话1959年张闻天在庐山会议上受到错误批判文革时期遭到残酷迫害1975年8月25日他从肇庆搬到无锡居住在此1976年7月1日病逝这是一座2层清水砖墙洋楼建于20世纪30年代今楼前立张闻天半身像楼内陈列张闻天生平图片和遗物

顾毓琇故居清光绪三十一年1905年顾惟桢为其子顾赓明建造宝善堂顾毓琇1902-2002为顾赓明次子出生后在此生活了14年1915年考入清华学校顾毓琇文理兼擅他科研成果丰硕被国际电机学界誉为现代电机理论的最有贡献者曾任中央大学校长清华大学工学院院长和宾夕法尼亚大学教授等桃李满天下同时还是翻译家小说家和剧作家与闻一多梁实秋等是清华文学社首批成员被誉为文坛耆宿桂冠诗人创作诗词4000余首话剧先驱和古乐泰斗在诸多领域都取得了极高的成就这处故居原有五进现存四进是无锡规模较大保存较好的一座今为顾毓琇纪念馆展出顾毓琇的生平和成就
缪公馆近代政治人物缪斌1902-1946是无锡人抗战期间卖身投靠日寇1946年被判处死刑1932年缪斌委托著名建筑师江应麟设计建造了这座公馆抗战期间曾用作日本特务机关外围青砖墙从南门进入为太湖石所砌五松坛后为清水砖砌两层洋楼立面有混凝土罗马式立柱
projects.content_zh: 无锡名人故居包括薛汇东故居、钱钟书故居、张闻天旧居、顾毓琇故居和缪公馆等多处省保单位。1. 薛汇东故居：薛汇东故居位于崇安区前西溪2号，薛福成故居北门对面，1995年列为省保单位，今为无锡史志办公室。1911—1917年薛福成之子薛南溟建，采用巴洛克风格，由门楼、主楼和西楼组成，是中国人设计的最早的西式住宅之一。此宅原为薛南溟与人合办公司时的写字楼，后作为其次子薛学海（1897—1965，字汇东）与袁世凯之女袁昭的结婚新居，民间戏称为"驸马府"。2. 钱钟书故居：钱钟书故居位于崇安区健康路新街巷30、32号，2002年列为省保单位，9:00—16:30免费开放。江南钱氏为吴越王钱镠之后，历代人才辈出，家风醇厚。1923年钱钟书祖父钱福烔筹建"绳武堂"，1926年其叔父钱孙卿续建。这处故居包括前后两进庭院，正房均为七开间建筑，采用江南清式做法，局部吸取西洋风格。1926年钱基厚又在后园增建楼房，称"梅花书屋"。大门东侧三间房分别用作家祠和钱钟书之父钱基博讲学的家塾。钱钟书（1910—1998）在这里度过了青少年时期，直到1929年考入清华大学。全宅现辟为钱钟书文学馆。3. 张闻天旧居：张闻天旧居位于崇安区学前街汤巷45号，2011年列为省保单位，9:00—16:30免费开放。张闻天又名洛甫，祖籍无锡，1900年出生在南汇县（今上海浦东新区），是中国共产党早期重要领导人，遵义会议中对确定毛泽东的领导地位起到关键作用。他被誉为"红色教授"式的学者领袖，曾短期担任党的总书记，三次主动让贤，传为佳话。1959年张闻天在庐山会议上受到错误批判，"文革"时期遭到残酷迫害，1975年8月25日他从肇庆搬到无锡，居住在此，1976年7月1日病逝。这是一座2层清水砖墙洋楼，建于20世纪30年代，今楼前立张闻天半身像，楼内陈列张闻天生平图片和遗物。4. 顾毓琇故居：顾毓琇故居位于崇安区学前街3号，2011年被列为省保单位，9:00—16:30免费开放。清光绪三十一年（1905年）顾惟桢为其子顾赓明建造"宝善堂"，顾毓琇（1902—2002）为顾赓明次子，出生后在此生活了14年，1915年考入清华学校。顾毓琇文理兼擅：他科研成果丰硕，被国际电机学界誉为"现代电机理论的最有贡献者"；曾任中央大学校长、清华大学工学院院长和宾夕法尼亚大学教授等，桃李满天下；同时还是翻译家、小说家和剧作家，与闻一多、梁实秋等是清华文学社首批成员，被誉为文坛耆宿、桂冠诗人（创作诗词4000余首）、话剧先驱和古乐泰斗，在诸多领域都取得了极高的成就。这处故居原有五进，现存四进，是无锡规模较大、保存较好的一座。今为顾毓琇纪念馆，展出顾毓琇的生平和成就。5. 缪公馆：缪公馆位于崇安区新生路7号，2011年被列为省保单位。近代政治人物缪斌（1902—1946）是无锡人，抗战期间卖身投靠日寇，1946年被判处死刑。1932年缪斌委托著名建筑师江应麟设计建造了这座公馆，抗战期间曾用作日本特务机关。外围青砖墙，从南门进入为太湖石所砌"五松坛"，后为清水砖砌两层洋楼，立面有混凝土罗马式立柱。
projects.content_en: The Former Residences of Celebrities in Wuxi include multiple provincial protected sites: Xue Huidong's Former Residence, Qian Zhongshu's Former Residence, Zhang Wentian's Former Residence, Gu Yuxiu's Former Residence, and Miao Mansion. 1. Xue Huidong's Former Residence: Located at No. 2 West Qianxi, Chong'an District, opposite the north gate of Xue Fucheng's Former Residence, designated a provincial protected site in 1995, today the Wuxi Local Records Office. Built from 1911 to 1917 by Xue Nanming, son of Xue Fucheng, in Baroque style, composed of a gate tower, main building, and west building—one of the earliest Western-style residences designed by Chinese. This residence was originally an office building when Xue Nanming co-founded a company, later used as the wedding new residence of his second son Xue Xuehai (1897-1965, style name Huidong) and Yuan Zhao, daughter of Yuan Shikai—folk-nicknamed the "Prince Consort's Mansion." 2. Qian Zhongshu's Former Residence: Located at Nos. 30 and 32 Xinjie Lane, Jiankang Road, Chong'an District, designated a provincial protected site in 2002, open 9:00-16:30 free of charge. The Jiangnan Qian family were descendants of Qian Liu, King of Wuyue, with talents emerging generation after generation and a profound family tradition. In 1923, Qian Zhongshu's grandfather Qian Futong prepared to build the "Shengwu Hall"; in 1926, his uncle Qian Sunqing continued construction. This residence includes front and rear courtyards, with the main buildings all seven bays wide, adopting Jiangnan Qing-style construction with partial Western style. In 1926, Qian Jihou added a building in the rear garden, called the "Plum Blossom Study." The three rooms east of the gate were respectively used as the family ancestral hall and the private school where Qian Zhongshu's father Qian Jibo lectured. Qian Zhongshu (1910-1998) spent his youth here until entering Tsinghua University in 1929. The whole residence is now the Qian Zhongshu Literature Museum. 3. Zhang Wentian's Former Residence: Located at No. 45 Tang Lane, Xueqian Street, Chong'an District, designated a provincial protected site in 2011, open 9:00-16:30 free of charge. Zhang Wentian, also known as Luo Fu, with ancestral home in Wuxi, was born in 1900 in Nanhui County (today's Pudong New Area, Shanghai). He was an important early leader of the Chinese Communist Party, playing a key role in determining Mao Zedong's leadership at the Zunyi Conference. Hailed as a "Red Professor"-style scholar-leader, he briefly served as General Secretary of the Party and voluntarily yielded the position three times—a story passed down as a good example. In 1959, Zhang Wentian was wrongly criticized at the Lushan Conference; during the Cultural Revolution he suffered brutal persecution. On August 25, 1975, he moved from Zhaoqing to Wuxi and lived here, dying on July 1, 1976. This is a two-story exposed-brick Western-style building, built in the 1930s; today a bust of Zhang Wentian stands in front of the building, with pictures and relics of Zhang Wentian's life displayed inside. 4. Gu Yuxiu's Former Residence: Located at No. 3 Xueqian Street, Chong'an District, designated a provincial protected site in 2011, open 9:00-16:30 free of charge. In the 31st year of Guangxu of the Qing (1905), Gu Weizhen built the "Baoshan Hall" for his son Gu Gengming. Gu Yuxiu (1902-2002), the second son of Gu Gengming, lived here for 14 years after birth, entering Tsinghua School in 1915. Gu Yuxiu excelled in both arts and sciences: his scientific research achievements were abundant, hailed by the international electrical engineering community as "the most contributor to modern electrical engineering theory"; he served as President of Central University, Dean of the School of Engineering at Tsinghua University, and professor at the University of Pennsylvania, with students everywhere; he was also a translator, novelist, and playwright, one of the first members of the Tsinghua Literature Society with Wen Yiduo and Liang Shiqiu, hailed as a literary elder, laureate poet (creating over 4,000 poems), pioneer of modern drama, and master of ancient music—achieving extremely high accomplishments in many fields. This residence originally had five bays, with four surviving today—a relatively large and well-preserved one in Wuxi. Today it is the Gu Yuxiu Memorial Hall, exhibiting Gu Yuxiu's life and achievements. 5. Miao Mansion: Located at No. 7 Xinsheng Road, Chong'an District, designated a provincial protected site in 2011. Modern political figure Miao Bin (1902-1946) was from Wuxi; during the War of Resistance against Japan he defected to the Japanese invaders and was sentenced to death in 1946. In 1932, Miao Bin commissioned famous architect Jiang Yinglin to design and build this mansion, which was used as a Japanese secret service agency during the war. Surrounded by exposed brick walls, entering from the south gate is the "Five Pine Altar" built of Taihu rocks, behind which is a two-story exposed-brick Western-style building with concrete Roman-style columns on the facade.

projects.name: 无锡县学旧址
projects.level: 第六批全国重点文物保护单位（2006年）
projects.level_en: 6th Batch National Key Cultural Heritage Site (2006)
projects.address: 崇安区学前街睦亲坊巷3号
projects.address_en: No. 3 Muqinfang Lane, Xueqian Street, Chong'an District
highlights: 无锡县学创建于北宋嘉祐三年1058年
清雍正四年1726年改成无锡金匮县学
民国年间作为无锡县立中学
现存戟门明伦堂和讲堂皆为清同治十三年1874年重建1982年重修
今为无锡碑刻陈列馆展出70余通碑刻
projects.content_zh: 无锡县学创建于北宋嘉祐三年（1058年），清雍正四年（1726年）改成无锡金匮县学，民国年间作为无锡县立中学。现存戟门、明伦堂和讲堂，皆为清同治十三年（1874年）重建，1982年重修。今为无锡碑刻陈列馆，展出70余通碑刻。
projects.content_en: Wuxi County School was founded in the 3rd year of Jiayou of the Northern Song (1058), changed to Wuxi-Jinkui County School in the 4th year of Yongzheng of the Qing (1726), and used as Wuxi County Middle School during the Republic era. The surviving Halberd Gate, Minglun Hall, and Lecture Hall were all rebuilt in the 13th year of Tongzhi of the Qing (1874) and repaired in 1982. Today it is the Wuxi Stele Carving Exhibition Hall, displaying over 70 steles.

projects.name: 无锡县商会旧址
projects.name_en: Site of Wuxi County Chamber of Commerce
projects.level: 第七批全国重点文物保护单位（2013年）
projects.level_en: 7th Batch National Key Cultural Heritage Site (2013)
projects.address: 崇安区解放北路汉昌西街6号
projects.address_en: No. 6 West Hanchang Street, North Jiefang Road, Chong'an District
projects.type_en: Former Chamber of Commerce / Modern Architecture
highlights: 清光绪三十一年1905年六月周舜卿和祝大椿等呈清政府发起创办锡金商会
1912年无锡金匮两县合并更名为无锡县商会
1917年6月22日商会大厦正式落成
这是两座二层西式建筑采用砖木结构正立面用砖砌成罗马柱外墙采用青红相间的清水砖
两座建筑如今得以原地保存现作为餐馆使用
projects.content_zh: 清光绪三十一年（1905年）六月，周舜卿和祝大椿等呈清政府发起创办锡金商会，1912年无锡、金匮两县合并，更名为无锡县商会。1917年6月22日商会大厦正式落成。这是两座二层西式建筑，采用砖木结构，正立面用砖砌成罗马柱，外墙采用青红相间的清水砖。两座建筑如今得以原地保存，现作为餐馆使用。
projects.content_en: In June of the 31st year of Guangxu of the Qing (1905), Zhou Shunqing, Zhu Dachun, and others petitioned the Qing government to initiate the founding of the Xijin Chamber of Commerce. In 1912, Wuxi and Jinkui counties merged, renamed the Wuxi County Chamber of Commerce. On June 22, 1917, the Chamber of Commerce building was officially completed. These are two two-story Western-style buildings, adopting brick-wood structure, with brick Roman columns on the front facade and exposed bricks in alternating blue and red on the exterior walls. The two buildings are today preserved in situ and currently used as restaurants.

projects.name: 京杭大运河无锡段
projects.name_en: Wuxi Section of Beijing-Hangzhou Grand Canal
projects.level: 世界文化遗产（2014年），含多处国保省保
projects.level_en: World Cultural Heritage (2014), including multiple national/provincial protected sites
projects.address_en: Along the Grand Canal in Wuxi urban area
highlights: 京杭大运河无锡段西起五牧口连接常州东至五七桥连接苏州全长39公里2014年列入世界文化遗产
沿河两岸古迹众多尤以环古城一段最为集中自南向北有南水仙庙窑群遗址清名桥西水仙庙和黄埠墩等
南水仙庙明初双忠祠祭祀文天祥部将麻士龙和尹玉清康熙二十二年1683年百姓在庙南建松滋王侯庙祭祀明嘉靖年间抗倭厘田有功的无锡知县王其勤将两庙合为一所
窑群遗址分布在运河东岸大窑路和伯渎港南岸有明清砖瓦窑遗址108处长约1.5公里保存较好的约19处2013年列为国保单位
清名桥明万历年间寄畅园主秦耀的儿子秦秦埏秦德修建两人号太清公和太宁公因此命名为清宁桥清道光间避皇帝旻宁的名讳改为清名桥全长43.3米全用花岗岩构筑是无锡市区现存最大的石拱桥
南禅寺始建于南朝梁武帝太清初年原名护国寺唐改称灵山寺北宋赐名福胜禅院俗称南禅寺寺内有七层八角的妙光塔北宋崇宁三年1104年宋徽宗赐名为运河航道转弯处和杨腰湾运河交会处的入城标志
茂新面粉厂1901年荣宗敬荣德生兄弟在此创建茂新面粉厂1937年遭到日军轰炸1946年荣毅仁奉父之命重建聘请上海华盖事务所设计工厂主体4层局部5层采用砖墙承重的钢木结构高大的红色砖墙与运河对岸低矮的灰色民居形成对比今为无锡民族工商业博物馆
西水仙庙位于茂新面粉厂北的西水墩上与无锡城北运河中的黄埠墩并称为地轴和天关是两处重要的地理坐标西水墩原名窑墩太保墩是古运河与梁溪河的分水处墩上曾建有明代太子太保秦金的别业荒废后邑人改建为关帝庙和水仙庙清初又改为刘侯庙祀明天启无锡知县刘五纬

黄埠墩位于城外西北古运河中心惠山浜出口处墩呈圆形仅200多平方米据传为春申君黄歇疏浚芙蓉湖时堆成因而得名明王永积锡山景物略称墩上有文昌阁环翠楼水月轩垂柳掩映不接不离登阁九峰环列风帆片片时过几案间梁章钜楹联丛话称皇甫墩在芙蓉湖中四面皆水飞楼缥缈极似西湖之湖心亭古代人们乘舟经过无锡常在此暂歇在墩上眺望锡惠两山景致绝佳文天祥曾登岛作过无锡诗明代海瑞称赞墩上环翠楼为临水玩山第一楼康熙乾隆两位皇帝都对此墩情有独钟南巡时曾在岛上驻扎并由此前往惠山乾隆还在清漪园仿黄埠墩堆筑了凤凰墩将玉泉山比作锡山万寿山比作惠山再现无锡的山水风光墩南建有运河公园东岸有接官亭
三里桥天主堂明崇祯十三年1640年意大利耶稣会士毕方济在此建房后屡毁屡建今天主堂建于清光绪十八年1892年也称若瑟堂坐东朝西采用砖木结构内部设2000多座位是江苏最大的天主教堂也是天主教南京教区无锡总铎区的总铎教堂
projects.content_zh: 京杭大运河无锡段西起五牧口连接常州，东至五七桥连接苏州，全长39公里，2014年列入世界文化遗产。沿河两岸古迹众多，尤以环古城一段最为集中，自南向北有南水仙庙、窑群遗址、清名桥、西水仙庙和黄埠墩等。1. 南水仙庙：南水仙庙位于运河西岸的南长街598号，坐西朝东，面对运河。明初这里是双忠祠，祭祀文天祥的部将麻士龙和尹玉，因在运河西岸的驿道上，被人们奉为水仙，俗称"南水仙庙"。清康熙二十二年（1683年）百姓在庙南建"松滋王侯庙"，祭祀明嘉靖年间抗倭、厘田有功的无锡知县王其勤，将两庙合为一所。太平天国时期庙被毁，清同治年间重建，自东向西有头门、二门（带戏台）、大殿、酒厅、茶厅、蚕师殿，以及北侧的双忠祠正殿、书厅等建筑，并保存着王其勤书写的"湖山胜概"石刻。庙后曾有供神灵栖息的憩园，现已不存。2. 窑群遗址：窑群遗址分布在运河东岸大窑路和伯渎港南岸，有明清砖、瓦窑遗址108处，长约1.5公里，保存较好的约19处，2013年列为国保单位。大窑路上建有无锡窑群遗址博物馆。3. 祝大椿故居（祝家花园）：祝大椿故居位于伯渎港117—127号，2006年列为省保单位。祝大椿（1855—1926）是无锡首位红顶商人，致力于发展缫丝、造纸、电器等民族工业，被誉为电气大王。他发迹后热心于社会公益和地方教育，捐资建造了多座桥梁和学校。他还在祖居两侧拓建住宅，成为东、中、西三路。现存中路三进、东路转盘楼和西路平房。4. 保安寺：保安寺位于塘南过渡房1—51号，1983年列为市保单位。寺庙始建于梁武帝大同初年，南宋孝宗赐"保安禅寺"匾，今仅存明嘉靖年间所建三间移迹殿的一间，采用砖石拱券结构，俗称无梁殿，内部曾供奉善治皮肤病的秽迹金刚。5. 清名桥：清名桥位于古运河与伯渎港（传为泰伯所凿）交汇处，明万历年间寄畅园主秦耀的儿子秦秦埏、秦德修建，两人号太清公和太宁公，因此命名为清宁桥，清道光年间避皇帝旻宁的名讳，改为清名桥。太平天国时期桥被拆毁，清同治八年（1869年）重建。清名桥全长43.3米，全用花岗岩构筑，宏伟简朴，是无锡市区现存最大的石拱桥。桥西北为清名桥历史文化街区，有镇塘庵、坎宫救熄会、钱同义旧宅和周氏余庆堂等古迹。6. 南禅寺：沿南长街一路向北，在原城南门运河向西转弯处，河北岸有南禅寺。寺庙始建于南朝梁武帝太清初年，原名护国寺，唐改称灵山寺，北宋赐名福胜禅院，俗称南禅寺。寺内有七层八角的妙光塔，北宋崇宁三年（1104年）宋徽宗赐名，为运河航道转弯处和杨腰湾运河交会处的入城标志。妙光塔屡毁屡建，今存塔心为明正统十四年（1449年）所建，1982年重修。7. 无锡中国民族工商业博物馆（茂新面粉厂旧址）：无锡中国民族工商业博物馆位于南长区振新路，2013年列为国保单位，9:00—16:30（周三闭馆）免费开放。1901年荣宗敬、荣德生兄弟在此创建茂新面粉厂，1937年遭到日军轰炸，1946年荣毅仁奉父之命重建，聘请上海华盖事务所设计。面粉厂东、北、南三面环水，水运便利，生产的"兵船"牌面粉畅销全国，荣氏兄弟被誉为"面粉大王"。工厂主体4层，局部5层，采用砖墙承重的钢木结构，高大的红色砖墙与运河对岸低矮的灰色民居形成对比。今为无锡民族工商业博物馆，内容丰富，值得一看。8. 西水仙庙（西水墩）：西水仙庙位于茂新面粉厂北的西水墩上，与无锡城北运河中的黄埠墩并称为"地轴"和"天关"，是两处重要的地理坐标。清光绪《无锡金匮县志》称："黄埠墩在运河中流寺塘泾（惠山浜）口。形家言，鹤势直下而益广，须以此砥之，故谓黄埠墩为天关，太保墩为地轴。"西水墩原名窑墩、太保墩，是古运河与梁溪河的分水处，墩上曾建有明代太子太保秦金的别业，荒废后邑人改建为关帝庙和水仙庙，清初又改为刘侯庙，祀明天启无锡知县刘五纬。太平天国时期墩上建筑被毁，同治、光绪年间重建，有工字大殿、内外戏台、天后宫、前后偏殿、娘娘殿和东西辕门等。9. 黄埠墩：黄埠墩位于城外西北古运河中心，惠山浜出口处，墩呈圆形，仅200多平方米，据传为春申君黄歇疏浚芙蓉湖时堆成，因而得名。明王永积《锡山景物略》称："墩上有文昌阁、环翠楼、水月轩，垂柳掩映，不接不离。登阁九峰环列，风帆片片，时过几案间。"梁章钜《楹联丛话》称："皇甫墩在芙蓉湖中，四面皆水，飞楼缥缈，极似西湖之湖心亭。窗户轩槛，皆九龙山翠所涵渲。登览胜概，甲于通邑。"古代人们乘舟经过无锡常在此暂歇，在墩上眺望锡、惠两山，景致绝佳。文天祥曾登岛作《过无锡》诗，明代海瑞称赞墩上环翠楼为"临水玩山第一楼"。康熙、乾隆两位皇帝都对此墩情有独钟，南巡时曾在岛上驻扎，并由此前往惠山；乾隆还在清漪园仿黄埠墩堆筑了凤凰墩，将玉泉山比作锡山、万寿山比作惠山，再现无锡的山水风光。墩南建有运河公园，东岸有接官亭。10. 三里桥天主堂：三里桥天主堂位于北塘区民主街86号，黄埠墩东，2006年列为省保单位。明崇祯十三年（1640年）意大利耶稣会士毕方济在此建房，后屡毁屡建。今天主堂建于清光绪十八年（1892年），也称若瑟堂，坐东朝西，采用砖木结构，内部设2000多座位，是江苏最大的天主教堂，也是天主教南京教区无锡总铎区的总铎教堂。后部钟楼1976年拆毁，2006年复建。
projects.content_en: The Wuxi Section of the Beijing-Hangzhou Grand Canal starts at Wumu Mouth in the west connecting Changzhou, ends at Wuqi Bridge in the east connecting Suzhou, with a total length of 39 km, inscribed on the World Cultural Heritage List in 2014. There are numerous historical sites along both banks, especially concentrated in the section around the ancient city; from south to north are the South Water Immortal Temple, Kiln Group Site, Qingming Bridge, West Water Immortal Temple, and Huangbu Dun. 1. South Water Immortal Temple: Located at No. 598 Nanchang Street on the west bank of the canal, facing west toward east, facing the canal. In the early Ming this was the Double Loyalty Shrine, sacrificing to Wen Tianxiang's generals Ma Shilong and Yin Yu; because it was on the post road west of the canal, people worshipped them as water immortals, commonly called the "South Water Immortal Temple." In the 22nd year of Kangxi of the Qing (1683), people built the "Songzi Wanghou Temple" south of the temple, sacrificing to Wang Qiqin, Wuxi County Magistrate in the Jiajing reign of the Ming who meritoriously fought Japanese pirates and clarified land taxes, merging the two temples into one. During the Taiping Rebellion the temple was destroyed; rebuilt during the Tongzhi reign of the Qing, from east to west there are the first gate, second gate (with stage), main hall, wine hall, tea hall, silkworm master hall, and the north Double Loyalty Shrine main hall, book hall, etc., preserving the stone carving "Lake and Mountain Scenery" written by Wang Qiqin. Behind the temple there was once a Qiyuan (Rest Garden) for deities to dwell, now no longer existing. 2. Kiln Group Site: Distributed on Dayao Road east of the canal and the south bank of Bodou Port, with 108 Ming-Qing brick and tile kiln sites, about 1.5 km long, with about 19 well-preserved ones, designated a national protected site in 2013. The Wuxi Kiln Group Site Museum is built on Dayao Road. 3. Former Residence of Zhu Dachun (Zhu Family Garden): Located at Nos. 117-127 Bodou Port, designated a provincial protected site in 2006. Zhu Dachun (1855-1926) was Wuxi's first red-topped merchant, devoted to developing national industries such as silk reeling, papermaking, and electrical appliances, hailed as the "Electrical King." After becoming wealthy, he was enthusiastic about social welfare and local education, donating to build many bridges and schools. He also expanded his residence on both sides of his ancestral home, forming east, middle, and west roads. Today the middle road's three bays, east road's revolving corridor building, and west road's bungalows survive. 4. Bao'an Temple: Located at Nos. 1-51 Tangnan Transitional Housing, designated a municipal protected site in 1983. The temple was first built in the early Datong reign of Emperor Wu of the Liang; Emperor Xiaozong of the Southern Song bestowed the plaque "Bao'an Chan Temple." Today only one bay of the three-bay Yiji Hall built during the Jiajing reign of the Ming survives, adopting a brick-stone arch structure, commonly called the Beamless Hall, which once enshrined the Huiji Vajra who was good at curing skin diseases. 5. Qingming Bridge: Located at the confluence of the ancient canal and Bodou Port (legendarily dug by Taibo), built during the Wanli reign of the Ming by Qin Yao's sons Qin Shan and Qin De, owners of Jichang Garden. Their hao were Taiqing Gong and Taining Gong, hence the name Qingning Bridge; during the Daoguang reign of the Qing, to avoid the taboo of Emperor Minning's name, it was changed to Qingming Bridge. During the Taiping Rebellion the bridge was demolished; rebuilt in the 8th year of Tongzhi of the Qing (1869). Qingming Bridge has a total length of 43.3 meters, entirely constructed of granite—grand and simple, the largest surviving stone arch bridge in Wuxi urban area. Northwest of the bridge is the Qingming Bridge Historical and Cultural Block, with historical sites such as Zhentang Nunnery, Kangong Firefighting Society, Qian Tongyi's Former Residence, and Zhou Family Yuqing Hall. 6. Nanchan Temple: Following Nanchang Street northward, at the westward turn of the canal at the former south city gate, on the north bank of the river is Nanchan Temple. The temple was first built in the early Taiqing reign of Emperor Wu of the Liang, originally named Huguo Temple; in the Tang renamed Lingshan Temple; in the Northern Song bestowed the name Fusheng Chan Temple, commonly called Nanchan Temple. Inside the temple is the seven-story octagonal Miaoguang Pagoda, named by Emperor Huizong of the Northern Song in the 3rd year of Chongning (1104), serving as the city-entry marker at the canal channel turn and the confluence of the Yangyaowan Canal. Miaoguang Pagoda was repeatedly destroyed and rebuilt; today's surviving pagoda core was built in the 14th year of Zhengtong of the Ming (1449), repaired in 1982. 7. Wuxi China National Industry and Commerce Museum (Former Site of Maoxin Flour Mill): Located on Zhenxin Road, Nanchang District, designated a national protected site in 2013, open 9:00-16:30 (closed Wednesdays) free of charge. In 1901, brothers Rong Zongjing and Rong Desheng founded the Maoxin Flour Mill here; it was bombed by the Japanese in 1937; in 1946 Rong Yiren, following his father's order, rebuilt it, hiring the Shanghai Huagai Firm for design. The flour mill is surrounded by water on east, north, and south sides, with convenient water transport; its "Warship" brand flour sold well nationwide, and the Rong brothers were hailed as the "Flour Kings." The factory main body is 4 stories, partially 5 stories, adopting a brick-wall load-bearing steel-wood structure; the tall red brick walls contrast with the low gray residences across the canal. Today it is the Wuxi National Industry and Commerce Museum, rich in content and worth a visit. 8. West Water Immortal Temple (Xishui Dun): Located on Xishui Dun north of the Maoxin Flour Mill, together with Huangbu Dun in the canal north of Wuxi city called the "Earth Axis" and "Heavenly Gate"—two important geographic coordinates. The Guangxu-era "Wuxi-Jinkui County Gazetteer" states: "Huangbu Dun is in the middle of the canal at the mouth of Sitang Jing (Huishan Brook). Fengshui practitioners say the crane momentum goes straight down and widens, needing this to砥 it, hence Huangbu Dun is called the Heavenly Gate, and Taibao Dun the Earth Axis." Xishui Dun was originally named Yaodun or Taibao Dun, the watershed between the ancient canal and the Liangxi River; on the墩 was once the villa of Qin Jin, Crown Prince's Tutor of the Ming; after falling into ruin, local people converted it into the Guandi Temple and Water Immortal Temple, and in the early Qing changed to the Liu Hou Temple, sacrificing to Liu Wuwei, Wuxi County Magistrate in the Tianqi reign of the Ming. During the Taiping Rebellion the buildings on the墩 were destroyed; rebuilt during the Tongzhi and Guangxu reigns, with the I-shaped main hall, inner and outer stages, Tianhou Palace, front and rear side halls, Niangniang Hall, and east and west gates. 9. Huangbu Dun: Located in the center of the ancient canal northwest of the city, at the mouth of Huishan Brook, the墩 is circular, only over 200 square meters, legendarily piled up when Lord Chunshen Huang Xie dredged Furong Lake, hence the name. Ming Wang Yongji's "Record of Scenic Spots of Xishan" states: "On the墩 are Wenchang Pavilion, Huancui Tower, and Shuiyue Pavilion, with weeping willows shading, neither connected nor separated. Climbing the pavilion, nine peaks surround in rows, with sails片片, sometimes passing between the desks." Liang Zhangju's "Collected Talks on Couplets" states: "Huangfu Dun is in Furong Lake, surrounded by water on all sides, with soaring towers ethereal, extremely like the Lake Heart Pavilion of West Lake. Windows and railings are all imbued with the green of the Nine Dragon Mountain. The panoramic views from climbing are the best in the whole county." In ancient times, people traveling by boat through Wuxi often rested here temporarily, gazing at the Xi and Hui mountains from the墩—excellent scenery. Wen Tianxiang once landed on the island and wrote the poem "Passing Wuxi"; in the Ming, Hai Rui praised the Huancui Tower on the墩 as the "Number One Tower for Viewing Mountains by Water." Both Emperors Kangxi and Qianlong had a special affection for this墩, stationing on the island during their southern tours and proceeding from there to Huishan; Qianlong also piled up the Phoenix Dun in the Qingyi Garden in imitation of Huangbu Dun, comparing Yuquan Mountain to Xishan and Wanshou Mountain to Huishan, reproducing Wuxi's landscape. South of the墩 is the Canal Park, and on the east bank is the Jieguan (Receiving Officials) Pavilion. 10. Sanliqiao Catholic Church: Located at No. 86 Minzhu Street, Beitang District, east of Huangbu Dun, designated a provincial protected site in 2006. In the 13th year of Chongzhen of the Ming (1640), Italian Jesuit Francesco Sambiasi built a house here, later repeatedly destroyed and rebuilt. Today's main church was built in the 18th year of Guangxu of the Qing (1892), also called St. Joseph's Church, facing west from the east, adopting brick-wood structure, with over 2,000 seats inside—the largest Catholic church in Jiangsu and the deanery church of the Wuxi Deanery of the Nanjing Diocese. The rear bell tower was demolished in 1976 and rebuilt in 2006.
