projects.address_en: Huishan Ancient Town, Beitang District
projects.ticket: 70元，五园通票170元，两日内有效（含锡惠公园、鼋头渚、梅园、蠡园和吟苑）
highlights: 锡惠公园位于北塘区惠山古镇以锡山惠山命名包括锡山全部、惠山东麓及连接两山的映山湖重要景点有惠山寺及其园林祠堂、寄畅园和锡山名胜等
惠山有多个古称据唐代陆羽游惠山寺记载老子枕中记作吴西神山南朝时多取北方山川郡邑之名取舜耕于历山之意称作历山顾欢吴地记作华山因山有九峰又称作九龙山或斗龙山传说晋僧慧照曾在此弘法还称作慧山最后一种称呼流传最广因慧惠相通最后定名惠山

惠山寺前身是南朝宋长史湛挺的历山草堂南朝宋景平元年423年舍宅为寺称华山精舍南朝梁大同三年537年建大雄宝殿寺名法云禅院因山中出青莲花又称慧山寺唐会昌年间寺毁大中元年847年重建唐乾符三年876年建陀罗尼经幢北宋至道二年996年赐额普利院北宋熙宁三年1070年建大白伞盖神咒幢北宋靖康元年1126年钦宗将普利禅院赐给李纲为功德院南宋绍兴年间宋高宗又赐给信安郡王孟忠厚元末明初寺庙屡遭火灾多次重建明永乐五年1407年重建大雄宝殿始称惠山寺禅院明正统十年1445年又毁于火风水家认为惠山寺坐西朝东右前方锡山高耸左前方却是平地右有青龙而左缺白虎因此火灾频发于是巡抚周忱用烧毁的瓦石在寺庙左前方堆筑了一座护山即今寄畅园西部假山的前身当时惠山寺的发展达到巅峰寺前左右遍布僧房有14座之多后来的碧山吟社寄畅园愚公谷等都是在这些僧房的基础上改建而成明天顺四年1460年僧楚光重修惠山寺明万历年间又毁于火邹迪光修复明清之际寺庙遭到破坏清康熙年间修复到乾隆年间达到鼎盛清咸丰十年1860年四月湘军与太平军在惠山激战寺庙又毁清同治四年1865年李鸿章在寺庙废墟上建昭忠祠祭祀激战中牺牲的湘军将士2002年开始修复惠山寺2004年开放
惠山寺背倚惠山从东面的古华山门起向西依次有唐宋经幢金刚殿日月池天王殿金莲桥御碑亭听松石床古银杏树和大雄宝殿等景点寺庙南北分布着大量的园林和祠堂
古华山门为惠山寺正门始建于清乾隆十五年1750年以迎接次年乾隆临幸惠山外面悬古华山门匾背面悬胜地名泉匾皆为古砖刻今门为2008年重建

唐宋经幢位于惠山寺山门外2013年第七批列为国保单位南侧经幢为唐乾符三年876年李端符建高6.26米底径1.48米塔身刻佛顶尊胜陀罗尼经李端符书北侧经幢为北宋熙宁三年1070年刘元规仿唐幢建高6.22米底径1.40米塔身刻大白伞盖神咒刻咒而不刻经是宋代以后的流行做法两幢大小形制基本相同皆分为幢基9级幢身1级和幢顶9级三部分每级都由整块青石雕成共19级幢基有三层束腰底层为须弥山中层为四只狮子上层为八座佛龛龛上有仰莲座上立八角形幢身高1.6米遍刻经文幢身上部的垫石和圆扁石上托仰莲瓣其上立束腰柱也刻有八座佛龛其上覆宝盖角隅雕力士头像其上又为一圆扁石上覆八角攒尖顶檐角高翘最上部为宝珠两座经幢幢身高大雕刻精美是江苏保存最好的经幢代表了唐宋石雕的艺术风格

寄畅园前身是明嘉靖六年1527年尚书秦金在沤寓僧房旧址修筑的凤谷行窝明嘉靖三十九年1560年凤谷行窝转给同宗的秦瀚秦梁父子明万历二十年1592年都察院右副都御史秦燿罢官回无锡大加拓建万历二十七年1599年完工取王羲之取欢仁智乐寄畅山水阴诗意改名寄畅园秦燿卒后园林分归四个儿子管理清康熙七年1668年前后秦德藻秦松龄父子聘请张南垣之侄张鉽合并改筑基本形成今日园貌雍正年间九王爷胤糖被治罪秦松龄长子秦道然担任王府总管受此牵连寄畅园没官南部被划出卖清乾隆元年1736年秦道然长子秦蕙田考中探花上书陈情乾隆将寄畅园发还由族中富户秦瑞熙出资修葺清乾隆十一年1748年秦道然聚族合议改园中嘉树堂为双孝祠将寄畅园变作宗祠成为公产避免再次没官清咸丰十年1860年兵火延烧园中建筑仅剩双孝祠和凌虚阁清光绪九年1883年秦宝瓒重建知鱼槛凌虚阁民国初拆掉倾圮的凌虚阁改建三层西式楼房此后陆续修复了清响斋清籁轩涵碧亭郁盘和含贞斋等1937年园林遭到日机轰炸北部破坏严重1952年秦氏将寄畅园捐给国家进行修复2000年又复建了园林东南部的凌虚阁卧云堂先月榭和游廊等秦燿时期园门朝北清康熙年间将园门改为朝东1954年拓宽惠山横街时园墙向西缩进3-7米园门也向北移动1955年开始以贞节祠南门作为主入口东门留而不开进入南门是一处庭院西侧墙上嵌康熙山色溪光和乾隆玉戛金枞原刻院中正堂外悬凤谷行窝匾内悬康熙松风水月匾为仿香雪海康熙同名碑刻重题由堂前游廊向西过洞门为秉礼堂庭院以水池为中心池南为秉礼堂其他三面设游廊廊壁嵌寄畅园法帖及续刻84方游廊西侧辟门通二泉书院经游廊东北角小门则可达含贞斋是当年园主的书房含贞斋东面对着近代堆筑的九狮峰峰南是二层的临梵阁可由假山登阁阁东为园林南部正堂卧云堂是主人雅集会客之所堂东尽处是一座方池池内有龙头吐水为园林的出水口池东特置造型优美的介如峰庭园南部建有御碑亭碑上刻乾隆所绘介如峰图和题诗院北是二层的凌虚阁可登阁欣赏园林内外景色寄畅园分为南部起居和北部山池两区以上为南部起居区园林的精华则在北部山池区过凌虚阁沿游廊向西是先月榭明代先月榭在池西可向东隔池欣赏月色到乾隆年间已移至池南站在榭前平台上北望南北狭长的锦汇漪景深丰富池东是知鱼槛七星桥桥后的水湾和挑出水面的涵碧亭池西是人工与天然相衬相映沿游廊折回东岸一路向北先后穿过郁盘和知鱼槛右侧墙壁嵌有寄畅园东岸刻左侧则可欣赏对岸的假山与矶岸东岸知鱼槛和西岸鹤步滩双双伸向水面将水池拦腰束住宛如腰身纤细的少女婀娜多姿清代园主常在知鱼槛欣赏优伶们在鹤步滩上演奏昆曲槛北一道长长的七星桥将池面隔为一大一小小池东北岸有涵碧亭和清籁廊掩住水尾悠远不尽过七星桥北岸为园林正厅嘉树堂站在堂前南望景致绝佳锦汇漪知鱼槛郁盘亭园中树木逐层呈现在它们后方远处山巅上还矗立着一座高塔将游人的思绪带出园外为园林借景的经典之笔寄畅园的高潮是水池西岸的大假山沿山共有四条路径一条在假山东侧贴山临池有石桥滩头和古树等突隐曲折为山水结合部位处理之佳例沿此路走回水池南岸可重温池边景致其西另有一条入山小径景致相对平淡行至山南右转向西走尽头一折又豁然开朗置身其中眼前是浑厚兀立的石壁脚下是叮咚流淌的清泉头顶是遮天蔽日的古木仿佛与尘世隔绝置身幽谷深林之间从山谷走出又回到嘉树堂前堂西有小路可登至山顶梅亭是全园的制高点和收束处坐在亭中园林内外的美景尽收眼底

碧山吟社明成化十八年1482年秦旭等十人在龙泉僧房旧址创建吟社效仿白居易等香山九老号为碧山十老尚书王恕王亻舆和吴宽都常与诸老唱和沈周为之绘碧山吟社雅集图成为当地的文化盛事明弘治七年1494年秦旭父子相继过世碧山吟社被豪家霸占1521年秦金与潘绪邵宝谋划重开吟社但豪家不肯松动直到明嘉靖三十三年1554年秦旭曾孙秦瀚协同当地士绅19人终于从豪家手中购回吟社大学士徐阶撰重复碧山吟社记陈彦生作复碧山吟社序文徵明题碧山吟社匾再次轰动县邑此后碧山吟社成为无锡的重要文化记忆不断有文士名流重开吟社文风诗韵延续至今2005年全面复建碧山吟社坐北朝南有两进庭院从尤祠向南先进入最北面的十老堂内有漆绘文徵明兰亭修禊图沿堂前檐廊向西为望益楼出楼向南为流觞山房由山房南门向西出庭院可看到秦瀚等人的摩崖石刻南侧是涵碧池东岸临水建濯缨轩池水向北伏流进入龙缝泉流向望益楼西北回到庭院进入碧山吟社正堂堂前庭院对假山南面是正门门厅东厢是诗台沿诗舍前廊一直向北东侧开吟社门仅设门头门外嵌文徵明碧山吟社砖刻碧山吟社南为春申涧相传春申君曾在此饮马是观瀑佳处继续向南通往阿炳墓和杜鹃园杜鹃是无锡市花皆为近年所建公园碧山吟社东面是胡文昭公祠祀宋代理学大家胡瑗清顺治年间借愚公谷旧址营建2005年重建祠北有莲池向东为映山湖传说秦始皇东巡时望气者以金陵太湖之间有天子气故掘而厌之陆羽游惠山寺记因此民间称此湖为秦王坞胡祠北为尊贤祠原在今陆子祠附近始建于宋元年间祀陆羽湛挺李绅三贤后陆续增祀华宝秦观尤袤倪瓒王绂邵宝和秦旭等改称尊贤祠清乾隆十六年1751年迁今址2005年重建华孝子祠尊贤祠北为华孝子祠祀东晋孝子华宝原在二泉西侧唐代迁今址为惠山祠堂群重点建筑2006年列为国保单位祠庙坐西朝东沿轴线展开东首为四面牌坊清乾隆十二年1747年建是一座盈顶方亭四面都为牌坊内外皆有题刻盈顶中央开天窗便于采光看清内部榜文亭内水井凿于1959年这种牌坊在无锡曾有四座包括史家弄顾可久祠顾氏牌坊已复建仓桥东堍秦金北四牌坊凤光桥秦氏世科南四牌坊今仅存一座具有较高的价值向西为一楼一门牌坊坊内为永锡堂始建于明成化二十一年14852004年重建堂西为承泽池和溯源桥建于明成化年间桥西为鼋池八角形池内南面螭首吐水北面螭首吸水通向金莲池故称双龙泉是惠山水系的重要枢纽池西为孝祖享堂建于明成化二十一年1485年清乾隆二十七年1762年重修享堂南壁嵌12方1982年重刻的真赏斋帖此帖当年是华夏请文徵明父子钩摹章藻刻石被誉为明代第一刻帖文徵明曾为华夏绘真赏斋图2005年在享堂北面增建碑廊享堂西面为成志楼始建于明弘治十七年1504年2005年重建楼前庭院花石秀美登楼可眺望锡山华孝子祠东南为至德祠祀泰伯始建于清乾隆三十年1765年1959年复建为惠山祠堂群重点建筑2006年列为国保单位至德祠北面自西向东还有李忠定祠祀抗金名将李纲始建于清康熙五年1666年2005年复建邹忠公祠祀宋学士邹浩附祀邹迪光邹德基父子邹迪光始建2005年复建张义士祠嵇留山祠祀清代忠烈嵇永仁始建于清雍正七年1729年2005年复建过郡马祠祀宋郡马过孟玉2005年复建由嵇留山祠北门出即回到惠山寺金刚殿结束游览
projects.content_zh: 锡惠公园位于北塘区惠山古镇，以锡山、惠山命名，包括锡山全部、惠山东麓及连接两山的映山湖，重要景点有惠山寺及其园林祠堂、寄畅园和锡山名胜等。1. 惠山寺：惠山有多个古称。据唐代陆羽《游惠山寺记》载：老子《枕中记》称作吴西神山；南朝时多取北方山川郡邑之名，取舜耕于历山之意称作历山；顾欢《吴地记》作华山；因山有九峰，又称作九龙山或斗龙山；传说晋僧慧照曾在此弘法，还称作慧山。最后一种称呼流传最广，因慧、惠相通，最后定名惠山。惠山寺前身是南朝宋长史湛挺的历山草堂，南朝宋景平元年（423年）舍宅为寺，称华山精舍。南朝梁大同三年（537年）建大雄宝殿，寺名法云禅院，因山中出青莲花，又称慧山寺。唐会昌年间寺毁，大中元年（847年）重建。唐乾符三年（876年）建陀罗尼经幢。北宋至道二年（996年）赐额"普利院"，北宋熙宁三年（1070年）建大白伞盖神咒幢。北宋靖康元年（1126年）钦宗将普利禅院赐给李纲为功德院。南宋绍兴年间，宋高宗又赐给信安郡王孟忠厚。元末明初，寺庙屡遭火灾，多次重建。明永乐五年（1407年）重建大雄宝殿，始称惠山寺禅院。明正统十年（1445年）又毁于火。风水家认为，惠山寺坐西朝东，右前方锡山高耸，左前方却是平地，右有青龙而左缺白虎，因此火灾频发。于是巡抚周忱用烧毁的瓦石在寺庙左前方堆筑了一座护山，即今寄畅园西部假山的前身。当时惠山寺的发展达到巅峰，寺前左右遍布僧房，有14座之多，后来的碧山吟社、寄畅园、愚公谷等都是在这些僧房的基础上改建而成。明天顺四年（1460年）僧楚光重修惠山寺，明万历年间又毁于火，邹迪光修复。明清之际寺庙遭到破坏，清康熙年间修复，到乾隆年间达到鼎盛。清咸丰十年（1860年）四月，湘军与太平军在惠山激战，寺庙又毁。清同治四年（1865年）李鸿章在寺庙废墟上建昭忠祠，祭祀激战中牺牲的湘军将士。2002年开始修复惠山寺，2004年开放。惠山寺背倚惠山，从东面的古华山门起，向西依次有唐宋经幢、金刚殿、日月池、天王殿、金莲桥、御碑亭、听松石床、古银杏树和大雄宝殿等景点。寺庙南北分布着大量的园林和祠堂。古华山门：为惠山寺正门，始建于清乾隆十五年（1750年），以迎接次年乾隆临幸惠山。外面悬"古华山门"匾，背面悬"胜地名泉"匾，皆为古砖刻。今门为2008年重建。2. 唐宋经幢：位于惠山寺山门外，2013年（第七批）列为国保单位。南侧经幢为唐乾符三年（876年）李端符建，高6.26米，底径1.48米，塔身刻《佛顶尊胜陀罗尼经》，李端符书。北侧经幢为北宋熙宁三年（1070年）刘元规仿唐幢建，高6.22米，底径1.40米，塔身刻《大白伞盖神咒》。刻咒而不刻经，是宋代以后的流行做法。两幢大小、形制基本相同，皆分为幢基9级、幢身1级和幢顶9级三部分，每级都由整块青石雕成，共19级。幢基有三层束腰，底层为须弥山，中层为四只狮子，上层为八座佛龛，龛上有仰莲座，上立八角形幢身，高1.6米，遍刻经文。幢身上部的垫石和圆扁石上托仰莲瓣，其上立束腰柱，也刻有八座佛龛，其上覆宝盖，角隅雕力士头像。其上又为一圆扁石，上覆八角攒尖顶，檐角高翘，最上部为宝珠。两座经幢幢身高大，雕刻精美，是江苏保存最好的经幢，代表了唐、宋石雕的艺术风格。3. 寄畅园：过香花桥向北为寄畅园南门，门匾集自乾隆书法，1988年（第三批）列为国保单位。寄畅园前身是明嘉靖六年（1527年）尚书秦金在"沤寓"僧房旧址修筑的凤谷行窝，明嘉靖三十九年（1560年）凤谷行窝转给同宗的秦瀚、秦梁父子。明万历二十年（1592年）都察院右副都御史秦燿罢官，回无锡大加拓建，万历二十七年（1599年）完工，取王羲之"取欢仁智乐，寄畅山水阴"诗意，改名寄畅园。秦燿卒后，园林分归四个儿子管理。清康熙七年（1668年）前后，秦德藻、秦松龄父子聘请张南垣之侄张鉽合并改筑，基本形成今日园貌。雍正年间，九王爷胤糖被治罪，秦松龄长子秦道然担任王府总管，受此牵连，寄畅园没官，南部被划出卖。清乾隆元年（1736年）秦道然长子秦蕙田考中探花，上书陈情，乾隆将寄畅园发还，由族中富户秦瑞熙出资修葺。清乾隆十一年（1748年）秦道然聚族合议，改园中嘉树堂为双孝祠，将寄畅园变作宗祠成为公产，避免再次没官。清咸丰十年（1860年）兵火延烧，园中建筑仅剩双孝祠和凌虚阁。清光绪九年（1883年）秦宝瓒重建知鱼槛、凌虚阁。民国初拆掉倾圮的凌虚阁，改建三层西式楼房。此后陆续修复了清响斋、清籁轩、涵碧亭、郁盘和含贞斋等。1937年园林遭到日机轰炸，北部破坏严重。1952年秦氏将寄畅园捐给国家，进行修复，2000年又复建了园林东南部的凌虚阁、卧云堂、先月榭和游廊等。秦燿时期园门朝北，清康熙年间将园门改为朝东，1954年拓宽惠山横街时，园墙向西缩进3—7米，园门也向北移动。1955年开始以贞节祠南门作为主入口，东门留而不开。进入南门是一处庭院，西侧墙上嵌康熙"山色溪光"和乾隆"玉戛金枞"原刻。院中正堂外悬"凤谷行窝"匾，内悬康熙"松风水月"匾，为仿香雪海康熙同名碑刻重题。由堂前游廊向西，过洞门为秉礼堂庭院，以水池为中心，池南为秉礼堂，其他三面设游廊，廊壁嵌《寄畅园法帖》及续刻84方。游廊西侧辟门通二泉书院，经游廊东北角小门则可达含贞斋，是当年园主的书房。含贞斋东面对着近代堆筑的九狮峰，峰南是二层的临梵阁，可由假山登阁。阁东为园林南部正堂卧云堂，是主人雅集会客之所，堂东尽处是一座方池，池内有龙头吐水，为园林的出水口。池东特置造型优美的介如峰。庭园南部建有御碑亭，碑上刻乾隆所绘《介如峰图》和题诗。院北是二层的凌虚阁，可登阁欣赏园林内外景色。寄畅园分为南部起居和北部山池两区，以上为南部起居区，园林的精华则在北部山池区。过凌虚阁沿游廊向西是先月榭。明代先月榭在池西，可向东隔池欣赏月色，到乾隆年间已移至池南。站在榭前平台上北望，南北狭长的锦汇漪景深丰富，池东是知鱼槛、七星桥、桥后的水湾和挑出水面的涵碧亭，池西是人工与天然相衬相映。沿游廊折回东岸，一路向北，先后穿过郁盘和知鱼槛，右侧墙壁嵌有《寄畅园东岸刻》，左侧则可欣赏对岸的假山与矶岸。东岸知鱼槛和西岸鹤步滩双双伸向水面，将水池拦腰束住，宛如腰身纤细的少女，婀娜多姿。清代园主常在知鱼槛欣赏优伶们在鹤步滩上演奏昆曲。槛北一道长长的七星桥将池面隔为一大一小，小池东北岸有涵碧亭和清籁廊，掩住水尾，悠远不尽。过七星桥，北岸为园林正厅嘉树堂。站在堂前南望，景致绝佳，锦汇漪、知鱼槛、郁盘亭、园中树木逐层呈现，在它们后方，远处山巅上还矗立着一座高塔，将游人的思绪带出园外，为园林借景的经典之笔。寄畅园的高潮是水池西岸的大假山，沿山共有四条路径。一条在假山东侧，贴山临池，有石桥、滩头和古树等，突隐曲折，为山水结合部位处理之佳例。沿此路走回水池南岸，可重温池边景致；其西另有一条入山小径，景致相对平淡。行至山南右转，向西走尽头，一折又豁然开朗。置身其中，眼前是浑厚兀立的石壁，脚下是叮咚流淌的清泉，头顶是遮天蔽日的古木，仿佛与尘世隔绝，置身幽谷深林之间。从山谷走出，又回到嘉树堂前。堂西有小路可登至山顶梅亭，是全园的制高点和收束处，坐在亭中，园林内外的美景尽收眼底。4. 天下第二泉：庭院占地805平方米，2006年（第六批）列为国保单位。二泉开凿于唐大历五年（770年）左右。惠山泉水来自降雨，经岩根松隙过滤，含矿物质丰富，色清味醇，被茶圣陆羽（733—804）品定为天下第二。稍后刘伯刍（755—815）再评天下名泉，又将其定为第二，从此奠定了"天下第二泉"的地位。李绅曾向李德裕推荐二泉水，李德裕千里运水煮茶。宋徽宗将二泉水列为贡品，每月进贡100坛。元代很多人不远千里汲水，"舟车络绎，水陆并运，但见瓶盎樽缶，交错于道，汲取无虚日"（王永积《锡山景物略》）。明正德十三年（1518年）文徵明与蔡羽、汤珍、王守、王宠等到惠山茶会，绘《惠山茶会图》。走下竹炉山房门厅，南面院中即为二泉亭，三面开敞，其西墙壁上镶三排石刻。上为赵孟頫书"天下第二泉"，中为明万历四年（1576年）王球书《修泉亭记》，下为清雍正八年（1730年）杜诏记、王澍书《重修惠山泉亭记》、宋之晋《天下第二泉说》及清嘉庆八年（1803年）顾皋《天下第二泉碑记》。亭中池为上池与中池。上池深1.94米，井口八边形，中池深约1米，井口四边形，象征天圆地方。两池相距0.65米，井壁间有孔相通，井口皆围以青石井栏。二泉亭向西拾级而上为陆子祠，供奉茶圣陆羽，祠南有山道，向西可登惠山头茅峰。二泉亭向东为漪澜堂，是院内主堂，近年重建，内设与二泉有关的11位历代名人展。堂东为长方形的下池，凿于北宋明道年间（1032—1033），池西石螭首出自明代良工之手，雕刻精良。堂北院墙上镶清雍正六年（1728年）王澍"天下第二泉"等六篇题刻。下池东侧墙边是一组太湖石，原在明人顾可学惠岩小筑中，乾隆年间移至二泉庭院，称鳌鱼观音石，上有三段铭文。墙东南角开门，为二泉庭院门头。由漪澜堂向南为尤文简公祠，供南宋礼部尚书尤袤，清光绪十六年（1890年）尤侗筹建，为惠山祠堂群重点建筑，2006年被列为国保单位。尤祠坐北朝南，最北一进为万卷楼，二楼面北设落地长窗，为观赏二泉庭院佳处，楼西堆假山，楼南天井中有遂初泉。天井南为遂初堂，堂南为祠门。出祠门向南为碧山吟社。5. 碧山吟社：明成化十八年（1482年）秦旭等十人在龙泉僧房旧址创建吟社，效仿白居易等"香山九老"，号为"碧山十老"，尚书王恕、王亻舆和吴宽都常与诸老唱和，沈周为之绘《碧山吟社雅集图》，成为当地的文化盛事。明弘治七年（1494年）秦旭父子相继过世，碧山吟社被豪家霸占。1521年秦金与潘绪、邵宝谋划重开吟社，但豪家不肯松动，直到明嘉靖三十三年（1554年）秦旭曾孙秦瀚协同当地士绅19人，终于从豪家手中购回吟社，大学士徐阶撰《重复碧山吟社记》，陈彦生作《复碧山吟社序》，文徵明题"碧山吟社"匾，再次轰动县邑。此后，碧山吟社成为无锡的重要文化记忆，不断有文士名流重开吟社，文风诗韵延续至今，2005年全面复建。碧山吟社坐北朝南，有两进庭院。从尤祠向南，先进入最北面的十老堂，内有漆绘文徵明《兰亭修禊图》。沿堂前檐廊向西为望益楼，出楼向南为流觞山房。由山房南门向西出庭院，可看到秦瀚等人的摩崖石刻，南侧是涵碧池，东岸临水建濯缨轩，池水向北伏流进入龙缝泉，流向望益楼西北。回到庭院进入碧山吟社正堂，堂前庭院对假山，南面是正门门厅，东厢是诗台。沿诗舍前廊一直向北，东侧开吟社门，仅设门头，门外嵌文徵明"碧山吟社"砖刻。碧山吟社南为春申涧，相传春申君曾在此饮马，是观瀑佳处。继续向南通往阿炳墓和杜鹃园（杜鹃是无锡市花），皆为近年所建公园。碧山吟社东面是胡文昭公祠，祀宋代理学大家胡瑗，清顺治年间借愚公谷旧址营建，2005年重建。祠北有莲池，向东为映山湖，传说秦始皇东巡时，"望气者以金陵太湖之间有天子气，故掘而厌之"（陆羽《游惠山寺记》），因此民间称此湖为秦王坞。胡祠北为尊贤祠，原在今陆子祠附近，始建于宋元年间，祀陆羽、湛挺、李绅三贤，后陆续增祀华宝、秦观、尤袤、倪瓒、王绂、邵宝和秦旭等，改称尊贤祠，清乾隆十六年（1751年）迁今址，2005年重建。华孝子祠：尊贤祠北为华孝子祠，祀东晋孝子华宝，原在二泉西侧，唐代迁今址，为惠山祠堂群重点建筑，2006年列为国保单位。祠庙坐西朝东，沿轴线展开。东首为四面牌坊，清乾隆十二年（1747年）建，是一座盈顶方亭，四面都为牌坊，内外皆有题刻，盈顶中央开天窗，便于采光看清内部榜文。亭内水井凿于1959年。这种牌坊在无锡曾有四座，包括史家弄顾可久祠顾氏牌坊（已复建）、仓桥东堍秦金北四牌坊、凤光桥秦氏世科南四牌坊，今仅存一座，具有较高的价值。向西为一楼一门牌坊，坊内为永锡堂，始建于明成化二十一年（1485），2004年重建。堂西为承泽池和溯源桥，建于明成化年间。桥西为鼋池，八角形，池内南面螭首吐水，北面螭首吸水，通向金莲池，故称双龙泉，是惠山水系的重要枢纽。池西为孝祖享堂，建于明成化二十一年（1485年），清乾隆二十七年（1762年）重修。享堂南壁嵌12方1982年重刻的《真赏斋帖》，此帖当年是华夏请文徵明父子钩摹、章藻刻石，被誉为"明代第一刻帖"，文徵明曾为华夏绘《真赏斋图》。2005年在享堂北面增建碑廊。享堂西面为成志楼，始建于明弘治十七年（1504年），2005年重建，楼前庭院花石秀美，登楼可眺望锡山。华孝子祠东南为至德祠，祀泰伯，始建于清乾隆三十年（1765年），1959年复建，为惠山祠堂群重点建筑，2006年列为国保单位。至德祠北面，自西向东还有李忠定祠，祀抗金名将李纲，始建于清康熙五年（1666年），2005年复建；邹忠公祠祀宋学士邹浩，附祀邹迪光、邹德基父子，邹迪光始建，2005年复建；张义士祠、嵇留山祠祀清代忠烈嵇永仁，始建于清雍正七年（1729年），2005年复建；过郡马祠祀宋郡马过孟玉，2005年复建。由嵇留山祠北门出，即回到惠山寺金刚殿，结束游览。
projects.content_en: Xihui Park is located in Huishan Ancient Town, Beitang District, named after Xishan (Tin Mountain) and Huishan (Kindness Mountain). It includes all of Xishan, the eastern foot of Huishan, and the Yingshan Lake connecting the two mountains. Important scenic spots include Huishan Temple and its gardens and ancestral halls, Jichang Garden, and Xishan scenic spots. 1. Huishan Temple: Huishan has several ancient names. According to Tang Lu Yu's "Record of Visiting Huishan Temple": Laozi's "Record of the Pillow" called it Wuxi West Divine Mountain; during the Southern Dynasties, names from northern mountains and commanderies were often adopted, taking the meaning of Shun plowing at Lishan, it was called Lishan; Gu Huan's "Record of Wu Region" called it Huashan (Flower Mountain); because the mountain has nine peaks, it was also called Jiulong Mountain (Nine Dragons) or Doulong Mountain; legend says Jin monk Huizhao once propagated Buddhism here, so it was also called Huishan (Wisdom Mountain). The last name spread most widely; because hui (wisdom) and hui (kindness) are interchangeable, it was finally named Huishan. Huishan Temple's predecessor was the Lishan Thatched Cottage of Zhan Ting, Chief Clerk of the Liu Song in the Southern Dynasties; in the 1st year of Jingping of the Liu Song (423), he donated his residence as a temple, called Huashan Jingshe (Flower Mountain Retreat). In the 3rd year of Datong of the Southern Dynasties Liang (537), the Mahavira Hall was built, with the temple name Fayun Chan Yuan, also called Huishan Temple because green lotuses grew in the mountain. During the Huichang reign of the Tang, the temple was destroyed; rebuilt in the 1st year of Dazhong (847). In the 3rd year of Qianfu of the Tang (876), the Dharani Pillar was built. In the 2nd year of Zhidao of the Northern Song (996), the temple was granted the plaque "Puli Courtyard"; in the 3rd year of Xining of the Northern Song (1070), the Great White Umbrella Divine Spell Pillar was built. In the 1st year of Jingkang of the Northern Song (1126), Emperor Qinzong granted Puli Chan Courtyard to Li Gang as a merit courtyard. During the Shaoxing reign of the Southern Song, Emperor Gaozong granted it to Meng Zhonghou, Prince of Xin'an. At the end of the Yuan and beginning of the Ming, the temple suffered repeated fires and was rebuilt multiple times. In the 5th year of Yongle of the Ming (1407), the Mahavira Hall was rebuilt, beginning to be called Huishan Temple Chan Courtyard. In the 10th year of Zhengtong of the Ming (1445), it was destroyed by fire again. Fengshui masters believed that Huishan Temple faces west with its back to east, with Xishan towering at the right front but flat ground at the left front—having the Azure Dragon on the right but lacking the White Tiger on the left, hence frequent fires. So Governor Zhou Xun piled the burned tiles and stones into a protective mountain in front of the temple's left side—the predecessor of today's western rockery in Jichang Garden. At that time Huishan Temple reached its peak, with monk rooms spread all around in front of the temple, as many as 14; later Bishan Poetry Society, Jichang Garden, and Yugong Valley were all rebuilt on the basis of these monk rooms. In the 4th year of Tianshun of the Ming (1460), monk Chuguang repaired Huishan Temple; during the Wanli reign it was destroyed by fire again and repaired by Zou Diguang. At the Ming-Qing transition the temple was damaged; repaired during the Kangxi reign of the Qing, reaching its peak during the Qianlong reign. In the 10th year of Xianfeng of the Qing (1860), in April, the Xiang Army and Taiping Army fought fiercely at Huishan, and the temple was destroyed again. In the 4th year of Tongzhi of the Qing (1865), Li Hongzhang built the Zhaozhong (Loyal Martyrs) Shrine on the temple ruins, sacrificing to the Xiang Army soldiers who died in the fierce battle. Restoration of Huishan Temple began in 2002 and opened in 2004. Huishan Temple backs onto Huishan; starting from the ancient Huashan Gate on the east, going west are successively the Tang-Song Dharani Pillars, Vajra Hall, Sun-Moon Pond, Heavenly King Hall, Golden Lotus Bridge, Imperial Stele Pavilion, Listening-to-Pine Stone Bed, Ancient Ginkgo Tree, and Mahavira Hall. North and south of the temple are distributed numerous gardens and ancestral halls. Ancient Huashan Gate: the main gate of Huishan Temple, first built in the 15th year of Qianlong of the Qing (1750) to welcome Emperor Qianlong's visit to Huishan the following year. Outside hangs the plaque "Ancient Huashan Gate," inside hangs the plaque "Famous Scenic Spot and Famous Spring," both ancient brick carvings. Today's gate was rebuilt in 2008. 2. Tang-Song Dharani Pillars: located outside the Huishan Temple gate, designated a national protected site in 2013 (7th batch). The south pillar was built by Li Duanfu in the 3rd year of Qianfu of the Tang (876), 6.26 meters high, base diameter 1.48 meters, with the pillar body carved with the "Buddha's Top Superior Victorious Dharani Sutra," written by Li Duanfu. The north pillar was built by Liu Yuangui in imitation of the Tang pillar in the 3rd year of Xining of the Northern Song (1070), 6.22 meters high, base diameter 1.40 meters, with the pillar body carved with the "Great White Umbrella Divine Spell." Carving spells rather than sutras was a popular practice after the Song Dynasty. The two pillars are basically the same in size and form, each divided into three parts: 9-level pillar base, 1-level pillar body, and 9-level pillar top, each level carved from a single piece of bluestone, totaling 19 levels. The pillar base has three layers of waisted sections: the bottom layer is Mount Sumeru, the middle layer is four lions, the upper layer is eight Buddhist niches; above the niches is an upward-lotus seat, on which stands the octagonal pillar body, 1.6 meters high, covered with carved scriptures. Above the pillar body, the cushion stone and round flat stone support upward-lotus petals, on which stands a waisted column also carved with eight Buddhist niches, covered by a treasure canopy with guardian deity head carvings at the corners. Above that is another round flat stone, covered by an octagonal pyramidal roof with high upturned eaves, and at the very top is a precious pearl. The two dharani pillars are tall with exquisite carvings—the best-preserved dharani pillars in Jiangsu, representing the artistic style of Tang and Song stone carving. 3. Jichang Garden: Crossing the Fragrant Flower Bridge northward is the south gate of Jichang Garden, with the gate plaque collected from Qianlong's calligraphy, designated a national protected site in 1988 (3rd batch). Jichang Garden's predecessor was the Fenggu Xingwo (Phoenix Valley Travel Nest) built in the 6th year of Jiajing of the Ming (1527) by Minister Qin Jin on the site of the "Ouyu" monk room. In the 39th year of Jiajing (1560), Fenggu Xingwo was transferred to his clansmen Qin Han and Qin Liang. In the 20th year of Wanli of the Ming (1592), Qin Yao, Vice Censor-in-Chief of the Censorate, was dismissed from office and returned to Wuxi to greatly expand it, completed in the 27th year of Wanli (1599), taking the meaning from Wang Xizhi's "finding joy in benevolence and wisdom, finding comfort in mountains and waters" poetry, renaming it Jichang Garden (Comfortable Garden). After Qin Yao's death, the garden was divided among four sons. Around the 7th year of Kangxi of the Qing (1668), Qin Dezao and Qin Songling father and son hired Zhang Shi, nephew of Zhang Nanyuan, to merge and rebuild it, basically forming today's garden appearance. During the Yongzheng reign, the Ninth Prince Yintang was convicted; Qin Songling's eldest son Qin Daoran served as the prince's steward and was implicated, so Jichang Garden was confiscated and its southern part sold off. In the 1st year of Qianlong of the Qing (1736), Qin Daoran's eldest son Qin Huitian passed the third-place exam (tanhua) and submitted a memorial appealing; Qianlong returned Jichang Garden, with wealthy clansman Qin Ruixi funding the repair. In the 11th year of Qianlong (1748), Qin Daoran gathered the clan to discuss and changed the Jiashu Hall in the garden into the Shuangxiao (Double Filial Piety) Shrine, turning Jichang Garden into a clan ancestral hall as public property to avoid future confiscation. In the 10th year of Xianfeng (1860), war fires spread, leaving only the Shuangxiao Shrine and Lingxu Pavilion in the garden. In the 9th year of Guangxu (1883), Qin Baozan rebuilt the Zhiyu (Knowing Fish) Threshold and Lingxu Pavilion. In the early Republic, the crumbling Lingxu Pavilion was demolished and replaced with a three-story Western-style building. Thereafter, Qingxiang Studio, Qinglai Studio, Hanbi Pavilion, Yupan, and Hanzhen Studio were successively restored. In 1937 the garden was bombed by Japanese aircraft, with severe damage to the northern part. In 1952 the Qin family donated Jichang Garden to the state for restoration; in 2000 the Lingxu Pavilion, Woyun Hall, Xianyue Pavilion, and corridors in the southeastern part of the garden were rebuilt. During Qin Yao's period the garden gate faced north; during the Kangxi reign it was changed to face east; in 1954 when widening Huishan Heng Street, the garden wall was indented 3-7 meters westward and the gate moved northward. From 1955, the south gate of the Chastity Shrine was used as the main entrance, with the east gate kept but not opened. Entering the south gate is a courtyard, with the west wall embedded with Kangxi's "Mountain Colors and Stream Light" and Qianlong's "Jade Clacking and Gold Thumping" original carvings. The main hall in the courtyard hangs the plaque "Fenggu Xingwo" outside, and inside hangs Kangxi's "Pine Wind and Water Moon" plaque, re-inscribed in imitation of Kangxi's same-named stele at Xiangxuehai. From the hall's front corridor westward, through a cave gate is the Bingli Hall courtyard, centered on a pond, with Bingli Hall south of the pond and corridors on the other three sides; the corridor walls are embedded with 84 pieces of the "Jichang Garden Calligraphy Album" and its continuation. A door on the west side of the corridor leads to the Erquan (Second Spring) Academy; through a small door at the northeast corner of the corridor reaches Hanzhen Studio, the garden master's study in those years. East of Hanzhen Studio faces the modernly piled Nine Lions Peak; south of the peak is the two-story Linfan Pavilion, climbable via rockery. East of the pavilion is the southern main hall Woyun Hall, where the master entertained guests; at the east end of the hall is a square pond with a dragon head spouting water—the garden's water outlet. East of the pond is the exquisitely shaped Jieru Peak. In the southern part of the courtyard is the Imperial Stele Pavilion, with the stele carved with Qianlong's painting "Jieru Peak" and inscribed poems. North of the courtyard is the two-story Lingxu Pavilion, climbable to appreciate the scenery inside and outside the garden. Jichang Garden is divided into the southern living quarters and the northern mountain-pond area; the above is the southern living area, while the essence of the garden is in the northern mountain-pond area. Passing Lingxu Pavilion and following the corridor westward is the Xianyue (First Moon) Pavilion. In the Ming, Xianyue Pavilion was west of the pond, allowing appreciation of the moonlight across the pond eastward; by the Qianlong reign it had been moved south of the pond. Standing on the platform in front of the pavilion and looking north, the north-south elongated Jinhui Yi (Splendid Gathering Ripple) has rich depth; east of the pond are the Zhiyu Threshold, Seven-Star Bridge, the water bay behind the bridge, and the Hanbi Pavilion cantilevering over the water; west of the pond is the contrast between artificial and natural. Following the corridor back to the east bank, going northward, one passes successively through Yupan and Zhiyu Threshold; the right wall is embedded with the "Jichang Garden East Bank Carvings," while the left side allows appreciation of the opposite rockery and rocky shore. The east bank's Zhiyu Threshold and the west bank's Hebu (Crane Step) Beach both extend toward the water, cinching the pond at the waist like a slender-waisted young girl, graceful and charming. Qing-dynasty garden masters often enjoyed actors performing Kunqu opera on Hebu Beach from the Zhiyu Threshold. North of the threshold, a long Seven-Star Bridge divides the pond into a large and small part; on the northeast bank of the small pond are the Hanbi Pavilion and Qinglai Corridor, concealing the water's end with distant endlessness. Crossing the Seven-Star Bridge, the north bank is the garden's main hall Jiashu Hall. Standing in front of the hall and looking south, the scenery is superb: Jinhui Yi, Zhiyu Threshold, Yupan Pavilion, and garden trees appear layer by layer; behind them, a tall pagoda still stands on the distant mountain peak, carrying the visitor's thoughts beyond the garden—a classic example of garden borrowed scenery. The climax of Jichang Garden is the large rockery west of the pond, with four paths along the mountain. One path is on the east side of the rockery, hugging the mountain by the pond, with stone bridges, beaches, and ancient trees, hidden and winding—an excellent example of handling the mountain-water junction. Following this path back to the south bank of the pond allows revisiting the pond-side scenery; west of it is another mountain path with relatively plain scenery. Reaching the south of the mountain and turning right, going west to the end, a turn suddenly opens up. Inside, one sees thick and towering stone walls, gurgling clear springs underfoot, and ancient trees blocking the sky overhead—as if cut off from the mortal world, placed in a deep valley and dense forest. Exiting the valley, one returns to Jiashu Hall. West of the hall is a path to climb to the Plum Pavilion at the mountain top—the highest point and concluding place of the whole garden; sitting in the pavilion, the beautiful scenery inside and outside the garden is fully visible. 4. The Second Spring Under Heaven: The courtyard covers 805 square meters, designated a national protected site in 2006 (6th batch). The Second Spring was excavated around the 5th year of Dali of the Tang (770). Huishan spring water comes from rainfall, filtered through rock roots and pine gaps, rich in minerals, clear in color and mellow in taste, ranked as the second best under heaven by the Tea Sage Lu Yu (733-804). Later Liu Bochou (755-815) re-evaluated famous springs under heaven and also ranked it second, hence establishing its status as "The Second Spring Under Heaven." Li Shen once recommended the Second Spring water to Li Deyu, who transported water a thousand li to boil tea. Emperor Huizong of the Northern Song listed the Second Spring water as a tribute, paying 100 jars monthly. In the Yuan Dynasty, many people traveled a thousand li to draw water: "boats and carts came and went, transported by land and water, only to see jars and bottles crisscrossing the road, drawing water without an empty day" (Wang Yongji, "Record of Scenic Spots of Xishan"). In the 13th year of Zhengde of the Ming (1518), Wen Zhengming, together with Cai Yu, Tang Zhen, Wang Shou, and Wang Chong, had a tea gathering at Huishan and painted the "Huishan Tea Gathering Painting." Descending the Zhulu Mountain Cottage gate hall, the south courtyard is the Second Spring Pavilion, open on three sides; its west wall is embedded with three rows of stone carvings. The top is Zhao Mengfu's calligraphy "The Second Spring Under Heaven"; the middle is Wang Qiu's "Record of Repairing the Spring Pavilion" in the 4th year of Wanli of the Ming (1576); the bottom is Du Zhao's record and Wang Shu's calligraphy "Record of Rebuilding the Huishan Spring Pavilion" in the 8th year of Yongzheng of the Qing (1730), Song Zhijin's "On the Second Spring Under Heaven," and Gu Gao's "Record of the Second Spring Under Heaven Stele" in the 8th year of Jiaqing of the Qing (1803). The pond in the pavilion is the upper pond and middle pond. The upper pond is 1.94 meters deep with an octagonal well mouth; the middle pond is about 1 meter deep with a quadrilateral well mouth—symbolizing the round heaven and square earth. The two ponds are 0.65 meters apart, with holes connecting the well walls, and both well mouths surrounded by bluestone railings. From the Second Spring Pavilion, climbing steps westward is the Luzi (Lu Yu) Shrine, enshrining the Tea Sage Lu Yu; south of the shrine is a mountain path, westward可 climb to the first peak of Huishan. East of the Second Spring Pavilion is the Yilan (Ripple) Hall, the main hall of the courtyard, rebuilt in recent years, with an exhibition of 11 historical figures related to the Second Spring. East of the hall is the rectangular lower pond, excavated during the Mingdao reign of the Northern Song (1032-1033); the stone chi-dragon head on the west side of the pond was made by a skilled Ming craftsman, exquisitely carved. On the north courtyard wall are embedded six inscriptions including Wang Shu's "The Second Spring Under Heaven" in the 6th year of Yongzheng of the Qing (1728). By the east wall of the lower pond is a group of Taihu rocks, originally in Gu Kexue's Huiyan Small Cottage of the Ming, moved to the Second Spring courtyard during the Qianlong reign, called the Ao Fish Guanyin Stone, with three inscriptions. A door opens at the southeast corner of the wall, serving as the courtyard gate. From Yilan Hall southward is the You Wenjian (You Mao) Shrine, enshrining You Mao, Minister of Rites of the Southern Song, built by You Dong in the 16th year of Guangxu of the Qing (1890), a key building of the Huishan Ancestral Hall Complex, designated a national protected site in 2006. The You Shrine faces south, with the northernmost bay being the Wanjuan (Ten Thousand Volumes) Building, with floor-to-ceiling windows on the north side of the second floor—an excellent place to view the Second Spring courtyard; rockery is piled west of the building, and in the courtyard south of the building is the Suichu (Returning to Beginnings) Spring. South of the courtyard is the Suichu Hall, and south of the hall is the shrine gate. Exiting the shrine gate southward is the Bishan Poetry Society. 5. Bishan Poetry Society: In the 18th year of Chenghua of the Ming (1482), Qin Xu and nine others founded a poetry society on the site of the Longquan monk room, imitating Bai Juyi's "Nine Elders of Xiangshan," calling themselves the "Ten Elders of Bishan"; Ministers Wang Shu, Wang Yu, and Wu Kuan often joined the elders in poetry exchanges, and Shen Zhou painted the "Bishan Poetry Society Elegant Gathering Painting" for them—becoming a local cultural event. In the 7th year of Hongzhi of the Ming (1494), Qin Xu and his son passed away successively, and the Bishan Poetry Society was seized by a powerful family. In 1521, Qin Jin, together with Pan Xu and Shao Bao, planned to reopen the poetry society, but the powerful family refused to yield; it was not until the 33rd year of Jiajing of the Ming (1554) that Qin Xu's great-grandson Qin Han, together with 19 local gentry, finally purchased the poetry society back from the powerful family. Grand Secretary Xu Jie wrote the "Record of Re-establishing the Bishan Poetry Society," Chen Yansheng wrote the "Preface to Re-establishing the Bishan Poetry Society," and Wen Zhengming inscribed the plaque "Bishan Poetry Society"—causing a sensation in the county again. Thereafter, the Bishan Poetry Society became an important cultural memory of Wuxi, with literati and celebrities continuously reopening the poetry society, and the literary style and poetic charm continuing to this day; it was fully rebuilt in 2005. The Bishan Poetry Society faces south, with two courtyards. From the You Shrine southward, one first enters the northernmost Shilao (Ten Elders) Hall, with a lacquer painting of Wen Zhengming's "Orchid Pavilion Gathering." Following the hall's front eave corridor westward is the Wangyi (Looking at Benefit) Tower; exiting the tower southward is the Liushang (Floating Wine Cups) Mountain Room. From the mountain room's south gate westward out of the courtyard, one can see the cliff carvings by Qin Han and others; south of it is the Hanbi (Green Jade) Pond, with the Zhuoying (Washing Tassel) Pavilion built by the water on the east bank; the pond water flows northward underground into the Longfeng (Dragon Seam) Spring, flowing toward the northwest of Wangyi Tower. Returning to the courtyard and entering the Bishan Poetry Society main hall, the courtyard in front of the hall faces the rockery; south of it is the main gate hall, and the east wing is the Poetry Platform. Following the poetry room's front corridor northward, the east side opens the poetry society gate, only a gate head, with Wen Zhengming's brick carving "Bishan Poetry Society" embedded outside. South of the Bishan Poetry Society is the Chunshen (Lord Chunshen) Stream, legend says Lord Chunshen once watered horses here, an excellent place for viewing waterfalls. Continuing southward leads to A Bing's Tomb and the Azalea Garden (azalea is Wuxi's city flower), both recently built parks. East of the Bishan Poetry Society is the Hu Wenzhao (Hu Yuan) Shrine, enshrining the great Song Neo-Confucian Hu Yuan, built during the Shunzhi reign of the Qing on the former site of Yugong Valley, rebuilt in 2005. North of the shrine is the Lotus Pond, eastward is the Yingshan (Reflecting Mountain) Lake; legend says when Qin Shi Huang made his eastern tour, "a qi-watcher said there was son-of-heaven qi between Jinling and Taihu, so he dug to suppress it" (Lu Yu, "Record of Visiting Huishan Temple"), hence folk call this lake the Qin King Dock. North of the Hu Shrine is the Zunxian (Honoring Worthies) Shrine, originally near today's Luzi Shrine, first built during the Song-Yuan period, enshrining Lu Yu, Zhan Ting, and Li Shen; later successively adding Hua Bao, Qin Guan, You Mao, Ni Zan, Wang Fu, Shao Bao, and Qin Xu, renamed the Zunxian Shrine, moved to today's site in the 16th year of Qianlong of the Qing (1751), rebuilt in 2005. Hua Xiaozi (Hua the Filial Son) Shrine: North of the Zunxian Shrine is the Hua Xiaozi Shrine, enshrining the Eastern Jin filial son Hua Bao, originally west of the Second Spring, moved to today's site in the Tang Dynasty—a key building of the Huishan Ancestral Hall Complex, designated a national protected site in 2006. The shrine faces west, with its back to east, unfolding along the axis. At the east end is the Four-Sided Archway, built in the 12th year of Qianlong of the Qing (1747), a square pavilion with a flat top, with archways on all four sides and inscriptions inside and outside; a skylight opens in the center of the flat top for lighting to clearly see the internal plaques. The well inside the pavilion was dug in 1959. This type of archway once existed in four places in Wuxi, including the Gu family archway at Gu Kejiu's Shrine in Shijia Lane (rebuilt), the Qin Jin North Four Archways at the east end of Cangqiao Bridge, and the Qin Family Shike South Four Archways at Fengguang Bridge—today only one survives, with relatively high value. Westward is a one-story one-door archway; inside the archway is the Yongxi (Eternal Blessing) Hall, first built in the 21st year of Chenghua of the Ming (1485), rebuilt in 2004. West of the hall is the Chengze (Inheriting Grace) Pond and Sanyuan (Tracing Origins) Bridge, built during the Chenghua reign of the Ming. West of the bridge is the Yuan (Soft-Shelled Turtle) Pond, octagonal, with a chi-dragon head spouting water on the south side inside the pond and a chi-dragon head absorbing water on the north side, leading to the Golden Lotus Pond—hence called the Double Dragon Spring, an important hub of the Huishan water system. West of the pond is the Xiaozu (Filial Ancestor) Enjoyment Hall, built in the 21st year of Chenghua of the Ming (1485), repaired in the 27th year of Qianlong of the Qing (1762). The south wall of the enjoyment hall is embedded with 12 pieces of the 1982 re-carved "Zhenshang Studio Album"; this album was originally carved by Hua Xia asking Wen Zhengming father and son to trace and Zhang Zao to carve, hailed as the "number one carved album of the Ming Dynasty"; Wen Zhengming once painted the "Zhenshang Studio Painting" for Hua Xia. In 2005, a stele corridor was added north of the enjoyment hall. West of the enjoyment hall is the Chengzhi (Aspiring to Ambition) Tower, first built in the 17th year of Hongzhi of the Ming (1504), rebuilt in 2005; the courtyard in front of the tower has beautiful flowers and rocks, and climbing the tower offers a view of Xishan. Southeast of the Hua Xiaozi Shrine is the Zhide (Ultimate Virtue) Shrine, enshrining Taibo, first built in the 30th year of Qianlong of the Qing (1765), rebuilt in 1959—a key building of the Huishan Ancestral Hall Complex, designated a national protected site in 2006. North of the Zhide Shrine, from west to east, are also the Li Zhongding Shrine, enshrining the anti-Jin general Li Gang, first built in the 5th year of Kangxi of the Qing (1666), rebuilt in 2005; the Zhou Zhonggong Shrine enshrines the Song scholar Zhou Hao, with Zhou Diguang and Zhou Deji father and son as accompanying deities, first built by Zhou Diguang, rebuilt in 2005; the Zhang Yishi Shrine; the Ji Liushan Shrine enshrines the Qing loyal martyr Ji Yongren, first built in the 7th year of Yongzheng of the Qing (1729), rebuilt in 2005; the Guo Junma Shrine enshrines the Song commandery prince consort Guo Mengyu, rebuilt in 2005. Exiting through the north gate of the Ji Liushan Shrine, one returns to the Vajra Hall of Huishan Temple, ending the tour.

projects.name: 惠山祠堂群
projects.name_en: Ancestral Hall Complex at Huishan Mountain
projects.level: 第六批全国重点文物保护单位（2006年），其中华孝子祠、至德祠、尤文简公祠、钱武肃王祠、淮湘昭忠祠（以上在锡惠公园内）、潜庐（留耕草堂）、王恩绶祠（武愍公）、杨藕芳祠、顾可久祠（洞阳先生）、陆宣公祠10座为重点祠堂
projects.level_en: 6th Batch National Key Cultural Heritage Site (2006), with 10 key ancestral halls including Hua Xiaozi Shrine, Zhide Shrine, You Wenjian Shrine, Qian Wusu Shrine, Huaixiang Zhaozhong Shrine (in Xihui Park), Qianlu (Liugeng Caotang), Wang Enshou Shrine (Wumin Gong), Yang Oufang Shrine, Gu Kejiu Shrine (Dongyang Xiansheng), and Lu Xuangong Shrine
projects.address: 惠山寺南北，向东延伸到直街、横街、寺塘泾和惠山浜一带
projects.address_en: North and south of Huishan Temple, extending east to Zhijie, Hengjie, Sitangjing, and Huishanbang areas
projects.type_en: Ancestral Hall Complex / Historical and Cultural Block
projects.ticket: 通票30元，可参观任何已开放的祠堂；单座祠堂门票10元
highlights: 从唐代开始惠山就建有华孝子祠和春申君祠等明清以来民间立祠出现了大量家祠无锡皆以能在惠山占得一席之地祭祀先贤先祖为荣如今在惠山寺南北向东延伸到直街横街寺塘泾和惠山浜一带有大小祠堂118处这些祠堂时间跨度近500年主要包括钦定官设和民间联宗立庙两大类细分为神祠先贤祠墓祠寺院祠贞节祠宗祠专祠书院祠园林祠行会祠十小类祭祀人物之多建筑密度之大祠堂类型之全为国内外所罕见生动地诠释了中国的忠孝文化

潜庐留耕草堂位于上河塘20号西与2008年复建的寄畅园朝房相通为惠山祠堂群重点建筑杨宗濂字艺芳1832-1905曾先后追随曾国藩李鸿章攻伐太平军捻军军功卓著清史稿列传239有传清光绪八年1882年其母病重他潜行回乡探视遭到政敌弹劾罢官于是在惠山脚构筑园亭取易经潜龙勿用之意命名潜庐并在庐旁祭祀父亲杨延望留耕草堂为园中主厅向南隔池对着戏台另有望山亭丛桂轩诸景清光绪十一年1885年杨宗濂复出先后为李鸿章筹建北洋武备学堂与人合办天津自来火公司等清光绪二十一年1895年与其弟杨宗瀚筹办无锡第一家纺织企业业勤纱厂杨宗濂任官期间胞弟杨以退隐居潜庐教授子弟读书间与士绅雅集名声颇著潜庐后传杨翰西杨彦斌之手得以修复保存杨翰西另在鼋头渚修筑了横云草堂
王恩绶祠武愍公位于下河塘8号为惠山祠堂群重点建筑王恩绶1804-1855字乐山太平军攻克武昌时死于武昌知县任上清同治十三年1874年状元洪钧奏请敕建祠堂祠园分为东中西三组院落中院由门厅碑亭二门和工字殿组成西院祭祀王恩绶之子东院有月洞门水池戏台和介福堂今为无锡非遗展览馆主要展示无锡泥人
杨藕芳祠位于下河塘为惠山祠堂群重点建筑杨宗瀚字藕芳1839-1910是杨宗濂胞弟曾入李鸿章刘铭传幕府到台湾担任台北道员总办水陆商务洋务他开发建设了台湾第一条铁路后又创办了上海机器织布厂和无锡业勤纱厂是我国近代工业的创始人这座祠堂建于1911年采用青砖拱券的西洋风格在惠山祠堂中独具特色

顾可久祠洞阳先生与杨藕芳祠相连为惠山祠堂群重点建筑顾可久1485-1561字与新号洞阳明正德九年1514年进士他为官耿直曾两次因进谏遭受廷杖可同官至广东按察司副使督学粤东时注意选拔人才举荐了海瑞后来他受到权臣中伤罢官回乡明隆庆四年复碧山吟社参与赋诗雅集度过晚年明万历元年1573年海瑞亲临谒拜题诗曰两朝崇祀庙谟新抗疏名传骨鲠臣志矢回天曾叩马功同浴日再批鳞庭留训诲留余泽史阙忠贞忆旧臣清康熙二十七年1688年祠庙毁于火次年重建乾隆年间两次重修祠中有拜石山房丈人峰浴日泉和四面牌坊近年复建等以丈人峰最为珍贵此石原在明代冯夔的竹素园中乾隆年间顾光旭将其移至祠内请秦瀛作拜石山房记此石高近4米与拜石山房隔水相望犹如伟岸的丈人顾光旭借此象征先祖的精神与品格

李公祠惠山园入口在百岁街祭祀李鸿章之弟淮军将领李鹤章李鹤章1825-1880是李鸿章创办淮军时的骨干攻伐太平军期间躬冒矢石奋勇争先战功显赫获赐黄马褂和三品甘凉道台后因李鸿章避嫌不举李鹤章辞官不就隐居故里无锡是李鹤章与太平军激战并取得成功之地他去世后曾国荃上疏为其在惠山建造专祠祠堂为徽派风格集木砖石三雕和彩绘于一体1929年合并改筑为惠山公园1950年李鸿章李鹤章被视为镇压太平军的刽子手祠园被拆除2008年复建李公祠和惠山园
惠山泥人厂旧址位于古华路今为中国泥人博物馆隈研吾设计2006年惠山泥人入选国家级非物质质文保名录惠山北坡出产黑泥质地细腻塑性极强从明代起附近守祠堂的祠丁就在闲暇时做泥人每到庙会期间香客游人络绎不绝祠丁多在门口出摊或沿街叫卖形成惠山泥人一条街孩子买阿福老人买寿星恋人买和合二仙商人买财神精巧的泥人成为最受欢迎的无锡特产
陆宣公祠位于直街绣嶂街43号祭祀唐代宰相陆贽754-805为惠山祠堂群重点建筑北宋建中靖国元年1101年陆氏迁锡始祖陆棐在惠山为陆贽建祠明代毁坏清康熙年间陆慧玉奉檄复建嘉庆年间重修今祠共三进有戏楼池沼石桥和仰贤堂大殿和后殿等陆宣公祠东为范文正公祠西为倪云林祠
张中丞庙位于直街120号祀唐代安史之乱中抗击叛军殉职的御史中丞张巡始建于南宋建炎二年1128年明成化九年1473年重建清道光十一年1831年毁后又建并增筑许远祠太平天国时期庙毁清同治八年1869年重建1995年列为省保单位庙坐南朝北背倚锡山由北向南依次为门厅二层戏台大殿和后殿等大殿前院有两株400多年的古银杏院东有明万历十五年1587年所凿云泉古井主殿西侧为许远殿其西有花篮厅和古鲁班殿

龙光塔张中丞庙后殿有山道通向锡山山顶锡山龙光塔为无锡的地标建筑是一座文峰塔塔下建龙光寺惠山又称九龙山锡山在其东侧被风水家视为龙角建议在山顶建塔能使无锡文风昌盛明嘉靖元年1522年顾懋章顾可学父子在山顶建石塔但无锡科举未见起色风水家又说龙靠角来听中空才能听音实心的石塔并不相宜明万历四年1576年常州知府施观民又在石塔旁建了一座八角七层砖塔题名龙光塔在明代万历年间绘制的寄畅园图册中有三幅图表现了山顶一石一砖两塔共存的景致康熙雍正道光年间龙光塔多次重修1999年再次大修
