从唐代开始，惠山就建有华孝子祠和春申君祠等；明清以来民间立祠，出现了大量家祠，无锡皆以能在惠山占得一席之地祭祀先贤、先祖为荣。如今在惠山寺南北，向东延伸到直街、横街、寺塘泾和惠山浜一带，建有大小祠堂118处。这些祠堂时间跨度近500年，主要包括钦定官设和民间联宗立庙两大类，细分为神祠、先贤祠、墓祠、寺院祠、贞节祠、宗祠、专祠、书院祠、园林祠、行会祠十小类，祭祀人物之多、建筑密度之大、祠堂类型之全，为国内外所罕见，生动地诠释了中国的忠孝文化。1. 潜庐（留耕草堂）：位于上河塘20号，西与2008年复建的寄畅园朝房相通，为惠山祠堂群重点建筑。杨宗濂（字艺芳，1832—1905）曾先后追随曾国藩、李鸿章攻伐太平军、捻军，军功卓著，《清史稿·列传239》有传。清光绪八年（1882年）其母病重，他潜行回乡探视，遭到政敌弹劾罢官，于是在惠山脚构筑园亭，取《易经》"潜龙勿用"之意命名潜庐，并在庐旁祭祀父亲杨延望。留耕草堂为园中主厅，向南隔池对着戏台，另有望山亭、丛桂轩诸景。清光绪十一年（1885年）杨宗濂复出，先后为李鸿章筹建北洋武备学堂，与人合办天津自来火公司等；清光绪二十一年（1895年）与其弟杨宗瀚筹办无锡第一家纺织企业——业勤纱厂。杨宗濂任官期间，胞弟杨以退隐居潜庐，教授子弟读书，间与士绅雅集，名声颇著。潜庐后传杨翰西、杨彦斌之手，得以修复保存。杨翰西另在鼋头渚修筑了横云草堂。2. 王恩绶祠（武愍公）：位于下河塘8号，为惠山祠堂群重点建筑。王恩绶（1804—1855）字乐山，太平军攻克武昌时死于武昌知县任上，清同治十三年（1874年）状元洪钧奏请敕建祠堂。祠园分为东、中、西三组院落，中院由门厅、碑亭、二门和工字殿组成，西院祭祀王恩绶之子，东院有月洞门、水池、戏台和介福堂。今为无锡非遗展览馆，主要展示无锡泥人。3. 杨藕芳祠：位于下河塘，为惠山祠堂群重点建筑。杨宗瀚（字藕芳，1839—1910）是杨宗濂胞弟，曾入李鸿章、刘铭传幕府，到台湾担任台北道员，总办水陆商务、洋务，他开发建设了台湾第一条铁路，后又创办了上海机器织布厂和无锡业勤纱厂，是我国近代工业的创始人。这座祠堂建于1911年，采用青砖拱券的西洋风格，在惠山祠堂中独具特色。4. 顾可久祠（洞阳先生）：与杨藕芳祠相连，为惠山祠堂群重点建筑。顾可久（1485—1561）字与新，号洞阳，明正德九年（1514年）进士。他为官耿直，曾两次因进谏遭受廷杖，可同官至广东按察司副使，督学粤东时注意选拔人才，举荐了海瑞。后来他受到权臣中伤，罢官回乡，明隆庆四年复碧山吟社，参与赋诗雅集，度过晚年。明万历元年（1573年）海瑞亲临谒拜，题诗曰："两朝崇祀庙谟新，抗疏名传骨鲠臣。志矢回天曾叩马，功同浴日再批鳞。庭留训诲留余泽，史阙忠贞忆旧臣。功同浴日再批鳞……"从中可见顾可久对海瑞的影响。清康熙二十七年（1688年）祠庙毁于火，次年重建，乾隆年间两次重修。祠中有拜石山房、丈人峰、浴日泉和四面牌坊（近年复建）等。以丈人峰最为珍贵，此石原在明代冯夔的竹素园中，乾隆年间顾光旭将其移至祠内，请秦瀛作《拜石山房记》。此石高近4米，与拜石山房隔水相望，犹如伟岸的丈人，顾光旭借此象征先祖的精神与品格。5. 李公祠（惠山园）：入口在百岁街，祭祀李鸿章之弟、淮军将领李鹤章。李鹤章（1825—1880）是李鸿章创办淮军时的骨干，攻伐太平军期间，"躬冒矢石，奋勇争先"，战功显赫，获赐黄马褂和三品甘凉道台。后因李鸿章"避嫌不举"，李鹤章辞官不就，隐居故里。无锡是李鹤章与太平军激战并取得成功之地，他去世后曾国荃上疏为其在惠山建造专祠。祠堂为徽派风格，集木、砖、石三雕和彩绘于一体。1929年合并改筑为惠山公园，1950年李鸿章、李鹤章被视为镇压太平军的刽子手，祠、园被拆除。2008年复建李公祠和惠山园。6. 惠山泥人厂旧址：位于古华路，今为中国泥人博物馆，隈研吾设计。2006年惠山泥人入选国家级非物质质文保名录。惠山北坡出产黑泥，质地细腻，塑性极强，从明代起附近守祠堂的祠丁就在闲暇时做泥人。每到庙会期间，香客游人络绎不绝，祠丁多在门口出摊或沿街叫卖，形成惠山泥人一条街。孩子买阿福，老人买寿星，恋人买和合二仙，商人买财神……精巧的泥人成为最受欢迎的无锡特产。7. 陆宣公祠：位于直街（绣嶂街）43号，祭祀唐代宰相陆贽（754—805），为惠山祠堂群重点建筑。北宋建中靖国元年（1101年），陆氏迁锡始祖陆棐在惠山为陆贽建祠。明代毁坏，清康熙年间陆慧玉奉檄复建，嘉庆年间重修。今祠共三进，有戏楼、池沼、石桥和仰贤堂、大殿和后殿等。陆宣公祠东为范文正公祠，西为倪云林祠。8. 张中丞庙：位于直街120号，祀唐代安史之乱中抗击叛军殉职的御史中丞张巡，始建于南宋建炎二年（1128年），明成化九年（1473年）重建，清道光十一年（1831年）毁后又建，并增筑许远祠。太平天国时期庙毁，清同治八年（1869年）重建，1995年列为省保单位。庙坐南朝北，背倚锡山，由北向南依次为门厅、二层戏台、大殿和后殿等。大殿前院有两株400多年的古银杏，院东有明万历十五年（1587年）所凿云泉古井。主殿西侧为许远殿，其西有花篮厅和古鲁班殿。9. 龙光塔：张中丞庙后殿有山道通向锡山山顶。锡山龙光塔为无锡的地标建筑，是一座文峰塔，塔下建龙光寺。惠山又称九龙山，锡山在其东侧，被风水家视为龙角，建议在山顶建塔，能使无锡文风昌盛。明嘉靖元年（1522年）顾懋章、顾可学父子在山顶建石塔。但无锡科举未见起色。风水家又说，龙靠角来听，中空才能听音，实心的石塔并不相宜。明万历四年（1576年），常州知府施观民又在石塔旁建了一座八角七层砖塔，题名龙光塔。在明代万历年间绘制的《寄畅园图册》中，有三幅图表现了山顶一石一砖两塔共存的景致。康熙、雍正、道光年间龙光塔多次重修，1999年再次大修。
projects.content_en: From the Tang Dynasty, Huishan already had the Hua Xiaozi (Hua the Filial Son) Shrine and Chunshen Jun Shrine; during the Ming and Qing,民间 established shrines, with numerous family shrines appearing, and Wuxi people all took pride in being able to occupy a place at Huishan to sacrifice to former worthies and ancestors. Today, north and south of Huishan Temple, extending eastward to Zhijie, Hengjie, Sitangjing, and Huishanbang areas, there are 118 ancestral halls of various sizes. These ancestral halls span nearly 500 years, mainly including two categories: officially established by imperial decree and jointly established by clans; subdivided into ten minor categories: deity shrines, former-worthy shrines, tomb shrines, temple shrines, chastity shrines, clan shrines, special shrines, academy shrines, garden shrines, and guild shrines. The number of people sacrificed to, the density of buildings, and the completeness of shrine types are rare at home and abroad, vividly interpreting Chinese culture of loyalty and filial piety. 1. Qianlu (Liugeng Caotang): Located at No. 20 Shanghetang, connected westward to the Jichang Garden audience hall rebuilt in 2008, a key building of the Huishan Ancestral Hall Complex. Yang Zonglian (style name Yifang, 1832-1905) successively followed Zeng Guofan and Li Hongzhang to attack the Taiping Army and Nian Army, with outstanding military merits, recorded in "Draft History of Qing·Biography 239." In the 8th year of Guangxu of the Qing (1882), when his mother was seriously ill, he secretly returned home to visit, was impeached by political opponents and dismissed, so he built pavilions and gardens at the foot of Huishan, taking the meaning of "a hidden dragon should not act" from the "Book of Changes" to name it Qianlu (Hidden Cottage), and sacrificed to his father Yang Yanwang beside the cottage. Liugeng Caotang (Plowing-Gone Thatched Hall) is the main hall of the garden, facing a stage across a pond to the south, with other scenic spots such as Wangshan Pavilion and Conggui Studio. In the 11th year of Guangxu (1885), Yang Zonglian returned to office, successively preparing to build the Beiyang Military Academy for Li Hongzhang and co-founding the Tianjin Self-Match Company etc.; in the 21st year of Guangxu (1895), together with his younger brother Yang Zonghan, he prepared to establish Wuxi's first textile enterprise—Yiqin Cotton Mill. During Yang Zonglian's official tenure, his younger brother Yang Yi retired to live in seclusion at Qianlu, teaching children to read and occasionally gathering with gentry for elegant gatherings, with a considerable reputation. Qianlu later passed to Yang Hanxi and Yang Yanbin,得以 repaired and preserved. Yang Hanxi also built the Hengyun Thatched Hall at Yuantouzhu. 2. Wang Enshou Shrine (Wumin Gong): Located at No. 8 Xiahetang, a key building of the Huishan Ancestral Hall Complex. Wang Enshou (1804-1855), style name Leshan, died in office as magistrate of Wuchang when the Taiping Army captured Wuchang; in the 13th year of Tongzhi of the Qing (1874), zhuangyuan Hong Jun petitioned for an imperial decree to build the shrine. The shrine garden is divided into east, middle, and west groups of courtyards; the middle courtyard consists of the gate hall, stele pavilion, second gate, and I-shaped hall; the west courtyard sacrifices to Wang Enshou's son; the east courtyard has a moon gate, pond, stage, and Jiefu Hall. Today it is the Wuxi Intangible Cultural Heritage Exhibition Hall, mainly displaying Wuxi clay figures. 3. Yang Oufang Shrine: Located at Xiahetang, a key building of the Huishan Ancestral Hall Complex. Yang Zonghan (style name Oufang, 1839-1910) was Yang Zonglian's younger brother, once served in the shogunates of Li Hongzhang and Liu Mingchuan, went to Taiwan as Taipei Circuit Intendant, in charge of land and water commerce and foreign affairs; he developed and built Taiwan's first railway, later founded the Shanghai Machine Weaving Factory and Wuxi Yiqin Cotton Mill—a founder of China's modern industry. This shrine was built in 1911, adopting the Western style of blue brick arches, unique among the Huishan ancestral halls. 4. Gu Kejiu Shrine (Dongyang Xiansheng): Connected to the Yang Oufang Shrine, a key building of the Huishan Ancestral Hall Complex. Gu Kejiu (1485-1561), style name Yuxin, hao Dongyang, passed the jinshi examination in the 9th year of Zhengde of the Ming (1514). He was upright in office, twice suffered court flogging for remonstrating; Gu Ke served as Vice Commissioner of the Guangdong Provincial Surveillance Commission, paying attention to selecting talents when supervising education in eastern Guangdong, recommending Hai Rui. Later he was maligned by powerful officials and dismissed, returning home; in the 4th year of Longqing of the Ming (1570) he revived the Bishan Poetry Society, participating in poetry gatherings and elegant assemblies, spending his later years. In the 1st year of Wanli of the Ming (1573), Hai Rui personally came to pay homage, inscribing a poem: "Two dynasties worship the temple with new plans, his name of upright remonstrance spreads like a bone-loyal minister. His will aimed to turn back heaven and he once knocked the horse, his merit same as bathing the sun and he again scaled the scales. The courtyard retains teachings and remaining grace, history lacks loyalty but recalls the old minister..." From this one can see Gu Kejiu's influence on Hai Rui. In the 27th year of Kangxi of the Qing (1688), the shrine was destroyed by fire, rebuilt the following year, and repaired twice during the Qianlong reign. In the shrine are the Baishi (Worshiping Stone) Mountain Room, Zhangren (Elder) Peak, Yuri (Bathing Sun) Spring, and Four-Sided Archway (recently rebuilt) etc. The Zhangren Peak is the most precious; this stone was originally in Feng Kui's Zhusu Garden of the Ming, and during the Qianlong reign Gu Guangxu moved it into the shrine, asking Qin Ying to write the "Record of the Baishi Mountain Room." This stone is nearly 4 meters high, facing the Baishi Mountain Room across the water, like a towering elder; Gu Guangxu used it to symbolize the spirit and character of his ancestors. 5. Li Gong Shrine (Huishan Garden): The entrance is on Baisui Street, sacrificing to Li Hezhang, younger brother of Li Hongzhang and a Huai Army general. Li Hezhang (1825-1880) was a backbone when Li Hongzhang founded the Huai Army; during the campaign against the Taiping Army, he "braved arrows and stones, fighting bravely in the vanguard," with outstanding military merits, awarded the Yellow Riding Jacket and the third-rank Ganliang Circuit Intendant. Later, because Li Hongzhang "avoided suspicion and did not recommend," Li Hezhang resigned and lived in seclusion in his hometown. Wuxi was the place where Li Hezhang fought fiercely against the Taiping Army and achieved success; after his death, Zeng Guoquan petitioned to build a special shrine for him at Huishan. The shrine is in Huizhou style, integrating wood, brick, and stone carvings and painted decorations. In 1929 it was merged and rebuilt into Huishan Park; in 1950, Li Hongzhang and Li Hezhang were regarded as executioners suppressing the Taiping Army, and the shrine and garden were demolished. In 2008, Li Gong Shrine and Huishan Garden were rebuilt. 6. Former Site of Huishan Clay Figure Factory: Located on Guhua Road, today the China Clay Figure Museum, designed by Kengo Kuma. In 2006, Huishan clay figures were included in the national intangible cultural heritage list. The north slope of Huishan produces black clay, fine in texture and highly plastic; from the Ming Dynasty, shrine servants guarding nearby ancestral halls made clay figures in their spare time. During temple fairs, pilgrims and tourists came in an endless stream, and shrine servants mostly set up stalls at the gate or sold along the street, forming a Huishan clay figure street. Children bought Afu, the elderly bought the God of Longevity, lovers bought the He-He Twins, merchants bought the God of Wealth... exquisite clay figures became the most popular Wuxi specialty. 7. Lu Xuangong Shrine: Located at No. 43 Zhijie (Xiuzhang Street), sacrificing to Tang Dynasty Chancellor Lu Zhi (754-805), a key building of the Huishan Ancestral Hall Complex. In the 1st year of Jianzhong Jingguo of the Northern Song (1101), Lu Fei, the ancestor of the Lu family who moved to Wuxi, built a shrine for Lu Zhi at Huishan. Destroyed in the Ming, rebuilt by Lu Huiyu under imperial decree during the Kangxi reign of the Qing, and repaired during the Jiaqing reign. Today the shrine has three bays, with a stage, pond, stone bridge, Yangxian Hall, main hall, and rear hall etc. East of the Lu Xuangong Shrine is the Fan Wenzheng Shrine, west is the Ni Yunlin Shrine. 8. Zhang Zhongcheng Temple: Located at No. 120 Zhijie, sacrificing to Zhang Xun, Censorate Vice Censor-in-Chief who died fighting the rebel army during the An Lushan Rebellion of the Tang, first built in the 2nd year of Jianyan of the Southern Song (1128), rebuilt in the 9th year of Chenghua of the Ming (1473), destroyed and rebuilt in the 11th year of Daoguang of the Qing (1831), with the Xu Yuan Shrine added. Destroyed during the Taiping Rebellion, rebuilt in the 8th year of Tongzhi of the Qing (1869), designated a provincial protected site in 1995. The temple faces south with its back to Xishan, from north to south successively the gate hall, two-story stage, main hall, and rear hall etc. In the front courtyard of the main hall are two ancient ginkgo trees over 400 years old; east of the courtyard is the Yunquan ancient well dug in the 15th year of Wanli of the Ming (1587). West of the main hall is the Xu Yuan Hall, west of which are the Flower Basket Hall and Ancient Luban Hall. 9. Longguang Pagoda: From the rear hall of the Zhang Zhongcheng Temple, a mountain path leads to the top of Xishan. The Xishan Longguang Pagoda is Wuxi's landmark building, a cultural-prosperity (wenfeng) pagoda, with the Longguang Temple built below it. Huishan is also called Jiulong (Nine Dragons) Mountain; Xishan is on its east side, regarded by fengshui masters as the dragon's horn, suggesting that building a pagoda on the mountain top would make Wuxi's literary culture prosper. In the 1st year of Jiajing of the Ming (1522), Gu Maozhang and Gu Kexue father and son built a stone pagoda on the mountain top. But Wuxi's imperial examination success did not improve. Fengshui masters then said that dragons hear through their horns, and hollow horns can hear, while a solid stone pagoda is not suitable. In the 4th year of Wanli of the Ming (1576), Shi Guanmin, Prefect of Changzhou, built an octagonal seven-story brick pagoda beside the stone pagoda, named Longguang (Dragon Light) Pagoda. In the "Jichang Garden Album" painted during the Wanli reign of the Ming, three paintings show the scene of one stone and one brick pagoda coexisting on the mountain top. During the Kangxi, Yongzheng, and Daoguang reigns, the Longguang Pagoda was repaired multiple times, and again majorly repaired in 1999.

projects.name: 荣氏梅园
projects.level: 第六批全国重点文物保护单位（2006年）
projects.level_en: 6th Batch National Key Cultural Heritage Site (2006)
projects.address: 滨湖区梁溪西路卞家湾13号
projects.address_en: No. 13 Bianjiawan, West Liangxi Road, Binhu District
projects.ticket: 60元（或购买五园联票，见锡惠公园）
highlights: 1906年工商实业家荣德生游览苏州留园萌生造园之念1912年他购得荣巷以西的东山坡地种植梅花并开筑连接梅园与城区的公路方便人们游赏此后陆续盖房凿泉建寺立塔1934年基本建成在中国近代公园史上具有重要意义

梅园入口原在今大门之西入门有荣德生手植紫藤右侧墙角为洗心泉沿紫藤棚架向前可见荣德生手书梅园刻石向北一座高台掩映在繁密的梅林中其上点缀六角小亭为天心台台基用黄石垒砌登台入亭可周赏园景台南屹立三块湖石题名米襄阳拜石为乾隆朝大学士兼军机大臣曾编著日下旧闻考的金坛人于敏中1714-1779园中旧物台西为揖蠡亭向商界之祖范蠡致敬继续向北为香海轩轩前有荣德生铜像轩后建楠木正厅诵豳堂堂后为招鹤亭与乐农别墅别墅前安放着三片石磨乃荣家始创面粉厂时从法国进口后来改用粉机拆下的石磨被安放在新建的梅园中沿山路向北迎面耸立一塔八角三层乃1930年荣氏兄弟为纪念母亲80冥寿建造的念劬塔塔位于高处成为园中的标志建筑在多处都可见到登塔可俯瞰园内景色北倚惠山群峰南对太湖万顷借景绝佳塔东为建于1923年的宗敬别墅采用西洋风格更东为建于1926年的秋丹阁荣氏子弟求学的读书处豁然洞以及建于1933年的开原寺出寺沿山路折而向西经植物博览馆可达古梅奇石圃远香堂花溪和积雪堂等返回景区入口以上为梅园主景区此外北区为梅品种登录园展示梅品种和梅桩造型等东区为中日梅花观赏园由吟风阁纮齐苑和畹芬堂等组成
projects.content_zh: 1906年工商实业家荣德生游览苏州留园，萌生造园之念，1912年他购得荣巷以西的东山坡地种植梅花，并开筑连接梅园与城区的公路，方便人们游赏。此后陆续盖房、凿泉、建寺、立塔，1934年基本建成，在中国近代公园史上具有重要意义。梅园入口原在今大门之西，入门有荣德生手植紫藤，右侧墙角为洗心泉，沿紫藤棚架向前可见荣德生手书"梅园"刻石。向北，一座高台掩映在繁密的梅林中，其上点缀六角小亭，为天心台，台基用黄石垒砌，登台入亭可周赏园景。台南屹立三块湖石，题名"米襄阳拜石"，为乾隆朝大学士兼军机大臣、曾编著《日下旧闻考》的金坛人于敏中（1714—1779）园中旧物。台西为揖蠡亭，向商界之祖范蠡致敬。继续向北为香海轩，轩前有荣德生铜像，轩后建楠木正厅诵豳堂，堂后为招鹤亭与乐农别墅。别墅前安放着三片石磨，乃荣家始创面粉厂时从法国进口，后来改用粉机，拆下的石磨被安放在新建的梅园中。沿山路向北，迎面耸立一塔，八角三层，乃1930年荣氏兄弟为纪念母亲80冥寿建造的"念劬塔"。塔位于高处，成为园中的标志建筑，在多处都可见到；登塔可俯瞰园内景色，北倚惠山群峰，南对太湖万顷，借景绝佳。塔东为建于1923年的宗敬别墅，采用西洋风格；更东为建于1926年的秋丹阁，荣氏子弟求学的读书处、豁然洞，以及建于1933年的开原寺。出寺沿山路折而向西，经植物博览馆可达古梅奇石圃、远香堂、花溪和积雪堂等，返回景区入口。以上为梅园主景区，此外，北区为梅品种登录园，展示梅品种和梅桩造型等；东区为中日梅花观赏园，由吟风阁、纮齐苑和畹芬堂等组成。
projects.content_en: In 1906, industrialist Rong Desheng visited Suzhou's Lingering Garden and conceived the idea of building a garden. In 1912, he purchased the east hillside land west of Rongxiang to plant plum blossoms, and built a road connecting the Plum Garden with the city to facilitate people's visits. Thereafter he successively built houses, dug springs, built temples, and erected pagodas, basically completed in 1934, with important significance in the history of modern Chinese parks. The Plum Garden entrance was originally west of today's main gate; entering, there is a wisteria planted by Rong Desheng himself, the Xixin (Heart-Cleansing) Spring at the right corner, and along the wisteria trellis forward one can see the "Plum Garden" stone carving in Rong Desheng's own handwriting. Northward, a high terrace is hidden among dense plum forests, with a hexagonal small pavilion on it—the Tianxin (Heavenly Heart) Terrace; the terrace base is built of yellow stone, and climbing onto the terrace and entering the pavilion allows one to enjoy the garden scenery all around. South of the terrace stand three Taihu rocks, titled "Mi Xiangyang Worshiping Rocks," originally from the garden of Yu Minzhong (1714-1779) of Jintan, a Grand Secretary and Grand Councilor of the Qianlong reign who compiled the "Investigations into Old News under the Sun." West of the terrace is the Yili (Saluting Li) Pavilion, paying tribute to Fan Li, the ancestor of the business world. Continuing northward is the Xianghai (Fragrant Sea) Studio, with a bronze statue of Rong Desheng in front; behind the studio is the nanmu main hall Songbin (Reciting Bin) Hall, and behind the hall are the Zhahe (Crane-Calling) Pavilion and Lenong (Happy Farmer) Villa. In front of the villa are placed three stone millstones, imported from France when the Rong family first founded the flour mill; later switching to powder machines, the removed stone millstones were placed in the newly built Plum Garden. Following the mountain path northward, a pagoda rises head-on, octagonal and three-story—the "Nianqu (Remembering Toil) Pagoda" built by the Rong brothers in 1930 to commemorate their mother's 80th posthumous birthday. The pagoda is located at a high place, becoming the landmark building of the garden, visible from many places; climbing the pagoda offers a bird's-eye view of the garden scenery, backed by the Huishan peaks to the north and facing the vast Taihu Lake to the south—excellent borrowed scenery. East of the pagoda is the Zongjing Villa built in 1923, adopting Western style; further east is the Qiudan Pavilion built in 1926, the study place for the Rong family's children, the Huoran (Suddenly Enlightened) Cave, and the Kaiyuan Temple built in 1933. Exiting the temple and turning west along the mountain path, passing the Plant Expo Hall, one reaches the Ancient Plum and Strange Rock Garden, Yuanxiang (Distant Fragrance) Hall, Flower Stream, and Jixue (Accumulated Snow) Hall etc., returning to the scenic area entrance. The above is the main scenic area of the Plum Garden; in addition, the north area is the Plum Variety Registration Garden, displaying plum varieties and plum stump shapes etc.; the east area is the Sino-Japanese Plum Blossom Viewing Garden, composed of the Yinfeng Pavilion, Hongqi Garden, and Wanfen Hall etc.

projects.name: 荣巷
projects.level: 第五批江苏省文物保护单位（2002年）
projects.level_en: 5th Batch Jiangsu Provincial Cultural Heritage Site (2002)
projects.address_en: Rongxiang Street, Binhu District
highlights: 明正统初年1436年无锡荣氏始祖荣清从金陵迁居此地繁衍为荣氏家族太平天国时期荣巷大半被毁1896年荣宗敬荣德生兄弟随父亲到上海开设钱庄后回无锡创办茂新面粉厂和振新纱厂成为中国民族工业巨擘荣德生之子荣毅仁被称为红色资本家1993年至1998年担任国家副主席荣巷是中国近代民族工商业发祥地之一长约380米街道集市各业齐全有150多幢老宅包括祠堂学校图书馆钱庄医院等是一处保存完整的历史街区
projects.content_zh: 明正统初年（1436年）无锡荣氏始祖荣清从金陵迁居此地，繁衍为荣氏家族。太平天国时期荣巷大半被毁，1896年荣宗敬、荣德生兄弟随父亲到上海开设钱庄，后回无锡创办茂新面粉厂和振新纱厂，成为中国民族工业巨擘。荣德生之子荣毅仁被称为红色资本家，1993年至1998年担任国家副主席。荣巷是中国近代民族工商业发祥地之一，长约380米，街道集市各业齐全，有150多幢老宅，包括祠堂、学校、图书馆、钱庄、医院等，是一处保存完整的历史街区。
projects.content_en: In the early years of Zhengtong of the Ming (1436), Rong Qing, the ancestor of the Wuxi Rong family, moved here from Jinling (Nanjing), multiplying into the Rong family clan. During the Taiping Rebellion, most of Rongxiang was destroyed. In 1896, brothers Rong Zongjing and Rong Desheng followed their father to Shanghai to open a money shop, later returning to Wuxi to found the Maoxin Flour Mill and Zhenxin Cotton Mill, becoming giants of Chinese national industry. Rong Desheng's son Rong Yiren was called a "red capitalist," serving as Vice President of the People's Republic of China from 1993 to 1998. Rongxiang is one of the birthplaces of modern Chinese national industry and commerce, about 380 meters long, with complete streets and markets of all trades, over 150 old houses including ancestral halls, schools, libraries, money shops, and hospitals—a well-preserved historical block.

projects.name: 蠡园
projects.level: 第五批江苏省文物保护单位（2002年）
projects.level_en: 5th Batch Jiangsu Provincial Cultural Heritage Site (2002)
projects.address: 滨湖区环湖路青祁路70号
projects.address_en: No. 70 Qingqi Road, Huanhu Road, Binhu District
projects.ticket: 门票60元（或购买五园联票，见锡惠公园）
highlights: 由梅园沿环湖路直到金城湾公园为蠡湖风景区主要景点有管社山庄万顷堂渤公岛鸥鹭岛渔父岛蠡湖中央公园双虹园宝界公园茹经堂蠡园及渔庄蠡湖公园西施庄水居苑和大桥公园等其中渤公岛与蠡园及渔庄较为精彩蠡湖是太湖伸入无锡的内湖相传范蠡引退后偕西施隐居于此又名五里湖漆湖或小五湖1927年至1937年间王禹卿父子建蠡园1930年至1937年间陈梅芳建渔庄又名赛蠡园1952年将两园连通成为一处景区2002年蠡园及渔庄成为省保单位2005年成为4A景区游览蠡园最好的时节是三月的桃花节或七八月的荷花展园中较精彩的是归云峰假山为陈梅芳聘请浙江东阳叠山家蒋家元所叠用大量的湖石和笋石堆出山峦洞窟人行其中如入迷宫此外在千步长廊和湖心亭欣赏湖景和凝春塔也别有趣味
projects.content_zh: 由梅园沿环湖路直到金城湾公园为蠡湖风景区，主要景点有管社山庄、万顷堂、渤公岛、鸥鹭岛、渔父岛、蠡湖中央公园、双虹园、宝界公园、茹经堂、蠡园及渔庄、蠡湖公园、西施庄、水居苑和大桥公园等。其中渤公岛与蠡园及渔庄较为精彩。蠡湖是太湖伸入无锡的内湖，相传范蠡引退后偕西施隐居于此，又名五里湖、漆湖或小五湖。1927年至1937年间王禹卿父子建蠡园，1930年至1937年间陈梅芳建渔庄，又名"赛蠡园"，1952年将两园连通，成为一处景区。2002年"蠡园及渔庄"成为省保单位，2005年成为4A景区。游览蠡园最好的时节是三月的桃花节或七八月的荷花展。园中较精彩的是归云峰假山，为陈梅芳聘请浙江东阳叠山家蒋家元所叠，用大量的湖石和笋石堆出山峦洞窟，人行其中，如入迷宫。此外，在千步长廊和湖心亭欣赏湖景和凝春塔也别有趣味。
projects.content_en: From the Plum Garden along Huanhu Road to Jinchengwan Park is the Li Lake Scenic Area, with main scenic spots including Guanshe Villa, Wanqing Hall, Bogong Island, Oulu Island, Yufu Island, Li Lake Central Park, Shuanghong Garden, Baojie Park, Rujing Hall, Li Garden and Fishing Villa, Li Lake Park, Xishi Village, Shuiju Garden, and Daqiao Park etc. Among them, Bogong Island and Li Garden & Fishing Villa are more splendid. Li Lake is an inner lake of Taihu extending into Wuxi; legend says that after Fan Li retired, he lived in seclusion here with Xishi, hence also called Wuli Lake, Qi Lake, or Xiaowu Lake. From 1927 to 1937, Wang Yuqing father and son built Li Garden; from 1930 to 1937, Chen Meifang built the Fishing Villa, also called "Sai Li Garden" (Surpassing Li Garden); in 1952 the two gardens were connected into one scenic area. In 2002 "Li Garden and Fishing Villa" became a provincial protected site, and in 2005 became a 4A scenic area. The best seasons to visit Li Garden are the Peach Blossom Festival in March or the Lotus Exhibition in July-August. The most splendid part of the garden is the Guiyun Peak rockery, piled by Jiang Jiayuan, a rockery master from Dongyang, Zhejiang, hired by Chen Meifang, using large amounts of Taihu rocks and bamboo shoot stones to pile up mountains and caves—walking through it is like entering a labyrinth. In addition, enjoying the lake scenery and the Ningchun Pagoda from the Thousand-Step Corridor and the Lake Center Pavilion is also quite interesting.

projects.name: 鼋头渚
projects.level: 国家5A景区，2006年列为江苏省文物保护单位
projects.level_en: National 5A Scenic Area, designated Jiangsu Provincial Cultural Heritage Site in 2006
projects.address_en: Yuantouzhu Scenic Area, Binhu District
projects.ticket: 105元（或购买五园联票，见锡惠公园），学生票50元，含园内游览车门票和往返太湖仙岛船票
highlights: 鼋头渚位于滨湖区是充山西南麓深入太湖中的半岛因状如鼋头而得名被誉为太湖第一名胜锡惠公园荟萃了无锡的人文名胜鼋头渚则是无锡天然山水的代表西汉末期王莽篡位无锡人虞俊不肯附逆而殉难归葬宝界山刘秀登基后赐朱衣覆盖坟茔朱衣宝界渐成名胜南朝萧梁时僧人在充山北麓建广福庵北宋末期钱绅康熙无锡县志卷20有传在宝界山筑别业构通惠亭蒋瑑为作通惠亭记元明以来文人墨客到此游玩题诗者络绎不绝明代著名画家王问王鉴父子在钱绅别业旧址筑湖山草堂鼋头渚的大规模开发始于民国1918年乡绅杨翰西建横云山庄1924年又捐地助僧人迁建广福寺于今址1934年荣德生捐出六十寿辰寿金建造宝界桥2011年列为省保单位共60孔将鼋头渚与东岸相连此后陆续修建各类建筑2002年鼋头渚被列为国家5A景区2006年列为省保单位
projects.content_zh: 鼋头渚位于滨湖区，是充山西南麓深入太湖中的半岛，因状如鼋头而得名，被誉为"太湖第一名胜"。锡惠公园荟萃了无锡的人文名胜，鼋头渚则是无锡天然山水的代表。西汉末期王莽篡位，无锡人虞俊不肯附逆而殉难，归葬宝界山，刘秀登基后赐朱衣覆盖坟茔，"朱衣宝界"渐成名胜。南朝萧梁时僧人在充山北麓建广福庵。北宋末期钱绅（康熙《无锡县志》卷20有传）在宝界山筑别业、构通惠亭，蒋瑑为作《通惠亭记》。元明以来，文人墨客到此游玩题诗者络绎不绝，明代著名画家王问、王鉴父子在钱绅别业旧址筑湖山草堂。鼋头渚的大规模开发始于民国。1918年乡绅杨翰西建横云山庄，1924年又捐地助僧人迁建广福寺于今址，1934年荣德生捐出六十寿辰寿金建造宝界桥（2011年列为省保单位），共60孔，将鼋头渚与东岸相连。此后陆续修建各类建筑，2002年鼋头渚被列为国家5A景区，2006年列为省保单位。
projects.content_en: Yuantouzhu (Turtle Head Isle) is located in Binhu District, a peninsula extending into Taihu Lake from the southwestern foot of Chongshan Mountain, named for its turtle-head shape, hailed as "the number one scenic spot of Taihu." While Xihui Park gathers Wuxi's cultural and historical scenic spots, Yuantouzhu is the representative of Wuxi's natural mountains and waters. At the end of the Western Han, when Wang Mang usurped the throne, Wuxi native Yu Jun refused to submit to the traitor and died for his cause, buried at Baojie Mountain; after Liu Xiu ascended the throne, he bestowed red garments to cover the tomb, and "Red Garment Baojie" gradually became a famous scenic spot. During the Southern Dynasties Liang, monks built the Guangfu Nunnery at the northern foot of Chongshan. At the end of the Northern Song, Qian Shen (with a biography in Kangxi's "Wuxi County Gazetteer" vol. 20) built a villa and the Tonghui Pavilion at Baojie Mountain, and Jiang Zhuan wrote the "Record of the Tonghui Pavilion." Since the Yuan and Ming, literati and poets have come here to play and inscribe poems in an endless stream; the famous Ming painters Wang Wen and Wang Jian father and son built the Hushan Thatched Hall on the site of Qian Shen's villa. The large-scale development of Yuantouzhu began in the Republic of China. In 1918, local gentry Yang Hanxi built the Hengyun Mountain Villa; in 1924 he donated land to help monks relocate the Guangfu Temple to today's site; in 1934, Rong Desheng donated his 60th birthday celebration funds to build the Baojie Bridge (designated a provincial protected site in 2011), with 60 arches, connecting Yuantouzhu with the east bank. Thereafter various buildings were successively constructed; in 2002 Yuantouzhu was listed as a national 5A scenic area, and in 2006 designated a provincial protected site.

projects.name: 阖闾城遗址
projects.level: 第七批全国重点文物保护单位（2013年）
projects.level_en: 7th Batch National Key Cultural Heritage Site (2013)
projects.address: 无锡胡埭镇闾江村与常州雪堰镇城里村之间
projects.address_en: Between Lüjiang Village, Hudai Town, Wuxi and Chengli Village, Xueyan Town, Changzhou
highlights: 阖闾城位于无锡市滨湖区胡埭镇和常州市武进区雪堰桥交界处吴王阖闾在位期间前515-前496为进攻越国建造阖闾城此城北倚胥山南临太湖西阻越囯北拒楚兵可攻可守筑城取土后形成的闾江穿城而过汇入太湖外围有大城内包东西两城西城规格较高又分成南城和北城反映了吴国以西为尊的传统建有阖庐宫南城宫东宫和西宫今大城城垣已无仅存长方形环濠东西小城尚存城墙高土台及部分环濠以及练兵场点将台伍子胥屯兵处和兵器库遗址如今将建成吴都阖闾城遗址公园另外在无锡滨湖区马山闾江2号有阖闾城遗址博物馆
projects.content_zh: 阖闾城位于无锡市滨湖区胡埭镇和常州市武进区雪堰桥交界处。吴王阖闾在位期间（前515—前496）为进攻越国建造阖闾城，此城北倚胥山，南临太湖，西阻越国，北拒楚兵，可攻可守，筑城取土后形成的闾江穿城而过汇入太湖。外围有大城，内包东、西两城，西城规格较高，又分成南城和北城，反映了吴国以西为尊的传统，建有阖庐宫、南城宫、东宫和西宫。今大城城垣已无，仅存长方形环濠，东、西小城尚存城墙、高土台及部分环濠，以及练兵场、点将台、伍子胥屯兵处和兵器库遗址。如今将建成吴都阖闾城遗址公园。另外在无锡滨湖区马山闾江2号有阖闾城遗址博物馆。
projects.content_en: Helv City Site is located at the junction of Hudai Town, Binhu District, Wuxi and Xueyanqiao, Wujin District, Changzhou. During the reign of King Helü of Wu (515-496 BC), Helü City was built to attack the State of Yue; this city backs onto Xu Mountain to the north, faces Taihu Lake to the south, blocks Yue to the west, and resists Chu troops to the north—able to attack and defend. The Lüjiang River formed by excavating earth for the city walls passes through the city and flows into Taihu. The outer part has a large city, containing east and west small cities; the west small city has higher specifications, divided into south and north cities, reflecting the Wu tradition of honoring the west, with the Helü Palace, South City Palace, East Palace, and West Palace built. Today the large city's walls are gone, only a rectangular moat remains; the east and west small cities still preserve walls, high earth platforms, and parts of the moat, as well as a training ground, general's platform, Wu Zixu's troop station, and armory ruins. It will now be developed into the Wu Capital Helü City Site Park. Additionally, there is the Helü City Site Museum at No. 2 Lüjiang, Mashan, Binhu District, Wuxi.

projects.name: 泰伯庙和墓
projects.level: 第六批全国重点文物保护单位（2006年）
projects.level_en: 6th Batch National Key Cultural Heritage Site (2006)
projects.address_en: No. 21 Middle Taibo Road, Binhu District
highlights: 商末泰伯在梅里建立勾吴开挖最早的人工运河伯渎河东汉永兴二年154年桓帝命吴郡太守糜豹修泰伯庙并在鸿山立泰伯墓北宋元符三年1100年谥泰伯为至德侯崇宁年间扩建泰伯庙明清多次重修泰伯梅里志泰伯庙图反映了明弘治年间的格局太平天国战争中庙被毁仅存正殿至德殿今庙前立照池上架香花桥北依次为至德名邦牌坊棂星门享堂和至德殿至德殿建于明代前出青石月台三面环以栏杆台上置宝鼎正面铸泰伯庙至德殿六个金字大殿面阔五间进深六架采用单檐歇山顶外部有檐廊檐柱皆用石柱殿内立14根楠木柱大殿正中设汉白玉石座供奉泰伯坐像殿内嵌有清代历朝修庙碑记13方是重要的史料泰伯墓位于鸿山南麓距梅村三公里依山而筑由月牙池棂星门享堂丹陛甬道拜坛月台泰伯墓四面碑罗城和墓墩组成
projects.content_zh: 商末泰伯在梅里建立勾吴，开挖最早的人工运河伯渎河。东汉永兴二年（154年）桓帝命吴郡太守糜豹修泰伯庙，并在鸿山立泰伯墓。北宋元符三年（1100年）谥泰伯为"至德侯"，崇宁年间扩建泰伯庙，明清多次重修，《泰伯梅里志》"泰伯庙图"反映了明弘治年间的格局。太平天国战争中庙被毁，仅存正殿至德殿。今庙前立照池，上架香花桥，北依次为"至德名邦"牌坊、棂星门、享堂和至德殿。至德殿建于明代，前出青石月台，三面环以栏杆，台上置宝鼎，正面铸"泰伯庙至德殿"六个金字。大殿面阔五间，进深六架，采用单檐歇山顶，外部有檐廊，檐柱皆用石柱，殿内立14根楠木柱。大殿正中设汉白玉石座，供奉泰伯坐像。殿内嵌有清代历朝修庙碑记13方，是重要的史料。泰伯墓位于鸿山南麓，距梅村三公里。依山而筑，由月牙池、棂星门、享堂、丹陛、甬道、拜坛、月台、泰伯墓四面碑、罗城和墓墩组成。
projects.content_en: At the end of the Shang Dynasty, Taibo established Gouwu in Meili and excavated the earliest artificial canal, the Bodu River. In the 2nd year of Yongxing of the Eastern Han (154), Emperor Huan ordered Mi Bao, Governor of Wu Commandery, to repair the Taibo Temple and establish the Taibo Tomb at Hongshan. In the 3rd year of Yuanfu of the Northern Song (1100), Taibo was posthumously titled "Marquis of Ultimate Virtue"; during the Chongning reign the Taibo Temple was expanded, and repaired multiple times during the Ming and Qing. The "Taibo Meili Gazetteer"'s "Map of Taibo Temple" reflects the layout during the Hongzhi reign of the Ming. During the Taiping Rebellion war the temple was destroyed, only the main hall Zhide (Ultimate Virtue) Hall survived. Today in front of the temple stands a reflection pond with a Fragrant Flower Bridge over it; northward are successively the "Ultimate Virtue and Famous State" archway, Lingxing Gate, Enjoyment Hall, and Zhide Hall. The Zhide Hall was built in the Ming, with a bluestone platform projecting in front, surrounded by railings on three sides; a precious tripod is placed on the platform, with the six golden characters "Taibo Temple Zhide Hall" cast on the front. The main hall is five bays wide and six rafters deep, adopting a single-eave hip-and-gable roof, with an eave corridor outside, all eave columns made of stone, and 14 nanmu columns inside the hall. In the center of the main hall is a white marble seat, enshrining a seated statue of Taibo. Embedded in the hall are 13 stele records of temple repairs from various Qing dynasties—important historical materials. The Taibo Tomb is located at the southern foot of Hongshan, three kilometers from Meicun. Built along the mountain, it consists of the Crescent Pond, Lingxing Gate, Enjoyment Hall, Imperial Steps, Path, Worship Altar, Platform, Four-Sided Stele of Taibo Tomb, Enclosing Wall, and Tomb Mound.

projects.name: 荡口古镇
projects.level: 含4处13座省保，1处市保，50处历史建筑
projects.level_en: Including 4 sites with 13 provincial protected buildings, 1 municipal protected building, and 50 historical buildings
projects.address: 无锡市锡山区鹅湖镇荡口
projects.address_en: Dangkou, Ehu Town, Xishan District, Wuxi
projects.type_en: Famous Historical and Cultural Town / Ancient Town
highlights: 荡口古镇位于无锡苏州交界处古名丁舍相传是东汉孝子丁兰故里后因位于鹅肫荡口得名明洪武年间华贞固迁居此地名声渐显明中期荡口所在的南延乡成为江南缴纳粮赋第一乡华氏也发展成无锡的煌煌大族明清两代出了37名进士著名人物如明代侍读学士华察出版家华燧收藏家华夏东林党人复社成员华允诚著名音乐家华秋苹著名数学家华蘅芳华世芳兄弟等镇上有4处13座省保1处市保50处历史建筑多与华氏家族有关
华氏建筑群包括漫画家华君武旧居新当里花沿街北侧的数学双星华蘅芳华世芳故居进步街北仓河的华氏老义庄庄内有楠木厅被誉为江南第一义庄学海路上有果育鸿模小学和荡口中学和平街小巷内的明代华氏进士第尚存振始堂和明代假山石旺儿桥旁的华氏始迁祖祠以及锡甘路旁的华氏真赏斋遗址等2002年列为省保单位

荡口义庄群荡口古建筑以义庄最具特色自清初以来先后兴建了10余处以华氏为主过殷徐氏为辅义庄数量之多义田规模之大善举范围之广均为国内罕见荡口义庄从单一封建田租发展为多元化收益办庄从义田义仓拓展为义庄义学从本族慈善事业推向社会慈善义举从济贫扶弱救急解困扩展为崇文兴教办学兴国为荡口做出了重要贡献如今保存较好的有华氏老义庄永喜义庄华氏襄义庄徐氏义庄和须义庄五座2002年列为省保单位华氏老义庄位于进步街清乾隆年间华进思华公弼父子创建是当地的第一座义庄规模也最大现存四进房屋自南向北依次为隔河照壁码头八字照壁门厅轿厅楠木正厅和后厅西路辟有花园有水池假山亭桥廊榭目前筹建为荡口义庄展示馆永喜义庄位于青虹路清道光二十四年1845年华永喜妻华锡鳞建现存四进房屋由南向北依次为前屋前厅大厅和后屋义庄三面环水建筑精美墙中夹有金山石柱河埠设有闸门防盗功能完善华氏襄义庄位于生产街1924年华襄云建现存门厅前厅和后厅共三进和两座侧厢徐氏义庄位于新桥村老湖桥清光绪初年进士徐焕后裔所建俗称红墙门清光绪三十三年1907年在庄内创办湖桥小学堂新中国成立前曾遭火灾现存门厅前厅大厅和后厅共四进每进9间两侧皆有备弄其中大厅规模较大梁柱粗壮雕工细致体现了苏州民居营造技术对荡口的影响须义庄位于团结街今存门厅前厅和后厅共三进原为须家祠堂后改为米行现为私人宅院
三公祠含步弓石刻位于荡口镇鹅湖新桥边三公路2006年列为省保单位三公祠是明嘉靖三十六年1557年华察为孙慎翁大立王其勤所立生祠赞颂三人丈量土地厘清田赋造福百姓清代多次重修祠内有思泉亭学海书院望月楼遗爱堂致斋所和衍庆道院等丈量工具步弓石刻嵌在遗爱堂前院西墙上
projects.content_zh: 荡口古镇位于无锡、苏州交界处，古名丁舍，相传是东汉孝子丁兰故里，后因位于鹅肫荡口得名。明洪武年间华贞固迁居此地，名声渐显。明中期荡口所在的南延乡成为江南缴纳粮赋第一乡，华氏也发展成无锡的煌煌大族，明、清两代出了37名进士，著名人物如明代侍读学士华察、出版家华燧、收藏家华夏、东林党人、复社成员华允诚、著名音乐家华秋苹、著名数学家华蘅芳、华世芳兄弟等。镇上有4处13座省保，1处市保，50处历史建筑，多与华氏家族有关。1. 华氏建筑群：包括漫画家华君武旧居；新当里花沿街北侧的"数学双星"华蘅芳、华世芳故居；进步街北仓河的华氏老义庄，庄内有楠木厅，被誉为"江南第一义庄"；学海路上有果育鸿模小学和荡口中学；和平街小巷内的明代华氏进士第，尚存振始堂和明代假山石；旺儿桥旁的华氏始迁祖祠，以及锡甘路旁的华氏真赏斋遗址等，2002年列为省保单位。2. 荡口义庄群：荡口古建筑以义庄最具特色，自清初以来，先后兴建了10余处，以华氏为主，过、殷、徐氏为辅，义庄数量之多、义田规模之大、善举范围之广，均为国内罕见。荡口义庄从单一封建田租发展为多元化收益办庄，从义田、义仓拓展为义庄、义学，从本族慈善事业推向社会慈善义举，从济贫扶弱、救急解困扩展为崇文兴教、办学兴国，为荡口做出了重要贡献。如今保存较好的有华氏老义庄、永喜义庄、华氏襄义庄、徐氏义庄和须义庄五座，2002年列为省保单位。华氏老义庄位于进步街，清乾隆年间华进思、华公弼父子创建，是当地的第一座义庄，规模也最大。现存四进房屋，自南向北依次为隔河照壁、码头、八字照壁、门厅、轿厅、楠木正厅和后厅。西路辟有花园，有水池假山、亭桥廊榭。目前筹建为荡口义庄展示馆。永喜义庄位于青虹路，清道光二十四年（1845年）华永喜妻华锡鳞建。现存四进房屋，由南向北依次为前屋、前厅、大厅和后屋。义庄三面环水，建筑精美，墙中夹有金山石柱，河埠设有闸门，防盗功能完善。华氏襄义庄位于生产街，1924年华襄云建。现存门厅、前厅和后厅共三进和两座侧厢。徐氏义庄位于新桥村老湖桥，清光绪初年进士徐焕后裔所建，俗称红墙门。清光绪三十三年（1907年）在庄内创办湖桥小学堂，新中国成立前曾遭火灾。现存门厅、前厅、大厅和后厅共四进，每进9间，两侧皆有备弄。其中大厅规模较大，梁柱粗壮，雕工细致，体现了苏州民居营造技术对荡口的影响。须义庄位于团结街，今存门厅、前厅和后厅共三进，原为须家祠堂，后改为米行。现为私人宅院。3. 三公祠（含步弓石刻）：位于荡口镇鹅湖新桥边三公路，2006年列为省保单位。三公祠是明嘉靖三十六年（1557年）华察为孙慎、翁大立、王其勤所立生祠，赞颂三人丈量土地，厘清田赋，造福百姓，清代多次重修。祠内有思泉亭、学海书院、望月楼、遗爱堂、致斋所和衍庆道院等。丈量工具"步弓石刻"嵌在遗爱堂前院西墙上。
projects.content_en: Dangkou Ancient Town is located at the junction of Wuxi and Suzhou, anciently named Dingshe, legend says it was the hometown of the Eastern Han filial son Ding Lan, later named for being at the mouth of Ezhun Dang. During the Hongwu reign of the Ming, Hua Zhenggu moved here, and its fame gradually grew. In the mid-Ming, Nanyan Township where Dangkou was located became the number one township in Jiangnan for paying grain taxes, and the Hua family developed into a prominent clan in Wuxi, producing 37 jinshi during the Ming and Qing dynasties. Famous figures include Ming Reader-in-Waiting Hua Cha, publisher Hua Sui, collector Hua Xia, Donglin Party members, Fushe member Hua Yuncheng, famous musician Hua Qiuping, and famous mathematicians Hua Hengfang and Hua Shifang brothers etc. The town has 4 sites with 13 provincial protected buildings, 1 municipal protected building, and 50 historical buildings, mostly related to the Hua family. 1. Hua Family Building Complex: Includes the former residence of cartoonist Hua Junwu; the former residences of "mathematics twin stars" Hua Hengfang and Hua Shifang on the north side of Huayan Street in Xindangli; the Hua Family Old Charity Estate on Beicang River, Jinbu Street, with a nanmu hall inside, hailed as "the number one charity estate in Jiangnan"; on Xuehai Road are Guoyu Hongmo Primary School and Dangkou Middle School; the Ming Hua Family Jinshi Mansion in the alley of Heping Street, with the Zhenshi Hall and Ming rockery stones still preserved; the Hua Family First Ancestor Shrine beside Wang'er Bridge, and the site of the Hua Family Zhenshang Studio on Xigan Road etc., designated a provincial protected site in 2002. 2. Dangkou Charity Estate Group: Dangkou's ancient buildings are most distinctive for their charity estates (yizhuang); since the early Qing, more than 10 have been successively built, mainly by the Hua family, supplemented by the Guo, Yin, and Xu families. The number of charity estates, the scale of charity fields, and the breadth of charitable acts are rare in China. Dangkou charity estates developed from single feudal land rent to diversified income management; from charity fields and charity granaries to charity estates and charity schools; from clan charity to social charity; from helping the poor and rescuing the needy to advocating culture and education and running schools for national rejuvenation—making important contributions to Dangkou. Today, five are well preserved: Hua Family Old Charity Estate, Yongxi Charity Estate, Hua Family Xiang Charity Estate, Xu Family Charity Estate, and Xu Family Charity Estate, designated provincial protected sites in 2002. The Hua Family Old Charity Estate is located on Jinbu Street, founded by Hua Jinsi and Hua Gongbi father and son during the Qianlong reign of the Qing—the first charity estate in the area and also the largest. It preserves four rows of houses, from south to north successively: riverside screen wall, dock,八字 screen wall, gate hall, sedan hall, nanmu main hall, and rear hall. The west road has a garden with pond, rockery, pavilions, bridges, and corridors. It is currently being prepared as the Dangkou Charity Estate Exhibition Hall. The Yongxi Charity Estate is located on Qinghong Road, built by Hua Yongxi's wife Hua Xilin in the 24th year of Daoguang of the Qing (1845). It preserves four rows of houses, from south to north successively: front house, front hall, main hall, and rear house. The charity estate is surrounded by water on three sides, with exquisite architecture, Jinshan stone pillars embedded in the walls, and gates at the river landings with complete anti-theft functions. The Hua Family Xiang Charity Estate is located on Shengchan Street, built by Hua Xiangyun in 1924. It preserves three rows: gate hall, front hall, and rear hall, plus two side wings. The Xu Family Charity Estate is located at Laohu Bridge, Xinqiao Village, built by the descendants of jinshi Xu Huan in the early Guangxu reign of the Qing, commonly called the Red Wall Gate. In the 33rd year of Guangxu (1907), the Huqiao Primary School was founded inside the estate; before the founding of New China it suffered a fire. It preserves four rows: gate hall, front hall, main hall, and rear hall, each row with 9 bays, with service corridors on both sides. The main hall is relatively large, with thick beams and columns and exquisite carvings, reflecting the influence of Suzhou residential construction techniques on Dangkou. The Xu Family Charity Estate is located on Tuanjie Street, today preserving three rows: gate hall, front hall, and rear hall, originally the Xu family ancestral hall, later changed to a rice shop. Now a private residence. 3. Sangong (Three Dukes) Shrine (including Step-Bow Stone Carving): Located on Sangong Road by Ehu New Bridge in Dangkou Town, designated a provincial protected site in 2006. The Sangong Shrine was a living shrine established by Hua Cha in the 36th year of Jiajing of the Ming (1557) for Sun Shen, Weng Dali, and Wang Qinqin, praising the three for measuring land, clarifying field taxes, and benefiting the people; repaired multiple times during the Qing. Inside the shrine are the Siquan Pavilion, Xuehai Academy, Wangyue Tower, Yi'ai (Remaining Love) Hall, Zhai Studio, and Yanqing Daoist Temple etc. The surveying tool "Step-Bow Stone Carving" is embedded in the west wall of the front courtyard of the Yi'ai Hall.

projects.name: 昭嗣堂
projects.level: 第六批全国重点文物保护单位（2006年）
projects.level_en: 6th Batch National Key Cultural Heritage Site (2006)
projects.address_en: Yu'an Road, Shuofang Street, Binhu District
highlights: 明嘉靖七年1528年进士曹察建清乾隆十三年1748年改为曹氏家祠名昭嗣堂现存门厅过厅和正厅昭嗣堂庭院前窄后宽呈凸字形是当地流行的吉宅形制昭嗣堂是明代原构面阔五间进深十一架全用上等金丝楠木建成又名香楠厅是江苏保存最完整的明代楠木建筑厅内明间有草架双脊梁枋等处施彩画檐下砖雕纹样细致曹察女为嘉靖端妃曹氏因宫变牵连被处死据说曹察回乡后为纪念女儿倾尽财产建造了这座香楠厅寓意香囡之厅厅内北面正中的两根青石柱则代表双亲青
projects.content_zh: 明嘉靖七年（1528年）进士曹察建，清乾隆十三年（1748年）改为曹氏家祠，名昭嗣堂，现存门厅、过厅和正厅昭嗣堂。庭院前窄后宽呈"凸"字形，是当地流行的吉宅形制。昭嗣堂是明代原构，面阔五间，进深十一架，全用上等金丝楠木建成，又名香楠厅，是江苏保存最完整的明代楠木建筑。厅内明间有草架、双脊，梁枋等处施彩画，檐下砖雕纹样细致。曹察女为嘉靖端妃曹氏，因宫变牵连被处死，据说曹察回乡后为纪念女儿倾尽财产建造了这座香楠厅，寓意"香囡之厅"，厅内北面正中的两根青石柱则代表"双亲（青）"。
projects.content_en: Built by jinshi Cao Cha in the 7th year of Jiajing of the Ming (1528), changed to the Cao family ancestral hall in the 13th year of Qianlong of the Qing (1748), named Zhaosi Hall; today preserves the gate hall, passage hall, and main hall Zhaosi Hall. The courtyard is narrow in front and wide at the back,呈 a "convex" shape—a popular auspicious house form in the area. Zhaosi Hall is an original Ming structure, five bays wide and eleven rafters deep, entirely built of high-quality golden-thread nanmu, also called the Fragrant Nanmu Hall—the best-preserved Ming nanmu building in Jiangsu. Inside the hall, the central bay has a hidden frame and double ridges, with painted decorations on beams and lintels, and exquisite brick carving patterns under the eaves. Cao Cha's daughter was Consort Duan of the Jiajing Emperor, surnamed Cao, who was executed due to implication in a palace coup; it is said that after returning home, Cao Cha exhausted his fortune to build this fragrant nanmu hall in memory of his daughter, meaning "Hall of the Fragrant Daughter," and the two bluestone columns in the center of the north side of the hall represent "parents (qing/bluestone)."

projects.name: 兴国寺塔
projects.level: 第七批全国重点文物保护单位（2013年）
projects.level_en: 7th Batch National Key Cultural Heritage Site (2013)
projects.address_en: In Xingguo Garden, No. 58 South Zhongshan Road
highlights: 兴国寺塔始建于北宋太平兴国796-983年间原属太平教寺后来寺庙荒废唯塔尚存塔原高七层外壁呈八边形内壁呈四边形塔内有转角木梯可登高临眺各层皆开壶门和直棂假窗上下相错元至正年间塔遭毁坏明正统年间修复增高为九层木檐砖身楼阁式塔清嘉庆二十二年1817年塔内木构和塔顶毁于火仅存砖壁塔身1925年直奉军阀混战时炮弹削去顶层西南半侧塔颠变成钢笔尖状1985年重修塔现高42.83米6层以下为宋代原物2002年围绕寺塔拓建为宋代风格的兴国园塔东有经幢亭内置唐咸通十一年870年所刻经幢
projects.content_zh: 兴国寺塔始建于北宋太平兴国（796—983）年间，原属太平教寺，后来寺庙荒废唯塔尚存。塔原高七层，外壁呈八边形，内壁呈四边形，塔内有转角木梯，可登高临眺。各层皆开壶门和直棂假窗，上下相错。元至正年间塔遭毁坏，明正统年间修复，增高为九层木檐砖身楼阁式塔。清嘉庆二十二年（1817年），塔内木构和塔顶毁于火，仅存砖壁塔身。1925年直奉军阀混战时，炮弹削去顶层西南半侧，塔颠变成钢笔尖状。1985年重修，塔现高42.83米，6层以下为宋代原物。2002年围绕寺塔拓建为宋代风格的兴国园。塔东有经幢亭，内置唐咸通十一年（870年）所刻经幢。
projects.content_en: Xingguo Temple Pagoda was first built during the Taiping Xingguo reign of the Northern Song (976-983), originally belonging to the Taipingjiao Temple; later the temple fell into disrepair and only the pagoda survived. The pagoda was originally seven stories high, with an octagonal outer wall and a quadrilateral inner wall, with a corner wooden ladder inside allowing climbing to overlook. Each story has pot-door openings and straight-lattice false windows, alternating up and down. During the Zhizheng reign of the Yuan, the pagoda was damaged; repaired during the Zhengtong reign of the Ming, raised to a nine-story wooden-eave brick-body pavilion-style pagoda. In the 22nd year of Jiaqing of the Qing (1817), the wooden structure and pagoda top were destroyed by fire, leaving only the brick wall body. In 1925 during the Zhili-Fengtian warlord melee, a shell削去 the southwest half of the top story, and the pagoda top became pen-nib shaped. Repaired in 1985, the pagoda is now 42.83 meters high, with the six lower stories being original Song structures. In 2002, the area around the temple pagoda was expanded into the Song-style Xingguo Garden. East of the pagoda is a dharani pillar pavilion, containing a dharani pillar carved in the 11th year of Xiantong of the Tang (870).

projects.name: 刘氏兄弟故居
projects.level: 第七批全国重点文物保护单位（2013年）
projects.level_en: 7th Batch National Key Cultural Heritage Site (2013)
projects.address_en: No. 49 West Heng Street
highlights: 刘氏兄弟故居是文学家教育学家语言学家刘半农音乐家刘天华和刘北茂三兄弟出生和青少年时期生活和学习的场所他们被冰心誉为刘氏三杰是中国近代文化界的杰出人物这处故居由他们的曾祖父刘荣建于清末坐西朝东现存三间两进及后院的两座厢房今为刘氏兄弟纪念馆展示他们少年生活的细节和后来的成就清丽朴素的建筑和器物配着细腻生动的解说古朴而别具情趣在城市扩建过程中周围老宅已被拆光只留下这组院落处在人民路中央两侧车水马龙行客匆匆刘氏故居则环绕在青草绿树间粉墙黛瓦老井深院腊梅月桂在喧嚣和繁华中显得幽静安详
projects.content_zh: 刘氏兄弟故居是文学家、教育学家、语言学家刘半农，音乐家刘天华和刘北茂三兄弟出生和青少年时期生活和学习的场所，他们被冰心誉为"刘氏三杰"，是中国近代文化界的杰出人物。这处故居由他们的曾祖父刘荣建于清末，坐西朝东，现存三间两进及后院的两座厢房，今为刘氏兄弟纪念馆，展示他们少年生活的细节和后来的成就，清丽朴素的建筑和器物，配着细腻生动的解说，古朴而别具情趣。在城市扩建过程中，周围老宅已被拆光，只留下这组院落处在人民路中央，两侧车水马龙、行客匆匆，刘氏故居则环绕在青草绿树间，粉墙黛瓦、老井深院、腊梅月桂……在喧嚣和繁华中显得幽静安详。
projects.content_en: The Former Residence of the Liu Brothers is the place where writer, educator, and linguist Liu Bannong, and musicians Liu Tianhua and Liu Beimao, three brothers, were born and lived and studied during their youth; they were hailed by Bing Xin as the "Three Outstanding Liu Brothers," distinguished figures in modern Chinese cultural circles. This residence was built by their great-grandfather Liu Rong in the late Qing, facing west with its back to east, today preserving three bays in two rows and two wing rooms in the rear courtyard, now the Liu Brothers Memorial Hall, displaying details of their teenage life and later achievements; the elegant and simple buildings and objects, paired with delicate and vivid explanations, are quaint and uniquely charming. During urban expansion, the surrounding old houses were all demolished, leaving only this courtyard complex in the center of Renmin Road, with heavy traffic and hurrying pedestrians on both sides; the Liu residence, surrounded by green grass and trees, with white walls and black tiles, old well and deep courtyard, wintersweet and cassia... appears serene and peaceful amid the noise and prosperity.

projects.name: 江阴文庙
projects.level: 第四批江苏省文物保护单位（1995年）
projects.level_en: 4th Batch Jiangsu Provincial Cultural Heritage Site (1995)
projects.address_en: No. 196 Middle Renmin Road
highlights: 这处文庙始建于北宋淳化三年992年原在监狱旁边北宋景祐三年1036年在范仲淹庆历新政带动下江阴守令范宗古在今址重建文庙并邀请范仲淹撰写景祐重建文宣王庙记南宋绍熙年间此庙已具较大规模此后屡毁屡建今存建筑多建于明清两代江阴文庙坐北朝南由南向北依次为棂星门泮池大成门大成殿和明伦堂南部的半月形泮池及池上三桥皆为明正统二年1437旧物居中的大成殿面阔五间进深十架采用重檐歇山顶内供孔子塑像殿内梁架皆施彩绘古朴可观
projects.content_zh: 这处文庙始建于北宋淳化三年（992年），原在监狱旁边，北宋景祐三年（1036年）在范仲淹"庆历新政"带动下，江阴守令范宗古在今址重建文庙，并邀请范仲淹撰写《景祐重建文宣王庙记》。南宋绍熙年间此庙已具较大规模，此后屡毁屡建，今存建筑多建于明清两代。江阴文庙坐北朝南，由南向北依次为棂星门、泮池、大成门、大成殿和明伦堂。南部的半月形泮池及池上三桥皆为明正统二年（1437）旧物。居中的大成殿面阔五间，进深十架，采用重檐歇山顶，内供孔子塑像，殿内梁架皆施彩绘，古朴可观。
projects.content_en: This Confucian Temple was first built in the 3rd year of Chunhua of the Northern Song (992), originally beside the prison; in the 3rd year of Jingyou of the Northern Song (1036), driven by Fan Zhongyan's "Qingli New Policies," Jiangyin magistrate Fan Zonggu rebuilt the Confucian Temple at today's site and invited Fan Zhongyan to write the "Record of Rebuilding the Temple of King Wenxuan in Jingyou." During the Shaoxi reign of the Southern Song, this temple already had a relatively large scale; thereafter it was repeatedly destroyed and rebuilt, and today's surviving buildings were mostly built during the Ming and Qing dynasties. Jiangyin Confucian Temple faces south, from south to north successively the Lingxing Gate, Pan Pond, Dacheng Gate, Dacheng Hall, and Minglun Hall. The crescent-shaped Pan Pond in the south and the three bridges over it are all original objects from the 2nd year of Zhengtong of the Ming (1437). The central Dacheng Hall is five bays wide and ten rafters deep, adopting a double-eave hip-and-gable roof, with a seated statue of Confucius inside; the beam frames inside the hall are all painted, quaint and viewable.

projects.name: 中山公园（季园）
projects.level: 含心经碑殿（省保1982年）
projects.level_en: Including Heart Sutra Stele Hall (provincial protected 1982)
projects.address_en: East side of North Hongqiao Road
highlights: 北宋初在此建孙氏万春园明代改为清机园清代先后成为季园和寄园1930年更名中山公园其中以寄园最知名位于今公园东部有假山地沼亭榭廊壁上嵌有清人所作寄园诗文较有文献价值的是王先谦的重修寄园记寄园东北角为铁佛寺旧址今为心经碑殿内供心经碑原为唐代高僧道松所书明万历间毁清嘉庆三年1798年据拓本重刻1982年列为省保单位殿中另有赵孟頫乾明广福禅寺重建观音殿记寄园外部西侧为六角忠邦亭纪念明末江阴抗清英雄阎应元亭子周围是由宋代千年紫藤攀附而成的环廊忠邦亭西北南北中轴线北端是建于1925年的孙中山先生纪念塔纪念塔西北为明代聚奎亭俗称状元亭明万历三十八年1610年知县许达道建勉励邑人刻苦攻读此亭原在启圣祠东南后移置园内这是一座四角亭下为须弥石座上立青石柱梁以榫口相接并刻有精美浮雕造型结构独具一格
projects.content_zh: 北宋初在此建孙氏万春园，明代改为清机园，清代先后成为季园和寄园，1930年更名中山公园。其中以寄园最知名，位于今公园东部，有假山、地沼、亭榭，廊壁上嵌有清人所作寄园诗文，较有文献价值的是王先谦的《重修寄园记》。寄园东北角为铁佛寺旧址，今为心经碑殿，内供心经碑，原为唐代高僧道松所书，明万历间毁，清嘉庆三年（1798年）据拓本重刻，1982年列为省保单位。殿中另有赵孟頫《乾明广福禅寺重建观音殿记》。寄园外部西侧为六角忠邦亭，纪念明末江阴抗清英雄阎应元。亭子周围是由宋代千年紫藤攀附而成的环廊。忠邦亭西北，南北中轴线北端，是建于1925年的孙中山先生纪念塔。纪念塔西北为明代聚奎亭，俗称状元亭，明万历三十八年（1610年）知县许达道建，勉励邑人刻苦攻读。此亭原在启圣祠东南，后移置园内。这是一座四角亭，下为须弥石座，上立青石柱、梁，以榫口相接，并刻有精美浮雕，造型、结构独具一格。
projects.content_en: In the early Northern Song, the Sun Family Wanchun Garden was built here; in the Ming it was changed to the Qingji Garden; in the Qing it successively became the Jiyuan and Jiyuan (Send Garden); in 1930 it was renamed Dr. Sun Yat-sen Park. Among them, the Jiyuan (Send Garden) is the most famous, located in the eastern part of today's park, with rockery, ponds, pavilions and terraces; the corridor walls are embedded with poems and essays about the Jiyuan written by Qing people, with the more documentarily valuable being Wang Xianqian's "Record of Rebuilding the Jiyuan." The northeast corner of the Jiyuan is the former site of the Iron Buddha Temple, today the Heart Sutra Stele Hall, containing the Heart Sutra stele, originally written by the eminent Tang monk Daosong, destroyed during the Wanli reign of the Ming, re-carved from a rubbing in the 3rd year of Jiaqing of the Qing (1798), designated a provincial protected site in 1982. In the hall there is also Zhao Mengfu's "Record of Rebuilding the Guanyin Hall of the Qianming Guangfu Chan Temple." West of the outside of the Jiyuan is the hexagonal Zhongbang (Loyal to the State) Pavilion, commemorating Yan Yingyuan, the late-Ming Jiangyin hero who resisted the Qing. Around the pavilion is a circular corridor formed by a thousand-year-old wisteria from the Song climbing. Northwest of the Zhongbang Pavilion, at the north end of the north-south central axis, is the Dr. Sun Yat-sen Memorial Tower built in 1925. Northwest of the memorial tower is the Ming Juqui (Gathering Excellence) Pavilion, commonly called the Zhuangyuan (Top Scholar) Pavilion, built by magistrate Xu Dadao in the 38th year of Wanli of the Ming (1610), encouraging local people to study hard. This pavilion was originally southeast of the Qisheng Shrine, later moved into the park. It is a four-corner pavilion, with a Sumeru stone base below, and bluestone columns and beams above, joined by mortise-and-tenon joints, with exquisite relief carvings—unique in shape and structure.

projects.name: 适园
projects.level: 第七批全国重点文物保护单位（2013年）
projects.level_en: 7th Batch National Key Cultural Heritage Site (2013)
projects.address_en: Inside the residential compound at No. 234 South Street, Chengjiang Town
highlights: 清咸丰四年1854年书画家陈式金1817-1867急人之用双倍价钱购下邻家宅基他运用书画理论亲自指挥开池堆山筑房构屋由于是无意为园而适成之取名适园太平天国时期适园被太平军占为王府得以保存收复后其子陈曦唐主持重修陈氏父子皆擅长书画兼工诗词适园营造颇得诗情画意文革时期适园作为印刷厂工人宿舍而幸免于难是江阴现存最好的古典园林适园西侧为陈氏住宅近年修复园门在靠近住宅一侧园林以南部镜湖和北部假山为主体南东北三侧环绕湖山布置亭堂轩馆等建筑北部假山用土堆成三面皆有路可以登山路旁立黄石峰山顶为超然台设有石桌石凳供人休憩眺远假山北部是得蝶绕云山馆原为陈家祭祖厅堂向南隔着水池与主堂水流云在轩相对这一馆一轩都含有云字喻指北部这座假山古代将石比作云得蝶绕云山馆处在山林间为蝶绕云山水流云在轩前临水池含水流心不竞云在意俱迟之意水流云在轩西侧有王羲之换鹅碑秋入湳波室和适安斋陈氏父子富于收藏曾收名人书画碑帖500余种当年便藏在适安斋中轩东经香廊通向池东的响秋书房书房东侧紧贴园墙北为黄石假山南为湖石假山采用立体作法其下为洞其上为台两山一脉通贯气势相连书房北部是易画轩陈式金以画会友来求画者需当场作诗以诗易画由此得名轩北为倪云林山水石刻和得爽亭当年陈式金曾聘石匠张萃山将自己收藏中最著名的20余种名帖镌刻在廊壁上王羲之换鹅碑和倪云林山水石刻为其中精品
projects.content_zh: 清咸丰四年（1854年）书画家陈式金（1817—1867）急人之用，用双倍价钱购下邻家宅基，他运用书画理论，亲自指挥开池堆山、筑房构屋，由于是"无意为园而适成之"，取名适园。太平天国时期适园被太平军占为王府，得以保存，收复后其子陈曦唐主持重修。陈氏父子皆擅长书画，兼工诗词，适园营造颇得诗情画意。"文革"时期，适园作为印刷厂工人宿舍而幸免于难，是江阴现存最好的古典园林。适园西侧为陈氏住宅，近年修复，园门在靠近住宅一侧。园林以南部镜湖和北部假山为主体，南、东、北三侧环绕湖、山布置亭堂轩馆等建筑。北部假山用土堆成，三面皆有路可以登山，路旁立黄石峰，山顶为超然台，设有石桌石凳，供人休憩眺远。假山北部是得蝶绕云山馆，原为陈家祭祖厅堂，向南隔着水池与主堂水流云在轩相对。这一馆一轩都含有"云"字，喻指北部这座假山。古代将石比作云，得蝶绕云山馆处在山林间，为"蝶绕云山"；水流云在轩前临水池，含"水流心不竞，云在意俱迟"之意。水流云在轩西侧有"王羲之换鹅碑"、秋入湳波室和适安斋。陈氏父子富于收藏，曾收名人书画碑帖500余种，当年便藏在适安斋中。轩东经香廊通向池东的响秋书房，书房东侧紧贴园墙，北为黄石假山，南为湖石假山，采用立体作法，其下为洞，其上为台，两山一脉通贯，气势相连。书房北部是易画轩，陈式金以画会友，来求画者需当场作诗，以诗易画，由此得名。轩北为"倪云林山水石刻"和得爽亭。当年陈式金曾聘石匠张萃山将自己收藏中最著名的20余种名帖镌刻在廊壁上，"王羲之换鹅碑"和"倪云林山水石刻"为其中精品。
projects.content_en: In the 4th year of Xianfeng of the Qing (1854), calligrapher-painter Chen Shijin (1817-1867), in urgent need of space, purchased the neighbor's house foundation at double the price; using calligraphy and painting theory, he personally directed digging ponds, piling mountains, building houses and constructing rooms; because it was "not intended as a garden but became one appropriately," it was named Shiyuan (Appropriate Garden). During the Taiping Rebellion, Shiyuan was occupied by the Taiping Army as a royal residence and thus preserved; after recovery, his son Chen Xitang directed the restoration. The Chen father and son were both skilled in calligraphy and painting, and also excelled in poetry, so the construction of Shiyuan gained much poetic and pictorial charm. During the Cultural Revolution, Shiyuan survived as a workers' dormitory for a printing factory, and is the best-preserved classical garden in Jiangyin. West of Shiyuan is the Chen family residence, restored in recent years, with the garden gate near the residence side. The garden takes the southern Jinghu (Mirror Lake) and northern rockery as the main body, with pavilions, halls, and studios arranged around the lake and mountain on the south, east, and north sides. The northern rockery is piled with earth, with paths on three sides for climbing; yellow stone peaks stand by the paths, and at the mountain top is the Chaoran (Transcendent) Terrace, with stone tables and stools for rest and distant viewing. North of the rockery is the Dedie Raoyun (Butterflies Circling Clouds) Mountain Hall, originally the Chen family's ancestral worship hall, facing the main hall Shuiliu Yunzai (Flowing Water and Stationary Cloud) Studio across the pond to the south. Both this hall and studio contain the character "yun" (cloud), metaphorically referring to this northern rockery. In ancient times, stones were compared to clouds; the Dedie Raoyun Mountain Hall is in the mountain forest, meaning "butterflies circling cloud mountains"; the Shuiliu Yunzai Studio faces the pond, containing the meaning "flowing water does not compete in the heart, stationary clouds linger in intention." West of the Shuiliu Yunzai Studio are the "Wang Xizhi Goose-Exchange Stele," Qiuru Nanbo Room, and Shi'an Studio. The Chen father and son were rich in collections, once collecting over 500 kinds of famous calligraphy, paintings, and model calligraphy albums, which were stored in the Shi'an Studio in those years. East of the studio, through the Fragrant Corridor, leads to the Xiangqiu (Autumn Sound) Study east of the pond; east of the study紧贴 the garden wall, with a yellow stone rockery to the north and a Taihu stone rockery to the south, adopting a three-dimensional method with caves below and terraces above, the two mountains connected in one vein with connected momentum. North of the study is the Yihua (Exchange Painting) Studio; Chen Shijin made friends through painting, and those who came to request paintings had to compose poems on the spot, exchanging poems for paintings, hence the name. North of the studio are the "Ni Yunlin Landscape Stone Carvings" and Deshuang Pavilion. In those years, Chen Shijin hired stonemason Zhang Cuishan to carve over 20 of the most famous model calligraphy albums from his collection on the corridor walls, with the "Wang Xizhi Goose-Exchange Stele" and "Ni Yunlin Landscape Stone Carvings" being the finest among them.

projects.name: 黄山炮台旧址
projects.level: 第七批全国重点文物保护单位（2013年）
projects.level_en: 7th Batch National Key Cultural Heritage Site (2013)
projects.address: 公园路北端，鹅鼻嘴公园对面
projects.address_en: North end of Park Road, opposite Ebi Zui Park
highlights: 江阴是防卫长江的要塞市内的黄山距长江北岸最窄岩壁陡峭素有江海门户镇航要塞之称清康熙年间清政府就在此修筑炮台同治光绪年间为防外舰入侵再次增筑炮台成为中外闻名的江阴要塞如今清理出土了7座清同治十三年1874的古炮和2尊耀武大将军万斤铁炮及弹丸黄山炮台对面为鹅山炮台皆可供人凭吊古战场遗迹
projects.content_zh: 江阴是防卫长江的要塞，市内的黄山距长江北岸最窄，岩壁陡峭，素有"江海门户""镇航要塞"之称。清康熙年间清政府就在此修筑炮台，同治、光绪年间，为防外舰入侵，再次增筑炮台，成为中外闻名的江阴要塞。如今清理出土了7座清同治十三年（1874）的古炮和2尊"耀武大将军"万斤铁炮及弹丸。黄山炮台对面为鹅山炮台，皆可供人凭吊古战场遗迹。
projects.content_en: Jiangyin is a fortress defending the Yangtze River; Huangshan (Yellow Mountain) in the city is at the narrowest point from the north bank of the Yangtze, with steep rock walls, known as the "Gateway of River and Sea" and "Navigational Fortress." During the Kangxi reign of the Qing, the Qing government already built batteries here; during the Tongzhi and Guangxu reigns, to prevent foreign warship invasion, batteries were again added, becoming the internationally famous Jiangyin Fortress. Today, 7 ancient cannons from the 13th year of Tongzhi of the Qing (1874) and 2 "Yaowu General" ten-thousand-catty iron cannons with cannonballs have been excavated. Opposite the Huangshan Battery is the Eshan Battery, both可供 people to pay homage to the ancient battlefield ruins.

projects.name: 徐霞客故居
projects.level: 第五批全国重点文物保护单位（2011年，含晴山堂石刻）
projects.level_en: 5th Batch National Key Cultural Heritage Site (2011, including Qingshan Hall Stone Carvings)
projects.address_en: Xu Xiake Town (Mazhen), Jiangyin City
highlights: 徐霞客1587-1641名弘祖字振之号霞客是明代伟大的地理学家探险家和旅行家足迹遍及今19个省区市留下60余万字的徐霞客游记故居始建于明代原有三进两侧有厢房故居内有徐霞客塑像和生平事迹陈列故居正厅前东侧有古罗汉松原植于江阴君山徐霞客曾在松下读书后移此故居东南为晴山堂始建于明万历四十八年1620年徐霞客为庆贺母亲大病初愈而建取四月清和雨乍晴南山当户转分明诗意堂内嵌有元末明初84位名家撰写的95块石刻具有很高的历史和书法艺术价值故居西南为徐霞客墓1978年迁建于此墓前立石碑上刻十七世霞客徐公之墓故居北侧为徐霞客旅游博物馆展示徐霞客的旅行路线和探险精神
projects.content_zh: 徐霞客（1587—1641），名弘祖，字振之，号霞客，是明代伟大的地理学家、探险家和旅行家，足迹遍及今19个省区市，留下60余万字的《徐霞客游记》。故居始建于明代，原有三进，两侧有厢房，故居内有徐霞客塑像和生平事迹陈列。故居正厅前东侧有古罗汉松，原植于江阴君山，徐霞客曾在松下读书，后移此。故居东南为晴山堂，始建于明万历四十八年（1620年），徐霞客为庆贺母亲大病初愈而建，取"四月清和雨乍晴，南山当户转分明"诗意，堂内嵌有元末明初84位名家撰写的95块石刻，具有很高的历史和书法艺术价值。故居西南为徐霞客墓，1978年迁建于此，墓前立石碑，上刻"十七世霞客徐公之墓"。故居北侧为徐霞客旅游博物馆，展示徐霞客的旅行路线和探险精神。
projects.content_en: Xu Xiake (1587-1641), given name Hongzu, style name Zhenzhi, hao Xiake, was a great geographer, explorer, and traveler of the Ming Dynasty, with footprints spanning today's 19 provinces, autonomous regions, and municipalities, leaving over 600,000 characters of the "Travels of Xu Xiake." The former residence was first built in the Ming Dynasty, originally with three rows and wing rooms on both sides; inside the residence are a statue of Xu Xiake and an exhibition of his life and deeds. East of the front of the main hall is an ancient Podocarpus tree, originally planted at Junshan in Jiangyin, where Xu Xiake once studied under the tree, later moved here. Southeast of the residence is the Qingshan (Clear Mountain) Hall, first built in the 48th year of Wanli of the Ming (1620), built by Xu Xiake to celebrate his mother's recovery from a serious illness, taking the poetic meaning "April clear and mild, rain just cleared, the southern mountain facing the door turns distinct"; embedded in the hall are 95 stone carvings written by 84 famous masters from the late Yuan to early Ming, with high historical and calligraphic artistic value. Southwest of the residence is the Tomb of Xu Xiake, relocated here in 1978, with a stone stele in front of the tomb inscribed "Tomb of Lord Xu, 17th Generation Xiake." North of the residence is the Xu Xiake Tourism Museum, displaying Xu Xiake's travel routes and spirit of exploration.

projects.name: 周王庙
projects.level: 第七批全国重点文物保护单位（2013年）
projects.level_en: 7th Batch National Key Cultural Heritage Site (2013)
projects.address_en: No. 9 Dongmiao Lane, Yicheng Town
highlights: 周王庙奉祠晋平西将军周处242-297始建于晋元康九年299年原名周孝侯庙南宋绍兴年间赠英烈庙额称周王庙明嘉靖四十五年1566年重建现存戏台正殿和后殿共三进并有唐至清碑刻一百余方其中唐碑2方宋碑8方元碑2方明碑64方清民国碑23方具有很高的历史价值和艺术价值周处240-297是阳羡今宜兴人自幼膂力过人好生事端邻里乡亲将他与山中虎水中蛟并称为三害他后来悔过自新斩蛟射虎又拜陆机陆云为师学识大进受到乡里称道周处除三害的故事被刘义庆收入世说新语自新广为流传后经州府推荐周处历任多县太守及楚内史散骑常侍御史中丞等职晋元康六年296年氐族起兵反晋周处被任命为建威将军第二年在陕西六陌今属乾县力战而死晋建武元年304年朝廷追赠他为平西将军清流亭侯后世称为周孝侯周王庙第一进戏楼为1994年重建第二进大殿建于明嘉靖四十五年1566年采用前轩后殿布局宽五间深九架建筑立柱用花岗岩阳山石和青石制作高敞宏伟大殿内存唐至清碑刻18通最珍贵的是唐元和六年811年平西将军周府君碑和明重刻王羲之王晋周孝侯碑第三进后殿世泽堂也建于明代2000年增建两侧耳房东西围墙碑廊中有唐贞义女碑宋李曾柏生平碑宋苏东坡楚颂碑和明净云枝法帖等80余通
projects.content_zh: 周王庙奉祠晋平西将军周处（242—297），始建于晋元康九年（299年），原名周孝侯庙，南宋绍兴年间赠"英烈"庙额，称周王庙，明嘉靖四十五年（1566年）重建，现存戏台、正殿和后殿共三进，并有唐至清碑刻一百余方（其中唐碑2方、宋碑8方、元碑2方、明碑64方、清民国碑23方），具有很高的历史价值和艺术价值。周处（240—297）是阳羡（今宜兴）人，自幼膂力过人，好生事端，邻里乡亲将他与山中虎、水中蛟并称为"三害"。他后来悔过自新，斩蛟射虎，又拜陆机、陆云为师，学识大进，受到乡里称道，"周处除三害"的故事被刘义庆收入《世说新语·自新》，广为流传。后经州府推荐，周处历任多县太守及楚内史、散骑常侍、御史中丞等职。晋元康六年（296年）氐族起兵反晋，周处被任命为建威将军，第二年在陕西六陌（今属乾县）力战而死。晋建武元年（304年）朝廷追赠他为平西将军、清流亭侯，后世称为周孝侯。周王庙第一进戏楼为1994年重建。第二进大殿建于明嘉靖四十五年（1566年），采用前轩后殿布局，宽五间、深九架，建筑立柱用花岗岩、阳山石和青石制作，高敞宏伟。大殿内存唐至清碑刻18通，最珍贵的是唐元和六年（811年）《平西将军周府君碑》和明重刻王羲之《晋周孝侯碑》。第三进后殿世泽堂也建于明代，2000年增建两侧耳房，东西围墙碑廊中有唐贞义女碑、宋李曾柏生平碑、宋苏东坡楚颂碑和明净云枝法帖等80余通。
projects.content_en: Zhouwang Temple enshrines Zhou Chu (242-297), General Who Pacifies the West of the Jin Dynasty, first built in the 9th year of Yuankang of the Jin (299), originally named the Zhou Xiaohou (Zhou the Filial Marquis) Temple; during the Shaoxing reign of the Southern Song, it was granted the temple plaque "Yinglie" (Heroic Martyr), called Zhouwang Temple; rebuilt in the 45th year of Jiajing of the Ming (1566), today preserves three rows: stage, main hall, and rear hall, with over a hundred stele carvings from the Tang to Qing (including 2 Tang steles, 8 Song steles, 2 Yuan steles, 64 Ming steles, and 23 Qing-Republic steles), with high historical and artistic value. Zhou Chu (240-297) was a native of Yangxian (today's Yixing); from childhood he had extraordinary physical strength and liked to cause trouble, and neighbors and villagers called him, together with the tiger in the mountains and the flood dragon in the water, the "Three Scourges." He later repented and reformed, killing the flood dragon and shooting the tiger, and then became a disciple of Lu Ji and Lu Yun, greatly advancing his learning, receiving praise from the village; the story of "Zhou Chu Eliminating the Three Scourges" was included by Liu Yiqing in "A New Account of the Tales of the World·Self-Renewal," widely circulated. Later recommended by prefectural and county authorities, Zhou Chu successively served as magistrate of multiple counties, as well as Interior Minister of Chu, Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary, and Censorate Vice Censor-in-Chief etc. In the 6th year of Yuankang of the Jin (296), the Di people rose up against Jin, and Zhou Chu was appointed General Who Establishes Might; the following year he died fighting at Liumo in Shaanxi (today belonging to Qianxian). In the 1st year of Jianwu of the Jin (304), the court posthumously awarded him General Who Pacifies the West and Marquis of Qingliu Ting, later generations calling him Zhou Xiaohou. The first row of Zhouwang Temple, the opera tower, was rebuilt in 1994. The second row, the main hall, was built in the 45th year of Jiajing of the Ming (1566), adopting a front-veranda rear-hall layout, five bays wide and nine rafters deep, with building columns made of granite, Yangshan stone, and bluestone, tall and magnificent. The main hall preserves 18 stele carvings from the Tang to Qing, the most precious being the "Stele of Lord Zhou's Mansion, General Who Pacifies the West" from the 6th year of Yuanhe of the Tang (811) and the Ming re-carving of Wang Xizhi's "Stele of Jin Zhou Xiaohou." The third row, the rear hall Shize (Inheriting Grace) Hall, was also built in the Ming; in 2000 side rooms were added on both sides, and the stele corridors on the east and west enclosure walls contain over 80 pieces including the Tang Zhenyi (Chaste Righteous) Daughter Stele, Song Li Zengbai's Life Stele, Song Su Dongpo's Chu Song Stele, and Ming Jingyunzhi Model Calligraphy Album etc.

projects.name: 瀛园
projects.level: 第七批江苏省文物保护单位（2011年）
projects.level_en: 7th Batch Jiangsu Provincial Cultural Heritage Site (2011)
projects.address: 宜城镇人民中路文化大厦B幢（青云巷）东，城隍庙（今电影院）左侧
projects.address_en: East of Building B, Cultural Mansion, Middle Renmin Road, Yicheng Town (Qingyun Lane), left of the City God Temple (today's cinema)
highlights: 瀛园原为清乾隆年间谢庭扬的私宅取潘岳秋兴赋体以行和之义命名为行园后来行园毁于兵火邑人将其与旁边建于清康熙年间的竹荫轩合并改建为城隍庙花园取瀛洲仙境之意称瀛园园林以荷池为中心北为正堂行和厅西为望来亭和逸兴遄飞阁南为竹荫轩东部建有曲廊园中山水模拟宜兴的自然风光山像铜官水似西氿池西石桥则仿善卷洞张公洞颇具匠心
projects.content_zh: 瀛园原为清乾隆年间谢庭扬的私宅，取潘岳《秋兴赋》"体以行和"之义命名为行园。后来行园毁于兵火，邑人将其与旁边建于清康熙年间的竹荫轩合并，改建为城隍庙花园，取"瀛洲仙境"之意称瀛园。园林以荷池为中心，北为正堂行和厅，西为望来亭和逸兴遄飞阁，南为竹荫轩，东部建有曲廊。园中山水模拟宜兴的自然风光，山像铜官，水似西氿，池西石桥则仿善卷洞、张公洞，颇具匠心。
projects.content_en: Yingyuan Garden was originally the private residence of Xie Tingyang during the Qianlong reign of the Qing, taking the meaning of "the body acts in harmony" from Pan Yue's "Ode to Autumn Awakening" to name it Xingyuan (Action-Harmony Garden). Later Xingyuan was destroyed by war fires; local people merged it with the adjacent Zhuyin (Bamboo Shade) Studio built during the Kangxi reign of the Qing, rebuilding it into the City God Temple Garden, taking the meaning of "Yingzhou Immortal Realm" to call it Yingyuan (Immortal Isle Garden). The garden centers on the lotus pond, with the main hall Xinghe (Action-Harmony) Hall to the north, Wanglai (Welcoming Arrivals) Pavilion and Yixing Chuanfei (Leisurely Soaring) Pavilion to the west, Zhuyin Studio to the south, and a winding corridor built in the east. The mountains and waters in the garden imitate Yixing's natural scenery: the mountains resemble Tongguan, the waters resemble West Jiu (a local lake), and the stone bridge west of the pond imitates Shanjuan Cave and Zhanggong Cave—quite ingenious.

projects.name: 太平天国辅王府
projects.name_en: Mural on the Wall of Prince Fu's Mansion in the Taiping Heavenly Kingdom
projects.level: 第三批江苏省文物保护单位（1982年）
projects.level_en: 3rd Batch Jiangsu Provincial Cultural Heritage Site (1982)
projects.address: 宜城镇和平街通真观巷9号
projects.address_en: No. 9 Tongzhenguan Lane, Heping Street, Yicheng Town
highlights: 这处王府原为史氏私宅太平军进驻宜兴时成为辅王杨辅清府第后又作为忠王李秀成行辕王府原有四进第四进转盘楼1912年失火被烧府中最具特色的是壁画表现了太平天国希望构建的理想社会第一进大门有四扇屏门绘鲤鱼跃龙门第二进大厅绘山亭花木等八幅壁画第三进东西墙绘四季山水和官农劳作等四幅壁画
projects.content_zh: 这处王府原为史氏私宅，太平军进驻宜兴时成为辅王杨辅清府第，后又作为忠王李秀成行辕。王府原有四进，第四进转盘楼1912年失火被烧。府中最具特色的是壁画，表现了太平天国希望构建的理想社会：第一进大门有四扇屏门，绘鲤鱼跃龙门；第二进大厅绘山亭花木等八幅壁画；第三进东西墙绘四季山水和官农劳作等四幅壁画。
projects.content_en: This prince's mansion was originally the private residence of the Shi family; when the Taiping Army occupied Yixing, it became the residence of Prince Fu Yang Fuqing, and later served as the field headquarters of Prince Zhong Li Xiucheng. The mansion originally had four rows; the fourth row, the revolving tower, burned down in a fire in 1912. The most distinctive feature of the mansion is its murals, expressing the ideal society that the Taiping Heavenly Kingdom hoped to build: the first row's main gate has four screen doors painted with carp leaping over the dragon gate; the second row's main hall is painted with eight murals including mountain pavilions, flowers and trees; the third row's east and west walls are painted with four murals including four-season landscapes and official-farmer labor.

regions.overview: 远古时期常州已有人类活动，在溧阳发现了旧石器时代的中华曙猿化石，金坛有新石器时代的三星村遗址等。常州保存着中国现存最古老的地面城池遗址，即距今2500多年前的淹城遗址，为中国城市史添写了精彩而独特的一笔；在今常州与无锡交界处，还有吴王阖闾修筑的阖闾城。常州最早见诸史册的名称是延陵，公元前574年季札封在此地，后世称其为延陵季子。《左传》有"季札观乐"的故事，他在鲁国欣赏周乐，对风、雅、颂一一作出精辟的分析和点评。季札重信义，他出访列国途经徐国时，徐君爱慕他的佩剑，但不好意思开口，季札心知其意，因还要访问列国，不便相赠。待他归途再经徐国时，徐君已死，季札慨然解下佩剑悬在徐君墓旁树上，"季子挂剑"的故事传为千古美谈。司马迁《史记》称誉季札是"慕义无穷，见微而知清浊"的仁者，"闳览博物"的君子。今常州市中心大道称延陵路，人民公园有季子亭。秦置延陵县，汉称毗陵，西晋太康二年（281年）设毗陵郡，永兴元年（305年）为避司马毗讳，改称晋陵。隋开皇九年（589年）在常熟县置州，得名常州，后来常熟割给苏州，州治移至晋陵，随着京杭大运河的开通，常州进入迅速发展时期。唐天宝年间，常州已被称作"江左大郡"，"兵食之所资，财富之所出，公家之所给，岁以万计"（梁肃《独孤公行状》）。在唐末的战乱中钱镠创建吴越国，使江南获得安定；南宋人口和财富的南迁，使常州成为重要的粮食产地，时有"苏常熟，天下足"的民谚。唐宋之际是常州地位发生大转折的时期，如清人靳辅所称："江南之苏、松、常、镇，浙江之杭、嘉、湖等府，在汉唐以前不过一泽国尔，自钱镠窃据，南宋偏安，民聚而地辟，遂为财富之薮。"此后常州与苏州、杭州、湖州等并称，成为国家财政的支柱，如康熙朝江南巡抚慕天颜所奏："江南财赋甲天下，苏、松、常、镇课额尤冠于江南。"与财富积累相伴随的是人文的昌盛，尤以明清两代最著：常州学派、常州词派、常州画派……竞相涌现，唐顺之、洪亮吉、恽南田……名家辈出，在建筑上则体现为大批宅第和园林的建造。唐顺之家族有唐氏八宅、陈渡草堂、半园，吴亮、吴玄兄弟有青山庄、白鹤园、嘉树园、止园、五亩园和罗浮园等，杨廷鉴有东皋园，李长祥有桃园……造园名家周秉忠、周廷策父子、计成、戈裕良都活跃在这一带，陆燕喆《张陶庵传》评价康熙朝御用造园师张然称："所假有延陵之石，有高阳之石，有安定之石……"首先提到的就是张然在常州的作品。明清时期的常州俨然是一座"百园之城"。但现代常州园林并不知名，这与这座城市的遭遇有关。早在南宋末年元兵南侵，常州人便奋起抵御，元《大德毗陵志》称他们为"不达时宜者，不能望风迎降，所以衣冠文物，扫荡无余"，如今常州几乎没有元代之前的建筑遗存。经过明清两代的休养生息，到晚清太平军与清军又在常州发生激烈的巷战，巨宅名园焚烧殆尽。常州人留下的是不屈的气节，实物保存反倒很少。尽管如此，今天仍能看到北宋的经幢，苏轼的砚池，前后北岸、青果巷的民居，近园、未园和约园等精巧的园林，让游人凭借这些劫后的遗存，联想常州曾有的辉煌。常州于2015年6月被国务院公布为国家历史文化名城，今辖天宁区、钟楼区、戚墅堰区、新北区（市政府驻地）和武进区5个区，代管溧阳市、金坛市2个县级市，有国家级文物保护单位10处，省级文物保护单位45处，本书介绍国保建筑4处，省保建筑11处，其他建筑4处。
regions.overview_en: In ancient times, Changzhou already had human activities; fossils of Sinopithecus (Chinese Dawn Ape) from the Paleolithic Age were discovered in Liyang, and the Sanxingcun Site from the Neolithic Age exists in Jintan etc. Changzhou preserves China's oldest existing above-ground city site—the Yancheng (Sunken City) Site from over 2500 years ago, adding a brilliant and unique chapter to Chinese urban history; at the junction of today's Changzhou and Wuxi, there is also the Helü City built by King Helü of Wu. The earliest name of Changzhou in historical records is Yanling; in 574 BC, Jizha was enfeoffed here, and later generations called him Yanling Jizi. The "Zuo Zhuan" has the story of "Jizha Observing Music," in which he appreciated Zhou music in the State of Lu and made incisive analyses and comments on the Feng, Ya, and Song one by one. Jizha valued faith and righteousness; when he passed through the State of Xu on a diplomatic mission, the Lord of Xu admired his sword but was too embarrassed to ask; Jizha understood his intention but, because he still had to visit other states, could not give it away. When he returned through Xu, the Lord of Xu had already died, so Jizha generously unfastened his sword and hung it on a tree beside the Lord of Xu's tomb—the story of "Jizi Hanging the Sword" became an eternal tale of beauty. Sima Qian's "Records of the Grand Historian" praised Jizha as a benevolent man who "pursued righteousness endlessly, seeing the subtle and knowing the clear and turbid," and a gentleman of "broad vision and extensive knowledge." Today the central avenue of Changzhou is called Yanling Road, and People's Park has the Jizi Pavilion. The Qin established Yanling County, the Han called it Piling; in the 2nd year of Taikang of the Western Jin (281), Piling Commandery was established; in the 1st year of Yongxing (305), to avoid the name taboo of Sima Pi, it was renamed Jinling. In the 9th year of Kaihuang of the Sui (589), a prefecture was established in Changshu County, giving the name Changzhou; later Changshu was ceded to Suzhou, and the prefecture seat moved to Jinling. With the opening of the Beijing-Hangzhou Grand Canal, Changzhou entered a period of rapid development. During the Tianbao reign of the Tang, Changzhou was already called a "great commandery east of the Yangtze," where "military provisions are sourced, wealth produced, and public supplies given, counted in tens of thousands annually" (Liang Su, "Account of the Deeds of Dugu Gong"). During the late-Tang wars, Qian Liu founded the Wuyue Kingdom, bringing stability to Jiangnan; the southward migration of population and wealth in the Southern Song made Changzhou an important grain-producing area, with the folk saying "When Su and Chang are ripe, the world is full." The Tang-Song transition was a period of major转折 in Changzhou's status, as Qing person Jin Fu stated: "The Su, Song, Chang, Zhen of Jiangnan, and the Hang, Jia, Hu etc. of Zhejiang, before the Han and Tang were merely marshlands; since Qian Liu's separatist rule and the Southern Song's partial security, people gathered and land was opened, becoming a gathering place of wealth." Thereafter Changzhou ranked alongside Suzhou, Hangzhou, and Huzhou etc., becoming a pillar of national finance, as Mu Tianyan, Governor of Jiangnan during the Kangxi reign, memorialized: "Jiangnan's taxes and finances lead the world, and the tax quotas of Su, Song, Chang, Zhen especially lead Jiangnan." Accompanying the accumulation of wealth was the flourishing of culture and humanities, most notably in the Ming and Qing dynasties: the Changzhou School of Classical Learning, Changzhou School of Ci Poetry, Changzhou School of Painting... emerged in competition; Tang Shunzhi, Hong Liangji, Yun Nantian... famous masters appeared in abundance, reflected architecturally in the construction of large numbers of residences and gardens. Tang Shunzhi's family had the Tang Family Eight Residences, Chen Du Thatched Hall, and Banyuan; Wu Liang and Wu Xuan brothers had Qingshan Manor, Baihe Garden, Jiashu Garden, Zhiyuan, Wumu Garden, and Luofu Garden etc.; Yang Tingjian had Donggao Garden; Li Changxiang had Taoyuan... garden masters Zhou Bingzhong, Zhou Tingce father and son, Ji Cheng, and Ge Yuliang were all active in this area. Lu Yanzhe's "Biography of Zhang Tao'an" evaluated Zhang Ran, the imperial garden master of the Kangxi reign: "What he borrowed included stones from Yanling, stones from Gaoyang, stones from Anding..." The first mentioned was Zhang Ran's works in Changzhou. During the Ming and Qing, Changzhou was truly a "city of a hundred gardens." But modern Changzhou gardens are not well-known, related to this city's experiences. As early as the late Southern Song, when Yuan troops invaded south, Changzhou people rose up to resist; the Yuan "Dade Piling Gazetteer" called them "people who did not understand the times, unable to surrender at the sight of the wind, so their robes, hats, cultural relics were swept away without remainder," and today Changzhou has almost no architectural remains before the Yuan Dynasty. After recuperation during the Ming and Qing, in the late Qing the Taiping Army and Qing Army again fought fierce street battles in Changzhou, burning great mansions and famous gardens to ashes. What Changzhou people left behind was unyielding integrity, while physical preservation was comparatively rare. Nevertheless, today one can still see Northern Song dharani pillars, Su Shi's inkstone pool, the residences of Qianhou Beian and Qingguo Lane, and exquisite gardens such as Jinyuan, Weiyuan, and Yueyuan, allowing visitors to rely on these post-catastrophe remains to imagine Changzhou's former glory. Changzhou was announced by the State Council as a National Historical and Cultural City in June 2015; today it administers 5 districts: Tianning, Zhonglou, Qishuyan, Xinbei (municipal government seat), and Wujin, and代管 2 county-level cities: Liyang and Jintan; it has 10 national-level cultural heritage protection units and 45 provincial-level cultural heritage protection units; this book introduces 4 national-protected buildings, 11 provincial-protected buildings, and 4 other buildings.
