highlights: 淹城是中国目前保存最完整的春秋时期城市遗址有学者认为是春秋中期吴国的都城也有学者认为是淹国移民南迁时的都城淹城由三重城垣和城壕组成当地民谣形象地称作里罗城外罗城中间方形紫罗城最内部是方形的子城俗称紫罗城或王城城周约500米外绕子城河向外是方形的内城又称内罗城或中城城周1500米外绕内城河最外面是椭圆形的外城东西长850米南北宽750米总面积约65公顷外绕外城河三道城垣都用土堆成存高3-10米底部宽30米左右三条护城河均深4-10米宽30-50米展示了中国先民筑城的形制和技艺淹城出土了中国最古老最巨大的独木舟推测是当时进出淹城的交通工具今收藏在南京博物院三道城墙像三条逶迤盘踞的长龙外面环绕着三条清波荡漾的河流掩映在茂林修竹间漫步其中仿佛回到了两千多年前予人一种深沉浑厚的沧桑感2010年在淹城北侧建成以先秦诸子为主题的淹城春秋乐园让游人在娱乐中品味传统文化
projects.content_zh: 淹城是中国目前保存最完整的春秋时期城市遗址。有学者认为是春秋中期吴国的都城，也有学者认为是淹国移民南迁时的都城。淹城由三重城垣和城壕组成，当地民谣形象地称作："里罗城，外罗城，中间方形紫罗城。"最内部是方形的子城，俗称紫罗城或王城，城周约500米，外绕子城河。向外是方形的内城，又称内罗城或中城，城周1500米，外绕内城河。最外面是椭圆形的外城，东西长850米，南北宽750米，总面积约65公顷，外绕外城河。三道城垣都用土堆成，存高3—10米，底部宽30米左右；三条护城河均深4—10米，宽30—50米，展示了中国先民筑城的形制和技艺。淹城出土了中国最古老、最巨大的独木舟，推测是当时进出淹城的交通工具，今收藏在南京博物院。三道城墙像三条逶迤盘踞的长龙，外面环绕着三条清波荡漾的河流，掩映在茂林修竹间，漫步其中，仿佛回到了两千多年前，予人一种深沉浑厚的沧桑感。2010年在淹城北侧建成以先秦诸子为主题的淹城春秋乐园，让游人在娱乐中品味传统文化。
projects.content_en: Yancheng (Sunken City) Site is China's best-preserved city site from the Spring and Autumn Period. Some scholars believe it was the capital of the State of Wu in the mid-Spring and Autumn Period, while others believe it was the capital of migrants from the State of Yan who moved south. Yancheng consists of three layers of city walls and moats, vividly described in a local folk song: "Inner Luo City, outer Luo City, with a square purple Luo City in the middle." The innermost part is the square Zicheng (Child City), commonly called the Purple Luo City or King's City, with a circumference of about 500 meters, surrounded by the Zicheng River. Outward is the square inner city, also called the Inner Luo City or Middle City, with a circumference of 1500 meters, surrounded by the Inner City River. The outermost is the oval outer city, 850 meters east-west and 750 meters north-south, with a total area of about 65 hectares, surrounded by the Outer City River. All three city walls are piled with earth, surviving at a height of 3-10 meters, with a base width of about 30 meters; all three moats are 4-10 meters deep and 30-50 meters wide, demonstrating the form and technique of ancient Chinese city building. Yancheng yielded China's oldest and largest dugout canoe, presumed to be the transportation vehicle for entering and leaving Yancheng at that time, now collected in the Nanjing Museum. The three city walls resemble three winding and coiling long dragons, surrounded by three clear-wave rivers, shaded by dense forests and bamboo groves; strolling among them, one feels as if returned to over two thousand years ago, giving a deep and profound sense of vicissitudes. In 2010, the Yancheng Spring and Autumn Paradise, themed on pre-Qin philosophers, was built north of Yancheng, allowing visitors to savor traditional culture through entertainment.

projects.name: 近园
projects.level: 第七批全国重点文物保护单位（2013年）
projects.level_en: 7th Batch National Key Cultural Heritage Site (2013)
projects.address: 天宁区晋陵中路418号，常州宾馆内
projects.address_en: Inside Changzhou Hotel, No. 418 Middle Jinling Road, Tianning District
highlights: 近园原为明万历年间陕西布政使恽厥初1572-1652的别业清康熙六年1667年杨青岩字兆鲁购得改筑康熙十一年1672年完工取近乎成园之意命名为近园杨兆鲁作近园记邀请书画名家恽南田书石王翚绘近园图笪重光题跋文士方邵村龚百药董文骥等常到园中做客堪称一时之盛清同治初年归福建按察使刘翊宸光绪十一年1885年又归恽彦琦因重回恽氏手中更名复园后又称静园民间则呼为恽家花园园林中部为水池周遭紧贴园墙布置建筑和游廊池中小岛面积较大将园林分隔为南北两区各成一体小岛东西两侧皆有石桥与岸相连岛上堆叠假山树木葱郁今入口在容膝居北侧游廊下原入口在园西靠近住宅入门站在廊内可望见岛上假山沿游廊向北可入秋水亭小坐此亭位置较高为隔池赏山佳处出亭沿游廊北行东折池北为主厅西野草堂堂前平台开阔适宜宴饮聚会其东南角有数级石阶通向水面可在此登舟游泛堂东有游廊通向容膝居廊壁嵌名家书画碑刻其西竹木掩映别成幽境适合闲步读碑容膝居东侧出临池敞廊题名虚舟可倚在美人靠上欣赏假山至此游客已在入口游廊高亭草堂和敞廊等多处或远或近地欣赏过假山穿过虚舟南侧的小桥则可登岛入山近距离地游览岛上假山用黄石叠成分为南北两组北山高耸可沿蹬道登顶临眺山下叠筑垂纶洞又可在洞内静坐窥望洞外风景南山相对平缓上立见一亭典雅精致可在亭内周览园景水池南岸有天香阁和得月轩两座建筑向北与掩映在竹林间的见一亭相对南部的池面以清幽取胜与北部池面的开阔形成对比近园造园手法洗练园景丰富为现存江南园林中的佳作
projects.content_zh: 近园原为明万历年间陕西布政使恽厥初（1572—1652）的别业，清康熙六年（1667年）杨青岩（字兆鲁）购得改筑，康熙十一年（1672年）完工，取"近乎成园"之意命名为近园。杨兆鲁作《近园记》，邀请书画名家恽南田书石，王翚绘《近园图》，笪重光题跋，文士方邵村、龚百药、董文骥等常到园中做客，堪称一时之盛。清同治初年归福建按察使刘翊宸，光绪十一年（1885年）又归恽彦琦，因重回恽氏手中，更名复园，后又称静园，民间则呼为"恽家花园"。园林中部为水池，周遭紧贴园墙布置建筑和游廊。池中小岛面积较大，将园林分隔为南北两区，各成一体。小岛东西两侧皆有石桥与岸相连，岛上堆叠假山，树木葱郁。今入口在容膝居北侧游廊下，原入口在园西，靠近住宅，入门站在廊内可望见岛上假山。沿游廊向北，可入秋水亭小坐，此亭位置较高，为隔池赏山佳处。出亭沿游廊北行东折，池北为主厅西野草堂，堂前平台开阔，适宜宴饮聚会。其东南角有数级石阶通向水面，可在此登舟游泛。堂东有游廊通向容膝居，廊壁嵌名家书画碑刻，其西竹木掩映，别成幽境，适合闲步读碑。容膝居东侧出临池敞廊，题名虚舟，可倚在美人靠上欣赏假山。至此，游客已在入口、游廊、高亭、草堂和敞廊等多处或远或近地欣赏过假山，穿过虚舟南侧的小桥则可登岛入山，近距离地游览。岛上假山用黄石叠成，分为南北两组。北山高耸，可沿蹬道登顶临眺；山下叠筑垂纶洞，又可在洞内静坐，窥望洞外风景。南山相对平缓，上立见一亭，典雅精致，可在亭内周览园景。水池南岸有天香阁和得月轩两座建筑，向北与掩映在竹林间的见一亭相对。南部的池面以清幽取胜，与北部池面的开阔形成对比。近园造园手法洗练，园景丰富，为现存江南园林中的佳作。
projects.content_en: Jinyuan (Near-Completion Garden) was originally the villa of Yun Juechu (1572-1652), Governor of Shaanxi during the Wanli reign of the Ming; in the 6th year of Kangxi of the Qing (1667), Yang Qingyan (style name Zhaolu) purchased and rebuilt it, completed in the 11th year of Kangxi (1672), taking the meaning of "nearly becoming a garden" to name it Jinyuan. Yang Zhaolu wrote the "Record of Jinyuan," inviting the famous calligrapher-painter Yun Nantian to inscribe on stone, Wang Hui to paint the "Painting of Jinyuan," and Da Chongguang to write the colophon; literati Fang Shaocun, Gong Baiyao, Dong Wenji etc. often visited the garden as guests, arguably a grand gathering of the time. In the early Tongzhi reign of the Qing, it passed to Liu Yichen, Surveillance Commissioner of Fujian; in the 11th year of Guangxu (1885), it again passed to Yun Yanqi; because it returned to the Yun family, it was renamed Fuyuan (Restored Garden), later also called Jingyuan (Quiet Garden), while folk called it the "Yun Family Garden." The center of the garden is a pond, with buildings and corridors arranged around it紧贴 the garden wall. The small island in the pond is relatively large, dividing the garden into north and south zones, each forming an integrated whole. Both east and west sides of the island have stone bridges connecting to the banks; rockeries are piled on the island, with lush trees. Today's entrance is under the corridor north of Rongxiju (Knees-Fit Residence); the original entrance was west of the garden, near the residence, and entering and standing in the corridor one can see the rockery on the island. Following the corridor northward, one can sit for a while in the Qiushui (Autumn Water) Pavilion; this pavilion is relatively high, an excellent place to admire the mountain across the pond. Exiting the pavilion and following the corridor northward then turning east, north of the pond is the main hall Xiye (West Wild Grass) Hall, with an open platform in front suitable for banquets and gatherings. At its southeast corner are several stone steps leading to the water, where one can board a boat for a tour. East of the hall is a corridor leading to Rongxiju, with the corridor walls embedded with famous calligraphy and painting stele carvings; west of it, shaded by bamboo and trees, forms a secluded realm suitable for leisurely strolling and reading steles. East of Rongxiju, an open corridor facing the pond emerges, titled Xuzhou (Empty Boat), where one can lean on the beauty-rest (backrest railing) to admire the rockery. By this point, visitors have already admired the rockery from near and far at multiple places: the entrance, corridor, high pavilion, thatched hall, and open corridor; crossing the small bridge south of Xuzhou, one can climb onto the island and enter the mountain for a close-up tour. The rockery on the island is piled with yellow stone, divided into north and south groups. The north mountain is tall, and one can climb along the stone path to the top for a panoramic view; at the foot of the mountain, the Chuilun (Fishing Line) Cave is built, where one can sit quietly and peek at the scenery outside the cave. The south mountain is relatively gentle, with the Jianyi (Seeing One) Pavilion standing on it, elegant and refined, allowing a panoramic view of the garden from inside the pavilion. On the south bank of the pond are two buildings: the Tianxiang (Heavenly Fragrance) Pavilion and the Deyue (Getting the Moon) Studio, facing north toward the Jianyi Pavilion shaded among bamboo groves. The southern pond surface excels in serenity and seclusion, contrasting with the openness of the northern pond surface. Jinyuan's garden-building techniques are concise and refined, with rich garden scenery, making it a fine example among existing Jiangnan gardens.

projects.level: 第四批江苏省文物保护单位（1995年）

projects.address: 钟楼区天王堂弄少年宫内
projects.address_en: Inside the Children's Palace, Tianwangtang Lane, Zhonglou District
projects.opening_hours: 需从少年宫进入，仅周六、周日对个人开放，其他时间只接待团体
highlights: 未园原为钱祥丰木行主钱遴甫1879-1940的宅基地西侧曾建三座堂屋1920年在门客许秉煜建议下决定造园1923年建成一木为未未园喻指一名木商之园又隐含尚未成园的谦逊园林南北长东西宽入口原在西侧今改为东侧园内有四宜厅滴翠轩乐鱼榭垂虹亭汲玉亭挹爽亭和长春亭各景并点缀奇石假山清池卉木园中太湖石和黄石皆购自苏州耗银20余万两其中的福禄寿三奇石体现了商人的审美喜好整座园林布局精巧幽静雅致虽建于近代却颇得古典园林之精髓
projects.content_zh: 未园原为"钱祥丰"木行主钱遴甫（1879—1940）的宅基地，西侧曾建三座堂屋。1920年在门客许秉煜建议下决定造园，1923年建成。"一木为未"，未园喻指一名木商之园，又隐含"尚未成园"的谦逊。园林南北长、东西宽，入口原在西侧，今改为东侧，园内有四宜厅、滴翠轩、乐鱼榭、垂虹亭、汲玉亭、挹爽亭和长春亭各景，并点缀奇石假山、清池卉木。园中太湖石和黄石皆购自苏州，耗银20余万两。其中的福、禄、寿三奇石体现了商人的审美喜好。整座园林布局精巧、幽静雅致，虽建于近代却颇得古典园林之精髓。
projects.content_en: Weiyuan (Not-Yet Garden) was originally the homestead of Qian Linfu (1879-1940), owner of the Qianxiangfeng Timber Merchant; three main halls were once built on the west side. In 1920, on the suggestion of retainer Xu Bingyu, it was decided to build a garden, completed in 1923. "One wood makes 'wei' (not yet)," so Weiyuan metaphorically means a timber merchant's garden, and also implies the humility of "not yet a completed garden." The garden is long north-south and wide east-west, with the entrance originally on the west side, today changed to the east side; inside the garden are the Siyi (Suitable for All) Hall, Dicui (Dripping Green) Studio, Leyu (Happy Fish) Waterside Pavilion, Chuihong (Hanging Rainbow) Pavilion, Jiyu (Drawing Jade) Pavilion, Yishuang (Embracing Refreshing Coolness) Pavilion, and Changchun (Eternal Spring) Pavilion, with exotic rockeries, clear ponds, and flowers and trees interspersed. The Taihu stones and yellow stones in the garden were all purchased from Suzhou, costing over 200,000 taels of silver. Among them, the three exotic stones of Fortune, Prosperity, and Longevity reflect the aesthetic preferences of merchants. The entire garden has an exquisite layout, serene and elegant, and although built in modern times, it well captures the essence of classical gardens.

projects.name: 瞿秋白故居
projects.level: 第四批全国重点文物保护单位（1996年）
projects.level_en: 4th Batch National Key Cultural Heritage Site (1996)
projects.address_en: No. 188 West Yanling Road, Zhonglou District
highlights: 中国共产党早期领导人瞿秋白1899-1935出生在青果巷82-84号的天香楼原为唐氏八宅之八桂堂后楼清末仅存废基由秋白叔祖瞿赓甫购得1890年至1898年拓建为宅第天香楼原有五进今存四进自南而北依次为大门正厅楠木厅和经楼天香楼瞿秋白便出生在二楼西间今瞿秋白故居原为瞿氏宗祠1898年瞿赓甫入京面圣后回湖北途经常州建造宗祠包括东西两院前后四进正屋在西首内设祖宗牌位瞿秋白一家寓住在东首厢房内瞿赓甫常年在湖北任官辅佐张之洞家眷随其同住秋白幼年祖父早逝家境贫寒全家寄居在叔祖的常州宅第内清光绪二十九年1903年瞿赓甫去世家眷返回常州秋白一家先迁往乌衣浜再迁城西星聚堂颠沛流离直到1912年迁居瞿氏宗祠才稍为安定瞿氏宗祠是秋白在常州的最后居住地他少年时期在常州府中学堂读书同学张太雷任乃讷常来宗祠聚会1915年秋白因贫困辍学次年母亲不堪贫苦煎熬自尽1916年11月秋白离开家乡开始为革命奔波直到1935年6月18日英勇就义今故居东路辟为瞿秋白纪念馆入口瞿秋白雕像后题有他的名句我是江南第一燕为衔春色上云霄贴切地勾勒出瞿秋白的精神和品格
projects.content_zh: 中国共产党早期领导人瞿秋白（1899—1935）出生在青果巷82—84号的天香楼，原为唐氏八宅之八桂堂后楼，清末仅存废基，由秋白叔祖瞿赓甫购得，1890年至1898年拓建为宅第。天香楼原有五进，今存四进，自南而北依次为大门、正厅、楠木厅和经楼天香楼，瞿秋白便出生在二楼西间。今瞿秋白故居原为瞿氏宗祠，1898年瞿赓甫入京面圣后，回湖北途经常州建造宗祠。包括东、西两院，前后四进。正屋在西首，内设祖宗牌位。瞿秋白一家寓住在东首厢房内。瞿赓甫常年在湖北任官，辅佐张之洞，家眷随其同住。秋白幼年祖父早逝，家境贫寒，全家寄居在叔祖的常州宅第内。清光绪二十九年（1903年）瞿赓甫去世，家眷返回常州，秋白一家先迁往乌衣浜，再迁城西星聚堂，颠沛流离，直到1912年迁居瞿氏宗祠才稍为安定。瞿氏宗祠是秋白在常州的最后居住地。他少年时期在常州府中学堂读书，同学张太雷、任乃讷常来宗祠聚会。1915年，秋白因贫困辍学，次年母亲不堪贫苦煎熬自尽。1916年11月，秋白离开家乡开始为革命奔波，直到1935年6月18日英勇就义。今故居东路辟为瞿秋白纪念馆，入口瞿秋白雕像后题有他的名句"我是江南第一燕，为衔春色上云霄"，贴切地勾勒出瞿秋白的精神和品格。
projects.content_en: Qu Qiubai (1899-1935), an early leader of the Communist Party of China, was born in the Tianxiang (Heavenly Fragrance) Building at Nos. 82-84 Qingguo Lane, originally the rear building of the Bagui (Eight Osmanthus) Hall, one of the Tang Family Eight Residences; at the end of the Qing only ruins remained, purchased by Qu Qiubai's great-uncle Qu Gengfu, and expanded into a residence from 1890 to 1898. The Tianxiang Building originally had five rows, today four survive, from south to north successively the gate, main hall, nanmu hall, and scripture tower Tianxiang Building; Qu Qiubai was born in the west room on the second floor. Today's Former Residence of Qu Qiubai was originally the Qu Family Ancestral Shrine; in 1898, after Qu Gengfu went to Beijing to meet the emperor, he built the ancestral shrine in Changzhou on his way back to Hubei. It includes east and west courtyards, with four rows front and back. The main house is at the west end, with ancestral tablets inside. Qu Qiubai's family lived in the east wing rooms. Qu Gengfu served as an official in Hubei all year round, assisting Zhang Zhidong, with his family living with him. Qiubai's grandfather died early in his childhood, and the family was poor, all living in his great-uncle's Changzhou residence. In the 29th year of Guangxu of the Qing (1903), Qu Gengfu died, and the family returned to Changzhou; Qiubai's family first moved to Wuyibang, then to Xingju Hall west of the city, wandering and displaced, until moving to the Qu Family Ancestral Shrine in 1912 when they became somewhat settled. The Qu Family Ancestral Shrine was Qiubai's last residence in Changzhou. During his youth he studied at Changzhou Prefecture Middle School, and classmates Zhang Tailei and Ren Naine often came to the ancestral shrine for gatherings. In 1915, Qiubai dropped out of school due to poverty; the following year his mother, unable to bear the suffering of poverty, took her own life. In November 1916, Qiubai left his hometown to begin struggling for the revolution, until his heroic martyrdom on June 18, 1935. Today the east road of the former residence is opened as the Qu Qiubai Memorial Hall; behind the statue of Qu Qiubai at the entrance is inscribed his famous line "I am the first swallow of Jiangnan, to carry spring colors up to the clouds," aptly outlining Qu Qiubai's spirit and character.

projects.name: 人民公园
projects.level: 含崇法寺大殿、落星亭、浩然亭、意园等市保建筑
projects.level_en: Including municipal protected buildings such as Chongfa Temple Main Hall, Luoxing Pavilion, Haoran Pavilion, and Yiyuan
projects.address: 钟楼区延陵西路与公园路交汇处
projects.address_en: Intersection of West Yanling Road and Park Road, Zhonglou District
highlights: 人民公园前身是武进县商会会馆后花园建于1908年1913年对公众开放是常州首座公园时称公花园今园内有崇法寺大殿季子亭落星亭浩然亭和意园假山等市保建筑崇法寺相传最初为隋司徒陈国仁后圃宋宣和七年1125年赐名崇法禅院太平天国时期寺庙毁于战火光绪年间重建部分殿堂当时法会之盛几与天宁埒新中国成立后建设人民公园时拆除寺庙仅留大殿落星亭建于清宣统二年1910年用4根金山石柱支撑内砌石栏形式别致浩然亭建于明正德十五年1520年纪念宋末抗元死难的将士亭名取文天祥正气歌浩然者乃天地之正气之意此亭原在忠义祠后清乾隆年间移建于今址1984年重建意园位于后北岸4-8号原为康熙朝状元赵熊诏私园后来太平军英王陈玉成在此驻扎建筑毁于战火清光绪十二年1886年史干甫在此构园集蔡襄以意为之四字悬于门额因称意园园由粉墙隔为内外两区墙上开漏窗互通声气园内有花厅四季假山及恽南田曾寓居的瓯香馆画室外园为赵氏方玉堂旧址南北狭长有延桂山房明月廊鱼池亭榭等景北侧庑楼阁为园内最高处今园内假山被迁至人民公园东南角重建
projects.content_zh: 人民公园前身是武进县商会会馆后花园，建于1908年，1913年对公众开放，是常州首座公园，时称公花园。今园内有崇法寺大殿、季子亭、落星亭、浩然亭和意园假山等市保建筑。崇法寺相传最初为隋司徒陈国仁后圃，宋宣和七年（1125年）赐名崇法禅院。太平天国时期寺庙毁于战火，光绪年间重建部分殿堂，当时"法会之盛，几与天宁埒"。新中国成立后建设人民公园时拆除寺庙，仅留大殿。落星亭建于清宣统二年（1910年），用4根金山石柱支撑，内砌石栏，形式别致。浩然亭建于明正德十五年（1520年），纪念宋末抗元死难的将士，亭名取文天祥《正气歌》"浩然者，乃天地之正气"之意。此亭原在忠义祠后，清乾隆年间移建于今址，1984年重建。意园位于后北岸4—8号，原为康熙朝状元赵熊诏私园，后来太平军英王陈玉成在此驻扎，建筑毁于战火。清光绪十二年（1886年）史干甫在此构园，集蔡襄"以意为之"四字悬于门额，因称意园。园由粉墙隔为内外两区，墙上开漏窗互通声气。内园有花厅、四季假山及恽南田曾寓居的瓯香馆画室。外园为赵氏方玉堂旧址，南北狭长，有延桂山房、明月廊、鱼池、亭榭等景，北侧庑楼阁为园内最高处。今园内假山被迁至人民公园东南角重建。
projects.content_en: The predecessor of People's Park was the rear garden of the Wujin County Chamber of Commerce Guild Hall, built in 1908, opened to the public in 1913, Changzhou's first park, then called the Public Garden. Today the park contains municipal protected buildings such as the Chongfa Temple Main Hall, Jizi Pavilion, Luoxing (Falling Star) Pavilion, Haoran (Noble Spirit) Pavilion, and Yiyuan rockery. According to tradition, Chongfa Temple was originally the rear garden of Sui Situ Chen Guoren; in the 7th year of Xuanhe of the Song (1125), it was granted the name Chongfa Chan Courtyard. During the Taiping Rebellion the temple was destroyed by war fires, and part of the halls were rebuilt during the Guangxu reign; at that time "the grandeur of its religious assemblies was almost equal to Tianning Temple." When building People's Park after the founding of New China, the temple was demolished, leaving only the main hall. The Luoxing Pavilion was built in the 2nd year of Xuantong of the Qing (1910), supported by 4 Jinshan stone columns, with stone railings built inside, in a unique form. The Haoran Pavilion was built in the 15th year of Zhengde of the Ming (1520), commemorating the soldiers who died resisting the Yuan at the end of the Song; the pavilion name takes the meaning from Wen Tianxiang's "Song of the Noble Spirit": "The noble spirit is the righteous qi of heaven and earth." This pavilion was originally behind the Zhongyi (Loyalty and Righteousness) Shrine, moved to today's site during the Qianlong reign of the Qing, and rebuilt in 1984. Yiyuan (Intention Garden) is located at Nos. 4-8 Houbei'an, originally the private garden of Zhao Xiongzhao, a zhuangyuan of the Kangxi reign; later the Taiping Army's Prince Ying Chen Yucheng was stationed here, and the buildings were destroyed by war fires. In the 12th year of Guangxu of the Qing (1886), Shi Ganfu built a garden here, collecting Cai Xiang's four characters "acting by intention" to hang on the gate lintel, hence called Yiyuan. The garden is divided into inner and outer zones by a whitewashed wall, with lattice windows opened on the wall for communication. The inner garden has a flower hall, four-season rockery, and the Ouxiangguan painting studio where Yun Nantian once lived. The outer garden is the former site of the Zhao Family Fangyu Hall, long and narrow north-south, with scenes such as the Yangui (Extending Osmanthus) Mountain Room, Mingyue (Bright Moon) Corridor, fish pond, and pavilions and terraces; the wing building and pavilion on the north side are the highest point in the garden. Today the rockery in the garden has been moved to the southeast corner of People's Park and rebuilt.

projects.name: 前后北岸街区
projects.level: 历史文化街区，含藤花旧馆、吕宫府、管干贞故居、赵翼故居、文庙大成殿等省保单位
projects.level_en: Historical and Cultural Block, including provincial protected units such as Tenghua Old Hall, Lü Gong Mansion, Guan Ganzhen Former Residence, Zhao Yi Former Residence, and Confucian Temple Dacheng Hall
projects.address: 钟楼区延陵西路前后北岸
projects.address_en: Qianhou Beian, West Yanling Road, Zhonglou District
highlights: 前后北岸前临顾塘河今填平为延陵西路后依白云溪今填平为迎春步行街曾为一座三面环水东面接陆的半岛在这片三角地块上自宋代以来走出了5名状元霍端友杨廷鉴吕宫赵熊诏庄培因3名榜眼杨述曾庄存与洪亮吉3名探花管绍宁汤大绅赵翼及大量进士文风之盛举世罕见除了风水地利前后北岸的东端靠近文庙很多人曾在此读书求学西端有苏轼寓居过的藤花旧馆文人墨客常因贪慕东坡住顾塘从而使这一带名人故居毗连今自西向东有藤花旧馆汤润之故居东坡书院吕宫宰相府管干贞总督府赵翼探花第挥祖贻道台府洪亮吉故居恽南田瓯香馆赵熊诏故居及读书楼魁星阁等藤花旧馆位于延陵西路前北岸79-81号又名藤花旧馆1982年列为省保单位北宋时为孙氏馆建中靖国元年1101年贬官流放在海南儋州的苏轼遇赦北归路过常州时寓居在孙氏馆并终老于此苏轼一生到过常州11次馆内有苏轼手植紫藤及东坡洗砚池明中期在遗址上重建为藤花旧馆其中的三间楠木厅保存至今清乾隆二十二年1757年乾隆第二次南巡时洗砚池被官员移至万寿行宫今东坡公园吕宫府位于延陵西路前北岸64号2011年列为省保单位吕宫1603-1664原居马山埠清顺治四年1647年考中状元深受皇帝赏识顺治十年1653年12月跃升为弘文院大学士相当于宰相官居一品他曾与大学士陈名夏等联名举荐御史郝浴巡授四川顺治十一年1654年陈名夏倡言留发复衣冠天下即太平被处绞刑吕宫受到株连降二级留用吕宫目睹官场险恶以体病为由多次求退顺治保留了他的大学士头衔以示希望随时起用吕宫回到常州后没有住在祖居而是隐居在前北岸的一处普通民房中闭门不出地方官员和过访友人一概不见以致闲居十年而无人知晓这处故居南北共五进东西两侧都有前后贯通的夹弄两侧风火山墙高低起迭颇具徽派建筑特征管干贞故居位于延陵西路前北岸27-28号1995年列为省保单位管干贞1734-1798先祖管绍宁为晚明探花明代灭亡后因拒绝剃发在狱中自尽管干贞中清乾隆三十一年1766年进士官至漕运总督从一品其花鸟山水得恽南田真髓为常州画派代表画家管氏故居始建于明原有八进后三进毁于民国初年门厅毁于文革今存四进第一进为门屋第二进为三间楠木厅梁柱用料硕大柱下垫阴沉木柱础较为罕见管氏五世同堂乾隆御赐福字金匾故此厅又称锡福堂第三进为五间后厅管绍宁曾在此居住前围以隔墙自成院落第四进为五间楼厅是管干贞读书作画之处称读雪山房文庙大成殿文庙位于延陵西路2号工人文化宫内原为武进阳湖两县学宫始建于宋咸淳元年1265年2011年列为省保单位现存大成殿重建于清同治六年1867年歇山顶宽五间殿前有三间硬山顶享堂堂前有泮池石桥等遗物
projects.content_zh: 前后北岸前临顾塘河（今填平为延陵西路），后依白云溪（今填平为迎春步行街），曾为一座三面环水，东面接陆的半岛。在这片三角地块上，自宋代以来走出了5名状元（霍端友、杨廷鉴、吕宫、赵熊诏、庄培因）、3名榜眼（杨述曾、庄存与、洪亮吉）、3名探花（管绍宁、汤大绅、赵翼）及大量进士，文风之盛，举世罕见。除了风水地利，前后北岸的东端靠近文庙，很多人曾在此读书求学；西端有苏轼寓居过的藤花旧馆，文人墨客常因"贪慕东坡住顾塘"，从而使这一带名人故居毗连。今自西向东有藤花旧馆、汤润之故居、东坡书院、吕宫宰相府、管干贞总督府、赵翼探花第、挥祖贻道台府、洪亮吉故居、恽南田瓯香馆、赵熊诏故居及读书楼"魁星阁"等。1. 藤花旧馆：位于延陵西路前北岸79—81号，又名藤花旧馆，1982年列为省保单位。北宋时为孙氏馆，建中靖国元年（1101年）贬官流放在海南儋州的苏轼遇赦北归，路过常州时寓居在孙氏馆，并终老于此。苏轼一生到过常州11次，馆内有苏轼手植紫藤及东坡洗砚池，明中期在遗址上重建为藤花旧馆，其中的三间楠木厅保存至今。清乾隆二十二年（1757年）乾隆第二次南巡时，洗砚池被官员移至万寿行宫（今东坡公园）。2. 吕宫府：位于延陵西路前北岸64号，2011年列为省保单位。吕宫（1603—1664）原居马山埠，清顺治四年（1647年）考中状元，深受皇帝赏识，顺治十年（1653年）12月跃升为弘文院大学士（相当于宰相），官居一品。他曾与大学士陈名夏等联名举荐御史郝浴巡授四川，顺治十一年（1654年）陈名夏倡言"留发复衣冠，天下即太平"被处绞刑，吕宫受到株连，降二级留用。吕宫目睹官场险恶，以体病为由多次求退，顺治保留了他的大学士头衔，以示希望随时起用。吕宫回到常州后没有住在祖居，而是隐居在前北岸的一处普通民房中，闭门不出，地方官员和过访友人一概不见，以致闲居十年而无人知晓。这处故居南北共五进，东西两侧都有前后贯通的夹弄，两侧风火山墙高低起迭，颇具徽派建筑特征。3. 管干贞故居：位于延陵西路前北岸27—28号，1995年列为省保单位。管干贞（1734—1798）先祖管绍宁为晚明探花，明代灭亡后因拒绝剃发在狱中自尽。管干贞中清乾隆三十一年（1766年）进士，官至漕运总督（从一品），其花鸟山水得恽南田真髓，为"常州画派"代表画家。管氏故居始建于明，原有八进，后三进毁于民国初年，门厅毁于"文革"，今存四进。第一进为门屋，第二进为三间楠木厅，梁柱用料硕大，柱下垫阴沉木柱础，较为罕见。管氏五世同堂，乾隆御赐"福"字金匾，故此厅又称"锡福堂"。第三进为五间后厅，管绍宁曾在此居住；前围以隔墙，自成院落。第四进为五间楼厅，是管干贞读书作画之处，称"读雪山房"。4. 文庙大成殿：文庙位于延陵西路2号工人文化宫内，原为武进、阳湖两县学宫，始建于宋咸淳元年（1265年），2011年列为省保单位。现存大成殿重建于清同治六年（1867年），歇山顶，宽五间。殿前有三间硬山顶享堂，堂前有泮池、石桥等遗物。
projects.content_en: Qianhou Beian (Front and Rear North Bank) Block faces the Gutang River (today filled in as West Yanling Road) to the front and backs onto Baiyun Stream (today filled in as Yingchun Pedestrian Street), once a peninsula surrounded by water on three sides and connected to land on the east. On this triangular plot, since the Song Dynasty, 5 zhuangyuan (top scholars: Huo Duanyou, Yang Tingjian, Lü Gong, Zhao Xiongzhao, Zhuang Peiyin), 3 bangyan (second-place scholars: Yang Shuzeng, Zhuang Cunyu, Hong Liangji), 3 tanhua (third-place scholars: Guan Shaoning, Tang Dashen, Zhao Yi), and numerous jinshi have emerged—the flourishing of literary culture is rare in the world. Besides fengshui and geographical advantages, the east end of Qianhou Beian is near the Confucian Temple, where many people once studied; the west end has the Tenghua (Wisteria Flower) Old Hall where Su Shi once lived, and literati often "coveted Dongpo's residence at Gutang," making famous-person former residences adjacent in this area. Today from west to east are the Tenghua Old Hall, Tang Runzhi Former Residence, Dongpo Academy, Lü Gong Prime Minister's Mansion, Guan Ganzhen Governor's Mansion, Zhao Yi Tanhua Mansion, Hui Zuyi Circuit Intendant's Mansion, Hong Liangji Former Residence, Yun Nantian's Ouxiangguan, Zhao Xiongzhao Former Residence, and the reading tower "Kuixing Pavilion" etc. 1. Tenghua Old Hall: Located at Nos. 79-81 Qianbei'an, West Yanling Road, also called Tenghua Old Hall, designated a provincial protected unit in 1982. In the Northern Song it was the Sun Family Hall; in the 1st year of Jianzhong Jingguo (1101), Su Shi, who had been demoted and exiled in Danzhou, Hainan, was pardoned and returned north, staying at the Sun Family Hall when passing through Changzhou, and ended his days here. Su Shi visited Changzhou 11 times in his life; inside the hall are a wisteria planted by Su Shi himself and Dongpo's inkstone-washing pool; in the mid-Ming it was rebuilt on the site as the Tenghua Old Hall, of which three nanmu halls survive to this day. In the 22nd year of Qianlong of the Qing (1757), during Qianlong's second southern tour, the inkstone-washing pool was moved by officials to the Wanshou Travel Palace (today's Dongpo Park). 2. Lü Gong Mansion: Located at No. 64 Qianbei'an, West Yanling Road, designated a provincial protected unit in 2011. Lü Gong (1603-1664) originally lived at Mashanbu; in the 4th year of Shunzhi of the Qing (1647) he passed the zhuangyuan examination, deeply appreciated by the emperor; in December of the 10th year of Shunzhi (1653) he was promoted to Grand Secretary of the Hongwen Academy (equivalent to prime minister), holding the highest official rank. He once jointly recommended Censor Hao Yu to tour and administer Sichuan with Grand Secretary Chen Mingxia etc.; in the 11th year of Shunzhi (1654), Chen Mingxia advocated "keeping hair and restoring robes and hats, then the world will be at peace" and was sentenced to death by hanging; Lü Gong was implicated and demoted two ranks but retained in office. Witnessing the dangers of officialdom, Lü Gong repeatedly requested retirement on grounds of illness; Shunzhi retained his Grand Secretary title to indicate hope of employing him at any time. After returning to Changzhou, Lü Gong did not live in his ancestral home but secluded himself in an ordinary folk house at Qianbei'an, closing his door and not going out, seeing neither local officials nor visiting friends, so that he lived in retirement for ten years without anyone knowing. This former residence has five rows north-south, with through alleys front and back on both east and west sides, and the fire-break gable walls on both sides rise and fall in height, quite characteristic of Huizhou-style architecture. 3. Guan Ganzhen Former Residence: Located at Nos. 27-28 Qianbei'an, West Yanling Road, designated a provincial protected unit in 1995. Guan Ganzhen's (1734-1798) ancestor Guan Shaoning was a late-Ming tanhua; after the Ming fell, he committed suicide in prison for refusing to shave his hair. Guan Ganzhen passed the jinshi examination in the 31st year of Qianlong of the Qing (1766), rising to Governor of Grain Transport (second rank, first class); his flower-and-bird and landscape paintings obtained the true essence of Yun Nantian, making him a representative painter of the "Changzhou School of Painting." The Guan family residence was first built in the Ming, originally with eight rows; the last three rows were destroyed in the early Republic, and the gate hall was destroyed during the Cultural Revolution; today four rows survive. The first row is the gate house; the second row is a three-bay nanmu hall, with large beams and columns, and the columns rest on sunken-wood column bases, relatively rare. The Guan family had five generations living together, and Qianlong bestowed a gold plaque with the character "Fu" (Fortune), hence this hall is also called "Xifu (Bestowing Fortune) Hall." The third row is a five-bay rear hall, where Guan Shaoning once lived; enclosed by a partition wall in front, forming its own courtyard. The fourth row is a five-bay tower hall, where Guan Ganzhen read and painted, called "Duxue (Reading Snow) Mountain Room." 4. Confucian Temple Dacheng Hall: The Confucian Temple is located inside the Workers' Cultural Palace at No. 2 West Yanling Road, originally the school palace of Wujin and Yanghu counties, first built in the 1st year of Xianchun of the Song (1265), designated a provincial protected unit in 2011. The existing Dacheng (Great Achievement) Hall was rebuilt in the 6th year of Tongzhi of the Qing (1867), with a hip-and-gable roof and five bays wide. In front of the hall is a three-bay offering hall with a gable roof, and in front of the hall are relics such as the Pan Pond and stone bridge.

projects.name: 约园
projects.level: 第二批常州市文物保护单位（1987年）
projects.level_en: 2nd Batch Changzhou Municipal Cultural Heritage Site (1987)
projects.address: 兴隆巷第二人民医院内
projects.address_en: Inside the Second People's Hospital, Xinglong Lane
highlights: 约园原为明代官府养鹿之地清乾隆初年成为谢旻的别业后归赵翼之孙赵起1794-1860建造约园赵起工诗文善书画造园构景颇得诗情画意他将园林分为三区东池春华水面开阔置有大量湖石西园秋实是一座四周环水的小岛在东池和西园之间堆叠黄石假山题为南山涌翠园中罗置了大量奇石赵起一一题名有灵岩绉碧独秀玉屏朵云舞袖等共成约园十二峰此外还有梅坞风情海棠春榭小亭玩月城角风帆等24景太平军攻破常州时赵起一家39口投入约园池内自尽园林也被付之一炬清末由赵翼玄孙媳徐小娴主持修复并请人绘制了一幅约园图是古代女性参与园林建设的重要实例1953年约园划归第二人民医院大部分得以保存
projects.content_zh: 约园原为明代官府养鹿之地，清乾隆初年成为谢旻的别业，后归赵翼之孙赵起（1794—1860），建造约园。赵起工诗文、善书画，造园构景颇得诗情画意。他将园林分为三区："东池春华"水面开阔，置有大量湖石；"西园秋实"是一座四周环水的小岛；在东池和西园之间堆叠黄石假山，题为"南山涌翠"。园中罗置了大量奇石，赵起一一题名，有灵岩、绉碧、独秀、玉屏、朵云、舞袖等……共成"约园十二峰"；此外还有梅坞风情、海棠春榭、小亭玩月、城角风帆等24景。太平军攻破常州时，赵起一家39口投入约园池内自尽，园林也被付之一炬。清末由赵翼玄孙媳徐小娴主持修复，并请人绘制了一幅《约园图》，是古代女性参与园林建设的重要实例。1953年约园划归第二人民医院，大部分得以保存。
projects.content_en: Yueyuan (Approximate Garden) was originally a deer-raising place for the Ming government; in the early Qianlong reign of the Qing it became the villa of Xie Min, later passed to Zhao Qi (1794-1860), grandson of Zhao Yi, who built Yueyuan. Zhao Qi was skilled in poetry and prose and good at calligraphy and painting, and his garden construction and scene arrangement gained much poetic and pictorial charm. He divided the garden into three zones: "East Pond Spring Splendor" with open water and numerous Taihu stones; "West Garden Autumn Fruits" is a small island surrounded by water on all sides; between the east pond and west garden, a yellow stone rockery is piled, titled "South Mountain Surging Green." The garden is furnished with numerous exotic stones, which Zhao Qi named one by one, including Lingyan, Zhoubi, Duxiu, Yuping, Duoyun, Wuxiu etc.—altogether forming the "Twelve Peaks of Yueyuan"; in addition there are 24 scenes such as Plum坞 Style, Begonia Spring Pavilion, Small Pavilion Admiring the Moon, and City Corner Sailing Wind etc. When the Taiping Army captured Changzhou, Zhao Qi's family of 39 threw themselves into the pond in Yueyuan and committed suicide, and the garden was also burned to ashes. At the end of the Qing, restoration was directed by Xu Xiaoxian, great-granddaughter-in-law of Zhao Yi, who also had someone paint a "Painting of Yueyuan"—an important example of ancient women participating in garden construction. In 1953 Yueyuan was transferred to the Second People's Hospital, with most of it preserved.

projects.type_en: Historical and Cultural Block / Ancient Lane
highlights: 青果巷是常州城内最著名的老街巷始建于16世纪当时靠近运河船舶云集是南北果品的集散地因此称作千果巷后讹为青果巷巷中散布着大量名人故居如瞿秋白诞生地汤贻汾故居赵元任故居恽鸿仪故居等其中规模最大的是唐氏八宅位于青果巷82-96号1982年列为省保单位唐氏为常州明清两代的望族最著名的人物是唐顺之1507-1560唐顺之号荆川是明代文学流派唐宋派的代表人物与王慎中归有光并称嘉靖三大家他还精通军事曾亲率兵船击败崇明岛上的倭寇学者尊称其为荆川先生唐氏八宅建于明弘治至万历年间原有筠星易书贞和八桂四并复始松健礼和八堂今存五堂最具价值的是位于86号的贞和堂原名保合堂1633年唐荆川玄孙唐宇昭1602-1672改名贞和堂堂内大厅仍保持明代面貌是常州现存最大的楠木厅木构部分全用楠木紫檀木精做正间大梁有彩绘堂东廊壁上嵌有4方保合堂记石刻是1617年孙慎行为祝贺唐荆川之子唐鹤征的八十大寿所撰贞和堂后部有座半园清初唐宇昭建他自号半园居士清康熙元年1662年秋曾邀请王石谷恽南田在此雅集作画清乾隆年间园归钱维乔作半园之半记清代毗陵人小传后传钱以振新中国成立后园中太湖石移置人民公园池塘被填为操场1987年拆除明式花厅筠星堂位于92-94号原属唐荆川玄孙明崇祯年间举人唐宇量今存部分明代建筑清代回形转楼花厅及山石池木等八桂堂位于82-84号民国期间售予刘国钧现为刘国钧故居松健堂位于8弄3号和12弄8号原属唐荆川曾祖明书法家唐世英后归浙江兵备道挥祖贻现存房屋四进其中厅屋建于明代余为清代改建礼和堂位于141弄和163号原属唐荆川曾叔祖明画家唐世宁内有砖雕门楼
projects.content_zh: 青果巷是常州城内最著名的老街巷，始建于16世纪，当时靠近运河，船舶云集，是南北果品的集散地，因此称作"千果巷"，后讹为青果巷。巷中散布着大量名人故居，如瞿秋白诞生地、汤贻汾故居、赵元任故居、恽鸿仪故居等，其中规模最大的是唐氏八宅，位于青果巷82—96号，1982年列为省保单位。唐氏为常州明清两代的望族，最著名的人物是唐顺之（1507—1560）。唐顺之号荆川，是明代文学流派"唐宋派"的代表人物，与王慎中、归有光并称"嘉靖三大家"；他还精通军事，曾亲率兵船击败崇明岛上的倭寇，学者尊称其为"荆川先生"。唐氏八宅建于明弘治至万历年间，原有筠星、易书、贞和、八桂、四并、复始、松健、礼和八堂，今存五堂。最具价值的是位于86号的贞和堂，原名保合堂，1633年唐荆川玄孙唐宇昭（1602—1672）改名贞和堂。堂内大厅仍保持明代面貌，是常州现存最大的楠木厅，木构部分全用楠木、紫檀木精做，正间大梁有彩绘。堂东廊壁上嵌有4方《保合堂记》石刻，是1617年孙慎行为祝贺唐荆川之子唐鹤征的八十大寿所撰。贞和堂后部有座半园，清初唐宇昭建，他自号半园居士，清康熙元年（1662年）秋曾邀请王石谷、恽南田在此雅集作画。清乾隆年间园归钱维乔，作《半园之半记》（《清代毗陵人小传》），后传钱以振。新中国成立后园中太湖石移置人民公园，池塘被填为操场，1987年拆除明式花厅。筠星堂位于92—94号，原属唐荆川玄孙、明崇祯年间举人唐宇量，今存部分明代建筑、清代回形转楼、花厅及山石池木等。八桂堂位于82—84号，民国期间售予刘国钧，现为刘国钧故居。松健堂位于8弄3号和12弄8号，原属唐荆川曾祖、明书法家唐世英，后归浙江兵备道挥祖贻。现存房屋四进，其中厅屋建于明代，余为清代改建。礼和堂位于141弄和163号，原属唐荆川曾叔祖，明画家唐世宁，内有砖雕门楼。
projects.content_en: Qingguo Lane is the most famous old street and lane in Changzhou city, first built in the 16th century; at that time it was near the canal, with boats gathering in crowds, serving as a distribution center for north-south fruits, hence called "Qianguo (Thousand Fruits) Lane," later corrupted to Qingguo Lane. Scattered in the lane are numerous former residences of famous people, such as the birthplace of Qu Qiubai, former residence of Tang Yifen, former residence of Zhao Yuanren, former residence of Yun Hongyi etc.; among them the largest in scale is the Tang Family Eight Residences, located at Nos. 82-96 Qingguo Lane, designated a provincial protected unit in 1982. The Tang family was a prominent clan in Changzhou during the Ming and Qing dynasties, and the most famous figure was Tang Shunzhi (1507-1560). Tang Shunzhi, hao Jingchuan, was a representative figure of the "Tang-Song School" literary movement of the Ming, together with Wang Shenzhong and Gui Youguang called the "Three Great Masters of Jiajing"; he was also proficient in military affairs, once personally leading warships to defeat the Japanese pirates on Chongming Island, and scholars respectfully called him "Mr. Jingchuan." The Tang Family Eight Residences were built from the Hongzhi to Wanli reigns of the Ming, originally with eight halls: Yunxing, Yishu, Zhenhe, Bagui, Sibing, Fushi, Songjian, and Lihe; today five halls survive. The most valuable is the Zhenhe Hall at No. 86, originally named Baohe Hall; in 1633 Tang Yuzhao (1602-1672), great-grandson of Tang Jingchuan, renamed it Zhenhe Hall. The main hall inside still maintains its Ming appearance, the largest surviving nanmu hall in Changzhou; the wooden structure is all exquisitely made of nanmu and red sandalwood, with painted decorations on the main beam of the central bay. On the wall of the east corridor of the hall are embedded 4 stone carvings of the "Record of Baohe Hall," written by Sun Shenxing in 1617 to congratulate Tang Hezheng, son of Tang Jingchuan, on his 80th birthday. Behind the Zhenhe Hall is a Banyuan (Half Garden), built by Tang Yuzhao in the early Qing; he called himself the "Half Garden Scholar," and in the autumn of the 1st year of Kangxi of the Qing (1662) once invited Wang Shigu and Yun Nantian to gather and paint here. During the Qianlong reign of the Qing the garden passed to Qian Weiqiao, who wrote the "Record of Half of the Half Garden" ("Biographies of Qing Piling People"), later passed to Qian Yizhen. After the founding of New China, the Taihu stones in the garden were moved to People's Park, the pond was filled in as a playground, and the Ming-style flower hall was demolished in 1987. The Yunxing Hall is located at Nos. 92-94, originally belonging to Tang Yuliang, great-grandson of Tang Jingchuan and a juren of the Chongzhen reign of the Ming; today part of the Ming buildings, Qing zigzag turning tower, flower hall, and rocks, ponds, and trees survive. The Bagui Hall is located at Nos. 82-84, sold to Liu Guojun during the Republic, now the Former Residence of Liu Guojun. The Songjian Hall is located at No. 3, Lane 8 and No. 8, Lane 12, originally belonging to Tang Shiying, great-grandfather of Tang Jingchuan and a Ming calligrapher, later passed to Hui Zuyi, Circuit Intendant of Zhejiang. The existing house has four rows, of which the hall was built in the Ming, and the rest were rebuilt in the Qing. The Lihe Hall is located at Lane 141 and No. 163, originally belonging to Tang Shining, great-granduncle of Tang Jingchuan and a Ming painter, with a brick-carved gate tower inside.

projects.name: 天宁寺
projects.level: 第三批江苏省文物保护单位（1982年）
projects.level_en: 3rd Batch Jiangsu Provincial Cultural Heritage Site (1982)
projects.address_en: No. 636 East Yanling Road, Tianning District
highlights: 唐永徽年间650-655金陵今南京牛头山幽栖寺高僧法融禅师到常州化斋筑室十余楹是为天宁寺的前身唐天复年间901-904维元和尚在此施舍利卜寺址正式建造寺院取名广福寺唐末更名齐云寺尊称维元和尚为齐云长老北宋熙宁三年1070年遵诏改齐云寺为万寿崇宁寺北宋政和元年1111年始称天宁寺此后屡有改动元至元年间1335-1340复称常州天宁寺沿用至明代徐问重修常州天宁寺记称誉其为东南第一丛林中国佛教清代佛教将其与镇江金山寺扬州高旻寺宁波天童寺并列为禅宗四大丛林太平天国时期寺庙毁于战火清同治四年至光绪三十年1865-1904重建2008年建成的13层天宁宝塔是世界最高佛塔1982年天宁寺被列为省保单位1983年成为全国佛教重点寺院现为国家4A级旅游景区寺庙主体建筑位于南北中轴线上自南向北依次为山门天王殿大雄宝殿御书楼三宝殿和天宁宝塔东路有文殊殿罗汉殿和观音殿等西路有普贤殿罗汉殿地藏殿达摩阁学戒堂和放生池等大雄宝殿为寺内主殿采用重檐歇山顶内部八根铁梨木柱直径80多厘米是珍贵木料梁枋等构架雕工精美左右两壁嵌有清代雕刻的518尊罗汉石像造型生动为艺术精品
projects.content_zh: 唐永徽年间（650—655）金陵（今南京）牛头山幽栖寺高僧法融禅师到常州化斋，"筑室十余楹"，是为天宁寺的前身。唐天复年间（901—904）维元和尚在此"施舍利，卜寺址"，正式建造寺院，取名广福寺。唐末更名齐云寺，尊称维元和尚为齐云长老。北宋熙宁三年（1070年）遵诏改齐云寺为"万寿崇宁寺"。北宋政和元年（1111年）始称天宁寺，此后屡有改动，元至元年间（1335—1340）复称"常州天宁寺"，沿用至今。明代徐问《重修常州天宁寺记》称誉其为"东南第一丛林"，《中国佛教·清代佛教》将其与镇江金山寺、扬州高旻寺、宁波天童寺并列为"禅宗四大丛林"。太平天国时期寺庙毁于战火，清同治四年至光绪三十年（1865—1904）重建，2008年建成的13层天宁宝塔，是世界最高佛塔。1982年天宁寺被列为省保单位，1983年成为全国佛教重点寺院，现为国家4A级旅游景区。寺庙主体建筑位于南北中轴线上，自南向北依次为山门、天王殿、大雄宝殿、御书楼、三宝殿和天宁宝塔。东路有文殊殿、罗汉殿和观音殿等，西路有普贤殿、罗汉殿、地藏殿、达摩阁、学戒堂和放生池等。大雄宝殿为寺内主殿，采用重檐歇山顶，内部八根铁梨木柱直径80多厘米，是珍贵木料，梁、枋等构架雕工精美，左右两壁嵌有清代雕刻的518尊罗汉石像，造型生动，为艺术精品。
projects.content_en: During the Yonghui reign of the Tang (650-655), the eminent monk Chan Master Farong from Youqi Temple on Niutou Mountain in Jinling (today's Nanjing) came to Changzhou to collect alms, "building over ten rooms," which was the predecessor of Tianning Temple. During the Tianfu reign of the Tang (901-904), Monk Weiyuan "donated profits and divined a temple site" here, formally building a temple, named Guangfu Temple. At the end of the Tang it was renamed Qiyun Temple, and Monk Weiyuan was respectfully called Elder Qiyun. In the 3rd year of Xining of the Northern Song (1070), by imperial edict Qiyun Temple was changed to "Wanshou Chongning Temple." In the 1st year of Zhenghe of the Northern Song (1111) it began to be called Tianning Temple; thereafter it changed several times, and during the Zhiyuan reign of the Yuan (1335-1340) it was again called "Changzhou Tianning Temple," used to this day. Ming Xu Wen's "Record of Rebuilding Changzhou Tianning Temple" praised it as the "Number One Monastery in the Southeast"; "Chinese Buddhism·Qing Dynasty Buddhism" lists it together with Zhenjiang Jinshan Temple, Yangzhou Gaomin Temple, and Ningbo Tiantong Temple as the "Four Great Monasteries of the Chan Sect." During the Taiping Rebellion the temple was destroyed by war fires; rebuilt from the 4th year of Tongzhi to the 30th year of Guangxu of the Qing (1865-1904); the 13-story Tianning Pagoda completed in 2008 is the tallest Buddhist pagoda in the world. In 1982 Tianning Temple was designated a provincial protected unit; in 1983 it became a key national Buddhist monastery; today it is a national 4A-level tourist scenic area. The main buildings of the temple are located on the north-south central axis, from south to north successively the mountain gate, Heavenly King Hall, Mahavira Hall, Imperial Calligraphy Building, Three Treasures Hall, and Tianning Pagoda. The east road has the Manjushri Hall, Arhat Hall, and Guanyin Hall etc.; the west road has the Samantabhadra Hall, Arhat Hall, Ksitigarbha Hall, Bodhidharma Pavilion, Precept Study Hall, and Life Release Pond etc. The Mahavira Hall is the main hall of the temple, adopting a double-eave hip-and-gable roof; inside, eight ironwood columns are over 80 cm in diameter, precious timber; the beams and lintels etc. are exquisitely carved; the left and right walls are embedded with 518 Arhat stone statues carved in the Qing, with vivid shapes, artistic masterpieces.

projects.name: 红梅公园
projects.level: 含文笔塔、红梅阁等历史建筑
projects.level_en: Including historical buildings such as Wenbi Pagoda and Red Plum Pavilion
projects.address_en: No. 1 Luohan Road, Tianning District
highlights: 红梅公园位于天宁寺北部始建于1958年是市内最大的综合公园免费参观园内包括三区八景南部为文物古迹区有红梅春晓和文笔夕照两景西北为娱乐活动区有雪山劲松翠微秋霞林园钟声曲池风荷和青峦倒影五景东部为科普教育区有吴风遗韵一景园内较重要的古建筑遗存有文笔塔红梅阁半山亭袈裟塔冰梅石嘉贤坊塔影山房和文笔楼等文笔塔位于公园东南角南1入口处建于南齐建元年间480-482原属太平讲寺后来成为常州文化的象征与科举联系起来被称作文峰塔今塔建于清光绪三十年1904年塔身为砖木结构八角七层内部有楼梯可盘旋登顶眺览城内外景致塔底层的花岗岩须弥座上的浮雕莲瓣为宋代遗物红梅阁位于公园东南角南2入口处始建于唐昭宋年间原属水田寺今为清光绪二十六年1900年重建坐北朝南下有二层台基上为两层歇山顶楼阁庭院中遍植红梅翠竹一层是祀师堂祀道教祖师葛洪和张天师等二层是祀玉室祀斗姥和文昌等阁前冰梅石柱为元代天庆观牌坊石柱原物较为珍贵
projects.content_zh: 红梅公园位于天宁寺北部，始建于1958年，是市内最大的综合公园，免费参观。园内包括三区八景：南部为文物古迹区，有红梅春晓和文笔夕照两景；西北为娱乐活动区，有雪山劲松、翠微秋霞、林园钟声、曲池风荷和青峦倒影五景；东部为科普教育区，有吴风遗韵一景。园内较重要的古建筑遗存有文笔塔、红梅阁、半山亭、袈裟塔、冰梅石、嘉贤坊、塔影山房和文笔楼等。1. 文笔塔：位于公园东南角南1入口处，建于南齐建元年间（480—482），原属太平讲寺，后来成为常州文化的象征，与科举联系起来，被称作文峰塔。今塔建于清光绪三十年（1904年），塔身为砖木结构，八角七层，内部有楼梯可盘旋登顶，眺览城内外景致。塔底层的花岗岩须弥座上的浮雕莲瓣为宋代遗物。2. 红梅阁：位于公园东南角南2入口处，始建于唐昭宋年间，原属水田寺。今为清光绪二十六年（1900年）重建，坐北朝南，下有二层台基，上为两层歇山顶楼阁，庭院中遍植红梅翠竹。一层是祀师堂，祀道教祖师葛洪和张天师等；二层是祀玉室，祀斗姥和文昌等。阁前冰梅石柱为元代天庆观牌坊石柱原物，较为珍贵。
projects.content_en: Red Plum Park is located north of Tianning Temple, first built in 1958, the largest comprehensive park in the city, with free admission. The park includes three zones and eight scenes: the southern part is the cultural relics and historic sites zone, with two scenes: Red Plum Spring Dawn and Wenbi Sunset Glow; the northwest is the entertainment and activity zone, with five scenes: Snow Mountain Strong Pine, Cuiwei Autumn Sunset, Forest Garden Bell Sound, Winding Pond Wind Lotus, and Green Peak Reflection; the eastern part is the science education zone, with one scene: Wu Style Remaining Charm. The more important ancient architectural remains in the park include the Wenbi (Writing Brush) Pagoda, Red Plum Pavilion, Banshan (Half Mountain) Pavilion, Kasaya Pagoda, Ice Plum Stone, Jiaxian (Worthy Commendation) Archway, Taying (Pagoda Shadow) Mountain Room, and Wenbi Building etc. 1. Wenbi Pagoda: Located at the South 1 entrance in the southeast corner of the park, built during the Jianyuan reign of the Southern Qi (480-482), originally belonging to Taiping Lecture Temple; later it became a symbol of Changzhou culture, linked with the imperial examinations, and was called the Wenfeng (Cultural Prosperity) Pagoda. Today's pagoda was built in the 30th year of Guangxu of the Qing (1904), with a brick-wood structure, octagonal and seven stories, with a staircase inside allowing spiraling to the top to overlook the scenery inside and outside the city. The relief lotus petals on the granite Sumeru base at the bottom of the pagoda are Song Dynasty relics. 2. Red Plum Pavilion: Located at the South 2 entrance in the southeast corner of the park, first built during the Zhaosong reign of the Tang, originally belonging to Shuitian Temple. Today it was rebuilt in the 26th year of Guangxu of the Qing (1900), facing south with its back to north, with a two-story platform base below and a two-story hip-and-gable roof pavilion above; the courtyard is planted with red plums and green bamboo everywhere. The first floor is the Master Worship Hall, enshrining Daoist patriarchs Ge Hong and Celestial Master Zhang etc.; the second floor is the Jade Worship Room, enshrining Doumu and Wenchang etc. The Ice Plum stone columns in front of the pavilion are original objects from the Tianqing Temple archway of the Yuan Dynasty, relatively precious.

projects.name: 太平兴国石经幢
projects.level: 第四批江苏省文物保护单位（1995年）
projects.level_en: 4th Batch Jiangsu Provincial Cultural Heritage Site (1995)
projects.address: 天宁区延陵东路太平桥北
projects.address_en: North of Taiping Bridge, East Yanling Road, Tianning District
highlights: 经幢为北宋太平兴国四年979年太平禅寺遗物原有一对立于禅寺山门前今其一保存尚好幢高5.42米宽2.2米由基石浮雕八力神宝相花八佛像仰莲等须弥座及八棱形幢身缠枝牡丹花宝盖浮雕斗栱宝顶八部分叠成雕刻古朴浑厚体现了宋代的石刻风格基座为八角莲瓣型高1.5米周身遍刻陀罗尼经字迹已漫漶不清另一座仅存三层须弥座残件
projects.content_zh: 经幢为北宋太平兴国四年（979年）太平禅寺遗物，原有一对，立于禅寺山门前。今其一保存尚好，幢高5.42米，宽2.2米，由基石、浮雕八力神、宝相花、八佛像、仰莲等须弥座及八棱形幢身、缠枝牡丹花宝盖、浮雕斗栱、宝顶八部分叠成，雕刻古朴浑厚，体现了宋代的石刻风格。基座为八角莲瓣型，高1.5米，周身遍刻陀罗尼经，字迹已漫漶不清。另一座仅存三层须弥座残件。
projects.content_en: The dharani pillar is a relic of the Taiping Chan Temple from the 4th year of Taiping Xingguo of the Northern Song (979); originally there was a pair, standing in front of the temple's mountain gate. Today one is well preserved, 5.42 meters high and 2.2 meters wide, composed of eight parts stacked together: the base stone, relief eight strength deities, precious phase flowers, eight Buddha statues, upward-lotus Sumeru base, octagonal pillar body, interlocking peony flower canopy, relief bracket sets, and precious top. The carvings are simple and vigorous, reflecting the stone carving style of the Song Dynasty. The base is an octagonal lotus-petal shape, 1.5 meters high, covered with the Dharani Sutra carved all around, with the characters already blurred and illegible. The other one only retains the remnants of a three-layer Sumeru base.

projects.name: 东坡公园
projects.level: 含东坡古渡、舣舟亭、东坡洗砚池、万寿行宫等古迹
projects.level_en: Including historic sites such as Dongpo Ancient Ferry, Yizhou Pavilion, Dongpo Inkstone-Washing Pool, and Wanshou Travel Palace
projects.address_en: No. 9 Middle Yanling Road
highlights: 东坡公园包括三面环水的半岛和运河中的半月岛两部分据传北宋文学家苏轼一生曾11次造访常州乘船在此停泊现辟为公园以作纪念园内有东坡古渡舣舟亭东坡洗砚池和万寿行宫等古迹公园西侧由飞虹桥通往西岸的海潮寺今公园内的东坡古渡是当年苏东坡舍舟登岸处清代乾隆南巡也是在此上岸古渡向东经广济桥通向半月岛此桥建于明正德十二年1571年原在城西后来拓宽城西运河时整体迁移至此古渡西南山顶最高处为舣舟亭北宋熙宁六年1073年苏东坡路过常州时曾在此野宿作除夕夜宿常州城外曰重衾脚冷知霜重新沐头轻感发稀多谢残灯不嫌客孤舟一夜许相依后来人们在此建亭纪念乾隆第二次南巡到常州时重修此亭并御题玉局风流匾额今亭为1984年重建舣舟亭北部山下的水池和假山一带汇集了众多古迹池东假山后面藏有东坡洗砚池1757年由藤花旧馆移到此处洗砚池用白石凿成长1米宽半米底部有小孔去其楔塞子水立涸以新水盖之容十五六石许积水盛夏不败水池南岸有御碑亭内置六块乾隆在常州题写的诗碑水池西岸为龙亭乾隆曾在此召见当地文士亭东是康熙乾隆南巡时驻扎的万寿行宫今仅存遗址
projects.content_zh: 东坡公园包括三面环水的半岛和运河中的半月岛两部分，据传北宋文学家苏轼一生曾11次造访常州，乘船在此停泊，现辟为公园以作纪念。园内有东坡古渡、舣舟亭、东坡洗砚池和万寿行宫等古迹。公园西侧由飞虹桥通往西岸的海潮寺。今公园内的东坡古渡是当年苏东坡舍舟登岸处，清代乾隆南巡也是在此上岸。古渡向东经广济桥通向半月岛，此桥建于明正德十二年（1571年），原在城西，后来拓宽城西运河时整体迁移至此。古渡西南山顶最高处为舣舟亭。北宋熙宁六年（1073年）苏东坡路过常州时曾在此野宿，作《除夕夜宿常州城外》曰："重衾脚冷知霜重，新沐头轻感发稀。多谢残灯不嫌客，孤舟一夜许相依。"后来人们在此建亭纪念。乾隆第二次南巡到常州时，重修此亭，并御题"玉局风流"匾额。今亭为1984年重建。舣舟亭北部山下的水池和假山一带汇集了众多古迹。池东假山后面藏有东坡洗砚池，1757年由藤花旧馆移到此处。洗砚池用白石凿成，长1米，宽半米，底部有小孔，"去其楔（塞子），水立涸。以新水盖之，容十五六石许，积水盛夏不败"。水池南岸有御碑亭，内置六块乾隆在常州题写的诗碑。水池西岸为龙亭，乾隆曾在此召见当地文士。亭东是康熙、乾隆南巡时驻扎的万寿行宫，今仅存遗址。
projects.content_en: Dongpo (Su Dongpo) Park consists of two parts: a peninsula surrounded by water on three sides and the Half-Moon Island in the canal. According to tradition, Su Shi, a writer of the Northern Song, visited Changzhou 11 times in his life, anchoring his boat here; today it has been opened as a park in commemoration. Inside the park are historic sites such as the Dongpo Ancient Ferry, Yizhou (Tying Boat) Pavilion, Dongpo Inkstone-Washing Pool, and Wanshou (Longevity) Travel Palace. The west side of the park connects to the Haichao Temple on the west bank via the Feihong (Flying Rainbow) Bridge. The Dongpo Ancient Ferry in today's park is where Su Dongpo disembarked from his boat in those years; during the Qing, Qianlong's southern tour also came ashore here. East of the ancient ferry, via the Guangji Bridge, leads to the Half-Moon Island; this bridge was built in the 12th year of Zhengde of the Ming (1571), originally west of the city, and was later moved here as a whole when widening the west city canal. At the highest point of the mountain southwest of the ancient ferry is the Yizhou Pavilion. In the 6th year of Xining of the Northern Song (1073), when Su Dongpo passed through Changzhou, he once slept in the open here, writing "Staying Outside Changzhou City on New Year's Eve": "Under heavy quilts my feet are cold, knowing the frost is heavy; after newly washing my hair, my head feels light, sensing my hair thinning. Thank you to the remaining lamp for not disliking the guest, allowing the lonely boat to depend on it all night." Later people built a pavilion here in commemoration. When Qianlong made his second southern tour to Changzhou, he rebuilt this pavilion and personally inscribed the plaque "Yuju Fengliu" (Elegant Style of the Jade Bureau). Today's pavilion was rebuilt in 1984. The area around the pond and rockery at the foot of the mountain north of the Yizhou Pavilion gathers numerous historic sites. Behind the rockery east of the pond hides the Dongpo Inkstone-Washing Pool, moved here from the Tenghua Old Hall in 1757. The inkstone-washing pool is carved from white stone, 1 meter long and half a meter wide, with a small hole at the bottom; "removing its wedge (plug), the water dries up immediately. Filling it with fresh water, it holds about fifteen or six shi of water, and the stored water does not spoil even in midsummer." On the south bank of the pond is the Imperial Stele Pavilion, containing six steles with poems inscribed by Qianlong in Changzhou. On the west bank of the pond is the Dragon Pavilion, where Qianlong once summoned local literati. East of the pavilion is the Wanshou Travel Palace where Kangxi and Qianlong stayed during their southern tours, today only ruins remain.

projects.name: 张太雷旧居
projects.level: 第六批全国重点文物保护单位（2006年）
projects.level_en: 6th Batch National Key Cultural Heritage Site (2006)
projects.address: 天宁区和平中路子和里3号
projects.address_en: No. 3 Zihe Li, Middle Heping Road, Tianning District
highlights: 张太雷1898-1927是中国共产党早期领导人之一广州起义的主要领导者1918年他与陆静华在常州结婚在此租住了七年时间这处故居建于民国初年仅有两进三间平屋体现了早期革命家生活的简朴1987年修复后对外开放包括张太雷故居陈列和生平事迹展览两部分
projects.content_zh: 张太雷（1898—1927）是中国共产党早期领导人之一，广州起义的主要领导者。1918年他与陆静华在常州结婚，在此租住了七年时间。这处故居建于民国初年，仅有两进三间平屋，体现了早期革命家生活的简朴。1987年修复后对外开放，包括张太雷故居陈列和生平事迹展览两部分。
projects.content_en: Zhang Tailei (1898-1927) was one of the early leaders of the Communist Party of China and the main leader of the Guangzhou Uprising. In 1918 he married Lu Jinghua in Changzhou and rented here for seven years. This former residence was built in the early Republic of China, with only two rows and three bays of single-story houses, reflecting the simplicity of life of early revolutionaries. After restoration in 1987, it opened to the public, including two parts: the exhibition of Zhang Tailei's former residence and the exhibition of his life and deeds.

projects.name: 清凉寺
projects.level: 第三批江苏省文物保护单位（1982年）
projects.level_en: 3rd Batch Jiangsu Provincial Cultural Heritage Site (1982)
projects.address_en: No. 488 Middle Heping Road, Tianning District
highlights: 北宋治平元年1064年常州大儒胡宿996-1067请额建造原在常州城东南3里处称报恩感慈禅院南宋淳祐八年1248年常州郡守李迪在寺内建胡文恭公祠祭祀胡宿元末寺祠俱毁明永乐元年1403年移建今址始称清凉寺后又改为端明寺胡宿曾任端明殿学士太平天国时期寺庙被毁清末重建复称清凉寺今存天王殿海镜堂藏经楼法堂禅堂和大悲阁等建筑其中禅堂和藏经楼最具特色禅堂是一座回字形转楼形制独特藏经楼三层七开间藏有明代宗所赐大藏经和慈禧太后所赐大藏经龙藏
projects.content_zh: 北宋治平元年（1064年）常州大儒胡宿（996—1067）请额建造，原在常州城东南3里处，称报恩感慈禅院。南宋淳祐八年（1248年）常州郡守李迪在寺内建胡文恭公祠祭祀胡宿。元末寺、祠俱毁，明永乐元年（1403年）移建今址，始称清凉寺，后又改为端明寺（胡宿曾任端明殿学士）。太平天国时期寺庙被毁，清末重建，复称清凉寺。今存天王殿、海镜堂、藏经楼、法堂、禅堂和大悲阁等建筑。其中禅堂和藏经楼最具特色。禅堂是一座"回"字形转楼，形制独特。藏经楼三层七开间，藏有明代宗所赐大藏经和慈禧太后所赐大藏经（龙藏）。
projects.content_en: In the 1st year of Zhiping of the Northern Song (1064), Hu Su (996-1067), a great Confucian scholar of Changzhou, requested a plaque to build it, originally located 3 li southeast of Changzhou city, called the Bao'en Ganci Chan Courtyard. In the 8th year of Chunyou of the Southern Song (1248), Li Di, Prefect of Changzhou, built the Hu Wengong Shrine inside the temple to sacrifice to Hu Su. At the end of the Yuan, both the temple and shrine were destroyed; in the 1st year of Yongle of the Ming (1403), it was moved to today's site, beginning to be called Qingliang (Cool and Refreshing) Temple, later changed to Duanming Temple (Hu Su once served as a scholar of the Duanming Hall). During the Taiping Rebellion the temple was destroyed; rebuilt at the end of the Qing, again called Qingliang Temple. Today surviving buildings include the Heavenly King Hall, Haijing (Sea Mirror) Hall, Scripture Library, Dharma Hall, Chan Hall, and Great Compassion Pavilion etc. Among them, the Chan Hall and Scripture Library are the most distinctive. The Chan Hall is a "回" (return)-shaped revolving tower, unique in form. The Scripture Library is three stories and seven bays wide, containing the Great Canon bestowed by the Jingtai Emperor of the Ming and the Great Canon (Dragon Canon) bestowed by Empress Dowager Cixi.

projects.name: 荆川公园
projects.level: 含陈渡草堂、唐荆川墓、唐氏宗祠（原在青果巷，2002年移建至此）
projects.level_en: Including Chendu Thatched Hall, Tang Jingchuan Tomb, and Tang Family Ancestral Shrine (originally at Qingguo Lane, moved here in 2002)
projects.address: 清潭西路与长江中路交汇处
projects.address_en: Intersection of West Qingtan Road and Middle Changjiang Road
highlights: 荆川公园是为纪念明嘉靖年间抗倭英雄和文学家唐荆川而建公园东南北三面环水环境清幽内有陈渡草堂唐荆川墓和唐氏宗祠原在青果巷2002年移建至此各景使人们缅怀这位先贤陈渡草堂明嘉靖八年1529年唐荆川中会试第一主考官为文渊阁大学士张璁在嘉靖初年的大礼仪之争中张璁因支持嘉靖皇帝而获得迅速提升但也因此站到众多朝臣的对立面张璁有意提拔唐荆川但后者虽是后生晚辈却并不领情按部就班地到兵部任职明嘉靖十二年1533年唐荆川入翰林院参与编校实录仍然不肯依附张璁工作完成后托病辞官张璁开始不想批复后来有人向他点破唐荆川一直刻意与他保持距离璁发怒拟以吏部主事署罢归永不复叙明史卷215唐顺之传唐荆川回到常州在城外西南营建陈渡草堂潜心读书其子唐鹤征常州府志人物志记载他自编氓归贫不能给朝夕幸存其初第时有司例给牌坊银稍为筹划购田一顷民居数椽于陈渡桥之名曰陈渡草堂湫溢不蔽风雨公居之裕如也唐荆川与门生在草堂中读书历以实行不为虚谈二十余年如一日直到明嘉靖三十二年1553年复出与胡宗宪协同作战令倭寇闻风丧胆今陈渡草堂据清人谢应芝襄文读书书记处记有懒云阁五言楼春池馆和压溪榭等景致唐荆川墓出陈渡草堂南门向东为唐荆川墓1982年列为省保单位明嘉靖三十九年1560年唐荆川在行军途中病逝他官居四品皇帝特诏按三品赐葬明崇祯年间追谥襄文整座墓园坐东朝西西侧为一泻桥向东是一座木质飞檐石牌坊两侧排列石羊石兽石马和石翁仲东部有三座大土坟鼎足而立中央是荆川夫妇合葬墓两旁是他的玄孙唐宇亮和唐宇昭之墓
projects.content_zh: 荆川公园是为纪念明嘉靖年间抗倭英雄和文学家唐荆川而建。公园东南北三面环水，环境清幽，内有陈渡草堂、唐荆川墓和唐氏宗祠（原在青果巷，2002年移建至此）各景，使人们缅怀这位先贤。1. 陈渡草堂：明嘉靖八年（1529年）唐荆川中会试第一，主考官为文渊阁大学士张璁。在嘉靖初年的"大礼仪之争"中，张璁因支持嘉靖皇帝而获得迅速提升，但也因此站到众多朝臣的对立面。张璁有意提拔唐荆川，但后者虽是后生晚辈却并不领情，按部就班地到兵部任职。明嘉靖十二年（1533年）唐荆川入翰林院参与编校《实录》，仍然不肯依附张璁，工作完成后托病辞官。张璁开始不想批复，后来有人向他点破唐荆川一直刻意与他保持距离，"璁发怒，拟以吏部主事署罢归，永不复叙"（《明史·卷215·唐顺之传》）。唐荆川回到常州，在城外西南营建陈渡草堂，潜心读书。其子唐鹤征《常州府志·人物志》记载他"自编氓归，贫不能给朝夕，幸存其初第时有司例给牌坊银，稍为筹划，购田一顷、民居数椽于陈渡桥之，名曰陈渡草堂，湫溢不蔽风雨，公居之裕如也"，唐荆川与门生在草堂中读书，"历以实行，不为虚谈，二十余年如一日"，直到明嘉靖三十二年（1553年）复出，与胡宗宪协同作战，令倭寇闻风丧胆。今陈渡草堂据清人谢应芝《襄文读书处记》复建，有懒云阁、五言楼、春池馆和压溪榭等景致。2. 唐荆川墓：出陈渡草堂南门，向东为唐荆川墓，1982年列为省保单位。明嘉靖三十九年（1560年）唐荆川在行军途中病逝，他官居四品，皇帝特诏按三品赐葬，明崇祯年间追谥襄文。整座墓园坐东朝西，西侧为一泻桥，向东是一座木质飞檐石牌坊，两侧排列石羊、石兽、石马和石翁仲。东部有三座大土坟鼎足而立，中央是荆川夫妇合葬墓，两旁是他的玄孙唐宇亮和唐宇昭之墓。
projects.content_en: Jingchuan Park was built to commemorate Tang Jingchuan, the anti-Japanese pirate hero and writer of the Jiajing reign of the Ming. The park is surrounded by water on the east, south, and north sides, with a serene environment; inside are scenes such as the Chendu Thatched Hall, Tang Jingchuan Tomb, and Tang Family Ancestral Shrine (originally at Qingguo Lane, moved here in 2002), allowing people to remember this worthy predecessor. 1. Chendu Thatched Hall: In the 8th year of Jiajing of the Ming (1529), Tang Jingchuan ranked first in the metropolitan examination, with the chief examiner being Zhang Cong, Grand Secretary of the Wenyuan Pavilion. In the "Great Rites Controversy" of the early Jiajing reign, Zhang Cong gained rapid promotion for supporting Emperor Jiajing, but thus stood opposite many court officials. Zhang Cong intended to promote Tang Jingchuan, but the latter, though a junior, did not appreciate it and methodically took up a post at the Ministry of War. In the 12th year of Jiajing (1533), Tang Jingchuan entered the Hanlin Academy to participate in editing and collating the "Veritable Records," still refusing to attach himself to Zhang Cong, and after completing the work resigned on grounds of illness. Zhang Cong initially did not want to approve, but later someone pointed out to him that Tang Jingchuan had deliberately kept his distance; "Zhang Cong became angry, planning to dismiss him as acting director of the Ministry of Personnel, never to be reappointed" ("History of Ming·Volume 215·Biography of Tang Shunzhi"). Tang Jingchuan returned to Changzhou and built the Chendu Thatched Hall southwest of the city, devoting himself to reading. His son Tang Hezheng's "Changzhou Prefecture Gazetteer·Biographies" records that he "returned as a commoner, too poor to provide for morning and evening; fortunately, when he first passed the examination, the authorities had customarily given him archway silver, which he slightly managed to purchase a qing of farmland and several rafters of a dwelling at Chendu Bridge, named Chendu Thatched Hall; low and damp, not sheltering from wind and rain, yet he lived there comfortably." Tang Jingchuan and his disciples read in the thatched hall, "practicing with real action, not empty talk, for over twenty years as one day," until the 32nd year of Jiajing (1553) when he returned to office, fighting in coordination with Hu Zongxian, making the Japanese pirates flee at the news. Today's Chendu Thatched Hall was rebuilt according to Qing person Xie Yingzhi's "Record of the Place Where Xiangwen Read," with scenes such as the Lanyun (Lazy Cloud) Pavilion, Wuyan (Five-Character) Tower, Chunchi (Spring Pond) Hall, and Yaxi (Pressing Stream) Terrace. 2. Tang Jingchuan Tomb: Exiting the south gate of Chendu Thatched Hall, eastward is the Tang Jingchuan Tomb, designated a provincial protected unit in 1982. In the 39th year of Jiajing of the Ming (1560), Tang Jingchuan died of illness during a military march; he held the fourth rank, and the emperor specially ordered burial according to the third rank; during the Chongzhen reign of the Ming he was posthumously titled Xiangwen. The entire tomb garden faces west with its back to east; on the west side is the Yixie (One Gush) Bridge, eastward is a wooden upturned-eave stone archway, with stone sheep, stone beasts, stone horses, and stone guardian figures lined on both sides. In the east are three large earthen tombs standing like a tripod; in the center is the joint tomb of Jingchuan and his wife, and on both sides are the tombs of his great-grandsons Tang Yuliang and Tang Yuzhao.

highlights: 常州地区现有6座古代戏楼2006年第六批列为国保单位杨氏家庭戏楼位于钟楼区东下塘75号紧邻青果巷此戏楼建于清同治光绪年间又称杨氏雕花楼有上下两层一层存放乐器等二层为舞台除东面外三面临空周置20扇长窗雕刻虫鱼花鸟工艺精细平时长窗关闭自成一室演戏时将窗撤下露出舞台楼前建有花园和假山阳湖县城隍庙戏楼位于和平南路与青果巷交汇处的新坊桥小学内城隍庙建于清乾隆二十四年1759年戏台建于清同治九年1870年1896年重修戏台坐南朝北两层歇山顶平面呈凸字形台口正对城隍庙大殿1988年拆除戏台与大殿之间两侧原有上下各9间看戏楼戏台东墙上嵌清光绪二十二年1896年所刻阳湖县增修城隍庙记称戏楼特高春秋致祭作乐以娱神复取古今忠孝节义故事俾梨园子弟演之万绥东岳庙戏楼位于新北区孟河镇万绥东岳庙内东岳庙始建于唐贞观年间清道光年间重修戏楼附属于东岳庙建于道光年间坐东朝西台口正对东岳庙大殿戏楼平面呈凸字形正台屋檐外伸高出屋面做成八角屋顶内架藻井后台宽三间两侧设化妆间左侧还有供乐队演奏的架子台台板壁上记载了清末民初来此演出的戏班戏目和主角姓名等具有较高的史料价值西夏墅梅村戏楼位于新北区西夏墅镇梅林村附属于真武庙庙已不存戏楼始建于明代1688年重建1863年2004年两次重修戏楼坐南朝北二层歇山顶上下各三间平面呈凸字形礼嘉戏楼位于武进区礼嘉中学内此戏台台口向北正对烈帝庙大殿太平天国时期戏楼毁于战火光绪年间重建上下两层各三间平面呈凸字形两旁有台柱向上支撑着拱顶飞檐下部镇着楼板台角建筑风格颇似香山帮建造的苏州楼台戏楼前有开阔的广场可容2000多名观众顺庄戏楼位于武进区横林镇顺庄村张家自然村西首附属于东岳庙戏楼建于清代坐南朝北二层歇山顶平面呈凸字形前台三间较窄后台三间较宽
projects.content_zh: 常州地区现有6座古代戏楼，2006年第六批列为国保单位。1. 杨氏家庭戏楼：位于钟楼区东下塘75号，紧邻青果巷。此戏楼建于清同治、光绪年间，又称杨氏雕花楼。有上下两层，一层存放乐器等，二层为舞台。除东面外三面临空，周置20扇长窗，雕刻虫鱼花鸟，工艺精细。平时长窗关闭，自成一室；演戏时将窗撤下，露出舞台。楼前建有花园和假山。2. 阳湖县城隍庙戏楼：位于和平南路与青果巷交汇处的新坊桥小学内。城隍庙建于清乾隆二十四年（1759年），戏台建于清同治九年（1870年），1896年重修。戏台坐南朝北，两层歇山顶，平面呈"凸"字形，台口正对城隍庙大殿（1988年拆除）。戏台与大殿之间，两侧原有上下各9间看戏楼。戏台东墙上嵌清光绪二十二年（1896年）所刻《阳湖县增修城隍庙记》，称："戏楼特高，春秋致祭，作乐以娱神。复取古今忠孝节义故事俾梨园子弟演之。"3. 万绥东岳庙戏楼：位于新北区孟河镇万绥东岳庙内。东岳庙始建于唐贞观年间，清道光年间重修。戏楼附属于东岳庙，建于道光年间，坐东朝西，台口正对东岳庙大殿。戏楼平面呈"凸"字形，正台屋檐外伸，高出屋面，做成八角屋顶，内架藻井。后台宽三间，两侧设化妆间，左侧还有供乐队演奏的架子台。台板壁上记载了清末民初来此演出的戏班、戏目和主角姓名等，具有较高的史料价值。4. 西夏墅梅村戏楼：位于新北区西夏墅镇梅林村，附属于真武庙（庙已不存）。戏楼始建于明代，1688年重建，1863年、2004年两次重修。戏楼坐南朝北，二层歇山顶，上下各三间，平面呈"凸"字形。5. 礼嘉戏楼：位于武进区礼嘉中学内。此戏台台口向北，正对烈帝庙大殿。太平天国时期戏楼毁于战火，光绪年间重建。上下两层各三间，平面呈"凸"字形，两旁有台柱，向上支撑着拱顶飞檐，下部镇着楼板台角。建筑风格颇似香山帮建造的苏州楼台。戏楼前有开阔的广场，可容2000多名观众。6. 顺庄戏楼：位于武进区横林镇顺庄村张家自然村西首，附属于东岳庙。戏楼建于清代，坐南朝北，二层歇山顶，平面呈"凸"字形，前台三间较窄，后台三间较宽。
projects.content_en: There are currently 6 ancient theatrical towers in the Changzhou area, designated national protected units in the 6th batch of 2006. 1. Yang Family Theatrical Tower: Located at No. 75 Dongxiatang, Zhonglou District, adjacent to Qingguo Lane. This theatrical tower was built during the Tongzhi and Guangxu reigns of the Qing, also called the Yang Family Carved Tower. It has two stories: the first floor stores musical instruments etc., and the second floor is the stage. Except for the east side, it is open on three sides, with 20 long windows around, carved with insects, fish, flowers, and birds, with exquisite craftsmanship. Normally the long windows are closed, forming a room by itself; during performances the windows are removed, exposing the stage. In front of the tower are a garden and rockery. 2. Yanghu County City God Temple Theatrical Tower: Located in Xinfangqiao Primary School at the intersection of South Heping Road and Qingguo Lane. The City God Temple was built in the 24th year of Qianlong of the Qing (1759), the stage was built in the 9th year of Tongzhi of the Qing (1870), and rebuilt in 1896. The stage faces south with its back to north, with a two-story hip-and-gable roof, and the plan呈 a "convex" shape, with the stage opening directly facing the City God Temple main hall (demolished in 1988). Between the stage and the main hall, there were originally 9 viewing towers on each side, upper and lower. On the east wall of the stage is embedded the "Record of Adding to and Repairing the City God Temple of Yanghu County" carved in the 22nd year of Guangxu of the Qing (1896), stating: "The theatrical tower is especially tall; in spring and autumn sacrifices, music is played to entertain the gods. Furthermore, stories of ancient and modern loyalty, filial piety, chastity, and righteousness are taken for opera performers to enact." 3. Wansui Dongyue Temple Theatrical Tower: Located inside the Wansui Dongyue Temple in Menghe Town, Xinbei District. The Dongyue Temple was first built during the Zhenguan reign of the Tang, repaired during the Daoguang reign of the Qing. The theatrical tower is attached to the Dongyue Temple, built during the Daoguang reign, facing west with its back to east, with the stage opening directly facing the Dongyue Temple main hall. The theatrical tower plan呈 a "convex" shape; the main stage eaves extend outward, higher than the roof, forming an octagonal roof with a coffered ceiling inside. The backstage is three bays wide, with dressing rooms on both sides, and on the left there is also a rack platform for the band to perform. The stage board walls record the opera troupes, plays, and leading actor names that performed here from the late Qing to early Republic, with relatively high historical value. 4. Xixiashu Meicun Theatrical Tower: Located in Meilin Village, Xixiashu Town, Xinbei District, attached to the Zhenwu Temple (the temple no longer exists). The theatrical tower was first built in the Ming, rebuilt in 1688, and repaired twice in 1863 and 2004. The theatrical tower faces south with its back to north, with a two-story hip-and-gable roof, three bays upper and lower, and the plan呈 a "convex" shape. 5. Lijia Theatrical Tower: Located inside Lijia Middle School, Wujin District. This stage opening faces north, directly facing the Liedi Temple main hall. During the Taiping Rebellion the theatrical tower was destroyed by war fires, rebuilt during the Guangxu reign. Two stories with three bays each, the plan呈 a "convex" shape, with stage columns on both sides supporting the arched upturned eaves upward, and the lower part stabilizing the floor slab and stage corners. The architectural style is quite similar to the Suzhou towers built by the Xiangshan Gang. In front of the theatrical tower is an open square that can accommodate over 2000 spectators. 6. Shunzhuang Theatrical Tower: Located at the west end of Zhangjia Natural Village, Shunzhuang Village, Henglin Town, Wujin District, attached to the Dongyue Temple. The theatrical tower was built in the Qing, facing south with its back to north, with a two-story hip-and-gable roof, the plan呈 a "convex" shape, with the front stage three bays relatively narrow and the backstage three bays relatively wide.

regions.name: 常州

regions.overview: 镇江市位于江苏省西南部，地处长江三角洲的顶端，西邻南京，南接常州，东北临长江黄金水道段。早在旧石器时代中期，镇江沿江一带就有古人类繁衍生息。镇江有文字记载的历史可上溯到3000年前的西周时期为谷阳。秦始皇统一七国后，认为谷阳有"天子气"，遂凿断京岘山阻断，并改谷阳为丹徒，一直沿用至今。北宋政和三年（1113年）升润州为镇江府，丹徒属镇江府。镇江襟山带江，自然风光雄伟壮丽，地上地下文物、人文景观十分丰富。作为江防重镇，三国东吴孙权筑铁瓮城以固守，东晋郗鉴、王恭在京口花山湾筑晋陵城，延续至隋、唐又修缮加筑，今尚存城墙遗址2300米。镇江所辖丹阳市为东晋南朝齐梁帝王祖籍地，这些帝王死后多归葬丹阳，现丹阳、句容地区共存有南朝帝陵石刻12处，为六朝艺术精品。镇江焦山有六朝石刻《瘗鹤铭》，被誉为"大字之祖""书家冠冕"，为书法瑰宝。隋唐运河的开凿使镇江成为交通冲衢，漕运咽喉，唐代润州城西北蒜山下的渡口——蒜山渡逐渐兴盛，唐以后称西津渡，即今西津渡古街所在地。唐代后期大臣李德裕三次出任浙西观察使，在北固山后峰扩建寺庙，寺成后天降甘露，因名甘露寺，又在甘露寺入口处建石塔一座，瘗埋舍利子，北宋时改为铁塔，现为江苏省仅存的铁塔。唐代寺庙兴盛，城南创于东晋的鹤林寺后来成为禅系牛头宗的重要据点。中晚唐时期金山寺已成规模，处在江渡中是往来香客的方便去处。如今丹阳市内的唐中和铜钟，即为唐普宁寺遗物。宋代建炎南渡后，镇江成为屏障都城临安的重镇，城内水网密集，建桥甚多。名士苏轼多次游览镇江，在金山寺留下晒经台之佳话。沈括曾担任镇江知州，在京口置梦溪园，今其地犹存。元代在西津渡建造过街石塔。近代是镇江又一个繁荣时期，1858年《天津条约》规定镇江要在一年后通商，1861年设立租界，1964年在云台山坡建成英国领事馆。民国时期镇江曾作为江苏省会，长达20年之久。晚清至民国初年镇江租界及沿江地带洋行林立，洋楼栉比，建造了大量品质优良的近代建筑，以及马路、邮政、电讯和自来水等公共设施，大多保存在今赵伯先路沿线。1986年镇江成为国务院颁布的第二批国家历史文化名城。镇江今辖京口区（市政府驻地）、润州区和丹徒区3个区，代管丹阳市、扬中市和句容市3个县级市，有国家级文物保护单位17处，省级文物保护单位47处，本书介绍国保建筑6处，省保建筑4处，其他建筑1处。
regions.overview_en: Zhenjiang City is located in the southwestern part of Jiangsu Province, at the top of the Yangtze River Delta, bordering Nanjing to the west, Changzhou to the south, and the golden waterway section of the Yangtze River to the northeast. As early as the middle Paleolithic period, ancient humans already lived and multiplied along the Zhenjiang river area. Zhenjiang's recorded history can be traced back 3000 years to the Western Zhou period, when it was called Guyang. After Qin Shi Huang unified the seven states, believing that Guyang had "son-of-heaven qi," he cut through Jingxian Mountain to block it and renamed Guyang to Dantu, a name used to this day. In the 3rd year of Zhenghe of the Northern Song (1113), Runzhou was promoted to Zhenjiang Prefecture, with Dantu belonging to Zhenjiang Prefecture. Zhenjiang embraces mountains and the river, with magnificent natural scenery and rich above-ground and underground cultural relics and human landscapes. As a river defense stronghold, Sun Quan of Eastern Wu in the Three Kingdoms built the Tieweng (Iron Urn) City for defense; in the Eastern Jin, Chi Jian and Wang Gong built the Jinling City at Huashan Bay in Jingkou, continuing to the Sui and Tang when it was repaired and reinforced, with 2300 meters of city wall ruins surviving today. Danyang City under Zhenjiang's jurisdiction was the ancestral home of the emperors of the Qi and Liang dynasties of the Eastern Jin and Southern Dynasties; after death, these emperors were mostly buried in Danyang, and today there are 12 Southern Dynasties imperial tomb stone carvings in the Danyang and Jurong areas—fine artworks of the Six Dynasties. Jiaoshan in Zhenjiang has the Six Dynasties stone carving "Crane Burial Inscription," hailed as the "ancestor of large characters" and "crown of calligraphers," a calligraphic treasure. The excavation of the Sui-Tang Grand Canal made Zhenjiang a transportation hub and grain transport throat; the ferry at the foot of Suan Mountain northwest of Runzhou City in the Tang—Suan Mountain Ferry—gradually flourished, called Xijin Ferry after the Tang, today's location of the Xijin Ferry Ancient Street. Li Deyu, a late-Tang minister, served three times as Governor of Western Zhejiang, expanding a temple on the rear peak of Beigu Mountain; after its completion, sweet dew fell from heaven, hence named Ganlu (Sweet Dew) Temple; he also built a stone pagoda at the entrance of Ganlu Temple to bury relics, changed to an iron pagoda in the Northern Song—today the only surviving iron pagoda in Jiangsu Province. Tang Dynasty temples flourished; the Helin Temple south of the city, founded in the Eastern Jin, later became an important stronghold of the Niutou Sect of Chan Buddhism. In the mid-to-late Tang, Jinshan Temple had already taken shape, located in the river crossing as a convenient place for pilgrims coming and going. Today the Tang Zhonghe bronze bell in Danyang City is a relic of the Tang Puning Temple. After the Jianyan southern crossing of the Song, Zhenjiang became a strategic town shielding the capital Lin'an, with dense water networks inside the city and numerous bridges built. The famous scholar Su Shi visited Zhenjiang multiple times, leaving the fine story of the scripture-drying platform at Jinshan Temple. Shen Kuo once served as Governor of Zhenjiang, establishing the Mengxi Garden in Jingkou, whose site still exists today. In the Yuan Dynasty, a street-crossing stone pagoda was built at Xijin Ferry. Modern times were another prosperous period for Zhenjiang; the 1858 "Treaty of Tianjin" stipulated that Zhenjiang should open for trade a year later, a concession was established in 1861, and the British Consulate was built on the slope of Yuntai Mountain in 1964. During the Republic period, Zhenjiang served as the capital of Jiangsu Province for as long as 20 years. From the late Qing to early Republic, foreign firms stood in rows in the Zhenjiang concession and along the river, with Western-style buildings closely packed, constructing a large number of high-quality modern buildings, as well as public facilities such as roads, postal services, telecommunications, and tap water—mostly preserved along today's Zhao Boxian Road. In 1986, Zhenjiang became the second batch of National Historical and Cultural Cities promulgated by the State Council. Zhenjiang today administers 3 districts: Jingkou (municipal government seat), Runzhou, and Dantu, and代管 3 county-level cities: Danyang, Yangzhong, and Jurong; it has 17 national-level cultural heritage protection units and 47 provincial-level cultural heritage protection units; this book introduces 6 national-protected buildings, 4 provincial-protected buildings, and 1 other building.

highlights: 原称樵山相传东汉末年焦光隐居于此改名焦山又称浮玉山焦山与金山相距十余里遥遥相对山上有寺因焦山比金山高竹木丰茂寺庙掩映其中又有金山寺裹山焦山山裹寺之谚定慧寺2011年列为省保单位相传始建于东汉宋代改称普济禅院之后通称焦山寺元代被焚毁明宣德年间重建清康熙二十年1681年重修康熙南巡时改名定慧寺取由戒生定因定发慧之意抗战期间定慧寺遭日军炮击部分被毁新中国成立初期曾予修葺文革期间又遭到严重破坏1979年6月整修大殿和天王殿寺庙坐北朝南依次为山门天王殿和大雄宝殿寺西有华严阁天王殿始建于明正统年间清光绪二十九年1903年重建1983年因木柱衰朽拆除重建大雄宝殿为重檐庑殿顶出檐深远始建于唐自宋以来多次重建文革中破坏严重大殿倾斜1976年拨正1979年再加修缮华严阁位于焦山西麓清代僧人元漕创建新中国成立后重修1979年中国佛教协会会长赵朴初为题无尽藏匾华严月色为焦山十六景之一焦山碑林与瘗鹤铭第三批国保1988年焦山碑林由摩崖石刻和碑刻陈列两部分组成其中摩崖石刻环绕在焦山西侧悬崖边的浮玉岩观音岩罗汉岩距公崖雷轰岩和栈道岩一带绵延200余米有六朝以来刻石百余方受到历代书法家尊崇的瘗鹤铭原址在雷轰岩今已移入碑林陈列现存著名摩崖石刻有罗汉岩前唐贞观年间僧人书写的金刚经偈句宋代米芾瘗鹤铭铭书体写的仲宣法芝米芾元祐辛未孟夏观山樵书在西南转角处崖上的浮玉二字为北宋汴京今开封人赵孟奎题另有陆游与友人同观瘗鹤铭后书写的短文等碑刻陈列在焦山东麓宋庆历八年1048年在焦山建宝墨亭收藏王羲之字刻的唐代经幢和瘗鹤铭明代改为宝墨轩清代以来屡遭兵燹损毁严重1960年集合南郊鹤林寺等处的石碑共收碑刻265方移至定慧寺东自然庵香林庵和玉峰庵旧址陈列称为焦山碑林藏自六朝至民国碑500方展出400方除瘗鹤铭外著名碑刻还有南齐刘岱墓志唐魏法师碑宋米芾临兰亭序帖张即之金刚经徐铉临秦峄石门刻石元赵孟頫赤壁赋及东坡小像明文徵明千字文清套帖澄鉴堂石刻和乾隆御碑等瘗鹤铭原刻在焦山西麓石壁上铭文题记称华阳真逸撰上皇山樵书通常认为此铭刻于南朝梁时期铭文为大字楷书十分精美黄庭坚曾称赞大字无过瘗鹤铭宋代时山体滑移瘗鹤铭崩落江中清康熙五十年1711年从江中捞出残石五块移置寺中1960年在宝墨轩园内建亭按前人考证的位置依照当年摩崖原样将石块嵌入石壁中
projects.content_zh: 原称樵山，相传东汉末年焦光隐居于此，改名焦山，又称浮玉山。焦山与金山相距十余里，遥遥相对，山上有寺，因焦山比金山高，竹木丰茂，寺庙掩映其中，又有"金山寺裹山，焦山山裹寺"之谚。1. 焦山定慧寺：2011年列为省保单位，相传始建于东汉，宋代改称普济禅院，之后通称焦山寺，元代被焚毁，明宣德年间重建，清康熙二十年（1681年）重修，康熙南巡时改名定慧寺，取"由戒生定，因定发慧"之意。抗战期间定慧寺遭日军炮击，部分被毁，新中国成立初期曾予修葺，"文革"期间又遭到严重破坏。1979年6月整修大殿和天王殿。寺庙坐北朝南，依次为山门、天王殿和大雄宝殿，寺西有华严阁。天王殿始建于明正统年间，清光绪二十九年（1903年）重建，1983年因木柱衰朽拆除重建。大雄宝殿为重檐庑殿顶，出檐深远，始建于唐，自宋以来多次重建，"文革"中破坏严重，大殿倾斜，1976年拨正，1979年再加修缮。华严阁位于焦山西麓，清代僧人元漕创建，新中国成立后重修。1979年，中国佛教协会会长赵朴初为题"无尽藏"匾。"华严月色"为焦山十六景之一。2. 焦山碑林与瘗鹤铭：第三批国保（1988年）。焦山碑林由摩崖石刻和碑刻陈列两部分组成，其中摩崖石刻环绕在焦山西侧悬崖边的浮玉岩、观音岩、罗汉岩（距公崖）、雷轰岩和栈道岩一带，绵延200余米，有六朝以来刻石百余方。受到历代书法家尊崇的《瘗鹤铭》原址在雷轰岩，今已移入碑林陈列。现存著名摩崖石刻有罗汉岩前唐贞观年间僧人书写的《金刚经偈句》，宋代米芾瘗鹤铭铭书体写的"仲宣、法芝、米芾元祐辛未孟夏观山樵书"，在西南转角处崖上的"浮玉"二字，为北宋汴京（今开封）人赵孟奎题，另有陆游与友人同观《瘗鹤铭》后书写的短文等。碑刻陈列在焦山东麓。宋庆历八年（1048年）在焦山建宝墨亭，收藏王羲之字刻的唐代经幢和《瘗鹤铭》，明代改为宝墨轩，清代以来屡遭兵燹，损毁严重。1960年集合南郊鹤林寺等处的石碑，共收碑刻265方，移至定慧寺东自然庵、香林庵和玉峰庵旧址陈列，称为"焦山碑林"，藏自六朝至民国碑500方，展出400方。除《瘗鹤铭》外，著名碑刻还有南齐《刘岱墓志》、唐《魏法师碑》、宋米芾临《兰亭序帖》、张即之《金刚经》、徐铉临《秦峄石门刻石》、元赵孟頫《赤壁赋及东坡小像》、明文徵明《千字文》、清套帖《澄鉴堂石刻》和《乾隆御碑》等。《瘗鹤铭》原刻在焦山西麓石壁上，铭文题记称华阳真逸撰，上皇山樵书，通常认为此铭刻于南朝梁时期。铭文为大字楷书，十分精美，黄庭坚曾称赞"大字无过《瘗鹤铭》"。宋代时山体滑移，《瘗鹤铭》崩落江中，清康熙五十年（1711年）从江中捞出残石五块，移置寺中。1960年在宝墨轩园内建亭，按前人考证的位置，依照当年摩崖原样将石块嵌入石壁中。
projects.content_en: Originally called Qiaoshan (Firewood Mountain), legend says Jiao Guang lived in seclusion here at the end of the Eastern Han, hence renamed Jiaoshan (Jiao Mountain), also called Fuyu Mountain (Floating Jade Mountain). Jiaoshan and Jinshan are over ten li apart, facing each other from afar; there is a temple on the mountain, and because Jiaoshan is higher than Jinshan with abundant bamboo and trees, the temple is hidden among them, hence the proverb "Jinshan Temple wraps the mountain, Jiaoshan Mountain wraps the temple." 1. Jiaoshan Dinghui Temple: Designated a provincial protected unit in 2011, traditionally founded in the Eastern Han; in the Song it was renamed Puji Chan Courtyard, thereafter commonly called Jiaoshan Temple; destroyed by fire in the Yuan, rebuilt during the Xuande reign of the Ming, repaired in the 20th year of Kangxi of the Qing (1681), and during Kangxi's southern tour renamed Dinghui Temple, taking the meaning of "from precepts arises samadhi, from samadhi arises wisdom." During the War of Resistance against Japan, Dinghui Temple was shelled by Japanese troops and partially destroyed; in the early days of New China it was repaired, and during the Cultural Revolution it suffered severe damage again. In June 1979, the main hall and Heavenly King Hall were renovated. The temple faces south, with the mountain gate, Heavenly King Hall, and Mahavira Hall in sequence, and the Huayan Pavilion west of the temple. The Heavenly King Hall was first built during the Zhengtong reign of the Ming, rebuilt in the 29th year of Guangxu of the Qing (1903), and demolished and rebuilt in 1983 due to decaying wooden columns. The Mahavira Hall has a double-eave hip roof with deep eaves, first built in the Tang, rebuilt multiple times since the Song; severely damaged during the Cultural Revolution with the hall tilting, it was straightened in 1976 and further repaired in 1979. The Huayan Pavilion is located at the western foot of Jiaoshan, founded by Qing monk Yuan Cao, rebuilt after the founding of New China. In 1979, Zhao Puchu, President of the Buddhist Association of China, inscribed the plaque "Endless Treasury." "Huayan Moonlight" is one of the sixteen scenes of Jiaoshan. 2. Jiaoshan Stele Forest and Crane Burial Inscription: 3rd Batch National Protected (1988). The Jiaoshan Stele Forest consists of two parts: cliff carvings and stele display. The cliff carvings surround Fuyu Rock, Guanyin Rock, Luohan Rock (Jugong Rock), Leihong Rock, and Plank Road Rock along the cliff on the west side of Jiaoshan, stretching over 200 meters, with over a hundred carved stones since the Six Dynasties. The "Crane Burial Inscription," revered by calligraphers of all dynasties, was originally at Leihong Rock and has now been moved into the stele forest display. Existing famous cliff carvings include the "Vajra Sutra Verse" written by a monk during the Zhenguan reign of the Tang in front of Luohan Rock; the Song Mi Fu's inscription in the calligraphic style of the Crane Burial Inscription: "Zhongxuan, Fazhi, Mi Fu viewed the mountain woodcutter's writing in the early summer of Yuanyou Xinwei"; the two characters "Fuyu" (Floating Jade) on the cliff at the southwest corner, inscribed by Zhao Mengkui, a native of Bianjing (today's Kaifeng) in the Northern Song; and a short essay written by Lu You after viewing the "Crane Burial Inscription" with friends etc. The stele display is at the eastern foot of Jiaoshan. In the 8th year of Qingli of the Northern Song (1048), the Baomo (Precious Ink) Pavilion was built on Jiaoshan, collecting the Tang dharani pillar with Wang Xizhi's characters and the "Crane Burial Inscription"; in the Ming it was changed to the Baomo Studio, and since the Qing it has repeatedly suffered from wars with severe damage. In 1960, stone steles from places such as Helin Temple in the southern suburbs were gathered, collecting 265 stele carvings in total, moved to the former sites of Ziran Temple, Xianglin Temple, and Yufeng Temple east of Dinghui Temple for display, called the "Jiaoshan Stele Forest," housing 500 steles from the Six Dynasties to the Republic, with 400 on display. Besides the "Crane Burial Inscription," famous stele carvings include the Southern Qi "Epitaph of Liu Dai," Tang "Stele of Master Wei," Song Mi Fu's copy of the "Preface to the Orchid Pavilion," Zhang Jizhi's "Vajra Sutra," Xu Xuan's copy of the "Stone Carving at Yi Gate of Qin," Yuan Zhao Mengfu's "Ode to the Red Cliff and Portrait of Dongpo," Ming Wen Zhengming's "Thousand Character Classic," Qing multi-model album "Chengjian Hall Stone Carvings," and "Qianlong Imperial Stele" etc. The "Crane Burial Inscription" was originally carved on the stone wall at the western foot of Jiaoshan; the inscription's colophon says it was composed by Huayang Zhenyi and written by Shanghuang Shanqiao, and it is generally believed this inscription was carved during the Liang Dynasty of the Southern Dynasties. The inscription is in large-character regular script, extremely exquisite; Huang Tingjian once praised that "no large characters surpass the 'Crane Burial Inscription.'" During the Song, the mountain body shifted and the "Crane Burial Inscription" collapsed into the river; in the 50th year of Kangxi of the Qing (1711), five remnant stones were fished out of the river and moved into the temple. In 1960, a pavilion was built in the Baomo Studio garden, and according to the location verified by predecessors, the stones were embedded into the stone wall in the original cliff-carving style of that year.

highlights: 北固山北临长江由前峰中峰和后峰三部分组成前峰三面皆是悬崖地势险固山上多建亭台楼阁古迹众多有天下第一江山之誉甘露寺铁塔第七批国保2013年铁塔在后峰东部甘露寺长廊入口唐长庆四年824年11月19日长干寺发现佛舍利李德裕在甘露寺建石塔长庆五年825年瘗下唐大和三年829年正月二十四日禅众寺又出土佛舍利也葬在塔下唐乾符年间石塔倒塌北宋熙宁二年1069年在原址挖出李德裕所葬遗物由信徒焦巽出钱200万铸铁塔北宋熙宁九年1076年五月开工元丰元年1078年完工同时葬入一些宋代物品这座铁塔原有九级据康熙镇江府志记载明万历十一年1583年塔颓海啸可能在重建时减了两层因为在高从龙摹绘的甘露寺图和清代嘉庆道光年间画家张夕庵和周镐的册页中铁塔都只有七层19世纪末铁塔遭遇雷击塔刹被英军掠走1960年对塔基进行发掘出土了两千多件珍贵文物当时残存明代铸造的四五层塔身第四层从腰间折去一半上有两处残缺铭文今铁塔的莲花座和第一二层为宋代原构第三第四层为明代补铸铁塔残高约8米每层高约5尺直径约8尺塔身八面四面辟门上下相闪铸有佛像飞天犹存唐风檐口置斗栱柱头有卷杀都是宋代风格下部铁铸须弥座八面饰海水波浪纹上铸力士像及龙凤戏珠图第二层铸楷书国泰安宁法轮常转及僧人姓名第四层有中宪大夫等明代官名
projects.content_zh: 北固山北临长江，由前峰、中峰和后峰三部分组成，前峰三面皆是悬崖，地势险固，山上多建亭台楼阁，古迹众多，有"天下第一江山"之誉。1. 甘露寺铁塔：第七批国保（2013年）。铁塔在后峰东部甘露寺长廊入口。唐长庆四年（824年）11月19日，长干寺发现佛舍利，李德裕在甘露寺建石塔，长庆五年（825年）瘗下；唐大和三年（829年）正月二十四日禅众寺又出土佛舍利，也葬在塔下。唐乾符年间石塔倒塌，北宋熙宁二年（1069年）在原址挖出李德裕所葬遗物，由信徒焦巽出钱200万铸铁塔，北宋熙宁九年（1076年）五月开工，元丰元年（1078年）完工，同时葬入一些宋代物品。这座铁塔原有九级。据康熙《镇江府志》记载，明万历十一年（1583年）"塔颓海啸"，可能在重建时减了两层，因为在高从龙摹绘的《甘露寺图》和清代嘉庆、道光年间画家张夕庵和周镐的册页中，铁塔都只有七层。19世纪末铁塔遭遇雷击，塔刹被英军掠走。1960年对塔基进行发掘，出土了两千多件珍贵文物。当时残存明代铸造的四、五层塔身，第四层从腰间折去一半，上有两处残缺铭文。今铁塔的莲花座和第一、二层为宋代原构，第三、第四层为明代补铸。铁塔残高约8米，每层高约5尺，直径约8尺。塔身八面，四面辟门，上下相闪，铸有佛像飞天，犹存唐风。檐口置斗栱，柱头有卷杀，都是宋代风格。下部铁铸须弥座八面饰海水波浪纹，上铸力士像及龙凤戏珠图。第二层铸楷书"国泰安宁""法轮常转"及僧人姓名。第四层有"中宪大夫"等明代官名。
projects.content_en: Beigu Mountain faces the Yangtze River to the north, composed of three parts: front peak, middle peak, and rear peak; the front peak has cliffs on three sides, with a strategic and solid terrain; the mountain has many pavilions, terraces, and towers, with numerous historical sites, hailed as "the number one mountain and river under heaven." 1. Ganlu Temple Iron Pagoda: 7th Batch National Protected (2013). The iron pagoda is at the entrance of the Ganlu Temple corridor on the eastern part of the rear peak. On November 19, the 4th year of Changqing of the Tang (824), Buddha relics were discovered at Changgan Temple; Li Deyu built a stone pagoda at Ganlu Temple, burying them in the 5th year of Changqing (825); on January 24, the 3rd year of Dahe of the Tang (829), Buddha relics were unearthed again at Chanzhong Temple and also buried under the pagoda. The stone pagoda collapsed during the Qianfu reign of the Tang; in the 2nd year of Xining of the Northern Song (1069), the relics buried by Li Deyu were excavated at the original site, and believer Jiao Xun donated 2 million coins to cast an iron pagoda; construction began in May of the 9th year of Xining (1076) and was completed in the 1st year of Yuanfeng (1078), with some Song objects buried at the same time. This iron pagoda originally had nine stories. According to Kangxi's "Zhenjiang Prefecture Gazetteer," in the 11th year of Wanli of the Ming (1583) "the pagoda collapsed in a sea tsunami," and two stories may have been reduced during reconstruction, because in Gao Conglong's copied "Painting of Ganlu Temple" and in the albums of painters Zhang Xi'an and Zhou Gao during the Jiaqing and Daoguang reigns of the Qing, the iron pagoda has only seven stories. At the end of the 19th century, the iron pagoda was struck by lightning, and the pagoda finial was taken away by British troops. In 1960, the pagoda base was excavated, yielding over two thousand precious cultural relics. At that time, the fourth and fifth story bodies cast in the Ming remained, with the fourth story broken in half from the waist and two incomplete inscriptions on it. Today the lotus base and the first and second stories of the iron pagoda are original Song structures, while the third and fourth stories were recast in the Ming. The iron pagoda has a residual height of about 8 meters, each story about 5 chi high and about 8 chi in diameter. The pagoda body is octagonal, with doors opened on four sides, alternating up and down, cast with Buddha statues and flying apsaras, still retaining the Tang style. Bracket sets are placed at the eaves, and the column heads have entasis—both Song style. The lower iron-cast Sumeru base is decorated on eight sides with sea wave patterns, cast with guardian deity figures and dragon-phoenix playing-with-pearl designs. The second story is cast with regular script "National Peace and Tranquility," "Dharma Wheel Always Turning," and the names of monks. The fourth story has Ming official titles such as "Zhongxian Dafu" (Grand Master of Palace Rectitude).
