highlights: 金山是镇江三大名山之一高44米主要因山上的金山寺而驰誉天下建筑密度大有金山寺裹山之谚除金山寺外金山周围还有众多古迹如法海洞白龙洞和楞伽台等南侧笔架山上据传有郭璞衣冠冢现只剩巨石标志金山还有号称天下第一泉的中泠泉位于塔影湖中小岛上需乘船前往泉水今已干涸泉边石栏为20世纪50年代重修金山寺金山寺位于镇江西北长江南岸东晋时在江中小岛建寺称泽心寺佛教经忏法事中最隆重的水陆法会相传便起源于梁武帝时期的此寺传说唐代宰相裴休之子出家为僧法号法海在此开山得金大肆扩建寺院始称金山寺唐代已成为游览胜地白蛇传即以此为背景宋真宗曾梦游金山诏改寺名为龙游寺宋徽宗崇尚道教又改寺为道观称神霄玉清万寿宫宋代靖康之变后复称金山寺宋将韩世忠和虞允文曾先后在此据天险成功抵御金兵清代康熙南巡登金山见水天一色赐江天禅寺匾乾隆时期曾在金山寺文宗阁皮藏四库全书经过历代增修金山上殿阁密布从明代就有金山寺裹山之说太平天国期间寺庙毁于战火殿堂荡然无存文宗阁和藏书也付之一炬清同治十年1871年重修完毕清光绪二十六年1900年修复山北七层慈寿塔1948年又发生火灾寺内三百余间殿阁被焚仅存慈寿塔天王殿楞伽台观音阁和留云阁等处清光绪年间江水淤塞金山岛逐渐与陆地相连今寺中建筑多为70年代以后重修寺门朝西沿山西麓依次排列山门天王殿和大雄宝殿等留云山门建于民国初年上悬康熙御题江天禅寺匾山门外有牌坊坐东朝西为四柱三门式系民国初年用混凝土模板浇铸而成牌坊外有一对石狮天王殿始建于明正统年间清同治八年1869年重建大雄宝殿始建于明正统年间1948年毁于火灾1985年至1990年重建大雄宝殿后部山崖上为观音阁明永乐八年1410年郑和创建清同治年间重建今为寺内文物陈列室观音阁后部有近年重修的藏经阁慈寿塔位于金山西北角始建于南朝齐梁时期宋代曾立双塔明隆庆三年1569年在原北塔遗址重建改名慈寿塔清咸丰三年1853年毁于战火清光绪二十六年1900年复建新中国成立后将改木制栏杆改为钢筋混凝土结构文革期间遭破坏1989年塔身倾斜进行了扶正修缮山巅妙高峰有留云亭始建于宋清咸丰三年1853年毁于战火清同治十年1871年重建两江总督曾国荃将康熙手书江天一览四字石碑供享亭内改名江天一览亭文革时期石碑被毁1977年重新刻石金山寺藏有清代学者叶志诜赠送的周鼎传为苏东坡遗留的玉带镇江知府魁元赠送的铜鼓和明代画家文徵明所绘金山图四件珍贵文物并有宋佛顶尊胜陀罗尼经幢雪浪石和宋代名将宗泽画像等目前仅展示复制品
projects.content_zh: 金山是镇江三大名山之一，高44米，主要因山上的金山寺而驰誉天下，建筑密度大，有"金山寺裹山"之谚。除金山寺外，金山周围还有众多古迹，如法海洞、白龙洞和楞伽台等。南侧笔架山上据传有郭璞衣冠冢，现只剩巨石标志。金山还有号称"天下第一泉"的中泠泉，位于塔影湖中小岛上，需乘船前往，泉水今已干涸，泉边石栏为20世纪50年代重修。1. 金山寺：金山寺位于镇江西北长江南岸，东晋时在江中小岛建寺，称泽心寺。佛教经忏法事中最隆重的水陆法会，相传便起源于梁武帝时期的此寺。传说唐代宰相裴休之子出家为僧，法号法海，在此开山得金，大肆扩建寺院，始称金山寺，唐代已成为游览胜地，《白蛇传》即以此为背景。宋真宗曾梦游金山，诏改寺名为龙游寺；宋徽宗崇尚道教，又改寺为道观，称神霄玉清万寿宫；宋代靖康之变后复称金山寺。宋将韩世忠和虞允文曾先后在此据天险成功抵御金兵。清代康熙南巡登金山，见水天一色，赐"江天禅寺"匾。乾隆时期曾在金山寺文宗阁皮藏《四库全书》。经过历代增修，金山上殿阁密布，从明代就有"金山寺裹山"之说。太平天国期间寺庙毁于战火，殿堂荡然无存，文宗阁和藏书也付之一炬。清同治十年（1871年）重修完毕，清光绪二十六年（1900年）修复山北七层慈寿塔。1948年又发生火灾，寺内三百余间殿阁被焚，仅存慈寿塔、天王殿、楞伽台、观音阁和留云阁等处。清光绪年间江水淤塞，金山岛逐渐与陆地相连。今寺中建筑多为70年代以后重修，寺门朝西，沿山西麓依次排列山门、天王殿和大雄宝殿等。留云山门建于民国初年，上悬康熙御题"江天禅寺"匾。山门外有牌坊，坐东朝西，为四柱三门式，系民国初年用混凝土模板浇铸而成，牌坊外有一对石狮。天王殿始建于明正统年间，清同治八年（1869年）重建。大雄宝殿始建于明正统年间，1948年毁于火灾，1985年至1990年重建。大雄宝殿后部山崖上为观音阁，明永乐八年（1410年）郑和创建，清同治年间重建，今为寺内文物陈列室。观音阁后部有近年重修的藏经阁。慈寿塔位于金山西北角，始建于南朝齐梁时期，宋代曾立双塔，明隆庆三年（1569年）在原北塔遗址重建，改名慈寿塔。清咸丰三年（1853年）毁于战火，清光绪二十六年（1900年）复建。新中国成立后将改木制栏杆改为钢筋混凝土结构，"文革"期间遭破坏，1989年塔身倾斜，进行了扶正修缮。山巅妙高峰有留云亭，始建于宋，清咸丰三年（1853年）毁于战火，清同治十年（1871年）重建，两江总督曾国荃将康熙手书"江天一览"四字石碑供享亭内，改名江天一览亭。"文革"时期石碑被毁，1977年重新刻石。金山寺藏有清代学者叶志诜赠送的周鼎、传为苏东坡遗留的玉带、镇江知府魁元赠送的铜鼓和明代画家文徵明所绘《金山图》四件珍贵文物，并有宋佛顶尊胜陀罗尼经幢、雪浪石和宋代名将宗泽画像等，目前仅展示复制品。
projects.content_en: Jinshan (Gold Mountain) is one of the three famous mountains of Zhenjiang, 44 meters high, mainly renowned throughout the world for the Jinshan Temple on the mountain, with high building density, hence the proverb "Jinshan Temple wraps the mountain." Besides Jinshan Temple, there are numerous historical sites around Jinshan, such as Fahai Cave, White Dragon Cave, and Lengjia Terrace etc. On the southern Bijia (Pen Rack) Mountain, it is said there is Guo Pu's cenotaph, now only a giant stone marker remains. Jinshan also has the Zhongling Spring, known as "the number one spring under heaven," located on a small island in Taying Lake, requiring a boat to reach; the spring water has now dried up, and the stone railing by the spring was rebuilt in the 1950s. 1. Jinshan Temple: Jinshan Temple is located on the south bank of the Yangtze River northwest of Zhenjiang; in the Eastern Jin, a temple was built on a small island in the river, called Zexin Temple. The most solemn of Buddhist repentance ceremonies, the Water-Land Ceremony, is traditionally said to have originated at this temple during the reign of Emperor Wu of the Liang. Legend says the son of Tang Prime Minister Pei Xiu became a monk with the dharma name Fahai, who opened the mountain and found gold here, greatly expanding the temple, hence called Jinshan Temple; by the Tang it had become a tourist attraction, and the "Legend of the White Snake" takes this as its background. Emperor Zhenzong of the Song once dreamed of Jinshan and issued an edict to rename the temple Longyou Temple; Emperor Huizong of the Song, advocating Daoism, changed the temple into a Daoist temple, called the Shenxiao Yuqing Wanshou Palace; after the Jingkang Incident of the Song, it was again called Jinshan Temple. Song generals Han Shizhong and Yu Yunwen successively relied on the natural barrier here to successfully resist Jin troops. During the Qing, Kangxi's southern tour climbed Jinshan and, seeing the water and sky as one color, bestowed the plaque "Jiangtian Chan Temple." During the Qianlong reign, the "Complete Library in Four Sections" was stored in the Wenzong Pavilion of Jinshan Temple. Through successive dynasties' additions and repairs, Jinshan was densely covered with halls and pavilions, and from the Ming there was the saying "Jinshan Temple wraps the mountain." During the Taiping Rebellion the temple was destroyed by war fires, with halls completely gone, and the Wenzong Pavilion and its book collection were also burned to ashes. Repairs were completed in the 10th year of Tongzhi of the Qing (1871), and the seven-story Cishou (Longevity) Pagoda north of the mountain was restored in the 26th year of Guangxu (1900). Another fire broke out in 1948, burning over three hundred halls and pavilions in the temple, leaving only the Cishou Pagoda, Heavenly King Hall, Lengjia Terrace, Guanyin Pavilion, and Liuyun Pavilion etc. During the Guangxu reign of the Qing, the river silted up, and Jinshan Island gradually connected with the land. Today's temple buildings were mostly rebuilt after the 1970s, with the temple gate facing west, and the mountain gate, Heavenly King Hall, and Mahavira Hall etc. arranged in sequence along the western foot of the mountain. The Liuyun Mountain Gate was built in the early Republic, with Kangxi's imperial inscription "Jiangtian Chan Temple" plaque hanging above. Outside the mountain gate is an archway, facing west with its back to east, of four-column three-gate style, cast with concrete formwork in the early Republic, with a pair of stone lions outside the archway. The Heavenly King Hall was first built during the Zhengtong reign of the Ming, rebuilt in the 8th year of Tongzhi of the Qing (1869). The Mahavira Hall was first built during the Zhengtong reign of the Ming, destroyed by fire in 1948, and rebuilt from 1985 to 1990. On the cliff behind the Mahavira Hall is the Guanyin Pavilion, founded by Zheng He in the 8th year of Yongle of the Ming (1410), rebuilt during the Tongzhi reign of the Qing, today the temple's cultural relics exhibition room. Behind the Guanyin Pavilion is the recently restored Scripture Library. The Cishou Pagoda is located at the northwest corner of Jinshan, first built during the Qi-Liang period of the Southern Dynasties; twin pagodas were erected in the Song, and in the 3rd year of Longqing of the Ming (1569) it was rebuilt on the site of the original north pagoda, renamed Cishou Pagoda. Destroyed by war fires in the 3rd year of Xianfeng of the Qing (1853), it was rebuilt in the 26th year of Guangxu of the Qing (1900). After the founding of New China, the wooden railings were changed to reinforced concrete structures; damaged during the Cultural Revolution, in 1989 the pagoda body tilted and was straightened and repaired. At the mountain peak Miaogao Peak is the Liuyun (Remaining Cloud) Pavilion, first built in the Song, destroyed by war fires in the 3rd year of Xianfeng of the Qing (1853), rebuilt in the 10th year of Tongzhi of the Qing (1871); Zeng Guoquan, Viceroy of Liangjiang, placed a stone stele with Kangxi's handwritten four characters "Jiangtian Yilan" (River and Sky in One View) inside the pavilion, renaming it the Jiangtian Yilan Pavilion. The stele was destroyed during the Cultural Revolution, and re-carved in 1977. Jinshan Temple houses four precious cultural relics: the Zhou Ding (bronze vessel) donated by Qing scholar Ye Zhishen, the jade belt traditionally left by Su Dongpo, the bronze drum donated by Zhenjiang Prefect Kui Yuan, and the "Painting of Jinshan" by Ming painter Wen Zhengming; it also has the Song Buddha's Top Superior Victorious Dharani Pillar, Xuelang Stone, and a portrait of Song general Zong Ze etc., currently only displaying replicas.

highlights: 西津渡街又称观音洞一条街或小码头一条街东至大西路西至苏北路与小铁路交接处东西长484米宽3米此街原为沿山壁开辟的栈道下临长江后来在此设古渡口因靠近蒜山名蒜山渡六朝时称西津渡唐代称金陵渡元代成为交通命脉江浙闽海运货物由此达京师清代被誉为银码头一直是镇江南北驿道要冲上的主要渡口清道光以降长江主航道北移街区功能由渡口转变为区域商贸中心石板路上至今仍保留着深深的车辙印街上现存多处古迹包括元代昭关石塔清代观音洞救生会和待渡亭等其中昭关石塔为国保单位旧生会旧址为省保单位街道东端为五十三坡即东侧坡道上的53级台阶坡上街南有观音洞乃宋代借天然洞穴扩建成的庙宇今存清咸丰九年1859年依山重建的三层楼西侧渡口边有清同治七年1868年所建待渡亭云台山北麓有清末形成的传统民居街区镇江开埠后西津渡银山门一带被占为英租界现存英国领事馆美国领事馆英工部局大楼税务司公馆亚细亚火油公司和美孚火油公司等租界建筑昭关石塔第六批国保2006年昭关石塔立于观音洞和救生会之间是一座过街塔下部开圭形门洞类似城关门外是通往江北瓜州和江中金山的西津渡古渡口塔始建于元代为喇嘛塔形制明万历十年1582年重修塔基1959年1980年两次修整洞顶横额东西两面均刻昭关二字附会伍子胥逃离楚国时所过的昭关实际在今安徽省含山县过街塔发源于西藏地区中国始见于元代是藏传佛教的重要建筑类型昭关石塔与武汉胜像宝塔北京妙应寺白塔风格接近应为建于元代的噶当觉顿式喇嘛塔元代喇嘛塔塔身低相轮粗天盘宽称噶当觉顿式昭关石塔为典型代表明代中叶以后国内所建喇嘛塔塔身较高相轮较细天盘较小称为觉顿式昭关石塔下部是用青石砌筑的四根石柱南北洞口较低仅东西贯通行人柱顶有雕刻精美的石雀替上架石枋搭成平台地面至台顶高3.9米台上立喇嘛塔全用青石雕垒成高4.69米塔下部是两层的亚字形须弥座四角各形成五个转角上置莲花金刚座座上为覆钵形塔身其上又为亚字形平座上托周套重圈的圆锥形十三轮顶部是仰莲伞盖法轮和宝瓶形塔刹内置镇塔之宝佛镜等出石塔西门可望见渡口码头这段长江水道狭窄水流湍急常发生翻船溺水事件因而在此建塔保佑平安救生会第七批省保2011年救生会是古代救护各种船只和渡江人员的慈善机构清康熙四十二年1703年京口蒋元鼐朱用载蒋尚忠等十五人力劝邑中输钱救涉江覆舟者他们捐助白金若干在西津渡观音阁成立京口救生会康熙四十七年1708年救生会购得西津渡昭关晏公庙旧址建屋三间作为会址救生会南部临街为砖木结构二层楼房三开间坐北朝南为办公之所清光绪二十一年1895年在正门上门置办救生会石额其内为庭院院北建连廊和附属用房西南有角门出入整组建筑为清代风格保存完好京口救生会影响遍及大江南北江西湖北安徽各省纷纷效仿打造救生红船实施救助措施该会成立后持续活动长达200年之久在我国水上救生史以及古代民间慈善事业中均堪称奇迹
projects.content_zh: 西津渡街，又称观音洞一条街或小码头一条街，东至大西路，西至苏北路与小铁路交接处，东西长484米，宽3米。街道全天免费开放，观音洞和救生会需购票。此街原为沿山壁开辟的栈道，下临长江，后来在此设古渡口，因靠近蒜山，名蒜山渡。六朝时称西津渡，唐代称金陵渡，元代成为交通命脉，江浙闽海运货物由此达京师，清代被誉为银码头，一直是镇江南北驿道要冲上的主要渡口。清道光以降，长江主航道北移，街区功能由渡口转变为区域商贸中心。石板路上至今仍保留着深深的车辙印。街上现存多处古迹，包括元代昭关石塔，清代观音洞、救生会和待渡亭等。其中昭关石塔为国保单位，旧生会旧址为省保单位。街道东端为五十三坡，即东侧坡道上的53级台阶，坡上街南有观音洞，乃宋代借天然洞穴扩建成的庙宇，今存清咸丰九年（1859年）依山重建的三层楼。西侧渡口边有清同治七年（1868年）所建待渡亭。云台山北麓有清末形成的传统民居街区。镇江开埠后，西津渡银山门一带被占为英租界，现存英国领事馆、美国领事馆、英工部局大楼、税务司公馆、亚细亚火油公司和美孚火油公司等租界建筑。1. 昭关石塔：第六批国保（2006年）。昭关石塔立于观音洞和救生会之间，是一座过街塔，下部开圭形门洞，类似城关，门外是通往江北瓜州和江中金山的西津渡古渡口。塔始建于元代，为喇嘛塔形制，明万历十年（1582年）重修塔基，1959年、1980年两次修整。洞顶横额东西两面均刻"昭关"二字，附会伍子胥逃离楚国时所过的昭关（实际在今安徽省含山县）。过街塔发源于西藏地区，中国始见于元代，是藏传佛教的重要建筑类型。昭关石塔与武汉胜像宝塔、北京妙应寺白塔风格接近，应为建于元代的"噶当觉顿式"喇嘛塔。元代喇嘛塔塔身低，相轮粗，天盘宽，称"噶当觉顿式"，昭关石塔为典型代表。明代中叶以后国内所建喇嘛塔塔身较高，相轮较细，天盘较小，称为"觉顿式"。昭关石塔下部是用青石砌筑的四根石柱，南北洞口较低，仅东西贯通行人，柱顶有雕刻精美的石雀替，上架石枋搭成平台，地面至台顶高3.9米。台上立喇嘛塔，全用青石雕垒成，高4.69米。塔下部是两层的亚字形须弥座，四角各形成五个转角，上置莲花金刚座，座上为覆钵形塔身，其上又为亚字形平座，上托周套重圈的圆锥形"十三轮"，顶部是仰莲伞盖、法轮和宝瓶形塔刹，内置镇塔之宝佛镜等。出石塔西门可望见渡口码头，这段长江水道狭窄，水流湍急，常发生翻船溺水事件，因而在此建塔保佑平安。2. 救生会：第七批省保（2011年）。救生会是古代救护各种船只和渡江人员的慈善机构。清康熙四十二年（1703年），京口蒋元鼐、朱用载、蒋尚忠等十五人力劝"邑中输钱，救涉江覆舟者"。他们捐助白金若干，在西津渡观音阁成立"京口救生会"。康熙四十七年（1708年），救生会购得西津渡昭关晏公庙旧址，建屋三间作为会址。救生会南部临街为砖木结构二层楼房，三开间，坐北朝南，为办公之所。清光绪二十一年（1895年）在正门上置办"救生会"石额。其内为庭院，院北建连廊和附属用房，西南有角门出入。整组建筑为清代风格，保存完好。京口救生会影响遍及大江南北，江西、湖北、安徽各省纷纷效仿，打造救生红船，实施救助措施。该会成立后持续活动长达200年之久，在我国水上救生史以及古代民间慈善事业中均堪称奇迹。
projects.content_en: Xijindu Street, also called Guanyin Cave Street or Small Wharf Street, extends east to Daxi Road and west to the junction of Subei Road and the Small Railway, 484 meters long east-west and 3 meters wide. The street is open free all day; Guanyin Cave and the Rescue Society require tickets. This street was originally a plank road carved along the mountain cliff, overlooking the Yangtze River below; later an ancient ferry was established here, called Suanshan Ferry because it was near Suan Mountain. In the Six Dynasties it was called Xijin Ferry, in the Tang Jinling Ferry, and in the Yuan it became a transportation lifeline, with sea transport goods from Jiangsu, Zhejiang, and Fujian reaching the capital through here; in the Qing it was hailed as the Silver Wharf, always the main ferry on the key north-south post road of Zhenjiang. From the Daoguang reign of the Qing onward, the main channel of the Yangtze shifted north, and the district's function transformed from a ferry to a regional trade center. Deep wheel ruts are still preserved on the stone slab road today. Many historical sites exist on the street, including the Yuan Zhaoguan Stone Pagoda, and the Qing Guanyin Cave, Rescue Society, and Waiting-for-Ferry Pavilion etc. Among them, the Zhaoguan Stone Pagoda is a national protected unit, and the former Rescue Society site is a provincial protected unit. The east end of the street is the Fifty-Three Slope, i.e., the 53 stone steps on the east side ramp; south of the street on the slope is Guanyin Cave, a temple expanded from a natural cave in the Song, today preserving a three-story building rebuilt against the mountain in the 9th year of Xianfeng of the Qing (1859). By the ferry on the west side is the Waiting-for-Ferry Pavilion built in the 7th year of Tongzhi of the Qing (1868). At the northern foot of Yuntai Mountain is a traditional residential district formed in the late Qing. After Zhenjiang opened as a treaty port, the area around Yinshan Gate of Xijin Ferry was occupied as the British concession, today preserving concession buildings such as the British Consulate, American Consulate, British Municipal Council Building, Tax Commissioner's Residence, Asiatic Petroleum Company, and Standard Oil Company etc. 1. Zhaoguan Stone Pagoda: 6th Batch National Protected (2006). The Zhaoguan Stone Pagoda stands between Guanyin Cave and the Rescue Society; it is a street-crossing pagoda, with a guiform (sword-shaped) gate opening at the lower part, similar to a city gate; outside the gate is the ancient Xijin Ferry crossing leading to Guazhou north of the river and Jinshan in the river. The pagoda was first built in the Yuan, in the form of a Lamaist pagoda; its base was rebuilt in the 10th year of Wanli of the Ming (1582), and repaired twice in 1959 and 1980. The horizontal plaque above the cave opening is engraved with the two characters "Zhaoguan" on both east and west sides, associated with the Zhaoguan Pass that Wu Zixu passed when fleeing the State of Chu (actually in today's Hanshan County, Anhui Province). Street-crossing pagodas originated in Tibet and first appeared in China in the Yuan, an important architectural type of Tibetan Buddhism. The Zhaoguan Stone Pagoda is close in style to the Shengxiang Pagoda in Wuhan and the White Pagoda of Miaoying Temple in Beijing, and should be a "Kadam-Jokton-style" Lamaist pagoda built in the Yuan. Yuan Lamaist pagodas have a low body, thick harmika (ring of circles), and wide heaven disc, called "Kadam-Jokton style," with the Zhaoguan Stone Pagoda as a typical representative. After the mid-Ming, Lamaist pagodas built in China have a taller body, thinner harmika, and smaller heaven disc, called "Jokton style." The lower part of the Zhaoguan Stone Pagoda consists of four stone pillars built of bluestone; the north and south gate openings are low, only allowing pedestrians to pass east-west; the pillar tops have exquisitely carved stone spandrel brackets, with stone beams above forming a platform, 3.9 meters high from ground to platform top. On the platform stands the Lamaist pagoda, entirely carved and stacked from bluestone, 4.69 meters high. The lower part of the pagoda is a two-story ya-shaped (cross-shaped) Sumeru base, with five corners formed at each of the four corners; above it is a lotus vajra seat, on which is the overturned-bowl-shaped pagoda body, above which is another ya-shaped flat seat, supporting the conical "thirteen rings" wrapped with repeated circles; the top is an upward-lotus umbrella canopy, dharma wheel, and vase-shaped pagoda finial, with the pagoda-suppressing treasure Buddha mirror etc. placed inside. Exiting the west gate of the stone pagoda, one can see the ferry wharf; this section of the Yangtze waterway is narrow with rapid currents, and boat-capsizing and drowning incidents often occurred, hence a pagoda was built here to bless safety. 2. Rescue Society: 7th Batch Provincial Protected (2011). The Rescue Society was a charitable institution in ancient times for rescuing various boats and people crossing the river. In the 42nd year of Kangxi of the Qing (1703), fifteen people including Jiang Yuannai, Zhu Yongzai, and Jiang Shangzhong of Jingkou strongly urged "the county to contribute money to rescue those who capsize boats crossing the river." They donated several taels of platinum and established the "Jingkou Rescue Society" at the Guanyin Pavilion of Xijin Ferry. In the 47th year of Kangxi (1708), the Rescue Society purchased the former site of the Zhaoguan Yan Gong Temple at Xijin Ferry and built three rooms as its headquarters. The southern part of the Rescue Society facing the street is a two-story brick-wood building, three bays wide, facing south with its back to north, serving as office space. In the 21st year of Guangxu of the Qing (1895), a stone plaque "Rescue Society" was placed on the main gate. Inside is a courtyard, with a covered corridor and auxiliary rooms built north of the courtyard, and a corner gate for entry and exit in the southwest. The entire building complex is in Qing style and well preserved. The Jingkou Rescue Society's influence spread throughout the country, with provinces such as Jiangxi, Hubei, and Anhui following suit, building rescue red boats and implementing rescue measures. After its establishment, the society continued its activities for as long as 200 years, truly a miracle in the history of water rescue and ancient folk philanthropy in China.

highlights: 清同治元年1862年英国在镇江设立租界清同治三年1864年建领事馆清光绪十五年1889年因巡捕殴毙华人英人裁判不公激怒民众放火烧了领事馆和巡捕房清政府赔款4万两白银次年1890年用赔款重建原建筑群由5栋建筑组成分别为办公楼西北的员工宿舍南坡的正副领事官府邸和北面的工部局巡捕房均为砖木结构用青砖砌筑夹杂红砖装饰1933年售予江苏省民政厅长赵启騄现为镇江市博物馆办公大楼在最高处采用外廊式风格屋顶三角形山花中央刻有1890字样楼高三层沿台地布置首层仅有东侧一间北向开门二层为过厅和三个房间东侧券门额首两侧各嵌圆形花岗岩雕刻IR两字由过厅楼梯可至三层三层可从正门进入面积最大有8个房间五间带壁炉西侧过廊有地下室屋外以连廊通向辅助平房建筑采用木屋架瓦楞铁皮顶墙面以红砖为主用青砖砌出花纹券廊下的栏杆用宜兴产绿色琉璃瓷宝瓶室内地面先用砖做地垄上架密肋木梁再铺钉企口木地板楼板用密肋木梁上铺木地板天花及券廊用石膏抹面平顶四周做天花灯圈与线脚东面底层与二层券廊为砖砌弧形拱券天花二层底拱券廊天花用工字钢小梁上砌弧形砖拱券北侧云台山下是工部局巡捕房为东西向三层楼房用青砖砌筑红砖装饰南立面二三层有券廊底层为墙面开8个拱券窗办公楼南部东西两侧有两座三层小楼为正副领事住所东北方的白色二层楼房原为美国领事馆清光绪二十六年1900年美国领事馆迁往江宁今南京该建筑成为职员宿舍餐厅和娱乐房间东南两面有券廊现用玻璃封闭
projects.content_zh: 清同治元年（1862年）英国在镇江设立租界，清同治三年（1864年）建领事馆，清光绪十五年（1889年）因巡捕殴毙华人，英人裁判不公，激怒民众放火烧了领事馆和巡捕房。清政府赔款4万两白银，次年（1890年）用赔款重建。原建筑群由5栋建筑组成，分别为办公楼、西北的员工宿舍、南坡的正、副领事官府邸和北面的工部局巡捕房。均为砖木结构，用青砖砌筑，夹杂红砖装饰。1933年售予江苏省民政厅长赵启騄，现为镇江市博物馆。办公大楼在最高处，采用外廊式风格，屋顶三角形山花中央刻有"1890"字样。楼高三层，沿台地布置，首层仅有东侧一间，北向开门。二层为过厅和三个房间，东侧券门额首两侧各嵌圆形花岗岩，雕刻"IR"两字，由过厅楼梯可至三层。三层可从正门进入，面积最大，有8个房间，五间带壁炉，西侧过廊有地下室。屋外以连廊通向辅助平房。建筑采用木屋架、瓦楞铁皮顶，墙面以红砖为主，用青砖砌出花纹。券廊下的栏杆用宜兴产绿色琉璃瓷宝瓶。室内地面先用砖做地垄，上架密肋木梁，再铺钉企口木地板。楼板用密肋木梁，上铺木地板，天花及券廊用石膏抹面平顶，四周做天花灯圈与线脚。东面底层与二层券廊为砖砌弧形拱券天花，二层底拱券廊天花用工字钢小梁，上砌弧形砖拱券。北侧云台山下是工部局巡捕房，为东西向三层楼房，用青砖砌筑，红砖装饰。南立面二、三层有券廊，底层为墙面，开8个拱券窗。办公楼南部东西两侧有两座三层小楼，为正、副领事住所。东北方的白色二层楼房原为美国领事馆，清光绪二十六年（1900年）美国领事馆迁往江宁（今南京），该建筑成为职员宿舍、餐厅和娱乐房间，东南两面有券廊，现用玻璃封闭。
projects.content_en: In the 1st year of Tongzhi of the Qing (1862), Britain established a concession in Zhenjiang; in the 3rd year of Tongzhi (1864) the consulate was built; in the 15th year of Guangxu of the Qing (1889), because a patrolman beat a Chinese person to death and the British judged unfairly, the enraged people set fire to the consulate and police station. The Qing government paid 40,000 taels of silver in compensation, and the following year (1890) rebuilt it with the compensation. The original building complex consisted of 5 buildings: the office building, the staff dormitory to the northwest, the residences of the consul and vice-consul on the southern slope, and the Municipal Council police station to the north. All are brick-wood structures, built with grey bricks and interspersed with red brick decoration. In 1933 it was sold to Zhao Qilu, Director of the Civil Affairs Department of Jiangsu Province, and is now the Zhenjiang City Museum. The office building is at the highest point, adopting the veranda style, with the characters "1890" engraved in the center of the triangular gable of the roof. It is three stories high, arranged along the terrace; the first floor has only one room on the east side, with the door opening north. The second floor is a hallway and three rooms; on both sides of the arch door lintel on the east side are embedded round granites engraved with the two letters "IR"; from the hallway stairs one can reach the third floor. The third floor can be entered from the main gate, with the largest area, 8 rooms, 5 with fireplaces, and a basement in the west hallway. Outside, a covered corridor leads to auxiliary bungalows. The building uses wooden roof trusses and corrugated iron roofs; the walls are mainly red brick, with patterns laid in grey brick. The railings under the veranda use green glazed porcelain vases produced in Yixing. The indoor floor first uses bricks to make floor joists, with dense ribbed wooden beams above, then nailed tongue-and-groove wooden flooring. The floor slabs use dense ribbed wooden beams with wooden flooring above; the ceilings and verandas use plastered flat ceilings, with ceiling lamp rings and moldings around. The east ground and second-floor verandas have brick-built arched vaulted ceilings; the second-floor bottom veranda ceiling uses I-beam small girders with arched brick vaults above. North of Yuntai Mountain below is the Municipal Council police station, an east-west three-story building, built with grey bricks and decorated with red bricks. The south facade has verandas on the second and third floors, with the ground floor as a wall with 8 arched windows. On the east and west sides south of the office building are two three-story small buildings, the residences of the consul and vice-consul. The white two-story building to the northeast was originally the American Consulate; in the 26th year of Guangxu of the Qing (1900) the American Consulate moved to Jiangning (today's Nanjing), and this building became staff dormitory, dining room, and entertainment rooms, with verandas on the southeast sides, now enclosed with glass.

projects.name: 伯先路近代建筑群
projects.name_en: Modern Building Complex on Boxian Road
projects.level: 含广肇公所（第七批省保2011年）、镇江商会旧址（第六批省保2006年）、五卅演讲厅（第三批省保1982年）
projects.level_en: Including Guangzhao Guild Hall (7th Batch Provincial 2011), Former Zhenjiang Chamber of Commerce (6th Batch Provincial 2006), May 30th Lecture Hall (3rd Batch Provincial 1982)
projects.address: 润州区伯先路延伸至京畿路
projects.address_en: Boxian Road extending to Jingji Road, Runzhou District
highlights: 伯先路近代建筑群从润州区伯先路延伸至京畿路保存有大量晚清民国建筑类型多样质量上乘主要建筑有广肇公所浸礼会教堂镇江商会怀仁诊所屠家骅公馆内地会教堂镇江老邮政局世界红字会江苏省会定福寺旧址和伯先公园等广肇公所第七批省保2011年广肇公所是广东肇庆地区来镇江经商的同乡会所原在运粮河旁中华路菜场南清光绪三十三年1907年由卓翼堂主持在现址重建公所坐东朝西面积约600余平方米内有厅房正房偏房和厢房20多间厅南厢房内壁嵌广肇公所记碑记载公所历史及重建始末大门用磨砖砌成上有挑檐装饰五福盘寿砖雕白石横额镌刻广肇公所四字落款为前护川督陈橘书门上有福禄寿三星琴棋书画和渔樵耕读等砖雕装饰大门两侧磨砖倚柱底部有石刻蝙蝠纹样等镇江商会旧址第六批省保2006年镇江商会旧址现为镇江市工商业联合会1929年北伐军归还镇江工商联借款20万银圆实业家陆小波18821973等用其中4万元建造商会建筑为砖木结构青砖建造共三进院落外立面有中华巴洛克式门楼内部院落为中式风格正门朝南朝东另建一座大门楼两座门楼都用方砖柱砌出西式牌楼南门较为正式入口有砖砌罗马式拱券叠涩门上嵌于右任题写的镇江商会白石横额门内共有三进第一进院北为大厅宽三间南面采用中式槅扇门两侧为厢房第二进后部为二层楼第三进由东大门进入为三层楼房有走廊与第二进相连屋顶用平瓦坡度较缓五卅演讲厅第三批省保1982年位于伯先路18号伯先公园内
projects.content_zh: 伯先路近代建筑群从润州区伯先路延伸至京畿路，保存有大量晚清、民国建筑，类型多样，质量上乘。主要建筑有广肇公所、浸礼会教堂、镇江商会、怀仁诊所、屠家骅公馆、内地会教堂、镇江老邮政局、世界红字会江苏省会、定福寺旧址和伯先公园等。1. 广肇公所：第七批省保（2011年）。广肇公所是广东肇庆地区来镇江经商的同乡会所。原在运粮河旁中华路菜场南，清光绪三十三年（1907年）由卓翼堂主持在现址重建。公所坐东朝西，面积约600余平方米，内有厅房、正房、偏房和厢房20多间。厅南厢房内壁嵌"广肇公所记"碑，记载公所历史及重建始末。大门用磨砖砌成，上有挑檐，装饰"五福盘寿"砖雕，白石横额镌刻"广肇公所"四字，落款为"前护川督陈橘书"。门上有"福禄寿"三星，"琴棋书画"和"渔樵耕读"等砖雕装饰，大门两侧磨砖倚柱底部有石刻蝙蝠纹样等。2. 镇江商会旧址：第六批省保（2006年）。镇江商会旧址现为镇江市工商业联合会。1929年北伐军归还镇江工商联借款20万银圆，实业家陆小波（1882—1973）等用其中4万元建造商会。建筑为砖木结构，青砖建造，共三进院落，外立面有中华巴洛克式门楼，内部院落为中式风格。正门朝南，迎街朝东另建一座大门楼，两座门楼都用方砖柱砌出西式牌楼，南门较为正式，入口有砖砌罗马式拱券叠涩，门上嵌于右任题写的"镇江商会"白石横额。门内共有三进，第一进院北为大厅，宽三间，南面采用中式槅扇门，两侧为厢房；第二进后部为二层楼，第三进由东大门进入，为三层楼房，有走廊与第二进相连。屋顶用平瓦，坡度较缓。3. 五卅演讲厅：第三批省保（1982年），位于伯先路18号伯先公园内。
projects.content_en: The Modern Building Complex on Boxian Road extends from Boxian Road to Jingji Road in Runzhou District, preserving a large number of late Qing and Republic buildings, diverse in type and high in quality. The main buildings include the Guangzhao Guild Hall, Baptist Church, Zhenjiang Chamber of Commerce, Huairen Clinic, Tu Jiahua Mansion, China Inland Mission Church, Old Zhenjiang Post Office, World Red Swastika Society Jiangsu Provincial Association, former site of Dingfu Temple, and Boxian Park etc. 1. Guangzhao Guild Hall: 7th Batch Provincial Protected (2011). The Guangzhao Guild Hall was a fellow-townsmen's club for merchants from Zhaoqing area of Guangdong who came to do business in Zhenjiang. Originally located south of the Zhonghua Road vegetable market beside the grain transport river, in the 33rd year of Guangxu of the Qing (1907) it was rebuilt at the current site under the direction of Zhuo Yitang. The guild hall faces west with its back to east, with an area of about 600 square meters, containing over 20 rooms including halls, main rooms, side rooms, and wing rooms. On the inner wall of the south wing room of the hall is embedded the "Record of the Guangzhao Guild Hall" stele, recording the history of the guild hall and the process of its reconstruction. The main gate is built of ground bricks, with overhanging eaves above, decorated with "Five Blessings Surrounding Longevity" brick carvings; the white stone horizontal plaque is engraved with the four characters "Guangzhao Guild Hall," with the signature "Written by Chen Ju, former acting Governor of Sichuan." On the gate are brick-carving decorations such as the "Fu Lu Shou" (Fortune, Prosperity, Longevity) Three Stars, "Qin Qi Shu Hua" (Lute, Chess, Calligraphy, Painting), and "Yu Qiao Geng Du" (Fisherman, Woodcutter, Farmer, Scholar) etc.; at the bottom of the ground-brick pilasters on both sides of the main gate are stone-carved bat patterns etc. 2. Former Zhenjiang Chamber of Commerce: 6th Batch Provincial Protected (2006). The former Zhenjiang Chamber of Commerce is now the Zhenjiang City Federation of Industry and Commerce. In 1929, the Northern Expeditionary Army repaid the 200,000 silver dollars borrowed by the Zhenjiang Federation of Industry and Commerce; industrialist Lu Xiaobo (1882-1973) etc. used 40,000 yuan of it to build the chamber. The building is brick-wood structure, built with grey bricks, with a total of three courtyards; the exterior facade has a Chinese-Baroque style gate tower, and the internal courtyards are in Chinese style. The main gate faces south, and another large gate tower was built facing east toward the street; both gate towers use square brick columns to build Western-style archways; the south gate is more formal, with a brick Roman-style arch corbel entrance, and a white stone horizontal plaque with "Zhenjiang Chamber of Commerce" inscribed by Yu Youren embedded on the gate. Inside the gate there are three courtyards in total: the north of the first courtyard is a main hall, three bays wide, with Chinese lattice doors on the south side and wing rooms on both sides; the rear of the second courtyard is a two-story building; the third courtyard, entered from the east main gate, is a three-story building with a corridor connecting to the second courtyard. The roof uses flat tiles with a relatively gentle slope. 3. May 30th Lecture Hall: 3rd Batch Provincial Protected (1982), located inside Boxian Park at No. 18 Boxian Road.

projects.name: 山巷清真寺
projects.level: 第七批省级文物保护单位（2011年）
projects.level_en: 7th Batch Provincial Cultural Heritage Site (2011)
projects.address_en: No. 84 Mosque Street, west of Zhenjiang city
highlights: 山巷清真寺又称城西清真寺或西大寺因位于山巷东侧故名山巷清真寺初建时仅有三间茅舍清康熙年间扩建咸丰三年1853年毁于兵燹同治十二年1873年重建后由穆斯林信众集资光绪二十八年1902年大规模扩建文革前期被学校占用文革中期遭到破坏1982年市政府拨款修缮这是江苏省现存规模最大的清真寺之一也是全国三大伊斯兰印经处之一山巷清真寺坐东朝西占地三亩左右有门楼前天井大殿南讲堂对厅和望月楼围以条石基础的青砖围墙寺门对面有照壁门宽三间深两间中部有斗栱装饰门内经天井有宽三间的过廊折向西为第二道门两旁立雕花石鼓入门经巷道折向北有第三道门门内为主庭院庭院南侧是院门和游廊东侧为信一堂北侧为讲堂望月楼位于庭院东北角是一座两层六角攒尖顶小楼下部与庭院连为一体庭院西侧是礼拜殿由窑殿正殿和辅殿备殿组成殿前出卷棚前廊前后殿相连均为硬山式西边两角挑出长檐檐角翘起后部正中向西又伸出一间歇山式屋顶外部为半亭阁式墙身大殿正面用隔扇门宽深皆为五间内有52根圆木立柱梁上彩绘华丽精细殿内悬挂多块匾额西墙正中砌米哈拉布凹龛右首有红漆敏拜尔宣讲台两侧开明窗采光极佳使祭坛和讲坛显得格外明亮
projects.content_zh: 山巷清真寺又称"城西清真寺"或"西大寺"，因位于山巷东侧，故名"山巷清真寺"。初建时仅有三间茅舍，清康熙年间扩建，咸丰三年（1853年）毁于兵燹，同治十二年（1873年）重建。后由穆斯林信众集资，光绪二十八年（1902年）大规模扩建，"文革"前期被学校占用，"文革"中期遭到破坏，1982年市政府拨款修缮。这是江苏省现存规模最大的清真寺之一，也是全国三大伊斯兰印经处之一。山巷清真寺坐东朝西，占地三亩左右，有门楼、前厅、天井、大殿、南讲堂、对厅和望月楼，围以条石基础的青砖围墙。寺门对面有照壁，门宽三间，深两间，中部有斗栱装饰。门内经天井有宽三间的过廊，折向西为第二道门，两旁立雕花石鼓；入门经巷道折向北有第三道门，门内为主庭院。庭院南侧是院门和游廊，东侧为信一堂，北侧为讲堂，望月楼位于庭院东北角，是一座两层六角攒尖顶小楼，下部与庭院连为一体。庭院西侧是礼拜殿，由窑殿、正殿和辅殿（备殿）组成。殿前出卷棚前廊，前后殿相连，均为硬山式，西边两角挑出长檐，檐角翘起，后部正中向西又伸出一间，歇山式屋顶，外部为半亭阁式墙身。大殿正面用隔扇门，宽、深皆为五间，内有52根圆木立柱，梁上彩绘华丽精细。殿内悬挂多块匾额，西墙正中砌"米哈拉布"（凹龛），右首有红漆"敏拜尔"（宣讲台），两侧开明窗，采光极佳，使祭坛和讲坛显得格外明亮。
projects.content_en: Shanxiang Mosque, also called "West City Mosque" or "West Great Mosque," is named "Shanxiang Mosque" because it is located on the east side of Shanxiang Lane. When first built it had only three thatched rooms; it was expanded during the Kangxi reign of the Qing, destroyed by war fires in the 3rd year of Xianfeng (1853), and rebuilt in the 12th year of Tongzhi (1873). Later, with funds raised by Muslim believers, it was greatly expanded in the 28th year of Guangxu (1902); in the early Cultural Revolution it was occupied by a school, and in the mid-Cultural Revolution it was damaged; in 1982 the municipal government allocated funds for repair. This is one of the largest existing mosques in Jiangsu Province and one of the three major Islamic scripture-printing establishments in China. Shanxiang Mosque faces west with its back to east, covering about three mu, with a gate tower, front hall, courtyard, main hall, south lecture hall, opposite hall, and moon-watching tower, enclosed by a grey-brick wall on a strip-stone foundation. Opposite the temple gate is a screen wall; the gate is three bays wide and two bays deep, with bracket decoration in the middle. Inside the gate, through the courtyard, is a three-bay-wide corridor; turning west is the second gate, with carved stone drums on both sides; entering through a lane and turning north is the third gate, inside which is the main courtyard. South of the courtyard are the courtyard gate and covered corridor; east is the Xinyi Hall; north is the lecture hall; the moon-watching tower is at the northeast corner of the courtyard, a two-story hexagonal pyramidal-roof small building, with its lower part integrated with the courtyard. West of the courtyard is the prayer hall, composed of the mihrab hall, main hall, and auxiliary hall (reserve hall). In front of the hall is a rolling-roof front porch; the front and rear halls are connected, both of yingshan (gable) style; the two western corners project long eaves with upturned corners; at the rear center, extending westward, is another room with a xieshan (hip-and-gable) roof, externally a semi-pavilion wall body. The front of the main hall uses lattice doors, five bays wide and five bays deep, with 52 round wooden columns inside, and the beams are painted with ornate and delicate colors. Many plaques hang inside the hall; in the center of the west wall is built the "mihrab" (recessed niche), and on the right is the red-lacquered "minbar" (preaching platform); bright windows on both sides provide excellent lighting, making the altar and pulpit appear especially bright.

projects.name: 赛珍珠故居
projects.level: 第五批省级文物保护单位（2002年）
projects.level_en: 5th Batch Provincial Cultural Heritage Site (2002)
projects.address_en: Building B, No. 6 Runzhou Shan Road, Runzhou District
highlights: 美国著名作家赛珍珠Pearl Sydenstricker Buck18921973曾经在中国长期生活以中国为背景的长篇小说大地先后获得普利策文学奖和诺贝尔文学奖赛珍珠的父亲赛兆祥为美国南长老会传教士她出生四个月就随父母来到中国在镇江生活到18岁赛珍珠故居建于清光绪中期为青砖砌筑的二层西式楼房可能由美国南长老会传教士设计建造占地259平方米正立面朝南向前伸出一间凸字形两层外廊上层用玻璃封闭下为门廊入门迎面为木楼梯可登至二楼走廊两旁各有大小三个房间上下基本相似为会客室和卧室室内均铺木地板石灰抹面平顶天花原有四座壁炉东西两侧用长方形直高窗顶部平梁上砌券拱装饰东立面地势较低砌有地下室北立面上下均用连续高窗屋顶原为瓦楞铁皮今已改为平瓦故居现对外开放展览赛珍珠的著作物资料和镇江与外国友好交流的展品
projects.content_zh: 美国著名作家赛珍珠（Pearl Sydenstricker Buck，1892—1973）曾经在中国长期生活，以中国为背景的长篇小说《大地》先后获得普利策文学奖和诺贝尔文学奖。赛珍珠的父亲赛兆祥为美国南长老会传教士，她出生四个月就随父母来到中国，在镇江生活到18岁。赛珍珠故居建于清光绪中期，为青砖砌筑的二层西式楼房，可能由美国南长老会传教士设计建造，占地259平方米。正立面朝南，向前伸出一间"凸"字形两层外廊，上层用玻璃封闭，下为门廊。入门迎面为木楼梯，可登至二楼。走廊两旁各有大小三个房间，上下基本相似，为会客室和卧室。室内均铺木地板，石灰抹面平顶天花，原有四座壁炉。东西两侧用长方形直高窗，顶部平梁上砌券拱装饰。东立面地势较低，砌有地下室，北立面上下均用连续高窗。屋顶原为瓦楞铁皮，今已改为平瓦。故居现对外开放，展览赛珍珠的著作、物品、资料和镇江与外国友好交流的展品。
projects.content_en: The famous American writer Pearl Buck (Pearl Sydenstricker Buck, 1892-1973) lived in China for a long time; her novel "The Good Earth," set in China, successively won the Pulitzer Prize for Literature and the Nobel Prize in Literature. Pearl Buck's father, Absalom Sydenstricker, was a missionary of the American Southern Presbyterian Church; she came to China with her parents at four months old and lived in Zhenjiang until she was 18. The former residence of Pearl Buck was built in the mid-Guangxu reign of the Qing, a two-story Western-style building of grey brick, possibly designed and built by missionaries of the American Southern Presbyterian Church, covering 259 square meters. The main facade faces south, projecting forward a "convex"-shaped two-story veranda; the upper story is enclosed with glass, and the lower is a porch. Entering the gate, facing you is a wooden staircase leading to the second floor. On both sides of the corridor are three rooms of various sizes each, basically similar upstairs and downstairs, serving as reception rooms and bedrooms. The interiors are all paved with wooden floors, with plastered flat ceilings, and originally had four fireplaces. The east and west sides use rectangular tall straight windows, with arch vault decorations built on the top flat beams. The east facade has lower terrain, with a basement built; the north facade uses continuous tall windows both upstairs and downstairs. The roof was originally corrugated iron, now changed to flat tiles. The former residence is now open to the public, exhibiting Pearl Buck's works, objects, materials, and exhibits of friendly exchanges between Zhenjiang and foreign countries.

projects.name: 南山
projects.level: 含招隐寺、竹林寺、鹤林寺、赵伯先墓

projects.content_zh: 南山景区内重峦叠翠，茂林修竹，被北宋书画家米芾誉为"城市山林"，其中主要名胜为鹤林、竹林和招隐三座古寺。鹤林寺和竹林寺皆创建于东晋，招隐寺建于南朝宋。南山景区屡有兴废，太平天国和抗日战争时期遭遇战火，"文革"前后也受到毁坏，今大部分殿宇为毁后重建。1. 招隐寺：招隐寺在南郊招隐山中，据传戴颙曾在山中隐居，后来其女舍宅为寺，称招隐寺。南朝宋时金山寺高僧普慈住持该寺，曾以其法号作为寺名。南朝梁时萧统在此读书。明万历二十六年（1598年），为与鹤林寺呼应，改名鹿泉寺。清咸丰年间毁于战火，同治、光绪时期相继重建，1923年在今址复建，抗日期间被毁，新中国成立前被国民党军队占驻，"文革"又遭破坏。目前景点多为1980年以后陆续复建，有招隐坊、听鹂山房、虎跑泉、鹿跑泉、玉蕊亭、珍珠泉和鸟外亭等。2. 竹林寺：竹林寺在夹山北麓。始建于东晋，初名夹山禅院，唐代曾作为鹤林寺下院，后圮废。明崇祯年间（1635年前后）重建，独立成寺，因四周修竹环抱，改名竹林寺。清康熙三十八年（1699年）康熙帝南巡时曾在此驻跸，亲题寺匾。清雍正十一年（1733年）诏令重建，规模宏大，为其鼎盛时期。清咸丰六年（1856年）毁于战火，清咸丰八年（1858年）建后又毁，同治三年（1864年）重建，但规模已不如前。抗日战争时期部分被日军烧毁，"文革"中破坏殆尽。1981年部分修复，主要景点有林公泉和挹江亭等。3. 鹤林寺：鹤林寺在南郊磨笄山北麓，始建于东晋，初名竹林寺。传说南朝宋开国皇帝刘裕年轻时常在寺内劳作休息，时有黄鹤飞舞其上，他即位后改名为鹤林寺。南宋绍兴年间重建，咸淳年间迁至山南，明永乐十年（1412年）又毁，僧人就原古竹院稍加修缮为寺，即今址。明弘治八年（1495年）和万历二十四年（1596年）、清康熙四年（1665年）多次重建，清咸丰年间毁于战火，"文革"时期破坏严重，景致大多湮没，今存杜鹃花、杜鹃楼和米芾墓等。4. 赵伯先墓：赵伯先墓在竹林寺东侧文苑景区。赵声（1881—1911）字伯先，镇江大港人，同盟会主要领导人之一。1912年葬在镇江南郊，墓碑刻"大烈士赵伯先之墓"。后来又在墓道前方丘地上树赵声戎装骑马画像石碑亭一座，与坟包、墓道构成中轴线。抗日战争前曾扩建陵墓，因战争爆发中止。1966年陵墓被破坏，1981年重树"辛亥烈士赵声伯先之墓"碑，除石像外，基本恢复原貌。陵墓长330米，宽90米，坟包建在圆形台基上，前列石供桌，有凭吊场地、墓道和石牌坊，坊额篆刻"浩气长存"四字。牌坊前有3座小石拱桥。
projects.content_en: In the Nanshan (South Mountain) scenic area, layered peaks are covered in green, with dense forests and tall bamboo, hailed by Northern Song calligrapher-painter Mi Fu as "urban mountain forest"; the main scenic spots are the three ancient temples of Helin, Zhulin, and Zhaoyin. Both Helin Temple and Zhulin Temple were founded in the Eastern Jin, and Zhaoyin Temple was built in the Liu Song of the Southern Dynasties. The Nanshan scenic area has repeatedly risen and fallen; it suffered war fires during the Taiping Rebellion and the War of Resistance against Japan, and was also damaged before and after the Cultural Revolution; today most halls were rebuilt after destruction. 1. Zhaoyin Temple: Zhaoyin Temple is in Zhaoyin Mountain in the southern suburbs; legend says Dai Yong once lived in seclusion in the mountain, and later his daughter donated her residence as a temple, called Zhaoyin Temple. In the Liu Song of the Southern Dynasties, the eminent monk Puci of Jinshan Temple served as abbot of this temple, and it was once named after his dharma name. In the Liang of the Southern Dynasties, Xiao Tong studied here. In the 26th year of Wanli of the Ming (1598), to echo Helin Temple, it was renamed Luquan Temple. Destroyed by war fires during the Xianfeng reign of the Qing, it was successively rebuilt during the Tongzhi and Guangxu periods, rebuilt at the current site in 1923, destroyed during the War of Resistance against Japan, occupied by Kuomintang troops before the founding of New China, and damaged again during the Cultural Revolution. Currently most scenic spots were successively rebuilt after 1980, including Zhaoyin Archway, Tingli (Listening to Orioles) Mountain Room, Hupao (Tiger Running) Spring, Lupao (Deer Running) Spring, Yurui (Jade Stamen) Pavilion, Pearl Spring, and Niaowai (Beyond Birds) Pavilion etc. 2. Zhulin Temple: Zhulin Temple is at the northern foot of Jia Mountain. First built in the Eastern Jin, originally named Jiashan Chan Courtyard; in the Tang it served as a sub-temple of Helin Temple, later fell into ruin. Rebuilt during the Chongzhen reign of the Ming (around 1635), becoming an independent temple, renamed Zhulin (Bamboo Forest) Temple because surrounded by tall bamboo. In the 38th year of Kangxi of the Qing (1699), during his southern tour, Emperor Kangxi stayed here and personally inscribed the temple plaque. In the 11th year of Yongzheng of the Qing (1733), an imperial edict ordered its reconstruction, with a grand scale, marking its heyday. Destroyed by war fires in the 6th year of Xianfeng of the Qing (1856), rebuilt in the 8th year of Xianfeng (1858) then destroyed again, rebuilt in the 3rd year of Tongzhi (1864), but the scale was no longer as before. During the War of Resistance against Japan, part was burned by Japanese troops, and during the Cultural Revolution it was completely destroyed. Partially restored in 1981, the main scenic spots include Lingong Spring and Yijiang (Embracing the River) Pavilion etc. 3. Helin Temple: Helin Temple is at the northern foot of Moji Mountain in the southern suburbs, first built in the Eastern Jin, originally named Zhulin Temple. Legend says Liu Yu, the founding emperor of the Liu Song of the Southern Dynasties, often worked and rested in the temple when young, with yellow cranes flying above it; after he ascended the throne, he renamed it Helin (Crane Forest) Temple. Rebuilt during the Shaoxing reign of the Southern Song, moved to the south of the mountain during the Xianchun reign; destroyed again in the 10th year of Yongle of the Ming (1412), and monks slightly repaired the original Ancient Bamboo Courtyard as a temple, i.e., today's site. Rebuilt multiple times in the 8th year of Hongzhi of the Ming (1495), the 24th year of Wanli (1596), and the 4th year of Kangxi of the Qing (1665); destroyed by war fires during the Xianfeng reign of the Qing, severely damaged during the Cultural Revolution, with most scenes lost; today surviving are azaleas, Azalea Tower, and Mi Fu's Tomb etc. 4. Zhao Boxian Tomb: Zhao Boxian Tomb is in the Wenyuan scenic area east of Zhulin Temple. Zhao Sheng (1881-1911), courtesy name Boxian, a native of Dagang, Zhenjiang, was one of the main leaders of the Tongmenghui (Chinese Revolutionary Alliance). Buried in the southern suburbs of Zhenjiang in 1912, with the tombstone engraved "Tomb of the Great Martyr Zhao Boxian." Later, a stone stele pavilion with a portrait of Zhao Sheng in military uniform riding a horse was erected on the mound in front of the tomb path, forming a central axis with the grave mound and tomb path. Before the War of Resistance against Japan, the tomb was once expanded, but stopped due to the outbreak of war. The tomb was destroyed in 1966, and in 1981 the stele "Tomb of Zhao Sheng (Boxian), Martyr of the 1911 Revolution" was re-erected; except for the stone statues, it basically restored its original appearance. The tomb is 330 meters long and 90 meters wide; the grave mound is built on a circular platform base, with a stone altar table in front, a mourning ground, tomb path, and stone archway; the archway plaque is engraved with the four characters "Noble Spirit Endures Forever." In front of the archway are 3 small stone arch bridges.

projects.content_zh: 丹阳在南朝时期称"南兰陵"，为齐、梁两代帝王的祖籍地，两代帝王多归葬于此，丹阳有帝陵11处，句容有1处（详见列表），墓前布置精美石刻。石刻中以陵口二石兽最雄伟，是一对麒麟和天禄。东为天禄，双角，四足损缺，长4米，残高3.6米；西为麒麟，独角，四足残损，身长3.95米，残高2.9米。两只石兽精雕细刻，纹饰华丽，两翼造型巧丽，翼上鳞纹凸出翼面，是体型最大、最为秀美的一对石刻。诸陵中保存石刻最多的是梁文帝萧顺的建陵，现存石兽、石柱础、石柱和石龟跌各一对。其他石刻还有齐宣帝萧承之永安陵、齐武帝萧赜景安陵各存石麒麟、天禄一对，均为东侧完整天禄，永安陵西侧麒麟失去头部，景安陵失去四足。齐景帝萧道生修安陵尚存麒麟、天禄一对。齐明帝萧鸾兴安陵有石麒麟、天禄一对，北为天禄，肢体残断，半身湮没于土中，仅存部分前躯；南为麒麟，四足全失。金王陈南齐失名墓有麒麟、天禄一对。烂石弄南齐失名墓有石辟邪一对，一完整，一残缺。水经山南齐失名墓有石辟邪一对，这两个墓的主人可能为废帝。梁武帝萧衍修陵有一石麒麟，已残。梁简文帝萧纲庄陵有一麒麟。句容的梁南康简王萧绩墓存有一对石辟邪，西雌东雄，东西相向而立一对石柱，东石柱完好无损，西石柱上的小辟邪遭雷击破损。丹阳、句容南朝陵墓石刻一览表（参考梁白泉《南京的六朝石刻》）：1. 齐宣帝萧承之永安陵石刻（447年），丹阳市东北胡桥镇狮子湾张庄村东北水田里，石麒麟、天禄各一；2. 齐武帝萧赜景安陵石刻（493年），丹阳市云阳镇田家村南400米处，石麒麟、天禄各一，石柱一；3. 齐景帝萧道生修安陵石刻（494年），丹阳市胡桥镇仙塘湾（又称鹤仙塘）以东约一公里，石麒麟、天禄各一；4. 齐明帝萧鸾兴安陵石刻（498年），丹阳市城东荆林镇三城巷东北，石麒麟、天禄各一；5. 金王陈南齐失名陵墓石刻（南朝齐），丹阳市后巷镇陈家村西南，石麒麟、天禄各一；6. 烂石弄南朝失名墓石刻（494年），丹阳市后巷镇烂石弄北，石辟邪二；7. 水经山村南朝失名墓石刻（494年），丹阳市埤城水经山村东南，石辟邪二；8. 齐梁陵口陵墓石刻（南朝），丹阳市陵口镇东，石麒麟、天禄各一；9. 梁文帝萧顺之建陵石刻（502年），丹阳市城东荆林镇三城巷东北，石麒麟、天禄各一，石柱二，石碑座二，石台基二；10. 梁武帝萧衍修陵石刻（549年），丹阳市城东荆林镇三城刘家庄，石天禄一；11. 梁简文帝萧纲庄陵石刻（551年），丹阳市城东荆林镇三城刘家庄，石天禄一；12. 梁南康简王萧绩墓石刻（566年），栖霞区栖霞镇新合村狮子冲，石辟邪二，石柱二。
projects.content_en: Danyang was called "Southern Lanling" during the Southern Dynasties, the ancestral home of the emperors of the Qi and Liang dynasties; emperors of both dynasties were mostly buried here, with 11 imperial tombs in Danyang and 1 in Jurong (see list for details), with exquisite stone carvings arranged in front of the tombs. Among the stone carvings, the two stone beasts at Lingkou are the most majestic—a pair of qilin and tianlu. The east one is a tianlu, with double horns, four feet damaged, 4 meters long, with a residual height of 3.6 meters; the west one is a qilin, with a single horn, four feet damaged, 3.95 meters long, with a residual height of 2.9 meters. The two stone beasts are exquisitely carved with ornate patterns, with cleverly shaped wings, and the scale patterns on the wings protrude from the wing surface—they are the largest and most graceful pair of stone carvings. Among all the tombs, the one preserving the most stone carvings is the Jianling Tomb of Emperor Wen of Liang, Xiao Shunzhi, currently preserving one pair each of stone beasts, stone column bases, stone columns, and stone tortoise pedestals. Other stone carvings include: the Yong'an Tomb of Emperor Xuan of Qi, Xiao Chengzhi, and the Jing'an Tomb of Emperor Wu of Qi, Xiao Ze, each preserving one pair of stone qilin and tianlu—both with the east tianlu intact; the west qilin of Yong'an Tomb lost its head, and Jing'an Tomb lost its four feet. The Xiu'an Tomb of Emperor Jing of Qi, Xiao Daosheng, still preserves one pair of qilin and tianlu. The Xing'an Tomb of Emperor Ming of Qi, Xiao Luan, has one pair of stone qilin and tianlu; the north one is a tianlu, with limbs broken and half body buried in soil, only part of the forebody remaining; the south one is a qilin, with all four feet lost. The unnamed Jinwangchen Tomb of the Southern Qi has one pair of qilin and tianlu. The unnamed Lanshinong Tomb of the Southern Qi has one pair of stone bixie, one intact and one damaged. The unnamed Shuijingshan Tomb of the Southern Qi has one pair of stone bixie; the owners of these two tombs may have been deposed emperors. The Xiuling Tomb of Emperor Wu of Liang, Xiao Yan, has one stone qilin, already damaged. The Zhuangling Tomb of Emperor Jianwen of Liang, Xiao Gang, has one qilin. The tomb of Xiao Ji, Prince Jian of Nankang of Liang, in Jurong preserves one pair of stone bixie, west female and east male, facing each other east-west; one pair of stone columns, with the east column intact and the small bixie on the west column damaged by lightning. List of Southern Dynasties Tomb Stone Carvings in Danyang and Jurong (referencing Liang Baiquan's "Six Dynasties Stone Carvings of Nanjing"): 1. Yong'an Tomb Stone Carvings of Emperor Xuan of Qi, Xiao Chengzhi (447), in the paddy field northeast of Zhangzhuang Village, Shiziwan, Huqiao Town, northeast of Danyang City—one each of stone qilin and tianlu; 2. Jing'an Tomb Stone Carvings of Emperor Wu of Qi, Xiao Ze (493), 400 meters south of Tianjia Village, Yunyang Town, Danyang City—one each of stone qilin and tianlu, one stone column; 3. Xiu'an Tomb Stone Carvings of Emperor Jing of Qi, Xiao Daosheng (494), about one kilometer east of Xiantang Bay (also called Hexian Pond), Huqiao Town, Danyang City—one each of stone qilin and tianlu; 4. Xing'an Tomb Stone Carvings of Emperor Ming of Qi, Xiao Luan (498), northeast of Sancheng Lane, Jinglin Town, east of Danyang City—one each of stone qilin and tianlu; 5. Unnamed Jinwangchen Tomb Stone Carvings of Southern Qi, southwest of Chenjia Village, Houxiang Town, Danyang City—one each of stone qilin and tianlu; 6. Unnamed Lanshinong Tomb Stone Carvings of Southern Dynasties (494), north of Lanshinong, Houxiang Town, Danyang City—two stone bixie; 7. Unnamed Shuijingshan Village Tomb Stone Carvings of Southern Dynasties (494), southeast of Shuijingshan Village, Picheng, Danyang City—two stone bixie; 8. Lingkou Tomb Stone Carvings of Qi-Liang (Southern Dynasties), east of Lingkou Town, Danyang City—one each of stone qilin and tianlu; 9. Jianling Tomb Stone Carvings of Emperor Wen of Liang, Xiao Shunzhi (502), northeast of Sancheng Lane, Jinglin Town, east of Danyang City—one each of stone qilin and tianlu, two stone columns, two stele bases, two stone platform bases; 10. Xiuling Tomb Stone Carvings of Emperor Wu of Liang, Xiao Yan (549), Liujiazhuang, Sancheng, Jinglin Town, east of Danyang City—one stone tianlu; 11. Zhuangling Tomb Stone Carvings of Emperor Jianwen of Liang, Xiao Gang (551), Liujiazhuang, Sancheng, Jinglin Town, east of Danyang City—one stone tianlu; 12. Tomb Stone Carvings of Xiao Ji, Prince Jian of Nankang of Liang (566), Shizichong, Xinhe Village, Qixia Town, Qixia District—two stone bixie, two stone columns.

highlights: 隆昌寺在句容宝华山腹地始建于南朝梁天监元年502年初名千华寺千华社明万历三十三年1605年赐名护国圣化隆昌寺清康熙四十二年1703年康熙登宝华山赐额慧居寺1911年后复称隆昌寺明清时期全寺有殿堂楼坛及下院上千间民间传为九百九十九间半文革时期遭到破坏1985年以后重修山门在寺庙东北隅门内左折为正院大雄宝殿宽五间殿左为净土坛右为藏经楼左厢为文殊堂伽蓝堂等殿前为大悲楼山门右侧为戒坛前设照壁两旁翼以走廊戒坛原为木制后易为石雕寺院西南的山坡上坐落着铜殿和左右两座无梁殿均为明万历三十三年1605年神宗母亲慈圣皇太后捐款建造坐西朝东铜殿原全用铜铸后被毁改建为砖木结构仅殿顶小瓦用铜制成铜殿为重檐歇山顶宽深各一间殿前连接一亭阁阁前有汉白玉石坛坛壁四周雕刻莲花图案铜殿两侧的无梁殿左侧为文殊殿右侧为普贤殿形制相同均为砖造采用歇山屋顶高两层檐下有仿木斗栱殿身面阔三间进深仅一券下层为一券门二券窗二层中为券门两边各开一处方窗窗间为砖雕球纹格眼周围设砖雕平座栏杆裙板刻海棠花瓣和走兽在两殿次间各有阶梯砌在夹墙内无梁殿立面用垂莲柱分隔出檐较短屋角起翘不高这两座殿是明代最小的无梁殿采用罕见的双殿形制
projects.content_zh: 隆昌寺在句容宝华山腹地，始建于南朝梁天监元年（502年），初名千华寺、千华社。明万历三十三年（1605年）赐名"护国圣化隆昌寺"。清康熙四十二年（1703年）康熙登宝华山，赐额"慧居寺"。1911年后复称"隆昌寺"。明清时期全寺有殿、堂、楼、坛及下院上千间，民间传为九百九十九间半，"文革"时期遭到破坏，1985年以后重修。山门在寺庙东北隅，门内左折为正院，大雄宝殿宽五间，殿左为净土坛，右为藏经楼，左厢为文殊堂、伽蓝堂等，殿前为大悲楼。山门右侧为戒坛，前设照壁，两旁翼以走廊，戒坛原为木制，后易为石雕。寺院西南的山坡上坐落着铜殿和左右两座无梁殿，均为明万历三十三年（1605年）神宗母亲慈圣皇太后捐款建造，坐西朝东。铜殿原全用铜铸，后被毁，改建为砖木结构，仅殿顶小瓦用铜制成。铜殿为重檐歇山顶，宽深各一间，殿前连接一亭阁，阁前有汉白玉石坛，坛壁四周雕刻莲花图案。铜殿两侧的无梁殿，左侧为文殊殿，右侧为普贤殿，形制相同，均为砖造，采用歇山屋顶，高两层，檐下有仿木斗栱。殿身面阔三间，进深仅一券，下层为一券门二券窗，二层中为券门，两边各开一处方窗，窗间为砖雕球纹格眼，周围设砖雕平座栏杆，裙板刻海棠花瓣和走兽。在两殿次间各有阶梯，砌在夹墙内。无梁殿立面用垂莲柱分隔，出檐较短，屋角起翘不高。这两座殿是明代最小的无梁殿，采用罕见的双殿形制。
projects.content_en: Longchang Temple is in the hinterland of Baohua Mountain in Jurong, first built in the 1st year of Tianjian of the Liang of the Southern Dynasties (502), originally named Qianhua Temple and Qianhua Society. In the 33rd year of Wanli of the Ming (1605), it was bestowed the name "Huguo Shenghua Longchang Temple." In the 42nd year of Kangxi of the Qing (1703), Kangxi climbed Baohua Mountain and bestowed the plaque "Huiju Temple." After 1911 it was again called "Longchang Temple." During the Ming and Qing periods, the entire temple had over a thousand halls, rooms, towers, altars, and sub-temples, folk tradition saying nine hundred ninety-nine and a half; it was damaged during the Cultural Revolution and repaired after 1985. The mountain gate is at the northeast corner of the temple; inside the gate, turning left is the main courtyard; the Mahavira Hall is five bays wide, with the Pure Land Altar on the left of the hall and the Scripture Library on the right; the left wing consists of Manjushri Hall, Sangharama Hall etc.; in front of the hall is the Great Compassion Tower. On the right side of the mountain gate is the ordination altar, with a screen wall in front and corridors on both sides; the ordination altar was originally wooden, later changed to stone carving. On the hillside southwest of the temple sit the Copper Hall and the two left and right Beamless Halls, all built in the 33rd year of Wanli of the Ming (1605) with donations from Empress Dowager Cisheng, mother of Emperor Shenzong, facing east with their backs to west. The Copper Hall was originally entirely cast in copper, later destroyed and rebuilt as a brick-wood structure, with only the small tiles on the hall roof made of copper. The Copper Hall has a double-eave hip-and-gable roof, one bay wide and one bay deep; in front of the hall connects a pavilion, and in front of the pavilion is a white marble altar, with lotus patterns carved around the altar walls. The Beamless Halls on both sides of the Copper Hall—the left is the Manjushri Hall and the right is the Samantabhadra Hall—are identical in form, both built of brick, with hip-and-gable roofs, two stories high, and imitation-wood bracket sets under the eaves. The hall body is three bays wide and only one arch deep; the lower story has one arched door and two arched windows; the second story has an arched door in the center and a square window on each side; between the windows are brick-carved ball-pattern lattice openings, surrounded by brick-carved flat-seat railings, with the skirt boards carved with begonia petals and beasts. In the secondary bays of both halls there are staircases, built into the partition walls. The facade of the Beamless Halls is divided by hanging lotus columns, with relatively short eaves and low corner upturns. These two halls are the smallest Beamless Halls of the Ming, adopting the rare double-hall form.

regions.name: 镇江

regions.overview: 扬州是《禹贡》所载九州之一，因"州界多水，水扬波"（《晋书·地理志》）而得名。春秋末期，吴国雄心勃勃地计划征伐齐国，称霸天下。吴王夫差先吞并了邗国，公元前486年在今扬州城北的蜀冈修建邗城作为军事堡垒，并开凿邗沟连通长江与淮水，这是中国最早的运河。公元前319年楚怀王重筑邗城，更名广陵。当时列国纷争，扬州位于国境交界，经常作为军事重镇，发展受到抑制。秦汉统一全国后，公元前195年吴王刘濞重筑广陵城，日渐蓬勃繁荣。南朝诗人鲍照《芜城赋》追忆了汉代鼎盛时期的风貌："车挂轊，人驾肩。廛闬扑地，歌吹沸天。"城里车来人往，歌舞弹唱，一派繁华景象。进入三国时期，江淮一带又沦为战场。南朝宋时期竟陵王刘诞谋反，459年与朝廷军在此激战，广陵城化为废墟，南朝诗人鲍照百感交集，为作《芜城赋》。扬州的再度繁荣，在隋唐统一全国后。与战乱时期作为军事重镇对应，在和平时期，扬州则是绾接南北的重要枢纽。隋炀帝开通了大运河，修建了新城，努力将扬州打造成南方的统治中心。到唐代，扬州成为仅次于长安、洛阳的第三大城市，其最高长官淮南节度使常入京拜相或由宰相出任，被誉为"宰相回旋之地"。由于人口渐多，蜀冈上的隋城成为官衙集中的"衙城"，在其南新筑了供商人和百姓居住的罗城。南宋时期扬州作为"国之北门"，成为抗金要地，加筑了大城。宋、金曾在扬州激战，南宋淳熙三年（1176年）22岁的词人姜夔路过扬州，写下了著名的《扬州慢》，"淮左名都，竹西佳处，解鞍少驻初程。过春风十里，尽荠麦青青。自胡马窥江去后，废池乔木，犹厌言兵。渐黄昏，清角吹寒，都在空城……"，描绘出浩劫后的荒凉景象。辛弃疾也为扬州写下最沉痛的词章，"斜阳草树，寻常巷陌，人道寄奴曾住。想当年，金戈铁马，气吞万里如虎。元嘉草草，封狼居胥，赢得仓皇北顾。四十三年，望中犹记，烽火扬州路……"（《永遇乐·京口北固亭怀古》），战火纷飞的扬州成为宋人难解的心结。元代扬州则是蒙古人防御南方起义的重要据点。扬州的第三次繁荣在清代，两淮盐业设在扬州，大量的盐商成为当时最富有的阶层。盐商们注重修复古迹名刹，竞相营建宅第园亭，积极扶持文化事业，使扬州城焕然复兴，佳园荟萃，与苏州、杭州三足鼎立，清人刘大观将其总结为："杭州以湖山胜，苏州以市肆胜，扬州以园亭胜。"《履园丛话》的作者钱泳也认为扬州的园林胜过苏杭："造屋之工，当以扬州为第一。如作文之有变换，无雷同，虽数间之筑，必使门窗轩豁，曲折得宜，此苏杭工匠断断不能也。盖厅堂要整齐，如台阁气象；书斋密室要参差，如园亭布置，兼而有之，方称妙手。"（《履园丛话》卷12）扬州建筑荟萃了中国多地的特色：由于地处南北之间，兼有北方式官和江南民间的建筑特点，又因扬州盐商多来自徽州，带来了徽州的建筑手法，此外苏州香山帮匠师也常到扬州营建。扬州多水少山，因此扬州园林格外重视叠山，形成"扬州以名园胜，名园以叠石胜"的特点（《扬州画舫录》卷二）。1853年太平军占据南京，清军江北大营设在扬州，从此战火不断，城内外的风景名胜几乎无一幸存。太平军还切断了中国南北方的漕运，运河失于治理，淤塞严重，扬州赖以繁荣的经济基础被摧毁。击垮太平军后，清政府曾尝试恢复漕运，但已无财力清淤开河，只好废河运、行海运，上海自此崛起，扬州则日渐没落。由于特殊的地理位置，历史上的扬州时而作为军事堡垒，兵马辐辏；时而成为贸易中心，商贾云集。两千多年的岁月里，演奏着一曲征战与繁华反复交叠的乐章。每到和平时期，大运河和盐运河便扮演了重要角色，前者关系到国家的粮米税收，后者则是官方的垄断物资，借助这两条经济命脉积聚的财富，人们在这里铸就了扬州城的历史和今天。1982年扬州成为国务院颁布的首批国家历史文化名城。扬州今辖邗江区（市政府驻地）、广陵区、江都区和宝应县，代管高邮市和仪征市，有国家级文物保护单位21处，省级文物保护单位46处，本书介绍国保建筑18处，省保建筑14处，其他建筑5处。
regions.overview_en: Yangzhou is one of the Nine Provinces recorded in the "Tribute of Yu," named because "the prefecture's boundaries have much water, and the waves rise" ("Book of Jin·Geography Annals"). In the late Spring and Autumn period, the State of Wu ambitiously planned to conquer the State of Qi and dominate the world. King Fuchai of Wu first annexed the State of Han, and in 486 BC built Hancheng at Shugang north of today's Yangzhou as a military fortress, and excavated the Han Canal connecting the Yangtze and Huai rivers—this is China's earliest canal. In 319 BC, King Huai of Chu rebuilt Hancheng and renamed it Guangling. At that time, with disputes among the states, Yangzhou was located at the border of kingdoms and often served as a military stronghold, with its development restrained. After Qin and Han unified the country, in 195 BC Liu Pi, King of Wu, rebuilt Guangling City, which gradually flourished. The Southern Dynasties poet Bao Zhao's "Rhapsody on the Desolate City" recalled the prosperity of the Han Dynasty: "Chariots catch axles, people jostle shoulders. Markets and gates cover the ground, songs and music boil to the sky." The city was busy with people coming and going, singing and dancing—a scene of prosperity. Entering the Three Kingdoms period, the Jianghuai area again became a battlefield. During the Liu Song of the Southern Dynasties, Liu Dan, Prince of Jingling, rebelled, and in 459 fought fiercely with imperial troops here, reducing Guangling City to ruins; the Southern Dynasties poet Bao Zhao, with mixed feelings, wrote the "Rhapsody on the Desolate City." Yangzhou's renewed prosperity came after the Sui and Tang unified the country. Corresponding to being a military stronghold in wartime, in peacetime Yangzhou was an important hub connecting north and south. Emperor Yang of Sui opened the Grand Canal and built a new city, striving to make Yangzhou the ruling center of the south. By the Tang, Yangzhou had become the third largest city after Chang'an and Luoyang; its highest official, the Huainan Jiedushi (military governor), often went to the capital to become prime minister or was appointed from a prime minister, hailed as "the place where prime ministers rotate." Due to the growing population, the Sui city on Shugang became the "yamen city" where government offices were concentrated, and to its south a new "luocheng" (outer city) was built for merchants and common people to live in. During the Southern Song, Yangzhou, as the "north gate of the country," became a key anti-Jin stronghold, with a large city added. Song and Jin fought fiercely in Yangzhou; in the 3rd year of Chunxi of the Southern Song (1176), the 22-year-old poet Jiang Kui passed through Yangzhou and wrote the famous "Yangzhou Slow": "The famous capital of Huai Zuo, the fine place of Zhuxi, I unhitch my saddle for a brief stop. Passing the ten miles of spring breeze, all is wild oats and green wheat. Since the Hu horses peered across the river, abandoned ponds and old trees still hate to speak of war. Gradually at dusk, clear horns blow cold, all in an empty city..." depicting the desolate scene after the catastrophe. Xin Qiji also wrote the most painful ci poetry for Yangzhou: "The slanting sun on grass and trees, ordinary lanes and alleys, people say Jinu once lived here. Think of those years, golden spears and iron horses, swallowing ten thousand li like a tiger. Yuanjia was hasty, sealing at Wolf居胥, winning only a hasty northward look. Forty-three years, looking back I still remember, the beacon fires of Yangzhou road..." ("Yongyule·Meditating on the Past at Beigu Pavilion of Jingkou"), war-torn Yangzhou became an unresolved knot in the hearts of Song people. In the Yuan, Yangzhou was an important stronghold for the Mongols to defend against southern uprisings. Yangzhou's third prosperity was in the Qing, when the Lianghuai salt industry was based in Yangzhou, and a large number of salt merchants became the wealthiest class of the time. Salt merchants focused on restoring ancient sites and famous temples, competed in building residences and garden pavilions, and actively supported cultural undertakings, making Yangzhou city revive with splendor and fine gardens gathering together, standing with Suzhou and Hangzhou as three pillars; Qing person Liu Daguan summarized it as: "Hangzhou excels in lakes and mountains, Suzhou in markets and shops, Yangzhou in gardens and pavilions." Qian Yong, author of "Lüyuan Conghua," also believed Yangzhou's gardens surpassed those of Suzhou and Hangzhou: "The craft of building houses should take Yangzhou as first. Like writing, it has variation and no sameness; even a building of several bays must have doors and windows open and bright, winding and appropriate—this Suzhou and Hangzhou craftsmen absolutely cannot do. For halls should be neat, like the atmosphere of terraces and pavilions; studies and secret rooms should be varied, like the arrangement of gardens and pavilions; having both can be called a master hand." ("Lüyuan Conghua" Volume 12) Yangzhou architecture brings together features from many parts of China: due to its location between north and south, it combines both northern official and Jiangnan folk architectural characteristics; and because Yangzhou salt merchants mostly came from Huizhou, they brought Huizhou architectural techniques; in addition, Suzhou Xiangshan Gang craftsmen often came to Yangzhou to build. Yangzhou has much water and few mountains, so Yangzhou gardens pay special attention to rockery piling, forming the characteristic that "Yangzhou excels in famous gardens, and famous gardens excel in rockery piling" ("Yangzhou Huafang Lu" Volume 2). In 1853, the Taiping Army occupied Nanjing, and the Qing army's Jiangbei Great Camp was set up in Yangzhou; from then on war continued, and almost no scenic spots inside or outside the city survived. The Taiping Army also cut off the grain transport between north and south China; the canal fell into disrepair and became severely silted, destroying the economic foundation on which Yangzhou's prosperity relied. After defeating the Taiping Army, the Qing government tried to restore grain transport, but had no financial resources to dredge and open the river, so it had to abandon river transport and use sea transport; Shanghai rose from then on, while Yangzhou gradually declined. Due to its special geographical location, historically Yangzhou sometimes served as a military fortress with troops converging, and sometimes became a trade center with merchants gathering. Over more than two thousand years, it has played a movement of repeated alternation between warfare and prosperity. In every peaceful period, the Grand Canal and the Salt Canal played important roles—the former related to the country's grain and tax revenue, the latter being an officially monopolized commodity; with the wealth accumulated through these two economic lifelines, people forged the history and present of Yangzhou city here. In 1982, Yangzhou became one of the first batch of National Historical and Cultural Cities promulgated by the State Council. Yangzhou today administers Hanjiang District (municipal government seat), Guangling District, Jiangdu District, and Baoying County, and代管 Gaoyou City and Yizheng City; it has 21 national-level cultural heritage protection units and 46 provincial-level cultural heritage protection units; this book introduces 18 national-protected buildings, 14 provincial-protected buildings, and 5 other buildings.
