highlights: 清嘉庆二十三年1818年两淮盐总黄至筠17701838旗名应泰购得明代寿芝园旧址改筑为个园黄氏富可敌国被称为两淮八大总商之冠他喜爱竹子园中多处种竹因竹叶形似个字扬州名人袁枚又有诗称月映竹成千个字因此取名个园这是一座宅第园林其南有东中西三路住宅宅北为个园近年又在园北新建品种竹观赏区形成南中北三区园内最具特色的是春夏秋冬四季假山春山位于园门外在两侧花台上丛植修竹竹间置笋石象征雨后春笋如一幅竹石图石为幼年之竹竹为成年之年石竹合一点明个园主题作为游园起点的春山有如诗之起兴含蓄蕴藉背后漏窗则透出园中景致勾起游兴入园略偏左为正厅宜雨轩四面辟门窗可在轩内欣赏周围景致其南有桂树花台北临池视野开阔正北对抱山楼西北为夏山东北为秋山宜雨既指可在雨天赏景又含旧雨新知之意表达主人的好客之情夏山位于园西采用青白湖石叠筑玲珑剔透南面向阳皴纹繁密以光影变幻有如夏日行云而得名山顶设鹤亭宛如仙鹤栖落日内藏有石室可向外眺望园景旧传有12洞洞洞如画幅幅各异山下绕以水池多植荷花并有三折小桥贴水入洞探幽避暑皆宜夏山东北为两层七间的抱山楼体量巨大用于宴饮聚会为晚清扬州盐商园林典型特点夏山采取横向构图突出江南峰峦的连绵奇秀之态园东的秋山则采取竖向构图突出北方山川的高耸雄健之感两山为园中主山东西对仗并通过山石连绵相接过渡自然秋山采用黄石主面向西间植松枫在夕阳余照中最显风情山内有洞穴蹬道可盘旋登顶山巅拂云亭为全园制高点可在亭中北望蜀冈瘦西湖诸景有秋日登高之感秋山南侧有伫秋阁透风漏月轩轩南为冬山冬山采用白色宣石靠墙面北终年处在阴面有如冬日残雪南墙上开圆洞模仿北风呼啸东墙上的圆洞则可望见园外春山暗示冬去春来使四季循环相接个园四季假山的构思新颖独特选石构景布局都别具匠心并深得山水画意春山淡冶而如笑夏山苍翠而如滴秋山明净而如妆冬山惨淡而如睡郭熙林泉高致使人可在一园之内同时体验四季风景被誉为中国古典园林叠山的孤例和杰作
projects.content_zh: 清嘉庆二十三年（1818年），两淮盐总黄至筠（1770—1838，旗名应泰）购得明代寿芝园旧址，改筑为个园。黄氏富可敌国，被称为"两淮八大总商之冠"。他喜爱竹子，园中多处种竹，因竹叶形似"个"字，扬州名人袁枚又有诗称"月映竹成千个字"，因此取名"个园"。这是一座宅第园林，其南有东、中、西三路住宅，宅北为个园，近年又在园北新建"品种竹观赏区"，形成南、中、北三区。园内最具特色的，是春夏秋冬四季假山。春山位于园门外，在两侧花台上丛植修竹，竹间置笋石，象征雨后春笋，如一幅"竹石图"。石为幼年之竹，竹为成年之年，石竹合一，点明个园主题。作为游园起点的"春山"，有如诗之起兴，含蓄蕴藉，背后漏窗则透出园中景致，勾起游兴。入园略偏左为正厅宜雨轩，四面辟门窗，可在轩内欣赏周围景致：其南有桂树花台，北临池，视野开阔，正北对抱山楼，西北为夏山，东北为秋山。"宜雨"既指可在雨天赏景，又含"旧雨新知"之意，表达主人的好客之情。夏山位于园西，采用青白湖石叠筑，玲珑剔透，南面向阳皴纹繁密，以光影变幻有如夏日行云而得名。山顶设鹤亭，宛如仙鹤栖落。日内藏有石室，可向外眺望园景，旧传有12洞，洞洞如画，幅幅各异。山下绕以水池，多植荷花，并有三折小桥贴水入洞，探幽避暑皆宜。夏山东北为两层七间的抱山楼，体量巨大，用于宴饮聚会，为晚清扬州盐商园林典型特点。夏山采取横向构图，突出江南峰峦的连绵奇秀之态；园东的秋山则采取竖向构图，突出北方山川的高耸雄健之感。两山为园中主山，东西对仗，并通过山石连绵相接，过渡自然。秋山采用黄石，主面向西，间植松枫，在夕阳余照中最显风情。山内有洞穴蹬道，可盘旋登顶。山巅拂云亭为全园制高点，可在亭中北望蜀冈、瘦西湖诸景，有秋日登高之感。秋山南侧有伫秋阁、透风漏月轩，轩南为冬山。冬山采用白色宣石，靠墙面北，终年处在阴面，有如冬日残雪。南墙上开圆洞，模仿北风呼啸，东墙上的圆洞则可望见园外春山，暗示冬去春来，使四季循环相接。个园四季假山的构思新颖独特，选石、构景、布局都别具匠心，并深得山水画意，"春山淡冶而如笑，夏山苍翠而如滴，秋山明净而如妆，冬山惨淡而如睡"（郭熙《林泉高致》），使人可在一园之内同时体验四季风景，被誉为中国古典园林叠山的孤例和杰作。
projects.content_en: In the 23rd year of Jiaqing of the Qing (1818), Huang Zhiyun (1770-1838, banner name Yingtai), General Salt Commissioner of Lianghuai, purchased the former site of the Ming Shouzhi Garden and rebuilt it as Geyuan Garden. The Huang family was as wealthy as a country, called "the crown of the eight chief salt merchants of Lianghuai." He loved bamboo and planted bamboo in many places in the garden; because bamboo leaves resemble the character "ge" (individual), and the famous Yangzhou person Yuan Mei had a poem saying "the moon reflects on bamboo, forming a thousand 'ge' characters," hence the name "Geyuan" (Individual Garden). This is a residential garden, with east, middle, and west three-road residences to its south, and Geyuan Garden north of the residences; in recent years a "Variety Bamboo Viewing Area" was newly built north of the garden, forming south, middle, and north three zones. The most distinctive feature in the garden is the four-season rockery of spring, summer, autumn, and winter. The Spring Mountain is located outside the garden gate, with tall bamboo planted in clusters on both side flower terraces, and bamboo-shoot stones placed among the bamboo, symbolizing bamboo shoots after spring rain, like a "bamboo and stone painting." The stone is the young bamboo, the bamboo is the adult year; stone and bamboo unite, clarifying the theme of Geyuan Garden. As the starting point of the garden tour, the "Spring Mountain" is like the opening of a poem,含蓄 and profound, while the lattice windows behind reveal the garden scenery, arousing the desire to tour. Entering the garden, slightly to the left is the main hall Yiyu Xuan (Appropriate-Rain Studio), with doors and windows on all four sides, allowing one to admire the surrounding scenery from inside the studio: to its south is a osmanthus flower terrace, to the north it faces a pond with open views, directly north facing the Baoshan (Embracing Mountain) Tower, northwest to the Summer Mountain, and northeast to the Autumn Mountain. "Yiyu" (Appropriate Rain) both refers to admiring scenery in rainy weather and contains the meaning of "old rain and new knowledge" (old and new friends), expressing the master's hospitality. The Summer Mountain is located west of the garden, stacked with green-white Taihu stones, exquisite and translucent; its south face is sunny with dense texture patterns, named for the changing light and shadow like summer clouds. At the mountain top is the Crane Pavilion, like a crane perched. Inside there is a stone chamber, from which one can overlook the garden scenery; tradition says there are 12 caves, each cave like a painting, each different. Below the mountain winds a pond, mostly planted with lotus, and there is a three-fold small bridge over the water entering the cave, suitable for exploring seclusion and escaping summer heat. Northeast of the Summer Mountain is the two-story seven-bay Baoshan Tower, massive in scale, used for banquets and gatherings—a typical feature of late-Qing Yangzhou salt merchant gardens. The Summer Mountain adopts a horizontal composition, highlighting the continuous and wondrous beauty of Jiangnan peaks; the Autumn Mountain east of the garden adopts a vertical composition, highlighting the towering and vigorous feeling of northern mountains and rivers. The two mountains are the main mountains in the garden, facing each other east-west, and connected by continuous stones with natural transitions. The Autumn Mountain uses yellow stones, with its main face west, interspersed with pines and maples, most charming in the afterglow of the setting sun. Inside the mountain are caves and stone steps, allowing one to spiral up to the top. The Fuyun (Brushing Clouds) Pavilion at the mountain peak is the highest point in the garden, from which one can look north at the scenery of Shugang and Slender West Lake, with the feeling of climbing high in autumn. South of the Autumn Mountain are the Zhuqiu (Standing Autumn) Pavilion and Toufeng Louyue (Wind-Passing Moon-Leaking) Studio; south of the studio is the Winter Mountain. The Winter Mountain uses white Xuanshi (Xuan stone), leaning against the wall facing north, in shade all year round, like residual winter snow. Round holes are opened on the south wall, imitating the howling of the north wind; the round holes on the east wall allow one to see the Spring Mountain outside the garden, hinting at winter passing and spring coming, making the four seasons circulate and connect. The conception of Geyuan's four-season rockery is novel and unique, with stone selection, scene construction, and layout all showing special ingenuity, and deeply capturing the meaning of landscape painting: "Spring mountains are light and graceful as if smiling; summer mountains are verdant and lush as if dripping; autumn mountains are bright and clean as if adorned; winter mountains are bleak and desolate as if sleeping" (Guo Xi, "The Lofty and Reclusive Forest"), allowing one to experience four seasons of scenery within one garden, hailed as a unique and masterpiece example of rockery piling in Chinese classical gardens.

projects.name: 小玲珑山馆（街南书屋）
projects.level: 其他
projects.level_en: Other
projects.address_en: No. 309 Dongguan Street
highlights: 小玲珑山馆又名街南书屋原为清雍正三年1725年盐商马曰琯16871755马曰璐17111799兄弟所建落成时甘泉县令龚明赠送太湖巨石得名小玲珑山馆这块湖石高大秀美二马兄弟不惜贷财工力将其运至园内并请画家张庚16811756为绘小玲珑山馆图但他们的邻居迷信风水认为此石高过屋檐不祥马氏从安徽迁来扬州不愿得罪邻居只好将石放倒马曰璐感慨湖石犹如诸葛之高卧隆中后来马氏兄弟被举荐参加博学鸿儒考试名气渐高才将湖石立起两人卒后园归他人邻居又来申诉不得已这次竟将湖石掘坑埋起来直到园归当地名士汪礵1790字雪疆才从老园丁口中询知埋石之处纠集了上百人将石挖出在搜剔石孔中的泥土时不慎将其折断一块奇石就此损毁今尚存湖石上半段高约1米置于街南书屋看山楼内近年重建为会所恢复看山楼丛书楼七峰草堂等十二景规模颇大
projects.content_zh: 小玲珑山馆又名街南书屋，原为清雍正三年（1725年）盐商马曰琯（1687—1755）、马曰璐（1711—1799）兄弟所建，落成时甘泉县令龚明赠送太湖巨石，得名"小玲珑山馆"。这块湖石高大秀美，二马兄弟不惜贷财、工力将其运至园内，并请画家张庚（1681—1756）为绘《小玲珑山馆图》。但他们的邻居迷信风水，认为此石高过屋檐，不祥。马氏从安徽迁来扬州，不愿得罪邻居，只好将石放倒，马曰璐感慨湖石犹如"诸葛之高卧隆中"。后来马氏兄弟被举荐参加博学鸿儒考试，名气渐高，才将湖石立起。两人卒后园归他人，邻居又来申诉，不得已这次竟将湖石掘坑埋起来。直到园归当地名士汪礵（？—1790，字雪疆），才从老园丁口中询知埋石之处，纠集了上百人将石挖出。在搜剔石孔中的泥土时不慎将其折断，一块奇石就此损毁。今尚存湖石上半段，高约1米，置于街南书屋看山楼内。近年重建为会所，恢复看山楼、丛书楼、七峰草堂等十二景，规模颇大。
projects.content_en: Xiaolinglong Hill House, also called Jienan (South of the Street) Study, was originally built in the 3rd year of Yongzheng of the Qing (1725) by salt merchant brothers Ma Yueguan (1687-1755) and Ma Yuelu (1711-1799); upon completion, Gong Ming, Magistrate of Ganquan County, presented a giant Taihu stone, hence the name "Xiaolinglong Hill House" (Small Exquisite Hill House). This lake stone was tall and beautiful; the two Ma brothers did not hesitate to borrow money and labor to transport it into the garden, and asked painter Zhang Geng (1681-1756) to paint the "Painting of Xiaolinglong Hill House." But their neighbors were superstitious about feng shui, believing this stone taller than the eaves was inauspicious. The Ma family had moved from Anhui to Yangzhou and did not want to offend their neighbors, so they had to lay the stone down; Ma Yuelu lamented that the lake stone was like "Zhuge lying high in Longzhong." Later, the Ma brothers were recommended to take the Erudite Literati (Boxue Hongru) examination, and their fame gradually rose, so they had the lake stone erected. After both died, the garden passed to others, and the neighbors came to complain again; this time, out of necessity, they actually dug a pit and buried the lake stone. It was not until the garden passed to local scholar Wang Shen (?-1790, courtesy name Xuejiang) that he learned the location of the buried stone from an old gardener, and gathered over a hundred people to dig it out. While clearing the mud from the stone's holes, it was accidentally broken, and a rare stone was thus damaged. Today the upper half of the lake stone remains, about 1 meter high, placed inside the Kanshan (Mountain-Viewing) Tower of Jienan Study. In recent years it was rebuilt as a clubhouse, restoring twelve scenes including the Kanshan Tower, Congshu (Book Collection) Tower, and Qifeng (Seven Peaks) Thatched Hall, with a considerable scale.

projects.name: 逸圃
projects.level: 第七批全国重点文物保护单位（2013年）
projects.level_en: 7th Batch National Key Cultural Heritage Site (2013)
projects.address_en: No. 356 Dongguan Street, Guangling District
highlights: 逸圃为商人李松龄宅园李松龄18711937字鹤生1895年在扬州多子街今甘泉路创办惠馀钱庄后遭火灾迁到左卫街今广陵路继续营业以诚信驰名京沪1910年他购得朱四麻脚房产历时三年拓建成逸圃民国时期逸圃被国民党军长颜秀武占据近年重修为会所逸圃东侧紧邻个园坐北朝南包括西路住宅和东路园林两部分入口在东南角迎面开八角门上题逸圃二字过门是一处天井向北可瞥见东园景色向西则进入住宅部分住宅南北共五进宅北是一处庭园内有山石花木精舍长廊景致秀美由庭园东南角向东进入宅园之间的备弄其东有花厅书斋和藏书楼三进建筑花厅南侧便是东园园中主景是紧贴东墙叠筑的湖石假山逶迤而北在北端点缀一座小亭亭前开凿水池整组建筑布局紧凑园林清新秀雅为扬州近代园林佳作
projects.content_zh: 逸圃为商人李松龄宅园。李松龄（1871—1937）字鹤生，1895年在扬州多子街（今甘泉路）创办"惠馀钱庄"，后遭火灾迁到左卫街（今广陵路）继续营业，以诚信驰名京沪。1910年他购得"朱四麻脚"房产，历时三年拓建成逸圃。民国时期逸圃被国民党军长颜秀武占据，近年重修为会所。逸圃东侧紧邻个园，坐北朝南，包括西路住宅和东路园林两部分。入口在东南角，迎面开八角门，上题"逸圃"二字。过门是一处天井，向北可瞥见东园景色，向西则进入住宅部分。住宅南北共五进，宅北是一处庭园，内有山石花木、精舍长廊，景致秀美。由庭园东南角向东，进入宅、园之间的备弄，其东有花厅、书斋和藏书楼三进建筑，花厅南侧便是东园。园中主景是紧贴东墙叠筑的湖石假山，逶迤而北，在北端点缀一座小亭，亭前开凿水池。整组建筑布局紧凑，园林清新秀雅，为扬州近代园林佳作。
projects.content_en: Yipu Garden was the residential garden of merchant Li Songling. Li Songling (1871-1937), courtesy name Hesheng, founded the "Huiyu Money Shop" on Duozi Street (today's Ganquan Road) in Yangzhou in 1895; later, after a fire, it moved to Zuowei Street (today's Guangling Road) to continue business, renowned in Beijing and Shanghai for its integrity. In 1910 he purchased the "Zhu Sima Jiao" property and spent three years expanding and building it into Yipu Garden. During the Republic period, Yipu Garden was occupied by Kuomintang army commander Yan Xiuwu; in recent years it was rebuilt as a clubhouse. Yipu Garden is adjacent to Geyuan Garden on its east side, facing south with its back to north, including two parts: the west-road residence and the east-road garden. The entrance is at the southeast corner, with an octagonal gate facing forward, inscribed with the two characters "Yipu." Passing through the gate is a courtyard; looking north one can glimpse the east garden scenery, and turning west enters the residential part. The residence has five courtyards from north to south; north of the residence is a courtyard garden with mountain stones, flowers and trees, refined studios, and long corridors, with beautiful scenery. From the southeast corner of the courtyard garden eastward, one enters the service alley between the residence and garden; to its east are three courtyards of buildings: the flower hall, study, and book collection tower; south of the flower hall is the east garden. The main scene in the garden is a Taihu-stone rockery stacked tightly against the east wall, winding northward, with a small pavilion at the north end and a pond dug in front of the pavilion. The entire building complex has a compact layout, and the garden is fresh and elegant—a fine example of modern Yangzhou gardens.

projects.name: 谢馥春旧址（馥园）
projects.name_en: Former Residence of Xie Fuchun (Fuyuan Garden)
projects.level: 扬州市保单位（2012年）
projects.level_en: Yangzhou Municipal Protected Unit (2012)
projects.address_en: No. 243 Dongguan Street, Guangling District
projects.ticket: 门票18元（与汪氏小苑合买可半价）
highlights: 谢馥春是一座百年香粉老店清道光十年1830年谢宏业创办原在扬州城南下铺街清同治六年1867年谢馥春将其迁至今址谢氏香粉畅销大江南北有苏州胭脂扬州粉之誉馥园包括谢氏老宅后花园和粉妆坊三部分住宅园林作坊三位一体内主要种植桂花芳香馥郁花厅南部开凿水池叠筑湖石清丽精雅粉妆坊展示谢馥春鸭蛋粉的制作过程
projects.content_zh: 谢馥春是一座百年香粉老店，清道光十年（1830年）谢宏业创办，原在扬州城南下铺街，清同治六年（1867年）谢馥春将其迁至今址。谢氏香粉畅销大江南北，有"苏州胭脂扬州粉"之誉。馥园包括谢氏老宅、后花园和粉妆坊三部分，住宅、园林、作坊三位一体。园内主要种植桂花，芳香馥郁，花厅南部开凿水池、叠筑湖石，清丽精雅。粉妆坊展示谢馥春鸭蛋粉的制作过程。
projects.content_en: Xie Fuchun is a century-old fragrant powder shop, founded by Xie Hongye in the 10th year of Daoguang of the Qing (1830), originally on Xiapu Street south of Yangzhou city; in the 6th year of Tongzhi of the Qing (1867), Xie Fuchun moved it to today's site. The Xie family's fragrant powder sold well throughout the country, with the reputation of "Suzhou rouge, Yangzhou powder." Fuyuan Garden includes three parts: the old Xie family residence, the back garden, and the powder makeup workshop—residence, garden, and workshop in one. The garden mainly plants osmanthus, fragrant and rich; south of the flower hall a pond is dug and Taihu stones are stacked, fresh and elegant. The powder makeup workshop displays the production process of Xie Fuchun duck-egg powder.

projects.name: 汪氏小苑
projects.level: 第七批全国重点文物保护单位（2013年）
projects.level_en: 7th Batch National Key Cultural Heritage Site (2013)
projects.address_en: No. 14 Diguan Di, Guangling District
highlights: 汪氏小苑位于地官第因清代建有不少扬州地方官吏宅第而得名清代扬州盐商汪竹铭18601928祖籍安徽旌德太平天国时期祖传的皮货生意被付之一炬他的父辈来到扬州投身盐号传到汪竹铭时经营有方发家致富在地官第建造了汪氏小苑汪氏小苑有宅有园分两期建成清末汪竹铭购得中西两路民国初年他的儿子又建成东路在东中两路之间有狭长的火巷与通常南宅北园或西宅东园的布局不同汪氏小苑在中部布置东中西三路住宅各为三进每进各门正对前后中轴贯穿左右两厢对称格局极为规整庭园位于四角共有四处大小布置各异为住宅增添了生气汪氏小苑入口位于中路东南进门是一处天井其北为中路照厅正厅澍德堂和两进后进宅三进格局一致皆为三间两厢通过天井相连天井中有耳门通火巷由入门天井向右穿过月洞门为东路南部布置庭园有湖石假山和腊梅琼花等较为简单向北也是照厅正厅春晖堂和两进住宅宅北是一处较大的花园称小苑春深园北布置建筑其前有三处湖石砌边的花台园中铺砌笔直的石径园西辟月洞门通向西邻后园迎曦建筑也布置在北侧南侧靠墙堆筑湖石假山牡丹台西侧设游廊由西园向南又是三进厅堂堂前为西路前园可栖禊西南角设船轩旁凿水池其东为假山是四座庭园中最清雅的一处汪氏小苑以住宅为主园林为辅庭园点缀得当与生活结合密切在盐商宅园中特色鲜明现已辟为扬州盐商住宅陈列馆
projects.content_zh: 汪氏小苑位于地官第，因清代建有不少扬州地方官吏宅第而得名。清代扬州盐商汪竹铭（1860—1928）祖籍安徽旌德，太平天国时期祖传的皮货生意被付之一炬，他的父辈来到扬州投身盐号，传到汪竹铭时经营有方，发家致富，在地官第建造了汪氏小苑。汪氏小苑有宅有园，分两期建成。清末汪竹铭购得中、西两路，民国初年他的儿子又建成东路，在东、中两路之间有狭长的火巷。与通常南宅北园或西宅东园的布局不同，汪氏小苑在中部布置东、中、西三路住宅，各为三进，每进各门正对，前后中轴贯穿，左右两厢对称，格局极为规整；庭园位于四角，共有四处，大小、布置各异，为住宅增添了生气。汪氏小苑入口位于中路东南，进门是一处天井。其北为中路照厅、正厅澍德堂和两进后进宅，三进格局一致，皆为三间两厢，通过天井相连，天井中有耳门通火巷。由入门天井向右穿过月洞门为东路，南部布置庭园，有湖石假山和腊梅琼花等，较为简单。向北也是照厅、正厅春晖堂和两进住宅。宅北是一处较大的花园，称"小苑春深"，园北布置建筑，其前有三处湖石砌边的花台，园中铺砌笔直的石径。园西辟月洞门通向西邻后园"迎曦"，建筑也布置在北侧，南侧靠墙堆筑湖石假山牡丹台，西侧设游廊。由西园向南，又是三进厅堂，堂前为西路前园"可栖禊"，西南角设船轩，旁凿水池，其东为假山，是四座庭园中最清雅的一处。汪氏小苑以住宅为主，园林为辅，庭园点缀得当，与生活结合密切，在盐商宅园中特色鲜明。现已辟为扬州盐商住宅陈列馆。
projects.content_en: Wang's Family Residence is located at Diguan Di (Local Officials' Residences), named because many Yangzhou local officials' residences were built here in the Qing. Qing Yangzhou salt merchant Wang Zhuming (1860-1928), whose ancestral home was Jingde, Anhui; during the Taiping Rebellion, the family's ancestral fur business was burned to ashes, and his father's generation came to Yangzhou to join a salt firm; by the time it passed to Wang Zhuming, with skillful management, he became wealthy and built Wang's Family Residence at Diguan Di. Wang's Family Residence has both residence and garden, built in two phases. In the late Qing, Wang Zhuming purchased the middle and west roads; in the early Republic, his son built the east road, with a narrow fire alley between the east and middle roads. Unlike the usual layout of south residence north garden or west residence east garden, Wang's Family Residence arranges east, middle, and west three-road residences in the center, each with three courtyards; each courtyard's gates face directly, with the front-back central axis running through, and the left and right wing rooms symmetrical—the layout is extremely regular. The courtyard gardens are located at the four corners, totaling four, varying in size and arrangement, adding vitality to the residence. The entrance of Wang's Family Residence is at the southeast of the middle road; entering the gate is a courtyard. North of it are the middle road's reception hall, main hall Shude Hall, and two rear courtyards; the three courtyards have the same layout, all three bays with two wing rooms, connected through courtyards, with side doors in the courtyards leading to the fire alley. From the entrance courtyard, turning right through a moon gate is the east road; the south part arranges a courtyard garden with Taihu-stone rockery, wintersweet, and hydrangea etc., relatively simple. Northward are also the reception hall, main hall Chunhui (Spring Sunshine) Hall, and two courtyards of residence. North of the residence is a larger garden called "Xiaoyuan Chunshen" (Deep Spring in the Small Garden); buildings are arranged north of the garden, with three flower terraces edged with Taihu stones in front, and straight stone paths paved in the garden. West of the garden a moon gate is opened leading to the neighboring west back garden "Yingxi" (Greeting the Morning Sun); buildings are also arranged on the north side, with a Taihu-stone rockery peony terrace stacked against the wall on the south side, and a covered corridor on the west side. From the west garden southward are another three courtyards of halls; in front of the halls is the west road front garden "Keqi Xi" (Can Rest and Wash), with a boat pavilion at the southwest corner, a pond dug beside it, and a rockery to its east—the most elegant of the four courtyard gardens. Wang's Family Residence is mainly residential with the garden as auxiliary; the courtyard gardens are appropriately embellished and closely integrated with life, with distinctive features among salt merchant residential gardens. It has now been opened as the Yangzhou Salt Merchant Residence Exhibition Hall.

projects.name: 琼花观
projects.level: 扬州市保单位
projects.level_en: Yangzhou Municipal Protected Unit
projects.address_en: No. 360 Middle Wenchang Road, Guangling District
highlights: 琼花观始建于西汉北宋至道二年996年扬州太守王禹偁在观内赏琼花题琼花诗从此扬名欧阳修曾在花旁筑无双亭赞誉扬州琼花举世无无明万历二十年1592年吴秀在观内筑石牌坊三清殿和玉皇阁后仅存琼花台和石牌坊1993年重修后成为每年四月赏琼花的胜地今观前有从兴教寺移来的明代三清殿面阔五间重檐歇山顶作为扬州美术馆开放大殿东北角为琼花园入口是一座歇山顶门屋入门即为古琼花台内植琼花台北假山上近年复建了无双亭山下西侧是玉钩洞天亭覆盖着玉钩古井园林中部有水池和聚琼轩等建筑点缀在琼树之间每年四月花开如雪使人如置身于琼楼玉宇间
projects.content_zh: 琼花观始建于西汉，北宋至道二年（996年）扬州太守王禹偁在观内赏琼花，题《琼花诗》，从此扬名。欧阳修曾在花旁筑无双亭，赞誉扬州琼花举世无双。明万历二十年（1592年）吴秀在观内筑石牌坊、三清殿和玉皇阁。后仅存琼花台和石牌坊，1993年重修后成为每年四月赏琼花的胜地。今观前有从兴教寺移来的明代三清殿，面阔五间，重檐歇山顶，作为扬州美术馆开放。大殿东北角为琼花园入口，是一座歇山顶门屋。入门即为古琼花台，内植琼花。台北假山上近年复建了无双亭，山下西侧是玉钩洞天亭，覆盖着玉钩古井。园林中部有水池和聚琼轩等建筑，点缀在琼树之间，每年四月花开如雪，使人如置身于琼楼玉宇间。
projects.content_en: Qionghua Daoist Temple was first built in the Western Han; in the 2nd year of Zhidao of the Northern Song (996), Wang Yucheng, Governor of Yangzhou, admired the qionghua (jade flower) in the temple and wrote the "Poem on Qionghua," from which it became famous. Ouyang Xiu once built the Wushuang (Peerless) Pavilion beside the flowers, praising Yangzhou's qionghua as peerless under heaven. In the 20th year of Wanli of the Ming (1592), Wu Xiu built a stone archway, Sanqing (Three Purities) Hall, and Yuhuang (Jade Emperor) Pavilion in the temple. Later only the Qionghua Terrace and stone archway remained; after restoration in 1993, it became a famous place for admiring qionghua every April. Today in front of the temple is the Ming Sanqing Hall moved from Xingjiao Temple, five bays wide with a double-eave hip-and-gable roof, open as the Yangzhou Art Museum. The northeast corner of the main hall is the entrance to the Qionghua Garden, a gate house with a hip-and-gable roof. Entering the gate is the ancient Qionghua Terrace, with qionghua planted inside. On the rockery north of the terrace, the Wushuang Pavilion was rebuilt in recent years; west of the mountain foot is the Yugou Dongtian (Jade Hook Cave Heaven) Pavilion, covering the ancient Yugou Well. In the middle of the garden are buildings such as a pond and Juqiong (Gathering Qionghua) Studio, embellished among the qionghua trees; every April the flowers bloom like snow, making one feel as if placed among jade towers and jade pavilions.

projects.name: 朱自清故居
projects.level: 第六批全国重点文物保护单位（2006年）
projects.level_en: 6th Batch National Key Cultural Heritage Site (2006)
projects.address_en: No. 27 Anle Lane, Guangling District
highlights: 现代文学家朱自清18981948祖籍浙江绍兴1898年出生于江苏海州今东海1903年随父亲迁居扬州自此直到1915年考入北大前他一直住在扬州并在此结婚他的许多亲人卒后也葬在扬州因此朱自清将扬州视为自己生于斯死于斯歌哭于斯的故乡并曾在散文我是扬州人中追溯自己在扬州的生活朱家在扬州共租赁过七处房子1930年春迁入今安乐巷27号即现在的朱自清故居这是一套建于清光绪年间的普通民宅大门朝东入门北侧的小院为客人留宿的客房当时朱自清在外地教书每次回扬州都在客座小院中起居读书和写作客座西侧有两进庭院坐北朝南包括对灶堂屋后房和厢房是朱自清的父母子女日常生活之处整组庭院占地不多布置紧凑建筑用料也较纤细以实用为主反映了朱氏小康之家的经济状况故居后房今为朱自清纪念馆展览朱自清的生平与著作
projects.content_zh: 现代文学家朱自清（1898—1948）祖籍浙江绍兴，1898年出生于江苏海州（今东海），1903年随父亲迁居扬州，自此直到1915年考入北大前，他一直住在扬州并在此结婚，他的许多亲人卒后也葬在扬州。因此朱自清将扬州视为自己"生于斯，死于斯，歌哭于斯"的故乡，并曾在散文《我是扬州人》中追溯自己在扬州的生活。朱家在扬州共租赁过七处房子，1930年春迁入今安乐巷27号，即现在的朱自清故居。这是一套建于清光绪年间的普通民宅。大门朝东，入门北侧的小院为客人留宿的客房，当时朱自清在外地教书，每次回扬州都在客座小院中起居、读书和写作。客座西侧有两进庭院，坐北朝南，包括对灶、堂屋、后房和厢房，是朱自清的父母子女日常生活之处。整组庭院占地不多，布置紧凑；建筑用料也较纤细，以实用为主，反映了朱氏"小康之家"的经济状况。故居后房今为朱自清纪念馆，展览朱自清的生平与著作。
projects.content_en: Modern writer Zhu Ziqing (1898-1948), whose ancestral home was Shaoxing, Zhejiang, was born in Haizhou, Jiangsu (today's Donghai) in 1898; in 1903 he moved with his father to Yangzhou, and from then until he was admitted to Peking University in 1915, he lived in Yangzhou and married there; many of his relatives were also buried in Yangzhou after death. Therefore Zhu Ziqing regarded Yangzhou as his hometown where "I was born, died, sang and wept," and once traced his life in Yangzhou in the essay "I Am a Yangzhou Person." The Zhu family rented a total of seven houses in Yangzhou, and in the spring of 1930 moved into today's No. 27 Anle Lane, i.e., the current Former Residence of Zhu Ziqing. This is an ordinary folk house built during the Guangxu reign of the Qing. The main gate faces east; the small courtyard north of the entrance was a guest room for overnight guests; at that time Zhu Ziqing taught elsewhere, and every time he returned to Yangzhou he lived, read, and wrote in the guest courtyard. West of the guest courtyard are two courtyards, facing south with their backs to north, including the opposite kitchen, main hall, rear room, and wing rooms—where Zhu Ziqing's parents and children lived daily. The entire courtyard complex occupies little land with a compact layout; the building materials are also relatively slender, prioritizing practicality, reflecting the economic condition of the Zhu family as a "well-off family." The rear room of the former residence is now the Zhu Ziqing Memorial Hall, exhibiting Zhu Ziqing's life and works.

projects.name: 吴道台宅第
projects.level: 第六批全国重点文物保护单位（2006年）
projects.level_en: 6th Batch National Key Cultural Heritage Site (2006)
projects.address_en: No. 45 Taizhou Road, Guangling District
highlights: 吴道台指吴引孙曾先后担任浙江宁绍台道道员广东按察使和浙江布政使等职清光绪三十年1904年他升任广东时委托表兄在扬州城东效仿宁绍台道衙署结合扬州的建筑风格建造宅第当时吴引孙特地聘请了浙江的匠师并从浙南山区运来木料使建筑带有明显的宁绍影响这组宅第坐北朝朝东西共五路中间以火巷分隔号称九十九间半宅门位于东侧偏南是一座精致的砖雕门楼入门穿过天井折向北第二路为主路前有三开间的仪门南面设照壁自南向北有仪门轿厅和主厅爱日轩等七进建筑主路西侧隔着火巷是两路内宅格局基本相同皆为四进以满足兄弟共住的需求最西侧一路也是四进但开间较小主路东侧受到西方建筑的影响由小洋楼观音堂和测海楼组成小洋楼在最南端坐南朝北主体面阔三问东北西三面皆有开放式外廊向北是五开间的观音堂堂后以围墙隔出狭长的天井其北为测海楼庭院测海楼模仿浙江天一阁是一座藏书楼前方凿有方形水池布置亭廊花木成为一处优美的花园
projects.content_zh: 吴道台指吴引孙，曾先后担任浙江宁绍台道道员、广东按察使和浙江布政使等职。清光绪三十年（1904年）他升任广东时，委托表兄在扬州城东效仿宁绍台道衙署，结合扬州的建筑风格建造宅第。当时吴引孙特地聘请了浙江的匠师，并从浙南山区运来木料，使建筑带有明显的宁绍影响。这组宅第坐北朝南，东、西共五路，中间以火巷分隔，号称九十九间半。宅门位于东侧偏南，是一座精致的砖雕门楼。入门穿过天井，折向北第二路为主路，前有三开间的仪门，南面设照壁，自南向北有仪门、轿厅和主厅爱日轩等七进建筑。主路西侧隔着火巷是两路内宅，格局基本相同，皆为四进，以满足兄弟共住的需求。最西侧一路也是四进，但开间较小。主路东侧受到西方建筑的影响，由小洋楼、观音堂和测海楼组成。小洋楼在最南端，坐南朝北，主体面阔三间，东、北、西三面皆有开放式外廊。向北是五开间的观音堂，堂后以围墙隔出狭长的天井，其北为测海楼庭院。测海楼模仿浙江天一阁，是一座藏书楼，前方凿有方形水池，布置亭廊花木，成为一处优美的花园。
projects.content_en: "Wu Daotai" refers to Wu Yinsun, who successively served as Circuit Intendant of the Ning-Shao-Tai Circuit of Zhejiang, Administration Commissioner of Guangdong, and Provincial Administration Commissioner of Zhejiang etc. In the 30th year of Guangxu of the Qing (1904), when he was promoted to Guangdong, he entrusted his cousin to build a residence east of Yangzhou city, imitating the Ning-Shao-Tai Circuit yamen and combining Yangzhou's architectural style. At that time, Wu Yinsun specially hired Zhejiang craftsmen and transported timber from the mountainous areas of southern Zhejiang, giving the building obvious Ning-Shao influence. This residential complex faces south with its back to north, with a total of five roads east and west, separated by fire alleys in the middle, known as "ninety-nine and a half rooms." The residence gate is located on the east side slightly south, an exquisite brick-carved gate tower. Entering the gate through a courtyard, turning north, the second road is the main road; in front is a three-bay ceremonial gate, with a screen wall on the south; from south to north are seven courtyards of buildings including the ceremonial gate, sedan chair hall, and main hall Airi (Loving the Sun) Studio etc. West of the main road, separated by a fire alley, are two roads of inner residences, basically identical in layout, both four courtyards, to meet the needs of brothers living together. The westernmost road is also four courtyards, but with smaller bays. The east side of the main road, influenced by Western architecture, consists of a small Western-style building, Guanyin Hall, and Cehai (Sea-Measuring) Tower. The small Western-style building is at the southernmost end, facing north with its back to south, with the main body three bays wide and open verandas on the east, north, and west sides. Northward is the five-bay Guanyin Hall; behind the hall, a wall separates a narrow courtyard, north of which is the Cehai Tower courtyard. The Cehai Tower, imitating the Tianyi Pavilion of Zhejiang, is a book collection tower; in front a square pond is dug, with pavilions, corridors, flowers, and trees arranged, becoming a beautiful garden.

projects.name: 普哈丁墓
projects.level: 第五批全国重点文物保护单位（2001年）
projects.level_en: 5th Batch National Key Cultural Heritage Site (2001)
projects.address_en: Southeast of Jiefang Bridge, east bank of the Grand Canal
highlights: 伊斯兰先贤普哈丁1275传为穆罕默德第十六世孙南宋咸淳年间到扬州传教南宋德祐元年1275年病逝遵其遗嘱葬在此地俗称回回堂墓园位于运河东岸的高地上坐东朝西由清真寺墓域和园林区三部分组成皆为典型的阿拉伯式建筑从东部入口进入有一道长长的台阶向上通往门屋门额题天方矩蠖意为麦加楷模入门为墓域部分在其南侧是古清真寺由礼拜楼望月楼和沐浴室组成穿过墓域门屋先是资料陈列室介绍伊斯兰教知识普哈丁墓位于墓园东北外覆方形墓亭内部为圆拱顶四壁辟拱券门带有阿拉伯风格墓园中还葬有许多明清两代扬州著名的阿訇和一些虔诚的教徒较著名的是民族英雄左宝贵的衣冠冢在墓域西侧是园林部分建有高耸的望月楼周围绿树成荫环境清幽
projects.content_zh: 伊斯兰先贤普哈丁（？—1275）传为穆罕默德第十六世孙，南宋咸淳年间到扬州传教，南宋德祐元年（1275年）病逝，遵其遗嘱葬在此地，俗称"回回堂"。墓园位于运河东岸的高地上，坐东朝西，由清真寺、墓域和园林区三部分组成，皆为典型的阿拉伯式建筑。从东部入口进入，有一道长长的台阶向上通往门屋，门额题"天方矩蠖"，意为麦加楷模，入门为墓域部分。在其南侧是古清真寺，由礼拜楼、望月楼和沐浴室组成。穿过墓域门屋先是资料陈列室，介绍伊斯兰教知识。普哈丁墓位于墓园东北，外覆方形墓亭，内部为圆拱顶，四壁辟拱券门，带有阿拉伯风格。墓园中还葬有许多明、清两代扬州著名的阿訇和一些虔诚的教徒，较著名的是民族英雄左宝贵的衣冠冢。在墓域西侧是园林部分，建有高耸的望月楼，周围绿树成荫，环境清幽。
projects.content_en: The Islamic sage Puhaddin (?-1275), traditionally said to be the 16th-generation grandson of Muhammad, came to Yangzhou to preach during the Xianchun reign of the Southern Song; he died of illness in the 1st year of Deyou of the Southern Song (1275) and, according to his will, was buried here, commonly called "Huihui Hall." The tomb garden is located on high ground on the east bank of the Grand Canal, facing west with its back to east, consisting of three parts: the mosque, the tomb area, and the garden area—all typical Arabic-style architecture. Entering from the east entrance, a long flight of steps leads upward to the gate house; the gate lintel is inscribed "Tianfang Juhuo," meaning "Model of Mecca"; entering the gate is the tomb area. On its south side is the ancient mosque, consisting of the prayer tower, moon-watching tower, and ablution room. Passing through the tomb area gate house, first is the资料 exhibition room, introducing knowledge of Islam. The Tomb of Puhaddin is located northeast of the tomb garden, covered by a square tomb pavilion, with a domed vault inside and arched doors on the four walls, with Arabic style. Many famous Yangzhou imams of the Ming and Qing dynasties and some devout believers are also buried in the tomb garden; the more famous one is the cenotaph of the national hero Zuo Baogui. West of the tomb area is the garden part, with a towering moon-watching tower built, surrounded by green trees, with a serene environment.

projects.name: 蔚圃
projects.level: 第七批省级文物保护单位（2011年）
projects.level_en: 7th Batch Provincial Cultural Heritage Site (2011)
projects.address_en: No. 4-6 Fengxiang Lane, Guangling District
highlights: 蔚圃是扬州商人程汇新的宅园民国初年聘请造园名家余继之建造有东西两路东路七进西路五进今装修为会所不对游客开放蔚圃位于西路第二进是一处坐北朝南的庭院入口在东南角门内左侧堆叠湖石假山掩住院内景山下有洞可供穿行院北居中为正厅东西伸出游廊东廊与入口相通西廊连接西南角的方亭亭前隔一泓窄池与假山相对庭院虽小但堂亭廊山池树俱全清幽雅致
projects.content_zh: 蔚圃是扬州商人程汇新的宅园，民国初年聘请造园名家余继之建造，有东、西两路，东路七进，西路五进，今装修为会所，不对游客开放。蔚圃位于西路第二进，是一处坐北朝南的庭院。入口在东南角，门内左侧堆叠湖石假山，掩住院内景，山下有洞可供穿行。院北居中为正厅，东西伸出游廊，东廊与入口相通，西廊连接西南角的方亭，亭前隔一泓窄池与假山相对。庭院虽小，但堂、亭、廊、山、池、树俱全，清幽雅致。
projects.content_en: Weipu Garden was the residential garden of Yangzhou merchant Cheng Huixin, built in the early Republic by the famous garden designer Yu Jizhi; it has east and west two roads, with the east road seven courtyards and the west road five courtyards; today it is renovated as a clubhouse, not open to tourists. Weipu Garden is located at the second courtyard of the west road, a courtyard facing south with its back to north. The entrance is at the southeast corner; inside the gate on the left, a Taihu-stone rockery is stacked, hiding the courtyard scenery; there is a cave at the foot of the mountain for passage. In the center north of the courtyard is the main hall, with covered corridors extending east and west; the east corridor connects with the entrance, and the west corridor connects to the square pavilion at the southwest corner; in front of the pavilion, separated by a narrow pond, it faces the rockery. Although the courtyard is small, it has all of hall, pavilion, corridor, mountain, pond, and trees—quiet, secluded, and elegant.

projects.name: 二分明月楼
projects.level: 第七批全国重点文物保护单位（2013年）
projects.level_en: 7th Batch National Key Cultural Heritage Site (2013)
projects.address: 广陵区广陵路263号（盐商贾氏宅园）
projects.address_en: No. 263 Guangling Road, Guangling District (salt merchant Jia's residential garden)
highlights: 二分明月楼为清光绪年间盐商贾沅字颂平所建园内井栏上刻道光七年杏月员置可知此前曾属员氏贾沅是镇江人在扬州开设同福祥盐号热心公益1932年曾出资助修瘦西湖莲花桥二分明月楼南为贾氏祖宅大武城巷15号今存东路六进西路四进在丁家湾1号贾氏还有开盐号今存楠木厅一座二分明月楼以月为主题北侧七间主楼悬钱泳题额二分明月楼取唐代诗人徐凝忆扬州天下三分明月夜二分无赖是扬州诗意楼前设平台前临水池为豪家聚宴庭园的典型格局园中景致皆围绕水池布置东北角小拱桥的石栏呈弯月形掩住水尾其东叠黄石假山沿山可登至池东楼阁二层隔池赏月池南设扇面水榭漏窗皆如弯月入夜后月上柳梢天上明月与月栏月窗呼应又皆在池中映出倒影水声清灵光影荡漾通过匾额题名园林部件整座庭院将赏月的乐事演绎得淋漓尽致
projects.content_zh: 二分明月楼为清光绪年间盐商贾沅（字颂平）所建，园内井栏上刻"道光七年杏月员置"，可知此前曾属员氏。贾沅是镇江人，在扬州开设同福祥盐号，热心公益，1932年曾出资助修瘦西湖莲花桥。二分明月楼南为贾氏祖宅（大武城巷1—5号），今存东路六进，西路四进；在丁家湾1号贾氏还有开盐号，今存楠木厅一座。二分明月楼以"月"为主题，北侧七间主楼悬钱泳题额"二分明月楼"，取唐代诗人徐凝《忆扬州》"天下三分明月夜，二分无赖是扬州"诗意。楼前设平台，前临水池，为豪家聚宴庭园的典型格局。园中景致皆围绕水池布置，东北角小拱桥的石栏呈弯月形，掩住水尾。其东叠黄石假山，沿山可登至池东楼阁二层，隔池赏月。池南设扇面水榭，漏窗皆如弯月。入夜后月上柳梢，天上明月与月栏、月窗呼应，又皆在池中映出倒影，水声清灵，光影荡漾。通过匾额题名、园林部件，整座庭院将赏月的乐事演绎得淋漓尽致。
projects.content_en: Erfen Moon Tower was built by salt merchant Jia Yuan (courtesy name Songping) during the Guangxu reign of the Qing; the well railing in the garden is engraved "Placed by Yuan in the Apricot Moon of the 7th year of Daoguang," indicating it previously belonged to the Yuan family. Jia Yuan was a native of Zhenjiang who opened the Tongfuxiang Salt Firm in Yangzhou and was enthusiastic about public welfare; in 1932 he contributed funds to help repair the Lotus Bridge of Slender West Lake. South of Erfen Moon Tower is the Jia family ancestral residence (No. 1-5 Dawucheng Lane), today preserving six courtyards on the east road and four on the west road; at No. 1 Dingjiawan, the Jia family also had an open salt firm, today preserving one nanmu hall. Erfen Moon Tower takes the "moon" as its theme; the seven-bay main building on the north side hangs the plaque inscribed by Qian Yong "Erfen Moon Tower," taking the poetic meaning from Tang poet Xu Ning's "Recalling Yangzhou": "Of the three parts of bright moonlight under heaven, two parts shamelessly belong to Yangzhou." In front of the building is a platform, facing a pond—a typical layout of a wealthy family's banquet courtyard. The scenery in the garden is all arranged around the pond; the stone railing of the small arch bridge at the northeast corner is crescent-shaped, hiding the water's tail. To its east, a yellow-stone rockery is stacked; along the mountain one can climb to the second floor of the pavilion east of the pond, admiring the moon across the pond. South of the pond is a fan-shaped waterside pavilion, with lattice windows all like crescents. After nightfall, when the moon rises above the willow tops, the bright moon in the sky echoes with the moon railings and moon windows, and all are reflected in the pond; the water sounds are clear and the light and shadows ripple. Through plaque inscriptions and garden elements, the entire courtyard interprets the joy of moon-admiration to the fullest.

projects.name: 小盘谷
projects.level: 第六批全国重点文物保护单位（2006年）
projects.level_en: 6th Batch National Key Cultural Heritage Site (2006)
projects.address_en: No. 42 Dashu Lane, Guangling District
highlights: 小盘谷始建于清嘉庆初年清同治十一年1872年归蒋超伯后又归徐文达清光绪二十三年1897年周馥重加修葺达到全盛今西部为住宅包括东西两路东部小盘谷也由花墙隔为内外两园住宅东路对厅东廊有月洞门通向小盘谷上刻陈鸿寿题额进入外园南侧叠湖石假山上北侧为花厅沿花厅东侧向北一转可望见厅北水池豁然开朗花厅北侧作曲尺形与池岸进退呼应左前方有水阁悬临池上与东岸假山林木隔池相对池东假山全用太湖石其西北一峰峥嵘突起高出水面9米余通体若行云舒卷为叠山佳作被称作九狮图山山内洞穴宛转内置棋桌增添游趣山上设六角风亭可登临闲坐眺览内外两园景致内园以游廊连接通丛翠馆和桐韵山房为近年复建小盘谷用地不大但布置紧凑外庭与内园假山与水池建筑与山石山石与粉墙处处构成对比形成幻境陈从周扬州园林给予极高的评价花墙间隔得非常灵活山峦石壁步石谷口等的叠置正是危峰耸翠苍岩临流水石交融浑然一片了妙处在于运用以少胜多的艺术手法虽然园内没有崇楼与复道廊但是幽曲多姿浅画成图廊屋皆不髹饰以木材的本色出之叠山的技术尤佳足与苏州环秀山庄抗衡
projects.content_zh: 小盘谷始建于清嘉庆初年，清同治十一年（1872年）归蒋超伯，后又归徐文达，清光绪二十三年（1897年）周馥重加修葺，达到全盛。今西部为住宅，包括东、西两路；东部小盘谷也由花墙隔为内、外两园。住宅东路对厅东廊有月洞门通向小盘谷，上刻陈鸿寿题额。进入外园，南侧叠湖石假山，北侧为花厅，沿花厅东侧向北一转，可望见厅北水池，豁然开朗。花厅北侧作曲尺形，与池岸进退呼应，左前方有水阁悬临池上，与东岸假山林木隔池相对。池东假山全用太湖石，其西北一峰峥嵘突起，高出水面9米余，通体若行云舒卷，为叠山佳作，被称作"九狮图山"。山内洞穴宛转，内置棋桌，增添游趣；山上设六角风亭，可登临闲坐眺览内外两园景致。内园以游廊连接，通丛翠馆和桐韵山房，为近年复建。小盘谷用地不大，但布置紧凑，外庭与内园、假山与水池、建筑与山石、山石与粉墙，处处构成对比，形成幻境，陈从周《扬州园林》给予极高的评价："花墙间隔得非常灵活，山峦、石壁、步石、谷口等的叠置，正是危峰耸翠，苍岩临流，水石交融，浑然一片了。妙处在于运用'以少胜多'的艺术手法。虽然园内没有崇楼与复道廊，但是幽曲多姿，浅画成图。廊屋皆不髹饰，以木材的本色出之。叠山的技术尤佳，足与苏州环秀山庄抗衡。"
projects.content_en: Xiaopangu (Small Coiled Valley) Garden was first built in the early Jiaqing reign of the Qing; in the 11th year of Tongzhi (1872) it passed to Jiang Chaobo, later to Xu Wenda; in the 23rd year of Guangxu (1897), Zhou Fu heavily renovated it, reaching its heyday. Today the western part is the residence, including east and west two roads; the eastern Xiaopangu is also separated by a flower wall into inner and outer two gardens. The east corridor of the opposite hall on the east road of the residence has a moon gate leading to Xiaopangu, engraved with Chen Hongshou's inscription. Entering the outer garden, a Taihu-stone rockery is stacked on the south side, and on the north side is the flower hall; turning north along the east side of the flower hall, one can see the pond north of the hall, suddenly opening up. The north side of the flower hall is curved in a carpenter's-square shape, echoing the pond bank in advance and retreat; on the left front is a waterside pavilion suspended over the pond, facing the rockery and trees on the east bank across the pond. The rockery east of the pond is entirely made of Taihu stone; its northwest peak rises steeply, over 9 meters above the water surface, the whole body like rolling clouds—a masterpiece of rockery piling, called the "Nine Lions Picture Mountain." Inside the mountain, caves wind, with chess tables placed inside, adding to the pleasure of touring; on the mountain is a hexagonal wind pavilion, where one can climb to sit and admire the scenery of both inner and outer gardens. The inner garden is connected by covered corridors, leading to the Congcui (Gathering Green) Hall and Tongyun (Paulownia Rhyme) Mountain Room, rebuilt in recent years. Xiaopangu occupies little land but has a compact layout; the outer court and inner garden, rockery and pond, buildings and mountain stones, mountain stones and white walls—everywhere form contrasts, creating a dreamscape; Chen Congzhou's "Yangzhou Gardens" gave it extremely high praise: "The flower walls are separated very flexibly; the stacking of mountain ridges, stone walls, stepping stones, and valley mouths is precisely steep peaks rising in green, dark rocks facing the flow, water and stone blending,浑然 one piece. The beauty lies in the artistic technique of 'using the few to overcome the many.' Although there are no lofty towers and double-corridor galleries in the garden, it is secluded and winding with variety, lightly painted into a picture. The corridor rooms are all unpainted, appearing in the natural color of wood. The rockery-piling technique is especially excellent, enough to compete with Suzhou's Huanxiu Villa."

projects.name: 何园（含片石山房）
projects.level: 第三批全国重点文物保护单位（1988年）
projects.level_en: 3rd Batch National Key Cultural Heritage Site (1988)
projects.address_en: No. 66 Xuningmen Street, Guangling District
highlights: 何园是晚清官员何芷舠的宅园清同治元年1862年曾任湖北汉黄德道台的何芷舠辞官回到扬州在古城东南隅建造宅园中部为住宅包括东西两路以西路为主自南向北有楠木厅和玉绣楼等东路有骑马楼和牡丹厅等在住宅西侧和北侧建造大花园东南则购入小花园形成一组大规模的宅园何芷舠取陶渊明倚南窗以寄傲登东皋以舒啸之意将西北角的大花园命名为寄啸山庄民间俗称何园园林分为东西两部分今园林入口在东侧东园以静香轩船厅为中心周围铺设精美的铺地用卵石瓦片构成波浪使房屋有如船行水上船厅东侧和北侧紧贴园墙叠筑湖石假山西北角转折处设六角月亭山下则有流水环绕假山一直连绵至西北连接小楼登楼至二层可进入西园船厅南侧是牡丹亭朝向东面的山墙上有砖雕杰作风吹牡丹由牡丹厅西北角沿贴墙游廊向西也可进入西园入园前的复廊上开漏窗可先一窥园景南侧墙上也有漏窗能望见宅中的玉绣楼西园中部是东西横亘的大水池池西堆叠大型湖石假山山池占据园林的中心围绕四周贴墙布置楼厅和游廊池中偏东筑小岛上建水心亭用于演戏唱曲借水面回音可增强音效池周三面环楼临水皆有回廊可供凭临观戏其中池北的二层蝴蝶厅是园林正堂为主人宴客之所园西假山背后为桂花厅是何家子弟读书求学之所由此绕向西南小水池南侧的赏月楼是一座鸳鸯厅向北隔池可赏湖石假山西向也是一座山石庭园有洞有路可供日涉成趣西园虽以山池为中心但四周的建筑高大恢宏与山水并驾齐驱不分轩轾体现了晚清园林中建筑的突出地位由赏月楼前庭园可进入中路住宅如今展出当年何家的生活场景和用品从骑马楼前的庭院向东可进入东南小花园又称片石山房清乾隆初年吴家龙所辟后传其孙吴之黼钱泳履园丛话卷20提到园中的池上有太湖石山子一座高五六丈甚奇峭相传为石涛和尚手笔但此园初建时间晚于石涛园林学家曹汛考证认为园内假山是莲性寺的牧山和尚所筑虽年代推后但仍为扬州现存最早的假山艺术水平很高片石山房以水池为中心池南是楠木厅向北可隔池欣赏北岸的假山这组假山倚墙堆叠西首高耸为主峰俯临水池山脚设石桥横跨水上后植腊梅过桥循山道可登至峰顶山内筑有两间方形石室片石山房便由此得名
projects.content_zh: 何园是晚清官员何芷舠的宅园。清同治元年（1862年），曾任湖北汉黄德道台的何芷舠辞官回到扬州，在古城东南隅建造宅园。中部为住宅，包括东、西两路，以西路为主，自南向北有楠木厅和玉绣楼等，东路有骑马楼和牡丹厅等。在住宅西侧和北侧建造大花园，东南则购入小花园，形成一组大规模的宅园。何芷舠取陶渊明"倚南窗以寄傲""登东皋以舒啸"之意，将西北角的大花园命名为寄啸山庄，民间俗称"何园"。园林分为东、西两部分，今园林入口在东侧。东园以静香轩船厅为中心，周围铺设精美的铺地，用卵石、瓦片构成波浪，使房屋有如船行水上。船厅东侧和北侧紧贴园墙叠筑湖石假山，西北角转折处设六角月亭，山下则有流水环绕。假山一直连绵至西北，连接小楼，登楼至二层可进入西园。船厅南侧是牡丹亭，朝向东面的山墙上有砖雕杰作"风吹牡丹"。由牡丹厅西北角沿贴墙游廊向西也可进入西园，入园前的复廊上开漏窗，可先一窥园景。南侧墙上也有漏窗，能望见宅中的玉绣楼。西园中部是东西横亘的大水池，池西堆叠大型湖石假山，山、池占据园林的中心，围绕四周贴墙布置楼厅和游廊。池中偏东筑小岛，上建水心亭，用于演戏唱曲，借水面回音可增强音效。池周三面环楼，临水皆有回廊，可供凭临观戏。其中池北的二层蝴蝶厅是园林正堂，为主人宴客之所。园西假山背后为桂花厅，是何家子弟读书求学之所。由此绕向西南，小水池南侧的赏月楼是一座鸳鸯厅，向北隔池可赏湖石假山，西向也是一座山石庭园，有洞有路，可供日涉成趣。西园虽以山、池为中心，但四周的建筑高大恢宏，与山水并驾齐驱，不分轩轾，体现了晚清园林中建筑的突出地位。由赏月楼前庭园可进入中路住宅，如今展出当年何家的生活场景和用品。从骑马楼前的庭院向东可进入东南小花园，又称片石山房。清乾隆初年吴家龙所辟，后传其孙吴之黼。钱泳《履园丛话》卷20提到园中的"池上有太湖石山子一座，高五六丈，甚奇峭，相传为石涛和尚手笔"。但此园初建时间晚于石涛，园林学家曹汛考证认为园内假山是莲性寺的牧山和尚所筑，虽年代推后，但仍为扬州现存最早的假山，艺术水平很高。片石山房以水池为中心，池南是楠木厅，向北可隔池欣赏北岸的假山。这组假山倚墙堆叠，西首高耸为主峰，俯临水池。山脚设石桥横跨水上，后植腊梅，过桥循山道可登至峰顶。山内筑有两间方形石室，片石山房便由此得名。
projects.content_en: Heyuan Garden was the residential garden of late-Qing official He Zhidao. In the 1st year of Tongzhi of the Qing (1862), He Zhidao, who had served as Circuit Intendant of the Han-Huang-De Circuit of Hubei, resigned and returned to Yangzhou, building a residential garden in the southeast corner of the ancient city. The central part is the residence, including east and west two roads, with the west road as the main one; from south to north are the Nanmu Hall and Yuxiu (Jade Embroidery) Tower etc., and the east road has the Qima (Horse-Riding) Tower and Peony Hall etc. A large garden was built west and north of the residence, and a small garden was purchased to the southeast, forming a large-scale residential garden. He Zhidao, taking the meaning of Tao Yuanming's "leaning on the south window to express my pride" and "climbing the eastern highland to whistle freely," named the large garden in the northwest corner Jixiao (Whistling in Solitude) Villa, commonly called "Heyuan" (He Garden) by the people. The garden is divided into east and west two parts; today the garden entrance is on the east side. The east garden centers on the Jingxiang Xuan Boat Hall, with exquisite paving around it, using pebbles and tiles to form waves, making the house seem like a boat sailing on water. East and north of the boat hall, tightly against the garden wall, a Taihu-stone rockery is stacked; at the northwest corner turn is a hexagonal moon pavilion, and at the foot of the mountain running water surrounds it. The rockery extends continuously to the northwest, connecting a small building; climbing to the second floor one can enter the west garden. South of the boat hall is the Peony Pavilion; on the mountain wall facing east is a brick-carving masterpiece "Wind Blowing Peonies." From the northwest corner of the Peony Hall, along the wall-hugging covered corridor westward, one can also enter the west garden; on the double corridor before entering the garden, lattice windows are opened, allowing a first glimpse of the garden scenery. There are also lattice windows on the south wall, from which the Yuxiu Tower in the residence can be seen. The center of the west garden is a large pond stretching east-west; west of the pond a large Taihu-stone rockery is stacked; the mountain and pond occupy the center of the garden, with halls and covered corridors arranged around the four sides against the walls. A small island is built slightly east of the pond center, with a Water-Center Pavilion on it, used for acting and singing, using the water surface echo to enhance the sound effect. The pond is surrounded by buildings on three sides, with covered corridors by the water for watching performances. Among them, the two-story Butterfly Hall north of the pond is the main hall of the garden, where the master entertained guests. Behind the rockery west of the garden is the Osmanthus Hall, where the He family children studied. From there winding southwest, the Moon-Admiring Tower south of the small pond is a mandarin-duck hall; facing north across the pond one can admire the Taihu-stone rockery, and facing west is also a mountain-stone courtyard, with caves and paths for daily strolling pleasure. Although the west garden centers on mountain and pond, the surrounding buildings are tall and grand, keeping pace with the mountains and waters without distinction, reflecting the prominent position of architecture in late-Qing gardens. From the front courtyard of the Moon-Admiring Tower, one can enter the middle-road residence, which today exhibits the He family's life scenes and belongings of that time. From the courtyard in front of the Horse-Riding Tower eastward, one can enter the southeast small garden, also called Pianshi (Slab Stone) Rockery House. It was opened up by Wu Jialong in the early Qianlong reign of the Qing, later passed to his grandson Wu Zhifu. Qian Yong's "Lüyuan Conghua" Volume 20 mentions that in the garden "on the pond there is a Taihu-stone mountain, five to six zhang high, very steep and wondrous, traditionally said to be the handiwork of the monk Shitao." But this garden's initial construction time was later than Shitao; garden scholar Cao Xun's research believes the rockery in the garden was built by the monk Mushan of Lianxing Temple; although the date is pushed later, it is still the earliest existing rockery in Yangzhou, with a very high artistic level. Pianshi Rockery House centers on a pond; south of the pond is the Nanmu Hall, and facing north across the pond one can admire the rockery on the north bank. This group of rockeries is stacked against the wall, with the west end towering as the main peak, overlooking the pond. At the foot of the mountain a stone bridge spans the water, with wintersweet planted behind; crossing the bridge and following the mountain path one can climb to the peak. Inside the mountain are two square stone rooms, from which Pianshi Rockery House gets its name.

projects.name: 卢氏盐商住宅（康山草堂）
projects.level: 第七批全国重点文物保护单位（2013年）
projects.level_en: 7th Batch National Key Cultural Heritage Site (2013)
projects.address_en: No. 22 Kangshan Street, Guangling District
highlights: 卢氏住宅前身为明代文学家康海的故居明永乐年间浚治运河在此用河土堆成山丘明正德五年1510年名列前七子之一的康海14751540寓居山旁得名康山康海是陕西人明弘治十五年1502年状元及第明正德三年1508年同为前七子的李梦阳入狱康海往见同乡刘瑾救李梦阳出狱查继佐罪惟录两年后刘瑾被凌迟处死康海受牵连罢官李梦阳未进一言相救康海勘透世情退居扬州蓄伶赏乐作杂剧中山狼讽刺李梦阳并创建康家班社推动了秦腔艺术的发展晚明时期姚思孝购得康山旧址改筑拓建董其昌为题康山草堂匾额从此成为扬州名胜清乾隆年间归盐商江春乾隆曾两次驾临游赏达到鼎盛清道光年间又归大学士阮元江南河道总督麟庆曾来探访清光绪二十年1894年由盐商卢绍绪18431905购得历时三年建成扬州现存最大的盐商住宅卢宅前后九进堂厢廊亭共计200余间高敞宏大雕饰精美是晚清盐商豪华住宅的代表前五进皆为五开间有可容百席的百宴厅后四进为明三暗五间厅堂前各有小院布置花木湖石沿东侧夹道向北可直达后部意园意园中部为水池池北有书斋和藏书楼两进建筑池畔点缀画舫并有假山廊亭花卉树木等园景清幽西北角有一株百年紫藤枝繁叶茂郁郁葱葱卢宅今为中国淮扬菜博物馆宅东为曾公祠祭祀曾国藩
projects.content_zh: 卢氏住宅前身为明代文学家康海的故居。明永乐年间浚治运河，在此用河土堆成山丘，明正德五年（1510年）名列"前七子"之一的康海（1475—1540）寓居山旁，得名"康山"。康海是陕西人，明弘治十五年（1502年）状元及第，明正德三年（1508年）同为"前七子"的李梦阳入狱，康海往见同乡刘瑾救李梦阳出狱（查继佐《罪惟录》）。两年后刘瑾被凌迟处死，康海受牵连罢官，李梦阳未进一言相救。康海勘透世情，退居扬州蓄伶赏乐，作杂剧《中山狼》讽刺李梦阳，并创建"康家班社"，推动了秦腔艺术的发展。晚明时期姚思孝购得康山旧址改筑拓建，董其昌为题"康山草堂"匾额，从此成为扬州名胜。清乾隆年间归盐商江春，乾隆曾两次驾临游赏，达到鼎盛。清道光年间又归大学士阮元，江南河道总督麟庆曾来探访。清光绪二十年（1894年）由盐商卢绍绪（1843—1905）购得，历时三年建成扬州现存最大的盐商住宅。卢宅前后九进，堂厢廊亭共计200余间，高敞宏大，雕饰精美，是晚清盐商豪华住宅的代表。前五进皆为五开间，有可容百席的"百宴厅"，后四进为明三、暗五间，厅堂前各有小院，布置花木湖石。沿东侧夹道向北可直达后部意园。意园中部为水池，池北有书斋和藏书楼两进建筑，池畔点缀画舫，并有假山廊亭、花卉树木等，园景清幽。西北角有一株百年紫藤，枝繁叶茂，郁郁葱葱。卢宅今为中国淮扬菜博物馆。宅东为曾公祠，祭祀曾国藩。
projects.content_en: The Lu Residence was formerly the residence of Ming Dynasty writer Kang Hai. During the Yongle reign of the Ming, when dredging the Grand Canal, river soil was piled here into a hill; in the 5th year of Zhengde of the Ming (1510), Kang Hai (1475-1540), one of the "Former Seven Masters," lived beside the hill, hence the name "Kangshan" (Kang Mountain). Kang Hai was a native of Shaanxi; he came first in the palace examination in the 15th year of Hongzhi of the Ming (1502); in the 3rd year of Zhengde (1508), Li Mengyang, also one of the "Former Seven Masters," was imprisoned; Kang Hai went to see his fellow townsman Liu Jin to rescue Li Mengyang from prison (Cha Jizuo, "Zuiwei Lu"). Two years later Liu Jin was executed by lingchi (death by a thousand cuts), and Kang Hai was implicated and dismissed from office; Li Mengyang did not say a word to save him. Kang Hai saw through the ways of the world, retired to Yangzhou, kept actors and enjoyed music, wrote the zaju (variety play) "The Wolf of Zhongshan" satirizing Li Mengyang, and founded the "Kang Family Troupe," promoting the development of Qinqiang (Shaanxi opera) art. In the late Ming, Yao Sixiao purchased the former Kangshan site, rebuilt and expanded it; Dong Qichang inscribed the plaque "Kangshan Thatched Cottage," from which it became a famous Yangzhou scenic spot. During the Qianlong reign of the Qing, it passed to salt merchant Jiang Chun; Qianlong twice visited and toured it, reaching its heyday. During the Daoguang reign of the Qing, it passed to Grand Secretary Ruan Yuan; Lin Qing, Governor-General of the Jiangnan River Course, once came to visit. In the 20th year of Guangxu of the Qing (1894), it was purchased by salt merchant Lu Shaoxu (1843-1905), and after three years of construction became the largest existing salt merchant residence in Yangzhou. The Lu Residence has nine courtyards front to back, with halls, wing rooms, corridors, and pavilions totaling over 200 rooms—tall, spacious, and grand, with exquisite carvings and decorations, a representative of luxurious late-Qing salt merchant residences. The first five courtyards are all five bays wide, with a "Hundred-Banquet Hall" that can accommodate a hundred banquets; the last four courtyards are "apparently three, secretly five" bays, with small courtyards in front of each hall, arranged with flowers, trees, and Taihu stones. Along the east side alley northward, one can directly reach the rear Yiyuan (Meaning Garden). The center of Yiyuan is a pond; north of the pond are two courtyards of buildings: a study and a book collection tower; by the pond are decorated painted boats, as well as rockeries, corridor pavilions, flowers, and trees etc., with a quiet and elegant garden scene. At the northwest corner is a century-old wisteria, with lush branches and leaves, thriving and green. The Lu Residence is today the Museum of Chinese Huaiyang Cuisine. East of the residence is the Zeng Gong Shrine, sacrificing to Zeng Guofan.

projects.name: 廖可亭盐商住宅
projects.level: 第六批省级文物保护单位（2006年）
projects.level_en: 6th Batch Provincial Cultural Heritage Site (2006)
projects.address_en: No. 118 Nanhexia
highlights: 廖可亭是江西临江人清末到扬州经营盐业致富清光绪三十一年1905年他购得清道光年间山西人所建的余庆堂慎德堂1908年又购得宅后严姓空地和部分房屋拓建为东西两路住宅其间以火巷分隔宅后布置花园东路住宅南北共七进第一进是二层门楼下上下共十二间其北为五间照厅第三进是五间楠木大厅后四进皆为五开间的二层楼房西路住宅共有五进前两进为外厅后三进为内宅宅后原有花园建有八角亭和小亭以曲廊相连现已毁廖宅是扬州城区保存规模较大的盐商住宅建筑布局规整紧凑用料和工艺都属上乘东路的楠木大厅有木雕和石雕装饰精致厅内还悬有大总统徐世昌和黎元洪等所题写的匾额具有较高的艺术和历史价值
projects.content_zh: 廖可亭是江西临江人，清末到扬州经营盐业致富。清光绪三十一年（1905年），他购得清道光年间山西人所建的余庆堂、慎德堂，1908年又购得宅后严姓空地和部分房屋，拓建为东、西两路住宅，其间以火巷分隔，宅后布置花园。东路住宅南北共七进。第一进是二层门楼，上下共十二间；其北为五间照厅，第三进是五间楠木大厅，后四进皆为五开间的二层楼房。西路住宅共有五进，前两进为外厅，后三进为内宅。宅后原有花园，建有八角亭和小亭，以曲廊相连，现已毁。廖宅是扬州城区保存规模较大的盐商住宅，建筑布局规整紧凑，用料和工艺都属上乘，东路的楠木大厅有木雕和石雕，装饰精致。厅内还悬有大总统徐世昌和黎元洪等所题写的匾额，具有较高的艺术和历史价值。
projects.content_en: Liao Keting was a native of Linjiang, Jiangxi, who came to Yangzhou in the late Qing to operate the salt industry and became wealthy. In the 31st year of Guangxu of the Qing (1905), he purchased the Yuqing Hall and Shende Hall built by a Shanxi person during the Daoguang reign of the Qing; in 1908 he also purchased the vacant land of the Yan family behind the residence and part of the houses, expanding and building into east and west two-road residences, separated by a fire alley, with a garden arranged behind the residence. The east-road residence has seven courtyards from north to south. The first courtyard is a two-story gate tower, with twelve rooms upstairs and downstairs; north of it is a five-bay reception hall; the third courtyard is a five-bay nanmu main hall; the last four courtyards are all five-bay two-story buildings. The west-road residence has five courtyards in total, with the first two as outer halls and the last three as inner residences. Behind the residence there was originally a garden, with an octagonal pavilion and a small pavilion, connected by a winding corridor, now destroyed. The Liao Residence is a relatively large-scale salt merchant residence preserved in Yangzhou city, with a regular and compact architectural layout, and both materials and craftsmanship are of high quality; the nanmu main hall on the east road has wood carvings and stone carvings, with exquisite decoration. Inside the hall also hang plaques inscribed by Grand Presidents Xu Shichang and Li Yuanhong etc., with relatively high artistic and historical value.

projects.level_en: 7th Batch National Key Cultural Heritage Site (2013)
projects.address_en: No. 356 Dongguan Street, Guangling District
highlights: 汪咏沂18591940字鲁门安徽歙县人曾先后担任山阳今淮安县令海州今连云港知州后弃官从商在淮北开建产盐圩堤创办盐业公司在盐商中获得了崇高威望被推举为商总清光绪年间他在南河下建造了住宅汪氏住宅原包括西宅和东园宅园之间隔以火巷今东园已毁西宅共有九进又称世德堂自南向北各进地面逐渐增高寓意步步高升南部是一座磨砖大门门内天井北部有三间楠木大厅用料考究雕工精细为扬州目前保存最完整面积最大的楠木厅厅后腰门内有多进楼厅皆为两层高各进之间以走廊连成串楼这组住宅绵延百余米布局规整体量宏大是扬州盐商住宅的重要遗存
projects.content_zh: 汪咏沂（1859—1940）字鲁门，安徽歙县人，曾先后担任山阳（今淮安）县令、海州（今连云港）知州，后弃官从商，在淮北开建产盐圩堤，创办盐业公司，在盐商中获得了崇高威望，被推举为商总。清光绪年间，他在南河下建造了住宅。汪氏住宅原包括西宅和东园，宅园之间隔以火巷，今东园已毁。西宅共有九进，又称"世德堂"，自南向北各进地面逐渐增高，寓意"步步高升"。南部是一座磨砖大门，门内天井北部有三间楠木大厅，用料考究，雕工精细，为扬州目前保存最完整、面积最大的楠木厅。厅后腰门内有多进楼厅，皆为两层高，各进之间以走廊连成"串楼"。这组住宅绵延百余米，布局规整，体量宏大，是扬州盐商住宅的重要遗存。
projects.content_en: Wang Yongyi (1859-1940), courtesy name Lumen, a native of Shexian, Anhui, successively served as County Magistrate of Shanyang (today's Huai'an) and Prefect of Haizhou (today's Lianyungang), later abandoned officialdom for business, opening salt-producing dikes in northern Huai and founding a salt company, gaining high prestige among salt merchants and being elected as the chief merchant. During the Guangxu reign of the Qing, he built a residence at Nanhexia. The Wang Residence originally included a west residence and an east garden, separated by a fire alley between the residence and garden; today the east garden has been destroyed. The west residence has nine courtyards in total, also called "Shide Hall" (Hall of Inherited Virtue); from south to north, the ground level of each courtyard gradually rises,寓意 "step by step rising." The southern part is a ground-brick main gate; north of the courtyard inside the gate are three nanmu main halls, with exquisite materials and fine carving, the most completely preserved and largest nanmu hall in Yangzhou today. Inside the back door behind the hall are multiple courtyards of tower halls, all two stories high, connected by corridors between each courtyard into a "string tower." This group of residences stretches over a hundred meters, with a regular layout and massive scale—an important surviving example of Yangzhou salt merchant residences.

projects.name: 匏庐
projects.level: 第六批省级文物保护单位（2006年）
projects.level_en: 6th Batch Provincial Cultural Heritage Site (2006)
projects.address_en: No. 221 Ganquan Road
highlights: 匏庐为清末民初实业家卢殿虎的宅园建于民国初年整座建筑群居中为宅南北共三进在东南和西南角构园连接处狭似葫芦因称匏庐东园开圆洞门平面呈曲尺形沿贴墙曲廊东行居中为曲尺形水池池南筑半亭池北设水轩岸边则点置峰石绕有幽趣西园取名可栖犀开方洞门内部较东园宽敞入门先进一处小庭院垒有黄石花坛向南穿过花厅进入南院堆叠湖石假山山西南角开池筑阁种植芭蕉睡莲自成幽境西墙上开留余小门入门疑别有洞天向北行迎面望见黄石假山又折回北部庭园令游人得新奇之趣
projects.content_zh: 匏庐为清末民初实业家卢殿虎的宅园，建于民国初年。整座建筑群居中为宅，南北共三进，在东南和西南角构园，连接处狭似葫芦，因称"匏庐"。东园开圆洞门，平面呈曲尺形，沿贴墙曲廊东行，居中为曲尺形水池，池南筑半亭，池北设水轩，岸边则点置峰石，绕有幽趣。西园取名"可栖犀"，开方洞门，内部较东园宽敞。入门先进一处小庭院，垒有黄石花坛，向南穿过花厅进入南院，堆叠湖石假山。山西南角开池筑阁，种植芭蕉睡莲，自成幽境。西墙上开"留余"小门，入门疑别有洞天，向北行迎面望见黄石假山，又折回北部庭园，令游人得新奇之趣。
projects.content_en: Paolu (Bottle-gourd Garden) was the residential garden of industrialist Lu Dianhu of the late Qing and early Republic, built in the early Republic. The entire building complex has the residence in the center, with three courtyards from north to south; gardens are constructed at the southeast and southwest corners, with the connecting part narrow like a bottle gourd, hence called "Paolu." The east garden opens a round cave gate, with a carpenter's-square-shaped plan; walking east along the wall-hugging winding corridor, in the center is a carpenter's-square-shaped pond; south of the pond a half-pavilion is built, north of the pond a waterside studio is set, and on the bank peak stones are placed, with secluded charm all around. The west garden is named "Keqi Xi" (Can Rest and Wash), opening a square cave gate, with the interior more spacious than the east garden. Entering the gate, one first enters a small courtyard with a yellow-stone flower terrace piled; passing south through the flower hall into the south courtyard, a Taihu-stone rockery is stacked. At the southwest corner of the mountain a pond is dug and a pavilion built, with plantains and water lilies planted, forming a secluded realm of its own. On the west wall a "Liuyu" (Leaving Surplus) small gate is opened; entering it one suspects another world beyond; walking north, one faces a yellow-stone rockery, then turns back to the north courtyard, giving visitors a novel and interesting experience.

projects.name: 仙鹤寺
projects.level: 第四批省级文物保护单位（1995年），不对个人开放
projects.level_en: 4th Batch Provincial Cultural Heritage Site (1995), not open to individuals
projects.address_en: No. 111 Nanmen Street
highlights: 仙鹤寺是一座历史悠久的清真寺南宋咸淳年间伊斯兰先贤普哈丁筑明洪武二十三年1390年重建与广州怀圣寺泉州麒麟寺和杭州凤凰寺并称中国伊斯兰教四大名寺寺门朝东建筑格局有似仙鹤亮翅因而得名门如鹤首甬道为鹤颈大殿为鹤身两侧之半亭则如鹤翼殿后植两株古柏象征鹤腿最后以翠竹作为鹤尾寺内有传为南宋年间所植的银杏
projects.content_zh: 仙鹤寺是一座历史悠久的清真寺，南宋咸淳年间伊斯兰先贤普哈丁筑，明洪武二十三年（1390年）重建，与广州怀圣寺、泉州麒麟寺和杭州凤凰寺并称中国伊斯兰教四大名寺。寺门朝东，建筑格局有似仙鹤亮翅，因而得名：门如鹤首，甬道为鹤颈，大殿为鹤身，两侧之半亭则如鹤翼，殿后植两株古柏象征鹤腿，最后以翠竹作为鹤尾。寺内有传为南宋年间所植的银杏。
projects.content_en: Crane Mosque is a mosque with a long history, built by the Islamic sage Puhaddin during the Xianchun reign of the Southern Song, and rebuilt in the 23rd year of Hongwu of the Ming (1390); together with the Huaisheng Mosque in Guangzhou, the Qilin Mosque in Quanzhou, and the Fenghuang Mosque in Hangzhou, it is called one of the four famous mosques of Chinese Islam. The temple gate faces east, and the architectural layout resembles a crane spreading its wings, hence the name: the gate is like the crane's head, the corridor is the crane's neck, the main hall is the crane's body, the half-pavilions on both sides are like the crane's wings, two ancient cypresses planted behind the hall symbolize the crane's legs, and finally green bamboo serves as the crane's tail. Inside the temple there is a ginkgo tree traditionally said to have been planted during the Southern Song.

projects.name: 阮元家庙及宅第
projects.name_en: Ruan Yuan's Family Temple and Residence
projects.level: 第五批省级文物保护单位（2002年）
projects.level_en: 5th Batch Provincial Cultural Heritage Site (2002)
projects.address_en: No. 8 Yuxian Street
highlights: 阮元17641849字伯元为清代名臣曾任湖广两广云贵总督体仁阁大学士清道光十八年1838年致仕退休时由于他是乾嘉道三朝元老九省疆臣文经武纬加太子太保衔道光帝称赞他极三朝之宠遇为一代之完人清道光二十六年1846年阮元晋升太傅位列三公阮元在政事经史金石等方面都成就极高他的名字曾引起嘉庆皇帝的兴趣问古代可有类似的名字他答曰伊尹帝嘉其志冷庐杂识卷一阮元家庙位于住宅西侧清嘉庆八年1803年建坐北朝南有临街照壁头门厅二门厅享堂和文选井等庙前毓贤街原名太傅街因阮元官至太傅而得名在家庙东侧毓贤街12号有扬州市保单位怡庐正在修缮庭院颇为精雅家庙南侧旌忠巷2号有市保单位旌忠寺传为文选楼旧址在公道桥清嘉庆五年1800年建有阮家祠堂今已不存阮元及其家族墓地位于邗江区槐泗镇槐子村始建于明天启年间前后共安葬阮氏五代及附葬者20余人是清代一处重要墓葬群墓群北面1里左右为阮元误定的隋炀帝陵
projects.content_zh: 阮元（1764—1849），字伯元，为清代名臣，曾任湖广、两广、云贵总督，体仁阁大学士，清道光十八年（1838年）致仕退休时，由于他是乾嘉道三朝元老、九省疆臣、文经武纬，加太子太保衔。道光帝称赞他"极三朝之宠遇，为一代之完人"，清道光二十六年（1846年）阮元晋升太傅，位列三公。阮元在政事、经史、金石等方面都成就极高，他的名字曾引起嘉庆皇帝的兴趣，问古代可有类似的名字，他答曰"伊尹"，帝嘉其志（《冷庐杂识·卷一》）。阮元家庙位于住宅西侧，清嘉庆八年（1803年）建，坐北朝南，有临街照壁、头门厅、二门厅、享堂和文选井等。庙前毓贤街原名太傅街，因阮元官至太傅而得名。在家庙东侧，毓贤街12号有扬州市保单位怡庐，正在修缮，庭院颇为精雅。家庙南侧旌忠巷2号有市保单位旌忠寺，传为文选楼旧址。在公道桥清嘉庆五年（1800年）建有阮家祠堂，今已不存。阮元及其家族墓地位于邗江区槐泗镇槐子村，始建于明天启年间，前后共安葬阮氏五代及附葬者20余人，是清代一处重要墓葬群。墓群北面1里左右为阮元误定的隋炀帝陵。
projects.content_en: Ruan Yuan (1764-1849), courtesy name Boyuan, was a famous official of the Qing Dynasty, having served as Governor-General of Huguang, Liangguang, and Yun-Gui, and Grand Secretary of the Tiren Cabinet; when he retired in the 18th year of Daoguang of the Qing (1838), because he was a senior official of three reigns (Qianlong, Jiaqing, Daoguang), governor of nine provinces, and both literary and military, he was given the title of Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent. Emperor Daoguang praised him as "enjoying the utmost favor of three reigns, a complete man of his generation"; in the 26th year of Daoguang (1846), Ruan Yuan was promoted to Grand Tutor, ranking among the Three Dukes. Ruan Yuan achieved extremely high accomplishments in government affairs, classics and history, and epigraphy etc.; his name once aroused the interest of Emperor Jiaqing, who asked if there were similar names in ancient times; he answered "Yi Yin," and the emperor praised his ambition ("Lenglu Zashi" Volume 1). Ruan Yuan's Family Temple is located west of the residence, built in the 8th year of Jiaqing of the Qing (1803), facing south with its back to north, with a street-facing screen wall, first gate hall, second gate hall, worship hall, and Wenxuan Well etc. Yuxian Street in front of the temple was originally named Taifu (Grand Tutor) Street, named because Ruan Yuan rose to the rank of Grand Tutor. East of the family temple, at No. 12 Yuxian Street, is the Yangzhou municipal protected unit Yilu, currently under renovation, with a quite elegant courtyard. South of the family temple, at No. 2 Jingzhong Lane, is the municipal protected unit Jingzhong Temple, traditionally said to be the former site of the Wenxuan (Literary Selection) Tower. At Gongdao Bridge, in the 5th year of Jiaqing of the Qing (1800), the Ruan Family Ancestral Hall was built, today no longer existing. Ruan Yuan and his family's cemetery is located in Huaizi Village, Huaisi Town, Hanjiang District, first built during the Tianqi reign of the Ming, burying five generations of the Ruan family and over 20 accompanying burials in total—an important Qing Dynasty burial group. About 1 li north of the burial group is the Tomb of Emperor Yang of Sui, mistakenly identified by Ruan Yuan.

projects.name: 文昌阁—舍利塔—四望亭
projects.name_en: Wenchang Pavilion, Sarira Pagoda, Siwang Pavilion
projects.level: 省保单位（2011年）
projects.level_en: Provincial Protected Unit (2011)
projects.address: 汶河路、文昌路、石塔路、四望亭路
projects.address_en: Wenhe Road, Wenchang Road, Shita Road, Siwangting Road
highlights: 文昌阁位于汶河路文昌路交叉处始建于明万历十三年1585年万历二十四年1596年重建清代重修阁为八角三层形似天坛祈年殿2011年列为省保单位舍利塔木兰院舍利塔位于石塔路为市保建筑始建于唐开成三年838年原在扬州西门外古木兰院内南宋移建于今址清乾隆年间重修增建石栏这是一座仿木楼阁式青石塔六角五层较为精美四望亭四望亭位于四望亭路东首汶河路西侧为市保建筑据明万历江都县志引宋宝佑志记载四望亭在州治南宁宗嘉定年间特授直宝谟阁权发遣扬州事主管淮东安抚司事崔与之建认为此亭为南宋崔与之所建但清乾隆江都县志则认为此亭始建于明嘉靖三十八年1559年也称文奎楼魁星阁是江都县学的一部分四望亭为砖木结构八角三层攒尖顶底层四面开门与街道相通又称过街亭二三层可供登临欣赏市区景色
projects.content_zh: 1. 文昌阁：位于汶河路、文昌路交叉处，始建于明万历十三年（1585年），万历二十四年（1596年）重建，清代重修，阁为八角三层，形似天坛祈年殿，2011年列为省保单位。2. 舍利塔：木兰院舍利塔位于石塔路，为市保建筑，始建于唐开成三年（838年），原在扬州西门外古木兰院内，南宋移建于今址，清乾隆年间重修，增建石栏。这是一座仿木楼阁式青石塔，六角五层，较为精美。3. 四望亭：四望亭位于四望亭路东首，汶河路西侧，为市保建筑。据明万历《江都县志》引宋《宝佑志》记载"四望亭在州治南，宁宗嘉定年间特授直宝谟阁、权发遣扬州事、主管淮东安抚司事崔与之建"，认为此亭为南宋崔与之所建。但清乾隆《江都县志》则认为此亭始建于明嘉靖三十八年（1559年），也称文奎楼、魁星阁，是江都县学的一部分。四望亭为砖木结构，八角三层攒尖顶。底层四面开门与街道相通，又称"过街亭"。二、三层可供登临，欣赏市区景色。
projects.content_en: 1. Wenchang Pavilion: Located at the intersection of Wenhe Road and Wenchang Road, first built in the 13th year of Wanli of the Ming (1585), rebuilt in the 24th year of Wanli (1596), and repaired in the Qing; the pavilion is octagonal with three stories, resembling the Hall of Prayer for Good Harvests at the Temple of Heaven, designated a provincial protected unit in 2011. 2. Sarira Pagoda: The Mulan Courtyard Sarira Pagoda is located on Shita Road, a municipal protected building, first built in the 3rd year of Kaicheng of the Tang (838), originally in the ancient Mulan Courtyard outside the west gate of Yangzhou, moved to today's site in the Southern Song, repaired during the Qianlong reign of the Qing with a stone railing added. This is an imitation-wood pavilion-style bluestone pagoda, hexagonal with five stories, quite exquisite. 3. Siwang (Four-View) Pavilion: Siwang Pavilion is located at the east end of Siwangting Road, west of Wenhe Road, a municipal protected building. According to the Ming Wanli "Jiangdu County Gazetteer" quoting the Song "Baoyou Records," "Siwang Pavilion is south of the prefectural government; during the Jiading reign of Emperor Ningzong, it was built by Cui Yuzhi, who was specially appointed as Direct Baomo Ge, Acting Prefect of Yangzhou, and Director of the Huaidong Pacification Commission," believing this pavilion was built by Cui Yuzhi of the Southern Song. But the Qing Qianlong "Jiangdu County Gazetteer" believes this pavilion was first built in the 38th year of Jiajing of the Ming (1559), also called Wenkui Tower or Kuixing Pavilion, part of the Jiangdu County School. Siwang Pavilion is a brick-wood structure, octagonal with a three-story pyramidal roof. The ground floor has doors on all four sides connecting with the streets, also called the "Street-Crossing Pavilion." The second and third floors can be climbed to admire the city scenery.

projects.name: 西方寺大殿（扬州八怪纪念馆）
projects.name_en: Main Hall of Xifang Temple (Shrine of Yangzhou Eight Eccentrics)
projects.level: 第三批省级文物保护单位（1982年）
projects.level_en: 3rd Batch Provincial Cultural Heritage Site (1982)
projects.address_en: No. 18 Tuoling Lane
highlights: 西方寺为扬州八大名刹之一始建于唐永贞元年805年明洪武五年1372年重建清咸丰三年1853年除大殿外皆毁于火这座大殿采用重檐歇山顶楠木梁柱保存完好局部有明代彩绘平面接近方形宽五间深五进外圈柱距很小有似于周围廊但墙壁隔扇皆设在四周檐柱上使立面梢间显得很窄反映了江南殿堂建筑的典型特征清乾隆年间扬州八怪之一的金农曾在寺内度过晚今年今辟为扬州八怪纪念馆
projects.content_zh: 西方寺为扬州八大名刹之一，始建于唐永贞元年（805年），明洪武五年（1372年）重建，清咸丰三年（1853年）除大殿外皆毁于火。这座大殿采用重檐歇山顶，楠木梁柱保存完好，局部有明代彩绘。平面接近方形，宽五间，深五进。外圈柱距很小，有似于周围廊，但墙壁、隔扇皆设在四周檐柱上，使立面梢间显得很窄，反映了江南殿堂建筑的典型特征。清乾隆年间，扬州八怪之一的金农曾在寺内度过晚年，今辟为扬州八怪纪念馆。
projects.content_en: Xifang (Western) Temple is one of the eight famous temples of Yangzhou, first built in the 1st year of Yongzhen of the Tang (805), rebuilt in the 5th year of Hongwu of the Ming (1372); in the 3rd year of Xianfeng of the Qing (1853), everything except the main hall was destroyed by fire. This main hall adopts a double-eave hip-and-gable roof, with nanmu beams and columns well preserved, and local Ming Dynasty painted decorations. The plan is nearly square, five bays wide and five bays deep. The outer column spacing is very small, resembling a surrounding corridor, but the walls and lattice doors are all set on the surrounding eave columns, making the end bays of the facade appear very narrow—reflecting the typical characteristics of Jiangnan hall architecture. During the Qianlong reign of the Qing, Jin Nong, one of the Eight Eccentrics of Yangzhou, spent his later years in the temple; today it has been opened as the Memorial Hall of the Eight Eccentrics of Yangzhou.

projects.name: 罗聘故居（朱草诗林）
projects.name_en: Former Residence of Luo Pin (Alkanet and Poetic Realm)
projects.level: 第七批省级文物保护单位（2011年）
projects.level_en: 7th Batch Provincial Cultural Heritage Site (2011)
projects.address_en: No. 46 Mituo Lane, Guangling District
highlights: 罗聘17331799是扬州八怪之一年纪最小有八怪殿军之称擅画人物佛像与山水花卉最出色的是鬼趣图这处故居建于清乾隆年间罗聘自题朱草诗林与夫人方婉仪17321779在此吟诗作画被誉为画坛伉俪当时金农郑燮高翔汪士慎等都住在附近常到此雅集论画如今故居中的书斋香叶草堂和半亭倦鸟巢保存良好已辟为罗聘纪念馆展览罗聘的生平和作品
projects.content_zh: 罗聘（1733—1799）是"扬州八怪"之一，年纪最小，有"八怪殿军"之称，擅画人物佛像与山水花卉，最出色的是《鬼趣图》。这处故居建于清乾隆年间，罗聘自题"朱草诗林"，与夫人方婉仪（1732—1779）在此吟诗作画，被誉为"画坛伉俪"。当时金农、郑燮、高翔、汪士慎等都住在附近，常到此雅集论画。如今故居中的书斋"香叶草堂"和半亭"倦鸟巢"保存良好，已辟为罗聘纪念馆，展览罗聘的生平和作品。
projects.content_en: Luo Pin (1733-1799) was one of the "Eight Eccentrics of Yangzhou," the youngest, known as the "rear guard of the Eight Eccentrics"; he excelled in painting figures, Buddhist images, landscapes, flowers, and plants, with his most outstanding work being the "Ghost Amusement Paintings." This former residence was built during the Qianlong reign of the Qing; Luo Pin himself inscribed it "Zhucao Shilin" (Alkanet and Poetic Realm), and with his wife Fang Wanyi (1732-1779) he composed poetry and painted here, hailed as a "couple in the art world." At that time, Jin Nong, Zheng Xie, Gao Xiang, Wang Shishen etc. all lived nearby and often came here for elegant gatherings to discuss painting. Today the study "Xiangye Thatched Hall" and the half-pavilion "Juanniao Chao" (Tired Bird's Nest) in the former residence are well preserved, and it has been opened as the Luo Pin Memorial Hall, exhibiting Luo Pin's life and works.

projects.name: 史可法墓祠
projects.name_en: Tomb and Shrine of Shi Kefa
projects.level: 第七批省级文物保护单位（2011年）
projects.level_en: 7th Batch Provincial Cultural Heritage Site (2011)
projects.address: 维扬区广储门外梅花岭西麓
projects.address_en: Western foot of Meihua Ridge, outside Guangchu Gate, Weiyang District
highlights: 明万历二十年1592年扬州守令吴秀以浚河之土堆筑成山环山种梅民间呼为梅花岭岭周围布置楼台池沼总名偕乐园是当时一处游览胜地每佳晨韶景士女游观者轮蹄摩击无虚日后来官府压制冶游之风改作崇雅书院万历扬州府志卷21史可法16021645字宪之明末任南京兵部尚书北京沦陷后以兵部尚书兼东阁大学士督师扬州清顺治二年1645年清军包围扬州战前史可法嘱托嗣子史德威我死当葬梅花岭上扬州城破后史可法被执拒降不屈而死史德威遍寻遗骸不可得只好将其衣冠葬在岭上此地遂成为后人缅怀史公之地如清代全祖望梅花岭记所言圣贤家法其气浩然长留天地之间……百年而后予登岭上与客述忠烈遗言无不泪下如雨想见当日围城光景此即忠烈之面目宛然可遇当年在刚攻克扬州后清军将领多铎就在城内建祠纪念史可法清雍正十二年1734年个园主人马曰琯在岭东捐建梅花书院增建祠宇亭榭乾隆皇帝将史可法作为忠君忠国的榜样谥为忠正并在墓西建祠李斗扬州画舫录卷四描述了乾隆年间此地的景致古梅花岭旧址无考今因重宁寺旁土阜增而成岭皆土山间石石骨暴露任石之怪不加斧凿锋棱如削飘然有云姿鹤态栽梅花数百株皆玉蝶种花比十亩梅园迟开一月极高处有山亭六角花时便不见亭太平天国时期墓祠毁于战火清同治九年1870年重建文革时期墓冢被夷平后来复原今包括墓祠园三部分东部为墓南侧大门临河门额书史公墓三字入门庭院两侧为碑廊北部正中是飨堂门外悬张尔荩撰写的名联数点梅花亡国泪二分明月故臣心堂内置1985年塑的史可法坐像两边的生有自来文信国死而后已武乡侯楹联将史可法与文天祥诸葛亮并称堂东偏院有百年金桂桂前建桂花厅厅南是一处小园黄石花坛内植紫藤木香芍药丛桂等绿荫满庭并建有芍药亭和牡丹阁飨堂北为史可法衣冠墓墓前立牌坊与三面围墙形成墓地牌坊北部正中立青石墓碑上镌明督师兵部尚书兼东阁大学士史可法之墓墓后两边院墙各开一道月洞门额题梅花岭即为门后的土岭岭上遍植梅花象征史可法的铮铮风骨岭东为二层歇山顶的梅花仙馆可循石级登上二层欣赏腊梅湖石岭西北是单檐歇山顶的晴雪轩轩内墙壁上嵌史可法的复睿亲王多尔衮书遗书肖像及墨迹石刻等又称遗墨厅梅花岭东西横亘中部叠筑假山下有石洞可供穿行岭南开凿水池构成一处宜人的花园由花园西侧向南是史公祠南为祠门北为祠堂内悬史可法遗像向东与响堂相通史可法与岳飞文天祥齐名这处墓祠集建筑园林于一体是开展爱国主义和民族气节教育的重要场所
projects.content_zh: 明万历二十年（1592年）扬州守令吴秀以浚河之土堆筑成山，环山种梅，民间呼为梅花岭。岭周围布置楼台池沼，总名偕乐园，是当时一处游览胜地，"每佳晨韶景，士女游观者轮蹄摩击无虚日"。后来官府压制冶游之风，改作崇雅书院（万历《扬州府志》卷21）。史可法（1602—1645）字宪之，明末任南京兵部尚书，北京沦陷后以兵部尚书兼东阁大学士督师扬州。清顺治二年（1645年）清军包围扬州，战前史可法嘱托嗣子史德威："我死，当葬梅花岭上。"扬州城破后，史可法被执拒降，不屈而死。史德威遍寻遗骸不可得，只好将其衣冠葬在岭上。此地遂成为后人缅怀史公之地，如清代全祖望《梅花岭记》所言："圣贤家法，其气浩然，长留天地之间。……百年而后，予登岭上，与客述忠烈遗言，无不泪下如雨，想见当日围城光景，此即忠烈之面目，宛然可遇。"当年在刚攻克扬州后，清军将领多铎就在城内建祠纪念史可法。清雍正十二年（1734年）个园主人马曰琯在岭东捐建"梅花书院"，增建祠宇亭榭。乾隆皇帝将史可法作为忠君忠国的榜样，谥为"忠正"，并在墓西建祠。李斗《扬州画舫录》卷四描述了乾隆年间此地的景致："古梅花岭旧址无考，今因重宁寺旁土阜增而成岭。皆土山间石，石骨暴露，任石之怪，不加斧凿，锋棱如削，飘然有云姿鹤态。栽梅花数百株，皆玉蝶种，花比十亩梅园迟开一月，极高处有山亭，六角，花时便不见亭。"太平天国时期墓祠毁于战火，清同治九年（1870年）重建，"文革"时期墓冢被夷平，后来复原。今包括墓、祠、园三部分。东部为墓，南侧大门临河，门额书"史公墓"三字。入门庭院两侧为碑廊，北部正中是飨堂，门外悬张尔荩撰写的名联"数点梅花亡国泪，二分明月故臣心"，堂内置1985年塑的史可法坐像，两边的"生有自来文信国，死而后已武乡侯"楹联，将史可法与文天祥、诸葛亮并称。堂东偏院有百年金桂，桂前建桂花厅，厅南是一处小园，黄石花坛内植紫藤、木香、芍药、丛桂等，绿荫满庭，并建有芍药亭和牡丹阁。飨堂北为史可法衣冠墓，墓前立牌坊，与三面围墙形成墓地，牌坊北部正中立青石墓碑，上镌"明督师兵部尚书兼东阁大学士史可法之墓"。墓后两边院墙各开一道月洞门，额题"梅花岭"，即为门后的土岭。岭上遍植梅花，象征史可法的铮铮风骨。岭东为二层歇山顶的梅花仙馆，可循石级登上二层，欣赏腊梅、湖石；岭西北是单檐歇山顶的晴雪轩，轩内墙壁上嵌史可法的"复睿亲王多尔衮书"、遗书、肖像及墨迹石刻等，又称"遗墨厅"。梅花岭东西横亘，中部叠筑假山，下有石洞可供穿行，岭南开凿水池，构成一处宜人的花园。由花园西侧向南是史公祠，南为祠门，北为祠堂，内悬史可法遗像，向东与响堂相通。史可法与岳飞、文天祥齐名，这处墓祠集建筑、园林于一体，是开展爱国主义和民族气节教育的重要场所。
projects.content_en: In the 20th year of Wanli of the Ming (1592), Wu Xiu, Magistrate of Yangzhou, piled the soil from dredging the river into a mountain, planting plum trees around it, commonly called Meihua (Plum Blossom) Ridge. Around the ridge, towers, terraces, ponds, and marshes were arranged, collectively named Xiele (Joy Together) Garden, a tourist attraction at that time: "Every fine morning and beautiful scene, scholars and women tourists came with wheels and hooves rubbing against each other, without an empty day." Later, the authorities suppressed the atmosphere of pleasure-seeking and changed it into the Chongya Academy (Wanli "Yangzhou Prefecture Gazetteer" Volume 21). Shi Kefa (1602-1645), courtesy name Xianzhi, served as Minister of War of Nanjing in the late Ming; after the fall of Beijing, he supervised the army in Yangzhou as Minister of War and Grand Secretary of the Dongge Cabinet. In the 2nd year of Shunzhi of the Qing (1645), Qing troops surrounded Yangzhou; before the battle, Shi Kefa instructed his adopted son Shi Dewei: "When I die, bury me on Plum Blossom Ridge." After Yangzhou fell, Shi Kefa was captured, refused to surrender, and died unyielding. Shi Dewei searched everywhere for his remains but could not find them, so he had to bury his official hat and robes on the ridge. This place thus became a site for later generations to remember Lord Shi, as stated in Qing person Quan Zuwang's "Record of Plum Blossom Ridge": "The sage's family code, his qi is浩然 and remains between heaven and earth for a long time... A hundred years later, I climbed the ridge and, with guests, recounted the loyal martyr's last words; none did not weep like rain, imagining the scene of the city under siege that day—this is the loyal martyr's face, as if vividly encountered." That year, just after capturing Yangzhou, the Qing general Dodo built a shrine in the city to commemorate Shi Kefa. In the 12th year of Yongzheng of the Qing (1734), Ma Yueguan, owner of Geyuan Garden, donated to build the "Plum Blossom Academy" east of the ridge, adding shrine buildings and pavilions. Emperor Qianlong took Shi Kefa as a model of loyalty to the monarch and country, posthumously titling him "Zhongzheng" (Loyal and Upright), and built a shrine west of the tomb. Li Dou's "Yangzhou Huafang Lu" Volume 4 describes the scenery here during the Qianlong reign: "The old site of Plum Blossom Ridge is untraceable; today it was increased into a ridge because of the earth mound beside Chongning Temple. It is all earth mountain with interspersed stones, with stone bones exposed; letting the stones be strange, without chiseling, the edges and corners are as if cut, floating with cloud posture and crane demeanor. Several hundred plum trees are planted, all of the Yudie (Jade Butterfly) variety; their flowers bloom a month later than the ten-mu plum garden; at the highest point there is a hexagonal mountain pavilion, and when flowers bloom the pavilion cannot be seen." During the Taiping Rebellion the tomb and shrine were destroyed by war fires, rebuilt in the 9th year of Tongzhi of the Qing (1870); during the Cultural Revolution the tomb was leveled, later restored. Today it includes three parts: tomb, shrine, and garden. The eastern part is the tomb; the south gate faces the river, with the gate lintel inscribed with the three characters "Shi Gong's Tomb." Entering the gate, both sides of the courtyard are stele corridors; in the center north is the Xiangtang (Banquet Hall), with the famous couplet written by Zhang Erjin hanging outside: "A few dots of plum blossoms—tears of a fallen nation; two parts of bright moonlight—the heart of a loyal former minister"; inside the hall is a seated statue of Shi Kefa sculpted in 1985, and on both sides the couplet "Born like Wen Tianxiang, died like Zhuge Liang" compares Shi Kefa with Wen Tianxiang and Zhuge Liang. East of the hall, in a side courtyard, is a century-old golden osmanthus; in front of the osmanthus is the Osmanthus Hall; south of the hall is a small garden, with yellow-stone flower terraces planted with wisteria, rosewood, peonies, and clustered osmanthus etc., with green shade filling the courtyard, and a Peony Pavilion and Peony Pavilion built. North of the Xiangtang is Shi Kefa's cenotaph (hat-and-robe tomb); in front of the tomb stands an archway, forming a burial ground with three-sided walls; in the center north of the archway stands a bluestone tombstone, engraved with "Tomb of Shi Kefa, Ming Supervisor of Army, Minister of War, and Grand Secretary of the Dongge Cabinet." Behind the tomb, each side of the courtyard wall opens a moon gate, inscribed "Plum Blossom Ridge," which is the earth mound behind the gate. Plum trees are planted all over the ridge, symbolizing Shi Kefa's unyielding integrity. East of the ridge is the two-story hip-and-gable roof Plum Blossom Immortal Hall, where one can climb stone steps to the second floor to admire wintersweet and Taihu stones; northwest of the ridge is the single-eave hip-and-gable roof Qingxue (Clear Snow) Studio, whose inner walls are embedded with Shi Kefa's "Letter in Reply to Prince Regent Dorgon," last letters, portraits, and calligraphy stone carvings etc., also called the "Posthumous Ink Hall." Plum Blossom Ridge stretches east-west, with a rockery stacked in the middle, and a stone cave below for passage; south of the ridge a pond is dug, forming a pleasant garden. From the west side of the garden southward is the Shi Gong Shrine, with the shrine gate to the south and the shrine hall to the north, hanging a portrait of Shi Kefa, connected eastward to the Xiangtang. Shi Kefa is as famous as Yue Fei and Wen Tianxiang; this tomb and shrine integrates architecture and garden, an important place for patriotism and national integrity education.

projects.name: 扬州重宁寺
projects.level: 第七批省级文物保护单位（2011年）
projects.level_en: 7th Batch Provincial Cultural Heritage Site (2011)
projects.address_en: No. 15 West Changzheng Road
highlights: 清乾隆四十八年1783年扬州盐商为庆祝乾隆帝寿辰集资筹建重宁寺次年乾隆第六次南巡即驻跸于此赐万寿重宁寺碑记称合万姓之寿以为寿所以万寿也以下民之宁以为宁所以为重宁也八怪中的罗聘曾绘制寺内壁画清咸丰年间寺庙毁于兵火晚清重建寺内大雄宝殿建于清光绪十七年1891年五开间重檐歇山顶内有八根名贵的铁梨木方柱皆高15米以上殿内天花藻井上有精美彩绘今为某单位办公场所不开放
projects.content_zh: 清乾隆四十八年（1783年），扬州盐商为庆祝乾隆帝寿辰，集资筹建重宁寺，次年乾隆第六次南巡即驻跸于此，赐《万寿重宁寺碑记》，称"合万姓之寿以为寿，所以万寿也；以下民之宁以为宁，所以为重宁也"。八怪中的罗聘曾绘制寺内壁画。清咸丰年间寺庙毁于兵火，晚清重建。寺内大雄宝殿建于清光绪十七年（1891年），五开间，重檐歇山顶，内有八根名贵的铁梨木方柱，皆高15米以上，殿内天花、藻井上有精美彩绘。今为某单位办公场所，不开放。
projects.content_en: In the 48th year of Qianlong of the Qing (1783), Yangzhou salt merchants, to celebrate Emperor Qianlong's birthday, raised funds to build Chongning Temple; the following year, on his sixth southern tour, Qianlong stayed here, bestowing the "Stele Record of Wanshou Chongning Temple," stating: "Combining the longevity of all surnames as longevity, hence ten thousand longevity; combining the peace of the lower people as peace, hence heavy peace." Luo Pin, one of the Eight Eccentrics, once painted murals inside the temple. During the Xianfeng reign of the Qing, the temple was destroyed by war fires and rebuilt in the late Qing. The Mahavira Hall in the temple was built in the 17th year of Guangxu of the Qing (1891), five bays wide with a double-eave hip-and-gable roof; inside are eight precious iron pear wood square columns, all over 15 meters high, with exquisite painted decorations on the ceiling and coffered ceiling. Today it is the office of a certain unit and not open to the public.

projects.name: 天宁寺
projects.level: 第三批省级文物保护单位（1982年）
projects.level_en: 3rd Batch Provincial Cultural Heritage Site (1982)
projects.address_en: No. 3 Fengle Shang Street, Guangling District
highlights: 天宁寺为扬州八大古刹之首据传东晋太元十年385年谢安镇守广陵曾在此居住后来舍宅为寺东晋义熙十四年418年尼泊尔高僧在此译华严经北宋政和二年1112年宋徽宗赐名天宁禅寺康熙六次南巡皆驻跸天宁寺并命曹寅在寺内设书局刊刻全唐诗乾隆在寺西建御码头乾隆游瘦西湖登船处行宫和御花园以及储藏四库全书古今图书集成的文汇阁众多建筑和图书皆毁于太平天国战火今寺重建于清同治四年1865年有山门天王殿大雄宝殿华严阁和藏经楼万佛楼等现为扬州博物馆
projects.content_zh: 天宁寺为扬州八大古刹之首。据传东晋太元十年（385年）谢安镇守广陵曾在此居住，后来舍宅为寺。东晋义熙十四年（418年）尼泊尔高僧在此译《华严经》。北宋政和二年（1112年），宋徽宗赐名"天宁禅寺"。康熙六次南巡皆驻跸天宁寺，并命曹寅在寺内设书局，刊刻《全唐诗》。乾隆在寺西建御码头（乾隆游瘦西湖登船处）、行宫和御花园，以及储藏《四库全书》《古今图书集成》的文汇阁。众多建筑和图书皆毁于太平天国战火，今寺重建于清同治四年（1865年），有山门、天王殿、大雄宝殿、华严阁和藏经楼（万佛楼）等，现为扬州博物馆。
projects.content_en: Tianning Temple is the first of the eight ancient temples of Yangzhou. Legend says that in the 10th year of Taiyuan of the Eastern Jin (385), Xie An, when guarding Guangling, once lived here and later donated his residence as a temple. In the 14th year of Yixi of the Eastern Jin (418), a Nepalese eminent monk translated the "Avatamsaka Sutra" here. In the 2nd year of Zhenghe of the Northern Song (1112), Emperor Huizong bestowed the name "Tianning Chan Temple." On all six of his southern tours, Kangxi stayed at Tianning Temple and ordered Cao Yin to set up a book bureau in the temple to print the "Complete Tang Poems." Qianlong built an imperial dock (where Qianlong boarded a boat to tour Slender West Lake), an imperial palace, and an imperial garden west of the temple, as well as the Wenhui Pavilion storing the "Complete Library in Four Sections" and the "Gujin Tushu Jicheng" (Complete Collection of Ancient and Modern Books). Many buildings and books were destroyed in the Taiping Rebellion wars; today's temple was rebuilt in the 4th year of Tongzhi of the Qing (1865), with a mountain gate, Heavenly King Hall, Mahavira Hall, Huayan Pavilion, and Scripture Library (Ten-Thousand-Buddha Tower) etc., now the Yangzhou Museum.

projects.name: 瘦西湖
projects.level: 国家重点风景名胜区
