projects.address_en: Northwest suburb of Yangzhou City
highlights: 瘦西湖原名保障河扬州西北郊的山洪雨水经此汇入大运河很早就成为郊游胜地到清代乾隆年间盐商趁皇帝南巡之际极力兴造最称繁盛扬州人通常乘舟从城北门出欣赏沿途风光清代文人沈复17631825在浮生六记中点评道行其途有八九里虽全是人功而奇思幻想点缀天然即阆苑瑶池琼楼玉宇谅不过此其妙处在十余家之园亭合而为一联络至山气势俱贯金安清18171880水窗春呓也称两岸数十里楼台相接无一处重复并认为最佳处在虹桥迤西一转小金山矗其南五亭桥镇其中而白塔一区雄伟古朴往往夕阳返照萧鼓灯船如入汉宫图画瘦西湖小秦淮小金山这些名字贴切形容出扬州风景的灵秀之美今瘦西湖风景区东起天宁寺前御码头经冶春园卷石洞天西园曲水为第一段水道较窄折向北由虹桥揽胜经长堤春柳荷浦薰风桃花坞冶春后社徐园和四桥烟雨长春桥春波桥莲花桥和玉版桥为第二段水面渐宽由四桥烟雨折向西先后经过小金山钓鱼台凫庄五亭桥和莲性寺白塔直抵西端熙春台为第三段景致最为集中水系由此再度向北经二十四桥石壁流淙蜀冈朝旭和小吹台为第四段较为疏野有天然风味其中梅岭春深莲花桥和熙春台为三大景观节点以中段的吹台白塔凫庄和莲花桥最为精彩莲花桥和白塔莲性寺建于元代当时叫法海寺市民出城游玩常先在此泊舟拜佛寺址四周环水形如莲花更奇的是寺北高起一座土丘风水家称山脉来自北边蜀冈迤逦穿水而过与寺址相接宛如莲花的枝茎这条莲茎最初是座河堤称莲花堤人们相信其为寺庙命脉所系晚明之际一名杨姓宦官筑保扬城废堤为桥并阻断了寺西河水导致堤断脉伤而寺之殿宇日渐圮废入清后人们挖开河障改桥为堤并培高被视作寺脉的土丘次第兴建楼殿使寺庙粲然复兴乡人感慨地脉效灵形象之言不爽也1705年康熙南巡正式赐名莲性寺白塔位于寺北建于清乾隆年间模仿北京北海的白塔下为方形台座有梯可登中为喇嘛式白色塔身南面设龛室顶上是由十三重相轮伞盖和宝珠组成的塔刹徐珂清稗类钞讲述了建造白塔的戏剧性过程据说乾隆南巡时游玩至此对左右随从说此地景致颇似西苑的琼岛春阴可惜缺座白塔当时负责接驾的盐商江春听闻此言亟以千金贿近侍请他们画出北海白塔的状貌然后依图修建一夜就建成了第二天乾隆又来游玩见塔巍然大异之以为伪既至果砖石所成询知其故叹曰盐商之财力伟哉这个故事有夸张之处但却恰当地表现了扬州盐商的富足令皇帝都感到惊佩莲花桥位于原莲花堤的位置1757年为迎接乾隆南巡方便御舟行驶两淮盐政高恒改堤为桥为了延续莲脉又不阻断水上行舟采用了罕见的十五孔桥形式桥身和四翼下部各有3个桥洞总共15个扬州揽胜录描述了满月之夜的奇观三五之夕皓月当空每洞各衔一月计十五洞共得十五月金色漾藻众月争辉倒悬波心不可捉摸西湖之三潭印月不能专美于前此景特令扬州人自豪认为足可媲美西湖的三潭映月高恒还请名匠在桥上建了五座亭子因此又称五亭桥今桥为光绪年间重建
projects.content_zh: 瘦西湖原名保障河，扬州西北郊的山洪雨水经此汇入大运河，很早就成为郊游胜地。到清代乾隆年间，盐商趁皇帝南巡之际极力兴造，最称繁盛。扬州人通常乘舟从城北门出，欣赏沿途风光。清代文人沈复（1763—1825？）在《浮生六记》中点评道："行其途有八九里，虽全是人功，而奇思幻想，点缀天然，即阆苑瑶池，琼楼玉宇，谅不过此！其妙处在十余家之园亭合而为一，联络至山，气势俱贯。"金安清（1817—1880？）《水窗春呓》也称"两岸数十里楼台相接，无一处重复"，并认为最佳处"在虹桥迤西一转，小金山矗其南，五亭桥镇其中，而白塔一区，雄伟古朴。往往夕阳返照，萧鼓灯船，如入汉宫图画"。瘦西湖、小秦淮、小金山，这些名字贴切形容出扬州风景的灵秀之美。今瘦西湖风景区东起天宁寺前御码头，经冶春园、卷石洞天、西园曲水为第一段，水道较窄；折向北由虹桥揽胜经长堤春柳、荷浦薰风、桃花坞—冶春后社—徐园和四桥烟雨（长春桥、春波桥、莲花桥和玉版桥）为第二段，水面渐宽；由四桥烟雨折向西，先后经过小金山、钓鱼台、凫庄、五亭桥和莲性寺白塔，直抵西端熙春台为第三段，景致最为集中；水系由此再度向北，经二十四桥、石壁流淙、蜀冈朝旭和小吹台为第四段，较为疏野，有天然风味。其中梅岭春深、莲花桥和熙春台为三大景观节点，以中段的吹台、白塔、凫庄和莲花桥最为精彩。莲花桥和白塔：莲性寺建于元代，当时叫法海寺，市民出城游玩常先在此泊舟拜佛。寺址四周环水，形如莲花，更奇的是寺北高起一座土丘，风水家称山脉来自北边蜀冈，迤逦穿水而过与寺址相接，宛如莲花的枝茎。这条莲茎最初是座河堤，称莲花堤，人们相信其为寺庙命脉所系。晚明之际一名杨姓宦官筑保扬城，废堤为桥，并阻断了寺西河水，导致"堤断脉伤，而寺之殿宇，日渐圮废"。入清后人们挖开河障，改桥为堤，并培高被视作寺脉的土丘，次第兴建楼殿，使寺庙粲然复兴，乡人感慨"地脉效灵，形象之言不爽也"。1705年康熙南巡，正式赐名"莲性寺"。白塔位于寺北，建于清乾隆年间，模仿北京北海的白塔。下为方形台座，有梯可登；中为喇嘛式白色塔身，南面设龛室；顶上是由十三重相轮、伞盖和宝珠组成的塔刹。徐珂《清稗类钞》讲述了建造白塔的戏剧性过程：据说乾隆南巡时游玩至此，对左右随从说，此地景致颇似西苑的"琼岛春阴"，可惜缺座白塔。当时负责接驾的盐商江春听闻此言，"亟以千金贿近侍"，请他们画出北海白塔的状貌，然后依图修建，一夜就建成了。第二天乾隆又来游玩，"见塔巍然，大异之，以为伪。既至，果砖石所成。询知其故，叹曰：'盐商之财力伟哉！'"这个故事有夸张之处，但却恰当地表现了扬州盐商的富足，令皇帝都感到惊佩。莲花桥位于原莲花堤的位置，1757年为迎接乾隆南巡，方便御舟行驶，两淮盐政高恒改堤为桥。为了延续莲脉又不阻断水上行舟，采用了罕见的十五孔桥形式，桥身和四翼下部各有3个桥洞，总共15个。《扬州揽胜录》描述了满月之夜的奇观："三五之夕，皓月当空，每洞各衔一月，计十五洞，共得十五月，金色漾藻，众月争辉，倒悬波心，不可捉摸。西湖之三潭印月，不能专美于前。"此景特令扬州人自豪，认为足可媲美西湖的三潭映月。高恒还请名匠在桥上建了五座亭子，因此又称五亭桥。今桥为光绪年间重建。
projects.content_en: Slender West Lake was originally called Baozhang River; the mountain flood and rainwater from the northwest suburb of Yangzhou flows through it into the Grand Canal, and it early became an outing scenic spot. By the Qianlong reign of the Qing, salt merchants took advantage of the emperor's southern tours to vigorously build it, reaching its greatest prosperity. Yangzhou people usually took boats from the north gate of the city to admire the scenery along the way. Qing scholar Shen Fu (1763-1825?) commented in "Six Records of a Floating Life": "Traveling its path for eight or nine li, although entirely man-made, with wondrous thoughts and fantasies, embellished naturally—even the fairyland of Langyuan and Jade Pool, or the jade towers and jade pavilions, could hardly surpass this! Its beauty lies in the gardens and pavilions of over ten families merging into one, connecting to the mountain, with momentum all penetrating." Jin Anqing (1817-1880?) in "Shuichun Chuiyi" also said "for tens of li on both banks, towers and terraces connect, with no place repeated," and believed the best place is "at a turn west of Hongqiao, with Xiaojinshan standing tall to its south, Wuting Bridge in its middle, and the White Pagoda area, majestic and simple. Often at sunset with reflected light, with flute and drum lantern boats, it is like entering a Han palace painting." Slender West Lake, Xiaoqinhuai (Small Qinhuai), Xiaojinshan (Small Gold Mountain)—these names aptly describe the graceful beauty of Yangzhou's scenery. Today's Slender West Lake scenic area starts east at the imperial dock in front of Tianning Temple, passing through Yechun Garden, Juanshi Dongtian (Rolling Stone Cave Heaven), and Xiyuan Qushui (West Garden Winding Water) as the first section, with a relatively narrow waterway; turning north, from Hongqiao Lansheng (Hongqiao Embracing Scenery) through Changdi Chunliu (Long Embankment Spring Willows), Hepu Xunfeng (Lotus Pond Fragrant Wind), Taohuawu—Yechun Houshe—Xuyuan, and Siqiao Yanyu (Four Bridges Misty Rain) (Changchun Bridge, Chunbo Bridge, Lianhua Bridge, and Yuban Bridge) as the second section, with the water surface gradually widening; turning west from Siqiao Yanyu, successively passing Xiaojinshan, Diaoyutai (Fishing Terrace), Fuzhuang, Wuting Bridge, and the White Pagoda of Lianxing Temple, straight to Xichun Terrace at the west end as the third section, with the most concentrated scenery; from there the water system again goes north, through Ershisi Bridge (Twenty-Four Bridge), Shibi Liucong (Stone Wall Flowing Water), Shugang Zhaoxu (Shugang Morning Sun), and Xiaochuitai as the fourth section, relatively sparse and wild with natural flavor. Among them, Meiling Chunshen (Plum Ridge Deep Spring), Lianhua Bridge, and Xichun Terrace are three major scenic nodes, with the middle section's Chuitai, White Pagoda, Fuzhuang, and Lianhua Bridge the most wonderful. Lianhua Bridge and White Pagoda: Lianxing Temple was built in the Yuan Dynasty, then called Fahai Temple; citizens going out of the city for outings often first moored boats and worshipped Buddha here. The temple site is surrounded by water on all sides, shaped like a lotus; even more wonderful is a raised earth mound north of the temple, which feng shui experts say the mountain range comes from the northern Shugang, winding through the water to connect with the temple site, just like the stem of a lotus. This lotus stem was originally a river embankment called Lianhua (Lotus) Embankment, and people believed it was the lifeblood of the temple. In the late Ming, a eunuch surnamed Yang built the Baoyang City, abolishing the embankment and making it a bridge, and blocked the river west of the temple, causing "the embankment to break and the pulse to be injured, and the temple halls gradually fell into ruin." After entering the Qing, people dug open the river barrier, changed the bridge back to an embankment, and raised the earth mound regarded as the temple's pulse, successively building halls and pavilions, making the temple brilliantly revive; the townspeople sighed that "the earth pulse responds effectively, and the words of imagery are not wrong." In 1705, during Kangxi's southern tour, it was officially bestowed the name "Lianxing Temple." The White Pagoda is located north of the temple, built during the Qianlong reign of the Qing, imitating the White Pagoda of Beihai in Beijing. Below is a square platform base with a ladder for climbing; in the middle is a Lamaist-style white pagoda body, with a niche room on the south; on top is a pagoda finial composed of thirteen layers of harmika, umbrella canopy, and precious pearl. Xu Ke's "Qing Bai Lei Chao" tells the dramatic process of building the White Pagoda: It is said that during Qianlong's southern tour, when playing here, he said to his attendants that the scenery here is quite like the "Qiongdao Chunyin" (Jade Island Spring Shade) of the Western Garden, but unfortunately lacks a white pagoda. The salt merchant Jiang Chun, in charge of receiving the emperor, hearing this, "urgently bribed the close attendants with a thousand gold," asking them to draw the appearance of the Beihai White Pagoda, then built it according to the drawing, completing it in one night. The next day Qianlong came to play again, "seeing the pagoda towering, greatly surprised, thinking it was fake. Upon approaching, it was indeed made of bricks and stones. After inquiring the reason, he sighed: 'The financial power of salt merchants is mighty!'" This story has exaggerations, but it appropriately shows the wealth of Yangzhou salt merchants, which even the emperor found astonishing. Lianhua Bridge is located at the original Lianhua Embankment; in 1757, to welcome Qianlong's southern tour and facilitate the passage of the imperial boat, Gao Heng, Salt Commissioner of Lianghuai, changed the embankment into a bridge. To continue the lotus pulse without blocking water navigation, a rare fifteen-arch bridge form was adopted, with 3 arch holes each under the bridge body and four wings, totaling 15. "Yangzhou Lansheng Lu" describes the wonder on a full-moon night: "On the night of the fifteenth, the bright moon hangs in the sky; each arch holds a moon, totaling fifteen arches and fifteen moons, with golden color rippling in the algae, many moons competing in brilliance, hanging upside down in the wave center, unfathomable. The Three Pools Reflecting the Moon of West Lake cannot monopolize beauty before this." This scene especially makes Yangzhou people proud, believing it can rival the Three Pools Reflecting the Moon of West Lake. Gao Heng also asked famous craftsmen to build five pavilions on the bridge, hence also called Wuting (Five-Pavilion) Bridge. Today's bridge was rebuilt during the Guangxu reign.

highlights: 江苏地区以平原为主由北自山东入境一马平川扬州城北的蜀冈是沿途所见的第一座高丘蜀冈得名大致有三种说法第一种是风水家的形势说认为此冈是四川蜀山向东绵延的余脉如北宋梅尧臣所称冈形来自蜀山色去连吴南宋祝穆方舆胜览称旧传地脉通蜀故曰蜀冈第二种是江水说明刘绩霏雪录称山上有井其水味如蜀江号曰蜀冈第三种是字形说尔雅认为蜀意为独蜀冈的意思是一座独行之山各种说法为这座小山增添了许多趣味扬州人敝帚自珍将其媲美于苏州虎丘认为隔江南北两山相类蜀冈作为扬州不多的几块高地之一具有一定的防御优势历代多选择在此建城如春秋时期吴楚的邗城西汉的广陵城隋唐的扬州城也由于地势较高蜀冈成为供人登高望远的风景胜地今有大明寺平山堂和西园等景点大明寺第六批国保2006年大明寺始建于南朝宋孝武帝大明年间隋仁寿元年601年隋文帝诏海内立九层塔三十所庆祝他的六十大寿其中一所便是立在大明寺的扬州栖灵塔因此又称栖灵寺唐代高僧鉴真曾在此居住讲学并于天宝年间东渡日本创建唐招提寺成为日本律宗初祖1973年在寺东建造鉴真纪念堂由建筑学家梁思成设计唐末栖灵塔被火烧毁复称大明寺清初因讳改称栖灵寺清乾隆三十年1765年诏改法净寺现存建筑多为清同治九年1870年重建有山门大雄宝殿和藏经楼等平山堂平山堂位于大明寺西侧北宋庆历八年1048年欧阳修由滁州调任扬州趁公事余暇在蜀冈筑平山堂因能平望江南诸山而得名1056年刘攽出任扬州欧阳修填词相送追忆当年在堂内的文酒盛事称平山栏槛倚晴空山色有无中后有好事者调侃平山堂望江南诸山甚近拱列檐下若可攀取欧公言有无中莫非因为近视严有翼艺苑雌黄苏轼曾三过平山堂缅思旧事作水调歌头调笑好事者长记平山堂上欹枕江南烟雨渺渺没孤鸿认为山色有无是被烟雨所掩正写出欧公幽澹情怀岂是俗人能知平山堂为敞口厅宽五间前有石铺的行春台台前围以栏杆下临深池植有千竿修竹游人可坐在堂内或倚在栏前向南眺望江南群山由于与欧苏的关系平山堂名重士林历代游赏不绝多次重修其中最重要的一次是清乾隆元年1736年时任两淮商总的汪应庚出资重建平山堂并增建西园和远楼事成后汪氏编纂平山揽胜志收录历代题咏诗文供人怀想往贤盛游西园西园位于平山堂西青乾隆元年1736年汪应庚利用蜀冈的自然地势开池叠山布置亭榭点缀而成园林占地数十亩中央是一座巨大的水池沿池建造亭台楼阁主要位于南岸池中有岛屿上建单檐歇山顶房屋是1963年从城内壶园迁来池东叠黄石假山高五丈许极有气势山内洞穴上下贯穿可由山顶下至池边幽深险怪假山东侧为康熙御碑亭东壁嵌御碑北侧是乾隆御碑亭北壁嵌御碑碑亭附近有著名的天下第五泉
projects.content_zh: 江苏地区以平原为主，由北自山东入境，一马平川，扬州城北的蜀冈是沿途所见的第一座高丘。蜀冈得名大致有三种说法。第一种是风水家的形势说，认为此冈是四川蜀山向东绵延的余脉，如北宋梅尧臣所称"冈形来自蜀，山色去连吴"。南宋祝穆《方舆胜览》称："旧传地脉通蜀，故曰蜀冈。"第二种是江水说，明刘绩《霏雪录》称："山上有井，其水味如蜀江，号曰蜀冈。"第三种是字形说，《尔雅》认为蜀意为独，蜀冈的意思是一座独行之山。各种说法为这座小山增添了许多趣味，扬州人敝帚自珍，将其媲美于苏州虎丘，认为"隔江南北，两山相类"。蜀冈作为扬州不多的几块高地之一，具有一定的防御优势，历代多选择在此建城，如春秋时期吴、楚的邗城，西汉的广陵城，隋唐的扬州城……也由于地势较高，蜀冈成为供人登高望远的风景胜地，今有大明寺、平山堂和西园等景点。1. 大明寺：第六批国保（2006年）。大明寺始建于南朝宋孝武帝大明年间。隋仁寿元年（601年）隋文帝"诏海内立九层塔三十所"，庆祝他的六十大寿，其中一所便是立在大明寺的扬州栖灵塔，因此又称栖灵寺。唐代高僧鉴真曾在此居住讲学，并于天宝年间东渡日本，创建唐招提寺，成为日本律宗初祖。1973年在寺东建造鉴真纪念堂，由建筑学家梁思成设计。唐末栖灵塔被火烧毁，复称大明寺。清初因讳改称栖灵寺，清乾隆三十年（1765年）诏改法净寺。现存建筑多为清同治九年（1870年）重建，有山门、大雄宝殿和藏经楼等。2. 平山堂：平山堂位于大明寺西侧。北宋庆历八年（1048年）欧阳修由滁州调任扬州，趁公事余暇，在蜀冈筑平山堂，因能平望江南诸山而得名。1056年刘攽出任扬州，欧阳修填词相送，追忆当年在堂内的文酒盛事，称"平山栏槛倚晴空，山色有无中"。后有好事者调侃，平山堂望江南诸山甚近，拱列檐下，若可攀取，欧公言"有无中"，莫非因为近视？（严有翼《艺苑雌黄》）苏轼曾三过平山堂，缅思旧事，作《水调歌头》调笑好事者："长记平山堂上，欹枕江南烟雨，渺渺没孤鸿。"认为山色有无是被烟雨所掩，正写出欧公幽澹情怀，岂是俗人能知？平山堂为敞口厅，宽五间，前有石铺的行春台，台前围以栏杆，下临深池，植有千竿修竹。游人可坐在堂内或倚在栏前，向南眺望江南群山。由于与欧、苏的关系，平山堂名重士林，历代游赏不绝，多次重修。其中最重要的一次是清乾隆元年（1736年），时任两淮商总的汪应庚出资重建平山堂，并增建西园和远楼。事成后汪氏编纂《平山揽胜志》，收录历代题咏诗文，供人怀想往贤盛游。3. 西园：西园位于平山堂西。清乾隆元年（1736年）汪应庚利用蜀冈的自然地势，开池叠山、布置亭榭，点缀而成。园林占地数十亩，中央是一座巨大的水池，沿池建造亭台楼阁，主要位于南岸；池中有岛屿，上建单檐歇山顶房屋，是1963年从城内壶园迁来。池东叠黄石假山，高五丈许，极有气势；山内洞穴上下贯穿，可由山顶下至池边，幽深险怪。假山东侧为康熙御碑亭，东壁嵌御碑；北侧是乾隆御碑亭，北壁嵌御碑。碑亭附近有著名的"天下第五泉"。
projects.content_en: The Jiangsu region is mainly plains; entering from the north from Shandong, it is a vast flat expanse, and Shugang north of Yangzhou city is the first high hill seen along the way. The name Shugang (Shu Ridge) generally has three explanations. The first is the feng shui situation theory, believing this ridge is the eastern extension of the Shu Mountains in Sichuan, as Northern Song Mei Yaochen said: "The ridge shape comes from Shu, the mountain color connects to Wu." Southern Song Zhu Mu's "Fangyu Shenglan" says: "Tradition says the earth pulse connects to Shu, hence called Shugang." The second is the river water theory; Ming Liu Ji's "Feixue Lu" says: "There is a well on the mountain, its water tastes like the Shu River, called Shugang." The third is the character-shape theory; "Erya" believes 'shu' means 'alone,' so Shugang means a solitary mountain. Various explanations add much interest to this small hill; Yangzhou people, valuing their own, compare it to Suzhou's Tiger Hill, believing "across the river north and south, the two mountains are similar." As one of the few highlands in Yangzhou, Shugang has certain defensive advantages, and successive dynasties mostly chose to build cities here, such as the Han City of Wu and Chu in the Spring and Autumn period, the Guangling City of the Western Han, and the Yangzhou City of the Sui and Tang... Also due to its higher terrain, Shugang became a scenic spot for people to climb high and gaze into the distance; today it has Daming Temple, Pingshan Hall, West Garden, and other scenic spots. 1. Daming Temple: 6th Batch National Protected (2006). Daming Temple was first built during the Daming reign of Emperor Xiaowu of the Liu Song of the Southern Dynasties. In the 1st year of Renshou of the Sui (601), Emperor Wen of Sui "issued an edict to build thirty nine-story pagodas across the country" to celebrate his 60th birthday; one of them was the Yangzhou Qiling Pagoda built at Daming Temple, hence also called Qiling Temple. The Tang eminent monk Jianzhen once lived and lectured here, and during the Tianbao reign crossed east to Japan, founding the Toshodai-ji Temple and becoming the first patriarch of Japanese Risshu Buddhism. In 1973, the Jianzhen Memorial Hall was built east of the temple, designed by architect Liang Sicheng. At the end of the Tang, the Qiling Pagoda was destroyed by fire, and it was again called Daming Temple. In the early Qing, due to taboo, it was renamed Qiling Temple; in the 30th year of Qianlong of the Qing (1765), an edict renamed it Fajing Temple. The existing buildings were mostly rebuilt in the 9th year of Tongzhi of the Qing (1870), including the mountain gate, Mahavira Hall, and Scripture Library etc. 2. Pingshan Hall: Pingshan (Level Mountain) Hall is located west of Daming Temple. In the 8th year of Qingli of the Northern Song (1048), Ouyang Xiu was transferred from Chuzhou to Yangzhou; taking advantage of his spare time from official duties, he built Pingshan Hall on Shugang, named because one can look levelly at the mountains south of the Yangtze. In 1056, when Liu Ban was appointed to Yangzhou, Ouyang Xiu sent a ci poem to see him off, recalling the literary and drinking gatherings in the hall that year, saying "Pingshan's railings lean against the clear sky, mountain colors in being and non-being." Later, some busybody teased that from Pingshan Hall the mountains south of the Yangtze are very close, arching under the eaves as if reachable; Ouyang Gong saying 'in being and non-being'—could it be because he was nearsighted? (Yan Youyi, "Yiyuan Cihuang") Su Shi passed Pingshan Hall three times, recalling old times, and wrote "Shuidiao Getou" mocking the busybody: "Long remember on Pingshan Hall, leaning on a pillow in the misty rain south of the Yangtze, the lone goose disappears faintly." Believing the mountain colors' 'being and non-being' was obscured by misty rain, precisely expressing Ouyang Gong's serene and indifferent sentiment—how could ordinary people understand? Pingshan Hall is an open hall, five bays wide, with a stone-paved Xingchun (Spring-Walking) Terrace in front, surrounded by railings, overlooking a deep pool below with a thousand tall bamboos planted. Visitors can sit inside the hall or lean on the railing, looking south at the mountains south of the Yangtze. Due to its connection with Ouyang and Su, Pingshan Hall is highly regarded among scholars, with continuous visits through the dynasties and multiple renovations. The most important one was in the 1st year of Qianlong of the Qing (1736), when Wang Yinggeng, then chief merchant of Lianghuai, funded the rebuilding of Pingshan Hall and added the West Garden and Yuanlou (Distant Tower). After completion, Wang compiled the "Pingshan Lansheng Zhi," collecting inscriptions and poems through the dynasties for people to recall the elegant travels of former worthies. 3. West Garden: West Garden is located west of Pingshan Hall. In the 1st year of Qianlong of the Qing (1736), Wang Yinggeng used the natural terrain of Shugang to dig ponds, stack rockeries, arrange pavilions and terraces, and embellish it into a garden. The garden covers tens of mu, with a huge pond in the center; pavilions, terraces, and towers are built along the pond, mainly on the south bank; there is an island in the pond, with a single-eave hip-and-gable roof building on it, moved from the Huyuan Garden in the city in 1963. East of the pond, a yellow-stone rockery is stacked, about five zhang high, very imposing; caves inside the mountain penetrate up and down, allowing passage from the mountain top to the pond edge, deep and perilously strange. East of the rockery is the Kangxi Imperial Stele Pavilion, with an imperial stele embedded in the east wall; north is the Qianlong Imperial Stele Pavilion, with an imperial stele embedded in the north wall. Near the stele pavilions is the famous "Fifth Spring Under Heaven."

projects.name: 扬州城遗址（唐城遗址博物馆）
projects.name_en: Yangzhou City Site (The Ancient Tang City Ruins Museum)
projects.level: 第四批全国重点文物保护单位（1996年）
projects.level_en: 4th Batch National Key Cultural Heritage Site (1996)
projects.address_en: No. 20 East Pingshantang Road, Weiyang District
highlights: 春秋时期吴国已在蜀冈筑城其最兴盛的时期则在隋唐两宋隋在汉初广陵城的基础上扩建为江都宫城唐代拓展为子城和罗城两部分子城在蜀冈上为衙署区夯土筑墙四面开门城内以十字街贯通罗城在蜀冈下为工商业居民区宋代再次拓建成为宋大城堡城和夹城三城扬州唐城遗址是国内保存最完好的古城遗址之一唐代衙城的四周城垣夯土城墙城门和角楼至今仍高出地面510米历历在目博物馆位于衙城遗址的西南角复建了唐式城墙和阙楼可登临观赏唐城遗址和扬州城馆内展览唐杜佑题名八角石柱唐咸通十四年873年经幢和唐三绝碑等唐代文物精品并辟有崔志远史料陈列馆
projects.content_zh: 春秋时期吴国已在蜀冈筑城，其最兴盛的时期则在隋唐两宋。隋在汉初广陵城的基础上扩建为江都宫城。唐代拓展为子城和罗城两部分：子城在蜀冈上，为衙署区，夯土筑墙，四面开门，城内以十字街贯通。罗城在蜀冈下，为工商业居民区。宋代再次拓建，成为宋大城、堡城和夹城三城。扬州唐城遗址是国内保存最完好的古城遗址之一。唐代衙城的四周城垣、夯土城墙、城门和角楼至今仍高出地面5—10米，历历在目。博物馆位于衙城遗址的西南角，复建了唐式城墙和阙楼，可登临观赏唐城遗址和扬州城。馆内展览唐杜佑题名八角石柱、唐咸通十四年（873年）经幢和唐三绝碑等唐代文物精品，并辟有"崔志远史料陈列馆"。
projects.content_en: In the Spring and Autumn period, the State of Wu already built a city at Shugang, and its most prosperous period was in the Sui, Tang, and Song dynasties. The Sui expanded it into the Jiangdu Palace City on the basis of the early Han Guangling City. The Tang expanded it into two parts: the Zicheng (Sub-city) and Luocheng (Outer City). The Zicheng is on Shugang, serving as the government office area, with rammed-earth walls, gates on all four sides, and cross streets running through the city. The Luocheng is below Shugang, serving as the industrial, commercial, and residential area. The Song expanded again, forming three cities: the Song Great City, Fortress City, and Clamp City. The Yangzhou Tang City Site is one of the best-preserved ancient city sites in China. The surrounding city walls, rammed-earth walls, gates, and corner towers of the Tang yamen city still rise 5-10 meters above the ground today, clearly visible. The museum is located at the southwest corner of the yamen city site, with rebuilt Tang-style city walls and gate towers, which can be climbed to view the Tang city site and Yangzhou city. Inside the museum, fine Tang cultural relics such as the octagonal stone pillar inscribed by Du You of the Tang, the dharani pillar of the 14th year of Xiantong of the Tang (873), and the Tang Three Wonders Stele are exhibited, and a "Cui Zhiyuan Historical Materials Exhibition Hall" has been opened.

projects.name: 天山汉墓
projects.level: 第三批省级文物保护单位（1982年）
projects.level_en: 3rd Batch Provincial Cultural Heritage Site (1982)
projects.address_en: No. 97 East Pingshantang Road
highlights: 天山汉墓原在高邮市天山镇神居山上是汉武帝之子刘胥前54年的陵墓西汉元狩六年前117年刘胥封广陵王卒后葬神居山1979年发现了他与王后的合葬墓1992年迁至扬州又称汉陵苑汉陵苑馆内中央展厅陈列神居山一号汉墓王墓采用帝王级别的黄肠题凑木椁墓是全国罕见的大型汉代墓葬南北长16.65米东西宽14.28米是迄今发现的保存最完整的一座东厅陈列神居山二号汉墓后墓也采用黄肠题凑形制此外在东西侧室还展有汉广陵国出土的木器玉器铜器漆器陶器等供人了解汉代王侯生活
projects.content_zh: 天山汉墓原在高邮市天山镇神居山上，是汉武帝之子刘胥（？—前54年）的陵墓。西汉元狩六年（前117年）刘胥封广陵王，卒后葬神居山。1979年发现了他与王后的合葬墓，1992年迁至扬州，又称汉陵苑。汉陵苑馆内中央展厅陈列"神居山一号汉墓"（王墓），采用帝王级别的"黄肠题凑"木椁墓，是全国罕见的大型汉代墓葬。南北长16.65米，东西宽14.28米，是迄今发现的保存最完整的一座。东厅陈列"神居山二号汉墓"（后墓），也采用"黄肠题凑"形制。此外，在东西侧室还展有汉广陵国出土的木器、玉器、铜器、漆器、陶器等，供人了解汉代王侯生活。
projects.content_en: The Tianshan Han Tomb was originally on Shenju Mountain, Tianshan Town, Gaoyou City, and is the mausoleum of Liu Xu (?-54 BC), son of Emperor Wu of Han. In the 6th year of Yuanshou of the Western Han (117 BC), Liu Xu was enfeoffed as King of Guangling and buried at Shenju Mountain after death. In 1979, his joint tomb with the queen was discovered, and in 1992 it was moved to Yangzhou, also called the Han Mausoleum Garden. The central exhibition hall of the Han Mausoleum Garden displays the "Shenju Mountain Han Tomb No. 1" (king's tomb), adopting the imperial-level "Huangchang Ticou" (cypress heart timber frame) wooden outer-coffin tomb—a rare large Han Dynasty tomb in China. It is 16.65 meters long north-south and 14.28 meters wide east-west, the most completely preserved one discovered to date. The east hall displays the "Shenju Mountain Han Tomb No. 2" (queen's tomb), also adopting the "Huangchang Ticou" form. In addition, the east and west side chambers display wooden artifacts, jade, bronze, lacquerware, and pottery unearthed from the Han Guangling Kingdom, allowing people to understand the life of Han Dynasty kings and marquises.

projects.name: 隋炀帝陵
projects.name_en: Mausoleum of Emperor Yang of Sui

projects.level_en: 4th Batch Provincial Cultural Heritage Site (1995)
projects.address: 邗江区西湖镇隋炀西路102号
projects.address_en: No. 102 West Suiyang Road, Xihu Town, Hanjiang District
highlights: 隋代大业十四年618年隋炀帝杨广因困居在扬州行宫夜夜笙歌不久被部下勒死年仅五十岁萧皇后拆下床板作为棺木将其草草埋葬唐代平定江南后按帝王之礼在雷塘改葬隋炀帝陵墓规模狭小人罗隐隋炀帝陵感慨君王忍把平陈业只换雷塘数亩田清嘉庆十二年1807年阮元误将槐泗镇槐二村的一处土墩认作隋炀帝陵为其立碑建石1995年被列为省保单位2013年考古学家在西湖镇发现两座古墓出土隋炀帝墓志和鎏金铜铺首确定此处才是隋炀帝陵的真实位置更正了阮元的错误
projects.content_zh: 隋代大业十四年（618年）隋炀帝杨广因困居在扬州行宫，夜夜笙歌，不久被部下勒死，年仅五十岁，萧皇后拆下床板作为棺木，将其草草埋葬。唐代平定江南后，按帝王之礼在雷塘改葬隋炀帝。陵墓规模狭小，唐人罗隐《隋炀帝陵》感慨："君王忍把平陈业，只换雷塘数亩田。"清嘉庆十二年（1807年）阮元误将槐泗镇槐二村的一处土墩认作隋炀帝陵，为其立碑建石，1995年被列为省保单位。2013年考古学家在西湖镇发现两座古墓，出土隋炀帝墓志和鎏金铜铺首，确定此处才是隋炀帝陵的真实位置，更正了阮元的错误。
projects.content_en: In the 14th year of Daye of the Sui Dynasty (618), Emperor Yang of Sui, Yang Guang, trapped in the Yangzhou palace with nightly singing and music, was soon strangled by his subordinates at the age of fifty; Empress Xiao removed the bed board as a coffin and hastily buried him. After the Tang pacified Jiangnan, Emperor Yang of Sui was reburied at Leitang according to imperial rites. The mausoleum is small in scale; Tang person Luo Yin's "Mausoleum of Emperor Yang of Sui" lamented: "The king endured to trade the achievement of pacifying Chen for only a few mu of fields at Leitang." In the 12th year of Jiaqing of the Qing (1807), Ruan Yuan mistakenly identified an earthen mound at Huai'er Village, Huaisi Town as the Mausoleum of Emperor Yang of Sui, erecting a stele and stone for it, and it was listed as a provincial protected unit in 1995. In 2013, archaeologists discovered two ancient tombs in Xihu Town, unearthing the epitaph of Emperor Yang of Sui and gilded bronze door knockers, confirming that this place is the true location of the Mausoleum of Emperor Yang of Sui, correcting Ruan Yuan's error.

projects.name: 文峰塔
projects.level: 第六批省级文物保护单位（2006年）
projects.level_en: 6th Batch Provincial Cultural Heritage Site (2006)
projects.address_en: No. 16 Baota Road, Weiyang District
highlights: 文峰塔是一座砖木结构的楼阁式塔始建于明万历十年1582年清咸丰三年1853年寺毁仅剩塔心1923年修复2003年重修文峰塔与城市的文运攸关通常结合地形和水流选择甲东偏北丙南偏东丁南偏西等方位建塔扬州文峰塔选在丁位位于护城河出水口处既可弘扬文风又能锁住象征才华和财运的河水塔为八边形平面高七层内墙砖砌外檐与栏杆为木构此塔既是地标性建筑又可登塔南眺京口三山北望蜀冈诸胜被誉为扬州城南第一胜景塔下为文峰寺有前殿后殿及东西廊房等清代建筑
projects.content_zh: 文峰塔是一座砖木结构的楼阁式塔，始建于明万历十年（1582年），清咸丰三年（1853年）寺毁仅剩塔心，1923年修复，2003年重修。文峰塔与城市的文运攸关，通常结合地形和水流，选择甲（东偏北）、丙（南偏东）、丁（南偏西）等方位建塔。扬州文峰塔选在丁位，位于护城河出水口处，既可弘扬文风，又能锁住象征才华和财运的河水。塔为八边形平面，高七层，内墙砖砌，外檐与栏杆为木构。此塔既是地标性建筑，又可登塔南眺京口三山，北望蜀冈诸胜，被誉为扬州城南第一胜景。塔下为文峰寺，有前殿、后殿及东西廊房等清代建筑。
projects.content_en: Wenfeng Pagoda is a pavilion-style pagoda of brick-wood structure, first built in the 10th year of Wanli of the Ming (1582); in the 3rd year of Xianfeng of the Qing (1853) the temple was destroyed leaving only the pagoda core, repaired in 1923 and rebuilt in 2003. Wenfeng Pagoda is closely related to the city's literary fortune; usually, combining terrain and water flow, pagodas are built in positions such as Jia (east by north), Bing (south by east), and Ding (south by west). Yangzhou's Wenfeng Pagoda was chosen at the Ding position, located at the outlet of the moat, both to promote literary style and to lock in the river water symbolizing talent and wealth. The pagoda has an octagonal plan, seven stories high, with inner walls of brick and outer eaves and railings of wood. This pagoda is both a landmark building and allows climbing to gaze south at the Three Mountains of Jingkou and north at the scenic spots of Shugang, hailed as the number one scenic spot south of Yangzhou city. Below the pagoda is Wenfeng Temple, with Qing Dynasty buildings such as the front hall, rear hall, and east-west corridor rooms.

projects.name: 盂城驿
projects.level: 第四批全国重点文物保护单位（1996年），2014年成为世界文化遗产京杭大运河的组成部分
projects.level_en: 4th Batch National Key Cultural Heritage Site (1996), part of the World Cultural Heritage Grand Canal in 2014
projects.address_en: East of Nanmen Dajie
highlights: 盂城驿于2014年成为世界文化遗产京杭大运河的组成部分盂城是高邮的别称取秦观描写高邮吾乡如覆盂之意盂城驿是全国保存最完整的古驿站之一为研究古代邮驿和交通的重要实例这处驿站始建于明洪武八年1375年到嘉靖年间发展到很大规模有厅房库房神祠等共50多间明嘉靖三十六年1557年倭寇入侵驿站被毁明隆庆元年1567年重建现存建筑多建于清道光年间近年修复中路自南而北包括大门正厅皇华厅和后厅驻节堂等正厅与后厅皆为明代遗构皇华厅东南角建有鼓楼是古代值更守夜的制高点
projects.content_zh: 盂城驿于2014年成为世界文化遗产京杭大运河的组成部分，盂城是高邮的别称，取秦观描写高邮"吾乡如覆盂"之意。盂城驿是全国保存最完整的古驿站之一，为研究古代邮驿和交通的重要实例。这处驿站始建于明洪武八年（1375年），到嘉靖年间发展到很大规模，有厅房、库房、神祠等共50多间。明嘉靖三十六年（1557年）倭寇入侵，驿站被毁，明隆庆元年（1567年）重建。现存建筑多建于清道光年间，近年修复。中路自南而北包括大门、正厅皇华厅和后厅驻节堂等，正厅与后厅皆为明代遗构。皇华厅东南角建有鼓楼，是古代值更守夜的制高点。
projects.content_en: Yucheng Post House became part of the World Cultural Heritage Beijing-Hangzhou Grand Canal in 2014; Yucheng is another name for Gaoyou, taking the meaning of Qin Guan's description of Gaoyou "my hometown is like an overturned bowl." Yucheng Post House is one of the best-preserved ancient post stations in China, an important example for studying ancient postal services and transportation. This post station was first built in the 8th year of Hongwu of the Ming (1375), and by the Jiajing reign it had developed to a large scale, with over 50 rooms including halls, warehouses, and shrines. In the 36th year of Jiajing of the Ming (1557), Japanese pirates invaded and the post station was destroyed; it was rebuilt in the 1st year of Longqing of the Ming (1567). The existing buildings were mostly built during the Daoguang reign of the Qing and restored in recent years. The middle road from south to north includes the main gate, the main hall Huanghua Hall, and the rear hall Zhujie Hall etc.; both the main hall and rear hall are Ming Dynasty remains. A drum tower is built at the southeast corner of Huanghua Hall, the high point for keeping watch at night in ancient times.

projects.name: 文游台
projects.level: 其他
projects.level_en: Other
projects.address_en: No. 507 Renmin Road, Gaoyou City
highlights: 文游台原为东岳行宫始建于北宋太平兴国年间北宋元丰七年1084年苏轼由黄州到汝州赴任途经高邮与秦观孙觉和王巩登东山览眺饮酒论文当时四人都不得志登是台以啸咏发舒其无聊不平之气王士禛重修文游台记随后县令以群贤毕至将他们的登临之地题为文游台李公麟为之绘图纪胜此后文游台屡废屡兴因人而存后世骚人墨客常到此遐想苏秦诸公当时接袂登台挥麈剧谈的风神气概应武重修文游台记宋代曾几文游台诗曰忆昔坡仙此地游一时人物尽风流香莼紫蟹供杯酌彩笔银钩人唱酬现存建筑多建于晚清南部入口前立有牌坊入门院落中央为秦观立像东路偏院有汪曾祺文学馆秦观词社和高邮名人园西路偏院是一座园林有荷花池古鉴堂和水鉴馆等秦观立像北面拾阶而上为正堂益簪堂堂内四壁嵌秦邮帖乃清嘉庆年间高邮知州师兆龙集苏东坡黄庭坚米元章秦少游赵子昂董其昌等名家法书由著名金石学家钱泳勒刻而成书艺精湛刀法传神具有较高的艺术价值堂北为文游台主体楼这座二层楼建在高台上登高远眺东望田畴西观湖天古城景象尽收眼底主体楼西侧有泰山庙秦观读书台和建于明代的纪念苏轼孙觉秦观王巩的古四贤祠
projects.content_zh: 文游台原为东岳行宫，始建于北宋太平兴国年间。北宋元丰七年（1084年）苏轼由黄州到汝州赴任，途经高邮，与秦观、孙觉和王巩登东山览眺，饮酒论文。当时四人都不得志，"登是台以啸咏，发舒其无聊不平之气"（王士禛《重修文游台记》）。随后县令以群贤毕至，将他们的登临之地题为"文游台"，李公麟为之绘图纪胜；此后文游台屡废屡兴，因人而存，后世骚人墨客常到此遐想苏、秦诸公当时"接袂登台，挥麈剧谈"的风神气概（应武《重修文游台记》）。宋代曾几《文游台》诗曰："忆昔坡仙此地游，一时人物尽风流。香莼紫蟹供杯酌，彩笔银钩人唱酬。"现存建筑多建于晚清。南部入口前立有牌坊，入门院落中央为秦观立像，东路偏院有汪曾祺文学馆、秦观词社和高邮名人园，西路偏院是一座园林，有荷花池、古鉴堂和水鉴馆等。秦观立像北面拾阶而上为正堂益簪堂，堂内四壁嵌《秦邮帖》，乃清嘉庆年间高邮知州师兆龙集苏东坡、黄庭坚、米元章、秦少游、赵子昂、董其昌等名家法书，由著名金石学家钱泳勒刻而成，书艺精湛，刀法传神，具有较高的艺术价值。堂北为文游台主体楼，这座二层楼建在高台上，登高远眺，东望田畴，西观湖天，古城景象尽收眼底。主体楼西侧有泰山庙、秦观读书台和建于明代的纪念苏轼、孙觉、秦观、王巩的古四贤祠。
projects.content_en: Wenyou Platform was originally the Dongyue (Eastern Marchmount) Temporary Palace, first built during the Taiping Xingguo reign of the Northern Song. In the 7th year of Yuanfeng of the Northern Song (1084), Su Shi, traveling from Huangzhou to Ruzhou to take office, passed through Gaoyou and, with Qin Guan, Sun Jue, and Wang Gong, climbed East Mountain to gaze into the distance, drinking and discussing literature. At that time all four were unfulfilled in their ambitions, "climbing this platform to whistle and chant, releasing their bored and indignant qi" (Wang Shizhen, "Record of Rebuilding Wenyou Platform"). Subsequently, the county magistrate, considering the gathering of many worthies, titled the place where they climbed "Wenyou Platform" (Literary Gathering Platform), and Li Gonglin drew a picture to record the occasion; thereafter Wenyou Platform was repeatedly abandoned and revived, surviving because of its people. Later poets and scholars often came here to imagine the spirited bearing of Su, Qin and other gentlemen at that time, "walking arm in arm to the platform, waving horsetail whisks and discussing vigorously" (Ying Wu, "Record of Rebuilding Wenyou Platform"). Song Dynasty Zeng Ji's poem "Wenyou Platform" says: "Recalling the past when the Poet Immortal traveled here, the figures of that time were all romantic. Fragrant water shield and purple crabs served cups and goblets, colorful brushes and silver hooks people sang in response." The existing buildings were mostly built in the late Qing. In front of the southern entrance stands a memorial archway; in the center of the entrance courtyard is a standing statue of Qin Guan; the east side courtyard has the Wang Zengqi Literature Museum, Qin Guan Ci Poetry Society, and Gaoyou Celebrity Garden; the west side courtyard is a garden with a lotus pond, Gujian Hall, and Shuijian Hall etc. North of the Qin Guan statue, climbing steps up is the main hall Yizan Hall; the four walls of the hall are embedded with the "Qinyou Stele Album," which was compiled by Shi Zhaolong, Prefect of Gaoyou during the Jiaqing reign of the Qing, collecting calligraphy by famous masters such as Su Dongpo, Huang Tingjian, Mi Yuanzhang, Qin Shaoyou, Zhao Ziang, and Dong Qichang, engraved by the famous epigrapher Qian Yong—with exquisite calligraphy and vivid carving, having relatively high artistic value. North of the hall is the main building of Wenyou Platform, a two-story building built on a high platform; climbing high and looking far, one sees fields to the east and lake and sky to the west, with the ancient city scenery in full view. West of the main building are the Taishan Temple, Qin Guan's Reading Platform, and the ancient Four Worthies Shrine built in the Ming Dynasty commemorating Su Shi, Sun Jue, Qin Guan, and Wang Gong.

projects.name: 镇国寺塔
projects.level: 第三批省级文物保护单位（1982年）
projects.level_en: 3rd Batch Provincial Cultural Heritage Site (1982)
projects.address: 城西京杭大运河河心岛上
projects.address_en: On the river island in the Beijing-Hangzhou Grand Canal west of the city
highlights: 镇国寺塔位于城西京杭大运河河心岛上1956年拓宽运河时保留下河心岛的古塔镇国寺塔又称西门宝塔为七层方形砖塔始建于晚唐被誉为江南大雁塔今塔一至三层为宋构四至七层在明代重建塔刹为青铜铸葫芦刻有风调雨顺国泰民安字样
projects.content_zh: 镇国寺塔位于城西京杭大运河河心岛上，1956年拓宽运河时，保留下河心岛的古塔。镇国寺塔又称西门宝塔，为七层方形砖塔，始建于晚唐，被誉为"江南大雁塔"。今塔一至三层为宋构，四至七层在明代重建。塔刹为青铜铸葫芦，刻有"风调雨顺、国泰民安"字样。
projects.content_en: Zhenguo Temple Pagoda is located on the river island in the Beijing-Hangzhou Grand Canal west of the city; in 1956, when widening the canal, the ancient pagoda on the river island was preserved. Zhenguo Temple Pagoda, also called West Gate Pagoda, is a seven-story square brick pagoda, first built in the late Tang, hailed as the "Great Wild Goose Pagoda of Jiangnan." Today the first to third stories of the pagoda are Song structures, and the fourth to seventh stories were rebuilt in the Ming. The pagoda finial is a bronze-cast gourd, engraved with the characters "favorable weather, peaceful country and safe people."

projects.name: 净土寺塔
projects.level: 第六批省级文物保护单位（2006年）
projects.level_en: 6th Batch Provincial Cultural Heritage Site (2006)
projects.address_en: Southeast corner of the city
highlights: 净土寺塔又称东门宝塔与镇国寺塔相对始建于明万历三十四年1606年清光绪年间大修1945年被炮弹击毁一角次年修复这是一座八角七层砖塔高耸挺拔今围绕寺塔建成一处市民公园
projects.content_zh: 净土寺塔又称东门宝塔，与镇国寺塔相对，始建于明万历三十四年（1606年），清光绪年间大修，1945年被炮弹击毁一角，次年修复。这是一座八角七层砖塔，高耸挺拔，今围绕寺塔建成一处市民公园。
projects.content_en: Jingtu Temple Pagoda, also called East Gate Pagoda, opposite Zhenguo Temple Pagoda, was first built in the 34th year of Wanli of the Ming (1606), heavily repaired during the Guangxu reign of the Qing, had one corner destroyed by a shell in 1945, and was repaired the following year. This is an octagonal seven-story brick pagoda, tall and upright; today a citizen's park has been built around the temple pagoda.

projects.name: 高邮城墙及奎楼
projects.name_en: City Wall and Kuilou Tower of Gaoyou
projects.level: 其他
projects.level_en: Other
projects.address: 盂城路和琵琶路交叉口
projects.address_en: Intersection of Yucheng Road and Pipa Road
highlights: 宋城墙宋城墙位于盂城路和琵琶路交叉口北宋开宝四年971年高邮军知军高凝祐筑1972年大部分城墙被拆除仅存东南角约120余米的一段其中东西向51.7米南北向71米墙高6.6米雉堞39座城墙采用青砖叠筑拐角处有楼梯可登墙顶墙下有古护城河南北水关东水门和穿心河组成一套完整的城市防卫体系明奎楼明奎楼位于城墙东南角建于明天启三年1623年明崇祯九年1636年重修1984年大修2002年列为省保单位奎楼采用砖木结构八角三层底层朝北开门二三层四面开门原一二层顶部有精美彩绘今按清代图样恢复第一层重檐回廊登楼可眺望城内风光
projects.content_zh: 1. 宋城墙：宋城墙位于盂城路和琵琶路交叉口，北宋开宝四年（971年）高邮军知军高凝祐筑。1972年大部分城墙被拆除，仅存东南角约120余米的一段，其中东西向51.7米，南北向71米，墙高6.6米，雉堞39座。城墙采用青砖叠筑，拐角处有楼梯可登墙顶。墙下有古护城河、南北水关、东水门和穿心河，组成一套完整的城市防卫体系。2. 明奎楼：明奎楼位于城墙东南角，建于明天启三年（1623年），明崇祯九年（1636年）重修，1984年大修，2002年列为省保单位。奎楼采用砖木结构，八角三层，底层朝北开门，二、三层四面开门。原一、二层顶部有精美彩绘，今按清代图样恢复第一层重檐、回廊。登楼可眺望城内风光。
projects.content_en: 1. Song City Wall: The Song City Wall is located at the intersection of Yucheng Road and Pipa Road, built by Gao Ningyou, Military Commissioner of Gaoyou Army, in the 4th year of Kaibao of the Northern Song (971). In 1972 most of the city wall was demolished, leaving only a section of about 120 meters at the southeast corner, of which 51.7 meters runs east-west and 71 meters north-south, with a wall height of 6.6 meters and 39 crenellations. The city wall is built with stacked grey bricks, with stairs at the corners to climb to the top of the wall. Below the wall are the ancient moat, north and south water gates, east water gate, and Chuanxin River, forming a complete urban defense system. 2. Ming Kuilou (Kuixing Tower): The Ming Kuilou is located at the southeast corner of the city wall, built in the 3rd year of Tianqi of the Ming (1623), rebuilt in the 9th year of Chongzhen of the Ming (1636), heavily repaired in 1984, and listed as a provincial protected unit in 2002. Kuilou adopts a brick-wood structure, octagonal with three stories; the ground floor opens to the north, and the second and third floors open on all four sides. The original first and second floor tops had exquisite painted decorations; today the first floor's double eaves and corridors have been restored according to Qing Dynasty patterns. Climbing the tower, one can overlook the scenery inside the city.

projects.name: 高邮当铺
projects.level: 第六批全国重点文物保护单位（2006年）
projects.level_en: 6th Batch National Key Cultural Heritage Site (2006)
projects.address: 人民路和北门大街交汇处
projects.address_en: Intersection of Renmin Road and Beimen Dajie
highlights: 高邮当铺位于高邮市人民路和北门大街交汇处2006年列为第六批国保古建筑高邮当铺开设于清初原有四进平面近方形外观如城堡今极为破败正在动迁重修
projects.content_zh: 高邮当铺位于高邮市人民路和北门大街交汇处，2006年列为第六批国保古建筑。高邮当铺开设于清初，原有四进，平面近方形，外观如城堡。今极为破败，正在动迁重修。
projects.content_en: Gaoyou Pawnshop is located at the intersection of Renmin Road and Beimen Dajie in Gaoyou City, listed as a 6th Batch National Protected Ancient Building in 2006. Gaoyou Pawnshop opened in the early Qing, originally with four courtyards, nearly square in plan, with a castle-like exterior. Today it is extremely dilapidated and is currently being relocated and rebuilt.

regions.name: 扬州

regions.overview: 历史上泰州曾长期隶属扬州府，得益于明清时期兵灾较少，保存至今的日涉园比扬州现存园林都要古老，被陈从周先生誉为"淮左第一园"。此园原为明代陈鸢宅第，明万历年间其孙陈应芳（1543—1610）在宅旁造园，取陶渊明"园日涉以成趣"之意，题名日涉园。今园中假山主景，即为明代遗物。清初园归田氏，后来又归高凤翥（1707—1771），精心扩建为14景，并更名"三峰园"，奠定了今日格局。传世有道光五年（1825年）周庠所绘《三峰园四面景图》，表现了当时的园貌。清咸丰八年（1858年）园归吴文锡（1800—1870），改名蛰园，后又归两淮盐运使乔松年（1815—1875），俗称乔园。乔园是长江以北罕见的明代园林遗存，具有重要的历史价值和艺术价值；园林中区的山池主景，被陈从周赞誉为小园中的佳作："水池横中，假山对峙，洞曲藏岩，石梁卧波等，用极简单的数物组合成之，不落常套，光景自新。"
regions.overview_en: Historically, Taizhou was long subordinate to Yangzhou Prefecture; benefiting from fewer military disasters during the Ming and Qing periods, the preserved Rishe Garden is older than any existing garden in Yangzhou, and was praised by Mr. Chen Congzhou as the 'Number One Garden of Huaizuo.' This garden was originally the residence of Chen Yuan of the Ming; during the Wanli reign of the Ming, his grandson Chen Yingfang (1543-1610) built a garden next to the residence, taking Tao Yuanming's meaning 'the garden, daily entered, becomes a delight,' and titled it Rishe Garden. The main rockery scene in today's garden is a Ming Dynasty relic. In the early Qing, the garden passed to the Tian family, then to Gao Fengzhu (1707-1771), who carefully expanded it into 14 scenes and renamed it 'Sanfeng Garden' (Three Peaks Garden), establishing today's layout. A 'Four-Sided View of Sanfeng Garden' painted by Zhou Xiang in the 5th year of Daoguang (1825) survives, showing the garden's appearance at that time. In the 8th year of Xianfeng of the Qing (1858), the garden passed to Wu Wenxi (1800-1870), renamed Zhe Garden, then to Qiao Songnian (1815-1875), Salt Commissioner of Lianghuai, commonly called Qiao Garden. Qiao Garden is a rare Ming Dynasty garden remnant north of the Yangtze River, with important historical and artistic value; the mountain-pool main scene in the central area of the garden was praised by Chen Congzhou as a masterpiece among small gardens: 'The water pool lies horizontally in the middle, rockeries face each other, winding caves hide in the rocks, stone beams lie over the waves etc., composed with extremely simple few elements, not falling into common patterns, with scenery ever new.'

projects.name: 日涉园
projects.level: 第七批全国重点文物保护单位（2013年）
projects.level_en: 7th Batch National Key Cultural Heritage Site (2013)
projects.address_en: No. 68 North Hailing Road, Hailing District
highlights: 今乔园北西南三面皆有入口需从西门购票入园园林分为东中西三区中区属旧园遗存为园中精华东西两区皆为近年复建走进西门是一处天井小院向东直接通向西区也可向南经游廊曲折进入西区中部是一座大假山上建三层来青阁和皆绿山房东北角有一座大池绕池设文桂之舫午韵轩和蕉雨轩皆紧临水面互成对景东南角有一座小池掩在云墙之后两池通过环绕在假山东侧的溪流相连水脉相通中区采用前宅后园格局南部有宅门和大堂堂北设廊面向北部园林园中以山响草堂又名三峰草堂为主体分为南北两区堂南为开敞的平地绕着一湾溪流东西各跨一座小桥对面隔水是座大型石假山为珍贵的明代遗存假山下有石矶洞穴上有山路平台用黄石和湖石叠成下部近水及山洞底部用黄石规整古朴上部用湖石宛转多姿山顶树立三支石笋是当年三峰园旧物东侧的古柏是明代古树苍劲多姿为园景增色不少假山东侧设六角数鱼亭可俯临溪水观赏游鱼西侧贴墙设半亭位置较高可纵览园景山响草堂北侧是数级台地台上正中为书斋汲堂西侧为因巢亭京剧大师梅兰芳曾在此下榻东侧是小楼松吹阁可登阁临眺东区以建筑为主园景较为单调
projects.content_zh: 今乔园北、西、南三面皆有入口，需从西门购票入园。园林分为东、中、西三区，中区属旧园遗存，为园中精华；东、西两区皆为近年复建。走进西门是一处天井小院，向东直接通向西区，也可向南经游廊曲折进入。西区中部是一座大假山，其上建三层来青阁和皆绿山房。东北角有一座大池，绕池设文桂之舫、午韵轩和蕉雨轩，皆紧临水面，互成对景；东南角有一座小池，掩在云墙之后，两池通过环绕在假山东侧的溪流相连，水脉相通。中区采用前宅后园格局，南部有宅门和大堂，堂北设廊面向北部园林。园中以山响草堂（又名三峰草堂）为主体，分为南北两区。堂南为开敞的平地，绕着一湾溪流，东西各跨一座小桥，对面隔水是座大型石假山，为珍贵的明代遗存。假山下有石矶洞穴，上有山路平台，用黄石和湖石叠成：下部近水及山洞底部用黄石，规整古朴；上部用湖石，宛转多姿。山顶树立三支石笋，是当年"三峰园"旧物；东侧的古柏是明代古树，苍劲多姿，为园景增色不少。假山东侧设六角数鱼亭，可俯临溪水，观赏游鱼；西侧贴墙设半亭，位置较高，可纵览园景。山响草堂北侧是数级台地，台上正中为书斋汲堂，西侧为因巢亭，京剧大师梅兰芳曾在此下榻；东侧是小楼松吹阁，可登阁临眺。东区以建筑为主，园景较为单调。
projects.content_en: Today's Qiao Garden has entrances on the north, west, and south sides; tickets must be purchased and entry from the west gate. The garden is divided into east, central, and west areas; the central area belongs to the old garden remains and is the essence of the garden; the east and west areas were both rebuilt in recent years. Entering the west gate is a small courtyard; going east directly leads to the west area, or one can go south through a winding covered corridor. In the middle of the west area is a large rockery, on which the three-story Laiqing Pavilion and Jielü Mountain House are built. In the northeast corner is a large pond; around the pond are set the Wengui Boat, Wuyun Pavilion, and Jiaoyu Pavilion, all close to the water, forming opposite scenes; in the southeast corner is a small pond, hidden behind a cloud wall, and the two ponds are connected by a stream winding around the east side of the rockery, with water veins connected. The central area adopts a front-residence-back-garden layout, with a residence gate and main hall in the south, and a corridor north of the hall facing the northern garden. The garden centers on Shanxiang Thatched Hall (also called Sanfeng Thatched Hall), divided into north and south areas. South of the hall is open flat ground, winding around a bay of stream, with a small bridge spanning east and west each; across the water opposite is a large stone rockery, a precious Ming Dynasty relic. Below the rockery are stone banks and caves, above are mountain paths and platforms, stacked with yellow stone and lake stone: the lower part near water and the bottom of the cave use yellow stone, regular and simple; the upper part uses lake stone, graceful and varied. Three stone stalagmites stand on the mountain top, relics of the former 'Sanfeng Garden'; the ancient cypress on the east side is a Ming Dynasty ancient tree, vigorous and varied, adding much to the garden scenery. On the east side of the rockery is a hexagonal Fish-Counting Pavilion, overlooking the stream to watch swimming fish; on the west side against the wall is a half-pavilion, positioned higher, allowing a panoramic view of the garden. North of Shanxiang Thatched Hall are several terraces; in the center of the terrace is the study Jitang, west is Yinchao Pavilion, where Peking Opera master Mei Lanfang once stayed; east is the small building Songchui Pavilion, which can be climbed to overlook. The east area is mainly buildings, with relatively monotonous garden scenery.

projects.name: 学政试院
projects.level: 第七批全国重点文物保护单位（2013年）
projects.level_en: 7th Batch National Key Cultural Heritage Site (2013)
projects.address: 海陵区府前路府前路2号
projects.address_en: No. 2 Fuqian Road, Hailing District
highlights: 学政试院原为五代永宁宫旧址南唐昇元三年939年烈祖李昪派迁杨行密子孙至泰州建永宁宫后周时在永宁宫筑子城建州治明初凤阳军抚使院因避水患迁至此地明万历二十九年1601年都御使李三才将其改作督察院明末至清为扬州府属八县考生员场所即扬郡试院由省学政主持考试所以又称学政试院民国初年在这里设教育会与劝学所后驻兵称大营抗日战争期间被日本宪兵队占据新中国成立后泰州档案馆团市委市妇联总工会文化局文联等机关团体先后设于试院办公学政试院建筑群沿中轴线有四进院落主体建筑依次为头门仪门四教堂思补堂和上房清光绪年间废科举将后部东西二楼以及两厢考棚拆除只留下头门仪门和大堂1982年又拆除了仪门故原建筑仅保留下头门和大堂头门采用灰瓦硬山顶宽五间深两间前后檐用五踩斗栱前出向上翘曲的假昂柱间梁枋上有花草包袱图案清式彩绘梁架间以明式一斗六升斗栱承托大堂四教堂也是灰瓦硬山顶宽五间前出深三檩的硬山顶前廊殿身深七檩脊檩下以一斗六升斗栱逐层承托前檐采用带假昂的五踩斗栱斗栱也是明代风格正堂悬挂清乾隆督学款四教堂知府衔知泰州事张兆鹿重修墨书题记学政书院今为泰州科举院试博物馆近年复建了其他建筑大堂与仪门之间两侧为考棚头门前的广场两侧有东西辕门辕门内有东西吹鼓亭头门对面是大照壁照壁前东西两侧各竖一根旗杆
projects.content_zh: 学政试院原为五代永宁宫旧址，南唐昇元三年（939年），烈祖李昪派迁杨行密子孙至泰州，建永宁宫。后周时，在永宁宫筑子城，建州治。明初，凤阳军抚使院因避水患迁至此地。明万历二十九年（1601年），都御使李三才将其改作督察院。明末至清，为扬州府属八县考生员场所，即扬郡试院，由省学政主持考试，所以又称学政试院。民国初年，在这里设教育会与劝学所，后驻兵，称大营。抗日战争期间被日本宪兵队占据。新中国成立后，泰州档案馆、团市委、市妇联、总工会、文化局、文联等机关团体先后设于试院办公。学政试院建筑群沿中轴线有四进院落，主体建筑依次为头门、仪门、四教堂、思补堂和上房。清光绪年间废科举，将后部东、西二楼，以及两厢考棚拆除，只留下头门、仪门和大堂。1982年又拆除了仪门，故原建筑仅保留下头门和大堂。头门采用灰瓦硬山顶，宽五间，深两间，前后檐用五踩斗栱，前出向上翘曲的假昂，柱间梁枋上有花草、包袱图案清式彩绘，梁架间以明式一斗六升斗栱承托。大堂"四教堂"也是灰瓦硬山顶，宽五间，前出深三檩的硬山顶前廊，殿身深七檩。脊檩下以一斗六升斗栱逐层承托。前檐采用带假昂的五踩斗栱，斗栱也是明代风格。正堂悬挂清乾隆督学款"四教堂"、知府衔知泰州事张兆鹿重修"墨书题记。学政书院今为泰州科举院试博物馆，近年复建了其他建筑，大堂与仪门之间两侧为考棚，头门前的广场两侧有东、西辕门，辕门内有东、西吹鼓亭，头门对面是大照壁，照壁前东西两侧各竖一根旗杆。
projects.content_en: Xuezheng Examination Hall was originally the site of the Five Dynasties Yongning Palace; in the 3rd year of Shengyuan of the Southern Tang (939), Liezu Li Bian sent and relocated the descendants of Yang Xingmi to Taizhou, building Yongning Palace. In the Later Zhou, a sub-city was built at Yongning Palace to establish the prefectural government. In the early Ming, the Fengyang Military Commission moved here to avoid flood disasters. In the 29th year of Wanli of the Ming (1601), Censor-in-Chief Li Sancai converted it into the Censorate. From the late Ming to the Qing, it was the venue for the eight counties under Yangzhou Prefecture to take the student examination, i.e., the Yang Prefecture Examination Hall, with examinations presided over by the provincial education commissioner, hence also called Xuezheng Examination Hall. In the early Republic of China, an education association and study-promotion office were set up here, later troops were stationed, called the Great Camp. During the War of Resistance against Japan, it was occupied by the Japanese military police. After the founding of New China, government organizations and groups such as the Taizhou Archives, Municipal Youth League Committee, Municipal Women's Federation, General Trade Union, Cultural Bureau, and Federation of Literary and Art Circles successively set up offices in the examination hall. The Xuezheng Examination Hall building complex has four courtyards along the central axis; the main buildings are in sequence: the Outer Gate, Ceremonial Gate, Sijiao Hall, Sibu Hall, and Upper Quarters. During the Guangxu reign of the Qing, the imperial examination was abolished, and the rear east and west two-story buildings, as well as the two-side examination sheds, were demolished, leaving only the Outer Gate, Ceremonial Gate, and Main Hall. In 1982, the Ceremonial Gate was also demolished, so the original buildings only retain the Outer Gate and Main Hall. The Outer Gate adopts a grey-tile flush-gable roof, five bays wide and two bays deep, with five-step bracket sets on the front and rear eaves, with upward-curving fake ang (bracket arms) protruding forward; on the beams and lintels between columns are Qing-style painted decorations of flowers, plants, and cloth-bundle patterns; between the beam frames are Ming-style one-dou-six-sheng bracket sets for support. The Main Hall 'Sijiao Hall' also has a grey-tile flush-gable roof, five bays wide, with a front porch of flush-gable roof three purlins deep protruding forward, and the hall body is seven purlins deep. Under the ridge purlin are one-dou-six-sheng bracket sets supporting layer by layer. The front eaves adopt five-step bracket sets with fake ang, and the bracket sets are also in Ming style. The main hall hangs an ink inscription of the Qing Qianlong education commissioner's 'Sijiao Hall' and 'Prefect-rank Taizhou Magistrate Zhang Zhaolu rebuilt' in ink calligraphy. Xuezheng Academy is today the Taizhou Imperial Examination Hall Museum; other buildings were rebuilt in recent years, with examination sheds on both sides between the main hall and ceremonial gate, east and west yuan gates on both sides of the square in front of the outer gate, east and west drum-and-wind pavilions inside the yuan gates, a large screen wall opposite the outer gate, and a flagpole erected on each of the east and west sides in front of the screen wall.

projects.name: 泰州城隍庙
projects.level: 第六批全国重点文物保护单位（2006年）
projects.level_en: 6th Batch National Key Cultural Heritage Site (2006)
projects.address_en: No. 22 Yimiao Street, Hailing District
highlights: 泰州城隍庙又称邑庙位于泰州老城东北隅邑庙街是江苏省境内现存最大保存最完好的城隍庙此庙相传始建于唐北宋元符二年1099年重建建炎元年1127年毁于兵燹南宋重建元兵南下时又焚于火明洪武年间再建明正统四年1439年万历二十七年1599年两次翻新建清雍正初年咸丰四年1854年重修清代城隍庙规模盛大有山门四值功曹殿审事厅大殿与后宫五进左右各有配殿1929年神像被毁1953年拆除四值功曹殿和后宫1958年神像全部被毁一度改为医院民宅所幸主体建筑未损尚保留山门审事厅大殿和左右厢房等山门宽五间深两间灰瓦硬山顶门前两侧出八字影壁入门有青岗条石甬道通向审事厅审事厅建于明代灰瓦硬山顶宽五间深十檩构架分为前轩后堂两部分为圆堂半磕头轩做法前部四檩为轩廊卷棚天花后部七檩为明堂从内部看为碰檐做法外观则为整体屋面用料粗壮做工考究是泰州保存较好的明代厅堂建筑大殿建于明末清初宽五间灰色筒瓦硬山顶前出四檩硬山勾连搭前檐后部殿身为单檐歇山顶
projects.content_zh: 泰州城隍庙又称邑庙，位于泰州老城东北隅邑庙街，是江苏省境内现存最大、保存最完好的城隍庙。此庙相传始建于唐，北宋元符二年（1099年）重建，建炎元年（1127年）毁于兵燹，南宋重建，元兵南下时又焚于火，明洪武年间再建。明正统四年（1439年）、万历二十七年（1599年）两次翻新建，清雍正初年、咸丰四年（1854年）重修。清代城隍庙规模盛大，有山门、四值功曹殿、审事厅、大殿与后宫五进，左右各有配殿。1929年神像被毁，1953年拆除四值功曹殿和后宫，1958年神像全部被毁，一度改为医院、民宅，所幸主体建筑未损，尚保留山门、审事厅、大殿和左右厢房等。山门宽五间，深两间，灰瓦硬山顶，门前两侧出八字影壁。入门有青岗条石甬道通向审事厅，审事厅建于明代，灰瓦硬山顶，宽五间，深十檩，构架分为前轩后堂两部分，为圆堂半磕头轩做法。前部四檩为轩廊，卷棚天花，后部七檩为明堂；从内部看为碰檐做法，外观则为整体屋面，用料粗壮，做工考究，是泰州保存较好的明代厅堂建筑。大殿建于明末清初，宽五间，灰色筒瓦硬山顶，前出四檩硬山勾连搭前檐，后部殿身为单檐歇山顶。
projects.content_en: Taizhou City God Temple, also called Yimiao (County Temple), is located at Yimiao Street in the northeast corner of old Taizhou city, and is the largest and best-preserved City God Temple existing in Jiangsu Province. This temple is said to have been first built in the Tang, rebuilt in the 2nd year of Yuanfu of the Northern Song (1099), destroyed by war in the 1st year of Jianyan (1127), rebuilt in the Southern Song, burned again when Yuan troops marched south, and rebuilt in the Hongwu reign of the Ming. It was rebuilt twice in the 4th year of Zhengtong of the Ming (1439) and the 27th year of Wanli (1599), and repaired in the early Yongzheng and the 4th year of Xianfeng (1854) of the Qing. The Qing City God Temple was grand in scale, with five courtyards: mountain gate, Four Duty Officials Hall, Trial Hall, Main Hall, and Rear Palace, with side halls on left and right. In 1929 the statues were destroyed; in 1953 the Four Duty Officials Hall and Rear Palace were demolished; in 1958 all statues were destroyed, and it was once converted into a hospital and private residences; fortunately the main buildings were not damaged, still retaining the mountain gate, Trial Hall, Main Hall, and left and right wing rooms etc. The mountain gate is five bays wide and two bays deep, with a grey-tile flush-gable roof, with splayed screen walls on both sides in front of the gate. Entering the gate, a bluestone flagstone path leads to the Trial Hall; the Trial Hall was built in the Ming, with a grey-tile flush-gable roof, five bays wide and ten purlins deep, with the frame divided into front porch and rear hall two parts, adopting the round-hall half-kowtow porch method. The front four purlins are a porch corridor with a curved ceiling; the rear seven purlins are the main hall; from the inside it appears as a touching-eaves method, while from the outside it is an integral roof, with sturdy materials and exquisite workmanship, a well-preserved Ming hall building in Taizhou. The Main Hall was built in the late Ming and early Qing, five bays wide, with a grey tube-tile flush-gable roof, with a four-purlin flush-gable interlocking front eave protruding forward, and the rear hall body as a single-eave hip-and-gable roof.

projects.name: 南山寺大雄宝殿
projects.name_en: Hall of Mahavira in Nanshan Temple
projects.level: 第四批省级文物保护单位（1995年）
projects.level_en: 4th Batch Provincial Cultural Heritage Site (1995)
projects.address_en: No. 1 Nanshansi Road, Hailing District
highlights: 南山寺位于泰州老城东南隅始建于唐乾符三年876年朝廷赐额护国寺北宋治平元年1064年改为资福禅院北宋政和七年1117年改为道观神霄玉清万寿宫北宋建炎元年1127年恢复为资福禅寺南宋淳熙十年1183年寺毁南宋绍熙年间11901194重建明洪武十五年1382年改为祝圣道场1958年后寺院被逐渐拆除仅存明天启六年1626年重建的大雄宝殿大殿采用重檐庑殿顶正脊不做推山宽五间深六间殿中金柱用楠木制成柱头有卷杀上插较细的木柱承金檩为插柱造蜀柱上安叉手枋为琴面梁梁头下用丁头栱梁枋上有菱形锦地格和缠枝花彩画大殿的等级较高脊檩间枋下有明天顺七年1463年清道光年间及1957年重修的题记梁架结构为明代中期风格某些构件和做法带有宋元时期的特征但由于近年维修安装了平棋天花仅能看到梁枋间彩画屋顶梁架已不得见
projects.content_zh: 南山寺位于泰州老城东南隅，始建于唐乾符三年（876年），朝廷赐额"护国寺"，北宋治平元年（1064年）改为"资福禅院"。北宋政和七年（1117年）改为道观"神霄玉清万寿宫"，北宋建炎元年（1127年）恢复为"资福禅寺"，南宋淳熙十年（1183年）寺毁，南宋绍熙年间（1190—1194）重建。明洪武十五年（1382年）改为"祝圣道场"，1958年后寺院被逐渐拆除，仅存明天启六年（1626年）重建的大雄宝殿。大殿采用重檐庑殿顶，正脊不做推山，宽五间，深六间。殿中金柱用楠木制成，柱头有卷杀，上插较细的木柱，承金檩，为插柱造，蜀柱上安叉手。枋为琴面梁，梁头下用丁头栱。梁枋上有菱形锦地格和缠枝花彩画。大殿的等级较高，脊檩间枋下有明天顺七年（1463年）、清道光年间及1957年重修的题记。梁架结构为明代中期风格，某些构件和做法带有宋元时期的特征，但由于近年维修安装了平棋天花，仅能看到梁枋间彩画，屋顶梁架已不得见。
projects.content_en: Nanshan Temple is located in the southeast corner of old Taizhou city, first built in the 3rd year of Qianfu of the Tang (876), with the court bestowing the plaque 'Huguo Temple' (Nation-Protecting Temple); in the 1st year of Zhiping of the Northern Song (1064) it was renamed 'Zifu Chan Monastery.' In the 7th year of Zhenghe of the Northern Song (1117) it was converted into a Daoist temple 'Shenxiao Yuqing Wanshou Palace'; in the 1st year of Jianyan of the Northern Song (1127) it was restored to 'Zifu Chan Temple'; in the 10th year of Chunxi of the Southern Song (1183) the temple was destroyed, and rebuilt during the Shaoxi reign of the Southern Song (1190-1194). In the 15th year of Hongwu of the Ming (1382) it was renamed 'Zhusheng Daochang' (Blessing the Sage Ritual Site); after 1958 the temple was gradually demolished, leaving only the Mahavira Hall rebuilt in the 6th year of Tianqi of the Ming (1626). The Main Hall adopts a double-eave hip roof, with no mountain-push on the main ridge, five bays wide and six bays deep. The golden pillars in the hall are made of nanmu, with entasis at the column tops, with thinner wooden pillars inserted above to support the golden purlins, adopting the inserted-pillar method, with crossed hands (chashou) installed on the subsidiary pillars. The lintels are qinmian (lute-face) beams, with dingtou bracket sets under the beam heads. On the beams and lintels are diamond-pattern lattice and interlocking-flower painted decorations. The Main Hall has a relatively high grade; under the lintels between the ridge purlins are inscriptions of repairs in the 7th year of Tianshun of the Ming (1463), the Daoguang reign of the Qing, and 1957. The beam-frame structure is in the mid-Ming style, with some components and methods bearing characteristics of the Song-Yuan period; however, due to the installation of a coffered ceiling during recent repairs, only the painted decorations between beams and lintels can be seen, and the roof beam frame is no longer visible.

projects.name: 崇儒祠
projects.level: 第四批省级文物保护单位（1995年）
projects.level_en: 4th Batch Provincial Cultural Heritage Site (1995)
projects.address_en: No. 114 Wuyi Road, Hailing District
highlights: 崇儒祠现为王艮与泰州学派纪念馆位于泰州老城西北始建于明万历四年1576年是祭祀泰州学派创始人王艮的祠堂王艮14831541号心斋是泰州安丰场今属东台市人出身于盐民家庭幼年辍学自学成为儒学大师他曾在泰州安定书院和立诚社讲学创立淮南格物学说认为百姓日用即道在平民阶层影响广泛他去世后杭州府应天府宁国府扬州府泰县姜堰和海安等地都为他建造了祠堂明嘉靖四十三年1564年泰州在安定胡先生祠合祀王艮明万历四年1476年建立专祀王艮的崇儒祠其后多此重修现存门厅立本堂乐学堂和贤人堂南北共四进西侧附设园圃门厅宽三间灰瓦硬山顶两侧出八字影壁进入院落为仪门宽三间门在脊檩下入仪门为祠堂始建于明清嘉庆年间曾大修三间硬山顶出前廊平面布局柱础和部分梁架仍为明代遗构堂前檐东廊壁间有心斋王先生祠堂记碑保存完好是明代原物西廊壁间有崇儒祠记为残碑修补而成檐下有乐学堂横匾最后一进也是三间硬山顶悬先觉堂横匾内祀王艮像祠堂西侧新辟小园沿墙面设置长廊园内布置曲水花石修竹设王艮讲学立像
projects.content_zh: 崇儒祠现为王艮与泰州学派纪念馆，位于泰州老城西北，始建于明万历四年（1576年），是祭祀泰州学派创始人王艮的祠堂。王艮（1483—1541）号心斋，是泰州安丰场（今属东台市）人，出身于盐民家庭，幼年辍学，自学成为儒学大师。他曾在泰州安定书院和立诚社讲学，创立"淮南格物"学说，认为"百姓日用即道"，在平民阶层影响广泛。他去世后，杭州府、应天府、宁国府、扬州府、泰县姜堰和海安等地都为他建造了祠堂。明嘉靖四十三年（1564年）泰州在安定胡先生祠合祀王艮，明万历四年（1476年）建立专祀王艮的崇儒祠，其后多此重修。现存门厅、立本堂、乐学堂和贤人堂，南北共四进，西侧附设园圃。门厅宽三间，灰瓦硬山顶，两侧出八字影壁。进入院落为仪门，宽三间，门在脊檩下。入仪门为祠堂，始建于明，清嘉庆年间曾大修，三间硬山顶，出前廊，平面布局、柱础和部分梁架仍为明代遗构。堂前檐东廊壁间有《心斋王先生祠堂记》碑，保存完好，是明代原物。西廊壁间有《崇儒祠记》，为残碑修补而成，檐下有"乐学堂"横匾。最后一进也是三间硬山顶，悬"先觉堂"横匾，内祀王艮像。祠堂西侧新辟小园，沿墙面设置长廊，园内布置曲水、花石、修竹，设王艮讲学立像。
projects.content_en: Chongru Shrine is now the Wang Gen and Taizhou School Memorial Hall, located in the northwest of old Taizhou city, first built in the 4th year of Wanli of the Ming (1576), and is a shrine for sacrificing to Wang Gen, founder of the Taizhou School. Wang Gen (1483-1541), hao Xinzhai, was from Anfengchang in Taizhou (now belonging to Dongtai City), born into a salt-worker family; he dropped out of school in childhood and self-studied to become a master of Confucianism. He once lectured at Anding Academy and Licheng Society in Taizhou, founding the 'Huainan Gewu' (Huainan Investigation of Things) doctrine, believing that 'the daily use of the common people is the Way,' with wide influence among the common people. After his death, Hangzhou Prefecture, Yingtian Prefecture, Ningguo Prefecture, Yangzhou Prefecture, Jiangyan in Tai County, and Haian etc. all built shrines for him. In the 43rd year of Jiajing of the Ming (1564), Taizhou jointly sacrificed to Wang Gen at the Anding Mr. Hu Shrine; in the 4th year of Wanli of the Ming (1476), Chongru Shrine dedicated to Wang Gen was established, and subsequently repaired many times. The existing gate hall, Liben Hall, Xuetang Hall, and Xianren Hall form four courtyards north-south, with a garden attached on the west side. The gate hall is three bays wide, with a grey-tile flush-gable roof, with splayed screen walls on both sides. Entering the courtyard is the Ceremonial Gate, three bays wide, with the door under the ridge purlin. Entering the Ceremonial Gate is the shrine, first built in the Ming and heavily repaired during the Jiaqing reign of the Qing, three bays with a flush-gable roof and a front porch; the plan layout, column bases, and part of the beam frame are still Ming Dynasty remains. On the east corridor wall under the front eave of the hall is the stele 'Record of the Shrine of Mr. Wang Xinzhai,' well preserved and an original Ming artifact. On the west corridor wall is the 'Record of Chongru Shrine,' made from a repaired broken stele; under the eave is the horizontal plaque 'Xuetang Hall.' The last courtyard is also three bays with a flush-gable roof, hanging the horizontal plaque 'Xianjue Hall' (Hall of the First Awakened), with a statue of Wang Gen inside for sacrifice. West of the shrine, a small garden has been newly opened, with a long corridor along the wall; inside the garden are arranged winding water, flower rocks, and tall bamboos, with a standing statue of Wang Gen lecturing.

projects.name: 北山寺大殿
projects.level: 第五批省级文物保护单位（2002年）
projects.level_en: 5th Batch Provincial Cultural Heritage Site (2002)
projects.address_en: No. 92 Yangzhou Road, Hailing District
highlights: 北山寺在泰州老城外向北一公里处始建于唐宝历元年825年全称北山开化禅寺古称开化寺独佛寺传说唐代此地有百尺高塔百口水井南宋建炎年间毁于兵燹百口水井仅余卓锡泉南宋淳熙年间重建寺庙明弘治年间重铸铜钟明天启六年1626年重建大雄宝殿据清代文献记载因海陵城北地势低下遂将寺名改为北山以阜地气壮郡形清顺治四年1647年整修寺院顺治十八年1661年重铸铜钟康熙初年在大雄宝殿后建大悲楼道光年间寺又衰落咸丰年间重修清光绪四年1878年扩建为大寺在泰州规模仅次于光孝寺抗日战争时期二殿被日机炸毁1942年修茸大雄宝殿后被军队占用1960年拆除大悲楼文革时期铜钟被毁1984年拆除头殿和大部分寮屋现只存大雄宝殿大雄宝殿重建于明天启六年1626年清乾隆五十六年1791年咸丰二年1852年和1942年多次重修大殿坐北朝南宽五间深九檩黑瓦重檐歇山顶出前廊覆盆柱础梁架间承以斗栱脊檩蜀柱左右用叉手大殿西北角的卓锡泉已湮没难寻
projects.content_zh: 北山寺在泰州老城外向北一公里处，始建于唐宝历元年（825年），全称北山开化禅寺，古称开化寺、独佛寺。传说唐代此地有百尺高塔，百口水井，南宋建炎年间毁于兵燹，百口水井仅余卓锡泉。南宋淳熙年间重建寺庙，明弘治年间重铸铜钟，明天启六年（1626年）重建大雄宝殿。据清代文献记载，因海陵城北地势低下，遂将寺名改为"北山"，以"阜地气，壮郡形"。清顺治四年（1647年）整修寺院，顺治十八年（1661年）重铸铜钟，康熙初年在大雄宝殿后建大悲楼，道光年间寺又衰落，咸丰年间重修，清光绪四年（1878年）扩建为大寺，在泰州规模仅次于光孝寺。抗日战争时期二殿被日机炸毁，1942年修茸大雄宝殿，后被军队占用。1960年拆除大悲楼，"文革"时期铜钟被毁，1984年拆除头殿和大部分寮屋，现只存大雄宝殿。大雄宝殿重建于明天启六年（1626年），清乾隆五十六年（1791年）、咸丰二年（1852年）和1942年多次重修。大殿坐北朝南，宽五间，深九檩，黑瓦重檐歇山顶，出前廊，覆盆柱础，梁架间承以斗栱，脊檩蜀柱左右用叉手。大殿西北角的卓锡泉已湮没难寻。
projects.content_en: Beishan Temple is located one kilometer north outside old Taizhou city, first built in the 1st year of Baoli of the Tang (825), fully called Beishan Kaihua Chan Temple, anciently called Kaihua Temple and Dufo Temple. Legend says that in the Tang there was a hundred-chi-high pagoda and a hundred water wells here; during the Jianyan reign of the Southern Song it was destroyed by war, leaving only the Zhuoxi Spring among the hundred wells. The temple was rebuilt during the Chunxi reign of the Southern Song, the bronze bell was recast during the Hongzhi reign of the Ming, and the Mahavira Hall was rebuilt in the 6th year of Tianqi of the Ming (1626). According to Qing Dynasty documents, because the terrain north of Hailing city was low, the temple name was changed to 'Beishan' (North Mountain) to 'enrich the earth qi and strengthen the prefecture's form.' In the 4th year of Shunzhi of the Qing (1647) the temple was renovated; in the 18th year of Shunzhi (1661) the bronze bell was recast; in the early Kangxi, the Dabei (Great Compassion) Building was built behind the Mahavira Hall; during the Daoguang reign the temple declined again; it was repaired during the Xianfeng reign; in the 4th year of Guangxu of the Qing (1878) it was expanded into a large temple, second in scale only to Guangxiao Temple in Taizhou. During the War of Resistance against Japan, the second hall was bombed and destroyed by Japanese aircraft; in 1942 the Mahavira Hall was repaired, later occupied by the military. In 1960 the Dabei Building was demolished; during the Cultural Revolution the bronze bell was destroyed; in 1984 the front hall and most monk quarters were demolished; now only the Mahavira Hall remains. The Mahavira Hall was rebuilt in the 6th year of Tianqi of the Ming (1626), and repaired many times in the 56th year of Qianlong of the Qing (1791), the 2nd year of Xianfeng (1852), and 1942. The Main Hall faces south, five bays wide and nine purlins deep, with a black-tile double-eave hip-and-gable roof, with a front porch, inverted-basin column bases, bracket sets supporting between beam frames, and crossed hands on left and right of the ridge purlin subsidiary pillars. The Zhuoxi Spring at the northwest corner of the Main Hall has been buried and is hard to find.

projects.name: 周氏住宅（吴氏住宅）
projects.level: 第五批省级文物保护单位（2002年）
projects.level_en: 5th Batch Provincial Cultural Heritage Site (2002)
projects.address_en: No. 17 West Hanxi Street, Hailing District
highlights: 周氏住宅在泰州老城稻河古街区西侧始建于清咸丰年间原为富绅周彬的住宅周氏传两代即败落住宅转售给曾任广东监盐大使的吴希彭吴希彭认为周氏没落与屋宅风水有关清同治年间对住宅进行改造与扩建拆除原东向大门改为东南方向在门前新建高大影壁门内立砖雕佛龛并重建了大厅大小堂屋穿堂东西花厅照厅中西式蝴蝶厅花园厢房和厨房等改建工程浩大建筑材料上乘雕饰精细考究为泰州现存规模最大的民居院落号称九十九间半新中国成立后住宅收归国有曾作为机关学校沦为居民杂院2009年修缮一新住宅坐北向南包括东西四路14处天井10余座院落东南角的大门宽三间雕花门楼两侧为磨砖八字影壁门内为小天井内立带福祠的照壁天井北侧为中部轴线有男厅女厅和堂屋三进院落男厅高大宽敞采用抬梁式结构五架梁分为前后两部分前为船篷式卷棚后为仿古海棠如意卷棚前后檐下都安装玻璃隔扇门过天井为女厅与男厅梁架结构相同采用前后卷棚男女厅之间的庭院东侧有便门和厢房进出女厅需走东侧便门避免从男厅经过女厅后部为堂屋前后也用隔扇门男厅西南侧有雕花仪门门内为第二条轴线依次布置照厅厅屋穿堂和堂屋建筑比东侧更高大再向西为第三路前后四进院落和第四路西花园花厅花厅为歇山顶梁架有彩绘内用彩色水磨石地板中部刻水磨石拼花图案花厅东北角有一口水井
projects.content_zh: 周氏住宅在泰州老城稻河古街区西侧，始建于清咸丰年间，原为富绅周彬的住宅，周氏传两代即败落，住宅转售给曾任广东监盐大使的吴希彭。吴希彭认为周氏没落与屋宅风水有关，清同治年间对住宅进行改造与扩建。拆除原东向大门，改为东南方向，在门前新建高大影壁，门内立砖雕佛龛，并重建了大厅、大小堂屋、穿堂东西花厅、照厅中西式蝴蝶厅、花园、厢房和厨房等。改建工程浩大，建筑材料上乘，雕饰精细考究，为泰州现存规模最大的民居院落，号称九十九间半。新中国成立后住宅收归国有，曾作为机关、学校，沦为居民杂院。2009年修缮一新。住宅坐北向南，包括东、西四路，14处天井，10余座院落。东南角的大门宽三间，雕花门楼，两侧为磨砖八字影壁。门内为小天井，内立带福祠的照壁。天井北侧为中部轴线，有男厅、女厅和堂屋三进院落。男厅高大宽敞，采用抬梁式结构，五架梁，分为前后两部分，前为船篷式卷棚，后为仿古海棠如意卷棚，前后檐下都安装玻璃隔扇门。过天井为女厅，与男厅梁架结构相同，采用前后卷棚。男、女厅之间的庭院东侧有便门和厢房，进出女厅需走东侧便门，避免从男厅经过。女厅后部为堂屋，前后也用隔扇门。男厅西南侧有雕花仪门，门内为第二条轴线，依次布置照厅、厅屋、穿堂和堂屋，建筑比东侧更高大。再向西为第三路前后四进院落和第四路西花园花厅。花厅为歇山顶，梁架有彩绘，内用彩色水磨石地板，中部刻水磨石拼花图案，花厅东北角有一口水井。
projects.content_en: Zhou's Family Residence is located west of the Daohe Ancient Block in old Taizhou city, first built during the Xianfeng reign of the Qing, originally the residence of wealthy gentry Zhou Bin; the Zhou family declined after two generations, and the residence was resold to Wu Xipeng, who had served as Guangdong Salt Supervisor. Wu Xipeng believed the Zhou family's decline was related to the house's feng shui, and during the Tongzhi reign of the Qing he renovated and expanded the residence. The original east-facing main gate was demolished and changed to the southeast direction; a tall screen wall was newly built in front of the gate, a brick-carved Buddhist niche was erected inside the gate, and the main hall, large and small main rooms, corridor halls, east and west flower halls, reception hall, Chinese-Western butterfly hall, garden, wing rooms, and kitchen etc. were rebuilt. The renovation project was vast, with high-quality building materials and exquisite carvings, making it the largest existing folk residence compound in Taizhou, known as 'ninety-nine and a half rooms.' After the founding of New China, the residence was nationalized, once used as government offices and schools, and became a mixed residential courtyard. It was renovated anew in 2009. The residence faces south, including east and west four routes, 14 courtyards, and over 10 compounds. The main gate at the southeast corner is three bays wide, with a carved gate tower and ground-brick splayed screen walls on both sides. Inside the gate is a small courtyard, with a screen wall bearing a blessing shrine. North of the courtyard is the central axis, with three courtyards: male hall, female hall, and main room. The male hall is tall and spacious, adopting a post-and-lintel structure with five-frame beams, divided into front and rear parts: the front is a boat-awning curved ceiling, the rear is an antique crabapple-ruyi curved ceiling, with glass lattice doors installed under both front and rear eaves. Across the courtyard is the female hall, with the same beam-frame structure as the male hall, adopting front and rear curved ceilings. On the east side of the courtyard between the male and female halls are side doors and wing rooms; entering and exiting the female hall requires taking the east side door, avoiding passing through the male hall. The rear of the female hall is the main room, also using lattice doors front and rear. On the southwest side of the male hall is a carved ceremonial gate; inside the gate is the second axis, sequentially arranging the reception hall, hall room, corridor hall, and main room, with buildings taller and larger than the east side. Further west are the third route with four front-and-rear courtyards and the fourth route west garden flower hall. The flower hall has a hip-and-gable roof, with painted decorations on the beam frame, colored terrazzo flooring inside, with a terrazzo mosaic pattern carved in the center, and a water well at the northeast corner of the flower hall.

projects.name: 上池斋药店
projects.level: 第七批全国重点文物保护单位（2013年）
projects.level_en: 7th Batch National Key Cultural Heritage Site (2013)
projects.address: 昭阳镇文峰社区东城外大街10号
projects.address_en: No. 10 Dongchengwai Dajie, Wenfeng Community, Zhaoyang Town
highlights: 清雍正初年扬州药商方石川在兴化东城外大街购得旧屋改建为上池斋中药店集名医坐诊中药制作和销售于一体是江淮地区店史最长最负盛名的一家药店店名取自史记扁鹊传饮是以上池之水1932年业主方少泉为增强竞争力参照上海等地药店式样改建店面用进口瓷砖等装饰地坪和柜台立面并在店堂西壁安装进口玻璃镜面使药店显得洋气而亮堂1956年公私合营后上池斋药店隶属兴化县医药公司仍以上池斋为店名文革期间改称长春药店1983年恢复原名药店采用砖木结构坐南朝北前后两进前为店铺后为作坊店铺是两幢二层楼房面宽8.3米进深15米硬山顶底层为铺面由石库门进入东侧设曲尺柜台竖有清代制作的木质抱柱招牌上书本斋拣选药料遵古炮制发兑字样柜台内依墙立有药柜山架柜台外侧贴青花瓷方块地坪用彩花水泥方砖皆为1932年店主进口来的材料店堂立柱挂有水饮上池采芝寿世橘井流芳和杏林长春等牌匾南北之间有大型镂空木雕挂落内容为鹿鹤同春葫芦缠枝等图案前后隔而不断店内靠南墙设后柜东南隅朝东开拱券门门外有一口古井方便取水熬药西北角外侧有平台台上建四角方亭用于晾晒药材楼上为药材库房四围壁板中为回廊以木质雕花栏杆围护既增加了店堂采光又便于库房内药材通风透气前进店堂和后进作坊相互贯通作坊为三开间七檩平房硬山顶穿斗式结构柱下用木础系明代建筑这里是加工药材之处尚存部分传统制药工具作坊向南有天井通向主体建筑西侧的小花圃
projects.content_zh: 清雍正初年，扬州药商方石川在兴化东城外大街购得旧屋改建为"上池斋"中药店，集名医坐诊、中药制作和销售于一体，是江淮地区店史最长、最负盛名的一家药店。店名取自《史记·扁鹊传》："饮是以上池之水。"1932年业主方少泉为增强竞争力，参照上海等地药店式样，改建店面，用进口瓷砖等装饰地坪和柜台立面，并在店堂西壁安装进口玻璃镜面，使药店显得洋气而亮堂。1956年公私合营后，上池斋药店隶属兴化县医药公司，仍以"上池斋"为店名。"文革"期间改称长春药店，1983年恢复原名。药店采用砖木结构，坐南朝北，前后两进，前为店铺，后为作坊。店铺是两幢二层楼房，面宽8.3米，进深15米，硬山顶。底层为铺面，由石库门进入，东侧设曲尺柜台，竖有清代制作的木质抱柱招牌，上书"本斋拣选药料遵古炮制发兑"字样。柜台内依墙立有药柜山架。柜台外侧贴青花瓷方块，地坪用彩花水泥方砖，皆为1932年店主进口来的材料。店堂立柱挂有"水饮上池""采芝寿世""橘井流芳"和"杏林长春"等牌匾，南北之间有大型镂空木雕挂落，内容为鹿鹤同春、葫芦缠枝等图案，前后隔而不断。店内靠南墙设后柜。东南隅朝东开拱券门，门外有一口古井，方便取水熬药；西北角外侧有平台，台上建四角方亭，用于晾晒药材。楼上为药材库房，四围壁板，中为回廊，以木质雕花栏杆围护，既增加了店堂采光，又便于库房内药材通风透气。前进店堂和后进作坊相互贯通。作坊为三开间七檩平房，硬山顶，穿斗式结构，柱下用木础，系明代建筑。这里是加工药材之处，尚存部分传统制药工具。作坊向南有天井，通向主体建筑西侧的小花圃。
projects.content_en: In the early Yongzheng reign of the Qing, Yangzhou medicine merchant Fang Shichuan purchased an old house on Dongchengwai Dajie in Xinghua and converted it into the 'Shangchizhai' Chinese medicine pharmacy, integrating famous doctors' consultations, Chinese medicine production, and sales into one; it is the pharmacy with the longest history and greatest reputation in the Jianghuai region. The store name is taken from 'Records of the Grand Historian · Biography of Bian Que': 'Drink this with water from the upper pool.' In 1932, owner Fang Shaoquan, to enhance competitiveness,参照 the style of pharmacies in Shanghai and other places, renovated the storefront, using imported tiles etc. to decorate the floor and counter facade, and installed imported glass mirrors on the west wall of the store hall, making the pharmacy look foreign-style and bright. After public-private partnership in 1956, Shangchizhai Pharmacy was subordinate to the Xinghua County Pharmaceutical Company, still using 'Shangchizhai' as the store name. During the Cultural Revolution it was renamed Changchun Pharmacy, and restored its original name in 1983. The pharmacy adopts a brick-wood structure, facing south with north at the back, with two front-and-rear courtyards: the front is the shop, the rear is the workshop. The shop is two two-story buildings, 8.3 meters wide and 15 meters deep, with a flush-gable roof. The ground floor is the storefront, entered through a stone-framed door; on the east side is a carpenter's-square counter, with a Qing-made wooden pillar-hugging signboard vertically inscribed with 'This store selects medicinal materials, processes according to ancient methods, and distributes.' Inside the counter against the wall stand medicine cabinet mountain racks. Outside the counter are pasted blue-and-white porcelain squares, and the floor uses colored cement square bricks—all materials imported by the store owner in 1932. The store hall pillars hang plaques such as 'Water Drunk from Upper Pool,' 'Gathering Mushrooms for Longevity,' 'Orange Well Flowing Fragrance,' and 'Apricot Forest Eternal Spring'; between north and south is a large openwork wood-carved valance, with patterns of deer and crane sharing spring, gourd interlocking branches etc., separating front and rear without blocking. Inside the store against the south wall is a rear counter. In the southeast corner, an arched door opens east; outside the door is an ancient well, convenient for fetching water to boil medicine; outside the northwest corner is a platform, on which a four-corner square pavilion is built for drying medicinal materials. Upstairs is the medicinal material warehouse, with wall panels on all sides and a corridor in the middle, enclosed by wooden carved railings—both increasing the store hall's lighting and facilitating ventilation of medicinal materials in the warehouse. The front store hall and rear workshop are interconnected. The workshop is a three-bay seven-purlin single-story house, with a flush-gable roof and a column-and-tie structure, with wooden column bases—being a Ming Dynasty building. This is where medicinal materials are processed, with some traditional medicine-making tools still surviving. South of the workshop is a courtyard, leading to a small flower garden west of the main building.

regions.name: 泰州

regions.overview: 南通位于长江入海口北岸，古称通州，是中国近代第一城，由张謇先生一手规划建设。南通古建筑兼具江南园林之秀与近代建筑之新，南通博物苑是中国人自建的第一座公共博物馆，濠南别业是张謇故居，大生纱厂是中国近代民族工业的发祥地。
regions.overview_en: Nantong is located on the north bank of the Yangtze River estuary, anciently called Tongzhou, known as China's first modern city, planned and built single-handedly by Mr. Zhang Jian. Nantong's ancient architecture combines the elegance of Jiangnan gardens with the novelty of modern architecture; Nantong Museum is the first public museum built by Chinese themselves, Haonan Villa is Zhang Jian's former residence, and Dasheng Cotton Mill is the birthplace of China's modern national industry.
