highlights: 云龙山位于徐州城南共有9座山头绵延有如苍龙山间有北魏大石佛唐宋摩崖石刻宋代放鹤亭招鹤亭饮鹤泉和张山人旧居明代兴化禅寺清代大士岩山西会馆船厅御碑亭和碑廊等文物古迹兴化禅寺兴化禅寺位于云龙山东麓门票5元禅寺坐西朝东由山门天王殿石佛殿永宁库和禅院等组成寺内最著名的是北魏太武帝时期雕凿的大石佛头橡高近12米隋唐时期又在头像两侧峭壁上开凿崖龛雕像形成阿罗汉诸天龙女历落岩窦间天然如画的壮观景象今尚存72窟250余尊造像1995年列为省保单位明洪武三十一年1398年高僧胜吉依附云龙山构筑殿宇覆盖佛像至明万历年间形成大规模的寺院建筑群覆盖大石佛的石佛殿倚崖而建后檐距石崖只砌有三行砖民间称誉为三砖殿覆三丈佛徐州山西会馆山西会馆位于云龙山东麓兴化寺北侧清康熙年间由在徐州经商的20多位山西商人捐资修建会馆依山就势坐西朝东分为前后两进院落包括关圣殿戏楼和两座配殿两座厢房是山西人往来贸易聚会议事之所2006年列为省保单位放鹤亭招鹤亭饮鹤泉放鹤亭位于云龙山顶坐东朝西西侧有平台台旁即饮鹤泉泉南10余米处为招鹤亭三者合称张山人故址张山人是北宋隐士张天骥他在云龙山筑有草堂苏轼任职徐州期间常带宾客属吏和歌妓到放鹤亭饮酒为张天骥写下了著名的放鹤亭记放鹤亭屡废屡修今为1979年重修亭后碑廊中供有乾隆御书碑刻东坡石床东坡石床位于云龙山西麓是一座天然巨石上刻石床二字和苏轼的登云龙山诗石床南侧有一段长约50米的峭壁嵌有30多方石刻不少都是历代唱和苏诗的诗作徐州与苏轼相关的还有位于城内解放南路9号的快哉亭公园北宋熙宁十年1077年徐州节度使李邦直在唐薛能阳春亭故址建亭由苏轼命名很快成为著名的游览胜地今亭为1989年在原址重建大士岩观音殿大士岩位于云龙山西麓门票3元这是一座观音寺始建于清康熙五十七年1718年供奉玉带观音由山门圆通宝殿和千手观音殿等组成
projects.content_zh: 云龙山位于徐州城南，共有9座山头，绵延有如苍龙，山间有北魏大石佛，唐宋摩崖石刻，宋代放鹤亭、招鹤亭、饮鹤泉和张山人旧居，明代兴化禅寺，清代大士岩、山西会馆、船厅、御碑亭和碑廊等文物古迹。1. 兴化禅寺：兴化禅寺位于云龙山东麓，门票5元。禅寺坐西朝东，由山门、天王殿、石佛殿、永宁库和禅院等组成。寺内最著名的是北魏太武帝时期雕凿的大石佛头橡，高近12米。隋唐时期又在头像两侧峭壁上开凿崖龛雕像，形成阿罗汉、诸天、龙女，历落岩窦间，天然如画的壮观景象。今尚存72窟250余尊造像，1995年列为省保单位。明洪武三十一年（1398年）高僧胜吉依附云龙山构筑殿宇，覆盖佛像，至明万历年间形成大规模的寺院建筑群。覆盖大石佛的石佛殿倚崖而建，后檐距石崖只砌有三行砖，民间称誉为三砖殿覆三丈佛。2. 徐州山西会馆：山西会馆位于云龙山东麓，兴化寺北侧，清康熙年间由在徐州经商的20多位山西商人捐资修建。会馆依山就势，坐西朝东，分为前后两进院落，包括关圣殿、戏楼和两座配殿、两座厢房，是山西人往来贸易、聚会议事之所，2006年列为省保单位。3. 放鹤亭—招鹤亭—饮鹤泉：放鹤亭位于云龙山顶，坐东朝西，西侧有平台，台旁即饮鹤泉，泉南10余米处为招鹤亭，三者合称张山人故址。张山人是北宋隐士张天骥，他在云龙山筑有草堂，苏轼任职徐州期间，常带宾客、属吏和歌妓到放鹤亭饮酒，为张天骥写下了著名的《放鹤亭记》。放鹤亭屡废屡修，今为1979年重修，亭后碑廊中供有乾隆御书碑刻。4. 东坡石床：东坡石床位于云龙山西麓，是一座天然巨石，上刻石床二字和苏轼的《登云龙山》诗。石床南侧有一段长约50米的峭壁，嵌有30多方石刻，不少都是历代唱和苏诗的诗作。徐州与苏轼相关的还有位于城内解放南路9号的快哉亭公园。北宋熙宁十年（1077年）徐州节度使李邦直在唐薛能阳春亭故址建亭，由苏轼命名，很快成为著名的游览胜地。今亭为1989年在原址重建。5. 大士岩（观音殿）：大士岩位于云龙山西麓，门票3元。这是一座观音寺，始建于清康熙五十七年（1718年），供奉玉带观音，由山门、圆通宝殿和千手观音殿等组成。
projects.content_en: Yunlong Mountain is located south of Xuzhou city, with a total of 9 mountain peaks stretching like a blue dragon; between the mountains are the Northern Wei Great Stone Buddha, Tang-Song cliff carvings, Song Dynasty Crane-Releasing Pavilion, Crane-Calling Pavilion, Crane-Drinking Spring, and the former residence of Zhang Shanren, Ming Dynasty Xinghua Chan Temple, Qing Dynasty Dashi Rock, Shanxi Guild Hall, Boat Hall, Imperial Stele Pavilion, and stele corridor etc. 1. Xinghua Chan Temple: Xinghua Chan Temple is located at the eastern foot of Yunlong Mountain, with a 5-yuan ticket. The temple faces west with east at the back, composed of the mountain gate, Heavenly Kings Hall, Stone Buddha Hall, Yongning Storehouse, and meditation courtyard etc. The most famous in the temple is the Great Stone Buddha head carved during the reign of Emperor Taiwu of the Northern Wei, nearly 12 meters high. During the Sui and Tang periods, cliff niches and statues were carved on the cliffs on both sides of the head, forming a spectacular scene of arhats, devas, and dragon maidens scattered among the rock caves, naturally picturesque. Today 72 niches with over 250 statues remain, listed as a provincial protected unit in 1995. In the 31st year of Hongwu of the Ming (1398), the eminent monk Shengji built halls clinging to Yunlong Mountain to cover the Buddha statues, and by the Wanli reign of the Ming a large-scale temple complex had formed. The Stone Buddha Hall covering the Great Stone Buddha is built against the cliff, with only three rows of bricks laid between the rear eave and the stone cliff, folk-praised as 'three-brick hall covering a three-zhang Buddha.' 2. Xuzhou Shanxi Guild Hall: The Shanxi Guild Hall is located at the eastern foot of Yunlong Mountain, north of Xinghua Temple, built with donations from over 20 Shanxi merchants doing business in Xuzhou during the Kangxi reign of the Qing. The guild hall follows the mountain terrain, facing west with east at the back, divided into front and rear two courtyards, including the Guansheng (Lord Guan) Hall, opera tower, two side halls, and two wing rooms; it was a place for Shanxi people to trade, gather, and discuss affairs, listed as a provincial protected unit in 2006. 3. Crane-Releasing Pavilion—Crane-Calling Pavilion—Crane-Drinking Spring: The Crane-Releasing Pavilion is located on the top of Yunlong Mountain, facing west with east at the back, with a platform on the west side beside which is the Crane-Drinking Spring; over 10 meters south of the spring is the Crane-Calling Pavilion, and the three are collectively called the Former Site of Zhang Shanren. Zhang Shanren was the Northern Song hermit Zhang Tianji, who built a thatched cottage on Yunlong Mountain; during Su Shi's tenure in Xuzhou, he often brought guests, subordinates, and singing girls to drink at the Crane-Releasing Pavilion, writing the famous 'Record of the Crane-Releasing Pavilion' for Zhang Tianji. The Crane-Releasing Pavilion has been repeatedly abandoned and repaired; today it was rebuilt in 1979, and the stele corridor behind the pavilion houses Qianlong's imperial calligraphy stele carvings. 4. Dongpo Stone Bed: The Dongpo Stone Bed is located at the western foot of Yunlong Mountain, a natural giant stone inscribed with the two characters 'Stone Bed' and Su Shi's poem 'Climbing Yunlong Mountain.' South of the stone bed is a section of cliff about 50 meters long, embedded with over 30 stone carvings, many of which are poems echoing Su Shi's poems through the dynasties. Also related to Su Shi in Xuzhou is the Kuaizai Pavilion Park located at No. 9 South Jiefang Road in the city. In the 10th year of Xining of the Northern Song (1077), Li Bangzhi, Military Commissioner of Xuzhou, built a pavilion at the former site of the Tang Xue Neng Yangchun Pavilion, named by Su Shi, and it soon became a famous scenic spot. Today's pavilion was rebuilt at the original site in 1989. 5. Dashi Rock (Guanyin Hall): Dashi Rock is located at the western foot of Yunlong Mountain, with a 3-yuan ticket. This is a Guanyin temple, first built in the 57th year of Kangxi of the Qing (1718), enshrining the Jade Belt Guanyin, composed of the mountain gate, Yuantong (Universal Penetration) Hall, and Thousand-Hand Guanyin Hall etc.

highlights: 户部山位于徐州古城南门外旧称南山是离城最近的制高点为军事要地东晋刘裕北伐在此建造宅第和台头寺北魏太武帝南征也在此安营苏轼曾评论说戏马台其高十仞广袤百步若用武之士屯千人其上而积三年粮于城中虽用十万人不易取也宋代以后南山由军事要地变为登临胜地宋代黄河改道入淮徐州常发水灾到晚明徐州部分司署为避水患迁到南山改名户部山其后富户豪门陆续在户部山建房高宅大院密布当地开始流行穷北关富南关有钱都住户部山的民谚这一带成为街巷纵横店铺林立的城外之城这些古建筑依山就势参差错落梁架硕大雕琢精美既有北方民居的规整宏阔又具南方民居的曲折秀美成为一组风格独特的民居建筑群如今保存较好的有余家大院翟家大院郑家大院刘家大院崔家大院和魏家院等其他还有李家大楼苏家院王家院李蟠故居和老盐店等2014年正在全面整修暂未开放崔家大院翰林府崔家大院位于项王路和状元街交叉口西清道光年间崔焘奉旨在旧居上扩建而成整组院落依附山势自西向东逐渐升高分为西部的下院和东部的上院文革期间遭到破坏今下院门楼旗杆基座上院鸳鸯楼和西花厅保存尚好鸳鸯楼是户部山民居的一种独特做法在依山建房时因借地势建成二层楼下层部分墙体利用山体楼内不设楼梯一二层的门朝向相反另一处鸳鸯楼在翟家大院内
projects.content_zh: 户部山位于徐州古城南门外，旧称南山，是离城最近的制高点，为军事要地，东晋刘裕北伐，在此建造宅第和台头寺；北魏太武帝南征，也在此安营。苏轼曾评论说：（戏马台）其高十仞，广袤百步，若用武之士，屯千人其上……而积三年粮于城中，虽用十万人不易取也。宋代以后，南山由军事要地变为登临胜地。宋代黄河改道入淮，徐州常发水灾，到晚明徐州部分司署为避水患迁到南山，改名户部山。其后富户豪门陆续在户部山建房，高宅大院密布，当地开始流行穷北关，富南关，有钱都住户部山的民谚，这一带成为街巷纵横、店铺林立的城外之城。这些古建筑依山就势，参差错落，梁架硕大，雕琢精美，既有北方民居的规整宏阔，又具南方民居的曲折秀美，成为一组风格独特的民居建筑群。如今保存较好的有余家大院、翟家大院、郑家大院、刘家大院、崔家大院和魏家院等，其他还有李家大楼、苏家院、王家院、李蟠故居和老盐店等。2014年正在全面整修，暂未开放。1. 崔家大院（翰林府）：崔家大院位于项王路和状元街交叉口西，清道光年间崔焘奉旨在旧居上扩建而成。整组院落依附山势，自西向东逐渐升高，分为西部的下院和东部的上院。文革期间遭到破坏，今下院门楼、旗杆基座、上院鸳鸯楼和西花厅保存尚好。鸳鸯楼是户部山民居的一种独特做法，在依山建房时因借地势建成二层楼，下层部分墙体利用山体，楼内不设楼梯，一、二层的门朝向相反。另一处鸳鸯楼在翟家大院内。
projects.content_en: Hubu Mountain is located outside the south gate of old Xuzhou city, formerly called South Mountain, the closest high point to the city and a military stronghold. During the Eastern Jin, Liu Yu's northern expedition built residences and the Taitou Temple here; during the Southern Expedition of Emperor Taiwu of the Northern Wei, a camp was also set up here. Su Shi once commented: (The Horse-Playing Terrace) is ten ren high and a hundred bu wide; if military men station a thousand people on it... and store three years of grain in the city, even with a hundred thousand people it would not be easy to take. After the Song Dynasty, South Mountain changed from a military stronghold to a scenic spot for climbing. In the Song Dynasty, the Yellow River changed its course to enter the Huai River, and Xuzhou often suffered floods; by the late Ming, some government offices in Xuzhou moved to South Mountain to avoid floods, renaming it Hubu (Ministry of Revenue) Mountain. Thereafter, wealthy families and powerful clans successively built houses on Hubu Mountain, with tall residences and large courtyards densely distributed; locally the proverb 'poor North Gate, rich South Gate, those with money all live on Hubu Mountain' became popular, and this area became a city outside the city with crisscrossing streets and numerous shops. These ancient buildings follow the mountain terrain, scattered and staggered, with large beam frames and exquisite carvings, possessing both the regular grandeur of northern folk residences and the winding beauty of southern folk residences, forming a group of folk residence buildings with a unique style. Today, the better-preserved ones include the Yu Family Compound, Zhai Family Compound, Zheng Family Compound, Liu Family Compound, Cui Family Compound, and Wei Family Courtyard etc.; others include the Li Family Building, Su Family Courtyard, Wang Family Courtyard, Former Residence of Li Pan, and the Old Salt Shop etc. In 2014 it was undergoing comprehensive renovation and temporarily closed. 1. Cui Family Compound (Hanlin Mansion): The Cui Family Compound is located west of the intersection of Xiangwang Road and Zhuangyuan (Top Scholar) Street, expanded by Cui Tao on the former residence by imperial decree during the Daoguang reign of the Qing. The entire group of courtyards clings to the mountain terrain, gradually rising from west to east, divided into the lower courtyard in the west and the upper courtyard in the east. It was damaged during the Cultural Revolution; today the lower courtyard's gate tower, flagpole base, upper courtyard's Yuanyang (Mandarin Duck) Building, and West Flower Hall are relatively well preserved. The Yuanyang Building is a unique practice of Hubu Mountain folk residences: when building houses against the mountain, taking advantage of the terrain to build a two-story building, with part of the lower floor walls utilizing the mountain body, no staircase inside the building, and the doors of the first and second floors facing opposite directions. Another Yuanyang Building is in the Zhai Family Compound.

highlights: 李可染故居南面建有李可染纪念馆展出他的生平和作品李可染19071989在徐州出生1922年故居建成他在此度过了青少年时代生活了近30年这座故居包括东西两路门屋在东北角是一座北方风格的四合院今入口位于纪念馆前庭院中向西穿过题有东方既白的月洞门可进入故居院中有两棵古老的石榴树其中西屋为上房屋檐较高采用透风脊南北两屋为厢房东屋为客厅出西南角门折向西还有两座房屋整座故居青砖黛瓦朴素清雅2007年在故居南侧建成李可染艺术馆其中的生平陈列厅和作品展示厅系统介绍了李可染82年的生活和艺术历程展示了他的艺术精品和速写手稿
projects.content_zh: 李可染故居南面建有李可染纪念馆，展出他的生平和作品，李可染（1907—1989）在徐州出生，1922年故居建成，他在此度过了青少年时代，生活了近30年。这座故居包括东、西两路，门屋在东北角，是一座北方风格的四合院。今入口位于纪念馆前庭院中，向西穿过题有东方既白的月洞门可进入故居，院中有两棵古老的石榴树。其中西屋为上房，屋檐较高，采用透风脊；南北两屋为厢房，东屋为客厅。出西南角门，折向西还有两座房屋。整座故居青砖黛瓦、朴素清雅。2007年在故居南侧建成李可染艺术馆，其中的生平陈列厅和作品展示厅系统介绍了李可染82年的生活和艺术历程，展示了他的艺术精品和速写手稿。
projects.content_en: South of Li Keran's Former Residence is the Li Keran Memorial Hall, exhibiting his life and works. Li Keran (1907-1989) was born in Xuzhou; the former residence was completed in 1922, and he spent his youth here, living for nearly 30 years. This former residence includes east and west two routes, with the gate house at the northeast corner, a northern-style courtyard house. Today's entrance is in the front courtyard of the memorial hall; going west through the moon gate inscribed with 'The East Has Already Turned White' leads into the former residence, with two ancient pomegranate trees in the courtyard. Among them, the west room is the main room, with a higher eave adopting a ventilated ridge; the north and south rooms are wing rooms, and the east room is the living room. Exiting the southwest corner gate and turning west, there are two more houses. The entire former residence has grey bricks and black tiles, simple and elegant. In 2007, the Li Keran Art Museum was built south of the former residence; its Life Exhibition Hall and Works Exhibition Hall systematically introduce Li Keran's 82 years of life and artistic journey, displaying his artistic masterpieces and sketch manuscripts.

highlights: 1910年由法国传教士艾赉沃出资德国传教士吴若瑟设计并主持修建教堂坐北朝南采用拉丁十字平面入口在南侧最南端是由三座圆形拱门构成的前廊其后两侧为高耸的三层钟楼中央是三角形屋顶立面上装饰神龛顶端立十字架教堂内部南端是二层的音乐楼可从中登上廊顶平台堂内主体是礼拜堂东西宽24米南北长50米采用穹窿屋顶宽敞壮观堂内北端有弥撒台和圣殿这座圣心堂采用青色砖石砌筑节点处用红砖设计合理施工精良历经百年仍坚固如初反映了当年西方文化在徐州的传播
projects.content_zh: 1910年由法国传教士艾赉沃出资，德国传教士吴若瑟设计并主持修建。教堂坐北朝南，采用拉丁十字平面，入口在南侧。最南端是由三座圆形拱门构成的前廊，其后两侧为高耸的三层钟楼，中央是三角形屋顶，立面上装饰神龛，顶端立十字架。教堂内部南端是二层的音乐楼，可从中登上廊顶平台。堂内主体是礼拜堂，东西宽24米，南北长50米，采用穹窿屋顶，宽敞壮观。堂内北端有弥撒台和圣殿。这座圣心堂采用青色砖石砌筑，节点处用红砖，设计合理，施工精良，历经百年仍坚固如初，反映了当年西方文化在徐州的传播。
projects.content_en: In 1910, it was funded by French missionary Ai Laiwo, designed and supervised by German missionary Wu Ruose. The church faces south, adopting a Latin cross plan, with the entrance on the south side. At the southernmost end is a front porch composed of three round arches; behind it, on both sides are towering three-story bell towers, with a triangular roof in the center, decorated with shrines on the facade and a cross erected at the top. Inside the church, at the south end is a two-story music loft, from which one can climb to the corridor roof platform. The main body inside the church is the nave, 24 meters wide east-west and 50 meters long north-south, adopting a vaulted roof, spacious and spectacular. At the north end inside the church are the altar and sanctuary. This Sacred Heart Church is built with grey bricks and stones, with red bricks at the joints, with reasonable design and excellent construction; after a hundred years it remains as solid as ever, reflecting the spread of Western culture in Xuzhou at that time.

regions.name: 徐州

regions.overview: 淮安古称淮阴、楚州，是京杭大运河沿线的重要城市，明清两代漕运总督驻地，也是周恩来总理的故乡。淮安古建筑以府署、漕运遗址、古镇和古塔为特色，淮安府署是中国现存极少的古代衙署实物例证之一，文通塔是中国唐宋古塔形式嬗替演变的重要实例。
regions.overview_en: Huai'an, anciently called Huaiyin and Chuzhou, is an important city along the Beijing-Hangzhou Grand Canal, the seat of the Caoyun (Grain Transport) Governor-General in the Ming and Qing dynasties, and also the hometown of Premier Zhou Enlai. Huai'an's ancient architecture features government offices, grain transport ruins, ancient towns, and ancient pagodas; Huai'an Government Office is one of the few surviving physical examples of ancient government offices in China, and Wentong Pagoda is an important example of the evolution of ancient Chinese pagoda forms from the Tang to Song dynasties.

projects.name: 文通塔
projects.level: 第七批全国重点文物保护单位（2013年）
projects.level_en: 7th Batch National Key Cultural Heritage Site (2013)
projects.address: 淮安区西门大街46号勺湖公园内
projects.address_en: Inside Shaohu Park, No. 46 West Ximen Street, Huai'an District
highlights: 文通塔位于淮安古城西北隅北临勺湖关于此塔始建的年代有两种不同的说法一是东晋大兴二年319年建龙兴寺寺僧以砖砌筑二塔其中西南之塔名叫尊胜塔即为文通塔之前身此时淮安古城尚未修建塔已先建另一说法是塔初建于隋代仁寿三年603年无论此塔始建于哪一年之后都一度被毁唐景龙二年708年重建名为尊圣塔俗称敦煌塔采用木构形式此后又遭兵火焚烧北宋太平兴国九年984年再度重建改作七层砖塔直至20世纪70年代塔身第五六两级仍保存着当时主持修造者留下的碑刻题记南宋嘉熙四年1240年淮安知州王珪曾对此塔进行重修明崇祯二年1629年又一次修塔更名文通塔与漕运总督朱大典在城外西南侧所建的龙光阁遥相呼应据说在风水上很有意义可旺一郡文凤清康熙七年1668年淮安地震塔上部坍塌道光十八年1838年至咸丰元年1851年予以重修奠定了今日的宝塔形象1982年文物部门对塔进行整修恢复了内部的3层楼板楼梯供奉有4尊佛像还将所在地段辟为文通塔苑成为勺湖风景区的核心景点之一登塔可眺望城内的市井街道和城外的运河风光2013年文通塔被国务院公布为全国重点文物保护单位文通塔历经时光洗礼就其现存形制而言介于楼阁式塔和密檐式塔之间平面为八角形塔身全以砖砌筑而成高23米共分7层底层直径约10.6米高度超过全塔的14上面6层逐层收分每层设一圈腰檐出挑较短垂脊飞翘屋顶设塔刹尺度偏小后世镀为金色塔外壁刷为黄色屋顶和每层腰檐为青黑色整座宝塔结构简洁造型质朴被园林古建专家陈从周先生认为是中国唐宋古塔形式嬗替演变的重要实例历史价值科学价值和艺术价值都很高
projects.content_zh: 文通塔位于淮安古城西北隅，北临勺湖。关于此塔始建的年代有两种不同的说法。一是东晋大兴二年（319年）建龙兴寺，寺僧以砖砌筑二塔，其中西南之塔名叫尊胜塔，即为文通塔之前身，此时淮安古城尚未修建，塔已先建。另一说法是塔初建于隋代仁寿三年（603年）。无论此塔始建于哪一年，之后都一度被毁，唐景龙二年（708年）重建，名为尊圣塔，俗称敦煌塔，采用木构形式。此后又遭兵火焚烧，北宋太平兴国九年（984年）再度重建，改作七层砖塔，直至20世纪70年代塔身第五、六两级仍保存着当时主持修造者留下的碑刻题记。南宋嘉熙四年（1240年）淮安知州王珪曾对此塔进行重修。明崇祯二年（1629年）又一次修塔，更名文通塔，与漕运总督朱大典在城外西南侧所建的龙光阁遥相呼应，据说在风水上很有意义，可旺一郡文凤。清康熙七年（1668年）淮安地震，塔上部坍塌，道光十八年（1838年）至咸丰元年（1851年）予以重修，奠定了今日的宝塔形象。1982年文物部门对塔进行整修，恢复了内部的3层楼板、楼梯，供奉有4尊佛像，还将所在地段辟为文通塔苑，成为勺湖风景区的核心景点之一，登塔可眺望城内的市井街道和城外的运河风光。2013年文通塔被国务院公布为全国重点文物保护单位。文通塔历经时光洗礼，就其现存形制而言，介于楼阁式塔和密檐式塔之间。平面为八角形，塔身全以砖砌筑而成，高23米，共分7层，底层直径约10.6米，高度超过全塔的1/4；上面6层逐层收分，每层设一圈腰檐，出挑较短，垂脊飞翘；屋顶设塔刹，尺度偏小，后世镀为金色。塔外壁刷为黄色，屋顶和每层腰檐为青黑色。整座宝塔结构简洁，造型质朴，被园林古建专家陈从周先生认为是中国唐宋古塔形式嬗替演变的重要实例，历史价值、科学价值和艺术价值都很高。
projects.content_en: Wentong Pagoda is located in the northwest corner of old Huai'an city, north of Shaohu (Spoon Lake). There are two different accounts of the year this pagoda was first built. One is that in the 2nd year of Taixing of the Eastern Jin (319), Longxing Temple was built, and the temple monks built two pagodas with bricks; the southwest one was called Zunsheng Pagoda, the predecessor of Wentong Pagoda—at that time the old Huai'an city had not yet been built, but the pagoda was already built first. Another account is that the pagoda was first built in the 3rd year of Renshou of the Sui Dynasty (603). Regardless of which year the pagoda was first built, it was later destroyed for a time; in the 2nd year of Jinglong of the Tang (708) it was rebuilt, named Zunsheng Pagoda, commonly called Dunhuang Pagoda, adopting a wooden structure. Thereafter it was burned again by war; in the 9th year of Taiping Xingguo of the Northern Song (984) it was rebuilt again, changed to a seven-story brick pagoda, and until the 1970s the fifth and sixth levels of the pagoda body still preserved the stele inscriptions left by the presiding builder at that time. In the 4th year of Jiaxi of the Southern Song (1240), Wang Gui, Prefect of Huai'an, once repaired this pagoda. In the 2nd year of Chongzhen of the Ming (1629), the pagoda was repaired again and renamed Wentong Pagoda, echoing from afar with Longguang Pavilion built by Caoyun Governor-General Zhu Dadian on the southwest side outside the city; it is said to have great feng shui significance, able to prosper the literary fortune of the entire prefecture. In the 7th year of Kangxi of the Qing (1668), an earthquake in Huai'an caused the upper part of the pagoda to collapse; from the 18th year of Daoguang (1838) to the 1st year of Xianfeng (1851) it was repaired, establishing today's pagoda appearance. In 1982, the cultural relics department renovated the pagoda, restoring the internal 3 floors of slabs and stairs, enshrining 4 Buddha statues, and also designated the area as Wentong Pagoda Garden, becoming one of the core scenic spots of the Shaohu Scenic Area; climbing the pagoda offers a view of the city streets inside and the canal scenery outside. In 2013, Wentong Pagoda was announced by the State Council as a National Key Cultural Heritage Site. Wentong Pagoda has undergone the baptism of time; in terms of its existing form, it lies between pavilion-style pagodas and multi-eave pagodas. The plan is octagonal, the pagoda body is entirely built with bricks, 23 meters high, divided into 7 stories, with a bottom diameter of about 10.6 meters, its height exceeding 1/4 of the entire pagoda; the upper 6 stories taper layer by layer, each story with a ring of waist eaves with relatively short overhangs and flying vertical ridges; the roof has a pagoda finial of relatively small scale, later gilded. The outer wall of the pagoda is painted yellow, and the roof and each waist eave are blue-black. The entire pagoda has a simple structure and plain form, considered by Mr. Chen Congzhou, an expert in gardens and ancient architecture, as an important example of the evolution of ancient Chinese pagoda forms from the Tang to Song dynasties, with high historical, scientific, and artistic value.

projects.name: 淮安府署
projects.level: 第六批全国重点文物保护单位（2006年）
projects.level_en: 6th Batch National Key Cultural Heritage Site (2006)
projects.address_en: No. 38 East Dongmen Street, Huai'an District
highlights: 淮安府署位于淮安古城东门大街是明清两代淮安府行政中心元代在其旧址上建有一座五通庙和沂郑万户宅明洪武三年1370年淮安知府姚斌认为旧府署格局狭隘在此建造了一座新的府署按照明代正德淮安府志的记载明代专业的府署包含大门三间仪门三间正堂五间戒石亭经历司三间照磨所三间理刑厅三间龙亭库三间架格库三间草积库十六间六房并各科司四十间司狱司此外还有神祠府前总铺府前官亭等附属建筑明代天启淮安府志记载明末又加建了漕运库阜积库轻重监狱等建筑清代一直沿用明代旧署清康熙十六年1677年因为奉令拆取楠木而将正堂镇淮堂拆毁清康熙十八年1679年由各方捐资知府徐樞主持重建清乾隆十三年1748年府署的基本格局包含大门三间二门三间大堂五间二堂五间三堂五间以及其他附属建筑大门外东西两侧设申明旌善二亭和牌坊二座咸丰年间府署遭遇火灾大堂被焚毁清咸丰十一年1861年重建尺度比原状略小清同治山阳县志所附淮安府署图显示清末的府署格局相当复杂左右设有若干跨院共有房屋数十幢600余间淮安府署的大堂二堂等建筑一直留存至至近年得到重修同时复建了中路的部分建筑目前府署的格局是南设大门三间门内建戒石坊上镌公生明三字庭院左右分设六科办公用房东为吏科礼科户科西为兵科刑科工科北面正中为大堂五间硬山建筑总面阔26米进深达18.5米面积超过500平方米气度庄严室内恢复古代原貌脊檩枋下仍保存着晚清重建时的题记咸丰十一年岁次辛酉仲春谷日代理江南淮安知府陶金诒重修大堂之后为二堂及其他附属房屋淮安府署是中国现存极少的古代衙署实物例证之一历史悠久已于2006年被列为全国重点文物保护单位
projects.content_zh: 淮安府署位于淮安古城东门大街，是明清两代淮安府行政中心。元代在其旧址上建有一座五通庙和沂郑万户宅，明洪武三年（1370年）淮安知府姚斌认为旧府署格局狭隘，在此建造了一座新的府署。按照明代正德《淮安府志》的记载，明代专业的府署包含大门三间、仪门三间、正堂五间、戒石亭、经历司三间、照磨所三间、理刑厅三间、龙亭库三间、架格库三间、草积库十六间、六房并各科司四十间、司狱司，此外还有神祠、府前总铺、府前官亭等附属建筑，明代天启《淮安府志》记载明末又加建了漕运库、阜积库、轻重监狱等建筑。清代一直沿用明代旧署，清康熙十六年（1677年）因为奉令拆取楠木而将正堂镇淮堂拆毁，清康熙十八年（1679年）由各方捐资，知府徐樞主持重建。清乾隆十三年（1748年）府署的基本格局包含大门三间、二门三间、大堂五间、二堂五间、三堂五间以及其他附属建筑，大门外东西两侧设申明、旌善二亭和牌坊二座。咸丰年间府署遭遇火灾，大堂被焚毁，清咸丰十一年（1861年）重建，尺度比原状略小。清同治《山阳县志》所附《淮安府署图》显示清末的府署格局相当复杂，左右设有若干跨院，共有房屋数十幢、600余间。淮安府署的大堂、二堂等建筑一直留存至今，近年得到重修，同时复建了中路的部分建筑。目前府署的格局是南设大门三间，门内建戒石坊，上镌公生明三字。庭院左右分设六科办公用房，东为吏科、礼科、户科，西为兵科、刑科、工科，北面正中为大堂，五间硬山建筑，总面阔26米，进深达18.5米，面积超过500平方米，气度庄严，室内恢复古代原貌，脊檩枋下仍保存着晚清重建时的题记：咸丰十一年岁次辛酉仲春谷日代理江南淮安知府陶金诒重修。大堂之后为二堂及其他附属房屋。淮安府署是中国现存极少的古代衙署实物例证之一，历史悠久，已于2006年被列为全国重点文物保护单位。
projects.content_en: Huai'an Government Office is located on East Dongmen Street in old Huai'an city, and was the administrative center of Huai'an Prefecture in the Ming and Qing dynasties. In the Yuan Dynasty, a Wutong Temple and the residence of Yi Zheng Wanhu were built on its former site; in the 3rd year of Hongwu of the Ming (1370), Yao Bin, Prefect of Huai'an, believing the old government office layout was too narrow, built a new government office here. According to the records in the 'Huai'an Prefecture Gazetteer' of the Zhengde reign of the Ming, the professional Ming government office included three bays of main gate, three bays of ceremonial gate, five bays of main hall, warning stone pavilion, three bays of experience office, three bays of audit office, three bays of criminal justice hall, three bays of dragon pavilion warehouse, three bays of archive warehouse, sixteen bays of grass storage warehouse, forty bays of six offices and various departments, and the prison department; in addition there were附属 buildings such as shrines, the main post office in front of the prefecture, and official pavilions in front of the prefecture. The 'Huai'an Prefecture Gazetteer' of the Tianqi reign of the Ming records that at the end of the Ming, additional buildings such as the grain transport warehouse, grain accumulation warehouse, and heavy and light prisons were added. The Qing Dynasty continued to use the old Ming office; in the 16th year of Kangxi of the Qing (1677), because of an order to dismantle and take nanmu wood, the main hall Zhenhuai Hall was demolished; in the 18th year of Kangxi (1679), with donations from all parties, Prefect Xu Shu presided over the reconstruction. In the 13th year of Qianlong of the Qing (1748), the basic layout of the government office included three bays of main gate, three bays of second gate, five bays of grand hall, five bays of second hall, five bays of third hall, and other附属 buildings; outside the main gate, on the east and west sides, were the Shenming and Jingshan pavilions and two paifangs. During the Xianfeng reign, the government office suffered a fire and the grand hall was burned; in the 11th year of Xianfeng of the Qing (1861) it was rebuilt, with a scale slightly smaller than the original. The 'Map of Huai'an Government Office' attached to the 'Shanyang County Gazetteer' of the Tongzhi reign of the Qing shows that the layout of the government office at the end of the Qing was quite complex, with several side courtyards on the left and right, totaling dozens of buildings and over 600 rooms. The grand hall, second hall, and other buildings of Huai'an Government Office have survived to this day; in recent years they have been renovated, while部分 buildings on the central axis have been reconstructed. Currently, the layout of the government office has three bays of main gate in the south, with a warning stone archway inside the gate inscribed with the three characters 'Public Born Bright.' On the left and right of the courtyard are six office rooms: the east has the Personnel, Rites, and Revenue offices; the west has the War, Justice, and Works offices; in the center to the north is the grand hall, a five-bay flush-gable building with a total width of 26 meters and a depth of 18.5 meters, covering over 500 square meters, with a solemn bearing; the interior has been restored to its ancient appearance, and under the ridge purlin beam still preserves the inscription from the late Qing reconstruction: 'On an auspicious day in the second month of the year Xinyou, the 11th year of Xianfeng, Tao Jinzhi, Acting Prefect of Jiangnan Huai'an, rebuilt.' Behind the grand hall are the second hall and other附属 buildings. Huai'an Government Office is one of the few surviving physical examples of ancient government offices in China, with a long history, and was listed as a National Key Cultural Heritage Site in 2006.

projects.name: 镇淮楼
projects.level: 第五批省级文物保护单位（2002年）
projects.level_en: 5th Batch Provincial Cultural Heritage Site (2002)
projects.address_en: Center of old city, Huai'an District
highlights: 镇淮楼又名谯楼鼓楼位于淮安区镇淮楼东路是城市的重要象征2002年列为省保单位此楼始建于北宋时期原为镇江都统司酒楼位于州衙之南是城中文武官员富商巨贾文人墨客以及往来路过的官商宴集之处元代在楼上悬挂南北枢机天澈云衢匾额以彰显淮安扼守漕运通衢的特殊地位明代开始在楼上设置铜壶滴漏以报时辰又设巨鼓以鸣更报警为了镇压黄淮水患清乾隆年间正式改楼名为镇淮楼清光绪七年1881年曾经作大规模重修新中国成立后又多次重修以坚固挺拔的形象屹立于城内镇淮楼采用高台楼阁的形式底座为高大的砖砌台基长28米宽14米高8米上部略有收分显得十分沉稳台基正中设拱形门洞宛如城门南门大街从门中穿越而过台基东西两侧设砖砌踏步拾级而上台上建二层歇山楼阁视为砖木混合结构面阔三间带周围廊总宽13.6米重檐翘角凌空欲飞周围已经辟为城市广场与漕运总督署遗址一起成为古城中的核心文化标志和市民的休闲场所
projects.content_zh: 镇淮楼又名谯楼、鼓楼，位于淮安区镇淮楼东路，是城市的重要象征，2002年列为省保单位。此楼始建于北宋时期，原为镇江都统司酒楼，位于州衙之南，是城中文武官员、富商巨贾、文人墨客以及往来路过的官商宴集之处。元代在楼上悬挂南北枢机、天澈云衢匾额，以彰显淮安扼守漕运通衢的特殊地位。明代开始在楼上设置铜壶滴漏以报时辰，又设巨鼓以鸣更、报警。为了镇压黄淮水患，清乾隆年间正式改楼名为镇淮楼，清光绪七年（1881年）曾经作大规模重修，新中国成立后又多次重修，以坚固挺拔的形象屹立于城内。镇淮楼采用高台楼阁的形式，底座为高大的砖砌台基，长28米，宽14米，高8米，上部略有收分，显得十分沉稳。台基正中设拱形门洞，宛如城门，南门大街从门中穿越而过。台基东西两侧设砖砌踏步，拾级而上，台上建二层歇山楼阁，视为砖木混合结构，面阔三间，带周围廊，总宽13.6米，重檐翘角，凌空欲飞。周围已经辟为城市广场，与漕运总督署遗址一起成为古城中的核心文化标志和市民的休闲场所。
projects.content_en: Zhenhuai Tower, also called Qiaolou (Watchtower) and Gulou (Drum Tower), is located on East Zhenhuailou Road in Huai'an District, an important symbol of the city, listed as a provincial protected unit in 2002. This tower was first built during the Northern Song period, originally a wine tower of the Zhenjiang Military Command, located south of the prefectural yamen, a place for civil and military officials, wealthy merchants, literati, and passing officials and merchants to gather and feast in the city. In the Yuan Dynasty, plaques reading 'North-South Pivot' and 'Heaven-Clear Cloud Thoroughfare' were hung on the tower to demonstrate Huai'an's special position guarding the grain transport thoroughfare. In the Ming Dynasty, a copper clepsydra (water clock) was installed on the tower to tell time, and a giant drum was set to sound the night watches and give alarms. To suppress the Yellow River and Huai River floods, during the Qianlong reign of the Qing the tower was officially renamed Zhenhuai (Pacifying the Huai) Tower; in the 7th year of Guangxu of the Qing (1881) it underwent a major renovation, and after the founding of New China it was renovated multiple times, standing firm and upright in the city. Zhenhuai Tower adopts a high-platform pavilion form, with a tall brick platform base 28 meters long, 14 meters wide, and 8 meters high, with the upper part slightly tapering, appearing very stable. In the center of the platform base is an arched gate opening, like a city gate, through which South Gate Street passes. On the east and west sides of the platform base are brick steps; climbing up, a two-story hip-and-gable pavilion is built on the platform, regarded as a brick-wood composite structure, three bays wide with surrounding corridors, with a total width of 13.6 meters, with double eaves and upturned corners, seeming to fly in the air. The surrounding area has been turned into a city square, and together with the Caoyun Governor-General Office ruins, it has become a core cultural landmark in the old city and a leisure place for citizens.

projects.name: 周恩来故居
projects.level: 第三批全国重点文物保护单位（1988年）
projects.level_en: 3rd Batch National Key Cultural Heritage Site (1988)
projects.address_en: No. 7 Fuma Lane, Huai'an District
highlights: 一代伟人开国总理周恩来故居位于淮安古城驸马巷内1976年曾经进行过大规模整修1988年被国务院公布为全国重点文物保护单位周恩来祖父周攀龙是浙江绍兴人曾任山阳县师爷晚年捐得知县官职生前与其二兄合资购买了这座宅院供全家居住周恩来之父周贻能是清河县知县万青选之婿清光绪二十四年1898年3月5日周恩来在此宅出生乳名大鸾8个月时过继与叔父周贻淍清宣统二年1900年12岁的周恩来离开家乡赴东北求学之后再也没有回来过这是一座典型的苏北民居由东西两个宅园组成建筑采用青砖灰瓦和木结构装饰简洁朴素东院大门朝东门内设家塾馆周恩来童年曾在此读书向西穿过腰门来到主院北设正房三间为周恩来父母居室东厢房即为其诞生地院西有一条南北向的走廊南端设有两间亭子间幼年的周恩来与嗣母陈氏及乳母在此居住其后有小菜园园中有水井东南角设厨房后院另有百年的榆树观音柳各一株腊梅二株西院为周恩来二伯祖一家所住大门面南分为三进庭院共设19间房屋以一道随墙门与东院相通
projects.content_zh: 一代伟人、开国总理周恩来故居位于淮安古城驸马巷内，1976年曾经进行过大规模整修，1988年被国务院公布为全国重点文物保护单位。周恩来祖父周攀龙是浙江绍兴人，曾任山阳县师爷，晚年捐得知县官职，生前与其二兄合资购买了这座宅院供全家居住。周恩来之父周贻能是清河县知县万青选之婿。清光绪二十四年（1898年）3月5日周恩来在此宅出生，乳名大鸾，8个月时过继与叔父周贻淍。清宣统二年（1900年）12岁的周恩来离开家乡赴东北求学，之后再也没有回来过。这是一座典型的苏北民居，由东西两个宅园组成，建筑采用青砖、灰瓦和木结构，装饰简洁朴素。东院大门朝东，门内设家塾馆，周恩来童年曾在此读书。向西穿过腰门，来到主院，北设正房三间，为周恩来父母居室，东厢房即为其诞生地。院西有一条南北向的走廊，南端设有两间亭子间，幼年的周恩来与嗣母陈氏及乳母在此居住。其后有小菜园，园中有水井，东南角设厨房。后院另有百年的榆树、观音柳各一株，腊梅二株。西院为周恩来二伯祖一家所住，大门面南，分为三进庭院，共设19间房屋，以一道随墙门与东院相通。
projects.content_en: The former residence of Zhou Enlai, the great man and founding premier, is located in Fuma Lane in old Huai'an city; it underwent a large-scale renovation in 1976 and was announced by the State Council as a National Key Cultural Heritage Site in 1988. Zhou Enlai's grandfather Zhou Panlong was from Shaoxing, Zhejiang, and once served as a private secretary in Shanyang County; in his later years he donated to obtain the post of county magistrate, and during his lifetime he jointly purchased this residence with his second elder brother for the whole family to live in. Zhou Enlai's father Zhou Yineng was the son-in-law of Wan Qingxuan, County Magistrate of Qinghe County. On March 5, 1898 (the 24th year of Guangxu of the Qing), Zhou Enlai was born in this residence, with the milk name Daluan; at 8 months old he was adopted by his uncle Zhou Yichou. In 1900 (the 2nd year of Xuantong of the Qing), the 12-year-old Zhou Enlai left his hometown to study in Northeast China, and never returned again. This is a typical Northern Jiangsu folk residence, composed of east and west two residential gardens; the buildings use grey bricks, grey tiles, and wooden structures, with simple and plain decoration. The east courtyard gate faces east, with a family school inside the gate, where Zhou Enlai studied in his childhood. Going west through the side gate, one arrives at the main courtyard, with three main rooms in the north serving as the bedroom of Zhou Enlai's parents, and the east wing room being his birthplace. West of the courtyard is a north-south corridor, with two pavilion rooms at the south end, where the young Zhou Enlai lived with his adoptive mother Mrs. Chen and his wet nurse. Behind it is a small vegetable garden with a water well in it, and a kitchen at the southeast corner. In the rear courtyard there are also a century-old elm tree and a Guanyin willow tree each, and two wintersweet plants. The west courtyard was lived in by Zhou Enlai's second great-uncle's family, with the gate facing south, divided into three courtyards with a total of 19 rooms, connected to the east courtyard by a wall-following gate.

projects.name: 漕运总督部院遗址
projects.name_en: Former Government Office of Viceroy in Charge of Water Transport
projects.level: 第五批省级文物保护单位（2002年）
projects.level_en: 5th Batch Provincial Cultural Heritage Site (2002)
projects.address_en: West Yuan Street, Huai'an District
highlights: 明清两代淮安均为漕运总督驻跸地明景泰年间在城南设立总漕巡抚都察院明嘉靖年间迁于城东明万历年间再迁于谯楼北侧核心位置称总督漕抚部院清代在明代总督漕抚部院原址继续设立总督漕运公署仍作为漕运事务的最高管理官员漕运总督的驻节之所同时也是城中最重要的宪司公署乾隆年间陆续维修大堂修建大观楼改建花园厅舍数量增多格局雄伟清光绪三十一年1905年裁撤漕运总督显赫数百年的漕督署彻底退出历史舞台其旧址改作江北陆军学堂原建筑群于20世纪40年代逐渐被拆毁原有建筑基址大部尚存2002年重建其正门另在其北建漕运博物馆现存遗址总占地面积约2万平方米仍可清晰辨别仪门大堂二堂以及各种附属建筑的平面还挖掘出大量的柱础石件瓦件及带有铭文的古砖当年恢宏的气派依然隐约可见
projects.content_zh: 明清两代，淮安均为漕运总督驻跸地，明景泰年间在城南设立总漕巡抚都察院，明嘉靖年间迁于城东，明万历年间再迁于谯楼北侧核心位置，称总督漕抚部院。清代在明代总督漕抚部院原址继续设立总督漕运公署，仍作为漕运事务的最高管理官员漕运总督的驻节之所，同时也是城中最重要的宪司公署，乾隆年间陆续维修大堂、修建大观楼、改建花园，厅舍数量增多，格局雄伟。清光绪三十一年（1905年）裁撤漕运总督，显赫数百年的漕督署彻底退出历史舞台，其旧址改作江北陆军学堂，原建筑群于20世纪40年代逐渐被拆毁。原有建筑基址大部尚存，2002年重建其正门，另在其北建漕运博物馆。现存遗址总占地面积约2万平方米，仍可清晰辨别仪门、大堂、二堂以及各种附属建筑的平面，还挖掘出大量的柱础、石件、瓦件及带有铭文的古砖，当年恢宏的气派依然隐约可见。
projects.content_en: In both the Ming and Qing dynasties, Huai'an was the residence of the Caoyun (Grain Transport) Governor-General; during the Jingtai reign of the Ming, the General Grain Transport Governor Censorate was established south of the city, moved east of the city during the Jiajing reign of the Ming, and moved again to the core location north of the Qiaolou (Watchtower) during the Wanli reign of the Ming, called the Governor-General Grain Transport and Pacification Office. In the Qing Dynasty, the Governor-General Grain Transport Office continued to be established on the original site of the Ming Governor-General Grain Transport and Pacification Office, still serving as the residence of the Caoyun Governor-General, the highest administrative official for grain transport affairs, and also the most important constitutional office in the city; during the Qianlong reign, the grand hall was successively repaired, the Daguan (Grand View) Tower was built, and the garden was rebuilt, with an increased number of halls and rooms and a majestic layout. In the 31st year of Guangxu of the Qing (1905), the Caoyun Governor-General was abolished, and the prominent grain transport governor's office of several hundred years completely withdrew from the historical stage; its former site was converted into the Jiangbei Army Academy, and the original building complex was gradually demolished in the 1940s. Most of the original building foundations still survive; in 2002 its main gate was reconstructed, and a Grain Transport Museum was built north of it. The existing ruins cover a total area of about 20,000 square meters; the plans of the ceremonial gate, grand hall, second hall, and various附属 buildings can still be clearly distinguished, and a large number of column bases, stone pieces, tile pieces, and ancient bricks with inscriptions have been excavated, with the majestic style of that year still faintly visible.

projects.name: 河下古镇
projects.level: 其他
projects.level_en: Other
projects.address: 淮安古城淮安区西北侧
projects.address_en: Northwest side of Huai'an District, old Huai'an city
highlights: 河下古镇位于淮安古城淮安区西北侧靠近古邗沟入淮处的末口一般认为曾是古北辰坊的一部分宋代称满铺这一区域历来是淮安城外最重要的集镇位置优越水土丰腴人杰地灵传说汉代辞赋家枚乘唐代诗人赵嘏南宋巾帼英雄梁红玉的故居均在此处古镇在明清时期最为鼎盛文人雅士辈出如西游记的作者吴承恩明代状元沈坤清代经学大师阎若璩朴学家吴玉搢数学家骆腾凤医学家吴鞠通水利专家殷自芳均为其中的佼佼者至于诗人画家更是多不胜数明清时期的河下地区扼守大运河要冲交通便利车马漕船往来不绝聚集了更多的富商同时科举发达文人辈出修建了大量的店铺寺庙会馆宅第和园林盛况空前有小扬州的美誉清代中叶以后因为连续的天灾战乱而逐步衰落但至今仍保存着部分古街老店和旧民居建筑镇上的主要街道均以石板铺砌仍保留着当年车轮碾压的深深痕迹最重要的街道包括湖嘴大街估衣街花巷等其间分布着文楼老店来凤桥秦举人宅润州会馆等历史遗迹20世纪80年代以来重建了吴承恩故居吴鞠通故居闻思寺和部分桥梁店铺徜徉其中仍可体验到古朴的氛围
projects.content_zh: 河下古镇位于淮安古城淮安区西北侧，靠近古邗沟入淮处的末口，一般认为曾是古北辰坊的一部分，宋代称满铺。这一区域历来是淮安城外最重要的集镇，位置优越，水土丰腴，人杰地灵，传说汉代辞赋家枚乘、唐代诗人赵嘏、南宋巾帼英雄梁红玉的故居均在此处。古镇在明清时期最为鼎盛，文人雅士辈出，如《西游记》的作者吴承恩、明代状元沈坤、清代经学大师阎若璩、朴学家吴玉搢、数学家骆腾凤、医学家吴鞠通、水利专家殷自芳均为其中的佼佼者，至于诗人、画家更是多不胜数。明清时期的河下地区扼守大运河要冲，交通便利，车马漕船往来不绝，聚集了更多的富商，同时科举发达，文人辈出，修建了大量的店铺、寺庙、会馆、宅第和园林，盛况空前，有小扬州的美誉。清代中叶以后因为连续的天灾、战乱而逐步衰落，但至今仍保存着部分古街、老店和旧民居建筑。镇上的主要街道均以石板铺砌，仍保留着当年车轮碾压的深深痕迹。最重要的街道包括湖嘴大街、估衣街、花巷等，其间分布着文楼老店、来凤桥、秦举人宅、润州会馆等历史遗迹。20世纪80年代以来重建了吴承恩故居、吴鞠通故居、闻思寺和部分桥梁、店铺。徜徉其中，仍可体验到古朴的氛围。
projects.content_en: Hexia Ancient Town is located on the northwest side of Huai'an District in old Huai'an city, near the Mokou (End Mouth) where the ancient Han Canal enters the Huai River; it is generally believed to have been part of the ancient Beichen Fang, called Manpu in the Song Dynasty. This area has always been the most important market town outside Huai'an city, with a superior location, fertile land and water, and outstanding people; it is said that the former residences of the Han Dynasty rhapsodist Mei Cheng, the Tang Dynasty poet Zhao Gu, and the Southern Song heroine Liang Hongyu were all here. The ancient town was most prosperous during the Ming and Qing dynasties, with literati and scholars emerging in great numbers, such as Wu Cheng'en, author of 'Journey to the West'; Shen Kun, the Ming Dynasty top scholar; Yan Ruoju, the Qing Dynasty master of classical studies; Wu Yujin, a scholar of ancient learning; Luo Tengfeng, a mathematician; Wu Jutong, a physician; and Yin Zifang, a water conservancy expert—all outstanding among them, not to mention countless poets and painters. The Hexia area during the Ming and Qing dynasties guarded the strategic point of the Grand Canal, with convenient transportation and endless horse-drawn carriages and grain transport boats coming and going, gathering more wealthy merchants; at the same time, the imperial examinations flourished and literati emerged in great numbers, building a large number of shops, temples, guild halls, residences, and gardens, with an unprecedented prosperity and the reputation of 'Little Yangzhou.' After the mid-Qing Dynasty, it gradually declined due to continuous natural disasters and wars, but to this day some ancient streets, old shops, and old folk residence buildings are still preserved. The main streets in the town are all paved with stone slabs, still retaining the deep marks left by wheel ruts in those years. The most important streets include Huzui Street, Guyi (Used Clothing) Street, and Hua (Flower) Lane etc., with historical relics such as the Wenlou Old Shop, Laifeng Bridge, Qin Juren (Provincial Graduate) Residence, and Runzhou Guild Hall distributed among them. Since the 1980s, the Former Residence of Wu Cheng'en, the Former Residence of Wu Jutong, Wensi Temple, and some bridges and shops have been rebuilt. Wandering among them, one can still experience the simple and ancient atmosphere.

projects.name: 清晏园
projects.level: 2003年列为市保单位
projects.level_en: City-level Protected Unit (2003)
projects.address_en: No. 92 South Renmin Road, Qingpu District
highlights: 明代在清江浦镇设有管理仓粮运输和储存的户部部分司公署康熙年间开始河道总督靳辅将之改为行馆继任者张鹏翮在行馆西侧开设花园清雍正七年1729年朝廷正式设立江南河道总督一职并以行馆为总督署历任总督不断对花园进行建设尤其是乾隆年间的高斌和道光年间的麟庆做出很大的贡献清咸丰十年1860年总督署和清晏园惨遭捻军焚掠清同治元年1862年在此驻节的漕运总督吴棠在原址重建漕督行署和清晏园之后又屡经变迁20世纪8090年代得到整修和扩建是京杭大运河江苏段文物遗迹的重要组成部分清晏园现存建筑大部分均为重建但仍大致保持了原来的历史格局和意境特色园门东向入门即见一组湖石假山石峰嶙峋洞穴幽然沿曲廊北转过圆形随墙门西折为蕉吟馆其西为大水池形态近方池北有五间歇山正厅巍峨宏敞即为乾隆年间高斌所建之荷芳书院原构池中央立一座重檐攒尖六角亭通过曲桥与东岸相接东岸堆叠假山山北有较射亭再北为御碑亭内存康熙帝御笔澹泊宁静碑荷芳书院之西有紫藤花馆内藏一株300年以上树龄的古藤方池西岸建恬波楼其南水面上有一座重建的清晏舫再现了昔日画舫斋的神韵方池南岸堆叠大型黄石假山山北临水建槐香楼与荷芳书院水心亭形成一条中轴线园西部的关帝庙是一座古庙其中的大殿尚为明代原构庙南原有一所旧宅院并入清晏园后为了纪念叶挺将军而定名为叶园清晏园是一座衙署花园主要供历代河道总督和之后的漕运总督驻节期间休憩赏玩与皇家园林私家园林的属性有明显差异这是一座以治水为主题的古典园林初名淮园又名澹园后改清晏荷芳书院匾额既形容荷池之芬芳更取河防二字的谐音园中曾设澜恬风定之轩澜安风定轩恬波楼都含有安澜平波的意思这些题名寄托了历代总督平水患河道平顺的最高理想园中开辟大定胜天力挽狂澜的治水主题清晏园的景致融合南北园林之长融合南北园林之长其整体格局园具有疏朗旷达的特点更近于北方园林就建筑形式和假山植物的处理来看又具有素雅细腻的特点近于江南园林
projects.content_zh: 明代在清江浦镇设有管理仓粮运输和储存的户部分司公署，康熙年间开始，河道总督靳辅将之改为行馆，继任者张鹏翮在行馆西侧开设花园。清雍正七年（1729年）朝廷正式设立江南河道总督一职，并以行馆为总督署，历任总督不断对花园进行建设，尤其是乾隆年间的高斌和道光年间的麟庆做出很大的贡献。清咸丰十年（1860年）总督署和清晏园惨遭捻军焚掠，清同治元年（1862年）在此驻节的漕运总督吴棠在原址重建漕督行署和清晏园。之后又屡经变迁，20世纪80、90年代得到整修和扩建，是京杭大运河江苏段文物遗迹的重要组成部分。清晏园现存建筑大部分均为重建，但仍大致保持了原来的历史格局和意境特色。园门东向，入门即见一组湖石假山，石峰嶙峋，洞穴幽然。沿曲廊北转，过圆形随墙门西折，为蕉吟馆，其西为大水池，形态近方，池北有五间歇山正厅，巍峨宏敞，即为乾隆年间高斌所建之荷芳书院原构。池中央立一座重檐攒尖六角亭，通过曲桥与东岸相接。东岸堆叠假山，山北有较射亭，再北为御碑亭，内存康熙帝御笔澹泊宁静碑。荷芳书院之西有紫藤花馆，内藏一株300年以上树龄的古藤。方池西岸建恬波楼，其南水面上有一座重建的清晏舫，再现了昔日画舫斋的神韵。方池南岸堆叠大型黄石假山，山北临水建槐香楼，与荷芳书院、水心亭形成一条中轴线。园西部的关帝庙是一座古庙，其中的大殿尚为明代原构。庙南原有一所旧宅院，并入清晏园后，为了纪念叶挺将军而定名为叶园。清晏园是一座衙署花园，主要供历代河道总督和之后的漕运总督驻节期间休憩赏玩，与皇家园林、私家园林的属性有明显差异。这是一座以治水为主题的古典园林，初名淮园，又名澹园，后改清晏，荷芳书院匾额既形容荷池之芬芳，更取河防二字的谐音。园中曾设澜恬风定之轩、澜安风定轩、恬波楼，都含有安澜平波的意思。这些题名寄托了历代总督平水患、河道平顺的最高理想。园中开辟大定胜天、力挽狂澜的治水主题。清晏园的景致融合南北园林之长，其整体格局具有疏朗旷达的特点，更近于北方园林；就建筑形式和假山、植物的处理来看，又具有素雅细腻的特点，近于江南园林。
projects.content_en: In the Ming Dynasty, the Qingjiangpu town had a branch office of the Ministry of Revenue managing the transport and storage of grain; starting in the Kangxi reign, River Governor Jin Fu converted it into a temporary residence, and his successor Zhang Penghe opened a garden west of the residence. In the 7th year of Yongzheng of the Qing (1729), the court officially established the post of Jiangnan River Governor-General, using the temporary residence as the governor's office; successive governors continuously developed the garden, especially Gao Bin during the Qianlong reign and Lin Qing during the Daoguang reign, who made great contributions. In the 10th year of Xianfeng of the Qing (1860), the governor's office and Qingyan Garden were tragically burned and looted by the Nian Army; in the 1st year of Tongzhi of the Qing (1862), Caoyun Governor-General Wu Tang, stationed here, rebuilt the Caoyun temporary residence and Qingyan Garden on the original site. Thereafter it underwent repeated changes, and was renovated and expanded in the 1980s and 1990s; it is an important part of the cultural relics of the Jiangsu section of the Beijing-Hangzhou Grand Canal. Most of the existing buildings in Qingyan Garden are reconstructions, but they still generally maintain the original historical layout and artistic conception. The garden gate faces east; upon entering, one sees a group of lake-rock rockeries with rugged stone peaks and secluded caves. Turning north along the winding corridor, passing through the round wall-following gate and turning west, is the Jiaoyin (Banana Chanting) Studio; west of it is a large water pool, nearly square in shape; north of the pool are five bays of a hip-and-gable main hall, towering and spacious, which is the original structure of the Hefang (Lotus Fragrance) Academy built by Gao Bin during the Qianlong reign. In the center of the pool stands a double-eave pyramidal hexagonal pavilion, connected to the east bank by a winding bridge. On the east bank, rockeries are piled up; north of the mountain is the Jiaoshe (Archery) Pavilion, and further north is the Imperial Stele Pavilion, containing the 'Tranquil and Indifferent' stele in Emperor Kangxi's imperial calligraphy. West of the Hefang Academy is the Ziteng (Wisteria) Flower Hall, housing an ancient wisteria over 300 years old. On the west bank of the square pool is built the Tianbo (Calm Waves) Tower; on the water south of it is a reconstructed Qingyan Boat, reproducing the charm of the former Painted Boat Studio. On the south bank of the square pool, large yellow-stone rockeries are piled up; north of the mountain, facing the water, is built the Huaixiang (Locust Fragrance) Tower, forming a central axis with the Hefang Academy and the Water Heart Pavilion. The Guandi (Lord Guan) Temple in the west of the garden is an ancient temple, whose main hall is still a Ming Dynasty original structure. South of the temple was originally an old residence; after being incorporated into Qingyan Garden, it was named Ye Garden in memory of General Ye Ting. Qingyan Garden is a government office garden, mainly for successive River Governors-General and later Caoyun Governors-General to rest and enjoy during their tenure, with明显 differences from the attributes of imperial gardens and private gardens. This is a classical garden with the theme of water control, initially named Huai Garden, also called Dan Garden, later renamed Qingyan (Clear Calm); the Hefang Academy plaque not only describes the fragrance of the lotus pond, but also takes the homophone of the two characters 'river defense.' The garden once had the Lantian Fengding (Calm Waves and Steady Wind) Studio, Lan'an Fengding Studio, and Tianbo Tower, all containing the meaning of calm waves and peaceful waters. These names express the highest ideal of successive governors to pacify floods and keep the river smooth. The garden opens up the water-control themes of 'man can conquer nature' and 'turning the tide.' The scenery of Qingyan Garden blends the strengths of northern and southern gardens; its overall layout has the characteristic of openness and spaciousness, closer to northern gardens; in terms of architectural forms and the treatment of rockeries and plants, it also has the characteristic of elegance and delicacy, close to Jiangnan gardens.

projects.name: 清江文庙
projects.level: 江苏省重点文物保护单位（2002年）
projects.level_en: Jiangsu Provincial Key Cultural Heritage Site (2002)
projects.address_en: No. 173 Lunbu Road, Qingpu District
highlights: 明嘉靖九年1530年工部主事邵经济在此处建崇景堂辟为清江书院清代康熙年间利用原户部分司设河道总督行馆清江浦的地位日渐提高于清康熙三十七年1698年在清江书院增设清江文庙庙学合一并由山阳县派驻训导清雍正七年1729年朝廷在清江浦设立江南河道总督署成为全国河道治理中心鼎盛一时清江文庙随之愈加显赫清乾隆二十六年1761年将清河县治迁移到清江浦清江文庙与书院正式成清河县的县学又称学宫清道光三年1823年河道总督黎世序在旧址南侧重建文庙包含棂星门大成门泮池大成殿明伦堂崇圣殿尊经阁东西庑房神库燎炉名宦祠忠孝祠东西学斋等建筑清咸丰十年1860年文庙毁于捻军焚掠清同治四年1865年漕运总督吴棠重建大成殿名宦祠明伦堂崇圣殿同治十一年1872年漕运总督文彬又重建尊经阁和左右斋房逐渐恢复原有格局清末废科举在此改办孔庙小学后历经战乱和政权更迭文庙先后被改为军营粮库器房建筑大多毁失仅存大成殿和崇圣殿等核心建筑近年来得到修复并于2002年被公布为江苏省重点文物保护单位大成殿位于文庙中轴线核心位置为五间周围廊歇山建筑南设月台总面积520平方米崇圣殿位于文庙之北五间硬山建筑这两座殿堂为苏北地区少见的文庙建筑遗存也是昔日淮安地区文教昌盛的重要见证
projects.content_zh: 明嘉靖九年（1530年）工部主事邵经济在此处建崇景堂，辟为清江书院。清代康熙年间利用原户部分司设河道总督行馆，清江浦的地位日渐提高，于清康熙三十七年（1698年）在清江书院增设清江文庙，庙学合一，并由山阳县派驻训导。清雍正七年（1729年）朝廷在清江浦设立江南河道总督署，成为全国河道治理中心，鼎盛一时，清江文庙随之愈加显赫。清乾隆二十六年（1761年）将清河县治迁移到清江浦，清江文庙与书院正式成清河县的县学，又称学宫。清道光三年（1823年）河道总督黎世序在旧址南侧重建文庙，包含棂星门、大成门、泮池、大成殿、明伦堂、崇圣殿、尊经阁、东西庑房、神库、燎炉、名宦祠、忠孝祠、东西学斋等建筑。清咸丰十年（1860年）文庙毁于捻军焚掠，清同治四年（1865年）漕运总督吴棠重建大成殿、名宦祠、明伦堂、崇圣殿，同治十一年（1872年）漕运总督文彬又重建尊经阁和左右斋房，逐渐恢复原有格局。清末废科举，在此改办孔庙小学。后历经战乱和政权更迭，文庙先后被改为军营、粮库、器房，建筑大多毁失，仅存大成殿和崇圣殿等核心建筑，近年来得到修复，并于2002年被公布为江苏省重点文物保护单位。大成殿位于文庙中轴线核心位置，为五间周围廊歇山建筑，南设月台，总面积520平方米。崇圣殿位于文庙之北，五间硬山建筑。这两座殿堂为苏北地区少见的文庙建筑遗存，也是昔日淮安地区文教昌盛的重要见证。
projects.content_en: In the 9th year of Jiajing of the Ming (1530), Shao Jingji, Director of the Ministry of Works, built the Chongjing Hall here and established it as the Qingjiang Academy. During the Kangxi reign of the Qing, the former branch office of the Ministry of Revenue was used to set up the River Governor's temporary residence, and the status of Qingjiangpu gradually increased; in the 37th year of Kangxi of the Qing (1698), the Qingjiang Confucian Temple was added to the Qingjiang Academy, combining temple and school, with an instructor dispatched from Shanyang County. In the 7th year of Yongzheng of the Qing (1729), the court established the Jiangnan River Governor-General Office in Qingjiangpu, becoming the national river management center, prosperous for a time, and the Qingjiang Confucian Temple became increasingly prominent. In the 26th year of Qianlong of the Qing (1761), the county seat of Qinghe County was moved to Qingjiangpu, and the Qingjiang Confucian Temple and Academy officially became the county school of Qinghe County, also called the Xuegong (School Palace). In the 3rd year of Daoguang of the Qing (1823), River Governor-General Li Shixu rebuilt the Confucian Temple south of the old site, including the Lingxing Gate, Dacheng (Great Achievement) Gate, Pan Pond, Dacheng Hall, Minglun (Ethics) Hall, Chongsheng (Worshiping Sages) Hall, Zunjing (Respecting Classics) Pavilion, east and west wing rooms, spirit warehouse, incense burner, Famous Officials Shrine, Loyalty and Filial Piety Shrine, and east and west study rooms etc. In the 10th year of Xianfeng of the Qing (1860), the Confucian Temple was destroyed by Nian Army burning and looting; in the 4th year of Tongzhi of the Qing (1865), Caoyun Governor-General Wu Tang rebuilt the Dacheng Hall, Famous Officials Shrine, Minglun Hall, and Chongsheng Hall; in the 11th year of Tongzhi (1872), Caoyun Governor-General Wen Bin rebuilt the Zunjing Pavilion and left and right study rooms, gradually restoring the original layout. At the end of the Qing, the imperial examinations were abolished, and a Confucius Temple Primary School was established here. Later, through wars and regime changes, the Confucian Temple was successively converted into military barracks, grain warehouses, and equipment rooms, with most buildings destroyed; only core buildings such as the Dacheng Hall and Chongsheng Hall survived, and have been restored in recent years, and was announced as a Jiangsu Provincial Key Cultural Heritage Site in 2002. The Dacheng Hall is located at the core position of the central axis of the Confucian Temple, a five-bay hip-and-gable building with surrounding corridors, with a moon platform to the south, with a total area of 520 square meters. The Chongsheng Hall is located north of the Confucian Temple, a five-bay flush-gable building. These two halls are rare surviving Confucian Temple buildings in the Northern Jiangsu region, and also important witnesses to the former cultural and educational prosperity of the Huai'an region.

projects.name: 涟水月塔
projects.level: 第七批全国重点文物保护单位（2013年）
projects.level_en: 7th Batch National Key Cultural Heritage Site (2013)
projects.address_en: Yueta Village, Tangji Township, Lianshui County
highlights: 月塔位于涟水县唐集乡月塔村始建年代不详从造型判断应为宋代遗物明万历三十四年1605年曾经重修过近代以来最上一层残缺新中国成立后得以修复2013年被公布为全国重点文物保护单位此塔为典型的楼阁式塔通体以砖砌而成塔身为八角形平面每边边长约1.83米总高16米共分7层底层在东南西三面设门自北门入可沿台阶踏步直达二层二层以上以内旋方式设置楼梯盘折而上塔外观模仿木结构每层均设倚柱额枋斗栱和腰檐而且除第六层外都设拱门局部隐刻宋式直棂窗和毬文窗月塔虽然高度有限但是造型秀美细部雕刻精致是淮安现存古塔中艺术水准最高的一座其内部结构也是江苏古塔中的孤例具有不可忽视的独特价值
projects.content_zh: 月塔位于涟水县唐集乡月塔村，始建年代不详，从造型判断，应为宋代遗物，明万历三十四年（1605年）曾经重修过。近代以来最上一层残缺，新中国成立后得以修复，2013年被公布为全国重点文物保护单位。此塔为典型的楼阁式塔，通体以砖砌而成，塔身为八角形平面，每边边长约1.83米，总高16米，共分7层。底层在东、南、西三面设门，自北门入，可沿台阶踏步直达二层，二层以上以内旋方式设置楼梯，盘折而上。塔外观模仿木结构，每层均设倚柱、额枋、斗栱和腰檐，而且除第六层外都设拱门，局部隐刻宋式直棂窗和毬文窗。月塔虽然高度有限，但是造型秀美，细部雕刻精致，是淮安现存古塔中艺术水准最高的一座，其内部结构也是江苏古塔中的孤例，具有不可忽视的独特价值。
projects.content_en: The Moon Pagoda is located in Yueta Village, Tangji Township, Lianshui County; its founding date is unknown, but judging from its form, it should be a Song Dynasty relic; it was once repaired in the 34th year of Wanli of the Ming (1605). In modern times the topmost story was damaged, and it was restored after the founding of New China; in 2013 it was announced as a National Key Cultural Heritage Site. This pagoda is a typical pavilion-style pagoda, entirely built with bricks; the pagoda body has an octagonal plan, with each side about 1.83 meters long, a total height of 16 meters, divided into 7 stories. The bottom story has doors on the east, south, and west sides; entering from the north gate, one can follow the steps directly to the second story; above the second story, a staircase is set in an inward-spiral manner, winding upward. The exterior of the pagoda imitates a wooden structure, with engaged columns, architraves, bracket sets, and waist eaves on each story; moreover, except for the sixth story, all have arched doors, with locally incised Song-style straight-lattice windows and ball-pattern windows. Although the Moon Pagoda has limited height, it has an elegant form and exquisite detail carvings; it is the pagoda with the highest artistic level among the existing ancient pagodas in Huai'an, and its internal structure is also a unique example among ancient pagodas in Jiangsu, with unique value that cannot be ignored.

projects.level: 第四批全国重点文物保护单位（1996年）
projects.level_en: 4th Batch National Key Cultural Heritage Site (1996)
projects.address: 盱眙县明祖陵镇明陵村
projects.address_en: Mingling Village, Mingzuling Town, Xuyi County
highlights: 明祖陵位于洪泽湖北岸的古泗州境内现属淮安市盱眙县仁集乡原名杨家墩是明太祖朱元璋的高祖朱百六曾祖朱四九祖父朱初一的衣冠冢朱元璋祖父母的实际葬地也在陵区内与凤阳皇陵南京孝陵和北京昌平十三陵共同组成明代皇家陵寝的完整体系明洪武十八年1385年朱元璋令皇太子朱标率领文武大臣各色工匠开始动工兴建祖陵至明成祖永乐十一年1413年方才完工前后历时达28年之久清代黄淮几度泛滥明祖陵和泗州古城不断受到洪水的严重威胁清康熙十九年1680年明祖陵终于被彻底淹没沉入洪泽湖底近300年直到1963年因为洪泽湖水位大幅下降这座陵寝才重见天日地面建筑已经不存但石像生和殿堂台基遗址却因为长期居于水下少经风蚀反而保存相对较好明祖陵经过考古研究和保护修复后对外开放并于1996年被公布为第四批全国重点文物保护单位整座明祖陵占地面积上万亩气魄宏伟陵区设砖城两道周长4里10步外面又加筑土城一道周长9里30步相当于一座明代地方城市的规模城外辟金水水河上架设3座金水桥砖墙四面各设一座城门内建五间正殿六间具服殿以及红门燎炉棂星门神厨东西屋值房斋房库房宰牲亭自南往北神道两旁对称排列21对大型石像生包括麒麟2对狮子6对望柱2对马官2对拉马侍者1对天马1对侍从1对文臣2对武将2对内侍太监2对雕刻精美栩栩如生每一座石像均以整块巨石雕成其中最大的拉马侍者像重达24.14米令人惊叹6对狮子形态基本相似细看则明显区分俯仰动静之势9对人像分别高2.9米至3.42米不等或怒目圆睁或面带微笑神态各异神道之北设有享殿配殿宝顶等陵区周围种植了7万多株树木郁郁葱葱
projects.content_zh: 明祖陵位于洪泽湖北岸的古泗州境内（现属淮安市盱眙县仁集乡），原名杨家墩，是明太祖朱元璋的高祖朱百六、曾祖朱四九、祖父朱初一的衣冠冢，朱元璋祖父母的实际葬地也在陵区内，与凤阳皇陵、南京孝陵和北京昌平十三陵共同组成明代皇家陵寝的完整体系。明洪武十八年（1385年），朱元璋令皇太子朱标率领文武大臣、各色工匠开始动工兴建祖陵，至明成祖永乐十一年（1413年）方才完工，前后历时达28年之久。清代黄淮几度泛滥，明祖陵和泗州古城不断受到洪水的严重威胁。清康熙十九年（1680年）明祖陵终于被彻底淹没，沉入洪泽湖底近300年。直到1963年，因为洪泽湖水位大幅下降，这座陵寝才重见天日，地面建筑已经不存，但石像生和殿堂台基遗址却因为长期居于水下，少经风蚀，反而保存相对较好。明祖陵经过考古研究和保护修复后对外开放，并于1996年被公布为第四批全国重点文物保护单位。整座明祖陵，占地面积上万亩，气魄宏伟。陵区设砖城两道，周长4里10步；外面又加筑土城一道，周长9里30步，相当于一座明代地方城市的规模。城外辟金水河，河上架设3座金水桥。砖墙四面各设一座城门，内建五间正殿、六间具服殿以及红门、燎炉、棂星门、神厨、东西屋、值房、斋房、库房、宰牲亭。自南往北，神道两旁对称排列21对大型石像生，包括麒麟2对、狮子6对、望柱2对、马官2对、拉马侍者1对、天马1对、侍从1对、文臣2对、武将2对、内侍太监2对，雕刻精美，栩栩如生。每一座石像均以整块巨石雕成，其中最大的拉马侍者像重达24.14米，令人惊叹。6对狮子形态基本相似，细看则明显区分俯仰动静之势。9对人像分别高2.9米至3.42米不等，或怒目圆睁，或面带微笑，神态各异。神道之北设有享殿、配殿、宝顶等。陵区周围种植了7万多株树木，郁郁葱葱。
projects.content_en: Mingzu Mausoleum is located in the ancient Sizhou territory on the north bank of Hongze Lake (now belonging to Renji Township, Xuyi County, Huai'an City), originally named Yangjiadun; it is the cenotaph of Zhu Yuanzhang, the founder of the Ming Dynasty's great-great-grandfather Zhu Bailiu, great-grandfather Zhu Sijiu, and grandfather Zhu Chuyi; the actual burial place of Zhu Yuanzhang's grandparents is also within the mausoleum area. Together with the Fengyang Imperial Mausoleum, Nanjing Xiaoling Mausoleum, and the Thirteen Ming Tombs in Changping, Beijing, it forms the complete system of Ming Dynasty royal mausoleums. In the 18th year of Hongwu of the Ming (1385), Zhu Yuanzhang ordered Crown Prince Zhu Biao to lead civil and military officials and various craftsmen to begin construction of the ancestral mausoleum; it was not completed until the 11th year of Yongle of the Ming Chengzu (1413), taking a total of 28 years. In the Qing Dynasty, the Yellow River and Huai River flooded several times, and Mingzu Mausoleum and the ancient Sizhou city were continuously threatened by floods. In the 19th year of Kangxi of the Qing (1680), Mingzu Mausoleum was finally completely submerged, sinking to the bottom of Hongze Lake for nearly 300 years. It was not until 1963, because the water level of Hongze Lake dropped significantly, that this mausoleum saw the light of day again; the above-ground buildings no longer exist, but the stone statues and hall foundation ruins, because they were long underwater and less exposed to wind erosion, are instead relatively well preserved. After archaeological research and conservation restoration, Mingzu Mausoleum was opened to the public and was announced as the 4th Batch National Key Cultural Heritage Site in 1996. The entire Mingzu Mausoleum covers an area of over ten thousand mu, with a majestic bearing. The mausoleum area has two brick walls, with a circumference of 4 li and 10 bu; outside, another earthen wall was added, with a circumference of 9 li and 30 bu, equivalent to the scale of a Ming Dynasty local city. Outside the city, a Golden Water River was opened, with 3 Golden Water Bridges spanning the river. Each of the four sides of the brick wall has a city gate; inside are built five bays of main hall, six bays of dressing hall, as well as the red gate, incense burner, Lingxing Gate, divine kitchen, east and west rooms, duty rooms, fasting rooms, warehouses, and slaughter pavilion. From south to north, 21 pairs of large stone statues are symmetrically arranged on both sides of the spirit way, including 2 pairs of qilin, 6 pairs of lions, 2 pairs of ornamental columns, 2 pairs of horse officials, 1 pair of horse-leading attendants, 1 pair of heavenly horses, 1 pair of attendants, 2 pairs of civil officials, 2 pairs of military generals, and 2 pairs of eunuch attendants, exquisitely carved and lifelike. Each stone statue is carved from a single整块 giant stone; among them, the largest horse-leading attendant statue weighs 24.14 tons, amazing. The 6 pairs of lions are basically similar in form, but upon close inspection clearly distinguish between looking up/down and moving/static postures. The 9 pairs of human figures are respectively 2.9 to 3.42 meters high, some with glaring eyes, some with smiling faces, with various expressions. North of the spirit way are the offering hall, side halls, and burial mound etc. Over 70,000 trees are planted around the mausoleum area, lush and verdant.

projects.name: 盱眙第一山
projects.level: 第七批全国重点文物保护单位（2013年）
projects.level_en: 7th Batch National Key Cultural Heritage Site (2013)
projects.address_en: North Huaihe Road, Xuyi County
highlights: 盱眙第一山又名南山都梁山雄踞于淮河南岸前临千里长河背依九座山峰景致优美人文遗迹与自然风光并胜是淮河流域一大名胜盱眙二字的原意是放眼远望即所谓张目为盱举目为眙通常认为正是因为登此山远望而得名第一山位于汴水与淮河的交汇处扼守航运要道唐宋以来无数达官显宦文人墨客途经盱眙时都曾经登山游览留下了大量的诗文碑刻北宋绍圣四年1097年大书画家米芾赴任涟水由首都东京今河南省开封市经汴水一路南下沿途均为平原地区入淮时突然看见岸边山峰耸立丘壑奇秀于是即兴作诗曰京洛风尘千里还船头出汴翠屏间莫论横霍撞星斗且是东南第一山并手书第一山三个大字勒碑留于山间从此此山得名第一山有趣的是明代淮安一代文豪吴承恩的巨著西游记中罗列了很多虚无缥缈的仙山极少提及现实中的真山却在第66回中以生动笔墨描写了一座盱眙山行者纵起筋斗云躲离怪处直奔盱眙山不一日早到细观真好去处南近江津北临淮水东通海峤西接封君山上有楼观峥嵘山凹里有涧泉浩涌嵯峨怪石磐秀乔松百般果品应时新千样花枝迎日放人如蚁阵往来多船似雁行归去广上边有瑞岩观东岳宫五星祠龟山寺等钟韵香烟冲碧汉又有玻璃泉五塔峪八仙台杏花园山光树色映虫宾城白云横不度幽鸟倦还唱说甚泰嵩衡华秀此间仙景若蓬瀛这正是第一山的真实写照很可能当年吴承恩本人曾经游赏过故乡附近的这座名山留下了美好的印象这才在西游记中留下了这段奇妙的文字由于历史的沧桑演变第一山诸多的古建筑遭到毁弃但有北宋以来部分遗物和若干石刻幸存至今改革开放以来陆续得到修复和重建1996年被评为国家级森林公园第一山题刻于2013年被国务院公布为第七批全国重点文物保护地位山麓的文庙始建于南宋绍兴十三年1143年之后屡废屡兴近年再次重建其中的明伦堂尚为清代原构山上的东坡草亭是纪念苏轼的景点建筑而倚靠石壁的玻璃泉和旁边的六角亭则是第一山的重要景致山壁左侧还保存着元朝大书法家赵孟頫晚年所作的泗州普照禅寺灵瑞塔残碑在秀岩瑞岩和西域寺3处摩崖存有88件题刻与山上其他78块碑碣同为第一山最宝贵的文化财富秀岩山崖上有苏轼手书的行书香子还有几处南宋使臣的题记沿石径而上可见会景亭遗址在此可南瞰长淮西赏宝积山视野开阔远近高低景致尽收眼底当年米芾亲题的第一山石碑立于坡上笔势雄健潇洒照耀千古山上的魁星亭建于清道光二十四年1844年亭内藏有一块非字非画图案奇异的魁星碑中央大书魁字左半如灵猫右半为北斗七星据说可保佑应试学子高中原碑毁于文革时期1987年根据拓片重刻
projects.content_zh: 盱眙第一山又名南山、都梁山，雄踞于淮河南岸，前临千里长河，背依九座山峰，景致优美，人文遗迹与自然风光并胜，是淮河流域一大名胜。盱眙二字的原意是放眼远望，即所谓张目为盱，举目为眙，通常认为正是因为登此山远望而得名。第一山位于汴水与淮河的交汇处，扼守航运要道，唐宋以来，无数达官显宦、文人墨客途经盱眙时都曾经登山游览，留下了大量的诗文、碑刻。北宋绍圣四年（1097年），大书画家米芾赴任涟水，由首都东京（今河南省开封市）经汴水一路南下，沿途均为平原地区，入淮时突然看见岸边山峰耸立，丘壑奇秀，于是即兴作诗曰：京洛风尘千里还，船头出汴翠屏间。莫论横霍撞星斗，且是东南第一山。并手书第一山三个大字，勒碑留于山间，从此此山得名第一山。有趣的是，明代淮安一代文豪吴承恩的巨著《西游记》中罗列了很多虚无缥缈的仙山，极少提及现实中的真山，却在第66回中以生动笔墨描写了一座盱眙山：行者纵起筋斗云，躲离怪处，直奔盱眙山。不一日，早到。细观，真好去处：南近江津，北临淮水。东通海峤，西接封君。山上有楼观峥嵘，山凹里有涧泉浩涌。嵯峨怪石，磐秀乔松。百般果品应时新，千样花枝迎日放。人如蚁阵往来多，船似雁行归去广。上边有瑞岩观、东岳宫、五星祠、龟山寺等，钟韵香烟冲碧汉；又有玻璃泉、五塔峪、八仙台、杏花园，山光树色映虫宾城。白云横不度，幽鸟倦还唱。说甚泰嵩衡华秀，此间仙景若蓬瀛。这正是第一山的真实写照，很可能当年吴承恩本人曾经游赏过故乡附近的这座名山，留下了美好的印象，这才在《西游记》中留下了这段奇妙的文字。由于历史的沧桑演变，第一山诸多的古建筑遭到毁弃，但有北宋以来部分遗物和若干石刻幸存至今，改革开放以来陆续得到修复和重建，1996年被评为国家级森林公园，第一山题刻于2013年被国务院公布为第七批全国重点文物保护地位。山麓的文庙始建于南宋绍兴十三年（1143年），之后屡废屡兴，近年再次重建，其中的明伦堂尚为清代原构。山上的东坡草亭是纪念苏轼的景点建筑，而倚靠石壁的玻璃泉和旁边的六角亭则是第一山的重要景致，山壁左侧还保存着元朝大书法家赵孟頫晚年所作的《泗州普照禅寺灵瑞塔》残碑。在秀岩、瑞岩和西域寺3处摩崖存有88件题刻，与山上其他78块碑碣同为第一山最宝贵的文化财富。秀岩山崖上有苏轼手书的行书《行香子》，还有几处南宋使臣的题记。沿石径而上，可见会景亭遗址，在此可南瞰长淮，西赏宝积山，视野开阔，远近高低景致尽收眼底。当年米芾亲题的第一山石碑立于坡上，笔势雄健潇洒，照耀千古。山上的魁星亭建于清道光二十四年（1844年），亭内藏有一块非字非画、图案奇异的魁星碑，中央大书魁字，左半如灵猫，右半为北斗七星，据说可保佑应试学子高中。原碑毁于文革时期，1987年根据拓片重刻。
projects.content_en: Xuyi First Mountain, also called South Mountain and Duliang Mountain, stands majestically on the south bank of the Huai River, facing the thousand-mile long river in front and backed by nine mountain peaks; with beautiful scenery, cultural relics and natural scenery both excelling, it is a major scenic spot in the Huai River basin. The original meaning of the two characters 'Xuyi' is to look far into the distance, the so-called 'opening eyes wide is xu, raising eyes is yi'; it is generally believed that the name comes precisely from climbing this mountain to look far away. First Mountain is located at the confluence of the Bian River and Huai River, guarding the shipping thoroughfare; since the Tang and Song dynasties, countless high officials and literati, when passing through Xuyi, have climbed the mountain for sightseeing, leaving a large number of poems, essays, and stele carvings. In the 4th year of Shaosheng of the Northern Song (1097), the great calligrapher and painter Mi Fu, going to take office in Lianshui, traveled south from the capital Dongjing (today's Kaifeng City, Henan Province) along the Bian River; the route was all plain terrain, and when entering the Huai River he suddenly saw mountain peaks rising on the bank, with奇特 ravines and beauty, so he improvised a poem: 'Returning a thousand li from the dust of Jingluo, the boat's bow emerges from Bian into the emerald screen. Do not speak of Heng and Huo striking the stars; this is the First Mountain of the Southeast.' And he personally wrote the three large characters 'First Mountain,' carving a stele to leave in the mountains; from then on this mountain was named First Mountain. Interestingly, in the masterpiece 'Journey to the West' by Wu Cheng'en, a great literary figure of Ming Dynasty Huai'an, many illusory immortal mountains are listed, with real mountains rarely mentioned, yet in Chapter 66 he vividly describes a Xuyi Mountain: 'The traveler soared on his somersault cloud, escaping from the monster's place, heading straight for Xuyi Mountain. In less than a day he arrived. Looking closely, what a wonderful place: south near the river ford, north facing the Huai River. East connecting to the sea promontory, west bordering Fengjun. On the mountain are towering pavilions and halls; in the mountain hollows are surging spring waters. Rugged strange rocks, graceful tall pines. All kinds of fruits fresh in season, a thousand kinds of flowering branches blooming toward the sun. People come and go like ant columns, boats return like wild geese in formation. Above are Ruiyan Temple, Dongyue Palace, Five-Star Shrine, Guishan Temple etc., with bell sounds and incense smoke rushing to the blue sky; also there are Glass Spring, Five-Tower Valley, Eight-Immortal Terrace, Apricot Flower Garden, with mountain light and tree colors reflecting the city. White clouds hang without moving, secluded birds tired yet still sing. Why speak of the beauty of Tai, Song, Heng, and Hua? This immortal scene here is like Penglai.' This is precisely the true portrayal of First Mountain; it is very likely that Wu Cheng'en himself once visited this famous mountain near his hometown, leaving a good impression, and thus left this wonderful text in 'Journey to the West.' Due to the vicissitudes of history, many ancient buildings on First Mountain were destroyed, but some relics since the Northern Song and several stone carvings have survived to this day; since the Reform and Opening Up they have been successively restored and rebuilt, and in 1996 it was rated as a national forest park; the First Mountain inscriptions were announced by the State Council as the 7th Batch National Key Cultural Heritage Site in 2013. The Confucian Temple at the foot of the mountain was first built in the 13th year of Shaoxing of the Southern Song (1143), and was repeatedly abandoned and revived thereafter; in recent years it was rebuilt again, among which the Minglun Hall is still a Qing Dynasty original structure. The Dongpo Thatched Pavilion on the mountain is a scenic building commemorating Su Shi, while the Glass Spring leaning against the stone wall and the adjacent hexagonal pavilion are important scenery of First Mountain; on the left side of the mountain wall also survives the残 stele of 'Lingrui Pagoda of Puzhao Chan Temple in Sizhou' made in the later years of the great Yuan Dynasty calligrapher Zhao Mengfu. At the three cliff locations of Xiuyan, Ruiyan, and Xiyu Temple, 88 inscriptions are preserved, which together with the other 78 steles on the mountain are the most precious cultural wealth of First Mountain. On the Xiuyan cliff is Su Shi's handwritten running script 'Xingxiangzi,' as well as several inscriptions by Southern Song envoys. Climbing up along the stone path, one can see the ruins of the Huijing (Scenery-Gathering) Pavilion, from which one can overlook the Long Huai to the south and enjoy Baoji Mountain to the west, with a broad视野 and all scenery near and far, high and low, in view. The 'First Mountain' stele personally inscribed by Mi Fu stands on the slope, with vigorous and elegant brush strokes, shining through the ages. The Kuixing (Star of Literature) Pavilion on the mountain was built in the 24th year of Daoguang of the Qing (1844); inside the pavilion is a Kuixing stele that is neither purely character nor purely painting, with a奇异 pattern; in the center the large character 'Kui' is written, the left half like a spirit cat, the right half the Big Dipper seven stars; it is said to bless exam-taking students to pass. The original stele was destroyed during the Cultural Revolution, and was recarved from a rubbing in 1987.

regions.name: 淮安

regions.overview: 连云港市地处黄海之滨，江苏省东北部，东与日本、韩国、朝鲜隔海相望。远古时期就有人类在这里生活。夏代海州被称为羽山，夏商时期属徐州，称人方东夷、人方国、隅夷。西周时期属青州（一说兖州），称人方国东夷。春秋战国时期先属鲁后属楚，称郯子国。秦代称东海郡，辖朐县、郯城等36个县，此后称东海郡、东海国等，秦朝设东海郡、改为朐县，东魏时期始称海州。连云港古建筑以摩崖石刻、岩画、古塔为特色，孔望山摩崖造像是我国最早的石窟寺艺术雕刻，将军崖岩画是中国最古老的原始岩画，被誉为东方天书。
regions.overview_en: Lianyungang City is located on the coast of the Yellow Sea, in the northeast of Jiangsu Province, facing Japan, South Korea, and North Korea across the sea to the east. Humans lived here in ancient times. In the Xia Dynasty, Haizhou was called Yushan; in the Xia and Shang periods it belonged to Xuzhou, called Renfang Dongyi, Renfang State, and Yuyi. In the Western Zhou period it belonged to Qingzhou (one theory says Yanzhou), called Renfang State Dongyi. During the Spring and Autumn and Warring States periods it first belonged to Lu and then to Chu, called the Tanzi State. In the Qin Dynasty it was called Donghai Commandery, administering 36 counties including Qu County and Tancheng; thereafter it was called Donghai Commandery, Donghai State etc.; the Qin Dynasty established Donghai Commandery and changed it to Qu County, and in the Eastern Wei period it began to be called Haizhou. Lianyungang's ancient architecture features cliff carvings, rock paintings, and ancient pagodas; the Kongwang Mountain cliff statues are the earliest grotto temple art carvings in China, and the General Cliff rock paintings are the oldest primitive rock paintings in China, known as the 'Eastern Heavenly Book.'
